16989598:
Distributor troubleshooting for a 500 Internal Server Error in Encompass: hard refresh, clear cache, find the trigger, and what details to send Support. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must have an active internet connection and access to the web application or service.

  • Requires access to the specific URL or system workflow where the error was generated.

  • For advanced troubleshooting, requires administrative or developer access to system logs, environment configurations, and deployment history.

Steps

  • Refresh the Page: Hard refresh your browser (Ctrl+F5 on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac) to ensure the error is not a momentary connectivity glitch or a temporary timeout.

  • Clear Browser Cache and Cookies: Clear your browser's cached data and cookies to ensure you are not loading stale or conflicting session data that might be causing a bad request to the server.

  • Identify the Trigger: Attempt to replicate the issue by repeating the exact steps you took before the error occurred. Note if the error happens on a specific page, during a specific data entry, or upon submitting a specific form.

  • Check for Recent Deployments (System Administrators): Review the deployment log to see if any recent software versions, configuration updates, or environment changes were introduced right before the issue started.

  • Verify Configurations (System Administrators): Check environment configurations, including connection strings, key vaults, and required secrets, to ensure none are missing or expired.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after attempting the steps above, please contact our support team. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, gather and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (including any trace IDs or detailed text displayed on the screen).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue occurring.

    • Log files (specifically server-side application logs or stack traces, if accessible).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue (e.g., "Logged in, clicked 'Reports', selected 'June', clicked 'Export'").

    • The date and time the issue was first observed, your time zone, and any recurrence patterns.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared (e.g., recent system upgrades, changed permissions).

Fields And Definitions

  • 500 Internal Server Error: A generic HTTP status code indicating that the server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request.

  • Unhandled Runtime Exception: An error that occurs during the execution of back-end code that the application is not programmed to handle or bypass gracefully.

  • Null Reference: A programmatic error where the code attempts to access or interact with an object, variable, or data point that has no assigned value (is null).

  • Type Cast Failure: A coding error that occurs when the system attempts to treat a piece of data as the wrong format (e.g., trying to read text as a number).

  • SQL Runtime Error: An error that occurs when the application attempts to communicate with the database, often caused by bad query formatting, missing data, or connection timeouts.

  • Downstream Dependency Failure: An outage or error that occurs when a secondary system, API, or service that the primary application relies upon fails to respond correctly.

Best Practices

  • Robust Error Handling: Ensure development teams implement comprehensive try/catch blocks within back-end code to gracefully handle exceptions and provide user-friendly error messages rather than raw 500 status codes.

  • Pre-Deployment Verification: Always verify environment configurations (like connection strings and key vaults) in a staging environment before deploying to production to prevent configuration incompatibilities.

  • Dependency Monitoring: Set up automated monitoring and alerting for all downstream dependencies and third-party APIs to quickly identify when an external service is causing internal failures.

  • Detailed Logging: Maintain detailed, centralized server logs that capture full stack traces for runtime exceptions, allowing for rapid root-cause analysis when 500 errors do occur.

16989600:
Distributor troubleshooting for orderIQ suggested quantities: trace Suggested Order History back to Num Units in orderIQ Model Data and Order Size overrides/configurations; fix low or missing suggestions. Requires v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Pre-Conditions

How to read this article: A table is where Encompass stores a set of records (for example, the Suggested Order History table). A field is a single piece of data on a record within a table (for example, the Suggested Order Quantity field). Table and field names appear in bold throughout, and each is labeled as a table or a field.

Before you begin, you will need:

  • The Customer, Product, and pre-sell date (or the downloaded Event) of the recommendation you are investigating.
    ​
    ​

  • Access to these tables: the Suggested Order History table, the orderIQ Model Data table, the Suggested Order Overrides table, the Suggested Order Configurations table, and the orderIQ Customer Product Combinations table.

Steps

How OrderIQ calculates the suggested quantity

The quantity a sales rep sees on the Invoice Edit page in Encompass Mobile is stored in the Suggested Order Quantity field on a record in the Suggested Order History table. OrderIQ calculates it with this formula:

Suggested Order Quantity = round( Num Units × Order Size )

The Num Units field (in the orderIQ Model Data table) is OrderIQ's forecast for that customer, product, and date. The Order Size field is the multiplier applied to that forecast. The result is rounded and saved as the Suggested Order Quantity field.

To trace a recommendation back to its source:

  1. Open the Suggested Order History table and filter by the Customer, Product, and Date fields (the pre-sell date; on mobile this is tied to the downloaded Event). Read the Suggested Order Quantity field – this is the number the rep saw.
    ​
    ​

  2. Open the orderIQ Model Data table and filter by the same Customer, Product, and Date fields. Read the Num Units field (the forecast), and for context the Lower Bound and Upper Bound fields.
    ​
    ​

  3. Find the Order Size multiplier that was applied. First check the Suggested Order Overrides table for a record that matches this Product (or its brand, package, or supplier). If one applies, use its Order Size field. If no override applies, use the Order Size field on the account's record in the Suggested Order Configurations table.
    ​
    ​

  4. Multiply and round: Num Units × Order Size, rounded, equals the Suggested Order Quantity field from step 1.

Fields And Definitions

Fields are grouped below by the table they belong to.

In the Suggested Order History table:

  • Suggested Order Quantity - The suggested number shown on the Invoice Edit page.
    ​
    ​

  • Date - The pre-sell date the suggestion is for.
    ​
    ​

  • Event - Links the suggestion to the route stop the salesperson downloaded.
    ​
    ​

  • Source - Indicates how the suggestion was generated.

In the orderIQ Model Data table:

  • Num Units - OrderIQ's forecast, in units, before the Order Size multiplier is applied.
    ​
    ​

  • Lower Bound / Upper Bound - The forecast confidence range around Num Units.
    ​
    ​

  • Is Used - Whether this record fed the suggestion.

In the Suggested Order Overrides table:

  • Order Size - The multiplier applied to Num Units when the override matches a product (or its brand, package, or supplier). Takes priority over the configuration value.
    ​
    ​

  • Round Threshold - Controls how the multiplied result is rounded.
    ​
    ​

  • Force To Case - Forces the result to whole-case quantities.

In the Suggested Order Configurations table:

  • Order Size - The account-level default multiplier, used when no override applies to the product.

In the orderIQ Customer Product Combinations table:

  • Sales Type - Classifies the product's sales pattern: Smooth, Intermittent, or Erratic. Only Smooth and Intermittent generate a record in the Suggested Order History table.

Best Practices

Use these troubleshooting paths when a suggestion looks wrong. Each one names the exact field and table to check.

  • If the suggested quantity is lower than what the rep usually orders, and the customer has two pre-sell stops in the week → Check the Order Size field in the Suggested Order Overrides table. For a two-stop customer, enter Order Size as a pair “xx;xx” – one value per stop. If you enter a single value, only the first stop uses the override; the second stop falls back to the smaller Order Size field in the Suggested Order Configurations table, so the second stop reads low.
    ​
    Example A – product 18174, customer 4926, override Order Size 2: first stop (7/14) = Num Units 9 × 2 = 18 (rep ordered 14); second stop (7/16) = Num Units × 0.62 (configuration Order Size) = 5 (rep ordered 7). Entering “2;2” applies the override to both stops.
    ​
    Example B – product 44074, customer 6182, override Order Size 4: second stop (7/16) = Num Units 1.940166 × 0.56 (configuration Order Size) ≈ 1 (rep ordered 3). The first stop used the override; the second fell back to the configuration.
    ​
    ​

  • If the forecast itself looks low → Check the Num Units, Lower Bound, and Upper Bound fields in the orderIQ Model Data table. Num Units accounts for holidays and promotions, so right after an event week (for example, the week of July 4th) with no upcoming event, the forecast drops toward the typical “no-event” level. Compare Num Units against its Lower Bound/Upper Bound range and the account's recent weekly sales before concluding it is wrong.
    ​
    ​

  • If no suggestion appears at all for a product → Check the Sales Type field in the orderIQ Customer Product Combinations table. Only products with Sales Type = Smooth or Intermittent generate a record in the Suggested Order History table. If the Sales Type is Erratic, OrderIQ creates no suggestion and nothing appears on Invoice Edit.
    ​
    ​

  • Remember the suggestion is a starting point → Reps can adjust the Suggested Order Quantity field on the invoice before submitting, so an occasional low or high suggestion can be corrected at the point of order.
16989601:
Producer steps for building equipment maintenance (CIP) recipes on the Recipe Management dashboard: Maintenance recipe type, non-inventory CIP product, recipe stages and instructions. Needs Maintenance stage types and expense mapping; v25.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.12

Pre-Conditions

  1. Production Stage Types built out for Maintenance

  2. Production Stage Type Equipment Types mapped to allow Maintenance to be done on the expected Equipment Types

  3. Products set up as non-inventory Product Types that represent the CIP/Maintenance that will be set on Mainteance Recipes

  4. Products set up as inventoried or non-inventoried to use in Maintenance Recipes as Components

  5. Expense Account Mapping set up for the Non-Inventory CIP/Maintenance Products that will credit the expected Overhead/Expense/Maintenance Accounts and Expense Account Maps for any Non-Inventory Products that will be used in CIP/Maintenance Recipes

Steps

How to Build Maintenance Recipes
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Recipe Management dashboard.
​
​ Note: The Recipe Management dashboard can also be access from the Production Cloud Home dashboard.
​
2. Click Add Recipe Version.
​
​This is the collection of steps and ingredients that will be used to schedule Production Orders and Batches.
​
3. Fill out all required fields as well as supporting fields:
​
​ a. Recipe Version - The unique name of the version. If there will be different Recipes for different Equipment Maintenance, identify which equipment can be scheduled with each recipe in its name

Example: FV CIP
​
​ b. Location -The Facility this maintenance will take place in.
​
c. Product - The Non-Inventory CIP Product that is mapped to the appropriate Expense Account for capturing Maintenance overhead
​
d. Recipe Type - Maintenance must be used
​
e. Planned Units = 1.
​
f. UoM (Unit of Measure) - Each / Unit

4. Click Add Recipe Version.
​
​ There is now an empty recipe with no Recipe Stages, Recipe Components or Instructions.
​
​

Adding Recipe Stages:
​
​1. Click Add Recipe Stages.
​
2. Fill out all required fields:
​
a. Stage Type - Choose the Maintenance Production Stage Type. If none exists, you will need to create one. See Preconditions on this Help Resource
​
b. Output per Turn - set to 1
​
c. Planned Units - set to 1
​
d. Turnable - False
​
e. Lead Time - Estimated time required to complete the Maintenance/CIP.
​
​

3. Click Add Recipe Stage.

Fields And Definitions

  • Recipe Versions - Set of Instructions, broken up into Stages to produce a predetermined Product.
    ​
    ​

  • Recipe Stages - A singular workflow for Users to follow. Grouping Instructions and Components by Timing and Sequence allows Users to do everything in the proper order at the proper time.
    ​
    ​

  • Recipe Management Dashboard - the hub for managing Recipes:
    ​
    - Products - includes Raw Material Products, Work in Process Products, and Finished Goods Products
    ​
    - Production Stage Types - A grouping of actions/inputs that comprise a single Recipe Stage in a Recipe. Verbs like Blending, Filtering, Pasteurizing, etc. feature here
    ​
    - QC Measurements - Quality Control Measurements that are taken during any Recipe at any Stage. Measurements are pulled from the QC Measurements Table
    ​
    ​ Note: To automatically add QC Templates into Recipes as they are being built, please refer to the QC Templates Training

Recipe Stages:
​
​

  • Transfer When Complete - Determines the end of this stage.
    ​
    Select True: If this stage ends by transferring to a new piece of equipment
    ​
    Select False: The current stage is completed, but we are not yet ready to move product into the equipment required for the next stage.
    ​
    ​

  • Memo - An overall note for Users during this Recipe Stage. It will appear at the top of the card on Users handhelds.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Instruction - Input direction for Users to see during Handheld processing. This adds line-by-line memos to guide users through processing.
    ​
    ​

  • Timing - This dictates the amount of time into the Recipe Stage that an Instruction or a Component is to be followed or added.
    ​
    Note: Timing also dictates which Components and Instructions show up on the same card when processing on the Handheld
    ​
    ​

  • Sequence -The order in which Components or Instructions with the same Timing are displayed on Users Handhelds.

Best Practices

  • Do not build CIP equipment- Maintenance recipes are designed to occupy production eequipment so batching cannot be run through them while maintenance is happening. Only the piece of equipment being worked on will be occupied in Batch Management.
    ​
    ​

  • Use Instructions in Recipes - Instructions give operators well-defined direction to perform these tasks.

  • Unit of Measure - Since Maintenance produces no inventory, only consuming it, set all outputs to a unit of 1
16989602:
Using AP IQ (v26.08+) to upload vendor invoices for OCR, resolve exceptions (Accounts Missing, Total Mismatched, PO Not Found), pre-code Non-PO invoices, review PO variances, and manage multi-tier approvals.

Watch video on Wistia

Step-by-Step Workflows

​

  • Navigate to the AP IQ Dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  • Click the Upload button.
    ​
    ​

  • In the modal, select the Invoice Type (PO or Non-PO).
    ​
    - Note: Non-PO workflows are exclusive to Encompass Financials.
    ​
    ​

  • Select the relevant Company and Location.
    ​
    ​

  • Select files from your local machine (Maximum 100 files per upload).
    ​
    ​

  • Click Upload to start the OCR processing.

​

​

  • Accounts Missing: Expand the grid to assign the necessary GL Account and Dimension tags.
    ​
    ​

  • Total Mismatched: Expand the grid and adjust line "Diff" amounts until their sum matches the Header Total.
    ​
    ​

  • Vendor Missing (PO): Manually link the correct Vendor or Purchase Order.

​

    ​
    ​

    ​

​

    ​
    ​

Fields And Definitions

Status Definitions & Troubleshooting

Non-PO Statuses
​
​

  • Failed: File did not import correctly. Review PDF for corruption and re-upload.
    ​
    ​

  • Accounts Missing: Invoice imported, but line items lack accounts. Assign accounts/tags on the dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  • Total Mismatched: Header total does not equal the sum of lines. Adjust line amounts to balance.
    ​
    ​

  • Ready to Approve: Imported and validated; awaiting initial submission.
    ​
    ​

  • In Progress: Partially approved; awaiting higher-level authorization.

PO Statuses
​
​

  • PO Not Found: Could not find a matching PO. Manually link the correct PO on the dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  • Product Mismatch: Line item does not match linked PurchaseTrans info. Link the correct Product ID.
    ​
    ​

  • Quantity/Price Variance: Discrepancies detected. Review and submit for investigation/approval.
    ​
    ​

  • Auto Approved: Invoice matched the received Purchase precisely; no action needed.

Best Practices

  • File Preparation: AP IQ handles only a single vendor invoice per file. Break out files containing multiple invoices before uploading.
    ​
    ​

  • 3-Way Reconciliation: To achieve strict comparison between the original PO, physical receipt, and invoice, enable the "Blind Receiving" flag for the specific Vendor.
    ​

  • Post-Approval Corrections: AP IQ handles creation and approval only. Corrections required after final approval must be performed using standard Encompass workflows.
    ​

  • Approval Routing: Remember that routing is determined by the Vendor's assigned Approval Team and the total invoice amount, not by GL accounts or dimensions.

16989603:
Distributor troubleshooting for a 414 Request-URI Too Long error in Encompass, usually from too many filters or API GET payloads: reduce filters, clear cache, use POST. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must have an active internet connection.

  • Must be able to access the web application or API endpoint experiencing the error.

  • Must know the specific actions (e.g., applying specific filters, running a report, or submitting a form) being performed when the error triggered.

  • For advanced steps, the user must have administrative access to network settings or developer tools.

Steps

  • Reduce Applied Filters: If you are using a web interface and selecting a massive amount of checkboxes, filters, or specific ID arrays, clear these selections. Attempt to run the query or load the page with fewer filters applied.

  • Clear Browser Cache and Cookies: To rule out a recursive redirect loop where routing parameters are being appended repeatedly by cached site data, clear your browser's cache and cookies, or attempt to replicate the action in an Incognito/Private browsing window.

  • Validate API Payload Methods (For API Users/Developers): If you are passing data programmatically, ensure your script is not incorrectly serializing a large data payload and appending it to the URL via a GET request. Switch to a POST request and place the payload in the request body.

  • Check Local Network and Proxy Settings: If you are on a corporate network, consult with your internal IT team to ensure a local firewall, reverse proxy, or web server isn't imposing abnormally strict URI length restrictions.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after attempting the steps above, please contact our support team to ensure an efficient investigation. Gather and provide the following specific information:

    • The exact error messages or codes encountered (e.g., "414 Request-URI Too Long").

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue, making sure the full URL in the address bar is visible.

    • Network Log files (e.g., a HAR file exported from your browser's developer tools) demonstrating the failed request.

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue, including the specific page and data being accessed.

    • The precise date and time (including time zone) the issue was first observed, and any recurrence patterns.

    • Any changes made to the system, network configurations, or code before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • 414 Request-URI Too Long: An HTTP status code (Client Error) indicating that the server is refusing to service the request because the requested URL is longer than the server is configured to interpret.

  • GET Request: An HTTP method used to request data from a specified resource. Data sent via a GET request is appended to the URL as a query string.

  • POST Request: An HTTP method used to send data to a server to create or update a resource. The data payload is stored in the request body, safely bypassing URL length limitations.

  • Query String: The portion of a URL that assigns values to specified parameters (often starting with a ? and separated by &), which can quickly inflate URL length if too many variables are included.

  • Recursive Redirect Loop: A routing error where a page continually redirects to itself or another page, appending additional data to the URL upon each hop until the server's character limit is broken.

  • Reverse Proxy: A server that sits in front of backend web servers and forwards client requests to them. These proxies have their own configurations that can limit allowed URL lengths.

Best Practices

  • Batch Your Queries: When attempting to pull data for hundreds or thousands of specific IDs, break the request into smaller batches rather than attempting to pass them all at once in a single URL.

  • Use the Right HTTP Method: Always design system integrations to use POST or PUT methods for operations that require transmitting significant amounts of serialized data.

  • Avoid Over-Filtering: Use broader search terms or utilize built-in reporting categories instead of manually clicking hundreds of individual filter variables within web application dashboards.

  • Standardize Server Limits: If you are managing internal servers, ensure that URI length restrictions across all web servers and reverse proxies are standardized and configured to handle the realistic maximum URL length generated by your specific applications.

16989605:
Distributor/API user troubleshooting for a 400 Bad Request error in Encompass: check query parameters, headers, JSON formatting and data types, and what to send Support. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Access to the application, API client (e.g., Postman, curl), or integration code initiating the request.

  • Access to the API documentation or expected request schema for the endpoint being called.

  • Basic understanding of how to inspect HTTP requests, including URLs, headers, and body payloads.

Steps

  • Check Query Parameters: Review the request URL to ensure all required query parameters are included, correctly spelled, and formatted according to the API documentation.

  • Verify Request Headers: Inspect the outgoing request headers. Ensure all required headers (such as Authorization or Content-Type) are present and that there are no invalid or unsupported headers included.

  • Validate JSON Formatting: If sending a payload, use a JSON linter or validator to confirm that the request body is valid JSON and not malformed (e.g., missing quotes, trailing commas, or unmatched brackets).

  • Confirm Data Types: Compare the data sent in your client payload against the server schema. Ensure there are no data type mismatches (e.g., sending a string like "123" when the server expects an integer 123).

  • Review Structural Validation: Check the overall structure of your payload to ensure it matches the exact hierarchy and nesting required by the server-side structural validation rules.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after attempting the steps above, please contact our support team. Provide the following information for efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (including the raw response body from the server).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue (e.g., showing the API client setup or application state).

    • Log files (specifically network logs, client application error logs, or exported HAR files).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue (including the exact endpoint URL, HTTP method, headers, and full payload).

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system, application code, or integration before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • 400 Bad Request: An HTTP response status code indicating that the server cannot or will not process the request due to an apparent client error (e.g., malformed request syntax, invalid parameters, or data mismatch).

  • Query Parameters: Key-value pairs appended to the end of a URL (after a ? mark) used to pass data or instructions to the server.

  • Request Headers: Metadata sent along with an HTTP request (like Content-Type: application/json) that provides the server with context about the request and the client making it.

  • JSON Format (JavaScript Object Notation): A standardized, lightweight format for storing and transporting data, frequently used for API request payloads.

  • Payload Body: The actual data message transmitted in the HTTP request, typically containing the information the server needs to create or update a record.

  • Server Schema: The defined blueprint or set of rules on the server that dictates the exact structure, mandatory fields, and data types a payload must adhere to.

Best Practices

  • Utilize API Testing Tools: Always test and build your requests in a dedicated API client (like Postman or Insomnia) to easily isolate configuration issues before hardcoding them into your application.

  • Implement Client-Side Validation: Add structural and data-type validation to your client-side application before the HTTP request is dispatched. This catches errors locally and prevents unnecessary server load.

  • Reference the Latest Documentation: API endpoints and schemas can evolve. Always ensure you are building requests against the most up-to-date version of the developer documentation.

  • Log Full API Responses: When building automated integrations, ensure your error-handling logic captures and logs the entire HTTP 400 response body, as servers often return detailed hints about exactly which field or header failed validation.
16989606:
Brewery/distillery steps in Encompass for generating the TTB Excise Tax Return (Form 5000.24) PDF from BRO or DRO reports, reviewing past returns and correcting them. Needs TTB Reporting access; v26.02+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.02

Pre-Conditions

Before generating a return, reports for the relevant Brewery Report of Operations (BRO) or Distilled Spirits Plant Operations (DRO) reports for the specific tax period should be created and reveiwed. Note: Finalized versions are not required to create the Excise Tax Form but are strongly recommended to maintain integrity in annual taxable volume and effective tax rates.

You must also have the appropriate user permissions to access the TTB Reporting dashboard and the system's document storage.

Steps

Creating the Excise Tax Return form:

The system automates the preparation of Form F5000.24 by pulling data directly from your BRO or DRO reports and applying tax rates based on your annual cumulative taxable volume withdrawals.

  1. Navigate to the TTB Excise Tax Return dashboard.

  2. Set the Start and End Date in alignment with the TTB Filing Period that you are filing for.

  3. Create Report

  4. Locate the option to generate the TTB Excise Tax Return PDF.

  5. Once generated, the system automatically calculates the tax due based on cumulative taxable volume withdrawals and the volumes recorded in the current BRO or DRO report you are creating the form from.

  6. Open the generated PDF to review the auto-populated values. If specific adjustments are required, you may edit the fields directly within the document. Note: This may result in a misalignment with system-calculate taxable removals.

  7. The finalized form is automatically saved to the system's document table for record-keeping and future retrieval.

Investigating past Excise Tax Return forms:

  1. Navigate to the Excise Tax History table

  2. Search for the Filing Period dates you want to review

  3. Click on the TTB Report ID to view the underlying BRO or DRO that contributed to the that period's calculation

Correcting past Excise Tax Return forms:

  1. If an error is identified after the form has been generated, simply create and save a new BRO or DRO report for that filing period and tax entity once the underlying transactions or configuration has been corrected.

  2. Note: This will overwrite the previous Excise Tax History values for that period and tax entity and recalculate annual taxable volume and effective tax rate.

Fields And Definitions

TTB Filing Periods and Tax Rates used by Encompass are sourced from the TTB website.

  • TTB Filing Periods

  • TTB Exicse Tax Rates

Best Practices

Always verify that the underlying BRO or DRO reports are accurate before generating the tax return to ensure the most accurate data is used for calculations.

Review the generated PDF thoroughly. While the system automates calculations, the editable nature of the PDF allows you to make necessary manual adjustments to meet specific federal requirements.

16989608:
Distributor troubleshooting for a 403 Forbidden error in Encompass: log back in, clear cache, check expired links, user permissions/roles and VPN or IP restrictions. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Requires an active internet connection.

  • Must have an active user account for the application or system.

  • Must be attempting to access a specific URL, page, or resource within the system that is currently returning the error.

Steps

  1. Verify Authentication Session: Ensure you are fully logged into the system. If your session has timed out, log out completely and log back in to refresh your authentication status.

  2. Refresh the Page and Clear Cache: Perform a hard refresh of your browser or clear your browser's cache and cookies. This resolves potential Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) verification failures or stale security tokens.

  3. Verify URL and Token Expiration: If you are using a shared link, signed URL, or access token, verify that it has not expired. Time-bound tokens will automatically restrict access once their timeframe elapses; request a new link if necessary.

  4. Check User Permissions: Confirm with your system administrator that your user account has the required functional permissions and is assigned to the correct security role or Access Control List (ACL) to view the requested resource.

  5. Review Network and IP Restrictions: Ensure you are accessing the system from an approved network environment. If your organization utilizes a Web Application Firewall (WAF) or IP restriction rules, being off-VPN or on a restricted public network can cause a 403 error.

  6. Contact Support: If the issue persists after completing the above steps, please contact support. To expedite troubleshooting, gather and provide the following specific information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered on the page.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Browser console logs or network trace files (e.g., HAR files), if applicable.

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue (including the specific URL being accessed).

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system, network, or user account before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • 403 Forbidden: An HTTP status code indicating that the server successfully received the request but refuses to authorize it, usually due to lacking appropriate rights.

  • Access Control List (ACL): A configuration list specifying which users or system processes are granted access to particular objects, as well as what operations are allowed on given objects.

  • CSRF Verification: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) tokens are unique, secret, and unpredictable values generated by the server side to protect against unauthorized commands. A failure in this validation prevents access.

  • WAF (Web Application Firewall): A security system that monitors, filters, and blocks HTTP traffic to and from a web application, often enforcing security policies and IP whitelisting.

  • Signed URL / Time-bound Token: A customized URL or temporary digital key providing limited permission and time to make a request, typically used for secure document sharing or API access.

Best Practices

  • Role Auditing: Administrators should regularly audit and update security roles, user permissions, and ACLs to ensure users have the exact access necessary for their operational duties.

  • Token Management: When generating signed URLs or time-bound tokens, clearly communicate the expiration time to the end-user to prevent access confusion.

  • Network Awareness: For systems behind strict firewalls, encourage users to verify their VPN connection or network environment before accessing restricted internal tools.

  • Session Maintenance: Users should avoid keeping idle tabs open for extended periods to prevent stale CSRF tokens and session timeouts.

Configuring Forecast Methods for a Specific Product:

  1. Find the specific product row on the main page.

  2. Click the overflow menu button next to the Forecasted Sales row header to open the product forecast settings dialog.

16989611:
Distributor/API user troubleshooting for a 404 Not Found error in Encompass: check the URL path, moved or renamed resources, case sensitivity, and what to send Support. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Access to the client application, web browser, or API testing tool (e.g., Postman) where the error is occurring.

  • Administrative or developer access to the server environment, file system, or deployment platform (if applicable).

  • Access to server logs, reverse proxy logs, or browser developer tools (Network tab).

  • Knowledge of the expected file paths, API routes, and deployment locations for the requested resources.

Steps

  • Verify the URL and Path: Check the exact API route or resource path requested. Ensure there are no typos, extra spaces, or missing trailing slashes in the URL.

  • Check for Renamed or Deleted Resources: Verify if the target resource (file, page, or API endpoint) has been permanently deleted, moved, or renamed in a recent update.

  • Validate Case Sensitivity: Compare the requested file path against the host operating system's directory structure. Ensure the casing matches exactly, as many operating systems (like Linux) are strictly case-sensitive.

  • Verify Asset Deployment: Check the server-side file location to confirm that the required static assets or files were successfully deployed and are not missing from the expected directory.

  • Review Reverse Proxy Configurations: If a reverse proxy is in use, inspect the path rewrite rules and routing configurations to ensure there is no mismatch between the requested path and the destination path on the internal server.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after completing the steps above, please contact support. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, gather and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (including the full URL returning the 404).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue (e.g., showing the browser's Network tab or API testing tool).

    • Log files (specifically server access logs, error logs, or reverse proxy logs).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system, codebase, or server configuration before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • 404 Not Found: An HTTP standard response code indicating that the client was able to communicate with the server, but the server could not find the requested resource.

  • API Route: The specific URL or endpoint designated for a particular API function or service.

  • Reverse Proxy: A server that sits in front of one or more web servers, intercepting client requests and forwarding them to the appropriate backend server based on configured rules.

  • Path Rewrite Rules: Configurations used by web servers or proxies to automatically modify the URL path of an incoming request before routing it to its final destination.

  • Static Asset: Files (such as images, CSS, HTML, or JavaScript) that are sent to the client exactly as they are stored on the server, without requiring dynamic generation.

  • Host Operating System: The underlying operating system running on the server where the application or website is hosted.

Best Practices

  • Implement Standardized Naming Conventions: Adopt strict, lowercase naming conventions for files and directories to avoid case-sensitivity mismatches across different operating systems.

  • Automate Link and Route Testing: Utilize automated testing pipelines during deployment to verify that all critical API routes and static assets return a 200 OK status before releasing to production.

  • Maintain Change Logs: Keep detailed records of any architectural changes, including renamed endpoints or deleted files, and ensure frontend applications are updated concurrently.

  • Document Proxy Rules: Maintain clear, up-to-date documentation for all reverse proxy configurations and rewrite rules to streamline troubleshooting when routing issues arise.

  • Use Custom 404 Pages: Implement a custom 404 error page to guide end-users back to active areas of your application if they happen to request a broken or outdated link.

16989613:
Developer troubleshooting for an invalid querySelector JavaScript error on a DOM element in Encompass custom front-end code: check selector syntax, null elements, CSS.escape. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Requires access to the application's front-end source code (HTML/JavaScript).

  • Must be using a modern web browser with Developer Tools enabled (e.g., Chrome DevTools, Firefox Developer Tools).

  • Requires basic knowledge of CSS selector syntax and JavaScript DOM manipulation.

Steps

  • Identify the exact error location: Open the browser's Developer Tools, navigate to the Console tab, and locate the exact file and line number throwing the querySelector syntax error.

  • Verify the calling object: Ensure that the object you are calling .querySelector() on is a valid, existing DOM element (or the document object) and is not null or undefined at the time of execution.

  • Validate static selectors: If the selector is hardcoded, verify that it adheres to standard CSS selector syntax (e.g., ensuring IDs start with #, classes with ., and brackets for attributes are properly closed).

  • Log dynamic strings: If the selector is dynamically constructed using variables, insert a console.log() immediately before the querySelector call to output the final, constructed string. Inspect this output for malformed patterns.

  • Escape special characters: If your dynamic selector includes variables that might contain special characters (like spaces, colons, or periods), ensure they are properly escaped using CSS.escape(variable) before appending them to the selector string.

  • If the issue persists, please contact support. Gather and provide the following information for efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered in the browser console.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue, including the console output.

    • A snippet of the relevant JavaScript code and the target HTML DOM structure.

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any recent code deployments or changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • querySelector: A standard JavaScript DOM method that returns the first Element within the document (or parent element) that matches the specified CSS selector string.

  • DOM (Document Object Model): The programming interface for web documents. It represents the page so that programs can change the document structure, style, and content.

  • CSS Selector: A string containing a pattern used to match elements in the DOM (e.g., #my-id, .my-class, [data-active="true"]).

  • CSS.escape(): A built-in JavaScript utility function that escapes a string for use as part of a CSS selector, ensuring that special characters are not misinterpreted by the browser's parsing engine.

Best Practices

  • Use CSS.escape() for dynamic data: Whenever building a query selector using data from an external source (like an API response, user input, or a database ID), always wrap the variable in CSS.escape() to prevent syntax errors caused by unexpected characters.

  • Null checking: Always implement a null check on the parent element before attempting to query inside it (e.g., if (parentElement) { parentElement.querySelector('.child'); }).

  • Keep selectors simple: Avoid overly complex or deeply nested CSS selectors in your JavaScript. Simpler selectors are less prone to string-building errors and execute faster.

  • Test edge cases: When unit testing front-end logic, intentionally pass variables containing special characters, numbers, and spaces to ensure your dynamic query generation handles them gracefully.

16989615:
Why PayLink rejects a Remote Check Capture image (blurry, too dark/light, too small, can't be processed), how to re-capture it without restarting payment, and what Pending Review and Failed mean. v26.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.09

Pre-Conditions

  • Your user role must have permissions to process electronic payment check transactions.

  • Remote Check Capture must be enabled for your system account.

  • A working camera or access to clear image files of the front and back of the check is required.

Steps

Resolving Immediate Scanning Errors

When processing a check payment, scan or upload the check image as prompted.

If the system detects an issue with image clarity or lighting, an error alert will immediately appear displaying the specific reason for rejection.

Follow the on-screen recommendation to re-capture or re-upload a clearer image of the check.

Submit the new image. The system will continue processing the transaction without requiring you to restart the payment workflow or re-enter payment details.

Handling Pending and Failed Check Reviews

If a check image passes initial capture checks but requires additional details verified (such as MICR line or check amount validation), the payment status will be updated to Pending Review.

Allow 1 to 2 business days for the manual review to complete. Do not re-submit the payment during this window to prevent duplicate processing.

If the check fails verification during review, the payment status will update to Failed. Select an alternative payment method to complete the transaction.

Fields And Definitions

Fields And Definitions:*

  • Image Out of Focus / Blurry: The text or numbers on the check are unreadable. Ensure camera lens focus is sharp before capturing.

  • Image Too Dark: The image lacks sufficient lighting. Capture the check in a brighter environment.

  • Image Too Light: Glare or bright reflections prevent text readability. Move away from direct lighting or disable flashlight settings.

  • Image Too Small: The check image does not fill enough of the frame. Position the camera closer to the check.

  • Image Cannot Be Processed: The image orientation or boundary detection failed. Place the check flat on a contrasting background and retry.

  • Pending Review: The check is undergoing manual optical character recognition (OCR) or secondary review. The funds remain unconfirmed until verification completes.

  • Failed: The check could not be verified or was rejected permanently. Another payment method must be selected.

Best Practices

Best Practices:*

Lay the check flat on a dark, non-reflective surface to create strong contrast around the edges of the check.

Ensure all four corners of the check and the bottom MICR numbers are fully visible and free of obstruction or shadows.

Avoid using camera flash, as reflections on shiny check paper can obscure critical banking numbers.

Monitor the payment ledger or status log regularly for checks placed in a Pending Review status to ensure timely follow-up if an alternative payment method becomes required.

Fields And Definitions

  • TableTranslation: A database table or system function responsible for storing and retrieving localized text strings to display in the user interface based on the user's selected language.

  • Language Identifier: A standardized code (such as 'en-US' for US English or 'es-MX' for Mexican Spanish) used by the system to fetch the correct language data.

  • Seed/Initialization Data: Base data that is automatically loaded into a database during the initial setup of an environment (e.g., default language packs and essential configurations).

Best Practices

  • Staging Environment Testing: Test new translation strings and initialization data in a staging environment before deploying them to production to ensure seed data applies correctly.

  • Audit System Changes: Keep a log of any changes made to language identifiers or tenant routing keys to quickly pinpoint misconfigurations when "not found" errors occur.
16989617:
Distributor troubleshooting for emails from Encompass bouncing or blocked by DMARC: check SPF/DKIM alignment, the From domain and DNS records on your domain. Requires v26.01+ and DNS admin access.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must have administrative access to the sender domain's DNS (Domain Name System) settings.

  • Requires access to email server delivery logs or bounced message headers.

  • Must be using an active internet connection to test email sending and run external validation tools.

Steps

  • Review the sender domain's DMARC policy to determine if it is explicitly set to reject or quarantine unaligned mail. If it is, legitimate emails failing alignment will be blocked.

  • Verify your email authentication checks; failures commonly occur when SPF (Sender Policy Framework) or DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail) alignment checks failed.

  • Confirm that the 'From' header domain cryptographically aligns with the signing domain.

  • Investigate the email transit path to ensure that the message body or header was not altered in transit, which breaks the cryptographic DKIM signature.

  • Check your DNS text records for DMARC to ensure they are configured correctly and are not experiencing propagation delays. If you recently updated settings, note that they can take up to 48 hours to update.

  • If the issue persists, please contact support and provide the following:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically original message headers and bounce message logs).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • DMARC: A DNS setting (entirely controlled on the customer's side) that tells the email server what to do with stuff that is not DKIM verified.

  • DKIM (DomainKeys Identified Mail): A security key added to the DNS settings that tells all the other email servers in the world that it is okay for the system to send emails on behalf of that domain.

  • SPF (Sender Policy Framework): An email authentication protocol that allows domain owners to specify which mail servers are authorized to send email on behalf of their domain.

  • Alignment: The process of ensuring that the 'From' header domain cryptographically aligns with the signing domain (DKIM) or the Return-Path domain (SPF).

  • DNS Propagation Delay: The time required for DNS changes to be updated across internet servers worldwide.

Best Practices

  • Monitor Before Enforcing: When initially configuring DMARC, always start with a policy of p=none (monitoring mode) to review reports and ensure valid emails are passing alignment before moving to p=quarantine or p=reject.

  • Avoid In-Transit Modifications: Configure email gateways, anti-virus scanners, or automated signature tools to avoid altering the message body or headers after the email has been DKIM-signed, as this will break the cryptographic signature.

  • Keep DNS Clean: Regularly audit your DNS records to remove obsolete SPF and DKIM entries, ensuring that records remain correctly formatted and do not exceed DNS lookup limits.

16989620:
Distributor admin troubleshooting for System.OutOfMemoryException errors in Encompass, often during large AP closes, exports or file loads: split work into smaller batches, check memory limits. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • System Access: Must have administrative access to the server, application hosting environment (e.g., IIS, Docker containers), or system monitoring tools.

  • Log Access: Requires access to system and application error logs to identify the exact timestamp and context of the exception.

  • Environment Knowledge: Basic understanding of the application's current environment configuration (e.g., container memory limits, worker process architecture).

Steps

  • Monitor Environment Resource Pressure: Check the host server or container environment for overall memory usage. Determine if the application pool or container has a strict memory limit, or if the application is running on a 32-bit worker process which restricts maximum available memory.

  • Identify the Triggering Action: Review the application logs to pinpoint exactly what was happening when the exception occurred. Look for actions such as a large Accounts Payable (AP) close, massive file operations, or complex data exports.

  • Review Large File Operations: If the error occurs during file handling, verify the size of the files being processed. The system may be attempting to load an excessively large file entirely into memory.

  • Analyze Data Aggregation and AP Closes: If the error occurred during an AP close, check if the system was attempting to process a massive batch of shipment lists or production orders at once. Attempt to break the close or the data export into smaller, manageable batches rather than processing the entire dataset simultaneously.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after evaluating the environment and attempting to process smaller data batches, please contact technical support. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, gather and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (including the full stack trace of the System.OutOfMemoryException).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue occurring, if reproducible via the user interface.

    • Log files (Application logs, Windows Event Logs, or container logs covering the time of the error).

    • The exact steps taken by the user that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence patterns.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared (e.g., server updates, configuration changes, or unusual data volume increases).

Fields And Definitions

  • System.OutOfMemoryException: A critical system error indicating that the application has exhausted all available Random Access Memory (RAM) allocated to it and cannot allocate more memory for continuous execution.

  • AP Close: The Accounts Payable period close process. In this context, it often involves executing complex database queries and gathering large lists of shipments and production orders.

  • SQL2Rs Loops: A process where database query result sets are translated and materialized directly into application memory.

  • GROUP_CONCAT: A database function used to concatenate multiple string values from a group into a single, often very large, string.

  • Worker Process: The underlying system process running the application. A 32-bit worker process has a hard memory limit (typically around 2GB to 4GB), regardless of the host server's total physical RAM.

Best Practices

  • Batch Processing: Avoid processing massive datasets or performing extremely large AP closes all at once. Implement workflows that process data in smaller, paginated batches to keep memory consumption stable.

  • Environment Optimization: Ensure your application is running in a 64-bit worker process to utilize the full memory capacity of your host server. Regularly review and optimize container or application pool memory limits.

  • Limit HTML Generation: Be cautious of generating massive HTML outputs (like rendering thousands of error messages or massive data tables on a single page) as string accumulations quickly consume memory.

  • Proactive Monitoring: Implement application performance monitoring (APM) tools to track memory spikes and high concurrency events, allowing administrators to intercept runaway memory consumption before an exception crashes the process.

Distributor troubleshooting for 'EC_Request: Failed to requestNetwork' HTTP client errors in Encompass API calls: check network, URL, CORS/API Origins and tokens. v26.01+; API Edit permission to edit origins.

  • Must be using a supported web browser or making an HTTP request via the Encompass SDK/Client.

Steps

  • Verify Network Connectivity: Check for any general network routing failures or packet loss that might be preventing the connection.

  • Validate the Endpoint URL: Confirm that the target endpoint URL is valid, properly formatted, and currently reachable.

  • Check Browser CORS and Security Policies: If the request is being blocked by browser CORS or security content policy restrictions, verify that the external domain making the request has been explicitly allowed. You must add records to the API Origins table under your Application to allow external JavaScript requests.

  • Verify Authentication Tokens: Ensure the authentication bearer token (or API Token) is included in the request, is properly formed, and has not prematurely expired.

  • Monitor Timeout Limits: Check if the HTTP request is timing out before receiving external headers. You may need to increase timeout allowances or investigate backend latency.

  • Inspect Backend Responses: Confirm that the backend system is returning a valid response and not an unparseable or corrupted payload.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after completing the above steps, please contact support and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue (e.g., browser console errors or network tab details).

    • Log files (specify Load Balancer Logs or application network logs if applicable).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system (e.g., API parameter updates, updated tokens) before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing): A browser security feature that dictates that JavaScript on a page cannot make a request to a different domain unless the receiving domain explicitly allows it.

  • API Origins: A table in Encompass where API builders add records to authorize specific external domains to communicate with their Encompass API Commands.

  • Endpoint URL: The specific web address or destination that the HTTP client is attempting to reach.

  • Bearer Token: A security key or token used in the HTTP headers to authenticate the request and prove the identity of the caller.

Best Practices

  • Test with API Clients: Before embedding HTTP requests in code, test the target endpoint URL and authentication tokens using a dedicated API client (like Postman) to isolate the connection.

  • Manage API Origins: Remember that by default, if no API Origins are created, only requests from the same Encompass domain are allowed to the API Commands. Add necessary domains proactively during setup.

  • Token Lifecycle Management: Implement a process to regularly rotate and refresh authentication tokens to prevent sudden expiration failures in production environments.

Distributor troubleshooting for Encompass runtime errors (TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined) and System.OutOfMemoryException during AP closes or large exports. Requires v26.01+.

  • Requires access to application error logs or the browser console to identify the exact error signature.

  • Must have an active connection to the application environment experiencing the issue.

Steps

  • Identify the Error Signature: Determine if the system is throwing a frontend/runtime error (TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined) or a data/localization error (System.OutOfMemoryException).

  • Troubleshoot TypeError (Frontend/Runtime):

    • Verify that you are not triggering actions before the page data has completely and asynchronously loaded.

    • Check if there have been recent custom schema changes, which could result in mismatched or misspelled field names.

    • Refresh the page to clear any potential race conditions in the asynchronous rendering lifecycles and attempt the action again.

  • Troubleshoot System.OutOfMemoryException (Data/Localization):

    • Identify if you are running a heavy process such as an Accounts Payable (AP) close, generating large shipment lists, or loading extensive production-order lists.

    • If processing a large file or dataset, attempt to break the operation into smaller batches to prevent accumulating big in-memory collections.

    • Check your environment limits, as high concurrency or low container memory (e.g., 32-bit worker pressure) can trigger this exception even on standard operations.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after attempting the above steps, please contact support immediately. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, you MUST gather and provide the following specific information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (e.g., the full stack trace of the TypeError or OutOfMemoryException).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue occurring.

    • Log files (Browser Console logs for frontend issues, or Server/Event logs for memory issues).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared (e.g., schema updates, data imports).

Fields And Definitions

  • TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined: A frontend application error that occurs when the code attempts to access a value that does not exist, often due to API responses returning null unexpectedly, misspelled fields, or data loading delays.

  • System.OutOfMemoryException: A critical system error indicating that the application has exhausted available RAM.

  • AP Close: The Accounts Payable period-end closing process, which often materializes very large query result sets into memory.

  • SQL2Rs loops: An iterative process used to map SQL database results into application recordsets.

  • GROUP_CONCAT: A database function used for string aggregation that can spike memory usage if session lengths are maximized.

Best Practices

  • Batch Processing: Avoid running reports or generating HTML outputs for massive datasets (like comprehensive shipment lists) all at once. Utilize date filters or pagination to reduce the memory footprint.

  • Resource Monitoring: Monitor application pool and container memory limits, especially during peak operational hours or when executing large closes. Ensure your environment is scaled appropriately for your concurrency needs.

  • Wait for Page Loads: To prevent frontend race conditions, ensure the application interface has fully rendered and data has asynchronously loaded before initiating complex commands or data exports.

  • Schema Consistency: When making updates to your data schema, ensure all related application codes and API calls are updated simultaneously to prevent undefined property errors.
16989624:
Troubleshooting steps for "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined" errors in Encompass: hard refresh, log out and in, check report fields, isolate the trigger, what to send Support. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must be accessing the application via a supported, up-to-date web browser (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari).

  • Requires an active and stable internet connection to ensure complete data payloads can be retrieved from backend APIs.

  • Must have appropriate user access permissions to load the specific page, dashboard, or module where the error is occurring.

Steps

  • Perform a Hard Refresh: Clear your browser's cache for the page (Ctrl+F5 on Windows, Cmd+Shift+R on Mac) to ensure you are loading the most recent frontend application code and not relying on stale, cached files.

  • Verify Data State: Log out of the application completely and log back in. This will force a refresh of your user session and securely reload your localized data, which can resolve temporary missing data values.

  • Check for Missing Fields: If this error occurs on a customizable page or report, verify that all requested fields, columns, and array indexes are spelled correctly and currently exist in the active schema.

  • Isolate the Trigger: Slowly replicate the workflow that causes the error. Note whether the error appears immediately upon page load (indicating an asynchronous loading or race condition issue) or after a specific button click or data entry.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after attempting the steps above, please contact our support team. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, explicitly gather and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (including any full red text or stack traces shown on screen).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue occurring.

    • Log files (specifically, export the Console logs and Network HAR files from your browser's Developer Tools).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue (e.g., "Logged in, clicked 'Reports', selected 'June', clicked 'Export'").

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system (e.g., recent software updates, custom field additions, or network changes) before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • TypeError: A runtime error that occurs when an operation is performed on a value of the wrong type.

  • Undefined: A programming state indicating that a variable, object, or data payload does not currently possess a value. The application is trying to read data that does not exist or has not arrived yet.

  • Asynchronous Loading: A process where the application interface continues to render and function while waiting for background data to load.

  • API (Application Programming Interface): The system that allows the frontend interface to request and retrieve the necessary data from the backend server.

  • Race Condition: An anomaly where the system attempts to perform two or more operations at the same time, but the operations must be done in the proper sequence to work correctly (e.g., the screen trying to draw a chart before the API has finished supplying the chart data).

  • Schema: The structured framework or blueprint that defines how data fields are named and organized in the database.

Best Practices

  • Maintain Stable Connectivity: Network interruptions can cause API responses to drop, leading to incomplete data payloads that render as "undefined." Ensure a stable connection when accessing complex dashboards.

  • Regular Cache Clearing: Periodically clear your browser cache and cookies to prevent outdated application scripts from conflicting with newly deployed server updates.

  • Audit Custom Configurations: When renaming fields or adjusting database schemas, audit all linked frontend reports and modules to ensure references are updated to match the new nomenclature, preventing misspelled code parameters.

  • Keep Browsers Updated: Always use the latest version of your web browser to ensure full compatibility with modern JavaScript asynchronous rendering lifecycles.

16989627:
Distributor WMS guide to the scheduled task that pre-builds Directed Replenishment move tasks in Encompass, and why tasks may not build (Dynamic Pick, Pre-Generate Tasks off). Requires v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Pre-Conditions

  • A WMS Replenish Plan must exist for the location, and it must not have Dynamic Pick turned on. Dynamic Pick plans build their own tasks in real time and are never touched by this scheduled task.
    ​
    ​

  • The plan's Pre-Generate Tasks option must be turned on. If it's off, this scheduled task skips the plan entirely, and tasks are only created when a picker presses Begin in Directed Replenishment.
    ​
    ​

  • If the plan uses a Start Time / End Time window, the scheduled task's run time must fall inside that window (checked in the location's own time zone).
    ​
    ​

  • The plan must have at least one WMS Replenish Rule configured, since these rules define which bins are considered low and what they should be replenished to.

Steps

How the AutoCreate_DirectedReplenishmentMoveTasks Scheduled Task Works

This task runs automatically in the background on a schedule (visible in the system scheduler as AutoCreate_DirectedReplenishmentMoveTasks). It doesn't require anyone to be logged in — it pre-builds replenishment work so Move Tasks are already waiting in Directed Replenishment when warehouse staff start their shift.

  1. For every location, it looks at each WMS Replenish Plan and keeps only the plans that have Dynamic Pick turned off, have Pre-Generate Tasks turned on, and are currently inside their Start Time / End Time window (if one is set).
    ​
    ​

  2. For each of those plans, it compares current bin inventory against the plan's WMS Replenish Rules to find products that have fallen below their target — whether that target is Replenish to Order, a target days of inventory, or Replenish to Capacity.
    ​
    ​

  3. It skips any product that already has an active, unexpired Move Task in progress, so it won't create duplicate work for something already queued.
    ​
    ​

  4. For everything left, it calculates how much product needs to move from the backstock (From Bin) to the pick slot (To Bin), respecting the plan's Move Unit (Case, Layer, or Pallet) and the To Bin's remaining capacity so it never asks staff to overfill a bin.
    ​
    ​

  5. It groups the needed moves into pallet-sized batches — splitting a large replenishment need across multiple Move Tasks when it won't fit on one pallet — and orders them using the plan's Sort Method (by To Bin, From Bin, or quantity needed).
    ​
    ​

  6. It creates the resulting WMS Move Tasks (Move Type: Replenish), which then appear in Directed Replenishment ready for staff to pick up — no one needs to press Begin for these to exist.

Fields And Definitions

  • Pre-Generate Tasks - Controls whether this scheduled task is allowed to build Move Tasks for the plan ahead of time. When off, the plan's Move Tasks are only created on demand when a user presses Begin in Directed Replenishment.
    ​
    ​

  • Dynamic Pick - Marks a plan as building Move Tasks in real time as a picker needs them, instead of in a scheduled batch. Plans marked this way are always excluded from this scheduled task.
    ​
    ​

  • Start Time / End Time - The daily window, in the location's local time, during which this scheduled task is allowed to build tasks for the plan. Outside that window, the plan is skipped until the next scheduled run.
    ​
    ​

  • Priority - The order in which plans are processed when several are ready to run at the same time. Lower numbers are processed first.
    ​
    ​

  • Move Unit - Whether product for this plan is moved by Case, Layer, or Pallet.
    ​
    ​

  • Sort Method - Determines the order individual bin moves are queued within a Move Task: by To Bin location, From Bin location, or by quantity needed.

Best Practices

  • Only turn on Pre-Generate Tasks for plans you want pre-built automatically before a shift starts. Leave it off for plans where staff should request tasks one at a time with Begin.
    ​
    ​

  • Set the Start Time / End Time window to line up with when staff actually need tasks ready — for example, ending shortly before a shift starts, so inventory levels used are as current as possible.
    ​
    ​

  • If a location's tasks aren't building overnight as expected, check that the plan isn't marked Dynamic Pick — those plans are always skipped by this scheduled task — and confirm Pre-Generate Tasks is turned on.
    ​
    ​

  • Use Priority to control which plans get processed first when multiple plans are eligible at the same time, especially at busy locations with several replenishment plans.

Distributor troubleshooting for generic fallback error messages and unhandled system exceptions in Encompass: find the triggering action, check outages and config, then send details to support. v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must be using the affected application environment where the fallback message or system issue was observed.

  • Requires an active user session or interaction with the system that triggered the global error handler.

Steps

  • Identify the specific system workflow or action that triggered the generic fallback message.

  • Verify if there is a known critical downstream microservice or resource dependency outage currently impacting the application.

  • Review the system setup for any missing application environment configurations, key vaults, or system secrets that may have been recently altered or omitted.

  • Recognize that the global error handler intentionally suppresses sensitive internal stack details, meaning standard front-end logs may not display the root cause of an unhandled server-side processing error.

  • If the issue persists, please contact support and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (application or server logs, if accessible).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • Generic Fallback Message: A standard, user-facing alert designed to mask a real unhandled system exception for security and stability purposes.

  • Unhandled Server-Side Processing Error: An unexpected disruption or failure that occurs on the backend servers while processing a user request or system function.

  • Microservice / Resource Dependency: A downstream internal system, third-party service, or database that the main application relies on to function correctly.

  • Global Error Handler: A system component that catches unexpected errors and intentionally suppresses sensitive internal stack details from being displayed to the end-user.

  • Key Vaults / System Secrets: Secure storage mechanisms for sensitive application environment configurations required for the system to run.

Best Practices

  • Ensure that all application environment configurations and key vaults are properly documented and verified after any deployment or system update to prevent missing credentials.

  • Proactively monitor downstream microservices and dependencies to quickly identify outages before they trigger fallback messages in the primary application.

  • Because internal stack details are suppressed, ensure that backend logging is robustly configured so that support teams can investigate unhandled exceptions safely behind the scenes.

Distributor guide to the background scheduled task that recalculates On Floor Inventory, PreSales and Pending Sales from bin inventories in Encompass, and why numbers may lag. Requires v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Steps

What the Update_Inventories_OnFloorInventory Scheduled Task Does

  1. Checks whether the system is temporarily busy (an internal safeguard used during heavy load). If active, the task exits immediately and makes no changes.
    ​
    ​

  2. Checks whether a full recalculation has already run in the last few minutes. If so, it exits right away since the numbers are already current.
    ​
    ​

  3. If a recalculation is due, it totals up the Bin Inventories for every product at every location, counting only bin zones that are marked to be included in on-floor totals, to produce an updated On Floor Inventory figure.
    ​
    ​

  4. It also recalculates PreSales (units already committed to open, not-yet-picked orders), Close Dated PreSales, Pending Sales (units on returned but not-yet-verified orders), and Close Dated Inventory for locations using multiple bin inventory.
    ​
    ​

  5. It compares these newly calculated figures against what's currently stored, and updates only the product/location records that have actually changed.
    ​
    ​

  6. Any leftover Pending Sales that no longer have a matching returned order are cleared back to zero.

Fields And Definitions

  • On Floor Inventory - The total physical quantity of a product sitting in bins at a location. This is the raw count before anything reserved for sale is subtracted.
    ​
    ​

  • PreSales - Units already assigned to open orders that haven't finished picking yet. Used together with On Floor Inventory to determine what's truly still available to sell (Available = On Floor Inventory − PreSales).
    ​
    ​

  • Close Dated PreSales - The portion of PreSales that is close-dated (nearing its sell-by date).
    ​
    ​

  • Pending Sales - Units tied to orders that have been returned but not yet verified, held out of available inventory until the return is finalized.
    ​
    ​

  • Close Dated Inventory - Quantity sitting in bin zones designated as Close Dated, tracked separately for locations that use Multiple Bin Inventory.

Best Practices

  • It's normal to see this task listed in the scheduler — it runs automatically in the background and doesn't need anyone to start or monitor it.
    ​
    ​

  • The task limits itself to one full recalculation every few minutes, so seeing it fire frequently doesn't mean extra work is happening each time.
    ​
    ​

  • If On Floor Inventory looks off right after a bin move or receipt, give it a few minutes before assuming something's wrong — most everyday changes are also caught by other real-time updates, and this task is the periodic safety net behind them.
    ​
    ​

  • If numbers still look wrong after the next scheduled run, contact support rather than trying to force a manual correction. See Setting 289 if you want to check whether report/background processing is currently suspended system-wide.

Distributor fix in Encompass for an EDI PER segment rule P0304 syntax error on an Exchange Task: interrogate the X12 file, compare the Exchange Map, fix the data and resend. Needs EDI access; v26.01+.
