Pre-Conditions

  • The trading partner must already have an active EDI connection setup configured within the system.

  • The user must have the appropriate EDI access permissions to view and interact with the Exchange Tasks table.

  • An active Exchange Task must exist in a "Warning" or "Error" status related to an inbound or outbound X12 file.

Steps

  • Navigate to the Exchange Tasks table and filter for tasks that are currently under a status of "Warning" or "Error".

  • Search for the specific Exchange Task that failed and click the magnifying glass icon (View Details) to open the task.

  • Review the memo on the Exchange Task to confirm the specific segment generating the PER Segment Rule P0304 Violation.

  • Click the Interrogate File button to open the file interrogator tool.

  • Using your mouse, hover over the segments within the file to see element-level details and locate where the malformed segment delimiters or incorrect positioning arrays are occurring.

  • Open the designated Exchange Map to compare the element segment in the file to what is expected, identifying if a paired required element is missing from the transaction loop due to upstream sender mapping logic.

  • Make the necessary data corrections in your Encompass system to satisfy the conditional relationship required by the protocol.

  • Manually update the EDI Status on the associated document (e.g., Invoice) to the appropriate resend status (such as "Resend Post-Delivery") and save your changes to re-queue the file for transmission.

  • If the issue persists after attempting to resolve the data format violation, please contact Encompass Support for further assistance. You must gather and provide the following specific information to support for efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically the Exchange Task ID and the associated X12 text file).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • PER Segment Rule P0304 Violation: An EDI X12 protocol rule violation where a required element conditional relationship is not satisfied, meaning one of the paired required elements is missing from the transaction loop.

  • X12 File: A commonly used file type of traded files consisting of a segmented format accompanied with a corresponding map.

  • Exchange Task: A background process that passes through configurations to synchronize data between trading partners, assigned a unique Exchange Task ID.

  • Exchange Map: A developed blueprint mapping out each element of a file as it is to be sequenced.

  • EDI Status: A field which will show the last type of EDI sent on the invoice and can be manually changed to resend EDI files.

Best Practices

  • Regularly monitor the EDI Warnings and Errors widget located in the Exchange Tasks by Type tab, as it serves as your first line of defense in combating EDI-related transaction issues.

  • Always ensure that accurate and consistent data is entered into core system records (such as Customer profiles and AR Accounts) prior to transmitting files, as missing data points are a leading cause of segment composition errors.

  • When troubleshooting mapping or segment issues, actively utilize the Interrogate File tool in conjunction with the Exchange Map to visually confirm where required data points are dropping from the loop.

Explains how MerchSync on Encompass Mobile auto-logs MerchSync Arrived and Departed events when reps enter or leave a customer geofence. Needs location set to Always and v26.02+.

Pre-Conditions

  • Users must be utilizing the Encompass Mobile with version 26.02 or higher.
    ​
    ​

  • The mobile device must have Location Services enabled for the Encompass Mobile app with the permission set to "Always all the time" (Android) or "Always" (iOS).
    ​
    ​

  • Customer locations must have associated Map Polygons (geofences) defined within the system to trigger events. See How to view or edit a customer's geofence for more information.
    ​
    ​

  • User must have an Event for the customer.

Steps

This feature automates the recording of customer visits by tracking when a user enters or leaves a specific customer location. No manual button presses are required for these specific events, provided the device is configured correctly.

1. Open the Encompass Mobile application and ensure you are logged in.
​
2. The application will automatically download relevant customer geofence data (Map Polygons).
​
3. The system performs a location check approximately every 5 minutes.
​
4. When the device location is detected inside a customer's defined Map Polygon, the system automatically creates a **"MerchSync Arrived"** Time Clock Event.
​
5. When the device location is detected outside the Map Polygon after a visit, the system automatically creates a **"MerchSync Departed"** Time Clock Event.
​
6. These events are uploaded to the server automatically. This process continues to function even if the application is minimized or the device screen is locked.

Fields And Definitions

  • MerchSync Arrived: An automated time clock entry recording the timestamp when a user enters a defined customer geofence.
    ​
    ​

  • MerchSync Departed: An automated time clock entry recording the timestamp when a user exits a defined customer geofence, or if a user logs off while a 'MerchSync Arrived' event exists for the same customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Map Polygon: The virtual geographic boundary drawn around a customer location that defines the area for arrival and departure triggers.

Best Practices

  • Location Permissions: It is critical to select "Always Allow" for location permissions. Selecting "While Using the App" may prevent the system from recording arrival/departure times if the phone is in your pocket or the screen is off.

    ​
    ​

Distributor troubleshooting for an 'AccountsRecTrans does not exist' database error in Encompass: check table spelling, schema context, recent deployments and case sensitivity. Needs admin access; v26.01+.

Pre-Conditions

  • Requires database administrator or developer access to review application query logic and schema configurations.

  • Must have access to verify deployment logs and recent migration or hotfix scripts.

  • Requires access to the target operating system or server configuration settings.

Steps

  • Verify Query Spelling: Review the application query logic for any typographical errors in the table name (e.g., ensure it is spelled exactly as AccountsRecTrans).

  • Verify Table Instantiation: Check the current environment to confirm whether the table has been created and properly instantiated.

  • Verify Target Schema: Review the database connection and query context to ensure the correct target database schema or catalog context is selected.

  • Review Recent Deployments: Check if recent migration, hotfix, or deployment scripts were successfully applied to the instance, as missing scripts can cause schema synchronization issues.

  • Check Server Configuration: Verify the case-sensitivity configuration on the target operating system or server to ensure there is no mismatch causing the table name to be unrecognized.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists, please contact support and provide the following information for efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically application, deployment, or system logs from the time of the error).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • AccountsRecTrans: The database table that the system is failing to locate.

  • Schema Out-of-Sync: A condition where the expected database structure does not match the actual database schema in the current environment.

  • Catalog Context: The specific database namespace or target environment that the application query is attempting to access.

  • Migration/Hotfix Scripts: Executable files designed to update the database schema, such as creating new tables or modifying existing ones.

Best Practices

  • Standardize Naming Conventions: Always use exact casing for table names in query logic to prevent case-sensitivity mismatch errors across different server operating systems.

  • Verify Deployments: After applying a hotfix or running migration scripts, perform a routine check of the database schema to ensure all expected tables are instantiated before resuming normal operations.

16989644:
Distributor WMS guide to the scheduled task that auto-runs Apply Pick Rules on upcoming load sheets in Encompass, its setup by location, route type and pick type, and why sheets are skipped. Requires v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Pre-Conditions

  • A record must exist for the Location in the Auto Run Apply Pick Rules setup table, with Run Apply Pick Rule checked. Locations without a record, or with the checkbox off, are skipped entirely.
    ​
    ​

  • The Location must have its Business Days calendar set up, since the task uses business days (not calendar days) to decide which Load Sheet dates to include.
    ​
    ​

  • At least one Route Type and one Customer Pick Type must be linked to the setup record — only Load Sheets matching one of these combinations are picked up automatically.

Steps

Auto Apply Pick Rules (Scheduled Task)

Auto_Run_ApplyPickRules is a background task that runs automatically on your system's scheduler. It doesn't require anyone to click anything — it exists so your warehouse team doesn't have to manually run Apply Pick Rules on every upcoming Load Sheet. Here is what happens each time it runs:
​
​

  1. The task checks the Auto Run Apply Pick Rules setup table for any Location where Run Apply Pick Rule is turned on.
    ​
    ​

  2. For each of those locations, it looks ahead the number of business days set in Days In Advance to find upcoming delivery dates, based on the location's Business Days calendar.
    ​
    ​

  3. It finds all Load Sheets for those dates that have not yet reached Loaded status, and narrows the list to the Route Types and Customer Pick Types configured on that location's setup record.
    ​
    ​

  4. For each matching Load Sheet, the task runs Apply Pick Rules automatically — the same process a warehouse user would run by hand. This assigns the correct pick method (pallet, layer, case, or bottle) to each product on the order and generates the Pick Sheets the warehouse uses to pick it.
    ​
    ​

  5. If a Load Sheet is already being processed — by this task or by a user — it's skipped for that run rather than processed twice.

Fields And Definitions

  • *Location - The location this automatic rule applies to. Each location has its own setup record.
    ​
    ​

  • *Run Apply Pick Rule - Turns the automatic scheduled run on or off for this location. If unchecked, the location is skipped entirely.
    ​
    ​

  • *Days In Advance - How many upcoming business days of Load Sheets the task should look at each time it runs, based on the location's Business Days calendar.
    ​
    ​

  • Route Types - The Route Types whose Load Sheets should be included. Only Load Sheets on a matching route type are processed.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Pick Types - The Customer Pick Types whose orders should be included. Only invoices for customers with a matching pick type are processed.

Best Practices

  • This task only touches Load Sheets that haven't reached Loaded status yet, so it's safe to leave running — it will never re-pick an order that's already loaded.
    ​
    ​

  • If results look incomplete, check the location's Business Days calendar and the Route Types/Customer Pick Types linked on its setup record — Load Sheets that don't match are skipped by design, not by error.
    ​
    ​

  • You can still run Apply Pick Rules manually on a Load Sheet at any time — it won't conflict with this task, since the system locks a Load Sheet while it's being processed so it isn't picked twice at once.

Distributor steps for the Data Hygiene Hub in Encompass: merge duplicate customers or products, fill missing data, and inactivate or delete stale records. Duplicate review needs ReportingIQ paid tier. v26.05+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.05

Pre-Conditions

  • ReportingIQ Add-on: To utilize AI-powered similarity scoring for duplicate detection, the ReportingIQ Paid-Tier add-on must be installed. Without it, the Duplicate Review features will not be available, but other features are still enabled
    ​
    ​

  • Permissions: Users must have the necessary permissions to view the Data Hygiene Hub and edit the respective core tables they are cleaning up.

Steps

1. Navigating the Overview

The Overview tab is your starting point.

  • Use the Core tables menu on the left sidebar to select the data set you want to review (e.g., Customers, Products, Brands, Vendors).
    ​
    ​

  • The dashboard cards will display the current status of the selected table, allowing you to jump directly into the cleanup workflow that matches the issue type: Potential duplicates, Rows with gaps, or Inactive candidates/Unused records.

2. Duplicate Review

This workflow helps you identify overlapping records and merge them cleanly.

  • Navigate to the Duplicate review tab.
    ​
    ​

  • Select a match group from the Duplicate clusters list on the left.
    ​
    ​

  • In the Resolve duplicate records panel, review the flagged records. The system will automatically suggest a recommended master record.
    ​
    ​

  • Choose which record should be kept as the master by selecting the radio button next to its name.
    ​
    ​

  • For any fields with conflicting data (marked with a warning icon), verify the data you want to keep.
    ​
    ​

  • Click Merge into [Master Record Name] on the duplicate records to merge their history, notes, and transactions into the master record.

3. Filling Missing Data (Gaps)

This workflow allows you to fill required and high-value fields from a single grid instead of opening records individually.

  • Navigate to the Missing data tab.
    ​
    ​

  • Review the grid containing records missing critical information. Cells highlighted in yellow indicate missing required data.
    ​
    ​

  • Click directly into the table cells to type, select from dropdowns, or use autocomplete to fill in the missing information.
    ​
    ​

  • Check the boxes on the left side of the rows you have updated (or use the select-all checkbox at the top).
    ​
    ​

  • Click the Save changes button in the top right corner to apply all your edits at once.

4. Cleaning Up Stale and Unused Records

Depending on the table you are viewing, this tab helps you safely remove clutter from your system.

  • Navigate to the Stale records (or Unused records) tab.

    ​

  • For Customers and Products (Stale Records): Select records that have been idle past your configured freshness threshold, then click Inactivate selected records to change their status to inactive without deleting data.
    ​
    ​

  • For Lookup Tables like Brands, Vendors, etc. (Unused Records): Review records with no linked sub-table activity. If the system confirms a record has 0 linked records, you can click the red Delete button to permanently remove it from the system.

Fields And Definitions

  • Similarity status: A panel indicating whether the AI similarity scoring is currently active and running on the selected table's search field.
    ​
    ​

  • Match confidence: A percentage score indicating how confident the AI is that the clustered records are duplicates.
    ​
    ​

  • Fields with differences: A count of how many data fields differ between the records in a duplicate cluster.
    ​
    ​

  • Recommended Master: The specific record within a duplicate cluster that the system flags as the most complete or relevant record to keep during a merge.
    ​
    ​

  • Linked records: Found in the Stale/Unused tab, this number shows how many transactions or sub-table entries are tied to the record, helping you decide if it is safe to delete.

Best Practices

  • Review Before Merging: Similarity scoring can occasionally produce false positives. Always manually review the field differences in a duplicate cluster before committing to a merge.
    ​
    ​

  • Save Frequently: When working in the Missing data grid, save your changes in batches rather than trying to update hundreds of rows at once.
    ​
    ​

  • Check Linked Records: Never delete an unused record without confirming that the Linked records count is 0.
16989646:
Distributor fix for 'Numeric value is not recognized' import errors in Encompass: remove commas, currency symbols and blanks, match decimal format and precision in source data. v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Requires an active data import, parsing sequence, or validation routine where source data is being evaluated against numeric database fields.

  • The user must have access to the raw source data (e.g., CSV, API payload, JSON file) generating the error to review the formatting.

  • Must be using a supported JSON Schema version (if applicable), as very old historical versions drop support for certain validations.

Steps

  • Inspect for Non-Numeric Characters: Open your source data and review the specific fields mapped to numeric columns. Remove any non-numeric characters present in these fields, including commas, currency symbols, and trailing spaces.

  • Verify Locale Decimal Notation: Check for locale decimal mismatch conflicts. Ensure the decimal separator used in your data (e.g., a comma , vs. a dot .) matches the expected regional format of the destination system.

  • Check for Value Overflow: Evaluate the length of the numerical values in the source data. Ensure that the values do not extend beyond the defined column decimal precision limit in the destination schema (e.g., trying to import 5 decimal places into a field strictly configured for 2).

  • Identify and Correct Empty Strings: Look for empty or blank strings within the source data that are being directly cast into a numeric data type. Replace these blank strings with a standard default value (such as 0) or map them to explicitly register as NULL.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after reviewing the data formatting and schema, please contact support. Provide the following information to ensure efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically import error logs or API response payloads).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system or source data format before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • Data Parsing / Validation: The process by which the system reads incoming data strings and verifies they conform to the required data types before committing them to the database.

  • Locale Decimal Mismatch: A formatting error that occurs when a number's decimal structure (using commas vs. dots) contradicts the system's expected regional settings.

  • Value Overflow: A condition that triggers an error when a numerical value contains more characters or decimal places than the database column is configured to accept.

  • JSON Schema: A vocabulary used to annotate and validate JSON documents. The system relies on a default JSON Schema unless explicitly referenced otherwise.

Best Practices

  • Standardize Source Data First: Whenever possible, use formatting tools or scripts to clean your source data before initiating a transfer. Stripping out currency signs and commas proactively will prevent the majority of parsing failures.

  • Manage Blank Fields Intentionally: Avoid relying on the system to interpret blank cells. Standardize your export processes to output a strict 0 or NULL instead of an empty text string when numerical data is missing.

  • Stay Updated on Schema Versions: If your integration explicitly references a specific JSON Schema version, audit it regularly. Extremely old versions lose support over time, which can trigger unexpected validation errors on previously functional workflows.

  • Test with Small Batches: When rolling out a new data integration or adjusting field types, run a test import with a small, highly varied sample of data to immediately highlight precision limits or locale mismatches.
16989647:
Distributor WMS guide to the scheduled task that recalculates bin lot and license plate inventory with FIFO logic in Encompass, and why lot-level quantities may look off. Requires v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Steps

What the Update Bin Lots FIFO Inventory Task Does

This task runs in the background as a scheduled system process. It is not something you run yourself, but you may see it listed in the system scheduler under the name Update_BinLots_FIFO_Inventory. Its job is to keep Bin Lot and License Plate inventory numbers accurate and in sync with the overall inventory in each bin, using FIFO (first in, first out) logic.

Each time it runs, it works through the following steps:

  1. Clears Bin Lot balances for any bin and product where the bin's overall on-hand inventory is already zero, so no leftover lot quantity lingers after everything has been picked or moved out.
    ​
    ​

  2. Clears Bin Lot balances for products that don't track batch codes, code dates, or vintages, since those products don't need lot-level detail.
    ​
    ​

  3. Wherever a bin's lot-level total doesn't match its actual on-hand inventory, recalculates the Bin Lot quantities using FIFO logic. It works back through recent inventory activity and assigns inventory to the oldest purchase receipts first (based on expiration date, then vintage, then receipt order), creating new lot records where needed and zeroing out any lots that no longer apply.
    ​
    ​

  4. After reconciling each bin, updates the bin's reference purchase receipt to point to the oldest remaining lot, so pick lists and other bin-level views reflect the oldest stock on hand.
    ​
    ​

  5. On a full system run, clears any leftover Bin Lot balances in bins where lot tracking has been turned off, and permanently removes Bin Lot records that have sat at zero inventory for more than 7 days (logging them to the deleted records history for auditing).
    ​
    ​

  6. Repeats the same cleanup and FIFO recalculation for License Plates (pallet-level detail within a bin lot) — clearing plates tied to depleted lots, recalculating plate quantities from recent activity, and, on a full run, removing plate records that have reached zero inventory.
    ​
    ​

  7. Finally, fixes any bin inventory records still linked to a purchase receipt with nothing left, redirecting them to a receipt in that bin that still has stock.

Fields And Definitions

  • Bin Lot - The portion of a product's inventory in a bin that belongs to one specific purchase receipt. Bin Lots exist for products that track batch codes, code dates, or vintages, so the system can tell which receipt a given quantity came from.
    ​
    ​

  • License Plate - A further breakdown of a Bin Lot down to an individual pallet or unit, used in bin zones set up to track license plates.
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO (First In, First Out) - The rule this task uses to decide which inventory counts as "used" first: the oldest receipt (by expiration date, then vintage, then receipt order) is depleted before newer ones.
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Inventory - The total on-hand quantity of a product in a bin, without the lot- or plate-level breakdown. This is the number Bin Lots and License Plates are reconciled against.

Best Practices

  • You don't need to run this task yourself. It's a background scheduled process that keeps Bin Lot and License Plate inventory accurate over time, even if something didn't reconcile immediately after a move, pick, or count.
    ​
    ​

  • If lot- or plate-level inventory looks off, this task will typically correct it automatically the next time it runs — there's usually no need to fix it manually.
    ​
    ​

  • Products that don't track batch codes, code dates, or vintages won't show Bin Lot detail. That's expected, since lots exist specifically to support that kind of tracking.
    ​
    ​

  • If lot- or plate-level numbers still look wrong after this task has run, check the product's batch code/code date/vintage tracking settings and the bin zone's lot and license plate tracking settings, since those control what this task reconciles.

Distributor troubleshooting for STR_TO_DATE() database errors in Encompass imports or reports: check for blank values, mismatched date format masks, invalid dates and mixed regional formats. v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Database Access: Requires active credentials and appropriate permissions to view and query the affected database or data warehouse.

  • Source Data Access: Requires the ability to view the raw source data (e.g., CSV files, external integration payloads, or staging tables) before it is processed by the SQL function.

  • Format Knowledge: Must know the exact SQL format mask (e.g., '%Y-%m-%d', '%m/%d/%Y') that the STR_TO_DATE() function is configured to expect.

Steps

  • Check for Null or Empty Values: Inspect the raw source data for null or empty strings being passed to the function; these must be validated before processing.

  • Verify the Format Mask: Ensure that the input string format in the data exactly matches the provided SQL format mask utilized by the function.

  • Validate Calendar Dates: Review the raw source data to identify and correct invalid calendar date values (e.g., Month 13, Day 32).

  • Standardize Locales: Analyze the raw source data to determine if there are mixed locale or regional date formats present. If found, standardize all date strings to a single uniform format before attempting the conversion.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after validating the source data and format masks, contact support. Please gather and provide the following information for efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically query execution logs or import error logs, if applicable).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system (or source data formats) before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • STR_TO_DATE(): A database function used to convert a string (text) representation of a date and/or time into an actual Date or DateTime data type based on a specific format.

  • Format Mask: A defined string of formatting characters (like %Y for a four-digit year or %m for a two-digit month) that instructs the database on how to interpret the incoming text string.

  • Null: A special marker used in databases to indicate that a data value does not exist in the database. It is distinct from a zero or an empty space.

  • Locale/Regional Date Format: The specific way dates are written based on geographic region (e.g., MM/DD/YYYY in the United States vs. DD/MM/YYYY in Europe).

Best Practices

  • Pre-Validation: Always implement data validation rules to catch empty strings, nulls, and malformed text before the data reaches the STR_TO_DATE() function.

  • Use Safe Conversion Functions: Where possible, utilize functions like TRY_CAST or TRY_TO_DATE (depending on your specific database system) which will return a NULL value instead of causing the entire query or import to fail when an invalid date is encountered.

  • Standardize at the Source: Enforce a strict, single date format (preferably ISO 8601, such as YYYY-MM-DD) across all APIs, file imports, and manual entry points to prevent mixed regional formats from corrupting the data pipeline.
16989650:
Distributor guide to the background scheduled task that cleans up expired report results, old drafts and versions, and archives report run history in Encompass. Requires v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Steps

What the Delete_ReportHistories Scheduled Task Does

Delete_ReportHistories is an automatic background maintenance task built into Encompass. It runs on a regular schedule to keep the reporting system fast by clearing out old, unused, or expired reporting data. If you see it listed on the Scheduled Tasks screen, that's expected — no action is needed on your part.

Each time it runs, it performs the following cleanup steps, in order:

  1. Clears expired report results - Temporary result sets kept so a report can display quickly are removed once they expire.
    ​
    ​

  2. Removes unused draft reports - Draft reports that haven't been updated or run in 30 or more days, and that no longer have a valid parent report, are deleted.
    ​
    ​

  3. Cleans up old report versions - Older versions of a report are removed once they are 30 or more days old and no longer referenced by any other report. Duplicate active versions of the same report are also cleaned up so each report keeps one active version.
    ​
    ​

  4. Archives report run history - Detailed records of when reports were run are summarized into monthly totals once they are over a month old, moved to long-term history, and cleared from the active log.
    ​
    ​

  5. Removes orphaned scorecard goals - Report Goals tied to a report version that no longer exists are deleted.

Best Practices

  • No action needed - This task runs automatically; you never need to start it, stop it, or configure it.
    ​
    ​

  • Your active reports are safe - Only expired caches, abandoned drafts (30+ days untouched), and unused old report versions are affected. Reports you're actively using are never touched.
    ​
    ​

  • Seeing it in Scheduled Tasks is normal - If you notice Delete_ReportHistories running in the system scheduler, that's routine maintenance, not an error.
16989651:
Distributor fix for 'SQL execution cancelled' or timeout errors when running Encompass reports, queries or API calls: check the connection, narrow date ranges and filters, split large reports. v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Requires an active and stable internet connection.

  • Must be attempting to run a database query, execute a report, or trigger an API call within the system.

  • Must be logged in with permissions to view the report or execute the target query.

Steps

  • Verify Network Stability: Confirm your internet connection is stable. A network connection dropped mid-query execution can cause the database call to cancel.

  • Check for Manual Cancellations: Ensure that the pending request was not explicitly canceled by the user or an integrated application mid-execution.

  • Evaluate Query Size and Complexity: If the command execution timeout limit is reached before the query is completed, attempt to reduce the date range or apply stricter filters to the report or query.

  • Monitor System Resources: Check for any known system latency or server resource pressure (CPU/Memory) that might be forcing query aborts.

  • Review Gateway Connections: If using an upstream API or external integration, verify that an upstream gateway timeout has not cascaded to cause a database call cancellation.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after attempting the steps above, please contact support. For efficient troubleshooting, you must gather and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (including Load Balancer Logs or API Processing Times, if applicable).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • SQL Execution Cancelled / Timeout: An exception indicating that a Structured Query Language (SQL) command failed to execute completely because it exceeded allowed time limits, lost network connection, or was manually aborted.

  • Command Execution Timeout Limit: A system-defined maximum allowed processing time for a single query or API request before it is forcefully stopped to preserve server health.

  • Upstream Gateway Timeout: An error that occurs when a server acting as a gateway or proxy does not receive a timely response from an upstream server, cascading down to cancel the original database request.

Best Practices

  • Apply Default Filters: Always configure and utilize default filters on reports to prevent massive, unfiltered executions that cause timeouts.

  • Filter Early on Date Ranges: Apply date range filters as early as possible in your query to significantly limit the volume of data being processed.

  • Break Down Large Reports: Split complex reports into smaller, focused reports or dashboard tabs to improve processing time and reduce the likelihood of server resource pressure.

  • Optimize Joins (Join Required = False): When building custom reports, use this setting where appropriate so the engine can implement automatic join-pruning, only pulling data when explicitly needed.

  • Limit Row Returns: Configure reports to return only the necessary number of rows. Exceptionally large result sets increase processing time and the risk of a dropped connection.

16989655:
Distributor troubleshooting for SQL deadlock errors in Encompass: check for concurrent updates, overlapping close or sync jobs, long-running transactions and missing indexes. Needs admin access; v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must have administrative or database management access to the system.

  • Requires active database monitoring tools or access to system error logs to view transaction statuses.

  • Must be currently experiencing database timeouts or SQL deadlock error messages during operations.

Steps

  • Check for Concurrent Operations: Review active system processes to determine if multiple transactions are attempting to update the same database rows simultaneously in a different order.

  • Review Job Scheduling: Look at the schedule for heavy close or synchronization jobs. Identify if high batch concurrency is occurring due to these jobs running at the same time.

  • Identify Long-Running Transactions: Query the active database processes to find any long-running transactions that might be holding database locks for too long.

  • Audit Database Indexes: Check the database schema for missing indexes that could be causing wide, inefficient lock scans across tables instead of targeted row locks.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after reviewing the above steps, please contact technical support. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, you must gather and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically database error logs and transaction logs).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • SQL Deadlock: A situation where two or more competing database actions are waiting for each other to finish, resulting in concurrent transactions attempting to update the same rows in a different order.

  • Concurrency: The execution of multiple system operations or database transactions at the same time. High batch concurrency can occur during heavy close or synchronization jobs.

  • Database Locks: Mechanisms used by the database to prevent data corruption by restricting access to a row or table while a transaction is occurring.

  • Lock Scans: The process of a database searching for available records to lock; inefficient lock scans across tables can occur if indexes are missing.

Best Practices

  • Optimize Job Schedules: Space out heavy close or synchronization jobs to run during off-peak hours to minimize high batch concurrency.

  • Maintain Database Indexes: Regularly audit and rebuild database indexes to prevent missing indexes from causing wide, inefficient lock scans.

  • Optimize Queries: Ensure that custom reports and data imports are optimized so they do not result in long-running transactions holding database locks for extended periods.

  • Standardize Update Logic: When writing custom API scripts or integrations, ensure that transactions update tables and rows in a consistent, standardized order to prevent cross-locking.
16989656:
Distributor FAQ on the paid Real Time Data Warehouse sync add-on in Encompass: setup, Snowflake Share, which tables stay on scheduled sync, failures, delays and cost. Enabled by Encompass Support. v26.03+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.03

Pre-Conditions

  • Real Time Data Warehouse sync is a paid add-on. It must be purchased before it can be enabled.
    ​
    ​

  • Enabling it requires the Enable RealTime Snowflake Sync setting, which is restricted to Encompass Support. Your Encompass team turns this on for you — it is not a customer-side toggle.
    ​
    ​

  • To query the Data Warehouse from your own Snowflake account, install the Snowflake Share application from the App Library and enter your Snowflake Account Locator. This requires the Global Setting Edit permission.

Steps

What do I need to do to set this up?

Very little. Encompass enables the Enable RealTime Snowflake Sync setting for your system once the add-on is purchased. There is no downtime, no re-seed, and no change to how you use Encompass — the same tables and columns you query today simply update sooner. If you also want to query the warehouse directly from your own Snowflake account, install the Snowflake Share application from the App Library and enter your Snowflake Account Locator. Encompass provisions the share automatically and emails you the SQL to run in a Snowflake worksheet to attach it (creating a warehouse, then creating a database from the share).

Which changes are not synchronized in real time?

These continue on the normal scheduled frequency rather than streaming:

  • Field Audit and Deleted Records history tables.

  • Encrypted fields, which use database-level encryption the Data Warehouse cannot evaluate.

  • System logging tables and cross-customer shared configuration tables.

  • A small set of high-volume transactional tables with specialized sync optimizations, including Invoice Trans and Bin Trans.

  • Changes made by specialized background routines that write to the database outside the standard record-save path.

Does the scheduled sync stop running once real-time is enabled?

No, and that is intentional. The scheduled sync keeps running underneath as a reconciliation pass: it compares each table's most recent change against the last successful sync, so anything the real-time path missed is picked up on the next run. Real-time is a fast path layered on top of the scheduled sync, not a replacement for it. This is what keeps the warehouse correct even if an individual streamed update fails.

What happens if a real-time update fails?

Each update is retried up to five times with an increasing delay between attempts. If it still fails, Encompass Support is notified automatically and the change is corrected by the next scheduled reconciliation pass. Under an unusually heavy burst of changes, updates queue rather than fail; if the queue stays saturated the oldest updates fall back to the scheduled sync, again with a notification to Support.

Is the real-time data identical to the operational database?

With one exception. Very large free-text values — long notes, comments, and stored documents' text bodies — are shortened in the real-time update, and the full value lands on the next scheduled sync of that table. Everything else is written in full. Reporting on these very large text columns should use the scheduled sync rather than expecting real-time completeness.

Are updates guaranteed to arrive in order?

Within a single table, yes — changes to the same record are applied in the order they happened. Across different tables, updates are processed independently, so a report joining two tables during a burst of activity may briefly see one table a moment ahead of the other. Both settle within seconds.

Is the cost one-time or recurring?

Recurring. It is an ongoing addition to your Encompass subscription, quoted as a percentage of your current total subscription fees, so it scales with the size of your system. Contact your account manager for a quote.

Are there other costs beyond the Encompass add-on?

If you query the Data Warehouse from your own Snowflake account through a share, you are responsible for your own Snowflake compute and storage charges for that account. Encompass does not bill or control those. Real-time sync does not change your Snowflake costs — it changes when data arrives, not how much you query. It also removes most of the need for the Manual Data Warehouse Sync action, which carries a per-second processing fee, so many systems see that usage drop to nearly zero.

Best Practices

  • Do not build a process that assumes a change is in the warehouse the instant it is saved. Real-time is typically a few seconds and occasionally 10–30 seconds, so any automation reading back its own write should tolerate a short delay.
    ​
    ​

  • If you were routinely using Manual Data Warehouse Sync to force fresh data before running a report, revisit that habit after enabling real-time. It is usually no longer needed, and it carries a per-second fee.

Distributor/IT troubleshooting for cascading errors (400, 403, 404, 429, 5xx) across Encompass integrations: check gateway routing, config drift, authentication and database load. Needs admin access; v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must have administrative access to the API gateway and routing configurations.

  • Requires access to multi-region environment settings and deployment logs.

  • Must have monitoring visibility into authentication services, database performance, and cache layers.

Steps

  • Verify Gateway Routing: Check the gateway routing rules to ensure they are fully synchronized with the application layer API definitions.

  • Inspect Configuration Consistency: Review multi-region environments for configuration drift, particularly if a release cycle was recently completed.

  • Check Authentication Stability: Investigate the authentication service for any instability that might be causing cascaded request rejections.

  • Analyze Performance Metrics: Review the database and cache layer performance for degradation that could be triggering aggressive retries and cascading topology crashes.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists, contact support immediately. Please gather and provide the following specific information for efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (e.g., 400, 403, 404, 429, 5xx).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue or monitoring dashboards.

    • Log files (specifically gateway routing logs, authentication logs, and database/cache performance logs).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared (e.g., recent release cycles or configuration changes).

Fields And Definitions

  • Cascading Errors: A sequence of failures where an error in one system or service triggers subsequent errors in dependent systems (e.g., HTTP 400, 403, 404, 429, and 5xx codes).

  • Configuration Drift: The phenomenon where environment configurations gradually become out of sync across multi-region environments over time or following release cycles.

  • Topology Crash: A broad architectural failure caused by cascading request rejections, aggressive retries, or systemic performance degradation.

  • Gateway Routing Rules: Configurations that dictate how incoming API traffic is directed to the appropriate backend application services.

Best Practices

  • Standardize Release Cycles: Implement automated configuration management checks after release cycles to prevent multi-region configuration drift.

  • Optimize Retry Logic: Implement exponential backoff strategies for system retries to prevent overwhelming the database or cache layers during temporary performance dips.

  • Audit API Definitions: Regularly synchronize gateway routing rules to ensure they align perfectly with active application layer API definitions.

  • Proactive Alerting: Set up early-warning alerts for authentication service instability to prevent request rejections from cascading through the architecture.

Distributor/API user troubleshooting for a 429 Too Many Requests error in Encompass integrations: check burst traffic, retry backoff and overlapping scheduled jobs. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Must be using an application, integration, or automated script that makes HTTP requests to an API endpoint.

  • Must be authenticated via a unique user, IP address, or API access key.

  • Must have encountered a "429 Too Many Requests" HTTP status code.

Steps

  • Verify the exact nature of the traffic to determine if sudden burst traffic is exceeding throttle thresholds.

  • Check your client application's error-handling logic to ensure it is not initiating a retry storm without proper exponential backoff.

  • Review your system's scheduled tasks to confirm that multiple automation jobs are not hitting the same endpoint within an identical window.

  • Audit your overall request volume to determine if the rate limit has been exceeded per your unique user, IP address, or API access key.

  • If the issue persists after reviewing your traffic and retry logic, please contact support. You must gather and provide the following specific information for efficient troubleshooting:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered.

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically API or network request logs).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • 429 Too Many Requests: An HTTP Client Error status indicating that the requester has sent too many requests in a given amount of time.

  • API Access Key: A unique token used to identify and authorize a client; rate limits are often applied against this key.

  • Throttle Thresholds: The maximum allowable limits for sudden burst traffic before requests are rejected by the server.

  • Retry Storm: A rapid succession of repeated requests initiated by clients that fail to use proper delay mechanisms after an initial error.

  • Exponential Backoff: A standard error-handling strategy where a client increases the delay time between consecutive retry attempts.

Best Practices

  • Implement proper exponential backoff algorithms in all custom clients or integrations to prevent retry storms.

  • Stagger the execution times of scheduled automation jobs so they do not concurrently hit the same endpoint within an identical time window.

  • Monitor your API integrations for sudden burst traffic to ensure you remain below the designated throttle thresholds.

  • Distribute heavy workloads across different time periods to avoid exceeding rate limits tied to your unique user, IP address, or API access key.

16989662:
Distributor guide to how OrderIQ in Encompass uses recent store inventory counts for Intermittent products to decide suggested orders, with the threshold formula and an example. Requires v26.03+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.03

Pre-Conditions

  • Inventory data must be actively recorded and synchronized with the system's Customer History.
    ​
    ​

  • OrderIQ must be active for the customer account.

Steps

OrderIQ automatically detects and processes store inventory values to improve predictive ordering accuracy. Manual configuration or opting into inventory tracking is no longer required, as the system seamlessly evaluates the latest inventory data to optimize order recommendations:

  1. Product Classification: Verify that your product is set to the "Intermittent" Sales Type in the Customer Product Combinations table. (See definitions below for how this is classified).
    ​
    ​

  2. Automated Inventory Ingestion: You don't need to change your workflow. The system automatically reads the most recent inventory entry recorded in the customer's history (such as counts logged via your Encompass Mobile app) for any given product.
    ​
    - Active Sync    : If valid, recent inventory data is found during the active synchronization cycle, OrderIQ will ingest that data and immediately factor it into the predictive ordering model.
    ​
    ​- Bypass Protocol: If the inventory data is empty or older than the current synchronization cycle, the system will automatically bypass the inventory ingestion for that specific product and customer, preventing outdated data from affecting order predictions.
    ​
    ​

  3. Invoice Maintenance: Simply continue processing your sales through Invoices. The system automatically pulls this sales data to calculate the "Weekly Consumption."
    ​
    ​

  4. Review Recommendations: When generating your Suggested Order report, OrderIQ evaluates the data. For Intermittent items with valid cycle data, it will suggest a reorder if the Estimated Current Inventory falls below your Inventory Threshold.

Fields And Definitions

Understanding these terms will help you see how the system makes decisions within the database:

  • Intermittent Sales Type:

    • Definition: A sales pattern characterized by irregular demand or infrequent purchase cycles (slower-moving products).

    • How it is Classified: On the Customer Product Combinations table, OrderIQ's AI automatically assigns this classification by analyzing your historical sales data. It evaluates the Sales Interval Weeks and the Sales Threshold. If a product does not sell on a highly predictable weekly schedule, the AI flags it as "Intermittent" and triggers the specialized, inventory-based formula.

  • Active Synchronization Cycle:

    • Definition: The current timeframe in which OrderIQ scans for recent inventory updates. Only inventory data recorded within this active cycle is factored into the daily predictive ordering model to ensure data freshness.

  • Inventory Threshold:

    • Definition: Your safety stock level. When estimated inventory hits or drops below this line, a reorder is triggered.

    • Calculation: It is automatically calculated based on the last 6 months of ingested inventory data, specifically looking at the count recorded immediately before a new shipment arrived.

  • Weekly Consumption:

    • Definition: The average volume of the product sold or consumed per week, derived automatically from historical Invoice data.

  • Recommendation Formula:

    • The Logic: (Most Recent Count from active sync cycle) + (Orders since that count) - (Weekly Consumption × Weeks since that count) ≤ Inventory Threshold.

    • If this condition is met, the product appears on your suggested order.

Best Practices

OrderIQ in Action

Let's look at how OrderIQ makes a calculation behind the scenes for a slow-moving item, such as a "Premium Craft Stout."

The System Data (Automatically Calculated):

  • Inventory Threshold: 5 cases (OrderIQ knows this store needs to reorder when stock hits 5 cases to avoid running out).

  • Weekly Consumption: 2 cases/week (Based on historical invoice data).

The Real-World Activity:

  • A sales rep visited the store and logged an inventory count of 12 cases via Encompass Mobile 2 weeks ago.

  • There have been 0 new deliveries (Orders) of this product since that count.

OrderIQ's Automated Calculation Today:

  1. Expected Depletion: 2 cases/week × 2 weeks = 4 cases consumed since the last count.

  2. Estimated Current Inventory: 12 (Recent Count) + 0 (Orders) - 4 (Expected Depletion) = 8 cases remaining.

  3. The Decision: OrderIQ compares the 8 remaining cases against the Inventory Threshold of 5. Since 8 is greater than 5, the system will NOT suggest a reorder this week, preventing overstocking.

Fast forward to next week: If no new inventory is counted and no deliveries are made, the expected depletion will be 6 cases (2 cases × 3 weeks). The new estimated inventory drops to 6 cases. If they sell slightly more than average and the estimated stock hits 5 or below, OrderIQ will automatically add the item to the Suggested Order report!

To ensure OrderIQ’s predictive models adapt accurately to your business, keep the following in mind:

  • Frequent & Accurate Counts: Ensure store inventory counts are recorded accurately and on a frequent schedule. Consistent tracking provides the predictive models with highly relevant information, leading to higher order accuracy and a significant reduction in returned items.
16989663:
Distributor troubleshooting for a 503 Service Unavailable error in Encompass: check maintenance windows, wait out traffic spikes, and what details to send Support. Requires v26.02+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.02

Pre-Conditions

  • Requires an active internet connection to test endpoint connectivity.

  • Requires administrative access to server infrastructure, load balancers, or application monitoring tools (e.g., AWS CloudWatch, Datadog, New Relic).

  • Requires visibility into the organization's deployment schedule and maintenance windows.

Steps

  • Check for Scheduled Maintenance: Verify if the target service is currently undergoing a planned restart, deployment, or routine maintenance. Check your internal communication channels or status page. If maintenance is ongoing, wait until the window closes and try the request again.

  • Monitor for Temporary Overload: Wait a few minutes and refresh the application. 503 errors are often temporary responses to brief traffic spikes.

  • Review Compute Instance Resources: Access your server monitoring dashboard to check for instance overload. Look specifically for CPU utilization nearing 100%, memory exhaustion (OOM errors), or exhausted database connection limits.

  • Verify Downstream Dependencies: Check the status of required downstream systems (e.g., databases, third-party APIs, or microservices). If a downstream service is experiencing an outage, it may be triggering an automated circuit breaker on your primary application, resulting in a 503 error.

  • Inspect Load Balancer Health Checks: Review your load balancer logs. Confirm whether application health checks are consistently failing. If they are failing, the load balancer may be removing instances from the available pool, leaving no servers available to process incoming requests.

  • Contact Support: If you have completed the above steps and the issue persists, please contact support. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, gather and provide the following specific information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (including full HTTP response headers if available).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue as it occurs in the user interface.

    • Log files (specifically load balancer logs, application error logs, and server access logs).

    • The exact steps taken by the customer that led to the issue.

    • The exact date, time, and timezone the issue was first observed, and details on any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system, network configurations, or code deployments immediately before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • 503 Service Unavailable: An HTTP status code indicating that the server is currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overloading or maintenance of the server.

  • Compute Instance Overload: A condition where a server runs out of critical processing resources (CPU, Memory, or Network Connections), rendering it incapable of accepting new tasks.

  • Circuit Breaker: An automated safety mechanism that halts requests to a downstream dependency that is known to be failing, preventing system-wide cascading failures.

  • Health Check: An automated process (often performed by a Load Balancer) that regularly pings a server to verify it is responsive and functioning correctly.

  • Load Balancer: A device or service that acts as a reverse proxy, distributing network or application traffic across a number of servers to increase capacity and reliability.

Best Practices

  • Implement Auto-Scaling: Configure auto-scaling rules based on CPU and memory utilization to dynamically add compute instances during high traffic periods, preventing resource exhaustion.

  • Optimize Health Checks: Ensure your load balancer health checks are robust and actually verify the application's ability to serve traffic, rather than just pinging the server's IP address.

  • Graceful Degradation: Design your application to handle downstream dependency outages gracefully (e.g., serving cached data) rather than dropping the connection with a 503 error.

  • Proactive Alerting: Set up proactive monitoring alerts for high CPU utilization, memory thresholds, and failed health checks so your team can intervene before a 503 outage occurs.

  • Communicate Maintenance: Always broadcast planned downtime to users well in advance and use custom, user-friendly maintenance pages instead of default browser 503 error screens.

16989667:
Distributor troubleshooting for a 504 Gateway Timeout error in Encompass, often from heavy reports or exports: retry, cancel long-running queries, check proxy timeouts. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Requires an active internet connection.

  • Requires administrative access to your network routing, load balancer, or reverse proxy settings (if self-hosting or managing your own network infrastructure).

  • Access to application, database, and proxy log files.

Steps

  • Retry the Request: Wait a few moments and refresh the page or retry the API call. Transient network degradation or temporary spikes in downstream API latency often resolve themselves quickly.

  • Review Active Database Queries: Check for long-running SQL executions or database lock waits. If a massive report or complex data export is tying up the database, cancel the operation to free up the thread pool.

  • Check Timeout Thresholds: Inspect the configurations on your intermediate proxy layers (e.g., Nginx, Apache, load balancers, or Cloudflare). Ensure that the timeout thresholds are not configured too low for operations that are expected to take a longer time to process.

  • Monitor Server Resources: Evaluate your application servers for thread pool saturation, thread starvation, or request queueing backlogs. Consider scaling up resources or restarting the application service to clear overloaded queues.

  • Contact Support: If the issue persists after attempting the above steps, please contact support immediately. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, please gather and provide the following information:

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered (including the URL or API endpoint returning the 504 error).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue.

    • Log files (specifically reverse proxy logs, application error logs, and slow query database logs).

    • The exact steps taken by the user that led to the issue (e.g., "I clicked 'Generate Report' on the Sales dashboard").

    • The date and time the issue was first observed, your local time zone, and any patterns of recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system, network architecture, or application code before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • 504 Gateway Timeout: An HTTP status code indicating that a server acting as a gateway or reverse proxy did not receive a timely response from an upstream server it needed to access to complete the request.

  • Reverse Proxy: A server that sits in front of web servers and forwards client requests to those backend servers.

  • Upstream Server: The backend server (like an application or database server) that the proxy is attempting to communicate with.

  • SQL Execution Block / Lock Wait: A scenario where a database query is stalled because the data it needs to read or write is currently locked by another active transaction.

  • Thread Pool Saturation: A condition where all available threads allocated to process incoming requests are currently in use, forcing new requests to wait in a queue or time out.

  • Downstream API Latency: Delays caused by third-party services or external systems that your application relies on to formulate a response.

Best Practices

  • Optimize Heavy Queries: Ensure database tables are properly indexed and optimize heavy SQL queries so they execute efficiently without causing lock waits.

  • Asynchronous Processing: Move long-running tasks (like heavy report generation or massive data imports) to background processing queues rather than tying up HTTP request threads.

  • Tune Proxy Configurations: Align the timeout settings of your intermediate proxy layers with the actual time required for your most complex application tasks to complete.

  • Implement Monitoring: Set up automated monitoring and alerting for thread pool usage, API latency, and database query times so you can identify and resolve saturation before it results in 504 errors.
16989668:
Distributor guide to the scheduled task that keeps each login's Switch Site list, email and user type in sync across Encompass sites, and why a site may be missing. Requires v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Steps

What the Update_AuthenticationsSitesDisplay Scheduled Task Does

This is a background maintenance task, not something you run yourself. It keeps a login's Switch Site list accurate and up to date for a site. Encompass runs it automatically on a recurring schedule, which is why you may see it listed in the system scheduler. Each time it runs, it performs four checks:

  1. Adds missing site links - Finds active users on this site whose login doesn't yet have a record linking it to this site, and creates one. This is what makes a site appear in a user's Switch Site list after they're granted access. It also removes links for logins that no longer have any active user on this site.
    ​
    ​

  2. Refreshes which sites are visible - Recalculates whether each linked site should actually be shown in the Switch Site list, based on whether the user is still active and still holds a permission that grants visibility. A site a user has lost access to drops out of the list without deleting the underlying record.
    ​
    ​

  3. Syncs the login email to user records - If someone's login email address changes, this copies the new email onto their linked user records on the company's other connected sites, so the email stays consistent everywhere.
    ​
    ​

  4. Syncs user type across sites - Updates the user type stored against each site link to match the user's current, most-privileged user type, keeping site-switching behavior consistent with the user's actual role.

Best Practices

  • No action needed - This task runs automatically. You don't need to run it manually or configure anything for it to work.
    ​
    ​

  • Switch Site list looks out of date? - It will correct itself the next time this task runs.

Distributor steps to make Encompass auto-run pick rules every 30 minutes per warehouse so bin allocations and replenishment tasks update early. Needs WMS (MultipleBinInventory) and v26.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.06

Pre-Conditions

Access to Warehouse Management System (WMS) table configurations is required. This is controlled by Locations.MultipleBinInventory = True.

Steps

Automatically running pick rules updates the pick-pending bin allocations on invoice transactions throughout the day. This ensures that directed replenishment can generate warehouse tasks earlier and with greater accuracy.

To configure automated pick rule processing:

  1. Navigate to the Auto Run Apply Pick Rules table.
    ​
    ​

  2. Select or add a record for the desired warehouse Location.
    ​
    ​

  3. Set the Auto Run Apply Pick Rule setting to True to enable automation.
    ​
    ​

  4. Enter the look-ahead window (in number of days) in the Load Sheet Days in Advance field.
    ​
    ​

  5. To limit the automation to specific deliveries, navigate to the associated subtables and add restricted Route Types or Customer Pick Types. If left empty, all routes and pick types for the location will be processed.
    ​
    ​

  6. Save the configuration. The system will automatically execute the pick rules every 30 minutes for eligible load sheets.

Fields And Definitions

  • Location: The warehouse site where the automated pick rule process will execute.
    ​
    ​

  • Auto Run Apply Pick Rules: A table that activates (True) or suspends (False) the automated 30-minute background job for the selected location.
    ​
    ​

  • Load Sheet Days in Advance: The number of days forward from the current date that the system will search for load sheets to process. For example, a value of 2 will process load sheets scheduled up to two days ahead.
    ​
    ​

  • Route Types: An optional subtable selection used to limit the automation to specific delivery routes. Leaving this empty applies the rule to all routes.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Pick Types: An optional subtable selection used to limit the automation to specific customer classifications. Leaving this empty applies the rule to all customer pick types.

Best Practices

  • Optimize Data Volume: Set the Load Sheet Days in Advance lookup window to the minimum required period (such as 1 or 2 days) to prevent processing excessive amounts of future data and to protect system performance.
    ​
    ​

  • Leverage Specific Restrictors: Utilize the Route Type and Customer Pick Type subtables to target only the segments of your business that actively benefit from automated replenishment visibility.
16989676:
Explains the CleanCacheTags scheduled task distributors see in Encompass: routine background cleanup of expired cache entries that needs no action and doesn't touch business data. v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Steps

CleanCacheTags Scheduled Task

  1. Encompass stores frequently accessed data in a temporary, high-speed cache to keep the system fast. Cached items are grouped into tags so related entries can be found and cleared together later (for example, when the underlying data changes).
    ​
    ​

  2. Every cached item has an expiration time. When an item expires, it is removed automatically, but the reference to it inside its tag group can be left behind.
    ​
    ​

  3. The CleanCacheTags task scans these tag groups on a regular schedule and removes references to items that have already expired.
    ​
    ​

  4. If a tag group ends up empty after cleanup, the task removes the group entirely.
    ​
    ​

  5. This keeps the caching system running efficiently and prevents it from using more memory than necessary over time.
    ​
    ​

  6. This task runs automatically in the background. It requires no input from you and does not change, delete, or affect any of your business data — it only manages temporary, internal system cache files.

Best Practices

  • No action is needed when you see CleanCacheTags running in the scheduler — this is expected, routine system maintenance.
    ​
    ​

  • Leave this task enabled. Disabling it can cause the system's cache to grow larger than necessary over time, which may slow performance.

16989678:
Distributor steps when Encompass Mobile deposit slips print with split totals: check split invoices, AR Account Maps, Mapped Locations and the load sheet route location. Needs admin access. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • System: Encompass Mobile.

  • Permissions: Administrative access to Financial Settings, AR Account Maps, and Company Records.

  • Configuration: Multiple company records or Mapped Locations exist within the site environment.

  • Scenario: Invoices are being processed through Load Sheets where "Split Invoicing" or specific AR Account Mapping is active.

Steps

  • Identify the Invoice Type: Determine if the invoices on the deposit slip are standard or if they utilize the Split Invoice functionality.

  • Verify AR Account Mapping: Navigate to the AR Account Maps settings. Check if the invoices in question are hitting an AR Account tied to a specific Mapped Location.

  • Check Load Sheet Route Location: If the invoice is NOT a split invoice, verify the Route.Location associated with the Load Sheet. The system will default to this location ID for grouping.

  • Analyze the Logic Trigger: Review the data based on the following logic flow:

    • If Invoice.SplitInvoice is empty: The system groups by the Load Sheet's Route Location.

    • If Invoice.SplitInvoice is NOT null: The system groups by the Mapped Location ID found in the invoice's ARAccount.ARMap.

  • Reconcile Company Records: Ensure that the desired "Expected Behavior" (combined totals) aligns with your AR mapping. If multiple company records exist, the system will naturally split the deposits if they map to different locations.

  • Contact Support: If the grouping logic remains inconsistent with your business requirements after verifying the mappings above, contact Encompass Support. Please provide the following information:

    • Exact Issue: Discrepancy between actual and expected grouping on Deposit Slips.

    • Examples: Specific Invoice numbers and Load Sheet IDs involved.

    • Evidence: Clear screenshots of the Deposit Slip showing the split totals.

    • System Details: The name of the site environment and the date/time the behavior was first observed.

    • Configuration Changes: Any recent changes to Company Records, AR Account Maps, or Mapped Locations.

Fields And Definitions

  • ARAccount.ARMap: The specific mapping configuration that determines which ledger account and location an Accounts Receivable entry is directed to.

  • Invoice.SplitInvoice: A field indicating whether a single transaction has been divided into multiple invoice records, often triggering specialized routing logic.

  • Mapped Location: A defined entity in Encompass used to segregate financial data and physical inventory, which directly influences how deposits are categorized.

  • Route.Location: The primary location associated with a specific delivery route and its corresponding load sheets.

  • LoadSheet.Location: The physical or logical site where a load sheet is generated and settled.

Best Practices

  • Consistency in Mapping: To maintain a single combined total on deposit slips, ensure that all relevant AR Accounts point to the same Mapped Location where possible.

  • Single Company Record: If your business structure allows, utilizing a single company record simplifies deposit grouping by tying all AR accounts to a single entity.
16989679:
Distributor steps to make OrderIQ suggested orders round up to full cases with the Force_to_Case setting, even for products not set to Sell By Case Only. Needs Suggested Order Configuration access and v25.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.10

Pre-Conditions

Users must have the necessary permissions to access and modify the Suggested Order Configuration or Suggested Order Overrides settings.

Steps

This configuration provides greater control over how the OrderIQ system suggests order quantities. It allows you to enforce case-unit rounding for automated order suggestions, even for products that are not flagged as "Sell By Case Only". This is useful when you want to encourage full-case orders through automated suggestions while still allowing sales representatives the flexibility to manually sell individual units when required.

To use this setting:

  1. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configuration or Suggested Order Overrides table.

  2. Locate or add a new configuration rule for the desired scope (e.g., a specific product, product type, or customer).

  3. Set the Force_to_Case parameter to "True" for that rule.

  4. When this parameter is enabled, any order quantities predicted by the OrderIQ algorithm for the products matching that rule will be automatically rounded up to the nearest whole case unit.

Fields And Definitions

Force_to_Case: A parameter that dictates the rounding behavior for suggested order quantities.

  • True: Forces the system to round all suggested quantities up to the nearest whole case. This overrides the product's individual "Sell By Case Only" setting for automated suggestions.
    ​
    ​

  • False (or blank): The system will use the default rounding logic, which is typically based on the product's "Sell By Case Only" setting.

Best Practices

  • Apply this setting at the product type level (e.g., for all wine and spirits) to standardize automated ordering for entire categories while maintaining sales flexibility.
    ​
    ​

  • Use this setting on a customer-specific basis for accounts that have a preference or requirement for receiving shipments in full-case quantities.

  • This provides a way to align automated suggestions with warehouse picking and shipping efficiencies without restricting the sales team from accommodating special requests for individual units.

16989681:
Explains the Delete_FieldAuditRecords scheduled task in Encompass and why old field change history disappears per Audit Retention Days, plus how distributors can keep custom field history longer. v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Steps

Delete_FieldAuditRecords Scheduled Task

  1. Whenever a tracked field's value changes anywhere in Encompass, the system logs the change in a hidden change-history log called FieldAudit — this keeps the previous value, the new value, who made the change, and when it happened.
    ​
    ​

  2. Each field has its own Audit Retention Days setting that controls how long that history needs to be kept.
    ​
    ​

  3. The Delete_FieldAuditRecords scheduled task runs automatically in the background. It checks the FieldAudit entries for every field and permanently deletes any entries older than that field's Audit Retention Days setting.
    ​
    ​

  4. This task never touches your live records — it only removes old change-history entries that have aged past their retention window.
    ​
    ​

  5. Because it's a system-scheduled task rather than something you run yourself, seeing Delete_FieldAuditRecords in the scheduler is expected and normal. No action is required on your part.

Fields And Definitions

  • Audit Retention Days - The number of days Encompass keeps a field's change history before Delete_FieldAuditRecords deletes it. Set per field on the Table Editor's Advanced Field Settings (0–365 days). This can only be changed for custom fields you've added; standard system fields use a fixed retention set by Encompass.

Best Practices

  • If a field's older change history seems to be missing, check its Audit Retention Days setting in Table Editor before assuming something went wrong — it may simply have aged out.
    ​
    ​

  • For custom fields where you need a longer change history (e.g., for compliance or troubleshooting), raise Audit Retention Days up to the 365-day maximum.
    ​
    ​

  • You don't need to disable or reschedule Delete_FieldAuditRecords — it's designed to run continuously in the background to keep the audit trail from growing indefinitely.

1. From the App Library, configure the Minimum Case Threshold by setting the value in Application Setting 3411.
