2. The system automatically monitors Merchandising Events and compares them against delivery volumes on the same day.
​
3. If a Customer has a scheduled normal delivery for a day, the system sums the total number of cases across all invoices for that Customer.
​
4. If the total number of cases for the day is less than the value specified in Application Setting 3411, the system automatically deletes the associated Merchandising Event.
​
5. This process runs as a background task every 15 minutes between 3:00 AM and 11:00 PM local time to ensure adjustments are made based on the latest load status.

Fields And Definitions

  • Min cases to cancel merchandiser events (Setting 3411): The threshold value used to determine if a delivery is considered "small." If the total case count for a day falls below this number, merchandising events will be eligible for automatic deletion.
    ​
    ​

  • Scheduled Delivery Event: An invoice recorded on a LoadSheet where the status is 'Loaded', the LS Type is 'Scheduled', and the invoice is not an 'Off Day Delivery'
    ​
    ​

  • Merchandising Event: An activity where 'IsMerchandiserAssigned' = True
16989683:
Distributor guide to OrderIQ suggested order settings in Encompass: order_size, round_threshold, product overrides, POS data, layer rounding, loss function and Partition ID. Needs the OrderIQ app and v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Pre-Conditions

Before configuring OrderIQ, ensure the following are in place to allow for certain features:

  • Install OrderIQ App: OrderIQ App is installed and suggested order configurations are enabled and configured for accounts

  • Retail Insights Data Connection: For leveraging POS data, a connection to Retail Insights must be active. This ensures the Handoff Product Inventory Daily Trace table is populating with data.

  • Inventory Layer Thresholds: To enable rounding to the next layer or pallet, the promptLayerThreshold must be set up for relevant products in the Inventory table.

Steps

OrderIQ is a solution that provides tailored product suggestions to users. It has several configuration parameters that allow for granular control over how these suggestions are generated. These parameters help optimize inventory and streamline the ordering process.

Granular Order Size Control

The order_size parameter allows users to control the size of a suggested order.

How it Works

  • It uses a percentage list (e.g., 0.5;0.4) to distribute a predicted weekly order across multiple delivery stops.

  • The default value is 1, which corresponds to a 100% order.

  • If you set order_size to 1.2 (120%), OrderIQ will recommend an order that is 120% of a standard order.

How to Configure

  1. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configuration dashboard.

  2. Update the order_size parameter.

  3. The value can be a percentage list or a single decimal.

  4. If the number of delivery stops is less than the number of percentages listed, the remaining percentages are summed and applied to the last delivery stop.

Adjustable Rounding Thresholds

The round_threshold parameter dictates how predicted quantities are rounded up or down.

How it Works

  • It is a decimal value between 0 and 1.

  • A higher round_threshold increases the confidence required to add the next incremental case, which is useful if you have a high product removal rate.

  • A lower round_threshold makes it easier to add the next incremental case, which is helpful if you have a high product addition rate.

  • For products designated as 'Sell By Case Only,' predicted quantities are converted to cases, rounded using the specific threshold, and then converted back to units for precise suggestions.

How to Configure

  1. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configuration dashboard.

  2. Update the round_threshold with a decimal value between 0 and 1.

  3. This setting ensures that suggestions align with your desired ordering patterns.

Product Type-Specific Customizations

You can apply unique order_size and round_threshold settings for specific products or product types.

How it Works

  • Specific settings for a product, product type or product type code take precedence over the general configurations.

  • For products designated as 'Sell By Case Only,' predicted quantities are converted to cases, rounded using the specific threshold, and then converted back to units for precise suggestions.

How to Configure

  1. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configurations table.

  2. Select the sub-table Suggested Order Overrides.

  3. Click Add Suggested Order Overrides.

  4. Add a product type, product, or product type code.

  5. Update the order_size or round_threshold parameters for the selected items.

  6. Click Add Record.

POS Data Integration

Integrating Point-of-Sale (POS) data can significantly boost the precision and reliability of order suggestions.

How it Works

  • By including historical POS sales and inventory metrics, the system can deliver more accurate forecasts.

  • This feature is controlled by the EnablePOSData parameter in the Suggested Order Configuration table.

  • The available options are:

    • False: Excludes all POS data.

    • Include POS Sales: Incorporates only retail sales data into the model.

    • Include POS Sales & Inventory: Includes both retail sales and inventory data. Note that this requires accurate inventory data.

How to Configure

  1. Ensure a Retail Insights Data connection is active and the Handoff Product Inventory Daily Trace table is populated.

  2. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configuration table.

  3. Update the Enable POS Data column to one of the three options.

Operational Packing Units

This feature automatically rounds suggested order quantities to the nearest full layer or pallet.

How it Works

  • It leverages existing system configurations for product packing and inventory thresholds.

  • The feature uses the inventory.promptLayerThreshold to determine when to round a suggested value to the next layer.

  • When a product's recommended order is greater than or equal to its prompt order layer threshold, OrderIQ will round the quantity up to the next layer. This ensures that recommended orders align with operational packing requirements.

How to Configure

  1. Go to the Inventory table and set up the prompt layer threshold for the products you wish to round.

  2. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configurations table.

  3. Set Enable Layer Round to True for OrderIQ accounts.

Fields And Definitions

  • order_size - A percentage value or a list of percentages that controls how predicted orders are scaled and distributed across multiple deliveries. A value of 1.2 suggests 120% of a standard order.
    ​
    ​

  • round_threshold - A decimal between 0 and 1 that sets the confidence level for rounding predicted quantities. A higher value reduces the chance of rounding up to the next case, while a lower value increases the likelihood to add the next case.
    ​
    ​

  • Partition ID - This setting determines how many models OrderIQ trains by grouping customer data.
    ​
    ​

  • Loss Function - The mathematical method used by the AI model to calculate prediction errors.

    • Squared Error (Default) - A general-purpose loss function that treats all errors equally. This is what OrderIQ uses unless the Loss Function is changed in the OrderIQ app settings.
      ​
      ​

    • Tweedie Loss - A specialized loss function designed for data with many zero values and occasional large spikes, common in beer distribution. Set the Loss Function to reg:tweedie to use it.
      ​
      ​

  • EnablePOSData - A configuration setting that dictates whether to include POS data in the OrderIQ model.

    • False - Excludes POS data.
      ​
      ​

    • Include POS Sales - Integrates only retail sales data.
      ​
      ​

    • Include POS Sales & Inventory - Includes both sales and inventory data.
      ​
      ​

  • Enable Layer Round - A boolean (True/False) setting that, when enabled, automatically rounds suggested quantities to the nearest full layer or pallet based on the promptLayerThreshold.

Best Practices

  • Start with Defaults: Begin with the default settings and observe performance before making extensive changes. This provides a baseline for evaluating the impact of your customizations.
    ​
    ​

  • Use Tweedie Loss for Specific Patterns: If your business has many products with zero sales on most days and occasional large orders (e.g., craft beers), switch the Loss Function to reg:tweedie. This will lead to more accurate suggestions.
    ​
    ​

  • Tailor with Specificity: Use the Suggested Order Overrides sub-table on Suggested Order Configurations to apply custom order_size and round_threshold settings for high-velocity or unique product types. This granular control prevents irrelevant recommendations and optimizes inventory for key products. Do not use Suggested Order Limitations for this: it is the legacy Retail Insights path and is ignored entirely for accounts with AI Suggested Order set to True.
    ​
    ​

  • Leverage POS Data: If available, enable Include POS Sales to improve prediction accuracy. If you have reliable and accurate inventory data, consider enabling Include POS Sales & Inventory for even greater precision.
    ​
    ​

  • Optimize for Operations: For products that are handled in specific packing units (layers, pallets), enable Enable Layer Round to ensure order suggestions align with operational requirements, reducing the need for manual adjustments. This makes the ordering process more efficient.
    ​
    ​

  • Best Practices for PartitionID Selection: Choosing the right Partition ID is a crucial step in optimizing your OrderIQ models. The best choice depends on the nature of your customer data. Here's a concise guide to help you decide:

    • CustomerID: Choose this for high-volume, consistent accounts where you need maximum personalization. This option trains a unique model for each customer. It's highly accurate for customers with rich historical data but performs poorly for new or low-volume accounts due to data scarcity.
      ​
      ​

    • CustomerTypeID: Use this for low-volume or low-velocity accounts with sparse data. By training a single model for each customer type (e.g., bars, restaurants), it pools data from similar customers. This improves the model's ability to learn general sales trends and prevents it from overfitting to limited data. However, it may overlook individual customer nuances and relies heavily on accurate customer categorization.
      ​
      ​

    • ChainID: Select this when ordering patterns are standardized across a chain. It trains a single model for all locations within a chain, providing consistent suggestions. This is particularly useful for new locations that can benefit from the collective data of the entire chain. A drawback is that it may ignore unique local variations and demands.
16989684:
Explains how the Scheduled Reports task sends Encompass reports by email, text or eChat on a set frequency, and what to check when a distributor's scheduled report stops arriving. v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Pre-Conditions

  • The report must be saved and assigned to a Report Category with a Frequency set (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly).
    ​
    ​

  • At least one Report User must be added to the schedule with a Delivery Method selected.
    ​
    ​

  • The report, the report's owner, and every recipient's user account must all be Active.

Steps

What the Scheduled Reports task does

  1. This runs automatically in the background as a system scheduled task — it is not something you run yourself, and it is normal to see it in the system scheduler.
    ​
    ​

  2. It checks every Report Category in your system that has a schedule set up, to see if any are due to send based on the Frequency, day, and Send Time configured.
    ​
    ​

  3. It checks the due time against each recipient's own time zone, so everyone receives their report at the correct local time.
    ​
    ​

  4. For every schedule that is due, it creates a secure link to the report.
    ​
    ​

  5. It delivers that link to each recipient using their configured Delivery Method: Email, Text Message, or eChat.
    ​
    ​

  6. It marks each recipient as sent for that period, so the same report is not delivered more than once per scheduled day.
    ​
    ​

  7. It skips any schedule where the report, the report's owner, or the recipient is Inactive, so reports are never sent to or on behalf of inactive users.

Fields And Definitions

  • *Frequency - How often the schedule runs: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly.
    ​
    ​

  • Day of Week / Day of Month / Day of Quarter - The specific day the report is due, based on the Frequency selected. Setting Day of Month to the 32nd schedules it for the last day of every month.
    ​
    ​

  • *Send Time - The time of day, in each recipient's own time zone, the report should go out.
    ​
    ​

  • *Delivery Method - How the report link is delivered to each recipient: Email, Text Message, or eChat.
    ​
    ​

  • Require Recipient to Log On - When enabled, recipients must log on to Encompass to view the report. When disabled, the report opens directly from the link.
    ​
    ​

  • Use Report Owner's Permissions - When enabled, the recipient views the report using the report owner's permissions instead of their own.
    ​
    ​

  • Expiration Days - How many days the report link stays valid before it expires.
    ​
    ​

  • Message Body - The custom message sent alongside the report link in the email, text, or eChat message.

Best Practices

  • You can view and manage your own report schedules from the Scheduled Reports screen.
    ​
    ​

  • If you no longer want a scheduled report, remove yourself from that schedule's Report User list rather than deactivating your account.
    ​
    ​

  • If a scheduled report stops arriving, check that the report, its owner, and your own user account are still Active — this task will not deliver to or on behalf of inactive users.

16989693:
Explains the daily Delete Old Records task in Encompass: why old records, field audit history and expired items get purged per retention settings, and why long runtimes are normal. v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Steps

What the Delete Old Records Scheduled Task Does

Delete Old Records is an automatic background maintenance task that runs once a day. You may notice it listed on the Scheduled Tasks screen, but it does not require any action from you - it keeps the system clean and running efficiently by removing data that is no longer needed. Each run performs the following:

  1. Purges records from any table that has a retention period configured, removing rows older than that table's Delete Records After Days setting.
    ​
    ​

  2. Trims the Field Audit Trail (the change history kept for individual fields) down to each field's Audit Retention Days setting, so history doesn't build up indefinitely.
    ​
    ​

  3. Removes expired system items that are no longer needed, including expired QuickLinks, expired Documents, and old entries in the internal log used to track recently deleted records.
    ​
    ​

  4. Cleans up leftover internal tables (temporary and old backup tables) that Encompass creates during upgrades and reporting, once they are no longer needed.
    ​
    ​

  5. Removes any custom scheduled tasks that reference an API command that no longer exists.
    ​
    ​

  6. Runs the same kind of cleanup inside specific Encompass modules, purging outdated operational data unique to each - for example, completed Load Sheets and pallet records in WMS, old EDI exchange files, unused DSDLink shopping cart records, and stale chat messages or mobile device logs in CRM.
    ​
    ​

  7. Performs routine database table maintenance (optimizing and analyzing tables) to help keep the system responsive.

Fields And Definitions

  • Delete Records After Days - Found on the Tables table. Sets how many days a table's records are kept, based on each record's Time Updated date, before Delete Old Records removes them. Leave this blank to keep a table's records indefinitely.
    ​
    ​

  • Audit Retention Days - Found on the TableFields table. Sets how many days a field's change history is kept in the Field Audit Trail before it is purged. Defaults to 30 days when not set.

Best Practices

  • This task runs automatically once a day - seeing it in the Scheduled Tasks list is expected and does not mean anything is wrong.
    ​
    ​

  • On databases with a lot of data, Delete Old Records can take a while to complete. A long runtime by itself is not a failure.
    ​
    ​

  • This scheduled task is non-critical, failures can happen when data builds up, but the task will catch up on the next run.

16989696:
Distributor steps when Avg Weekly Depletion looks wrong in Encompass Inventory Projections: compare Canned vs Fusion report math and use the Use Business Days filter for a 5-day week. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • System Access: Must have permissions to access the Report Library and Operations Reports.

  • Product Data: Must have active sales/invoice transaction history for the items being projected.

  • Calendar Configuration: Business days must be defined in the system settings if attempting to use business-day-specific calculations.

Steps

  1. Identify the Report Type: Determine if you are using the Canned Inventory Projections report or the Fusion version. The Canned report uses a fixed 7-day calculation, whereas the Fusion version allows for logic adjustments.

  2. Verify the Calculation Logic:

    • Canned Report: This report calculates the daily average by dividing total sales by the total calendar days in the period (e.g., 7 days). It then multiplies that daily average by 7 to reach the weekly depletion.

    • Fusion Report (Use Business Days = No): This mimics the Canned report logic ($Total Sales div Total Days$).

    • Fusion Report (Use Business Days = Yes): This "squeezes" the sales into a shorter work week by removing weekends from the divisor.

  3. Cross-Reference with Invoice Transaction Report: * Run the Invoice Trans Report for the same date range and Product ID.

    • Manually calculate the daily average: $ ext{Total Units} div ext{Total Days in Period}$.

    • Compare this to the "Avg Daily Depletion" shown in your Projection report to see which logic is currently being applied.

  4. Adjust Filters for a 5-Day Selling Week: If your weekly totals appear overstated because they include non-selling days (weekends), switch to the Fusion Inventory Projections report and set the filter Use Business Days = Yes.

    • Note: This will increase the Daily average but will align the Weekly average to a 5-day work week (Daily Avg $ imes$ 5).

  5. Contact Support: If the values in the Fusion report still do not align with your manual calculations from the Invoice Transaction Report, or if you require the Canned report to be modified for your environment, contact support.

When contacting support, please provide the following:

  • Exact Error/Discrepancy: Specify the Product ID and the "Expected" vs. "Actual" values.

  • Report Filters: Provide a screenshot of all filters used (Date Range, Period, Use Business Days, etc.).

  • Supporting Data: An export of the Invoice Trans Report for the same period.

  • Comparison Math: The exact steps and logic you used to arrive at your expected value.

  • Timestamp: The date and time the discrepancy was first observed.

Fields And Definitions

  • Avg Daily Depletion: The calculated average number of units sold per day over a specific period.

  • Avg Weekly Depletion: The projected number of units sold per week; calculated as (Avg Daily Depletion $ imes$ Days in Selling Week).

  • Canned Report: A standard, out-of-the-box report with hard-coded logic that typically follows a 7-day calendar week.

  • Fusion Report: A customizable report engine that allows for advanced filtering, such as excluding non-business days.

  • Use Business Days: A filter toggle that determines whether the report divisor includes weekends/holidays or only "selling days."

Best Practices

  • Use Fusion for Flexibility: Leverage the Fusion version of reports when your business logic deviates from standard 7-day calendar weeks.

  • Standardize Dashboard Reports: If you update your reporting logic, ensure the new Fusion reports are updated across all shared Dashboards to maintain "one version of the truth" for all end users.

  • Audit Business Calendars: Periodically verify that your system business calendar correctly identifies non-selling days to ensure "Use Business Days" filters function accurately.

Distributor steps for co-op buying group pricing: set Buying Group on a Zone, map customers, link quantity-restricted promotions, and run Recalculate Co-Op Pricing. Needs Invoice Edit permission, System Setting 85, v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Pre-Conditions

  • Users must have the "Invoice Edit" permission to manually run or trigger pricing recalculations.

  • System Setting 85 ("Use Backorder in Promotion min Num Units calculation for Quantity Restricted Promotions") must be configured to dictate whether backorders contribute to the group's qualifying quantity totals.

Steps

  • Configure the Buying Group Zone: Navigate to the Zones table. Locate or create the zone that represents your cooperative buying group, and set the Buying Group field to True.

  • Assign Customers: Map all participating customers to the designated buying group zone. Customers should be assigned using the customer-zone mapping tables.

  • Link Promotions: Attach the desired quantity-restricted promotions to the configured buying group zone. While a single promotion can be linked to multiple zones, quantities are aggregated individually for each specific zone.

  • Process Daily Transactions: Create daily customer invoices. Only unlocked, active daily invoices with a status up to "Return" are eligible for collective aggregation.

  • Recalculate Group Pricing: The system runs a daily automated task ("Recalculate Co-Op Pricing") to sum product quantities across all active transactions in the buying group (the net of both positive and negative transactions). This calculation can also be run manually by authorized users at any point.

Fields And Definitions

  • Buying Group: A setting in the Zones table. When enabled, it groups all customers assigned to that zone and aggregates their transaction quantities to qualify for shared, volume-based promotional pricing.

  • Promo Overridden (CoOp): A transaction flag indicating that a collective group promotion has been applied and locked to prevent recalculation from subsequent changes in quantity.

Best Practices

  • Verify Customer Mapping: Ensure customer-to-zone mappings are completed via the dedicated customer-zone mapping tables rather than relying solely on the main Customer Profile zone field.

  • Understand Net Return Dynamics: Keep in mind that negative invoice transactions are included in the daily volume. Daily product returns will reduce the group's aggregate total volume.

Distributor guide to how Encompass auto-assigns Google Place IDs to sale customers nightly via the Geocoding Assign PlaceIDs task, and why a customer may be skipped. Needs Google Maps geocoding, v26.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.06

Pre-Conditions

Ensure the following system setup requirements are met before utilizing this automated mapping utility:

  • The Google Maps and Geocoding integrations must be active and configured within the system settings.

  • Customer records must be designated with the account type of Sale.

  • The linked distribution location must be actively synced with DSDLink (the export status is verified as active and not set to Manual).

Steps

The system automatically retrieves location coordinates and assigns unique mapping identifiers (Google Place ID) during nightly scheduled task, 'Geocoding Assign PlaceIDs'.

When executed, the system evaluates all eligible sales customers, formats their full matching address (comprising Company Name, Street Address, City, State, and Postal Code), safely retrieves the unique identifier (PlaceID) from Google, and updates the customer's place ID.

The following criteria must be in place in order for a customer's place ID to be updated

  1. Customers.GPSAccuracy = Not Set

  2. Customers.PlaceID is blank

  3. Customers.CustomerAccountType = Sale

Fields And Definitions

Place ID: A unique, persistent identifier assigned by Google Maps to a physical location. This value matches local records with global customer databases (such as CRM networks) and reduces redundant, costly external calls.

GPS Accuracy: A value representing the precision of coordinates. A status of Not Set indicates the customer location is eligible for automated geocoding.

Report Company Address: A dynamic field that automatically concatenates the Customer Name, Street Address, City, State, and Postal Code. This composite string is sent to the mapping service to ensure highly accurate location matches.

Best Practices

Ensure Address Data Quality: Keep your customer directory accurate. Always populate complete and precise street addresses, city names, states, and postal codes. Incomplete or misspelled addresses might prevent the geocoding engine from resolving the correct coordinates and unique identifiers.

Distributor setup in Encompass to stop out of stock rules from splitting or backfilling combo promotions, using System Settings 3453 and 3454 so only complete sets ship. Requires v26.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.06

Pre-Conditions

Combo Promotion Setup

Steps


​The system includes specialized logic to ensure that "Combo" type promotions remain intact during Out of Stock (OOS) processing. By default, the system will prevent partial shipments of bundled items when inventory is insufficient. To manage this behavior, follow these steps:

1. Navigate to the System Settings.

2. Locate the setting "Prevent out of stock rules from splitting combo type promotions when cutting product" (ID: 3453). Enable this setting to force the system to adjust all components of a combo promotion to match the maximum number of complete sets available.

3. Locate the setting "Prevent Out of Stock Rules from Backfilling products (does not apply to combo type promotions)" (ID: 3454). Enable this to prevent the system from automatically adding back individual items to a combo if they become available after a previous cut, which helps maintain the integrity of the original bundled offer.

4. Once these settings are configured, the Out of Stock rules will automatically calculate the maximum number of complete combo sets possible based on current inventory for all products within the bundle. The system will then adjust all line item quantities accordingly to match those complete sets.

Setting Interaction Matrix

3453 (Prevent Split)

3454 (Prevent Backfill)

Cut Behavior

Backfill Behavior

OFF

OFF

Normal cut, may break combo

Normal backfill, may break combo

ON

OFF

Post-process adjusts all combo products to complete sets

Normal backfill, may break combo

OFF

Normal cut, may break combo

Combo Backfill blocked

ON

Post-process adjusts all combo products to complete sets

Combo Backfill blocked

Fields And Definitions

  • Combo Promotion: A bundled set of products sold together that requires specific quantities of each item to be considered a complete unit.

  • Cut (Out of Stock): The process where the system reduces the quantity of a product on an order because the inventory is unavailable for shipment.

  • Backfill: The process where the system automatically updates a previously "cut" order line with available inventory.

  • Setting 3453 (Prevent Split): When active, the system prevents the fragmentation of combo bundles. If one item in a bundle is unavailable, the entire bundle is adjusted down to the nearest whole, complete set.

  • Setting 3454 (Prevent Backfill): When active, the system disables automatic backfilling for items within a combo promotion, ensuring that the bundle does not become "partial" due to staggered inventory availability.

Best Practices

  • Maintain Bundle Integrity: Keep both Setting 3453 and 3454 enabled to ensure that customers always receive complete promotional bundles, which reduces manual customer service intervention and potential disputes over partial shipments.

  • Review Periodically: If your business model changes to allow partial fulfillment of combos, you may toggle these settings; however, note that disabling them may result in split combos on customer invoices.

  • Monitor Backorders: When these settings are enabled, be aware that items removed from a combo due to insufficient inventory will be moved to backorder. Use the backorder report to track when enough stock has arrived to fulfill the entire bundle.

16989709:
Distributor steps to include backorders and backfills in Encompass sales forecasts by setting Exclude Backorder to False, so forecasts reflect true demand after stockouts. Requires v26.04+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.04

Pre-Conditions

  • To include historical backorders and backfills in your current forecasting projections, the Exclude Backorder configuration setting must be set to False.

Steps

When generating sales forecasts, the system can account for historical demand that was not immediately met due to past stockouts. Instead of basing future projections solely on completed sales, you can instruct the system to calculate true customer demand.
​
​
When the Exclude Backorder setting is False, both System Forecasts and User Forecasts calculate expected future volume using the following logic:
​
​

  • The system calculates your total historical demand by taking the sum of your historical volume: (Last Year Sales + Last Year Backorders + Last Year Backfills).
    ​
    ​

  • It applies your selected forecasting trend percentage (e.g., a 4-week trend or 6-week trend) to this total historical demand.
    ​
    ​

  • If forecasting by average, it appies the averages based on Last Year Sales + Last Year Backorders + Last Year Backfills as well.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Setting the Exclude Backorder can be configured in two ways:
​
​

  1. Use the exclude backorder dropdown for each product/location in the forecasting dashboard
    ​
    ​

  2. Use the edit/filldown functionality in table view and edit the exclude backorder column from the inventory table.

See the example where a 4-week trend for a product is +20.00%
​
​

Description

Values

4-week Trend

+20.00%

Last year sales

150

Last year backorders

20

Last year backfills

-5

Total when Exclude Backorder = False
(150+20-5)

165

Total when Exclude Backorder = True

150

Sales Forecast when Exclude Backorder = False
(165 x .2) + 165

198

Sales Forecast when Exclude Backorder = True
(150 x .2) + 150

180

Fields And Definitions

  • Exclude Backorder: A configuration setting that dictates how historical data is utilized. When True, the forecast relies strictly on closed historical sales. When False, the forecast includes previous backorders and backfills to represent total true demand.
    ​
    ​

  • System Forecast / User Forecast: The final projected numerical value generated by the system based on the selected time period and historical data parameters.
    ​
    ​

  • Forecast Method / Trend: The calculated rate of market growth or decline over a selected period (such as 4 weeks or 6 weeks) that is applied to your historical totals.

Best Practices

  • Forecast True Demand: It is highly recommended to include backorders and backfills in your calculations if you frequently experience out-of-stock scenarios. 16989712:
Distributor steps to fix the redirect_uri query parameter value is invalid error when connecting Encompass to QuickBooks Online: check OAuth keys, clear cache, re-authorize. Requires v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Admin Access: You must have administrative privileges in both Encompass and your QuickBooks Online account.

  • Intuit Credentials: You have access to your Intuit Developer Portal to verify Keys and OAuth settings.

  • Browser Requirements: Use a modern browser (Chrome or Safari are recommended).

  • Oauth Settings: Oauth Settings have been generated for the site

Steps

Error Message:"The redirect_uri query parameter value is invalid"

This error typically occurs when there is a mismatch between the credentials stored in your system and the Intuit Developer portal, or when cached browser data prevents QuickBooks Online from recognizing the authorization request.

Pre-conditions

Before beginning troubleshooting, ensure you meet the following requirements:

  • Admin Access: You must have administrative privileges in both Encompass and your QuickBooks Online account.

  • Intuit Credentials: You have access to your Intuit Developer Portal to verify Keys and OAuth settings.

  • Browser Requirements: Use a modern browser (Chrome or Safari are recommended).

Steps to Resolve

Follow these steps in order. If one step resolves the issue, you do not need to proceed to the next.

1. Verify OAuth Settings

Mismatched credentials are the most common cause of "invalid redirect" errors.

  • Navigate to your system's OAuth Settings.

  • Log in to your Intuit Developer Portal and locate the Keys & OAuth page.

  • Compare Client ID: Ensure the App ID in your system matches the Client ID from Intuit exactly.

  • Compare Client Secret: Ensure the App Secret in your system matches the Client Secret from Intuit exactly.

  • Update: If there is any discrepancy, update the fields in your system to match Intuit and save changes.

2. Clear Browser Cache and Cookies

Stale data can "confuse" the redirect process.

  • In your browser, press Ctrl + Shift + Delete (Windows) or Cmd + Shift + Delete (Mac).

  • Set the time range to All Time.

  • Select Cookies and other site data and Cached images and files.

  • Click Clear Data.

3. Attempt Sync in Incognito/Private Mode

This ensures no extensions or remaining cache interfere with the connection.

  • Open a new Incognito (Chrome) or Private (Safari/Firefox) window.

  • Log into your site and attempt the Connect to QuickBooks process again.

4. Disconnect and Re-authorize

If the connection is "stuck," you may need to reset the link.

  • Locate the Company Record in your system.

  • Find the GL Company ID field and clear the value (delete the ID).

  • Save the record.

  • Return to the QuickBooks Online Sync Setup and attempt to re-authorize the connection.

Best Practices

  • Use Incognito Mode for Setup: When first linking QuickBooks and Encompass, always use an Incognito window to ensure a "clean" authorization handshake.

  • Secure Secrets: Never share your App Secret or Client Secret in unencrypted emails or public tickets.

Fields And Definitions

Field

Definition

App ID / Client ID

A unique identifier for your application provided by Intuit.

App Secret / Client Secret

A private "password" used to authenticate your application's identity to Intuit.

Redirect URI

The specific URL that QuickBooks sends you back to after you log in. If this doesn't match the URL you are currently on, the sync will fail.

GL Company ID

The internal ID that links your specific system record to a specific QuickBooks Online company file.

OAuth

The "Open Authorization" standard used to share account information between Encompass and QuickBooks without sharing passwords.

Encompass Mobile guide for merchandisers/drivers to see co-workers visiting the same customer today (ETA, late/early, cases, action items) via MerchSync in My Day. Needs MerchSync app, setting 3406, v26.02+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.02

Pre-Conditions

  • The MerchSync application (Application ID 2192) must be installed.

    ​

  • The Mobile Application must be listed in System Setting 3406 - Merchandiser Mobile Application - MerchSync Widgets added to My Day. This setting can be updated in the App Library by clicking on installed apps, and updated the setting from there.

Steps

MerchSync provides real-time visibility into the activities of other team members (such as merchandisers, delivery drivers, sales representatives, or other employees) who are scheduled to visit the exact same customer on the same day. This enables better on-site coordination and planning.

Viewing Quick Statuses in My Day

1. Navigate to the My Day button in the mobile app.
​
2. Ensure you are in the Stop View tab (this information is not currently visible on both Map and Service Time views).
​
3. Look for the Customer event tile. If another user is visiting the same customer today, the type of Activity (delivery, presell, etc;) and estimated time of arrival (ETA), and current time status (e.g., minutes early or late) is displayed.
​
4. Tap anywhere on the Event card to drill down into the full Customer View for more detailed information.
​
​

​Viewing Detailed Information in the Customer View

1. Open the Customer View from your daily itinerary.
​
2. Located under the customer information, the MerchSync section will show specific information for each scheduled co-worker, including their route name, full name, and their current ETA. If the co-worker is doing a delivery, the number of cases to be delivered will also be displayed.
​
3. If there is a specific 'Action Items' for you to pay attention to, it will also be displayed in the MerchSync section.

My Day Example:
​
​In the example image below, this merchandiser has 4 stops on route 1687 Fri. The Wal-mart and 7-11 both have a delivery on the same day. Notice the delivery to 7-11 was completed 6:50 AM, while the ETA for Walmart is 7:22 AM and the driver is 20 minutes late.
​
​

Screenshot

Customer View Example:
​
In the example below, the section below the customer information and above the replen survey task in the MerchSync section. Any action items will be displayed at the top. In the example below, the action item begins with "Change of plans. Also notice in this example, the delivery driver, JoshuaO is on route 104 Mon and is 20 min late with an ETA of 7:22 AM.

Screenshot

Fields And Definitions

  • ETA (Estimated Time of Arrival): The projected time the co-worker will arrive at the customer location, based on their adjusted or planned start times.
    ​
    ​

  • Status (Late/Early): A real-time calculation showing how many minutes early or late the co-worker is running compared to their originally planned start time.
    ​
    ​

  • Completed at [Time]: Replaces the ETA once the co-worker has finished their visit, displaying the exact time they completed their tasks at the location.
    ​
    ​

  • Cancelled: Indicates that a task for a co-worker was not completed or was actively cancelled by them from their route.
    ​
    ​

  • Action Item: This is a note or set of instructions that need to be seen by a mechandiser and/or delivery rep. An action item is linked to a customer on a particular day.

Best Practices

  • Time Your Visits: Use the early/late status and ETA indicators to adjust your own travel plans. For example, if you are a merchandiser waiting for a delivery driver to arrive with product, check their real-time ETA before heading to the account.
    ​
    ​

  • Verify Sync Times: Always check the "last updated" timestamp in the Customer View to ensure you are basing your decisions on the most current data available from your co-workers' devices.
    ​
    ​

  • Refreshing Data: While in Stop View, use 'Pull down to refresh' to get updated information.
    ​
    ​

  • Review Multiple Visitors: If more than two people (e.g., two merchandisers and a driver) are visiting the same customer, the MerchSync section will show both people.

16989715:
Distributor steps to create a display survey in Encompass by copying the Display Survey system objective, editing questions, setting statuses and deploying with an Objective Schedule. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Create the Display Survey Objective
​
​It's recommended to use the System Objective for display surveys as it contains specific pre-configured settings.
​
​

  1. Navigate to the Objectives table using Universal Search.
    ​
    ​

  2. Locate the Display Survey system objective.
    ​
    ​

  3. Click the Sub Tables button on the record and select Copy Objectives.
    ​
    ​

  4. Enter a new Name for your custom survey.
    ​
    - Important: Under "Subtables to Copy," ensure you click the plus (+) icon and check Survey Questions and Survey Question Values to include the actual questions in your copy.
    ​
    ​

  5. Click Copy Record, then select View New Record.

Edit Survey Questions
​
​

  1. Click Edit on your new objective record to open the Objective Edit Dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  2. To Add a Question: Click Add Survey Questions.
    ​
    ​

  3. Enter the question text (e.g., "How many competitive brands are on display?").
    ​
    ​

  4. Set the Data Type (e.g., Decimal for numbers, Photo for images).
    ​
    ​

  5. Toggle Required to True if the response is mandatory.
    ​
    ​

  6. Repeat Logic: Set the Repeat column to "False" for general questions you only want to ask once per visit. Leave the overall section set to "Repeat for multiple products" for questions that apply to every specific product found on display.
    ​
    ​

  7. Click Save Changesand Edit Objective Status.
    ​
    ​

See Create An Objective - Survey for more detailed steps on editing surveys.

Configure Statuses and Assignment
​
​

1. In the Objective Statuses section, locate the Assigned status.
​

Set the Prompt Task field:
​

  • Service Event Start: Prompts the user immediately upon tapping the customer event (forces completion before other tasks).
    ​

  • Service Event End: Prompts the user when they attempt to leave the customer event.
    ​

Set the Assign To Group: Change the dropdown from "Salesman" to the desired role (e.g., Merchandiser) for the Assigned, Failed, and Completed statuses to ensure the correct user receives credit.
​
​

2. Click Save Changes.

Deploy via Objective Schedule

Using an Objective Schedule is the best practice for Display Surveys as it allows for specific frequency and customer filtering.

  1. From the Objective record, click Sub Tables and select Objective Schedule.
    ​
    ​

  2. Click Add Objective Schedule.
    ​
    ​

  3. Set the Frequency (e.g., Weekly).
    ​
    ​

  4. Set Filters (Location, On Premise, Customer Type, etc.) Filters are additive meaning that multiple filters further limit the customers that will be assigned surveys.
    ​
    ​

  5. Set a Start Date: It is best practice to set this at least several days (or a full week) in advance to align with route generation cycles.
    ​
    ​

  6. Click Add Record.

Fields And Definitions

  • Survey - Set of questions to obtain data
    ​
    ​

  • Objective - The overall record that holds the Survey Questions, Objective Statuses, Objective Schedules, etc.
    ​
    1. Objective Type - This field is typically only used for System Objectives or copies of System Objectives. These include additional functionality that is not included with a normal survey. Examples of these are the Asset Request and Display Surveys or DOT surveys. Leave this field blank unless you are specifically creating a survey that falls under the Objective Type.
    ​
    2. Delete Tasks After Days - This defaults at one (1) year and will only delete the tasks, does not delete Survey answers.
    ​
    3. Copy Answers to Details - This copies Survey answers to the task details tied to the survey. Typically this is set to True.
    ​
    4. Active - Status to tell if the Survey will be live or not.
    ​
    5. New Task Status - What status the Survey will be in when first assigned.
    ​
    6. After Deadline Task Status - The status the system will switch the Survey to if it is not taken within the time frame
    ​
    7. Mobile Item - Typically used for System Objectives. Ties the survey to a button/Mobile Item in Encompass Mobile. Allows users to tap a button and be taken to the survey. Mobile Items are typically used in combination with an Objective Type. Leave this field blank unless you are creating a survey with this intended functionality.
    ​
    8. Customer ID Required - If a Survey will need to be taken at customer accounts. This should be set to yes unless taking a survey that is not customer-specific such as a DOT survey.
    ​
    ​

  • Survey Section - This is the container that defines a set of survey questions.
    ​
    ​    1. Sequence - Allows you to organize questions in a set numerical order.
    ​
    2. Survey Section - Creates multiple sections of questions. Allows for more organization of longer surveys or surveys that require selecting multiple products or brands.
    ​
    3. Section Type - Does not change the functionality of the survey. This is for categorization for Reporting purposes.
    ​
    4. Repeat Questions - Choose if needed to repeat questions for either Brand or Products. Links the Brand or Products to the task.
    ​
    5. Last Answer Auto Populate - Populates the last collected answer for the customer for all questions in the section. The answer can still be edited.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Section Values - Allows for repeating the questions in the survey section multiple times for different categories.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Survey Questions - The questions users will answer.
    ​
    ​    1. Sequence - The order in which the questions will be displayed. Drag and drop questions to reorder using the arrows.
    ​
    2. Question - The text displayed in the survey as the Question.
    ​
    3. Data Types - Used to collect different types of data. See Survey Question Data Types.
    ​
    4. Required - Required to complete the Survey. The question must be answered to complete.
    ​
    5. Remember - Populates the answer from the previous answer on a question by question basis instead of the entire section.
    ​
    6. Repeat - Use if you want the question to repeat for multiple Brands or Products.
    ​
    7. Ask if Survey Question - When set, the question will only be asked if the Ask If Questions answer meets the following:
    ​
    - Ask If Operator - Defines whether the answer to a question should be greater than, less than, equal to, etc.
    ​
    - Ask If Value - In combination with the Ask If Operator, how the Ask If Question needs to be answered to display the question.
    ​
    ​

  • Objective Status - Status of the task determining task flow. Additional statuses can be created for use on the Task Status table. See Objective Statuses.
    ​
    ​

  • Task - Individual instances of surveys being assigned/completed.

Best Practices

  • Start Dates: Always push the Start Date of a new objective schedule out as far as possible (matching your "Days in Advance" route settings) to ensure tasks populate on user plans correctly.
    ​
    ​

  • Copying over New: Avoid creating display surveys from scratch. Copy the system objective to ensure "Repeat" logic and product-linking settings remain intact.
    ​
    ​

  • Testing: Use the Take a Survey dashboard on the server to test the flow and sequence of questions before deploying to the field.

When the Repeat for Multiple Brands or Products setting is active, mobile users have the ability to select multiple products or brands at the start of a survey.
​
​

To enable:

  • Toggle on "Select multiple..." at the top of the product or brand selection list.
    ​
    ​

  • Choose all desired products or brands at the same time.
    ​
    ​

  • The survey will generate questions for each selection and track which have been answered and which are still in progress.
    ​
    ​

Screenshot

​
Users can save their survey answers when backing out of an incomplete survey, ensuring progress is preserved until the survey is completed. If a survey is incomplete, a prompt appears when the user clicks "Back," offering three options:

  • Save: Saves the answers and returns to the previous page.
    ​
    ​

  • Don’t Save: Discards the answers and returns to the previous page.
    ​
    ​

  • Cancel: Keeps the user on the current page.

When saved, answers are flagged as "Pending" and won’t be uploaded until the survey is edited again and completed. The Surveys page will display surveys with "Pending" or "Edited" statuses, ensuring easy tracking of incomplete tasks.
​

16989716:
Distributor troubleshooting for failed imports in the legacy Budget By Account/Month app: use Import Routine 634111 to load the Bgt_Budget table (not ZZ_Budget) and Report 12731031 to reconcile budget vs actuals. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Application: "Budget By Account/Month" (Legacy version).

  • System Requirement: Active access to the global Import Routine tool and the Report Library.

  • Schema Requirement: Applicable to customers on the modern database schema utilizing the Bgt_Budget table.

Steps

  1. Identify Schema Mismatch: If the import task within the "Budget By Account/Month" application fails, it is likely attempting to write to the legacy ZZ_Budget table which does not exist in your environment.

  2. Access the Modern Import Routine: Navigate to the system-wide Import Routine tool.

  3. Search by Routine ID: Search for and execute Import Routine ID: 634111. This routine is specifically configured to map data to the modern Bgt_Budget schema. Please note you may need to filter to EncompassID = Support to see this record.

  4. Verify Data via Report Library: Once the import is successful, navigate to the Report Library.

  5. Search by Report ID: Search for Report ID: 12731031. This report is designed to pull from the modern schema and should be used to reconcile your imported budget against actuals. Please note you may need to filter to EncompassID = Support to see this record.

  6. Discontinue Application-Level Imports: Move away from using the "Budget By Account/Month" application dashboard for imports, as it may still reference legacy data structures.

  7. Contact Support: If the IDs provided do not appear in your search results or the import fails, contact support with the following information:

    • IDs Attempted: Confirm use of Import ID 634111 and Report ID 12731031.

    • Error Messages: Provide the exact error code or text encountered.

    • Screenshots: Attach images of the search results or the import configuration screen.

    • Log Files: Provide any generated import error logs.

    • Step-by-Step: Document the exact path taken to reach the Import Routine tool.

    • System History: Note the date/time the issue started and if any recent migrations occurred.

Fields And Definitions

  • Use IDs for Accuracy: When searching for tools, use the unique ID numbers (634111/12731031) rather than names to ensure you are using the version compatible with the Bgt_Budget schema.

  • Transition to the Report Library: Favor the "Budget" section in the Report Library over application-specific dashboards, as these are more frequently updated for schema changes.

  • Verify Source Headers: Ensure your import file aligns with the requirements of the modern Bgt_Budget table to avoid mapping errors.

Best Practices

  • Bgt_BudgetModern Schema Table: The current standard database structure for all budget data.
    ​
    ​

  • ZZ_BudgetLegacy Schema Table: An older database structure no longer present in newer system environments.
    ​
    ​

  • Import Routine ID: 634111The specific system tool used to ingest budget data into the modern Bgt_Budget table.
    ​
    ​

  • Report ID: 12731031The designated report for reconciling modern budget data against actuals.SchemaThe underlying structure or "map" of the database that determines where data is stored.

16989720:
Distributor guide to OrderIQ New Placement campaigns in Encompass: how case goals, AI demand and primary delivery days shape automated order recommendations for campaign products. Requires v26.03+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.03

Pre-Conditions

  • OrderIQ must be active and enabled in your environment.
    ​
    ​

  • Campaign configuration records must be set up with a target Customer ID, Campaign Type (New Placement), Product ID, Case Goal, Start Date, and End Date.
    ​
    ​

  • Customers must have eligible stops or events scheduled during the campaign's delivery week.

Steps

OrderIQ allows you to seamlessly integrate strategic sales initiatives, such as new product launches or inventory pushes, directly into your automated ordering process. By establishing campaign goals, OrderIQ automatically adjusts its predictive recommendations to help fulfill your business objectives without manual intervention.

How New Placement Campaigns Work:

  1. Target Identification: The system evaluates if the product is a "New Placement," meaning the customer has no historical purchase records for that product prior to the campaign's Start Date.
    ​
    ​

  2. Quantity Calculation: OrderIQ calculates the necessary order quantity by taking your overall case goal and subtracting any successful purchases made during the active campaign window. Returns or negative quantities are ignored and do not reduce the remaining target goal.
    ​
    ​

  3. AI Optimization: The campaign goal acts as a minimum baseline. OrderIQ compares the remaining campaign goal against its own AI-predicted demand. If the AI predicts a higher quantity is needed, the system will recommend the higher AI quantity. If the AI predicts a lower quantity, the system defaults to the campaign goal to ensure your promotional targets are prioritized.
    ​
    ​

  4. Delivery Prioritization: OrderIQ targets the customer's primary delivery day to fulfill the campaign goal. On this day, it attempts to recommend the maximum possible quantity needed. If the goal is not met in a single delivery, the remaining quantity is distributed across other eligible delivery days within the campaign timeframe.

Fields And Definitions

  1. New Placement: A campaign configuration targeting customers who have not previously purchased a specific product. Any purchases made specifically during the campaign window count toward the goal and do not disqualify the placement.
    ​
    ​

  2. Campaign Goal: The target minimum quantity (measured in cases) that you aim to distribute to a specific customer within the defined Start and End Dates.
    ​
    ​

  3. Primary Delivery Day: The prioritized day of the week (configured in the customer's stop settings) when OrderIQ will focus on pushing the campaign product. If no primary day is explicitly flagged, the system defaults to the first eligible delivery day of the week.

Best Practices

  • Maintain Accurate Unit Configurations: Campaign goals are defined in "cases," but the final automated orders are placed in base units. Ensure the "Units per Case" configuration for your campaign products is completely accurate to prevent over-ordering or under-ordering.
    ​
    ​

  • Define Primary Delivery Days: To ensure the most efficient distribution of campaign products, always designate a "primary delivery day" in your customers' stop settings. This ensures the bulk of the placement goal lands on the most optimal day.
    ​
    ​

  • Leverage AI Upside: Allow the system to work for you; because the campaign goal acts as a minimum floor, you will never miss your target, but you can still capitalize on increased demand if the OrderIQ AI identifies that a customer can absorb a higher quantity.

16989723:
Admin and user steps for connecting an AI client (e.g. Claude) to Encompass via the Cowork MCP server: Allow MCP Access, MCP Servers record, OAuth or bearer token, endpoint URL. Needs Encompass Cowork app; v26.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.07

Pre-Conditions

  • App Library: Encompass Cowork must be installed in your system.

  • MCP access permission: Each user who connects needs the Allow MCP Access permission on their role. Administrators set this on the Roles table and need AI Agent Admin and Permission Edit rights to configure the connection.

  • External AI client: You need a third-party AI client that supports MCP connections (such as Claude).

Steps

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) server securely connects an external AI client directly to your Encompass system. Each person connects as their own Encompass user, so the AI can read and change only what that user's roles and field-level permissions allow, and every change is written to the Encompass audit trail as an MCP-server change.

There are two ways to authenticate, and both run as the individual user:

  • OAuth 2.1 (recommended): the user signs in with their own Encompass account when connecting. Required for clients such as Claude that use a "custom connector" flow.

  • Personal bearer token: the user generates a private token from their Profile page and pastes it into the AI client.

One-time setup (administrator)

  1. Grant MCP access: On the Roles table, enable Allow MCP Access for the role(s) whose users should be able to connect. It is checked on every request, so removing it cuts off access immediately.

  2. Create the connector record: In the MCP Servers configuration table, add one record for the AI client you are connecting (for example, "Claude"). Encompass automatically generates an OAuth Client ID and OAuth Secret for it. A single record can serve many users, so you no longer create a separate record per person.

  3. Set the redirect (callback) URL: In the connector record, set Redirect URI to the callback your AI client uses. For Claude this is https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback. OAuth sign-in is rejected if it does not match.

  4. Share the connection details: Give the endpoint URL, and for OAuth the Client ID and Secret, to the users who will connect.

Connecting your AI client (each user)

  1. Add a custom connector: In your AI client, add a new MCP server using the Encompass endpoint URL, formatted as https://api.e8.co/mcp?EncompassID=<YourEncompassID.> Your EncompassID is shown in the lower-left menu of any page, just under your username. Always use api.e8.co, not your normal Encompass domain.

  2. Authenticate with OAuth (recommended): enter the Client ID and Secret from your administrator, then sign in with your own Encompass credentials when prompted. The AI then acts as you, with your permissions.

  3. Or use a personal bearer token: in Encompass, open your Profile and choose Get MCP Bearer Token. Copy the token (it is shown only once) and paste it into your AI client. Generating a new token immediately revokes the previous one.

  4. Start working: Once connected, the AI automatically discovers the available Encompass tools. Prompt it normally (for example, "Show me this month's open orders") and it runs the request in Encompass using your permissions.

Fields And Definitions

  • MCP Endpoint: The web address an external client uses to reach your database, including your EncompassID (https://api.e8.co/mcp?EncompassID=<id).> Always use api.e8.co.

  • Allow MCP Access: The role permission that controls who may connect over MCP. It is verified on every request; a user without it cannot authenticate or run any tool.

  • OAuth Client ID / Secret: Per-connector credentials generated on the MCP Servers record. They identify the AI client, not the person, and each user still signs in with their own Encompass account.

  • Redirect URI: The callback the AI client returns to after sign-in, registered on the connector record (for Claude, https://claude.ai/api/mcp/auth_callback). The value sent during sign-in must match it exactly.

  • Personal Bearer Token: A private token a user generates from their Profile (stored only as a hash and shown once) to connect as themselves without the OAuth flow.

  • Available MCP Tools: Encompass exposes a focused subset of its core tools. Read-only: TableStructure, TableSearch, TableView, and FieldAudit. Write/delete: TableAdd, TableEdit, TableCopy, and TableDelete.

  • Rate Limits: To protect system performance, MCP connections are governed by limits on requests per minute and processing seconds per minute.

Best Practices

  • Grant access deliberately: Enable Allow MCP Access only for roles that need it. Because the AI runs as the individual user, it is automatically limited to that person's existing permissions, with no shared service account to over-provision.

  • Prefer OAuth over static tokens: OAuth ties each connection to a real sign-in and supports automatic token refresh and revocation. Use a personal bearer token only when a client cannot use the custom-connector flow, and treat it like a password.

  • Protect and rotate credentials: Keep OAuth Secrets and personal tokens confidential. Regenerate a personal token, or the connector's secret, immediately if it may have been exposed; the change takes effect right away.

  • Audit trail tracking: Every add, edit, and delete the AI makes is recorded in the standard Encompass audit trail, attributed to the real user and tagged as an MCP-server change, so you can see exactly what was changed and by whom.

Steps/General Instructions

Package: An optional field to apply specific rates to a specific package type. Rules including a Package ID take precedence over general rules.

16989730:
Distributor guide to automatic transfer invoices in Encompass after PO Generator purchases are received at the primary location, plus the uncreated transfer alert. Needs Forecast Group/Transfer Planner setup, v26.05+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.05

Pre-Conditions

  • Forecast Group must have a Receive Location set.

  • Forecast Group -> Auto Create Transfers must be set to either Yes - Ordered = Received for PO, or Yes - Ordered = Received for Product

  • Forecast Group must have inventory records for non-receive location (Forecast Group Effective)

  • Transfer Planner Setup must be completed. See help resources to learn about setting up Transfer Planner

  • Purchases must be generated through the PO Generator.

  • Shipments Status must be Received, Confirmed, or Verified.

  • Purchase must be received after the Last Success Time of the Auto Transfers From Transfer To Purchase Trans scheduled task (ReceiveTime > LastSuccessTime)

  • If Alternate Locations is being used and the receive location equals the altnerate location, the 'Use Alternate Location' field on the inventory record will control what product can be automatically transferred. See Steps for more detail.

Steps

Generate Purchase Orders:
​
​

  • Use the PO Generator to create purchases for products intended to meet demand for other locations.
    ​
    ​

  • As shown below, the purchase will have transactions with the transfer to location set for other locations
    ​
    ​

    Screenshot

  • Important Step! Review the PO and update the status to "Ordered" once it has been sent to the supplier or vendor.

How the Automated Transfer is created:
​
​1. Once the shipment is received in the "primary" location, the Auto Transfers From Transfer To Purchase Trans scheduled task will run within 15 minutes and a transfer invoice will be created for the "primary" location
​
2. In order for the transfer invoice to be created, the following conditions must be met:

  • The shipment must be received
    ​
    ​

  • The total ordered must equal the total (num units) received for the entire purchase.
    ​
    ​

  • It is important to point out that products that are not included in sales reporting (Product Types - Include in Sales Reports by Default = False) will be ignored. This means that if dunnage products, such as empty pallets are added to the purchase during receiving, that will not prevent the transfer from being created.

3. The transfer invoice will have a Load Sheet date = The default will be the Receive Date + 1 business day, however the routing method associated with the transfer routes used.
​
4. The transfer purchase for the "other" locations will be created using the existing transfer planner EDI logic.
​
5. Once the transfer invoice is created, the transfer to location will be cleared out on the original purchase. This is to prevent duplicate transfers from being created.

AlternateLocations

Regarding the auto transfer process for items where 'use alternate location' is set to true or false on the inventory record, this give distributors even more control of what product they want to transfer vs. what products they want to process through the alternate locations workflow.

If the forecast location has an alternate location equal to the receive location, and the forecast location's product 'Use Alternate Locations' is TRUE on the inventory record, this product will not qualify to be automatically transferred. However, if 'Use Alternate Locations' is FALSE, that product will qualify for automated transfers.

Alerting

If for some reason the automated transfer does not get created, users can set up and subscribe to an Uncreated Transfer Notification alert.

  • Go to the alerts table and filter on alert type = 47) Uncreated Transfers Notification
    ​
    ​

  • If there is not an alert with alert type 47, create a new alert
    ​
    ​

  • Click the Sub Table button and select Alert Users
    ​
    ​

  • Click Add Alert Users

In most cases, the alert will be sent if the purchases is in received status and the total amount ordered does not match the total amount received.

Fields And Definitions

  • PO Generator: A tool that generates Purchase Orders based on demand forecasts.
    ​
    ​

  • Primary Location: The main location designated to receive purchased products.

16989734:
Producer steps to split volume off a brewery, winery or distillery batch and blend it into another Production Order in Encompass Batch Management, with costing carried over. Requires v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Pre-Conditions

This guide is to help Users with Splitting volume off of an existing Batch and then consuming it into another Batch (AKA Production Order).

Requirements for this to work are:
​
​

  1. The "from" Production Order in the Batch that is being split from has a status of either In Progress or Completed.
    ​
    ​

  2. IF IN PROGRESS: there is an available, empty tank to hold the WIP being pulled off of the Production Order.
    ​
    ​

  3. The "to" Production Order is scheduled with a status of either in New or In Progress.

  • Splitting a batch reduces the volume of the from batch
    ​
    ​

  • Note: Costing will be locked in at the time of the split function. Whatever the "from" Production Order is valued at per unit at the time of the split will follow the volume pulled off of it and blended into subsequent Production Orders. EX: there are 10bbls valued at $100. When 1bbl is split, the 1bbl will be worth $10 and will roll up into any costing for any Production Order it is blended into. The remaining 9bbls in the "from-batch" will be valued at $90.

Steps

Before Proceeding: Be confident that the users is splitting from and to the correct Production Orders. It is difficult to unwind a split and blend.

The following steps will ensure costing is accurate and batch tracing works for split and blended batches.

Splitting from IN PROGRESS Production Orders:
​
​

  1. Navigate to the Batch Management dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  2. Filter to the Production Order needed to split from.
    ​
    ​

  3. Click Split Batch.
    ​
    ​

  4. Confirm the data in the dialogue is the product and stage wanted to execute the split.
    ​
    ​

  5. Click Split Into Equipment.
    ​
    ​

  6. Select the equipment wanting to transfer the WIP product into.
    ​
    ​

  7. Enter Transfer Quantity.
    ​
    ​

  8. Click Split Batch to execute the transfer.
    ​
    ​

  9. Navigate to the Batch Management dashboard and find the Production Order that the user wants to blend into.
    ​
    ​

  10. The Product that was split in steps 4-8 needs to be added as a "Component" in this Production Order.
    ​
    ​

  11. Consume the Product that was split from the previous batch in the Production Order that we are blending into.

Splitting from COMPLETED Production Orders:
​
​

  1. Navigate to the Batch Management dashboard and find the Production Order that we want to blend into.
    ​
    ​

  2. Add the Product that was created when the "from" Production Order was completed as a component on the Production Order we are blending it into.
    ​
    ​

  3. Process the Production as normal, consuming the material from the other Production Order.

Fields And Definitions

  • From Batch - the Batch that has a Production Order in it that users are pulling volume off of to redirect to a new batch or a different tank.
    ​
    ​

  • To Batch - the Batch that has a Production Order in it that users are transferring volume from another batch into.
    ​
    ​

  • Production Order - The set of stages that comprise a continuous workflow as part of a batch.

Best Practices

  • Double check that users are splitting from and to the correct batches. This is a difficult process to reverse.

16989736:
Brewery steps to fix Grist integration import errors in Encompass: Cannot find Location, Recipe or Product, batch or lot code not found, and partial imports, using Table Translations. Requires v25.11+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.11

Steps

Grist Integration Troubleshooting

The success of the Grist integration relies on precise data mapping and exact matching between Grist events and Encompass records. If the import encounters unmapped or missing data, it may result in a partial import or fail entirely.

Location and Recipe Errors

  • Error Message:Cannot find Location: xxxxxxx; Cannot find Recipe: xxxxxxx.
    ​
    ​

  • Cause: A Location or Recipe/Plan value in the Grist file does not have a corresponding mapping in Encompass.
    ​
    ​

  • Resolution: Use Table Translations to map the Grist Location or Recipe to the correct Encompass Location or Recipe Version. Once mapped, re-import the file.

Product Mapping Errors

  • Error Message:Cannot find Product: xxxxxxx.
    ​
    ​

  • Cause: An ingredient name in the Grist event cannot be resolved to a Product ID in Encompass.
    ​
    ​

  • Resolution: Map the Grist Ingredient name to the appropriate Encompass Product via Table Translations and re-import.
    ​
    ​

  • Note: Ensure a 1:1 mapping; the system cannot resolve two Grist ingredients to one Encompass product.

Batch and Lot Number Issues

  • Batch Matching: The system uses Batch Number and Lot Number as primary keys. These must match textually exactly.
    ​
    ​

  • Missing Batch Match: If a Batch Number cannot be matched, Encompass will create a new Production Order rather than updating an existing one. No specific error message is provided for this condition.
    ​
    ​

  • Lot/Batch Code Error:Product XXXXX with Batch Code CCCCC not found.
    ​
    ​

  • Cause: The system cannot find an inventory layer (Purchase Transaction) matching the Lot # provided by Grist.
    ​
    ​

  • Logic: If the specific Lot # isn't found, the system defaults to the oldest inventory layer (FIFO).
    ​
    ​

  • Failure: If no inventory layer exists at all (zero inventory), the component will not be imported.
    ​
    ​

  • Resolution: Re-open the PdO and manually enter the ingredient amount and batch.

16989738:
Distributor guide to MerchSync data in Encompass: how adjusted start and end times roll forward, daily average service times, and On Board Diagnostics and Vehicle Trips handheld data. Requires v26.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.09

Pre-Conditions

  • The MerchSync application must be installed.
    ​
    ​

  • This functionality applies specifically to users and routes that are not utilizing live GPS tracking.
    ​
    ​

  • Events must be assigned to a Plan for the current day.

Steps

Start/End Times:

This functionality operates automatically in the background to ensure your route estimates remain accurate throughout the day. As field users complete their planned stops, the system continually updates the Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) for all remaining scheduled events.

  • When a scheduled event is completed, the system receives the completion time (synced from the mobile app) and compares it to the originally planned completion time.
    ​
    ​

  • If the user is running ahead of or behind schedule, the system calculates the exact time difference.
    ​
    ​

  • The system then automatically rolls this time difference forward, updating the Adjusted Start and End times for all remaining, unserviced events on that daily plan.
    ​
    ​

  • Example: If a user finishes a morning stop 30 minutes later than their planned schedule, the Adjusted Start and End times for all remaining stops on their itinerary that day will automatically be pushed back by 30 minutes, giving users an accurate view of the new expected arrival times.


Service Times:
​
​With MerchSync installed Customers Average Service Times for all activities are averaged by day of the week. When events are planned for all activities the planned start/end times are based on these daily averages.
​

  • A customer's merchandiser average service time on the customer record could be different than the daily average on the Customers Daily Average Service Times table.
    ​

  • For example, customer A is visited 8 times total: Mon (11 minutes, 5 minutes), Tue (7 minutes), Wed (3 minutes, 9 minutes, 7 minutes), Thu (5 minutes), Fri (10 minutes). So the average is (11 + 5 + 7 + 3 + 9 + 7 + 5 + 10) / 8 = 7.125. This will not equal average of the daily times because the daily averages are calculated first (e.g., Mon 8, Tue 7, Wed 6.3, Thu 5, Fri 10). 36.3/5 = 7.26.

Other Data:
​
​

  • On Board Diagnostics and Vehicle Trips Data - Originally, data in these tables was for Fleet Tracker integrations only, however they have been repurposed to also include handheld data if MerchSync is installed.
    ​
    ​

  • On Board Diagnostics is a good way to validate that a device is "pinging" about every minutes. This can be done by searching for the On Board Diagnostic table and filtering a user's specific Handheld ID.
    ​
    ​

  • Vehicle Trips is another table that will link a Handheld, Plan, and Events, which can be tied to a customer.

Fields And Definitions

  • Planned Start / End Time: The initially scheduled times for an event before the route begins.
    ​
    ​

  • Adjusted Start / End Time: The recalculated, dynamically updating ETA based on the user's actual pace (whether they are running early or late).
    ​
    ​

  • Actual Start / End Time: The exact, real-world time the event was started and completed. This is typically recorded and synced directly from the mobile application when the user enters and leaves a customer's geofence.

Best Practices

  • Ensure mobile users are connected and syncing their application frequently throughout the day. Because the automatic ETA adjustments are triggered by the "Actual End Time" of completed stops, consistent syncing guarantees dispatchers and managers always have the most accurate, real-time visibility into route progress.
    ​
    ​

  • For best results when users arrive or depart a customer's geofence, users should ensure the Encompass Mobile location setting is set to Always.

Configuring Order Size Splitting:

​

​
