16989773:
Distributor and warehouse picker overview of ePick+ on Encompass Mobile Warehouse, which replaced legacy ePick: multi-scan, layer priority, replenish requests, bin corrections and bin changes. Requires v26.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.01

Pre-Conditions

  • The "ePick" field on your site's Location record must be set to True.
    ​
    ​

  • Picking team members should have Employee Pick Teams records on their relevant Pick Teams.
    ​
    ​

  • Invoices should be palletized and processed to see them in ePick+.

Steps

What is ePick+?

ePick+ is a digital solution for picking that integrates with handheld devices, allowing for a guided picking experience. It replaces older methods like paper picking and brings warehouse processes into a digital age. The tool offers more robust functionality, including an updated visual experience and simplified workflows.

  • Legacy vs. ePick+: The original tool, ePick (formerly Voice Pick), has been phased out. With the 26.01 release, ePick Legacy is no longer accessible or supported.
    ​
    Though no additional training is needed for ePick+ as the workflow is designed to be as similar as possible to the legacy version, this article serves as an overview of the tool, and reviews the most notable differences. For a closer look, check out the ePick+ Skills Kickstart.
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • Goals and Motivations: The development of ePick+ was driven by four key goals:
    ​
    ​

    • Modernize: Provide an updated, intuitive look with critical information presented upfront.
      ​
      ​

    • Streamline and Focus: Adjust settings and processes to reduce unnecessary steps and confusion.
      ​
      ​

    • Diversify: Built on a new code structure, ePick+ allows access on a wider range of devices, including Android (e.g., Zebra WS50) in addition to iOS.
      ​
      ​

    • Safeguard: Most changes in the ePick+ structure do not require a new mobile app version, which makes it easier to implement changes and release them at a quicker rate.

ePick+ Exclusive Features and How to Use Them

Here are the exclusive features in ePick+ and how they work:

1. Multi-Scan Prompt

This feature can be toggled on or off in the Settings menu. When a picker is picking the same product for multiple pallets, the system can be set to require a scan for each individual pick. Turning this off allows the picker to make one scan and then be prompted to pick the required quantity for each pallet.
​
​
​

2. Layer Prioritization

This setting re-sorts the pick sequence to place full-layer quantities first. This helps inexperienced pick team members build a more stable base for their pallets, leading to better transport and less potential for breakage. This can be toggled on even if you're not performing actual layer picking using special machinery.
​
​
​

3. Easier Navigation

Instead of repeatedly tapping the back button to return to the main page, users can now tap the menu in the top right corner to access the “Main Page” link. This allows navigation from anywhere in the picking process directly to the main screen.
​
​
​

4. Replenishment Requests

If there isn't enough inventory in a bin, pickers can create a replenish request on the fly. System Setting 527 allows you to control whether a prompt appears when a picker cuts a pick or skips it. The system will then create a replenishment move task that gets prioritized in the directed replenishment hierarchy.
​
​
​

5. Bin Inventory Correction

This feature allows a picker to reset bin inventory to zero if they make a quantity cut due to incorrect bin inventory. System Setting 3231 allows you to control whether a prompt will appear to ask if they want to count the current bin inventory to zero. This ensures the bin inventory is accurate and prevents other pickers from being directed to an empty bin. Bin Inventory corrections can be paired with Replenishment Requests to optimize pick bin inventory and time with product available.
​
​
​

6. Change Pick Bin

Controlled by the “Allow Bin Changes In ePick” field found on Pick Methods, pickers can now change the bin they are picking from. By tapping the bin location, they can see other bins and code dates with available inventory for that product. This helps reduce after-the-fact moves and keeps inventory accurate.

Best Practices

General Workflow and Tips

1. Accessing ePick+: Login to Encompass Mobile Warehouse. Find the picking section and select ePick+.

2. Using Filters: On the main page, filter by date, pallet type, or pick team. Pick Team selection is controlled by the Pick Teams assigned to the logged in Employee. These filters were previously found within ePick Settings in the legacy version of the tool.

3. Settings Menu: The menu in the top right corner gives you access to settings, and the Cognex camera scanner.

  • Upload Logs: If you experience an issue, use the "Upload logs" button at the top of the Settings page to send your data to developers to help them troubleshoot.
    ​
    ​

  • Default Printer: You can set a default printer for pallet tags, or leave it set to "None" to allow pickers to choose their printer at the end of each pallet.

Picking Process:

  • Clicking "Start Picking" is the same as the old "begin" button.
    ​
    ​

  • Before the first pick, a summary will be displayed showing the pallet's total cases and pallet type. All assigned pallets will be listed if picking more than one pallet at a time.
    ​
    ​

  • During picking, a progress bar shows the number of SKUs picked out of the total. The total number of units is also displayed at the top.
    ​
    ​

  • The "View all" button displays the list of all products on the pallet and provides a summary of the pallet's progress, including changes like skipped picks or cut quantities.

Finishing a Pallet:

  • Once all products are picked, pallet tag printing and QA options will appear depending on system configuration.
    ​
    ​

  • Pallet details can be viewed after the fact by tapping on the completed pallet from the ePick+ main page; this is the same view as Pallet Inquiry. Pallet Tags can also be reprinted from this view.
    ​
    ​

  • Clicking "Start Picking" again will assign new pallets to pick.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

For information regarding updating pallet tags for the new Costco ASN template released in 24.05, please click here.

How to set up Pick Rules


Add Load Groups
​
​

1. Using Universal search, navigate to the Load Groups table.

  • Load Groups determine how a Pallet needs to be loaded. Example: if they are layered by Product, or when Pallet Tags are printed, etc.

2. Click the Add Load Groups button
​
3. Enter values in the fields displayed on the Add Load Groups.

Note: Many of the required fields are default and can be changed based on the intended workflow.
​
4. Click Add Record when complete
​
​

Add Pallet Types
​
1. Using Universal search, navigate to the Pallet Types table.
​

  • Pallet Types are the physical pallets the products will be built on. The pallet type used is determined by the load group.
    ​
    ​

2. Click Add Pallet Types.
​
3. Enter values in the fields displayed.

- Pallet Type: This is a text field to title the Pallet record
​
​ - Build Height: How high can this Pallet be built
​
​ - Width / Length: The width and length of the physical pallet
​
​ - Weight: Is used for QA ONLY. (This is included on the weight in Delivery Optimizer)

4. Click Add Record when complete.
​
​

Add Pick Methods
​
​1. Using Universal search, navigate to the Pick Methods table
​
​

  • Pick Methods determine how a product needs to be picked
    ​
    ​

2. Click the Add Pick Methods button.
​
3. Enter values in the fields displayed on the Add Pick Methods form.

​ Note: Many of the required fields are default and can be changed based on the intended workflow.
​
4. Click Add Record when complete.
​
​

Add Pick Rules
​
​1. Using Universal search, navigate to the Pick Rules table.
​
​

  • Pick Rules determine which Pick Method will be used by looking at the Invoice Transaction. Think of them as IF-THEN statements. Example: IF the Invoice Transaction holds true for everything on the Pick Rule from Location to Bin Zone, THEN use the Pick Method on the record.
    ​
    ​

2. Click the Add Pick Rules button.
​
3. Enter values in the fields displayed on the Add Pick Rules form.
​
​

  • *Priority - This determines the order a Pick Rule is checked
    ​
    ​ Note: Pick Rules should never have the same priority
    ​
    ​

  • *Location - Will ONLY affect multi-location Distributorships and looks to the location on the Load Sheet
    ​
    ​

  • Route Type - Points to the Route’s Route Type on the Load Sheet
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Pick Type - Points to the Customer Record
    ​
    ​

  • Product Pick Type - On the Product Type or the Inventory Record. Note: A product’s Inventory record’s Product Pick Type will override the Product Type
    ​
    ​

  • Minimum Cases - Minimum requirement of cases to apply this pick rule. (Typically used for Bulk Picks to pick by Pallet)
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Unit - Determined by the Product record and is set on the Invoice Transaction when you apply Pick Rules
    ​
    ​

  • Close Date - Used for Close Dated Products. If this field is True the Bin Zone should be set to CLOSE DATED to ensure the products are being picked from the correct location
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Zone - What Bin Zone does this product live in and where does Encompass send the Pickers when this rule is applied? (IF NULL Bin Zone defaults to all Pick Zones.)
    ​
    ​

  • *Pick Method - How the Pick Method is tied to the Pick Rule
    ​
    ​

  • Oddball Bin - Used for Dynamic or Double Picking ONLY (Moving from Backstock to only one bin)
    ​
    ​

  • Dynamic Pick Line Bin Zone - Used for Dynamic or Double Picking Only (Moving from Backstock to Multiple Bins)
    ​

  • Skip - When Skip is set to True, if the inventory in a particular bin is not sufficient for palletization, this will skip over the bin with insuffiecient inventory, and move onto the next bin in the bin zone. This ignores the default logic of sending picks to bins regardless of inventory, as long as the inventory is active.
    ​
    ​

  • Label Printer - Indicates which APS printer box labels will print if the pick method is set to print box labels
    ​
    ​

  • Box Print Template - Set template for printing box labels when pick method is set to print box labels
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Sheet Printer - Indicates which APS printer pick sheets will print too if the pick method is set to voice pick = false

4. Click Add Record when complete.

16989786:
Distributor explanation of how Encompass calculates Available Inventory (Onfloor minus Presales minus Allocated) and why it may not update right away after bin imports. Requires v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Steps

Q: What is Available Inventory?
​
A: Available Inventory represents the quantity of a product that is immediately available for sale and customer invoicing.

It is calculated by taking the physical, accessible stock on hand and subtracting all quantities that have already been reserved or committed through orders.

The standard calculation for Available Inventory is:

Available Inventory=Onfloor Inventory−Presales−Allocated

All the above fields can be found on the inventory table in Encompass.

Fields And Definitions

  • Available Inventory - The final quantity of a product available for sale/invoicing. Calculated as Onfloor Inventory - Presales - Allocated.
    ​
    ​

  • Onfloor Inventory - The physical inventory quantity currently in the facility's bins, excluding specific bin zones like the Adjust Bin. This value is updated by the scheduled task.
    ​
    ​

  • Presales - The total quantity of a product that has been added to invoices but has not yet been delivered to the customer. This quantity is deducted from the Onfloor Inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Allocated - The total quantity of a product that has been reserved for a specific customer, chain, or rep via an allocation method. This quantity is deducted from the Onfloor Inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Inventories - The table or feature that records the specific quantity of a product held within individual storage locations (Bins). Direct imports to this table do not immediately update Available Inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Adjust Bin - A specific Bin Zone used by the system as a balancing ledger when inventory is imported directly into other bins. Inventory in this bin is excluded from the Onfloor Inventory calculation.
    ​
    ​

  • Update_Inventories_OnFloorInventory - A Scheduled Task that runs on a timer (e.g., every 60 minutes) to recalculate and update the Onfloor Inventory value, which then drives the Available Inventory display.

Best Practices

  • Please note alternate locations will calculate available inventory for both locations using the same calculation.
    ​
    ​

  • A good place to check the current available inventory without entering invoice edit is the inventory table.

16989788:
Warehouse picker and manager overview of ePick+ guided picking on Encompass Mobile: setup, filters, replenishment requests, bin corrections and changes vs. legacy ePick. Requires v25.01+ and ePick enabled.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

  • The "ePick" field on your site's Location record must be set to True.
    ​
    ​

  • Picking team members should have Employee Pick Teams records on their relevant Pick Teams.
    ​
    ​

  • Invoices should be palletized and processed to see them in ePick+.

Steps

Encompass has developed a guided picking experience called ePick+ for users on a digital device. This guide will walk you through its features and how to use them.

What is ePick+?

ePick+ is a digital solution for picking that integrates with handheld devices, allowing for a guided picking experience. It replaces older methods like paper picking and brings warehouse processes into a digital age. The tool offers more robust functionality, including an updated visual experience and simplified workflows.

  • Legacy vs. ePick+: The original tool, ePick (formerly Voice Pick), is being phased out. With the 25.09 release, ePick Legacy is no longer a supported tool, and Support will recommend using ePick+ to resolve any issues. In 25.10, ePick Legacy can still be accessed via custom Mobile Links, but will not be displayed in the Default view of Encompass Mobile. ePick Legacy will be removed from the system entirely in 26.01.
    ​
    Though no additional training is needed for ePick+ as the workflow is designed to be as similar as possible to the legacy version, this article serves as an overview of the tool, and reviews the most notable differences.
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • Goals and Motivations: The development of ePick+ was driven by four key goals:

    • Modernize: Provide an updated, intuitive look with critical information presented upfront.

    • Streamline and Focus: Adjust settings and processes to reduce unnecessary steps and confusion.

    • Diversify: Built on a new code structure, ePick+ allows access on a wider range of devices, including Android (e.g., Zebra WS50) in addition to iOS.

    • Safeguard: Most changes in the new code structure do not require a new mobile app version, which makes it easier to implement changes and release them at a quicker rate.

ePick+ Exclusive Features and How to Use Them

Here are the exclusive features in ePick+ and how they work:

1. Multi-Scan Prompt

This feature can be toggled on or off in the Settings menu. When a picker is picking the same product for multiple pallets, the system can be set to require a scan for each individual pick. Turning this off allows the picker to make one scan and then be prompted to pick the required quantity for each pallet.
​
​

2. Layer Prioritization

This setting re-sorts the pick sequence to place full-layer quantities first. This helps inexperienced pick team members build a more stable base for their pallets, leading to better transport and less potential for breakage. This can be toggled on even if you're not performing actual layer picking using special machinery.
​
​

3. Easier Navigation

Instead of repeatedly tapping the back button to return to the main page, users can now tap the menu in the top right corner to access the “Main Page” link. This allows navigation from anywhere in the picking process directly to the main screen.
​
​

4. Replenishment Requests

If there isn't enough inventory in a bin, pickers can create a replenish request on the fly. System Setting 527 allows you to control whether a prompt appears when a picker cuts a pick or skips it. The system will then create a replenishment move task that gets prioritized in the directed replenishment hierarchy.
​
​

5. Bin Inventory Correction

This feature allows a picker to reset bin inventory to zero if they make a quantity cut due to incorrect bin inventory. System Setting 3231 allows you to control whether a prompt will appear to ask if they want to count the current bin inventory to zero. This ensures the bin inventory is accurate and prevents other pickers from being directed to an empty bin. Bin Inventory corrections can be paired with Replenishment Requests to optimize pick bin inventory and time with product available.
​
​

6. Change Pick Bin

Controlled by the “Allow Bin Changes In ePick” field found on Pick Methods, pickers can now change the bin they are picking from. By tapping the bin location, they can see other bins and code dates with available inventory for that product. This helps reduce after-the-fact moves and keeps inventory accurate.

Best Practices

General Workflow and Tips

1. Accessing ePick+: Login to Encompass Mobile Warehouse. Find the picking section and select ePick+.

2. Using Filters: On the main page, you can filter by date, pallet type, and pick team. Pick Team selection is controlled by the Pick Teams assigned to the logged in Employee. These filters were previously found within ePick Settings in the legacy version of the tool.

3. Settings Menu: The menu in the top right corner gives you access to settings, and the Cognex camera scanner.

  • Upload Logs: If you experience an issue, use the "Upload logs" button at the top of the Settings page to send your data to developers to help them troubleshoot.

  • Default Printer: You can set a default printer for pallet tags, or leave it set to "None" to allow pickers to choose their printer at the end of each pallet.

Picking Process:

  • Clicking "Start Picking" is the same as the old "begin" button.

  • Before the first pick, a summary will be displayed showing the pallet's total cases and pallet type. All assigned pallets will be listed if picking more than one pallet at a time.

  • During picking, a progress bar shows the number of SKUs picked out of the total. The total number of units is also displayed at the top.

16989795:
Distributor steps to reconcile the AP Aging Report to the Trial Balance/Balance Sheet AP GL account: align dates, find when the variance began, and re-confirm Purchases paid via Check Run. Requires v25.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.10

Pre-Conditions

Financial Periods Closed: Both the AP Close and Financials Close processes should be completed for the period being compared (e.g., if comparing as of 9/30, both AP and Financials should be closed through 9/30). This is not always necessary depending on set filters for status.

Report Date Alignment: The Statement Date used for the Accounts Payable Aging Report must precisely match the date or period-end used for the General Ledger Trial Balance.

Correct Account Comparison: You must be comparing the Total of the Accounts Payable Aging Report to the balance of the designated Accounts Payable General Ledger Account (e.g., 1-00-2200-00 or similar).

Steps

  • Verify Period Closures: Confirm that both the AP Close and Financials Close processes have been run and completed for the period ending on the comparison date (e.g., month-end). Failure to close both can prevent certain transactions from generating or verifying the necessary General Ledger journal entries.

  • Ensure Date Consistency: Run the Accounts Payable Aging Report and the Trial Balance using the exact same period-end date. Even a slight difference can cause a variance due to how different reports pull data.

  • Find the Date the Discrepancy Began: Run both reports for consecutive prior periods (e.g., month-end) until they balance. The first date they don't balance is the date the variance started. This narrows down the transaction search.

  • Examine Transactions on the Discrepancy Date: On the date the variance began (from Step 3), examine all Purchase and Journal Entry transactions. Look specifically for:

    • Purchases that have been paid via a Check Run but are in a status (like Received or Ordered) that has not yet generated a Balanced Status journal entry.

    • Check Run journal entries that have posted to the General Ledger (verified) debiting AP, but the corresponding Purchase journal entry to credit AP has not posted.

    • In the provided example, the variance was a Purchase that was paid and verified via a Check Run (debiting GL) but was still in Received status, meaning the corresponding credit to the AP GL account had not yet posted.

  • Re-confirm the Affected Purchase Transaction: If a Purchase transaction is identified as the source of the variance (e.g., it was paid but not yet confirmed/balanced):

    • Reopen the AP period (if applicable and necessary).

    • Re-confirm the identified Purchase transaction(s) to ensure the balanced General Ledger entry is created and posted.

    • Re-close the AP period.

    • Re-run and compare the Trial Balance and Accounts Payable Aging Report.

  • Contact Support: If the variance persists after completing the above steps, you must contact support for advanced investigation. To ensure efficient troubleshooting, please provide the following information:

    • Exact variance amount and the date it occurred.

    • Exact error messages or codes encountered during closing or reporting (if any).

    • Screenshots or video recordings of the report criteria and the final totals.

    • The exact steps taken (including the specific Purchase and Check Run IDs) that led to the issue.

    • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

    • Any changes made to the system (e.g., new integrations, process changes, or setting updates) before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • Accounts Payable (AP) Aging Report A detailed report (the subsidiary ledger) listing all outstanding vendor invoices, organized by how long they are past due (aging buckets). The total should equal the General Ledger AP liability account balance.

  • Trial Balance (TB) A report listing all the General Ledger accounts and their debit/credit balances at a specific point in time. It's used to verify that the sum of all debits equals the sum of all credits.

  • General Ledger (GL) The main record-keeping system for a company's financial transactions, with all accounts (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, Expenses).

  • Subsidiary Ledger A detailed record supporting the summary balance in a General Ledger control account (e.g., the AP Aging Report is the subsidiary ledger for the Accounts Payable GL account).

  • AP Close The process that locks the Accounts Payable period, ensuring all related transactions are final for reporting.

  • Financials Close The process that locks the main General Ledger and financial statements for a given period.

  • Received Status (Purchase) A status on a Purchase transaction indicating the goods or services have been received, but the transaction may not have generated a full, Balanced Status journal entry yet.

  • Check Run A batch process used to select and pay multiple vendor invoices, which generates a corresponding journal entry to debit the AP liability account and credit the Cash account.

  • Balanced Status The status of a financial transaction (like a Purchase) that signifies a complete and balanced General Ledger journal entry has been created and is ready to post (credit to AP, debit to Inventory/Expense).

Best Practices

  • Routine Reconciliation: Make reconciling the AP Aging to the GL Trial Balance a routine, monthly process after the financial period is formally closed. This prevents small variances from accumulating and becoming difficult to trace.

  • Maintain Transaction Status Discipline: Always ensure that Purchase transactions are brought to a Confirmed status promptly, especially when they are tied to a payment. This ensures the subsidiary ledger and the general ledger are updated concurrently.

  • Review Payment Processes: If the variance is a recurring issue, review your Check Run or payment processes to confirm that payments are only being applied to Purchases that are ready to generate a balanced GL entry. Paying bills via a Check Run using a minimum status like Ordered or Received can frequently lead to this type of imbalance.

  • Utilize AP Close: It is suggested to run the AP Close process then the Financials Close for maximum integrity, as it finalizes the Accounts Payable sub-ledger.
16989796:
Troubleshooting for unexpected Average Costing: check CostingMethod, AvgLaidInCost on Inventory and PurchaseTrans layers, edits to old PdOs, then fix with the FIFO Adjustment tool and a manual FIFO adjustment invoice. Requires v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Pre-Conditions

The product in question must be configured to use Average Costing as its CostingMethod

Steps

  • Verify the CostingMethod: First, confirm that the product's CostingMethod is set to Average Costing on the Product Type.
    ​
    ​

  • Inspect the Inventory Table: Navigate to the inventory table for the specific product. The AvgLaidInCost field in this table reflects the system's calculated average cost. Compare this value to the laid-in cost shown on the invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • Review the Purchase Transactions: Examine the purchase transactions (PurchaseTrans) associated with the product. The system calculates the average laid-in cost based on the total value of all remaining inventory layers (Total FIFO Value) divided by the total remaining on-hand quantity (Sum (On Hand Remaining)). If recent edits to old production orders (PdOs) have restored inventory from older layers, this may be affecting the average cost.
    ​
    ​

  • Manually Adjust the Costing: If an incorrect cost layer is identified, use the FIFO Adjustment tool to correct it. Since the product is on average costing, the system will not automatically generate the adjustment invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • Create a Manual Invoice: After performing the FIFO adjustment, a "Pending FIFO Adjustment" will appear in the Inventory Valuation report. You must manually create a FIFO adjustment invoice to finalize the cost correction.

Fields And Definitions

  • CostingMethod: A product configuration field that determines how the system calculates the laid-in cost of an item. The options are FIFO, StandardCost, and Average Costing.
    ​
    ​

  • LaidInCost: The total cost of a product, including the purchase price and any additional fees, such as freight or duties.
    ​
    ​

  • AvgLaidInCost: The weighted average cost of a product, calculated by dividing the total value of remaining inventory by the total remaining on-hand quantity.
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO (First-In, First-Out): An inventory accounting method where the first items purchased are the first ones sold or used.
    ​
    ​

  • Production Order (PdO): A document used to manage the manufacturing process of a product.
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseTrans: The database table containing all purchase transactions, including LaidInCost data for individual inventory layers.
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO Adjustment Tool: A utility used to manually adjust the cost of specific inventory layers when there are discrepancies.

Best Practices

  • Avoid Editing Old Production Orders: Modifying old production orders can unpredictably restore inventory from outdated layers, which can distort the average laid-in cost and lead to incorrect accounting.
    ​
    ​

  • Regularly Review Inventory Valuation: Periodically check the Inventory Valuation report for any "Pending FIFO Adjustment" entries to ensure that all manual adjustments are finalized in a timely manner.
    ​
    ​

  • Understand Costing Methods: Be familiar with the differences between FIFO (First-In, First-Out) and Average Costing to anticipate how the system will handle inventory and cost calculations.

16989799:
Distributor steps for the Average Cost Adjustment (ACA) dashboard: reset a raw material's AvgLaidinCost, recalculate WIP and finished goods production orders, then revalue manually. Needs Purchase Cost Edit; v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Pre-Conditions

  • Must be using Average Costing method. This guide is not applicable for customers using the FIFO (First-In, First-Out) costing method.

  • Requires Purchase Cost Edit permission to access and execute cost adjustment dashboards.

  • The costing error must be related to a raw material or packaging product from a vendor purchase.

Steps

  • Identify the Problematic Product: First, identify the specific raw material or packaging product that has an incorrect average cost.

  • Reset the Average Cost: Use the Average Cost Adjustment (ACA) dashboard. Select the product and input the new, correct average cost that should be used moving forward. This action creates a purchase record to reset the Inventories.AvgLaidinCost.

    • Note: This step does not re-value on-hand inventory. It only corrects the average cost on the inventory record to prevent the bad average from affecting future production orders.

  • Recalculate WIP Products: Return to the ACA dashboard and search for all Work-in-Progress (WIP) products that consumed the raw material or packaging product you just adjusted. Recalculate these production orders to update their costs.

  • Recalculate Finished Goods (FGs): Repeat the process from the previous step for any finished goods (FGs) that consumed the adjusted raw material.

  • Perform Manual Revaluation: Unlike the FIFO method, there is no automatic adjustment invoice created for previously sold inventory. You must perform a manual revaluation to true up the cost of any inventory that was sold at the incorrect average cost.

Fields And Definitions

  • Average Costing: An inventory valuation method where the cost of goods sold and the ending inventory are valued at the weighted average cost of all inventory available for sale.

  • Inventories.AvgLaidinCost: A system field that stores the weighted average cost of a particular inventory item.

  • Work-in-Progress (WIP): Partially completed goods that are still in the production process.

  • Finished Goods (FG): Products that are completed and ready for sale.

  • Manual Revaluation: A process of manually adjusting the value of inventory in the accounting system to reflect a new, correct cost.

Best Practices

  • Use with Extreme Discretion: This dashboard is designed for handling large-scale production order recalculations stemming from a significant and material costing error.

  • Manual Revaluation is Required: Always remember that a manual revaluation is necessary to correct costs for previously sold inventory, as this tool does not automate that process for average costing.

  • Proactive Cost Management: The most effective way to avoid these issues is to ensure that vendor purchase costs are entered accurately from the start.
16989800:
Distributor steps for the Sub-distributor Sales Forecast dashboard: filter by Customer Type, group by product or customer, override and save forecasts, and read Forecast % and Total Forecast. Needs PurchasePOEdit/ForecastEdit; v25.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.07

Pre-Conditions

Requires forecast set up to be completed, see help resources for more information on forecasting.

To view the Sub-distributor Sales Forecast dashboard, users must have the 'PurchasePOEdit' permission.

To edit and save forecast data, users must have the 'ForecastEdit' permission.

Steps

Overview:

The Sub-distributor Sales Forecast dashboard allows you to analyze, adjust, and collaborate on sales forecasts for your sub-distributor customers. This ensures that purchasing decisions are based on the most accurate market demand information, preventing both overstocking and understocking of inventory.

Viewing and Analyzing Forecast Data

  1. Navigate to the Sub-distributor Sales Forecast Dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  2. Apply the necessary filters, such as Customer Type, Product, Supplier, or Purchase Agent. The Customer Type filter is required.
    ​
    ​

  3. Select how you want to group the data, either by Product or by Customer.
    ​
    ​

  4. Click the 'Search' button to load the forecast data based on your criteria.
    ​
    ​

  5. The dashboard will display the relevant forecast information, which can be reviewed and analyzed.

Updating and Saving Forecasts

  1. After loading the data, locate the product and customer row you wish to adjust.
    ​
    ​

  2. In the 'Forecast' column, click into the cell and override the existing value with the new forecast amount. The field must contain a numeric value; clearing it will set the forecast to 0.
    ​
    ​

  3. Once a value is modified, the cell will turn gray. The system will automatically recalculate the 'Total Forecast' and 'Forecast %' fields to reflect your change.
    ​
    ​

  4. After making all necessary adjustments, click the 'Save' button. This action will update the master forecast and lock the adjusted sales forecast from being automatically overwritten.
    ​
    ​

  5. You can also use the 'Export' and 'Print' buttons to create offline copies of the current view, or the 'Save Report' button to save your filter and view settings for future use.

Fields And Definitions

Filters and Options

  • Customer Type: (Required) Filter the report to only include customers of a specific type. Normally this shold be the customer type(s) of your distributor customers, such as 'Sub-distributor' or 'Sub-jobber'.
    ​
    ​

  • Show products with no customer history: A checkbox that, when selected, includes products that the filtered customers have not previously purchased. Using this option requires you to also apply a Product filter.
    ​
    ​

  • Group by: Organize the report data by either 'Product' or 'Customer' for different views of the forecast.
    ​
    ​

  • Zero Out Forecast: A button to set all currently displayed forecast values to zero.

Data Columns

  • Available: The current on-floor inventory minus any pre-sold or allocated quantities.
    ​
    ​

  • LY Sales: Last year's total sales for the product and customer during the same time period.
    ​
    ​

  • TY Sales: This year's total sales for the product and customer during the same time period.
    ​
    ​

  • Forecast: The system-generated or user-adjusted sales forecast for the specific product and customer. This field is editable.
    ​
    ​

  • Forecast %: The percentage that this customer's forecast represents out of the total forecast for the product. It is calculated as (Customer Forecast / Total Forecast) * 100.
    ​
    ​

  • Total LY Sales: The total sales for the product across all customers at that location during the same period last year.
    ​
    ​

  • Total Forecast: The total forecasted sales for the product at that location for the period, including all customer-specific adjustments.

Best Practices

  • To view products that a sub-distributor has never purchased before, check the 'Show products with no customer history' box. Remember to also apply a 'Product' filter when using this option to ensure the system returns data.
    ​
    ​

  • When you manually adjust a customer's 'Forecast' value, the system automatically recalculates the 'Total Forecast' for that product. Review this total to understand the full impact of your adjustment on purchasing needs.
    ​
    ​

  • Regularly save your work. If you navigate away from the page with unsaved changes, the system will prompt you to save before leaving.

Driver steps for completing the Vehicle Verification Survey in Encompass Mobile: open the event from My Day, scan cab and trailer barcodes, confirm vehicle changes with the server. Requires server setup first; v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Pre-Conditions

Complete the Vehicle Verification Survey - Server Setup

Steps

OBJECTIVE:

The purpose of this document is to outline the process of taking the Vehicle Verification Survey on the handheld. The Vehicle Verification survey is used to confirm the vehicle that is being used forthe day. This is important to make sure the DOT survey is taken forthe correct vehicle, and Fleet Tracker looking at the correct Plan.

Accessing the Vehicle Verification Objective
​
The Vehicle Verification Objective will be a part of the Event created by the Assignment Group. It will be listed in the user’s “My Day” page. This event will have the same name as the Assignment name that was created during the initial setup.


From the Encompass Mobile homepage:

  1. Click the “My Day” button
    ​
    ​

  2. In the My Day section, locate the Vehicle Verification event
    ​
    ​

  3. This event will have the same name as the assignment that was created during the initial setup
    ​
    ​

  4. Tap on the Event
    ​
    ​

  5. Locate the Vehicle Verification Event
    ​
    ​

  6. Tap on the Vehicle Verification task. It is possible that there may be multiple tasks in the event, such as DOT Survey, depending on how the assignment was configured

Completing the Vehicle Verification Objective
​
Within the Vehicle Verification Event, the user will be prompted to complete a vehicle verification. This will require the user to scan a vehicle barcode with their device’s camera.

  1. The barcode camera scanner will automatically open
    ​
    ​

  2. If this is the first time that the scanner has run on the device, you may be prompted to grant camera access to the Encompass Mobile application
    ​
    ​

  3. Hold the device so that the barcode lies within the crosshairs
    ​
    ​

  4. When the barcode has been accepted, the system will check the barcode against the expected vehicle. If the barcode is for a different vehicle than the one assigned, the user will be asked to confirm the change
    ​
    ​

  5. If the vehicle has a trailer, the user will be prompted to scan the trailer barcode after scanning the cab barcode
    ​
    ​

  6. After all barcodes have been scanned, the user will be prompted to confirm with the server
    ​
    ​

  7. The screen will return to the Vehicle Verification event
    ​
    ​

  8. The task will be marked with a blue-filled icon to denote that the task has been completed successfully
16989802:
Brewery reference in Encompass explaining the data source for each line of the TTB quarterly Brewers Report of Operations dashboard, incl. removals and cereal beverages. Requires v25.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.12

Steps

  • All calculations are based on data from a chosen Location and its related Tax Entity
    ​
    ​

  • All Invoice Load Sheets must be in Loaded, Balanced, or Verified status in order to populate on report
    ​
    ​

  • All Production Orders must be in Confirmed or Verified status in order to populate on report
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO Adjustment invoices as well as Inventory Adjustment invoices created without a TTB Tax Code are omitted from the report

Quarterly BRO
​
​
​

Additions to Beer Inventory
​
​

Line 1 - On hand beginning of this report period: Sum of Inventory on given start date of all Brands.TTB Category: Beer and Products with Product Type.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled
​

Line 2 - Beer produced by fermentation: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced brought into inventory through a Production Order
​

Line 3 - Beer received in bond: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled brought into inventory on a Purchase with positive NumUnits using Vendors with TTBTaxCode: Received in Bond or Purchase with Non-Production Order type Shipment (for example: imported purchase).

Line 4 - Beer returned to the brewery after removal from this brewery: Sum of Product with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled brought back into inventory on a negative Invoice which doesn't include reversal invoice

Line 5 - Physical inventory disclosed an overage: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled written out of inventory on an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Overage or Shortage
​

Line 6 - (not a standard BRO line) Packaged Products Out of Balance: Populates data when ttbOutput Product by Packaging Production Orders (Lines 25, 26) not equal Produced (WIP) Raw Material type component

Addition of water and other liquids: Not calculated. Additions of water and other liquids in ECP should be expressed by Production Orders

Line 8 - Total additions to inventory, plus beer on hand: The sum of Lines: 1 - 6

Removals from Beer Inventory
​
​

Line 10 - Removed for consumption or sale: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through a Non-Inventory Adjustment type Invoice with TTBTaxCode: None

- And Removed tax-determined for consumption or sale to tavern on brewery premises: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Tavern on Brewery Premises

Line 11 - Beer removed without payment of tax as outlined under Subpart L of 27 CFR part 25: Removed without payment of tax for export: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Export
​

- And Removed without payment of tax for use as supplies (vessels/aircraft): Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Used as Supplies
​

- And Removed without payment of tax for use in research and development: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Research and Development
​

- And Removed without payment of tax to other breweries and pilot brewing plants of same ownership: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Removed Without Payment of Tax to Other Brewery
​

- And Removed without payment of tax as beer unfit for sale removed for use in manufacturing: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Unfit for Sale

Line 12 - Beer consumed on premises: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Consumed on Premise

Line 13 - Beer destroyed at brewery: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Destroyed

Line 14 - Losses, including theft: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Loss.

Columns C and E also include Bulk Beer Loss (Consume as Component (Wasted Raw Material)) trans for Racking and Bottling.
​

Line 15 - Physical inventory disclosed a shortage: Sum of Product with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled written into inventory on an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Overage or Shortage

Line 16 - (not a standard BRO line): Populates data in situations where the BBLs consumed and received on a repackaging Production Order do not match.

Line 17 - Total amount of beeron hand at end of quarter: Sum of Inventory on given end date of all Brands.TTB Category: Beer and Products with Product Type.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled

Line 19 - Total Beer: The Sum of Lines 10 - 17

Part 2 - Cereal Beverage Summary
​
​

Line 1 - Produced: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced brought into inventory through a Production
​

Line 2 - Removed: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled, removed from inventory through an Invoice
​

Line 3 - Loss and Wastage: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Loss

Line 4 - Received: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled brought into inventory on a Purchase with positive NumUnits using

Vendors with TTBTaxCode: Received in Bond
​

Line 6 - Total on hand at end of period: Sum of Inventory on given end date of all Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and Products with Product Type.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled
16989803:
Producer steps for the Production Order FIFO Cost Adjustment: fix wrong raw material or packaging costs, recalculate In-Progress/Balanced production orders, and the overnight FIFO layer recalc. FIFO only; needs Purchase Cost Edit; v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Pre-Conditions

  • Must be using FIFO (First-In, First-Out) costing method. This tool is not applicable for customers using the Average Costing method.

  • Production Orders must be in an In-Progress or Balanced status to be eligible for recalculation.

  • Requires Purchase Cost Edit permission to access and execute cost adjustment tools and dashboards.

  • The costing error must be related to raw materials or packaging from a vendor purchase that has already been consumed by production orders.

  • The user must have a complete understanding of their inventory flow to ensure the correct products and dates are selected.

Steps

  • Identify the Source of the Costing Error: Before making any adjustments, pinpoint the specific vendor purchase and the raw material or packaging product that has the incorrect cost.

  • Adjust the Raw Material Cost: Utilize the designated FIFO Cost Adjustment tool to correct the cost of the raw material or packaging product. This step updates the original cost layer.

  • Run the Production Order FIFO Cost Adjustment: Navigate to the Production Order FIFO Cost Adjustment dashboard. Use this tool to automatically recalculate the costs of all production orders that consumed inventory from the updated FIFO layers within the specified date range.

  • Allow for Overnight Recalculation: The Recalculate Inventory FIFO Layers process runs overnight. This process automatically creates a FIFO adjustment for any finished goods (FGs) that were sold at the incorrect, previous cost.

  • Validate the Changes: After the overnight process is complete, review the affected production orders and sales records to ensure the costs have been correctly adjusted. Check for accuracy and consistency across the relevant financial reports.

Fields And Definitions

  • FIFO (First-In, First-Out) Costing: An inventory valuation method where the first goods purchased or produced are the first ones sold.The cost of the oldest inventory is expensed first.

  • Production Order: A document used to track the manufacturing process and the associated costs of producing a finished good.

  • FIFO Adjustment: An accounting entry or process that corrects the cost of inventory layers to reflect accurate purchase costs.

  • Recalculate Inventory FIFO Layers: An automated, overnight system process that recalculates and adjusts the cost of inventory layers based on manual corrections, generating necessary adjustment invoices for any sold inventory.

  • Finished Goods (FG): Products that are completed and ready for sale.

Best Practices

  • Use with Extreme Discretion: This tool is intended for correcting significant and material costing errors. Avoid using it for minor or routine adjustments.

  • Verify Before Execution: Always double-check the raw material, date ranges, and other parameters before running the adjustment tool to prevent unintended changes to production order costs.

  • Maintain Accurate Vendor Data: Proactively ensure that vendor purchase costs are accurate at the time of entry to prevent the need for these large-scale adjustments.

  • Understand Your Costing Method: Regularly review and understand the implications of your chosen costing method (FIFO vs. Average) on inventory and production order valuations.

Distributor setup steps for the Vehicle Verification survey: set Detachable Trailer, print vehicle/trailer barcodes, add Assignment Groups, Assignments and the objective, then assign to Routes. Requires v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Steps

The purpose of this document is to outline the method for setting up the Vehicle Verification survey. The Vehicle Verification survey is used to confirm the vehicle that is being used forthe day. This is important to make sure the DOT Survey is taken forthe correct vehicle, and that Fleet Trackeris looking at the correct Plan. If you need to set up a DOT Survey, start with the knowledge document “Encompass on Tap: DOT Vehicle Inspection Survey Set-Up”

Updating Trailer and Vehicle records - Defining whether the vehicle has a detachable trailer will cause the Vehicle Verification function to require the user to verify the trailer barcode as well as the vehicle barcode.

  1. Navigate to the ‘Vehicles’ table using the search bar in the top-left corner of the window

  2. Select the vehicle to be adjusted by clicking the arrow icon

  3. Click the pencil icon to edit the record for the vehicle selected

  4. Click the ‘Detachable Trailer’ dropdown fielda. Select ‘True’ if the user will be required to scan a separate trailer barcodeb. Select ‘False’ if the user will not be required to scan a separate trailer barcode

  5. Save Changes

  6. Repeat for each vehicle that requires adjustment

Print Vehicle and Trailer Barcodes - Use the Encompass Bar Code tool to print vehicle barcodes so the driver can scan them to verify the vehicle and trailer they are using.

  1. Navigate to the ‘Bar Codes’ tool by searching in the top-left search bar

  2. Click the ‘Vehicle Bar Codes’ tab

  3. Print Bar Codes for the Vehicles and Vehicle Trailers

  4. Select the appropriate location for the vehicle barcodes to be printed

  5. Select the print type
    -- Vehicle Label will print each vehicle barcode on a standard 8½” x 11” page
    -- Vehicle Label 2x1 will print multiple barcodes on one page
    -- Vehicle Trailer Label will print each trailer barcode on a standard 8½” x 11” page

  6. Click ‘Search’

  7. Select the checkbox of the vehicles that will be required to be verified

  8. Select the number of barcodes to print for each vehicle or trailer (the default is 1)

  9. Click ‘Print Labels’

  10. In the PDF frame, click the download icon or the printer icon to print directly from the browser
    -- It is recommended to download the PDF file as the system print dialog often provides more options to ensure an accurate print

  11. It is recommended to laminate the bar codes

  12. Place the printed vehicle label on the door jam of the driver’s door

  13. Place the printed trailer label in the first bin on the driver-side if the trailer is a side loader. If the trailer is an end loader place the label on the driver-side and out of the weather

Adding an Assignment Group - An assignment group can be used to apply various assignments to a route. An example of an Assignment Group could be called ‘Delivery DOT Compliance’. If an assignment group already exists, refer to ‘Adding an Assignment’.

  1. Navigate to the ‘Assignment Groups’ table using the search bar in the top-left corner of the window

  2. Click the ‘Add Assignment Groups’ button at the top of the window
    -- Input a name that is descriptive of the group, e.g. “DOT w/Vehicle Verification”

Adding an Assignment - An assignment is a collection of assignment objectives. An example of Assignments are Pre-Trips, Post-Trips, Breaks, Meals, and Meetings. The assignment governs when the task starts and ends as well as the duration. If an assignment already exists, refer to ‘Adding the Vehicle Verification Objective to an existing Assignment’.

  1. Navigate to the ‘Assignments’ table using the search bar in the top-left corner of thewindow

  2. Click the green ‘Add Assignments’ button at the top of the window
    -- In the ‘Assignment Group’ field, select the group created in the previous section
    -- Select a name that is descriptive of the group, e.g. “Pre-Trip”
    -- Set either static start/end times or dynamic timing using ‘Planned Start’
    -- If using ‘Planned Start’ set the timing and duration to what the user requires tocomplete the process
    -- Add Record

Add the Vehicle Verification Objective to an existing Assignment - The Vehicle Verification Objective will require the driver to scan a barcode in the vehicle, and trailer, if applicable, with the handheld device camera. This can be added to the existing Assignment of Pre-Trip.

  1. From the new assignment or the existing assignment, click the ‘Add AssignmentObjectives’ button. If the button is not present on the screen, click the black ‘Sub Tables’ dropdownmenu and select ‘Assignment Objectives’

  2. Complete the fields for the new Assignment Objective
    -- In the ‘Objective’ field, select the ‘Vehicle Verification’ option by typing in the fieldand selecting the option from the list
    -- Set the ‘Required’ field to ‘True’; this will remind users that they must completethis required task.
    -- Set the ‘Sequence’ field to ‘0’ or ‘1’; this sequence number must be the lowest ofall other assignment objectives in the assignment to ensure the vehicle is verifiedbefore the DOT survey is taken.

Add Assignment Group to Route - Once the assignment group has been created and configured correctly, the assignment group must be assigned to routes so the objectives apply to the routes.

  1. Navigate to the ‘Routes’ table using the search bar in the top-left corner of the window

  2. Filter routes as necessary to view the routes that you will require to complete vehicleverification

  3. If not already visible, add the ‘Assignment Group’ column by clicking the‘Columns’ dropdown menu, ticking the box labeled ‘Assignment Group”, thenclicking ‘Create View’

  4. Set the ‘Assignment Group’ in the following ways:
    -- Click the pencil icon on the row of the individual record you are trying to edit or use Column Edit and Fill Down functions
    -- Click ‘Save Changes’ when done

Video plus steps for distributors drawing boundaries on the Geocoding dashboard in Encompass (territories, distribution, charge or deposit areas) and assigning customers inside them. Requires v22.01+.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Create Different Boundary Areas
​
​

1. Using the Universal Search, Navigate to the Geocoding dashboard.
​
​

2. The boundary type defaults to Territories
​
​

  • The Territories dropdown shows different boundary options:
    ​
    - Territories: designated boundary area of customer locations
    ​
    - Distribution Areas: designated boundary based on distribution limits
    ​
    - Counties: boundaries set by County lines
    ​
    - Charge Areas: typically used for tax reasons
    ​
    - Deposit Areas: typically used for invoice reasons
    ​
    ​

3. Click the Draw Polygon option.
​
4. This gives users the option to draw the boundary in any shape.
​
5. Click Assign To Boundaries drop down and choose the boundary name needed.

​ Note: The boundaries available to assign to customers depend on the specific boundary type (ie. Territories, Distribution Areas, Charge Areas, Deposit Areas)

6. Click Save.
​
7. Click To Selected Territory under Assign Customers to assign the territory.
​
8. The next screen shows a list of customers with their current and new territory.
​
9. Click Confirm.
​
10. The Territory field is updated on the Customer’s record.
​
​ Note: The fields updated in the Customers record will depend on the boundary type selected (example: Distribution Areas boundary type will be the Distribution Area field).

Steps

How to Update a Customer Geocode Location

1. Using the Universal Search, navigate to the "Customer Search" dasboard.
​
2. Search for the intended customer using the filter criteria.
​
3. Click Search.
​
4. Arrow into the customer record.
​
5. Click the Map button.
​
6. This brings users to the interactive map with the customer’s map points showing.
​
7. Either drag/drop the pin to the new location or type in an address in the address bar to update the Geocode Location.

​ Note: This is useful when the customer has a different delivery location than their regular office location.

8. Click Save.
​
9. This brings users back to the Customer’s record. The longitude and latitude points will update and the GPS Accuracy field will change to Manually Set.
​
​ Note: Setting GPS Accuracy to "Manually Set" creates a manual override, stopping the API_1069 from automatically updating this information

16989821:
Explains the 99 Bottles 894 process: dsdlink receives distributor EDI 894 pre-delivery notices, creates dsdlink Orders, and sends a daily CSV to ABC boards; covers statuses and required fields. Needs EDI connection; v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • The following document assumes the trading partner already has an EDI connection setup with Encompass and/or Non-Encompass RAS.

Steps

Many ABC boards are not able to process EDI files. For this reason, Encompass has partnered with 99 Bottles to help deliver their 894 pre-delivery notices to ABC board customers. We do this by receiving 99 Bottles EDI files (894) and translating them into a CSV file via a Fusion Report. We then send this CSV file to the relevant ABC board.
​
​
1. Distributor creates an invoice in their RAS system (both Encompass and non-Encompass distributors are participating in this process).
​
​

2. At the appropriate time, the RAS system generates one or more EDI 894 documents and sends these to Encompass, which is process in dsdlink. A single 894 document can contain data for one or more invoices. Example: Documents.
​
​

3. 894 processing in dsdlink creates a dsdlink Order/OrderTrans for each invoice called out in the 894 document. When created, the dsdlink Order is set to Status = Received 894 from Distributor.
​
​

4. One per day, a scheduled task is executed on dsdlink that will generate a single CSV file containing all the Order/Invoice information from all dsdlink Order where Status = Received 894 from Distributor. Example: dsdlink Orders.
​
​

5. CSV file is submitted to 99 Bottles.
​
​

6. All dsdlink Orders participating in Step 4 above have their status changed to Status = Sent 894 to Retailer.

Fields And Definitions

  • EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) - business-to-business exchange of essential organizational documents (Purchase Order, Remittance, etc...).
    ​
    ​

  • Exchange Configuration -stores all necessary information relevant to file transfer (Mailbox, ISA IDs, Functional Type, etc…) Example: Exchange Configurations.
    ​
    ​

  • Exchange Task - a collection of invoices, pricing exports, etc., packaged into a single file, all of which is documented here.

Best Practices

If something is not going as expected, check first to see if the inbound 894 EDI file was processed successfully. Exchange Task in the warning status will point to data issues in the file data coming from the distributor.
​
Values that are required (outside of the standard set) in the inbound file that need to be transmitted to 99Bottles/ABC:
​
​

  • Invoice Num (G82_02)
    ​
    ​

  • DUNS = 407851000 (G82_03)<br style="box-sizing: inherit; color: #202020; font-family: 'Open S

16989829:
Distributor steps for Promotions Zones and Promotions Customers: add zones in the Zones table, attach chains, add Customers Promotions Zones, link single customers to a promotion, and when to use each. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Zones Overview

Promotions Zones allow you to connect a group of customers to a single promotion. By grouping customers with similar characteristics into a reusable zone, you can quickly and flexibly apply unique pricing for specific periods. Examples of common Zones might be Military, Chain-Specific, or Geographically based. A Promotions Zone can be further grouped under a Market or it can be used on a Promotion, depending on internal processes or preferences for Promotion management.

Customers can belong to multiple Promotions Zones, and each Zone can contain many customers. For example, a single liquor store might be in zones for their county, their city, and for all independent stores. This flexibility allows Encompass to apply the lowest qualifying price across all promotions a customer is eligible for.

How to Add Zones and Customers

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Zones table
​
​

2. Review existing Zones
​
​

a. Use the Arrow icon to view an individual Zone record
​
​

b. Click the Edit button or icon to edit the whole record or a single field
​
​

c. Save changes when complete
​
​

3. To add a new Zone, click Add Zones button
​
​

  • Enter Promo Zone name
    ​
    ​

  • Toggling the switch means all new customers will automatically be added to this zone
    ​
    ​

  • Click Add Record
    ​
    ​

4. Do you want to add one or more chains to this zone?
​
​

  • If Yes, search for Chains in the universal search bar
    ​
    ​

  • Select the chain and click the Pencil icon to edit, and attach it to a zone
    ​
    ​

  • Select the Zone and click Save Changes
    ​
    ​

5. To add a Customers Promotions Zone, click the Sub Tables button and select Customers Promotions Zones
​
​

6. Click the Add Customers Promotions Zones button
​
​

a. Search and select Customer
​
​

b. Start Date is set to Today and determines when the Customer qualifies for Promotions tied to this Zone; modify this field if needed
​
​

c. Click to Add Record
​
​

NOTE: If you have multiple customers to add to a zone, consider using a Table Import.

Promotions Customers Overview

Promotions Customers connect a single customer directly to a promotion. This is most effective for unique pricing scenarios that don't apply to a wider group, such as for samples, donations, or special negotiated rates. Using Promotions Customers saves time by directly applying pricing to a single customer, rather than creating a separate group for just one or two individuals.

How to Add Promotions Customers

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Promotions table
​
2. Search and Select a Promotion to view
​
3. Find (or add) the Promotions Customers sub table
​
4. Reivew and add Promotions Customers, as needed to tie individual Customers to the Promotion via the "Add Promotions Customers" button
​

Promotions Zones or Promotions Customers?
​

Q: How do I know when to use Promotions Zones versus Promotions Customers?

A: The choice between Promotions Zones and Promotions Customers comes down to efficiency: whether you need to apply a promotion to a large group of customers or to a unique, individual customer.

Promotions Zones

Use Promotions Zones when you want to apply a promotion to a large group of customers who share a common characteristic, like a specific chain or location. This is the most efficient method for promotions that will apply to many people. By putting customers into a zone, you can connect the entire group to a promotion with a single record, saving you from having to make dozens or even hundreds of individual connections.

Promotions Customers

Use Promotions Customers for unique, single-customer pricing scenarios. This is the ideal choice when a promotion applies to only one or a few customers, such as for a donation, sample, or negotiated pricing. Instead of creating a zone for a single customer—which would require extra steps—you can connect that customer directly to the promotion, making the process faster and more direct.

16989837:
Distributor steps for survey based pricing: link a promotion to a Yes/No objective survey (Prompt Task Invoice Total) and objective schedule via Zone Survey Rules, e.g. display discounts. Needs Objectives/Promotions edit; v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

  • You must have the necessary permissions to create and update Objectives and Surveys, as well as Promotions.
    ​
    ​

  • You must have an understanding of the relationship between promotions, objectives, objective schedules, and zone survey rules.

Steps

  1. Define the logic and confirm survey based pricing is needed: Start by thinking about what logic you would like to occur with survey based pricing. Sometimes you do not need to use surveys and can instead use regular promotion qualifications.

  2. Create the Promotion:

    • Add a new promotion and select the relevant Market.

    • From the drop-down menu, select the Line of products you created in the previous step.

    • Set the Amount of the discount.

    • Set the Start Date and End Date for the promotion.

  3. Create a New Objective:

    • Navigate to the Objectives section and create a new objective.

    • Set the Assigned To Group to Salesman.

    • Add a Survey Question (e.g., "Is there any type of Leinenkugel display?") and set the Data Type to Yes/No.

    • Set the Prompt Task to Invoice Total to ensure the survey appears after the user backs out of the Invoice Edit Screen.

  4. Set Up the Objective Schedule:

    • Add an objective schedule to define when the survey will be prompted.

    • Configure the Frequency (e.g., "Every Visit") and set the Start Date and End Date to match the promotion dates.

  5. Add Zone Survey Rules:

    • Go to the Zone Survey Rules table to tie the promotion and survey together.

    • Select the Promo Zone and the Survey Question you created.

    • In the Answer field, type the value that corresponds to a "Yes" answer (typically "1").

    • Set the Expire After Days to define how long the deal will remain active after the initial invoice.

  6. If you encounter issues, contact support and provide the exact error messages or codes, screenshots of the configuration, and the steps taken to set up the promotion and survey.

Fields And Definitions

What is Zone Survey Rules?

Zone Survey Rules link a promotion to a survey question and answer, allowing for dynamic pricing based on a survey response. The rules determine when a discount should be applied.

Use Cases

  • Giving a discount when a display is present: For example, a salesperson can answer "Yes" to a survey question asking if a Leinenkugel's display is in the store, and a $1.50 discount is then applied to the invoice for all Leinenkugel's products.

  • First-time buyer discounts: A customer who is a first-time buyer of any products could receive a 15% discount after a survey confirms their status.

  • Enforcing contracts and "What If" pricing: You can use Zone Survey Rules to enforce a contract with a retailer, such as a "Red Bull VIP" contract, or to demonstrate different pricing scenarios to a customer.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Fields and Definitions

  • Objective: A series of tasks or questions used to gather information, such as whether a customer has a product display.

  • Promotion: A pricing rule that applies a discount or other offer under specific conditions, which can be linked to a survey.

  • Objective Schedule: A configuration that dictates when a survey will be prompted to a user.

  • Zone Survey Rules: A set of conditions that link a survey answer to a promotion, enabling dynamic pricing.

  • Prompt Task: A setting that determines when a survey will appear on an Encompass Mobile device. For survey-based pricing, this is set to
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Total to trigger the survey after an order is entered.

  • Line: A grouping of products that allows a promotion or survey to apply to multiple items at once.

Best Practices

  • Always test new surveys on the Encompass Server before rolling them out to mobile users.

  • Set the Auto Fail Tasks After Deadline to "True" for scheduled surveys to prevent them from becoming stale.

  • Make sure that the Start/End Dates for the Objective Schedule match the Promotion Start/End Dates.

  • If no location is set at the Market level and you have multiple locations, ensure a Promotion Location is tied to the Promotion.

16989841:
Explains the Brand Strength Index in Encompass: the weighted weekly-recalculated score for comparing brands, with its formula using potential buyers, 13-week buyers, placements, sales and growth metrics. Requires v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

Brand Strength Index is a weighted sum of sales data that results in a single numerical value that can be used to compare brands to each other. This value is recalculated each weekend.

Steps

Below is the overall calculation. Some of the variables below are defined in the 'Fields and Definitions' section of this Help Resource

(WHEN PotentialBuyers < 100 THEN 0 ELSE 1.0) * WeeklySalesPerPotentialBuyers

+

(WHEN Buyers13Week / PotentialBuyers < 0.01 OR Buyers13Week < 10 THEN 0

WHEN Buyers13Week / PotentialBuyers < 0.10 THEN 0.25

ELSE 0.5) * (WeeklySalesPerBuyers + WeeklySalesPerPlacements)

+

(WHEN Buyers13Week / PotentialBuyers < 0.01 THEN 0 ELSE 1.0) * (BuyerGrowth13WeekSales + PlacementGrowth13WeekSales + SalesGrowth13Week + SalesGrowthLastYear13Week)

Fields And Definitions

  • WeeklySalesPerPotentialBuyers = Sales13Week / 13 / PotentialBuyers

  • WeeklySalesPerBuyers = Sales13Week / 13 / Buyers13Week

  • WeeklySalesPerPlacements = Sales13Week / 13 / Placements13Week

  • BuyerGrowth13WeekSales = Buyers13WeekChange / Buyers13Week * Sales13Week / 13 / Buyers13Week

  • PlacementGrowth13WeekSales = Placements13WeekChange / Placements13Week * Sales13Week / 13 / Placements13Week

  • SalesGrowth13Week = Sales13WeekChange / 13 / Buyers13Week

  • SalesGrowthLastYear13Week = SalesLastYear13WeekChange / 13 / Buyers13Week

1. Navigate to the App Library using the Universal Search bar.
​
2. Search for Dock Time Calendar for Carrier in the search bar and click on the app.
​
3. Click the "Install" button.
​
4. The app includes a dashboard that will allow your employees to invite carrier users to access your dock time calendar. Select the Roles that you want to have permission to invite users.
​
5. Set the Allow Carriers to Add Shipments field. Allowing carriers to add shipments gives carriers access to an Add Shipment button from the dock time calendar.
​
​

  • Select True to allow carriers to add a shipment when the shipment or purchase does not yet exist on your Encompass site.
    ​
    ​

  • Note that this setting can be changed later on from the App Library.

6. Set the Appointment Lead Time Days. This will define a mandatory advance period for scheduling appointments from DSDLink Dock Time Calendar.

  • The default value is 0, which means there is no lead time requirement.

  • If you want to enforce a longer lead time (e.g., 1 day), update the setting to your desired value. For example, setting it to 1 will require appointments to be scheduled for the next day or later.

7. Check to agree to the conditions of installing the app and click "Install Dock Time Calendar for Carrier".
​
8. A message will display indicating that the app has been successfully installed. Click on "Ok."

Also know that carriers will have access to all docks where the 'private dock' field is false. If you want restrict carriers from scheduling appointments on a dock from DSDLink Dock Time Calendar, it can be marked as a private dock either from the docks table or by editing the dock from your local Dock Time Calendar.

16989857:
Explains packaging run rates in Encompass production: how setup/lead time and packages per hour per pack type set packaging line run time. Needs Batch Management and Batch Processing (SystemSetting553); v22.05+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.05

Pre-Conditions

  • Site is a Production site that has Batch Management and Batch Processing turned on (SystemSetting553=True)
    ​
    ​

  • Packages have been set up for all Finished Goods to be produced
    ​
    ​

  • Packaging Equipment has been built

Steps

Packaging Run Rates are used to calculate run time for packaging orders in Encompass.

The system will calculate: LeadTime + (ProductionOrders.PlannedUnits/PackagesPerHour)=x

Example: A Packaging run rate for a canning Line is set to 100 units of 2/12 pack/12oz Cans per hour with a 20 minute lead time:

Screenshot

When a Packaging for 500 cases of 2/12 pack/12oz cans is scheduled, the canning line will be considered in use for 5 hours and 20 minutes: 20min+(500cases/100csper hour):

Screenshot

Packaging run rates will need to be set for every Pack Type that will be run on a packaging line.

Fields And Definitions

  • Setup Time: The time it takes to set up the packaging line before packaging can begin

  • Packages per Hour: the number of units of a certain package type that the packaging line can produce per hour

Best Practices

  • Packaging Run rates are calculated in minutes

  • Packaging lines can be double booked; this will not prevent operators from performing their tasks.

  • Do not sweat perfecting run rates; they are used to get a general idea of what kind of time blocks a packaging run will take. Actual packaging times in real life change often and will not prevent operators from performing their tasks.
16989858:
Producer steps for adding Equipment (tanks, barrels, packaging lines) used in Production: Equipment Type, UoM, Write Off Threshold, Completed Bin, TTB DRO Account and auto barrel numbering. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • All Production must be mapped through Equipment. Users need to add in correctly configured Equipment to be able to process Production

Steps

Creating the Equipment
​
​

  1. Navigate to the Equipment table
    ​
    ​

  2. Click the Add Equipment button
    ​
    ​

  3. Name the Equipment and Number it if desired
    ​
    ​

  4. Choose the Equipment Type that will determine how this Equipment can be used
    ​
    ​

  5. Select the Location
    ​
    ​

  6. Select the Unit of Measure (UoM) that will measure this equipments capacity
    ​
    ​

  7. Set a Write Off Threshold if desired. Write Off Threshold will prompt Users to write off remaining inventory in a tank after a batch has been processed if the remaining volume is less than the threshold set in this field.
    ​
    ​

  8. For Packaging Lines only, set the Completed Bin that all finished goods will be sent to once they are completed
    ​
    ​

  9. For Spirit Producers Only, set the TTB DRO Account to the report this equipment belongs to
    ​
    ​

  10. Click the Add Record button

Fields And Definitions

Bin Name Alignment: When new equipment is created, the system now automatically sets the Bin Name to match the Equipment Name (up to 15 characters). If the Equipment Name is later updated, the Bin Name will be updated as well to stay in sync.

Sequential Barrel Numbering: For equipment types designated as 'Barrels' , the system now automatically assigns Equipment Num based on sequential ordering from the last barrel added. This ensures barrel numbers are contiguous and easy to manage for reporting.

Flexibility: Users can still manually assign an Equipment Num during creation if specific requirements exist; the system will prioritize user-defined numbers and only apply sequential logic if no number is provided.
