Distributor reference for OrderIQ suggested order settings: order_size, round_threshold, Suggested Order Limitations, Tweedie loss function, EnablePOSData and Enable Layer Round. Needs OrderIQ app; v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Pre-Conditions

Before configuring OrderIQ, ensure the following are in place to allow for certain features:

  • Install OrderIQ App: OrderIQ App is installed and suggested order configurations are enabled and configured for accounts

  • Retail Insights Data Connection: For leveraging POS data, a connection to Retail Insights must be active. This ensures the Handoff Product Inventory Daily Trace table is populating with data.

  • Inventory Layer Thresholds: To enable rounding to the next layer or pallet, the promptLayerThreshold must be set up for relevant products in the Inventory table.

Steps

OrderIQ is a solution that provides tailored product suggestions to users. It has several configuration parameters that allow for granular control over how these suggestions are generated. These parameters help optimize inventory and streamline the ordering process.

Granular Order Size Control

The order_size parameter allows users to control the size of a suggested order.

How it Works

  • It uses a percentage list (e.g., 0.5;0.4) to distribute a predicted weekly order across multiple delivery stops.

  • The default value is 1, which corresponds to a 100% order.

  • If you set order_size to 1.2 (120%), OrderIQ will recommend an order that is 120% of a standard order.

How to Configure

  1. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configuration dashboard.

  2. Update the order_size parameter.

  3. The value can be a percentage list or a single decimal.

  4. If the number of delivery stops is less than the number of percentages listed, the remaining percentages are summed and applied to the last delivery stop.

Adjustable Rounding Thresholds

The round_threshold parameter dictates how predicted quantities are rounded up or down.

How it Works

  • It is a decimal value between 0 and 1.

  • A higher round_threshold increases the confidence required to add the next incremental case, which is useful if you have a high product removal rate.

  • A lower round_threshold makes it easier to add the next incremental case, which is helpful if you have a high product addition rate.

  • For products designated as 'Sell By Case Only,' predicted quantities are converted to cases, rounded using the specific threshold, and then converted back to units for precise suggestions.

How to Configure

  1. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configuration dashboard.

  2. Update the round_threshold with a decimal value between 0 and 1.

  3. This setting ensures that suggestions align with your desired ordering patterns.

Product Type-Specific Customizations

You can apply unique order_size and round_threshold settings for specific products or product types.

How it Works

  • Specific settings for a product, product type or product type code take precedence over the general configurations.

  • For products designated as 'Sell By Case Only,' predicted quantities are converted to cases, rounded using the specific threshold, and then converted back to units for precise suggestions.

How to Configure

  1. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configurations table.

  2. Select the sub-table Suggested Order Limitations.

  3. Click Add Suggested Order Limitations.

  4. Add a product type, product, or product type code.

  5. Update the order_size or round_threshold parameters for the selected items.

  6. Click Add Record.

Loss Function

OrderIQ offers different loss functions to improve prediction accuracy.

How it Works

  • A loss function measures the difference between the predicted and actual values.

  • The default option (Squared Error) is a "one-size-fits-all" approach that treats all errors the same. This can sometimes lead to unnecessary small orders or under-forecasting of large orders.

  • The Tweedie Loss function is specialized for products with high instances of zero sales mixed with occasional large orders, a common pattern in beer distribution. It is better at recognizing patterns of zero sales and large, infrequent orders, leading to more accurate forecasts and fewer unnecessary orders for slow-moving products.

How to Configure

  1. Navigate to the OrderIQ app in the Encompass App Library.

  2. View the app settings.

  3. Update the Loss Function to reg:tweedie.

  4. Click Save Settings.

POS Data Integration

Integrating Point-of-Sale (POS) data can significantly boost the precision and reliability of order suggestions.

How it Works

  • By including historical POS sales and inventory metrics, the system can deliver more accurate forecasts.

  • This feature is controlled by the EnablePOSData parameter in the Suggested Order Configuration table.

  • The available options are:

    • False: Excludes all POS data.

    • Include POS Sales: Incorporates only retail sales data into the model.

    • Include POS Sales & Inventory: Includes both retail sales and inventory data. Note that this requires accurate inventory data.

How to Configure

  1. Ensure a Retail Insights Data connection is active and the Handoff Product Inventory Daily Trace table is populated.

  2. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configuration table.

  3. Update the Enable POS Data column to one of the three options.

Operational Packing Units

This feature automatically rounds suggested order quantities to the nearest full layer or pallet.

How it Works

  • It leverages existing system configurations for product packing and inventory thresholds.

  • The feature uses the inventory.promptLayerThreshold to determine when to round a suggested value to the next layer.

  • When a product's recommended order is greater than or equal to its prompt order layer threshold, OrderIQ will round the quantity up to the next layer. This ensures that recommended orders align with operational packing requirements.

How to Configure

  1. Go to the Inventory table and set up the prompt layer threshold for the products you wish to round.

  2. Navigate to the Suggested Order Configurations table.

  3. Set Enable Layer Round to True for OrderIQ accounts.

Fields And Definitions

order_size: A percentage value or a list of percentages that controls how predicted orders are scaled and distributed across multiple deliveries. A value of 1.2 suggests 120% of a standard order.

round_threshold: A decimal between 0 and 1 that sets the confidence level for rounding predicted quantities. A higher value reduces the chance of rounding up to the next case, while a lower value increases the likelihood to add the next case.

Loss Function: The mathematical method used by the AI model to calculate prediction errors.

  • Squared Error (Default): A general-purpose loss function that treats all errors equally.

  • Tweedie Loss: A specialized loss function designed for data with many zero values and occasional large spikes, common in beer distribution.

EnablePOSData: A configuration setting that dictates whether to include POS data in the OrderIQ model.

  • False: Excludes POS data.

  • Include POS Sales: Integrates only retail sales data.

  • Include POS Sales & Inventory: Includes both sales and inventory data.

Enable Layer Round: A boolean (True/False) setting that, when enabled, automatically rounds suggested quantities to the nearest full layer or pallet based on the promptLayerThreshold.

Best Practices

  • Start with Defaults: Begin with the default settings and observe performance before making extensive changes. This provides a baseline for evaluating the impact of your customizations.

  • Use Tweedie Loss for Specific Patterns: If your business has many products with zero sales on most days and occasional large orders (e.g., craft beers), switch the Loss Function to reg:tweedie. This will lead to more accurate suggestions.

  • Tailor with Specificity: Use the Suggested Order Limitations table to apply custom order_size and round_threshold settings for high-velocity or unique product types. This granular control prevents irrelevant recommendations and optimizes inventory for key products.

  • Leverage POS Data: If available, enable Include POS Sales to improve prediction accuracy. If you have reliable and accurate inventory data, consider enabling Include POS Sales & Inventory for even greater precision.

  • Optimize for Operations: For products that are handled in specific packing units (layers, pallets), enable Enable Layer Round to ensure order suggestions align with operational requirements, reducing the need for manual adjustments. This makes the ordering process more efficient.

16989870:
Distributor steps for clearing a PendingFIFOAdj on Average Cost items: read it from the Inventory Valuation Report, then import +1/-1 lines with LaidInCost via the Invoice EDBL. Needs an open accounting period, v25.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.06

Pre-Conditions

  • Encompass System Access: User must have appropriate permissions to view inventory valuation reports and import invoices.
    ​
    ​

  • Item Costing Method: The product in question (e.g., Item 512) must be configured to use the Average Cost costing method. This troubleshooting guide is not applicable for items using the FIFO or LIFO costing methods, as FIFO adjustments are handled differently.
    ​
    ​

  • UOM Consistency: Ensure the Unit of Measure (UOM) for the item is correctly set up for purchasing, inventory, and consumption (e.g., purchased in kg, inventoried in lbs, used in lbs, with appropriate conversion factors).
    ​
    ​

  • Open Accounting Period: The accounting period corresponding to the desired adjustment date must be open in Encompass. If it's closed, it will need to be rolled back to allow transactions.

Steps

Identify the Pending FIFO Adjustment Value: Navigate to the Inventory Valuation Report in Encompass. Set the End Date of the report to today's date to obtain the most current PendingFIFOAdj value for the affected product (e.g., Item 512). Note the exact value of the PendingFIFOAdj. This value represents the discrepancy you need to correct. Prepare the Invoice Import File: Create a spreadsheet (e.g., a CSV or Excel file) for the invoice import. This file will contain two lines for the same product: one with a positive quantity and one with a negative quantity, along with the LaidInCost to offset the PendingFIFOAdj. The required columns for the import file are: CustomerID: Enter the relevant customer ID. Date: Enter the date for the adjustment. It is recommended to use the current date or a date within an open accounting period, such as the original transaction date (e.g., 6/2/2025). Your accounting team should confirm the appropriate date. ProductID: Enter the ID of the affected product (e.g., 512). NumUnits: This column will have two entries for the same ProductID: One row with 1 (positive one). One row with -1 (negative one). LocationID: Enter the ID of the inventory location (e.g., "Main Brewery"). LaidInCost: This is the critical field for the adjustment. If the PendingFIFOAdj value from Step 1 is negative, enter the absolute value of PendingFIFOAdj into the LaidInCost field for the row with the positive NumUnits (i.e., 1). The LaidInCost for the negative NumUnits row should be 0 or left blank. If the PendingFIFOAdj value from Step 1 is positive, enter the absolute value of PendingFIFOAdj into the LaidInCost field for the row with the negative NumUnits (i.e., -1). The LaidInCost for the positive NumUnits row should be 0 or left blank. Note: Do not include any other price information (e.g., Full Price). This specific type of adjustment relies solely on LaidInCost to affect the inventory value without altering the sale price. Perform the Invoice Import: Navigate to the Invoice EDBL import routine in Encompass (do not use InvoiceOrder EDBL). Upload the prepared import file. Follow the on-screen prompts to complete the import process. Verify the Adjustment: After the import is complete, re-run the Inventory Valuation Report for the affected product. Confirm that the PendingFIFOAdj for the item is now cleared or significantly reduced, and the inventory value accurately reflects the expected cost (e.g., 101 lbs at $12.43/lb). Review your financial reports (e.g., Trial Balance, COGS) to confirm the $53,606.82 entry has been corrected or reversed by the import. If the issue persists, re-check the Inventory Valuation Report's PendingFIFOAdj value and confirm your import file's LaidInCost, NumUnits, and LocationID columns match Step 2 exactly before re-running the Invoice EDBL import.

Fields And Definitions

  • Average Cost (Costing Method): An inventory costing method where the cost of goods available for sale is calculated by dividing the total cost of goods by the total number of units available. This average cost is then used to determine the value of both inventory and cost of goods sold.
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO (First-In, First-Out): An inventory costing method that assumes the first units purchased or produced are the first ones sold.
    ​
    ​

  • Pending FIFO Adj (Pending FIFO Adjustment): A value displayed in the Inventory Valuation report that represents a discrepancy between the system's calculated inventory value (often based on average cost) and what it would be if a FIFO costing method were applied. For average cost items, this adjustment is recognized but not automatically posted as an invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceTrans (Invoice Transaction): A specific line item on an invoice that records details of a product transaction, including quantity and cost/price.

  • NumUnits: The number of units of a product involved in a transaction.

  • LaidInCost: The total cost of an item, including its purchase price and any additional costs such as freight, duties, or other landed costs. This field is used in invoice imports to directly influence the inventory value.
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory EDBL (Electronic Data Batch Load): A utility or routine within Encompass used for importing invoice data in bulk.

Best Practices

  • Regular UOM Review: Periodically review and confirm that the Unit of Measure (UOM) settings for all inventory items are correct and consistent across purchasing, inventory, and sales/production processes to prevent discrepancies.
    ​
    ​

  • Costing Method Understanding: Ensure your team fully understands the implications of different costing methods (Average Cost, FIFO, LIFO) on inventory valuation and financial reporting.
    ​
    ​

  • Batch Adjustment for Historical Issues: For significant historical discrepancies, it may be necessary to process a single, larger adjustment to bring the inventory value in line with reality rather than attempting to correct every past transaction individually.
    ​
    ​

  • Test Environment: If possible, test complex adjustments or new import processes in a non-production (test) environment before applying them to your live system.
    ​
    ​

  • Documentation: Maintain clear internal documentation of all significant inventory adjustments, including the reason for the adjustment, the values involved, and the date it was performed.

Steps

Use a Fusion Report to Import Projects

Fusion report imports are a powerful tool that allows automation in reporting. They allow you to automatically import data into a related table based on a schedule to get the most up-to-date data.

1. Search for New Table import in the universal search bar
​
2. Input a title, a destination table, import action, as well as the source of the import
​

  • The Import Routine is the name of the import that is being created
    ​
    ​

  • The destination table is the table where the report data will be imported too
    ​
    ​

  • The source of the data can be a local file in the form of .xlsx, .csv, .zip files saved reports such as a fusion report, as well as google drive or an EDBL Client
    ​
    ​

3. For a fusion report import click Use Report
​
​4. Find and select the desired report
​
5. Click Save Changes to pull up the Map Field page
​
6. Use the field map to set import fields and click Save Changes, you can also select Link On to choose which field to link onto for the import
​
7. You can execute the import manually to ensure that it works as expected
​
​

  • Review data link will show the data will be imported
    ​
    ​

8. The Import Results page will show details about what was actually imported. If this looks correct, schedule the import by clicking the import scheduling tab
​
9. From this tab select the Import Project from the dropdown, if one does not exist create one from the Import Project table by clicking the green Add Import Project button
​
10. After the import project is selected, click New Schedule
​
​11. Fill in all information and then Save Changes

16989882:
Distributor best practices for switching Route Versions: setting start and end dates ahead using Routes.DaysInAdvance, avoiding plans from the old version, and how pre-sell plans generate before go-live. Requires v21.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 21.01

Steps

Best Practices for Switching Route Versions

To ensure a smooth transition when switching route versions, here's what you need to know:
​
​

Setting the Start Date

  • When modifying an inactive Route Version, set its start date at least as many days in advance as the highest "Routes.DaysInAdvance" value found on the Routes table for the old route version. This proactive measure prevents unwanted plans from the old version and ensures a smooth transition. Failing to set this date before plans are generated from the old version will likely require you to delete and regenerate them.
    ​
    ​

  • For a new Route Version, its Start Date must be the first delivery date for that version. Aligning this date with the initial delivery facilitates a seamless transition for plans and invoice routing.
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

Setting the End Date

  • Ensure the route version's End Date is either null or a distant future date to prevent premature termination. If a Route Version ends without an active alternative, no plans will generate beyond that end date. Once the new Route Version's Start Date is confirmed, set the old version's End Date to the day prior. This, like the start date, should be set in advance—specifically, at least as many days ahead as the highest "Routes.DaysInAdvance" value on the Routes table for the old route version.
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

Plans

  • Be aware that the system will generate plans for pre-sell events before a Route Version's start date if the corresponding Delivery Stop Next Date is on or after the Route Version Start Date. For instance, if a pre-sell stop is on Friday, the delivery stop on Monday, and the new Route Version goes live on Sunday, the Friday pre-sell event will still generate in the new Route Version, even though it's not yet active.

16989884:
Explains direct-to-customer multi-warehouse sourcing: link product groups to stops and set the Inventory Location on presell stops so reps see stock at the source warehouse (vs. Alternate Locations). Requires v25.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.08

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

This feature allows for the accurate display of inventory to sales reps based on the specific warehouse supplying products to a customer, rather than just the customer's primary location. This is especially useful for customers serviced from more than one warehouse and the orders are shipped directly from the source warehouse that is not the customer's home warehouse. With the proper routing setup, sales and delivery teams can ensure the orders get routed to the correct location.
​
​

  • This is different than the alternate locations feature because this setup is if you are delivering directly from multiple warehouses, whereas alternate locations involves picking from an alternate location and shuttling and cross-docking orders at the customer's location.

Example:

The Safeway customer has product groups set on their stop so that their orders for wine and spirits products are delivered directly from the Fort Collins warehouse, beer products from the Denver warehouse, and non-alcohol products from the Colorado Springs warehouse. Also notice the new inventory location field on the Stops table for the presell stops, which ensures that David Stone, the sales rep will see the available inventory at each source location.
​
​
​

Screenshot

Example:
​
The Sterling Walmart customer is serviced by the Sterling warehouse for beer for both sales and delivery, and non-alcohol products sourced from the Gering warehouse. Also notice that there are two different sales reps selling each of those two product groups. Since this is a Sterling customer, it is not necessary to set the inventory location on Colton Burton's presell stop, however on Joe Datel's presell stop, it is necessary to set the inventory location to the Gering warehouse since this is not the customer's location. This will ensure that when Joe is ordering non-alcohol products for this customer, he will see the available inventory in the Gering warehouse.
​
​
​

Screenshot

Best Practices

1. Go to the Stops table
​
​
2. Identify Customers Serviced by Multiple Warehouses:
​
​

  • Determine which customers receive different product groups from distinct warehouses.
    ​
    ​

  • This feature is designed for scenarios where orders are shipped directly from the source warehouse to the customer, not for cross-docking or shuttling operations like with Alternate Locations.

3. Associate Product Groups with Stops:
​
​

  • Ensure that the relevant product groups are correctly associated with their corresponding stops. This allows for granular control over which products are sourced from which warehouse.

​
4. Set the "Inventory Location" Field for Non-Primary Warehouses:
​
​

  • For each presell stop where products for a customer are sourced from a warehouse that is not their primary (home) warehouse, it is essential to populate the "Inventory Location" field on that specific stop.
    ​
    ​

  • Purpose: This explicitly tells the system which warehouse's inventory should be displayed to the sales representative for the products associated with that stop.
    ​
    ​

  • Example: If a customer's primary warehouse is "Sterling" but their non-alcohol products are sourced from "Gering," the presell stop for non-alcohol products must have the "Inventory Location" set to "Gering warehouse."

5. Omit "Inventory Location" for Primary Warehouses:
​
​

  • If a product group for a customer is sourced from their primary (home) warehouse, it is generally not necessary to explicitly set the "Inventory Location" on that presell stop. The system will typically default to the customer's primary location.
    ​
    ​

16989886:
Distributor fix for doubled purchase quantities in Encompass Mobile customer history: check the Update_CustomerHistory task, run Rebuild_CustomerHistory, and the 8-month History limit. Needs admin access; v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

Pre-conditions

Before proceeding with the troubleshooting steps, ensure the following:

  • You have administrative access to the Encompass system.
    ​
    ​

  • You have access to the Scheduled Tasks section of the Encompass system.
    ​
    ​

  • You have communication with your sales representatives to confirm the issue and verify the fix.

Steps

Follow these steps to address issues with duplicated purchase quantities and to understand the limitations of customer history display.Identify Duplicated Purchase Quantities: Sales representatives report that purchased quantities are doubled in the product history on the order screen in Encompass Mobile. Verify the affected customers and products by asking the sales representative for specific examples (e.g., customer ID, product name, and date of the duplicated entry). Check Scheduled Task Status: Navigate to the Scheduled Tasks section within your Encompass system. Look for the task named Update_CustomerHistory. Check the "Last Fail Time" for this task. If it shows a recent failure, especially around the time the duplication was reported, this is a strong indicator of the cause. Run Rebuild Customer History Date Array Task: Crucially, run this task at the end of the day or when there are no reps out in the field. This task rebuilds customer history and may reactivate inactive records based on system settings. Locate the scheduled task named Rebuild_CustomerHistory. Manually initiate this task. Monitor the task's completion. Verify the Fix for Duplicated Quantities: After Rebuild Customer History Date Array has completed, instruct the affected sales representatives to check the product history in Encompass Mobile for the previously duplicated entries. Confirm that the purchase quantities are now correctly displayed (no longer doubled). Understand Customer History Display Limitations: Be aware that after running Rebuild_CustomerHistory, the "History" button in Encompass Mobile will typically only display data going back 8 months. This is a system limitation due to the length limit of the Date Array field on Customer History. If sales representatives require historical data beyond 8 months for seasonal accounts, this is currently a feature request and not a configurable setting.

Fields And Definitions

  • Encompass Mobile: The mobile application used by sales representatives for tasks like order entry and viewing customer history.

  • Purchase Quantities: The number of units of a product purchased by a customer.

  • History Button (Encompass Mobile): A feature within Encompass Mobile that displays a customer's product purchase and inventory history.

  • Scheduled Tasks: Automated processes within the Encompass system that perform various functions at set intervals.

  • Update_CustomerHistory: A scheduled task responsible for updating customer history records.

  • Rebuild Customer History Date Array: A scheduled task that rebuilds the customer history data, which can resolve inconsistencies. This task should be run with caution during off-peak hours.

  • Customer ID: A unique identifier for each customer in the Encompass system.

  • Date Array (Customer History): A field within customer history records that stores a list of dates related to purchases or inventory updates. This field has a length limit, which affects how far back history can be displayed.

  • Inactive Records: Customer history entries that are not currently active or relevant but may still exist in the system.

Best Practices

  • Schedule Rebuild Customer History Date Array strategically: Always run this task during off-peak hours to minimize impact on sales operations.
    ​
    ​

  • Communicate with sales representatives: Keep your sales team informed about planned maintenance or troubleshooting steps that might affect their access to or display of data in Encompass Mobile.
    ​
    ​

  • Regularly monitor scheduled tasks: Periodically check the status of critical scheduled tasks like Update_CustomerHistory to proactively identify and address potential failures.

16989890:
Distillery steps for printing TTB-compliant barrel tags from the Barrel Management Console: required barrel data, PDF Laser or ZPL printer setup, tag fields and updating barrel notes. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

Barrel Data: Ensure all required barrel data is accurately entered into Encompass, including:

  • Distillery DBA (Location DBA)

  • DSP# (TaxEntity)

  • Fill date (from BarrelAttribute.LastFillDate)

  • Volume in gallons (from BarrelHistory.OriginalFillVolume where TransType = Fill)

  • Proof (from BarrelHistory.OriginalProof where TransType = Fill)

  • Original Proof Gallons (from BarrelHistory.OriginalProofGallons where TransType=Fill)

  • Barrel Type (EquipmentType Name)

  • Barrel Name (Equipment.EquipmentName)

  • Spirit Type (from TTBCategory3.TTBCategoryDescription)

  • Notes (from BarrelAttributes.memo)

Printer Setup:

  • For PDF printing, configure a printer with PrinterType = 1) PDF Laser. This is the recommended type for optimal output.

  • For ZPL printing, configure a printer with PrinterType = 3) ZPL Label.

  • If adding new printers, ensure the APS (Application Print Server) is installed on a PC, and that the Printer.Location in Encompass matches the location in your Barrel Management Console.

Steps

NOTE: You can print barrel tags at various stages of your workflow, including after filling, buying, or transferring barrels, and also on demand.

Printing Barrel Tags from Barrel Management Console
​
​

  1. Navigate to Barrel Management Console (BMC): Access the Barrel Management Console (Dashboard ID: 201339).

  2. Select Barrels: Select one or more barrels for which you want to print tags.

  3. Initiate Print: Click the 'Print Tag' button.

  4. Choose Printer: From the printer selection pop-up, choose your desired printer.

    • If you select a PDF Laser printer, a 'Preview' link will immediately appear in the dialog box. Click this link to open a PDF of the barrel tag(s) in a new browser tab, from which you can print directly.

    • If you select a ZPL Label printer, a print job will be generated directly. (Note: Due to current tool limitations, an in-system preview for ZPL is not always reliable. You may need to use an external ZPL viewer for review, if necessary).
      ​
      ​

Workflow Scenarios Supported:

  • After filling a barrel: Print the new tag immediately after the filling process is completed.

  • When buying a filled barrel: Generate a tag for a newly acquired filled barrel.

  • After completing a barrel transfer: Print a new tag for a barrel that has been transferred to another location (e.g., another DSP).

  • Re-Print on demand: Easily reprint lost, damaged, or outdated barrel tags at any time from the BMC.


Updating Barrel Notes (Memo Section on Tag)
​
​

  1. Navigate to Barrel Management Console (BMC): Access the Barrel Management Console.

  2. Select Barrel: Choose the barrel whose notes you wish to update.

  3. Edit Barrel Attributes: Use the Edit tool within Barrel Management to modify the BarrelAttributes.memo field.

  4. Save Changes: Save your changes. The updated notes will appear on subsequently printed barrel tags.

Fields And Definitions

Distillery DBA: The doing-business-as name of your location.

DSP#: Your registered Distilled Spirits Plant number.

Fill Date: The date the barrel was filled, pulled from BarrelAttributes.LastFillDate.

Date Code: A TTB-defined format for the fill date (YYMDD). For example, 22C08 represents March 8, 2022 (Year: 22, Month: C for March, Day: 08).

Months are represented alphabetically: A=January, B=February, C=March, D=April, etc.

Volume: The volume of liquid in the barrel. This will display the BarrelHistory.OriginalFillVolume (e.g., in Gallons) and BarrelHistory.OriginalProofGallons (e.g., in OPG for Original Proof Gallons). For example: 53 WG | 63.60 OPG.

Barrel Type: The type of equipment used as the barrel (e.g., Oak Bourbon Barrel).

Barrel #: The unique identification number or name of the barrel, typically from Equipment.EquipmentName.

Storage: A fixed input on spirits barrel tags indicating that the barrel should be reported in the DRO Storage Report.

Batch: The batch number of the aged liquid in the barrel.

Spirit Type: The classification of the spirit, derived from TTBCategory3.TTBCategoryDescription.

Report Type: A classification of spirits based on their proof, e.g., "Whisky 160° AND UNDER", "Brandy OVER 170°", "Rum", etc.

BSA or OC: These fields are placeholders for potential barrel manufacturing process or material descriptions. Their usage is currently under review; if a clear definition cannot be established, these boxes may be removed.

Notes: Displays information from the BarrelAttributes.memo field.

QR Code: A scannable code that links directly to the specific barrel's Equipment record within Encompass, allowing quick access to detailed barrel information via a mobile WMS application.

Best Practices

Printer Type for Preview: If you want to preview barrel tags before printing, always select a PDF Laser printer type. The system is designed to provide direct PDF previews for this type of printer.

Equipment Naming: For clarity and ease of use, it is recommended to keep your Equipment.EquipmentName and Equipment.Bin name consistent, as users typically identify barrels by their Equipment Name.

ZPL Troubleshooting: If you encounter errors when previewing ZPL commands within Encompass, use an external ZPL viewer tool (e.g., Labelary Online ZPL Viewer) to review the tag layout.

16989895:
Producer steps for spirits TTB case serial numbers: set System Setting 3181 and Track Serial Num on the Recipe Version, record runs in Production Packaging Logs and use Print Case Label. Requires v24.03+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.03

Pre-Conditions

Recipe Configuration: The packaging Recipe Version must have the 'Track Serial Num' field set to True. This setting is configured in the Recipe Management Dashboard.

System Setting 3181: Next Available TTB Case Serial Number must be configured. The value entered for "Next Case Serial Number" must be greater than the EndSerialNumber of the largest ID currently recorded in the Production Packaging Logs table.

Product Type: The product being packaged must be classified as a spirit.

Production Order Status: The Production Order Status must be greater than "In-Process" to access printing features.

Printer Setup: For PDF preview and printing, the selected printer must have PrinterType set to 1) PDF Laser. Otherwise, printing will occur in ZPL mode.

Steps

A. Initial Setup and Configuration

1. Configure Next Available TTB Case Serial Number:

  • Navigate to System Settings.

  • Locate Setting ID 3181: Next Available TTB Case Serial Number.

  • Set the numerical value for the next available case serial number. Ensure this number is higher than any existing EndSerialNumber in ProductionPackagingLogs.

2. Enable Serial Number Tracking on a Recipe Version:

  • Navigate to Recipe Management dashboard.

  • Select the relevant Packaging Recipe Version for your spirits product.

  • Edit the Recipe Version and set the Track Serial Num field to True.

B. Packaging and Serial Number Recording Workflow

1. Create a Production Order:

  • Create a new Production Order for the spirits product, ensuring it uses a packaging Recipe Version with 'Track Serial Num' set to True.

  • Set the Planned Units for the order.

2. Perform Packaging in Production Processing:

  • Navigate to the Production Processing Dashboard (Dashboard ID: 183629) for the created Production Order.

  • Click the Packaging button.

  • Enter the Packaging Units (e.g., 200).

  • Click Save.

  • The system will automatically add a record to the ProductionPackagingLogs table for this packaging run, recording the Start Serial Num and End Serial Num for the packaged units.

  • Repeat this step for each batch of units packaged (e.g., input another 300 units, click Save). Each packaging instance will create a new record in ProductionPackagingLogs.

C. Printing Case Labels

1. Access Print Case Label Feature:

  • From the Production Processing Dashboard for a relevant order, ensure the product is spirits, the order status is > 4-In-Process, and Track Serial Num is true. The Print Case Label button will be displayed.

  • Click the Print Case Label button.

2. Select Packaging Logs for Printing:

  • A list of ProductionPackagingLogs records associated with the current order will be displayed.

  • Select one or more records for which you wish to print case labels.

3. Initiate Printing:

  • If your printer's PrinterType is 1) PDF Laser, a PDF preview will be displayed, allowing you to review before printing.

  • For other printer types (e.g., ZPL Label), the system will generate a Print Job.

D. Handling Reverse Operations (Undo, Correct, Cancel)

  • Updating Production Packaging Logs Status: When an Undo, Correct, or Cancel operation is performed on a Production Order:

  • The Status of the associated records in the ProductionPackagingLogs table will be automatically set to Canceled.

  • Regenerating Records: If packaging is performed again after an Undo, Correct, or Cancel operation, new ProductionPackagingLogs records will be generated with a Status of Normal.

  • Printing Logic: The printing functionality will filter out and only print labels for ProductionPackagingLogs records with a Status of Normal.

Fields And Definitions

RecipeVersions.TrackSerialNum: A boolean field found on packaging Recipe Versions. When set to True, it enables the system to track and generate case serial numbers for production orders using that recipe.

Setting 3181: Next Available TTB Case Serial Number: A system-wide setting that stores the next available generic TTB-compliant serial number to be assigned.

ProductionPackagingLogs Table: A new table introduced to store detailed information about individual packaging runs within a Production Order. Each entry includes:

  • Start Serial Num: The starting serial number of the cases packaged in that specific run.

  • End Serial Num: The ending serial number of the cases packaged in that specific run.

  • Status: Indicates the state of the packaging log record.

    • Canceled: The packaging run represented by this log has been undone, corrected, or canceled.

    • Normal: The packaging run represented by this log is active and valid for printing.

ProductionOrders.StartSerialNum & ProductionOrders.EndSerialNum: These fields are no longer displayed on the Production Order as the serial number tracking has been moved to the more granular ProductionPackagingLogs table to support discontinuous serial number ranges.

The BinTrans EDBL is typically only needed for warehouses where WMS is enabled. Non-WMS warehouses have simplified inventory management that generally does not call for imported Bin Trans.

Steps

Please ensure you thoroughly understand this routine before implementation in your production environment

The BinTrans EDBL is designed to update, manage, and process bin transactions—records of inventory movement—in the system. This guide provides a detailed breakdown of the mappable fields, their purposes, prerequisites, and key considerations for running the EDBL successfully.

1. Review data & map fields

Ensure that all required and desired fields are properly mapped in the import data. See Fields & Definitions for more information about each field in the EDBL.

2. Before running the EDBL, ensure the following:
​
​

  • Location Mapping: Either LocationID or LocationID_Translation must be mapped.
    If no matching LocationID is found in the system, a warning will appear: "LocationID not mapped."

3. Import Actions
​
​

Only the following import actions are respected:

  • AddOnly

  • UpdateOrAdd

If other import actions are used, no data will be processed.

4. Special Cases
​
​

  • Updating PurchaseTransID:
    If PurchaseTransID is mapped, BinInventory.PurchaseTransID will be updated for the related product and bin combination.
    ​
    ​

  • Adding Bin Lot Data:
    If PurchaseTrans is not null, Bin Lot data will be added under these conditions:
    - The bin's BinZones.TrackBinLots field is set to Required or Optional
    - The product's tracking flags are enabled for Code Dates, Batch Codes, or Vintages.

5. Additional Notes
​
​

There are no scheduled tasks that need to run after this EDBL. BinTrans records are immediately created and impacting the system, though they may take up to 15 minutes to be visible in the Bin Trans table. Immediate impact can be seen in the Bin Audit tool, where changes to bin inventory over time can be reviewed for a specified product and bin.

Fields And Definitions

  • LocationID_Translation: Maps to LocationID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID: Directly provides the LocationID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • BinID_Translation: Maps to the BinID through table translation.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID_Translation: Maps to the ProductID through table translation.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID: Directly provides the ProductID.
    ​
    ​

  • BinTransType: Specifies the transaction type (BinTrans.BinTransType).
    Values: 1,Received;2,Unreceived;3,Put Away;4,Replenished;5,Pick Complete;6,Pick Uncompleted;7,Loaded;17,Add Ons;8,Unloaded;9,Returned;10,Unreturned;11,Return Put Away;12,Invoiced;13,Inventory Adjust;14,Moved;15,Skip;16,Picker Cut;18,Production Queue;19,Reverse Production Queue;20,Equipment Transfer;21,Re-picked
    ​
    ​

  • NumUnits: Specifies the number of units involved in the transaction (BinTrans.NumUnits).
    ​
    ​

  • BinID: Specifies the target bin ID.
    ​
    ​

  • LoadSheetID: Links the transaction to a load sheet (BinTrans.LoadSheetID).
    ​
    ​

  • PalletID: Links the transaction to a pallet (BinTrans.PalletID). This is only for picking outbound pallets, not for the pallet inventory is stored on while it resides in the warehouse.
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceTransID: Links the transaction to a specific invoice transaction (BinTrans.InvoiceTransID).
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseTransID: Links the transaction to a specific purchase layer of inventory (BinTrans.PurchaseTransID). This is how specific expiration dates, batch codes, or vintages are noted during a move, translating to a Bin Lot, if that data is being tracked.
    ​
    ​

  • BoxID: Links the transaction to a box used in unit or bottle picking. (BinTrans.BoxID).
    ​
    ​

  • Date: Specifies the transaction date. Defaults to the current date (LocalToday()) if not provided.

*Only one of the noted fields must be mapped, but both are not simultaneously required.

Best Practices

  • When to use: The BinTrans EDBL is best suited for situations where the "from bin" and the "to bin" need to be specified, as opposed to allowing inventory to always shift into an adjustment bin. If inventory is moving from one on-floor bin to another, for example, the BinTrans EDBL is the right choice.
    ​
    ​

  • The BinTrans EDBL is primarily intended for use within integrations or during the data migration process.
    ​
    ​

  • In most imports, the Bin Trans Type should be 14, Moved which simply notes that inventory is shifting from one bin to another, without involving more specific processes like receiving.

The Pallets EDBL is an import used to map, update, and manage pallet-related data in the system. This guide walks users through the available fields, their functions, prerequisites, and important considerations for running the EDBL successfully.

1. Review data & map fields
​
​

Ensure that all required and desired fields are properly mapped in the import data. See Fields & Definitions for more information about each field in the EDBL.

2. Before running the EDBL, ensure the following:
​
​

  • Location Mapping: Either LocationID or LocationID_Translation must be mapped.
    If no matching LocationID is found in the system, a warning will appear: "LocationID not mapped."
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Mapping: InvoiceNum or InvoiceID must be provided.
    The corresponding invoice must exist in the system for the pallet to be added, and InvoiceTransID must be accurate.
    If it is missing or incorrect, the pallet will not link to any invoice transaction, rendering it meaningless.

3. Import Actions
​
​

Only the following import actions are respected:

  • UpdateOnly

  • UpdateOrAdd

If other import actions are used, the process cannot link InvoiceTrans or update any other data.

4. Special Cases
​
​

  • Creating New Pallets:
    If only PalletID_Translation is mapped, and not PalletID, a new pallet will be created.
    ​
    ​

  • NumUnits Discrepancies:
    If the NumUnits in the provided InvoiceTransID does not match the system’s current value, the system will adjust the values.
    The latest provided value will overwrite and become the new NumUnits. This is how cuts can be communicated via the EDBL.

5. Additional Notes
​
​

There are no scheduled tasks that need to run after this EDBL. Pallet records are immediately updated, along with their related invoice trans data.

Fields And Definitions

  • LocationID_Translation: Maps to LocationID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID: Directly provides the LocationID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • PalletID_Translation: Maps to PalletID through table translation; if not found, a new pallet is created.
    ​
    ​

  • PalletID: Directly provides the PalletID.
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceNum: Maps to InvoiceID through table translation using InvoiceNum. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceID: Links the pallet to an existing invoice via Pallet.InvoiceID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID_Translation: Maps to ProductID through table translation, in the end providing InvoiceTrans.ProductID.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID: Directly provides InvoiceTrans.ProductID.
    ​
    ​

  • NumUnits: Updates InvoiceTrans.NumUnits.
    ​
    ​

  • SSCC18: Updates the SSCC18 value for pallets, which is the serialized shipping container code used universally for pallet recognition across systems.
    ​
    ​

  • Status: Updates pallet status; defaults to "New" if no value is provided.
    ​
    ​

  • PalletSeq: Updates InvoiceTrans.PalletSequence.
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceTransID: Links a related invoice transaction with the pallet.
    ​
    ​

  • PickedByUserID: Updates the PickedByUserID field for the pallet, indicating the User ID of the person that completed the pallet pick.

The routine works by:

    ​

    ​

    ​
    ​

The BinInventories EDBL updates and manages inventory levels for bins. This guide outlines the mappable fields, their purposes, prerequisites, and important considerations to ensure a smooth process.

1. Review data & map fields

Ensure that all required and desired fields are properly mapped in the import data. See Fields & Definitions for more information about each field in the EDBL.

2. Before running the EDBL, ensure the following:

  • Location Mapping: Either LocationID or LocationID_Translation must be mapped.
    If no matching LocationID is found in the system, a warning will appear: "LocationID not mapped."

3. Import Actions

Only the following import actions are respected:

  • AddOnly

  • UpdateOnly

  • UpdateOrAdd

If other import actions are used, no data will be processed.

4. How Inventory Updates Work

This EDBL updates bin inventory levels directly. Here’s how the process works:

  • The provided inventory value replaces the current BinInventory.Inventory.

  • Two BinTrans records are created to adjust the bin inventory:

    • A negative adjustment (AdjBinID) to decrease the previous inventory level.

    • A positive adjustment to reflect the new inventory level.

Example:
If BinInventoryID 1 has an initial inventory of 10 units and the import file specifies 20 units:

  1. The final inventory becomes 20 units.

  2. Two BinTrans records are added:

    • AdjBin reduces inventory by -10 units.

    • Bin adds +10 units.

5. Additional Notes

There are no scheduled tasks that need to run after this EDBL. Bin Inventories are immediately updated, and matching BinTrans records are created to reflect any moves. Bin Trans may take up to 15 minutes to be visible in the Bin Trans table. Immediate impact can be seen on the Bin Inventories table or in the Bin Audit tool, where changes to bin inventory over time can be reviewed for a specified product and bin.

Fields And Definitions

  • LocationID_Translation: External identifier for the location. Maps to a system LocationID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID: Directly provides the location ID of the desired warehouse. If not provided, defaults to the current user's location. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • BinID_Translation: External identifier for the bin. Maps to a system BinID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • BinID: Specifies the target bin ID in the warehouse. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • AdjBinID: Specifies the adjustment bin ID; defaults to DefaultBins.AdjustBinID if not mapped.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID_Translation: External identifier for the product. Maps to the ProductID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID: Specifies the target system product ID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory: The quantity of the product to set in the bin. This is the actual inventory count. Updates the number of units (NumUnits).
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseID: If mapped, finds a PurchaseTransID for the product in the specified purchase.
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseTransID: Updates BinInventory.PurchaseTransID. Creates BinLots if the bin’s BinZones.RequirePalletTag > 0.
    ​
    ​

  • WholesaleUnitsPerCase: Defaults to the product’s Package.WholesaleUnitsPerCase if not mapped.

*Only one of the noted fields must be mapped, but both are not simultaneously required.

Best Practices

  • When to use: The BinInventories EDBL is best suited for situations where the "from bin" needs to be specified, but any variance in inventory can shift into an adjustment bin. If new inventory quantities simply need to be updated for a collection of bins, for example, the BinInventories EDBL is the right choice.
    ​
    ​

  • The BinInventories EDBL is primarily intended for use within integrations or during the data migration process.
    ​
    ​

  • Always include LocationID or LocationID_Translation to ensure inventory is updated in the correct facility
    ​
    ​

  • Provide both BinID_Translation and ProductID_Translation values when possible for better matching to existing records
    ​
    ​

  • Verify that bins exist before running the import
    ​
    ​

  • If importing inventory for bins that track lots or batches, include PurchaseTransID to maintain lot traceability
    ​
    ​

  • After completing a WMS_BinInventories import, consider running inventory reports to verify the updated quantities match expectations
    ​
    ​

  • If you need to completely reset inventory in a bin, include records with an Inventory value of 0

16989907:
Distributor reference for the HTMLMessages EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-send email, text or eChat messages from a report, with SingleSendMD5 to block duplicates. Add-only; requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • This routine only supports "Add Only" import action

  • The source report for this import must contain a "SingleSendMD5" field mapped to prevent duplicate messages

  • User must have appropriate permissions to send messages

  • For email delivery, valid email addresses are required

  • For text message and eChat delivery, valid user IDs are required

  • Message content must be provided either in the Body field directly or through a document reference

Steps

The HTMLMessages EDBL routine allows you to import and send messages through multiple delivery channels (email, text, or eChat). The routine:

  1. Validates all recipient and sender information

  2. Processes message templates with field replacements

  3. Prevents duplicate messages using a unique identifier (SingleSendMD5)

  4. Transforms API calls and QuickLinks within the message content

  5. Automatically adds unsubscribe links to alert-based emails

  6. Sends messages immediately or schedules them for later delivery

  7. Tracks message delivery status

The routine will disable sending for invalid messages and include warnings in the import results. For performance reasons, if more than 200 messages are imported at once, they will be queued rather than sent immediately.

Special formatting options are available within the Body field:

  • <APICall>Display Text^APICommand^Parameters</APICall> will generate a clickable link

  • <QuickLink>Link Text^URL</QuickLink> will generate a tracked link

  • For text messages, <br> tags will be converted to new lines

Fields And Definitions

  • DeliveryMethod: Specifies the channel for message delivery. Values include: "Email" (2), "Text Message" (3), "eChat" (1), or "TestDoNotSend" (0).

  • FromUserID: The system user ID of the sender. Required for eChat and text messages unless AlertID is provided.

  • FromEmail: The sender's email address. Required for email delivery.

  • ToUserID: The system user ID of the recipient. Required for eChat and text messages.

  • ToEmail: The recipient's email address. Required for email delivery.

  • Subject: Message subject line. Required for email, optional for other delivery methods.

  • Body: The actual message content. HTML is supported for email, plain text for other methods.

  • BodyHTMLDocumentID: Reference to a document in the system containing the message template. Used when Body is not directly provided.

  • BodyHTMLGlobalDocumentID: Reference to a global document containing the message template. Used when Body and BodyHTMLDocumentID are not provided.

  • DelayedSendTime: Schedule messages for future delivery. If not specified, messages are sent immediately.

  • SingleSendMD5: Unique identifier to prevent duplicate sending. This must be mapped from your source report.

  • AlertID: If the message is associated with a system alert, this field links them. Also enables automatic unsubscribe links.

  • ImportTaskID: Reference to the import task that created this message.

  • SendDisable: Set to 1 to prevent sending. Defaults to 0 (send).

Best Practices

  • Always include the SingleSendMD5 field to prevent duplicate messages

  • Provide both email and user ID fields when possible for better matching

  • Test your message templates with a small sample using DeliveryMethod = "TestDoNotSend" before mass sending

  • Use placeholders like {FieldName} in your templates for personalization

  • For large message volumes, use a scheduled import with DelayedSendTime to spread out delivery

  • Consider using QuickLinks for tracking click-through rates in marketing campaigns

  • Ensure email templates comply with anti-spam regulations by including unsubscribe options

  • Validate all email addresses and user IDs before import to avoid failed deliveries

  • For text messages, keep content brief and use only essential formatting

  • If reusing templates, store them as HTML documents and reference them by BodyHTMLDocumentID

16989911:
Distributor reference for the Tasks EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-create or update tasks and task details with assignees, customers, objectives, statuses and deadlines. Requires v22.01+.

Required reference data should exist in the system before import:

  • Users (for task assignments)

  • Customers (if linking tasks to customers)

  • Objectives and Objective Types

  • Task Statuses

Steps

The Tasks EDBL routine imports task data along with associated task details. It supports Add Only, Update Only, and Update or Add actions.

Process Overview:

  1. The system processes task assignments, assigning the current user if no assignment is provided

  2. Customer references are resolved using Customer IDs or Names

  3. Objectives and Objective Types are translated and linked

  4. Task Status is determined or set to default value if not provided

  5. For existing tasks, the system attempts to find matches based on: Task name, Task status, Customer association

  6. Task details are created or updated as needed

  7. Additional fields like jobs, custom fields, dates and deadlines are processed

When updating tasks, the system will modify only the fields provided in your import file. During add operations, default values will be applied to required fields if not explicitly provided.

If the system finds a matching task within the past 3 days (based on task name, status, and customer), it will update that task instead of creating a duplicate record.

Fields And Definitions

  • TaskID_Translation - External identifier for the task that can be used to match existing records

  • AssignToUserID - User ID to assign the task to

  • AssignedTo - Username to assign the task to (alternative to AssignToUserID)

  • CustomerName - Name of the customer to associate with the task

  • CustomerID_Translation - External identifier for the customer

  • ObjectiveType - Name of the objective type

  • ObjectiveTypeID - ID of the objective type

  • Objective - Name of the objective

  • ObjectiveID - ID of the objective

  • Task - Name/description of the task (required)

  • TaskID - System ID of the task (used for updates)

  • TaskStatus - Status name for the task

  • TaskStatusID - ID of the task status

  • TaskDetail - Detailed description for the task

  • TaskDetailID - System ID of the task detail (used for updates)

  • TaskDetailID_Translation - External identifier for the task detail

  • EventID - ID of an associated event

  • JobID - ID of an associated job

  • Job - Name of the job to associate

  • CustomField501-512 - Custom field values

  • StartDate - When the task should start

  • Deadline - When the task is due

Best Practices

  • Always include a TaskStatus or the system will use the first available status

  • When assigning tasks, verify that the assigned user exists in the system

  • Provide both CustomerID and Task name to avoid duplicate tasks

  • If updating existing tasks, include unique identifiers (TaskID or combination of Task name, status, and customer)

  • When working with TaskDetails, include TaskDetail content and link to the correct TaskID

  • For recurring imports, consider using TaskID_Translation as a consistent external identifier

  • Include start dates and deadlines for better task management

  • To ensure proper task assignment routing, specify ObjectiveID when possible

  • Test your import with a small sample first to validate field mappings and behavior

16989914:
Explains Auto Forecast in Encompass Forecasting: why a product ignores its Forecast Group's Forecast Method (api?AutoForecast in audit) and how variance picks the Average or Trend method. Requires v21.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 21.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Leveraging the Forecasting tool and using Forecast Groups.

Steps

You might notice the Forecasting tool using a different Forecast Method for a particular Forecast Group. This is likely due to Auto-Forecast. If you audit the Inventory record, you'll may see "api?AutoForecast," which indicates an API is running specific logic to determine the forecast for each product in that group.
​
When this happens, the product isn't using the Forecast Method defined for its Forecast Group. Instead, it's relying on Auto-Forecast logic, which the system applies based on specific parameters. Here's how it works:
​
​
​
​

Step 1: Check if Variance is over 5% by comparing the last three weeks forecast sales to the last three weeks actual sales.

  • Last 3 weeks(SUM(Week(-1, -2, -3) forecast sales) - SUM(Week(-1,-2,-3) actual sales) / SUM(Week(-1, -2, -3) forecast sales) ) > 5%, Auto match Forecast Method is triggered, please see the previous task detail.

Step 2: If Step 1 is True, get percentdifference for:

  • 2.1. Last 3 weeks vs. Prev 6 Week (Average, 6 Weeks)
    ​
    ​

  • 2.2. Last 3 weeks vs. Prev 12 Week(Average, 12 Weeks)
    ​
    ​

  • 2.3. Last 3 weeks vs. Last year 6 Week(Trend, 6 Weeks)
    ​
    ​

  • 2.4. Last 3 weeks vs. Last year 12 Week(Trend, 12 Weeks)
    ​
    ​

  • 2.5. Last 3 weeks vs. Prev 6 Week with backorder (Average, 6 Weeks)
    ​
    ​

  • 2.6. Last 3 weeks vs. Prev 12 Weekwith backorder(Average,12 Weeks)
    ​
    ​

  • 2.7. Last 3 weeks vs. Last year 6 Weekwith backorder(Trend, 6 Weeks)
    ​
    ​

  • 2.8. Last 3 weeks vs. Last year 12 Week with backorder(Trend, 12 Weeks)

Step 3: Pick the calculation with the minimum absolute percent diff

Step 4:Set the Forecast Method and Forecast Percent based on the lowest percent difference.

Other Rules:

  • ExcludeBackorder = True or False, but do not change ExcludeBackorder after Forecast Method is changed.
    ​
    ​

  • If Forecast Method or Sales Period By Week is changed, then change ForecastPercent to Null.
    ​
    ​

  • If Forecast Method and Sales Period By Week do not change, then ForecastPercent is not changed.
    ​
    ​

  • For Forecast Method = Trend, only use it when Last Year has Sales.
    ​
    ​

  • First 6 weeks of the year, if there was a Sale in Last Year, we will use the Forecast Method = Trend
    ​
    ​

  • For ExcludeBackorder = False, still use NumUnits + Backorder + Backfill
    ​
    ​

(Notes: Backfill is a negative value)
16989915:
Distributor reference for the Assets EDBL import in Encompass: bulk add or update assets with Add Only, Update Only or Update or Add, and how AssetType and AssetCategory defaults apply. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • A default AssetCategory must exist in the system labeled 'Default'.

  • If you want to associate assets with specific AssetTypes, the AssetTypes should already exist in the system.

Steps

The Assets EDBL routine allows you to import assets into the system. Assets are tracked items that can be assigned various attributes based on their type. The routine automatically handles asset type associations and will use defaults when certain values are not provided.

The routine processes each record in your import file and does the following:

  1. If no AssetTypeID_Translation is provided, it will set it to 'Default'

  2. If both AssetTypeID and AssetCategoryID are missing, it will attempt to set the AssetCategoryID to the 'Default' category from the system

  3. The routine then processes records according to the selected import action:

  • Add Only: Adds new assets only, skipping records that already exist

  • Update Only: Updates existing assets only, skipping records that don't exist yet

  • Update or Add: Updates existing assets or adds new ones if they don't exist

The system will attempt to match existing records using the standard translation mechanisms

Fields And Definitions

The Assets routine inherits fields from both the Assets table and AssetTypes table. Key fields include:

  • AssetID: The system-generated unique identifier for each asset (generated automatically)

  • AssetName: The name of the asset

  • AssetTypeID: The ID of the asset type

  • AssetTypeID_Translation: The name or external identifier of the asset type to link to

  • AssetCategoryID: The ID of the asset category

  • Status: The status of the asset

  • SerialNumber: The serial number of the asset

  • Cost: The cost value of the asset

  • InstallDate: When the asset was installed

Additional fields from the Assets table can also be mapped in your import file

Best Practices

  • Always include an AssetName for each asset to ensure proper identification

  • Provide AssetTypeID_Translation values that match existing asset types in your system

  • If you're unsure about asset types, either ensure a 'Default' asset type exists or create the necessary asset types before importing

  • When updating assets, include a unique identifier (like AssetID or another unique field) to ensure proper matching

  • Use descriptive serial numbers or asset identifiers to make assets easier to locate

  • Include as much detail as possible for each asset to improve tracking and management

  • Test your import with a small sample file before running a large import to verify correct behavior

16989917:
Advanced reference for the WMSMoveTaskOrTaskTransUpdate EDBL: update WMS Move Task or transaction status (New, InTransit, Completed) to trigger bin inventory moves. Update Only/Update Or Add; outside standard support; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • User must have appropriate permissions to modify WMS Move Tasks and Move Task Transactions
    ​
    ​

  • The Move Tasks and Move Task Transactions you want to update must already exist in the system
    ​
    ​

  • The import action must be set to either "Update Only" or "Update Or Add" (the routine ignores records when set to "Add Only")
    ​
    ​

  • Sufficient inventory must exist in the source bins when status changes trigger inventory movements

Steps

EDBL Routines Disclaimer: This EDBL routine represents advanced functionality primarily intended for use by Encompass technical staff. While technically proficient customers may utilize these routines, please be aware that they fall outside the scope of standard support. Assistance with EDBL routines is not covered under standard support agreements and may require billable services from our Professional Services team. Please ensure you thoroughly understand this routine before implementation in your production environment

This EDBL routine allows you to update the status of existing WMS Move Tasks or individual Move Task Transactions. Depending on the status change, the system will automatically create appropriate bin transactions to move inventory between bins.

The routine can operate in two modes:

  • Update Move Tasks: When you provide WMSMoveTaskID and WMSMoveTaskStatus, the routine will update the main task status.
    ​
    ​

  • Update Move Task Transactions: When you provide WMSMoveTaskTransID and WMSMoveTaskTransStatus, the routine will update individual task transaction statuses.
    ​
    ​

Status changes trigger different behaviors:

  • When updating a transaction status from New to InTransit, the system creates bin transactions to move inventory from the source bin to an in-transit bin
    ​
    ​

  • When updating a transaction status from InTransit to Completed, the system creates bin transactions to move inventory from the in-transit bin to the destination bin
    ​
    ​

  • When updating a transaction status from New to Completed, the system directly moves inventory from the source bin to the destination bin
    ​
    ​

The routine automatically handles inventory movement based on the WMS Move Task type (Replenish, PutAway, Move, etc.) and assigns the appropriate BinTransType.

If you're updating the main Move Task status to "Completed," all associated task transactions will be processed accordingly

Fields And Definitions

For Updating Move Tasks:

  • WMSMoveTaskID: The ID of the WMS Move Task to update
    ​
    ​

  • WMSMoveTaskStatus: The new status for the WMS Move Task (numeric value)
    ​
    ​

For Updating Move Task Transactions:

  • WMSMoveTaskTransID: The ID of the WMS Move Task Transaction to update
    ​
    ​

  • WMSMoveTaskTransStatus: The new status for the WMS Move Task Transaction (numeric value)
    ​
    ​

Common Status Values:

  • Move Task Status: New (0), Printed (1), Completed (2)
    ​
    ​

  • Move Task Transaction Status: New (0), InTransit (1), Completed (2)

Best Practices

  • Verify that the referenced WMS Move Tasks and Transactions exist before importing
    ​
    ​

  • Ensure source bins have sufficient inventory before attempting status changes
    ​
    ​

  • Consider the impact of status changes on your warehouse operations - bulk updates through EDBL will trigger real inventory movements

The LicensePlateBinTrans EDBL routine allows you to move inventory that is tracked on license plates from one bin to another. The routine creates bin transaction records that record the movement of products.

The routine supports two methods of identifying license plates:

  1. Using the FromLicensePlateID field (direct method)

  2. Using SSCC18 barcode and FromBinID fields (indirect method)

When using the SSCC18 method, if a license plate is not found at the specified source bin but the SSCC18 exists elsewhere in the system, a new license plate will be created at the source bin before moving it to the destination.

The routine will validate that source and destination bins are in the same location. If they are in different locations, the import will fail with appropriate warnings.

The routine only supports the AddOnly and UpdateOrAdd import actions. UpdateOnly is not supported for this routine.

Required Fields:

Identification Fields (at least one set is required):

Method 1:

  • FromLicensePlateID: Integer. The ID of the license plate to be moved.

Method 2:

  • SSCC18: Text (20). The barcode identifier of the license plate.
    ​
    ​

  • FromBinID: Integer. The source bin ID where the license plate is currently located.

Best Practices

  • Always verify that source and destination bins are in the same location before attempting imports
    ​
    ​

The SurveyQuestions EDBL routine imports survey questions into the system. It takes data from your import file and creates new survey question records. This routine primarily supports adding new records to the SurveyQuestions table.

The routine performs the following actions:

  1. Validates and cleans the imported data

  2. Converts empty string values to NULL for most fields

  3. Sets default values of '0' for Required and Remember fields when they are empty

  4. Inserts the records into the SurveyQuestions table

This EDBL routine uses DISTINCT when inserting records, which helps prevent duplicate entries from being created.

Note that this routine appears to be focused on adding new records rather than updating existing ones, so it works best with the "Add Only" import action.

The PurchaseConfirm EDBL routine is used to confirm purchases that have already been created in the system. This routine will update existing purchases with confirmation information such as invoice numbers, dates, and purchase totals.

When you run this routine:

  1. The system validates each purchase ID provided in your import file

  2. The system checks if you have permission to confirm each purchase

  3. For valid purchases, the system updates the purchase with the confirmation information

  4. The system changes the status of the purchase to "Confirmed"

  5. Purchases that cannot be confirmed will generate warnings in your import results

This routine does not create new purchases. If a purchase ID does not exist in the system, it will be skipped and included in the warnings list.

Fields And Definitions

  • PurchaseID - Integer - The unique identifier for the purchase that needs to be confirmed. This field is required and must match an existing purchase in the system.

  • PurchaseTotal - Currency - The total amount for the purchase. This should match the calculated total on the purchase in the system. Significant discrepancies may prevent confirmation.

  • PostDate - Date - The date when this purchase should be posted to the accounting system. If not provided, the system may use the current date or the InvoiceDate as a default.

  • InvoiceDate - Date - The date on the vendor's invoice for this purchase.

  • InvoiceNum - Text - The invoice number from the vendor for this purchase. Maximum 24 characters.

  • PONum - Text - The purchase order number associated with this purchase. Maximum 50 characters.

Best Practices

  • Always include a valid Purchase ID for each record in your import file

  • Ensure the Purchase Total in your file matches the actual total in the system to avoid validation errors

  • Include accurate Invoice Num and Invoice Date fields, as these are typically required for proper confirmation. If Invoice Date is not provided, it will be set to Post Date.

  • If possible, include the PO Num field to maintain the relationship between the purchase and its originating purchase order

  • Before running this import, ensure the purchases you want to confirm are in the appropriate status (typically Received)

  • Review all warnings after import to identify any purchases that could not be confirmed

Steps

The MoveEvents EDBL routine allows you to update and move delivery events and their associated invoices from one route plan to another. The routine works by:

  1. Identifying existing events by the EventID provided in your import file

  2. Moving the events to a different plan if a new PlanID is specified

  3. Moving associated invoices to the load sheet of the destination plan

  4. Updating event sequence and/or start time values if provided

  5. Re-sequencing invoices on affected load sheets automatically if sequence changes are made

This routine is particularly useful when you need to move pre-order invoices along with driver sell stops to maintain routing consistency.

Note that the routine can only update existing events and will not create new ones. It will ignore any records in your import file that don't match existing EventIDs in the system.

Fields And Definitions

  • EventID - Integer - The unique identifier of the event to update. This field is required and used to identify the existing event in the system.

  • Sequence - Integer - The new sequence number for the event. If provided, this will update the event's sequence in the route plan.

  • StartTime - DateTime - The new start time for the event. If provided, this will update when the event is scheduled to begin.

  • PlanID - Integer - The identifier of the destination plan where the event should be moved. If provided and different from the current plan, the event and its associated invoices will be moved to this plan.

Best Practices

  • Always verify your EventIDs are correct before importing to avoid unintended changes

  • Check that destination plans (PlanID) exist in the system before attempting to move events

  • Ensure load sheets are not already in "Loaded" status before attempting to move invoices

  • Run this import outside of peak delivery hours to minimize impact on operations

  • Consider sequencing all events in a plan when making sequence changes to ensure proper route order

  • After import completion, verify events and invoices have moved correctly in the system

  • Use this routine in conjunction with OrderRouting EDBL when reorganizing complete routes

16989929:
Reference for the OrderRouting EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-move invoices between routes and update delivery sequence, trips, times, driver and vehicle. Needs InvoiceEdit permission; v25.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.09

Pre-Conditions

  • You must have the InvoiceEdit permission to run this EDBL

  • The source and destination LoadSheets must not be in "Loaded" status or beyond

  • Routes should already exist in the system, though the routine can create routes if needed

Steps

EDBL Routines Disclaimer: This EDBL routine represents advanced functionality primarily intended for use by Encompass technical staff. While technically proficient customers may utilize these routines, please be aware that they fall outside the scope of standard support. Assistance with EDBL routines is not covered under standard support agreements and may require billable services from our Professional Services team. Please ensure you thoroughly understand this routine before implementation in your production environment

The OrderRouting EDBL is designed to move invoices between routes. It allows you to:

  • Reassign invoices to different routes

  • Update delivery sequences of invoices

  • Update planned start and end times for deliveries

  • Organize deliveries by trip numbers

The system will identify invoices by matching on InvoiceNum, InvoiceID, or by CustomerID and Date combination if invoice identifiers are not provided. The routine then locates the appropriate LoadSheets and moves the invoices between them, updating sequences as specified.

If a route specified in your import does not exist, the system will create it automatically.

If a load sheet already has a "Loaded" status, the system will not move invoices to or from it, and will generate a warning message.

For events with times, the system updates both the Events table and fixes the timing of related events when applicable.

Fields And Definitions

  • Date - The delivery date for the invoice

  • RouteID - Identifier for the route; can be used to match existing routes

  • RouteNum - The route number; can be used to match existing routes or create new ones

  • CustomerID - The customer identifier for the invoice

  • CustomerID_Translation - Alternative identifier for matching customers

  • InvoiceID - Primary identifier for the invoice

  • InvoiceNum - The invoice number as an alternative way to identify invoices

  • DeliverySequence - The order in which deliveries should be made on a route

  • MoveCustomersInvoices - Controls whether all invoices for a customer should be moved (1) or just the specified invoice (0)

  • TripNumber - Organizes deliveries by trip; helps when multiple trips occur on the same route/day

  • StartTimePlanned - The planned start time for the delivery

  • EndTimePlanned - The planned end time for the delivery

  • RouteID_Translation - Alternative identifier for matching routes

  • DeliveryRepUserID - Updates the delivery rep on the load sheet by matching the UserID.

  • DeliveryRepUserID_Translation - Updates the delivery rep on the load sheet by matching an alternate identifier on the user.

  • VehicleID - Updates the vehicle on the load sheet by matching the VehicleID.

  • VehicleID_Translation - Updates the vehicle on the load sheet by matching an alternate identifier on the vehicle.

Best Practices

Provide at least one way to identify invoices - either InvoiceID, InvoiceNum, or CustomerID + Date

Ensure routes in your import file have unique identifiers that match your system

Check that all customers referenced exist in the system before importing

For sequence-critical operations, always include the DeliverySequence field

When moving multiple invoices:

  • Set MoveCustomersInvoices to 1 to move all invoices for the customer

  • Set MoveCustomersInvoices to 0 to move only the specified invoice

If timing is important, include both StartTimePlanned and EndTimePlanned

For multi-trip routes, use the TripNumber field to organize deliveries properly

Run the import when users aren't actively working with the affected routes to avoid conflicts
