Reference for the Routes EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-create or update routes, stops, customer sequences, schedules and vehicle assignments. Needs the RouteEdit permission; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • You need appropriate permissions to edit routes (RouteEdit permission)

  • Location and route version data must be properly configured in your database

  • User accounts referenced in the import file must exist in the system

  • Activity records must exist for any activity IDs referenced

Steps

The Routes EDBL routine allows importing or updating routes and stops data. This routine handles complex routing configurations including route versions, customer assignments, sequence ordering, and vehicle assignments.

The import process follows these steps:

  1. Processes location data, translating from LocationID_Translation if provided

  2. Sets default route version to 'A' if not specified

  3. Updates existing route versions or creates new ones

  4. Creates missing product groups if needed

  5. Updates route information and bindings

  6. Processes customer assignments to routes

  7. Updates or creates stops based on customer assignments

  8. Updates sequence numbers for stops

  9. Handles customer location moves if requested

  10. Updates the data warehouse

If your implementation uses a Phase-based route system, the Phase field is expected. For Scheduler-based systems, fields like StartOnDate, StartWeekFrom, RepeatEvery, and WeekOfMonth are utilized.

When using MoveCustomers=1, the system will attempt to move customers to the specified location. The area name in the destination location must start with the location name (e.g., "Raleigh Clayton" area would be valid for "Clayton" location).

The ClearStopsWithSameRouteNum flag allows deleting existing stops with the same route number before importing new stops.

Fields And Definitions

Core Routing Information:

  • LocationID_Translation - Text identifier for the location that will be translated to a LocationID

  • LocationID - Integer ID of the location (defaults to the current user's LocationID)

  • RouteVersion - Text identifier for the route version (defaults to 'A')

  • RouteVersionID_Translation - Text that combines location and route version for translation

  • RouteVersionID - Integer ID for the route version

  • RouteTypeID - Integer ID for the route type

  • RouteType - Text name of the route type

  • Route - Text name of the route (generated from RouteNum and day if not provided)

  • RouteNum - Integer identifying the route number

  • DayOfWeek - Integer (1-7) representing day of week (1=Sunday, 7=Saturday)

User Assignment:

  • UserID - Integer ID of the user assigned to the route

  • UserFullName - Text full name of the user (used to look up UserID)

  • UserName - Text username (used to look up UserID)

Customer and Stop Information:

  • CustomerID_Translation - Text identifier for the customer that will be translated to a CustomerID

  • CustomerID - Integer ID of the customer

  • Sequence - Integer determining the delivery sequence for the stop

  • ProductGroupID - Integer ID of the product group

  • ProductGroupID_Translation - Text identifier for product group

  • ProductGroup - Text name of the product group

  • PerpetualInventory - Boolean indicating if perpetual inventory is enabled

Scheduling Fields:

  • Phase - Integer representing the phase (Phase-based routing)

  • StartOnDate - Date when the route starts (Scheduler-based routing)

  • StartWeekFrom - Integer for starting week (Scheduler-based routing)

  • RepeatEvery - Integer for repetition interval (Scheduler-based routing)

  • WeekOfMonth - Integer week of month (Scheduler-based routing)

  • PresellDaysInAdvance - Integer days to presell

Activity Information:

  • ActivityID - Integer ID of the activity

  • Activity - Text name of the activity

  • StopActivityID - Integer ID for stop activity

  • StopActivity - Text name for stop activity

Route Operations:

  • StartTime - Time when the route starts

  • EndTime - Time when the route ends

  • StartMapPoint - Text name of starting map point

  • EndMapPoint - Text name of ending map point

  • VehicleID - Integer ID of the vehicle

  • Vehicle - Text name of the vehicle

  • AssignmentGroup - Text name of assignment group

  • ClearStopsWithSameRouteNum - Integer (0/1) flag to clear existing stops with the same route number

  • MoveCustomers - Integer (0/1) flag to move customers between locations

  • RouteVersionStartDate - Date when the route version starts

Best Practices

  • Always provide a RouteNum and DayOfWeek to ensure routes are properly identified

  • Use LocationID_Translation if importing routes between different environments

  • Set ClearStopsWithSameRouteNum to 1 only when you want to completely replace all stops for a route

  • Provide UserName or UserFullName to ensure routes are assigned to the correct users

  • If moving customers between locations (MoveCustomers=1), ensure area names in the destination location start with the location name

  • Set a valid RouteVersionStartDate when creating a new route version

  • For route scheduling, ensure proper values for Phase (Phase-based) or StartOnDate/StartWeekFrom (Scheduler-based)

  • Use ProductGroup names or IDs to ensure proper product grouping for stops

  • Provide a Sequence value for each stop to maintain the correct delivery order

  • If using TranslationMobilityRouteNum, ensure it matches your mobile system's route numbering

16989933:
Reference for the Remittance EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-import customer payments (checks, EFT, lockbox files) and apply them to open invoices or deposits. Needs AR Apply permission; v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Minimum requirements:

  • Invoice Num or PO Num

  • InvoiceDate

  • PaymentAmount

  • CustomerID/CustomerID_Translation or ARAccountID/ARAccountID_Translation

  • RouteNum or RoutID or RouteID_Translation
    ​
    ​

Optional Fields:

  • PONum

  • AbleCreateMultiDeposits

  • DepositID

  • AutoBalance (default value = True, we can set to false)

  • PaymentTypeID

  • PaymentTypeID_Translation

  • PaymentPONum

  • PaymentLoadSheetDate

  • DoNotRequireInvoiceNums

  • PaymentARNote

  • LocationID/LocationID_Translation

  • CheckNum

  • AutoARWriteOffProductID

  • ProductName

Steps

Overview

The Remittance EDBL routine allows you to import payments against existing invoices or create standalone payment records. This import is primarily used for recording check payments, electronic funds transfers, or other payment methods that were received outside of the system but need to be recorded in Encompass.

Purpose

  • Import payment data to apply against existing invoices

  • Create payment records in the system

  • Optionally add payments to existing deposits

Required Permissions

  • Accounts Receivable Apply permission

Supported Import Actions

  • Add Only

  • Update Only

  • Update or Add

Fields

Required Fields

At minimum, one of these identification combinations is required:

  • CustomerID (or CustomerID_Translation) OR ARAccountID (or ARAccountID_Translation)

  • PaymentAmount

Behavior Details

Invoice Matching Logic

The system uses a multi-step process to match invoices for payment application:

  • Exact Match: Matches on InvoiceNum/PONum, CustomerID/ARAccountID, amount, and date

  • Strong Match: Matches on InvoiceNum/PONum, CustomerID/ARAccountID, and amount

  • Customer/Date Match: Matches on InvoiceNum/PONum, CustomerID/ARAccountID, and date

  • Amount/Date Match: Matches on InvoiceNum/PONum, amount, and date

  • Basic Date Match: Matches on InvoiceNum/PONum and date

  • Customer/Amount Match: Matches on InvoiceNum/PONum, CustomerID/ARAccountID, and amount

  • Basic Customer Match: Matches on InvoiceNum/PONum and CustomerID/ARAccountID

The system only looks back for invoices up to the number of months specified in InvoiceLookupMonthsBack (default: 8 months).

Payment Processing

  1. If an invoice match is found, the payment will be applied to that invoice

  2. If DoNotRequireInvoiceNums = Yes and no match is found, a payment record will still be created

  3. If DoNotRequireInvoiceNums = No and no match is found, that row will be skipped and reported in results

Load Sheet Handling

  • Creates remittance-type load sheets for payment records

  • If AbleCreateMultiDeposits = Yes, creates separate load sheets for each import

  • If AbleCreateMultiDeposits = No, tries to find existing load sheets for the payment date

  • If AutoBalance = Yes, automatically sets load sheets to Balanced status

Deposit Integration

  • If DepositID is provided, payments are added to the specified deposit

  • Deposit must be in "New" status to accept payments

  • Deposit amount is updated with the sum of payments added

Special Notes

  • Route matching first tries to find a remittance-type route, then falls back to any matching route

  • Payment types with RequireCheckNum=1 will default to 'Remit EDBL' for CheckNum if not provided

  • ARAccounts with Terms associated will use the default PaymentType for that Term if not provided

  • If no PaymentType is found, it defaults to 'Cash'

  • The import will fail if attempting to use a DepositID that is not in "New" status

Results and Reporting

The import provides detailed results including:

  • File total amount processed

  • Total payments created amount

  • Total amount applied to invoices

  • List of invoices that could not be found

  • List of payments that could not be created

  • Total amount that could not be processed

Example Use Cases

  • Importing check payments received in the mail

  • Recording batch electronic payments

  • Adding payments to a bank deposit

  • Recording payments against a batch of invoices

Note:

  1. When creating the payment Invoice, the payment Invoice should be created separately according to the Memo field in the import file
    ​
    ​

  2. If customers want to run Remittance EDBL import on the same day and generate multiple LoadSheets, please Add Static Value AbleCreateMultiDeposits=1 in Import Fields. if you only want to generate one Loadsheet, please do not set the value of AbleCreateMultiDeposits.
    ​
    ​

  3. Remittance EDBL: Add Load Sheet Status field to set the status of the created Load Sheet

Fields And Definitions

Best used for:

  • Importing payments to pay open invoices
    ​
    ​

  • Custom remittance processes
    ​
    ​

  • Importing lockbox files

Best Practices

  • Import routines are an incredibly powerful tool and if used incorrectly, can affect a lot of data. Test thoroughly on small data sets before importing.
    ​
    ​

  • If you are running into setup issues or have questions, reach out to Encompass Support.
    ​
    ​

  • Do you have a complex process that consists of a report and import routines that you do not want to set up? Contact our professional services team to assist.

16989935:
Reference for the ImportTasks EDBL import in Encompass: add or update ImportTasks records that track import runs, mapping routine names and statuses. Needs the TableImport permission; v22.01+.

Pre-Conditions

  • User must have TableImport permission to execute this routine

  • The ImportRoutine values must correspond to existing import routines in the system

  • If updating existing records, valid ImportTaskIDs must be provided

Steps

The ImportTasks EDBL routine allows importing or updating records in the ImportTasks table. This table tracks import operations that have been performed in the system. The routine handles mapping external import routine names to internal IDs and manages status values.

When the routine runs:

  1. It translates ImportRoutine names to ImportRoutineID values using table translations

  2. It validates ImportRoutineIDs against existing records in the system

  3. It processes Status and StatusID fields to ensure consistency

  4. It calculates StartDate and EndDate values based on CloseDate or fallback values

  5. It adds or updates records based on your selected import action

Null ImportRoutineID values will occur if the system cannot find a matching import routine. These records will fail validation during import.

Fields And Definitions

ImportTaskID - Integer, primary key of the ImportTasks record. Required for update operations.

ImportRoutine - Text, the name of the import routine to run. This will be translated to an ImportRoutineID using table translations.

CloseDate - Date, when the import task was completed or closed. Used to calculate EndDate.

Status - Text, the status of the import task. Values like "New" will be translated to appropriate StatusID values.

StatusID - Integer, numeric representation of Status. When Status="New", StatusID=0; otherwise StatusID=1.

Generated Fields:

  • StartDate - Calculated as (EndDate + 1 day) or the ImportRoutine creation time

  • EndDate - Set to CloseDate or defaults to 2001-01-01 if not provided

Best Practices

  • Always provide ImportRoutine values that match existing import routines in the system

  • When updating existing tasks, always include the ImportTaskID field

  • For new tasks, set Status to "New" (StatusID=0)

  • For completed tasks, provide a valid CloseDate

  • Ensure external ImportRoutine values have proper translations if they differ from internal names

  • Review any warnings returned by the import process as they may indicate records that were not properly processed

  • Before large imports, test with a small sample to verify field mappings are correct
16989936:
Admin fix for the SQL syntax error ('ORDER BY Companies.Company ASC') when a user creates a password: add a Users Companies record or an AR Account Map for the user's location. Needs Permission Edit or General Accounting perms; v25.04+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.04

Pre-Conditions

To perform the troubleshooting steps, you'll need the following permissions:

  • For Adding Users Locations or Users Companies:

    • Add, View, and Delete Permissions: 'Everyone' permission and 'Permission Edit' permission.

  • For Creating a New AR Account Map:

    • Add and Delete Permissions: 'General Accounting Management'.

    • View Permission: 'General Accounting View'.

Users must have administrative access to modify user settings and location configurations within the system.

Steps

This guide outlines two possible solutions to help resolve a "Syntax Error" that may occur when a user attempts to create a password and log in. This error typically occurs when the system cannot find the user's associated company.
​
​

System Error: "SQL Failed, Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax to use near 'ORDER BY Companies.Company ASC' at line 7 QueryRunSeconds = 0.0xxx PageRunSeconds = 0.000 -- Page: api"
​
​

1. Identify the affected user: Note the name of the user(s) experiencing the syntax error during password creation.
​
2. Access User Record: Navigate to the Users table using the Universal Search bar.
​
3. Attempt Solution 1: Add a User Company:

  • Locate the profile for the affected user
    ​
    ​

  • Subtable "Users Companies"
    ​
    ​

  • Ensure a company is configured and assigned to this user. If not, add or select the correct company
    ​
    ​

  • Save the changes
    ​
    ​

  • Have the user attempt to create their password again

If the Users Companies is properly configured, a company record will exist, and creating the password should work successfully.
​
​

OR

4. Attempt Solution 2: Add an AR Account Map to the User's Location:
​

  • Identify the specific location associated with the user
    ​
    ​

  • Navigate to the affected users record, and subtable "Users Locations"
    ​
    ​

  • Then, navigate to the "AR Account Maps" table
    ​
    ​

  • Ensure an AR Account Map is configured for the user's primary working location
    ​
    ​

  • If an AR Account Map exists for other locations, you may need to create a new one for the problematic location.
    ​
    ​

  • Save the changes
    ​
    ​

  • Have the user attempt to create their password again

If the AR Account Map is configured for the location, the company will be recognized. This should result in successful password creation.
​
​

Please select one of the two options above, then proceed to create the password. Once the password is successfully created, the user will be able to log in.


​If the issue persists:

Please contact support if the issue persists after attempting both solutions, and provide the following information for efficient troubleshooting:

  • The exact error messages or codes encountered (e.g., "SQL Failed, Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax to use near 'ORDER BY Companies.Company ASC' at line 7").

  • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue, particularly of the error message and the locked webpage.

  • Log files (if accessible and relevant to user creation/login).

  • The exact steps taken by you and the new user that led to the issue.

  • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

  • Any changes made to the system (e.g., new user added, location created) before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • Syntax Error: An error in the structure or grammar of a command or statement, often in a programming language or database query (like SQL). In this context, it indicates a problem with how the system is trying to process information related to the user's company.

  • SQL (Structured Query Language): A standard language used to communicate with and manage relational databases. The error message indicates an issue with a database query.

  • Users Companies: A system setting or field that links a specific user account to an organizational company within the system. This is crucial for defining user permissions and data access.

  • AR Account Map: A configuration within the system that maps an Accounts Receivable (AR) account to a specific location. This mapping helps the system identify and associate financial transactions and company information with that location.

Best Practices

  • Verify Company Association: Always ensure that users (especially new users) are correctly associated with their respective companies and locations during the user creation process to prevent future login and password creation issues.

  • Complete Location Configurations: Before onboarding new employees to specific locations, confirm that all necessary configurations, such as AR Account Maps, are in place for those locations.

Steps

Overview

The AccountsRecPaymentApplication EDBL routine allows you to import payment application data that links payment invoices to regular invoices. This routine effectively records how payments are applied to outstanding invoices in your accounts receivable system.

Key Features

  • Creates payment records and applies them to invoices

  • Updates payment application amounts on existing records

  • Manages the connection between payments and invoices

  • Updates invoice open balances to reflect payments

  • Creates necessary load sheets for payment processing

Process Flow

  1. Matching Existing Records: The system first attempts to match payment applications to existing records if you provide IDs.

  2. Date Handling: If only one date is provided (either PaymentDate or InvoiceDate), the missing date will default to the provided date.

  3. Load Sheet Management: The system: Creates new load sheets for payments if needed, Sets load sheet status appropriately for payment processing

  4. Customer/AR Account Resolution: If CustomerID is provided, ARAccountID will be set to the customer's default AR account, If ARAccountID is provided, CustomerID will be set to the AR account's associated customer

  5. Payment Creation: Finds existing payment invoices that match the import data, Creates new payment invoices when needed

  6. Payment Application: Links payments to invoices, Updates the amount applied on each connection, Updates invoice receipts and open balances

Behavior by Import Action

  • Add Only: Creates new payment application records, load sheets, and payment invoices as needed

  • Update Only: Updates existing payment application amounts and related records

  • Add or Update: Both adds new records and updates existing ones as appropriate

Special Behaviors

  • When payment records are created, the system will properly update all related invoice records

  • The system handles both new payments and updating existing payment applications

  • If InvoicePaymentsID or InvoicePaymentsHistID are provided, the system will update those specific records

  • Automatically updates open balances on invoices after applying payments

  • Sets the Payment_ImportGroupID to distinguish sets of imported payments

Troubleshooting

  • If the routine returns "InvoiceID or PaymentInvoiceID IS NULL," it means the system could not find or create appropriate links between payments and invoices

  • Verify that your invoice numbers, AR accounts, or customer IDs match existing records in the system

  • Check that payment dates and invoice dates are within expected ranges

Related Database Impact

The routine affects the following tables:

  • Invoice

  • LoadSheet

  • InvoicePayments

  • InvoicePaymentsHist

Example Use Cases

  • Importing payment application data from an external accounting system

  • Mass updating how payments were applied to invoices

  • Rolling back AR to previous periods by importing historical payment applications

Note:

  1. If we do not map Payment Invoice ID/PaymentInvoiceNum, we need map Customer ID or ARAccount ID
    ​
    ​

  2. If you really want to import against InvoicePayments directly then that works but need to make sure to recalculate Open Balances after. because in the logic of the AccountsRecPaymentApplication EDBL, we did not call the Set_Invoice_OpenDebitCredit method of recalculating OpenDebit and OpenCredit,the user needs to manually run the Scheduled Task Update_OpenCredit_OpenDebit after execution.
    ​
    ​

  3. AccountsRecPaymentApplication doesn’t care about InvoicePaymentHist/InvoicePayment, If the value in the import file is 200, then the inserted invoicePayment is 200

Fields And Definitions

Best used for:

    ​

  • Data conversions

Reference for the StoreDepletions EDBL import in Encompass: load retail scanner data (e.g. Walmart Retail Link) by UPC and chain store number to track store sales and inventory. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • The product UPCs in your import file must exist in your system (matched via the BarCodeSearch table)

  • The chain store numbers in your import file must exist in your system (matched to Customers)

  • The product/customer combinations must exist in CustomerHistory and be authorized

  • User must have appropriate permissions to run imports and edit store depletion data

Steps

The StoreDepletions EDBL routine imports scanner data from retail systems (like Walmart's Retail Link) to track actual sales of products at retail locations. This data is used to predict future orders and maintain inventory accuracy.

The import routine attempts to find matching records in the following order:

  1. Maps UPC codes to ProductIDs using the BarCodeSearch table

  2. Maps ChainStoreNumbers to CustomerIDs in the Customers table

  3. Validates that the customer/product combinations exist in CustomerHistory and are authorized

  4. Updates or adds records to the StoreDepletions table based on your selected import action

If POSInventory data is included, the routine can update the Inventory and InvDate fields in CustomerHistory to reflect the latest retail inventory levels.

Fields And Definitions

Required Fields:

  • Date - The date of the depletion record

  • CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation - The ID of the customer in your system (can be matched from ChainStoreNumber)

  • ProductID or ProductID_Translation - The ID of the product in your system (can be matched from UPC)

Common Fields:

  • ChainStoreNumber - The identifier for the store in the retail chain's system

  • UPC - Universal Product Code for the product

  • NumUnits - Number of units sold/depleted

  • Inventory - Current inventory level in wholesale units

  • POSNumUnits - Point of Sale number of units sold

  • POSInventory - Point of Sale current inventory level

  • IsRetailUnit - Flag indicating if the units are retail (will be converted to wholesale)

Best Practices

  • Include UPC codes when possible as they provide the most reliable product matching

  • Include chain store numbers to accurately match to customer records

  • If providing quantities in retail units, set IsRetailUnit to 1 (the system will convert to wholesale units)

  • Include POSInventory data when available to keep CustomerHistory inventory levels accurate

  • Ensure all products and customers in your import file exist in your system before importing

  • Review customer authorization status before importing - only authorized product/customer combinations will be imported

  • For large chains, test with a small subset of stores first to ensure proper matching

  • When possible, include both sales (NumUnits/POSNumUnits) and inventory data (Inventory/POSInventory) in the same file for complete tracking

If you encounter missing records in your import, verify that:

  • The products exist in your system and have correct UPCs

  • The customers exist with matching chain store numbers

  • The product/customer combinations are authorized in CustomerHistory

Reference for the PurchaseByAccounts EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-import non-inventory purchases (services, one-time bills) charged straight to GL accounts. Needs Pay Bills permission and AP enabled; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • You must have Pay Bills permission to run this routine

  • Companies should be properly configured in the system

  • The import action is fixed to "Update or Add"

  • Accounts Payable should be enabled in Encompass

Steps

The PurchaseByAccounts EDBL routine allows importing purchase transactions with direct GL account assignments. This routine creates shipments, purchases, and corresponding journal entries in a single import.

The import process:

  1. Validates all required data (PostDate, AccountID, etc.)

  2. Creates any missing vendors if specified by VendorID_Translation

  3. Creates shipments for each unique combination of ShipmentNum, ReceiveDate, and LocationID

  4. Creates purchase records linked to these shipments

  5. Creates or updates journal entry transactions for accounting purposes

  6. Updates purchase statuses to the imported status level

The system will first attempt to match existing shipments and purchases by shipment number, invoice number, PO number, vendor, and date. When no matches are found, new records will be created.

Vendors specified by VendorID_Translation that don't exist in the system will be automatically created with minimal information. It's recommended to set up vendors before running this import.

All imported shipments will have ShipmentType = Imported_Accounts and will be tagged with the EDBLSourceID and ImportGroupID for future reference.

Fields And Definitions

Required Fields:

  • PostDate - Date when the purchase will be posted to the GL

  • AccountID - GL account to which the purchase will be charged (or AccountID_Translation)

  • VendorID - Vendor providing the purchase (or VendorID_Translation)

  • CompanyID - Company for the transaction (defaults to user's company if not specified)

Key Fields:

  • ImportGroupID - Groups imports together (defaults to "1" if not specified)

  • InvoiceNum - Invoice number for the purchase

  • PONum - PO number for the purchase

  • ShipmentNum - Identifier for the shipment

  • ReceiveDate - Date when goods were received

  • LocationID - Location receiving the goods (defaults to user's location)

  • Debit/Credit - Amount values for the transaction

  • ShipmentStatus - Status of the shipment (defaults to Confirmed)

  • PurchaseMemo - Notes for the purchase

Optional Fields:

  • InvoiceDate - Date of the invoice

  • DueDate - Date when payment is due

  • JournalEntryTransMemo - Description for journal entries

  • FinancialDimensionID_XXXX - Financial dimension assignments

  • CustomField fields - Additional custom field values

Best Practices

  • Always include PostDate, AccountID, and VendorID or their Translation fields

  • Use unique ShipmentNum, InvoiceNum, and PONum values to avoid duplicates

  • Group related records with the same ImportGroupID value

  • Set up vendors before running the import when possible

  • Ensure the PostDate is after the company's Purchase Close Date

  • If using AccountID_Translation, make sure the account mappings exist

  • Set ShipmentStatus to match your workflow needs

  • If importing multiple currencies, ensure exchange rates are properly configured

  • Confirm financial dimensions exist in the system before referencing them

  • The lowest acceptable ShipmentStatus value is "Received" - lower status values will cause import failure

When using this import to create purchase records, the system will create appropriate journal entries to maintain General Ledger balance. The purchase records will be created with transaction type "Accounts" to distinguish them from inventory purchases.

This import can be used for one-time purchases, service purchases, and any non-inventory purchases that need to be directly recorded to GL accounts.

16989943:
How to fix duplicate payments and incorrect AR credits created by an 820 remittance file: unapply credits, re-invoice on a load sheet, reapply payments, and offset the bad deposit with a negative deposit.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

  • You have identified invoices with duplicate payment applications.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer accounts are showing incorrect balances with credits equal to the originally debited amount.

Steps

  1. Identify the Affected Invoices: Compile a list of all invoices that are showing duplicate payments and the resulting incorrect AR credits. Note the invoice numbers and the affected customer accounts.
    ​
    ​

  2. Unapply Payments from Incorrect Credit Invoices: For each affected customer account, locate the incorrect credit invoices that were generated. Unapply any payments that were applied to these credit invoices.
    ​
    ​

  3. Create Load Sheets and Corresponding Invoices: For each payment that was incorrectly applied (and now unapplied from the credit invoice), create a new load sheet and corresponding debit invoice for the correct amount that should have been originally applied to the customer's account. Ensure these new invoices are for the correct invoice date .
    ​
    ​

  4. Apply Payments to the Correct Invoices: Apply the payments (either manually or through a payment processing function) to the newly created debit invoices. This will correctly reflect the payment against the original outstanding balance.
    ​
    ​

  5. Create a Negative Deposit: To offset the incorrect deposit created by the erroneous credit invoices, create a negative deposit for the total amount of the incorrect credits. Ensure this negative deposit is applied to the same deposit account where the incorrect deposit was initially recorded.
    ​
    ​

  6. Review and Verify: After completing the above steps, carefully review the affected customer accounts to ensure the duplicate payments are resolved and the AR credits have been correctly offset. Verify that the invoice balances now accurately reflect the outstanding amounts.
    ​
    ​

  7. Contact Support (If Issue Persists): If you encounter difficulties with any of the above steps or the issue persists after attempting these corrections, contact the Encompass Technologies Support team for further assistance. Please provide the following information to expedite the troubleshooting process:
    ​
    ​

    • A list of the affected invoice numbers and customer account IDs.
      ​
      ​

    • Details of the steps you have already taken to attempt to resolve the issue.
      ​
      ​

    • The Exchange Task numbers associated with the initial invoice submission and the subsequent remittance files (e.g., Exchange Task 22946, 22950, and 23052).
      ​
      ​

    • The deposit number associated with the incorrect credits (e.g., Deposits - 5544).
      ​
      ​

    • Any screenshots or documentation that illustrate the problem.

Fields And Definitions

  • 820 Post: Refers to the electronic remittance advice (ERA) file that provides details about payments made by customers.
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice: A commercial document issued by a seller to a buyer, indicating the products, quantities, and agreed prices for products or services the seller has provided the buyer.
    ​
    ​

  • AR (Accounts Receivable): The balance of money due to a company for goods or services delivered or used but not yet paid for by customers.
    ​
    ​

  • Credit Invoice: An invoice issued to reduce the amount a customer owes, often due to returns, overpayments, or errors. In this context, incorrect credit invoices were generated in error.
    ​
    ​

  • Load Sheet: A document used to record and track payments received, often used as a batch for processing deposits and applying payments to invoices.
    ​
    ​

  • Deposit: The act of placing funds into a bank account. In this context, a deposit record is created to account for customer payments.
    ​
    ​

  • Negative Deposit: A transaction used to reduce the balance of a bank deposit, often used to correct errors in previously recorded deposits.
    ​
    ​

  • Exchange Task: A system-generated identifier for specific data transfer or processing tasks within the software.
    ​
    ​

  • End Of Day Rollback: A system function that allows users to revert the system's data to a previous point in time, typically the end of a specific business day.

Best Practices

  • Timely Reconciliation: Regularly reconcile your accounts receivable and bank deposits to identify and address any discrepancies promptly.
    ​
    ​

  • User Training: Ensure all users involved in payment processing are adequately trained on the correct procedures for applying payments and handling remittance files.
    ​
    ​

  • Understanding System Notifications: Pay close attention to any system notifications or alerts related to invoice processing and investigate any unusual occurrences immediately.
    ​
    ​

  • Test in a Non-Production Environment (If Available): If your system has a non-production or test environment, consider replicating the issue and testing the correction steps there before implementing them in your live environment.

Reference for the PurchaseRemittance EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-import vendor bill payments against existing purchase invoices, with bank account assignment. Needs Apply AR permission; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • You must have the "Apply Accounts Receivables" permission to use this routine.

  • The purchase invoices you want to pay must already exist in the system.

  • You must provide PaymentDate and PaymentAmount for each payment you want to import.

  • The Location referenced in your import must exist.

Steps

The PurchaseRemittance EDBL routine allows you to import payment information for existing purchase invoices. It creates payment records for purchases that have already been entered into the system.

When you run this routine:

1. The system tries to find the existing purchases by matching:

  • First by PurchaseID (if provided)

  • Then by matching InvoiceNum + ShipmentID

  • Then by InvoiceNum + LocationID + approximate ReceiveDate

  • Finally by PurchaseTotal + VendorNum combination

2. If an existing purchase is found, the system:

  • Creates a payment shipment record with ShipmentType of BillPayment

  • Creates a payment purchase record

  • Links the payment to the original purchase

  • Updates the payment amount on the original purchase

3. If BankAccountID or BankAccountID_Translation is provided, the payment is assigned to that bank account.

If a purchase can't be found for a payment, the import will fail with an error message showing the invoices that couldn't be found.

Fields And Definitions

Required Fields:

  • PaymentAmount - The amount being paid on the purchase invoice

  • PaymentDate - The date the payment was made

Fields to Identify Purchases:

  • PurchaseID - Direct identifier for the purchase to be paid

  • InvoiceNum - Invoice number of the purchase to be paid

  • ShipmentID - The shipment ID associated with the purchase to be paid

  • VendorNum - Vendor number (used with PurchaseTotal to identify purchases)

  • PurchaseTotal - Total amount of the purchase (used with VendorNum to identify purchases)

Optional Fields:

  • LocationID - The location where the purchase was made (defaults to current user's location)

  • LocationID_Translation - Name of the location to translate to LocationID

  • ReceiveDate - The date the purchase was received

  • Memo - Notes or comments about the payment

  • BankAccountID - The GL bank account used for the payment

  • BankAccountID_Translation - Name of the bank account to translate to BankAccountID

System Fields (not typically mapped):

  • PaymentShipmentID - System-assigned ID for the payment shipment

  • PaymentPurchaseID - System-assigned ID for the payment purchase

  • VendorID - The vendor's system ID

Best Practices

  • Always include enough information to uniquely identify the purchases you're paying. The most reliable method is using PurchaseID.

  • If you don't know the PurchaseID, provide a combination of InvoiceNum, VendorNum, and PurchaseTotal.

  • Group payments by payment date and location for easier tracking.

  • Include the Memo field with a description of the payment batch to help with reconciliation.

  • When importing multiple payments, ensure the file is sorted by payment date for easier troubleshooting.

  • If your company uses multiple bank accounts, always specify the BankAccountID or BankAccountID_Translation to ensure payments are posted to the correct account.

  • After importing, verify that all payments were applied correctly by checking the original purchases.

Reference for the ZeroAccountsPayable EDBL routine in Encompass: zero out open balances on AP records imported by EDBL for an ImportGroupID. Needs GeneralAccountingEdit permission and AP enabled; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Accounts Payable module must be enabled in Encompass to use this routine

  • You must have the GeneralAccountingEdit permission to run this routine

  • Typically used after importing purchases through the AccountsPayable EDBL routine

Steps

The ZeroAccountsPayable routine clears (zeroes out) the open balances of previously imported Accounts Payable records. This is useful when you need to reset the balances of imported AP transactions to reflect that they have been fully paid.

This routine works by:

  1. Finding all imported purchases associated with the specified ImportGroupID and EDBLSourceID

  2. Setting the Payment amount equal to the PurchaseTotal (making it fully paid)

  3. Setting OpenCredit and OpenDebit values to zero

  4. Removing any existing payment applications

  5. Recalculating AP terms and due dates

  6. The routine only affects purchases that were previously imported via EDBL with the specified ImportGroupID. It will not modify purchases created manually in the system or imported with a different ImportGroupID.

Fields And Definitions

ImportGroupID - Integer, Default: 1

  • Identifies which group of imports to zero out

  • If not specified, defaults to 1

  • If set to NULL in the import file, the routine will zero out purchases where ImportGroupID is NULL

Note: This routine doesn't require a detailed data file. A simple file with just an ImportGroupID column is sufficient, as the actual work is performed based on existing data in the system.

Best Practices

  • This routine is a special process used for odd data situations, not normally run

  • Consider creating separate ImportGroupIDs for different import sources or cycles to allow targeted zeroing of specific imports

  • Before running this routine, make sure any payment applications you want to keep are not associated with the ImportGroupID you're zeroing out

  • This routine is often used when replacing previously imported AP data with a fresh import, rather than trying to calculate differences

  • Always verify your AP balances after running this routine to ensure the expected records were zeroed out

  • This routine permanently changes your AP data - consider backing up your data or testing in a non-production environment first

Troubleshooting for the SQL syntax error ('ORDER BY Companies.Company') when a user creates a password: add a Users Companies record or an AR Account Map for the user's location. Needs Permission Edit or General Accounting Management, v25.04+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.04

Pre-Conditions

To perform the troubleshooting steps, you'll need the following permissions:

  • For Adding Users Locations or Users Companies:

    • Add, View, and Delete Permissions: 'Everyone' permission and 'Permission Edit' permission.

  • For Creating a New AR Account Map:

    • Add and Delete Permissions: 'General Accounting Management'.

    • View Permission: 'General Accounting View'.

Users must have administrative access to modify user settings and location configurations within the system.

Steps

This guide outlines two possible solutions to help resolve a "Syntax Error" that may occur when a user attempts to create a password and log in. This error typically occurs when the system cannot find the user's associated company.
​
​

System Error: "SQL Failed, Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax to use near 'ORDER BY Companies.Company ASC' at line 7 QueryRunSeconds = 0.0xxx PageRunSeconds = 0.000 -- Page: api"
​
​

1. Identify the affected user: Note the name of the user(s) experiencing the syntax error during password creation.

2. Access User Record: Navigate to the Users table using the Universal Search bar.

3. Attempt Solution 1: Add a User Company:

  • Locate the profile for the affected user

  • Subtable "Users Companies"

  • Ensure a company is configured and assigned to this user. If not, add or select the correct company

  • Save the changes

  • Have the user attempt to create their password again

If the Users Companies is properly configured, a company record will exist, and creating the password should work successfully.
​
​

OR

4. Attempt Solution 2: Add an AR Account Map to the User's Location:
​

  • Identify the specific location associated with the user

  • Navigate to the affected users record, and subtable "Users Locations"

  • Then, navigate to the "AR Account Maps" table

  • Ensure an AR Account Map is configured for the user's primary working location

  • If an AR Account Map exists for other locations, you may need to create a new one for the problematic location.

  • Save the changes

​
​

Please select one of the two options above, then proceed to create the password. Once the password is successfully created, the user will be able to log in.


​If the issue persists:

Please contact support if the issue persists after attempting both solutions, and provide the following information for efficient troubleshooting:

  • The exact error messages or codes encountered (e.g., "SQL Failed, Error: You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your MySQL server version for the right syntax to use near 'ORDER BY Companies.Company ASC' at line 7").

  • Screenshots or video recordings of the issue, particularly of the error message and the locked webpage.

  • Log files (if accessible and relevant to user creation/login).

  • The exact steps taken by you and the new user that led to the issue.

  • The date and time the issue was first observed and any recurrence.

  • Any changes made to the system (e.g., new user added, location created) before the issue appeared.

Fields And Definitions

  • Syntax Error: An error in the structure or grammar of a command or statement, often in a programming language or database query (like SQL). In this context, it indicates a problem with how the system is trying to process information related to the user's company.

  • SQL (Structured Query Language): A standard language used to communicate with and manage relational databases. The error message indicates an issue with a database query.

  • Users Companies: A system setting or field that links a specific user account to an organizational company within the system. This is crucial for defining user permissions and data access.

  • AR Account Map: A configuration within the system that maps an Accounts Receivable (AR) account to a specific location. This mapping helps the system identify and associate financial transactions and company information with that location.

Best Practices

  • Verify Company Association: Always ensure that users (especially new users) are correctly associated with their respective companies and locations during the user creation process to prevent future login and password creation issues.

  • Complete Location Configurations: Before onboarding new employees to specific locations, confirm that all necessary configurations, such as AR Account Maps, are in place for those locations.

  • Test User Creation: After making system-wide changes or updates, it's a good practice to test the user creation and login workflow with a test account or site to identify potential issues proactively.

16989950:
Reference for the AccountsPayable EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-import vendor bills with open balances, terms and currency, creating missing vendors. Needs GeneralAccountingEdit permission and AP enabled; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Accounts Payable module must be enabled in your system

  • Vendors should exist in your system, though the routine can create missing vendors

  • User must have the GeneralAccountingEdit permission

  • If using currency features, the Currency module must be enabled and currencies must exist

Steps

The AccountsPayable EDBL routine imports accounts payable transactions (bills) that your company owes to vendors. It handles:

  1. Creating or updating purchase records and their associated shipments

  2. Setting payment information, including open balances

  3. Creating vendor records if they don't exist

  4. Handling payment applications

  5. Managing multi-currency transactions (if enabled)

The routine matches to existing purchases using:

  • Transaction ID (TxnID) and Vendor ID (with matching date)

  • Invoice number and Vendor ID (with matching date)

  • Shipment ID and Vendor ID

When creating new purchases, the routine:

  • Creates shipment records with Shipment Type = "Imported Inventory"

  • Creates purchase records with appropriate vendor and invoice information

  • Sets AP terms and due dates

  • Updates open balances

The "ZeroImportedAccountsPayable" option, when set to "1", will zero out previously imported AP records from the same import group. This is useful when completely replacing AP data rather than adding to it.

Fields And Definitions

Required Fields:

  • VendorID/VendorID_Translation - The vendor who issued the bill

  • InvoiceNum - The invoice number (will default to PONum if missing)

  • OpenBalance - The amount still owed on this invoice

Key Optional Fields:

  • ImportGroupID - Groups imports together (defaults to "1")

  • CompanyID/CompanyID_Translation - Company identifier (defaults to user's company)

  • Date/InvoiceDate - Date of purchase/invoice (they default to each other if one is missing)

  • DateMMDDYY/DateYYYYMMDD - Alternative date formats that will be converted

  • PONum - Purchase order number

  • Memo - Notes about the transaction

  • APAccountID - Accounts payable account

  • CheckNum - Check number for payments

  • APTerm - Payment terms

  • DaysOfCredit - Credit terms days

  • ZeroImportedAccountsPayable - Set to "1" to zero out prior imported AP

  • LocationID/LocationID_Translation - Location identifier

Vendor Creation Fields:

  • Address, Address2, City, State, PostalCode - Vendor address details

  • ListID, LicenseNum - External identifiers for the vendor

Multi-Currency Fields:

  • CurrencyID/CurrencyID_Translation - Currency identifier (if multi-currency enabled)

  • ExchangeRate - Exchange rate for currency conversion (defaults to "1")

Best Practices

  • Always include date fields - While the system provides defaults, explicit dates ensure accuracy

  • Provide vendor information - If vendor IDs don't match, include VendorID_Translation to link to existing vendors

  • Group related imports - Use consistent ImportGroupID values to keep related imports together

  • Check ZeroImportedAccountsPayable setting - Only set to "1" when you want to clear previous imports

  • Verify vendors first - Import vendors before accounts payable to ensure proper linking

  • Include invoice numbers - Without InvoiceNum, matching to existing purchases becomes difficult

  • Set company information - If you have multiple companies, explicitly set CompanyID to ensure correct company assignment

  • Import in batches - For large datasets, consider breaking imports into manageable chunks by date range

  • Review translations - If imports fail to match existing records, check TableTranslations for proper mapping

16989953:
Explains email bounce types (Permanent, Transient, Undetermined) and subtypes for failed messages in Encompass, and when to remove an address or retry. Requires v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

  • An email has bounced and on the messages table, the message shows as failed
    ​
    ​

  • There is an error message on the message that failed

Steps

Bounce types

  • The bounce object contains a bounce type of Undetermined, Permanent, or Transient. The Permanent and Transient bounce types can also contain one of several bounce subtypes.
    ​
    ​

  • When you receive a bounce notification with a bounce type of Transient, you might be able to send email to that recipient in the future if the issue that caused the message to bounce is resolved.
    ​

  • When you receive a bounce notification with a bounce type of Permanent, it's unlikely that you'll be able to send email to that recipient in the future. For this reason, you should immediately remove the recipient whose address produced the bounce from your mailing lists.

Fields And Definitions

Format:
​
​

bounceTypebounceSubType

  • Description

UndeterminedUndetermined

  • The recipient's email provider sent a bounce message. The bounce message didn't contain enough information for Amazon SES to determine the reason for the bounce. The bounce email, which was sent to the address in the Return-Path header of the email that resulted in the bounce, might contain additional information about the issue that caused the email to bounce.

PermanentGeneral

  • The recipient's email provider sent a hard bounce message.

Important

  • When you receive this type of bounce notification, you should immediately remove the recipient's email address from your mailing list. Sending messages to addresses that produce hard bounces can have a negative impact on your reputation as a sender. If you continue sending email to addresses that produce hard bounces, we might pause your ability to send additional email. See Using the Amazon SES account-level suppression list.

PermanentNoEmail

  • It was not possible to retrieve the recipient email address from the bounce message.

PermanentSuppressed

  • The recipient's email address is on the Amazon SES suppression list because it has a recent history of producing hard bounces. To override the global suppression list, see Using the Amazon SES account-level suppression list.

PermanentOnAccountSuppressionList

  • Amazon SES has suppressed sending to this address because it is on the account-level suppression list. This does not count toward your bounce rate metric.

TransientGeneral

  • The recipient's email provider sent a general bounce message. You might be able to send a message to the same recipient in the future if the issue that caused the message to bounce is resolved.

Note

  • If you send an email to a recipient who has an active automatic response rule (such as an "out of the office" message), you might receive this type of notification. Even though the response has a notification type of Bounce, Amazon SES doesn't count automatic responses when it calculates the bounce rate for your account.

TransientMailboxFull

  • The recipient's email provider sent a bounce message because the recipient's inbox was full. You might be able to send to the same recipient in the future when the mailbox is no longer full.

TransientMessageTooLarge

  • The recipient's email provider sent a bounce message because message you sent was too large. You might be able to send a message to the same recipient if you reduce the size of the message.

TransientContentRejected

  • The recipient's email provider sent a bounce message because the message you sent contains content that the provider doesn't allow. You might be able to send a message to the same recipient if you change the content of the message.

TransientAttachmentRejected

  • The recipient's email provider sent a bounce message because the message contained an unacceptable attachment. For example, some email providers may reject messages with attachments of a certain file type, or messages with very large attachments. You might be able to send a message to the same recipient if you remove or change the content of the attachment.
16989954:
Reference for the InvoicesAndPayments EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-create or update invoices and their payments in one file, matched by customer and invoice number. Needs InvoiceEdit permission; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • User must have InvoiceEdit permission to run this routine

  • At least one identifier for customers (CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation) is required

  • Date information must be provided in at least one supported format

  • If updating existing invoices, enough identifying information must be included to locate them

Steps

The InvoicesAndPayments EDBL routine imports invoice data and can also process associated payments in a single file. This routine handles both creating new invoices and updating existing ones.

The system performs these operations:

  1. Resolves customer information using CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation

  2. Sets LocationID from the customer record if not explicitly provided

  3. Processes date fields (using Date, DateYYYYMMDD, DateMMDDYY, or DateYYMMDD formats)

  4. Attempts to find existing invoices by matching CustomerID and InvoiceNum

  5. If RouteNum is provided (without RouteID), finds appropriate routes matching date and location

  6. Creates or updates loadsheets and invoices as needed

  7. For invoices marked as Paid, automatically processes payment information

When matching existing invoices, the system uses multiple fields for identification:

  • CustomerID + HandHeldInvoiceNum

  • Date + CustomerID + InvoiceNum

If the import action is "Add Only" and matching invoices exist, those records are skipped. For "Update Only", the system will only modify existing invoices. With "Update or Add", the system updates existing invoices or creates new ones as needed.

Fields And Definitions

Identifiers:

  • CustomerID - Integer, system ID of the customer

  • CustomerID_Translation - Text, external identifier for the customer used for matching

  • InvoiceID - Integer, system ID of the invoice

  • InvoiceNum - Text, invoice number (defaulted to "0" if not provided)

  • LoadSheetID - Integer, system ID of the load sheet

  • TranslationInvoiceNum - Text, external invoice number for translation

Date Fields (provide at least one):

  • Date - Standard date format

  • DateYYYYMMDD - Text, date in YYYYMMDD format

  • DateMMDDYY - Text, date in MMDDYY format

  • DateYYMMDD - Text, date in YYMMDD format

Location Information:

  • LocationID - Integer, defaults to user's location if not provided

  • LocationID_Translation - Text, external identifier for location used for matching

Route Information:

  • RouteID - Integer, system ID of the route

  • RouteNum - Text, route number used to look up RouteID if not provided

  • RoutingMethod - Integer, method to use for routing

Status Fields:

  • Paid - Yes/No, indicates if the invoice is paid

  • Locked - Yes/No, indicates if the invoice is locked

  • EDIStatus - Integer, electronic document interchange status

Amount Fields:

  • InvoiceTotal - Currency, total amount of the invoice

  • Receipt - Currency, payment amount

Additional Information:

  • PONum - Text, purchase order number

  • Memo - Text, additional notes

  • CheckNum - Text, check number for payment

  • Deliveryman - Text, person delivering the order

  • Salesman - Text, sales representative

  • SalesmanActual - Text, actual sales representative who fulfilled the order

  • ServerInvoiceID - Integer, server-side invoice ID

  • ServerLoadSheetID - Integer, server-side load sheet ID

Best Practices

  • Always include CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation for proper customer identification

  • Provide date information in a consistent format across all records

  • Use unique InvoiceNum values that match your existing invoice numbering system

  • When importing from another system, use consistent translation values for seamless matching

  • Set Paid to "Yes" only when you're actually including payment information

  • Include RouteNum if you want to associate invoices with specific routes

  • For recurring imports, maintain consistent naming conventions for easy tracking

  • If updating existing invoices, include enough identifying information to ensure the correct invoice is matched

16989957:
Distributor troubleshooting for invoices that won't palletize in Encompass: check product dimensions, pick type, cases per pallet/layer, bin inventory and pick rules. Requires v25.02+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.02

Steps

Issues with palletization of an invoice can be caused by many different things. A couple of requirements in order to palletize a product on an invoice is that the product has dimensions on the Product record. Those fields are Height, Width and Length and it is okay if those fields are blank which means the system will take what is on the Package but they cannot be 0. Also a Product Pick Type is required and that is brought through the Product Type on the Product record or set on the Inventory record for the Product. If an error message appears that is confusing without progressing to the next screen it could be because the fields Cases per Pallet or Cases Per Layer on the Purchase Transactions of the Products being palletized or the Product record itself are 0. These fields cannot be 0 they must be blank or the correct value (those fields on the Purchase Transactions can be blank so the system will then look at those fields on the Product record).

A common error message that comes up when trying to palletize an invoice that prevents the palletization is below:

​Warning:
​
​

  • The system could not apply Pick Rules to the following Products because current Bin Inventory does not exist, is inactive, OR does not have Pick Rules.
    ​
    ​

  • This will cause routes to be less than 100% printed and confirmed.

FIX:

1. Do an inventory count for the Product's current Bin Inventory
​
2. add a new Pick Rule for the Product's current Bin Inventory
​
3. Please run 'Apply Pick Rules' again.

If all 3 of the options are checked and confirmed to not be stopping the products listed from palletizing, the next thing is to check the Invoice Transaction records for the invoice and products listed and the field Purchase Trans ID Locked. If the field Purchase Trans ID Locked = Purchase Trans Assigned, Encompass will need to get involved to edit those to “No”. Then palletization should proceed.
16989958:
Reference for the InvoicePromoOverrides EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-apply promotion price overrides (unit price, full price, discount) to existing invoice lines. Needs PromoOverride permission; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • User must have the PromoOverride permission to access this routine.

  • Invoice transactions must already exist in the system.

  • Promotions must already exist in the system.

  • This routine requires mapping to at least InvoiceTransID and PromotionID fields.

Steps

The InvoicePromoOverrides routine allows users to import and apply promotion overrides to existing invoice transactions. This routine enables you to override pricing information for specific invoice transactions by associating them with promotions and defining custom pricing values.

When executed, this routine will:

  1. Look up existing invoice transactions based on the provided InvoiceTransID.

  2. Associate the specified promotion (PromotionID) with these transactions.

  3. Apply the provided pricing overrides (UnitPrice, FullPrice, and/or Discount).

Fields And Definitions

InvoiceTransID (Integer) - Required

  • The unique identifier for the invoice transaction to which the promotion override will be applied.

  • This field is required to identify which specific line item within an invoice should receive the promotion override.

PromotionID (Integer) - Required

  • The identifier for the promotion to apply to the invoice transaction.

  • The promotion must already exist in the system.

UnitPrice (Currency)

  • The overridden unit price for the invoice transaction.

  • This represents the final price after all discounts have been applied.

FullPrice (Currency)

  • The full price before discounts are applied.

Discount (Currency)

  • The discount amount to apply to the full price.

Best Practices

Use consistent pricing logic: When importing data, ensure that the relationship between FullPrice, Discount, and UnitPrice is consistent (FullPrice - Discount = UnitPrice). If all three fields are provided, the system will use the provided values.

Validate before importing: Before importing, verify that all InvoiceTransIDs exist in the system. Non-existent transaction IDs will be skipped during the import process.

Verify promotions: Ensure that all PromotionIDs in your import file correspond to valid promotions in the system. Invalid promotion IDs will not be applied.

Consider incremental imports: For large datasets, consider breaking your import file into smaller batches to minimize processing time and resource usage.

Check results: After import, review the results to ensure all promotion overrides were applied correctly. Look for any warnings or errors in the import results.

Maintain audit trail: Document when and why promotion overrides were imported to maintain a clear audit trail for pricing changes.

Test in non-production: Before running in a production environment, test the import in a test/staging environment to verify the expected behavior

Producer steps for Purchase Contract Edit: add a contract period with start/end dates, add products with per-unit or lump sum pricing, and add freight or other contract costs by vendor. Requires v25.01+.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

1. Click on Add a Contract Period from the Purchase Contract Edit screen.
​
2. Enter a Name in the Contract Period field.
​
3. Enter a Start Date.
​
​4. Enter an End Date.
​
​5. Add the Contract Period by clicking Add.
​
6. Click the open field in the Product column to search for a product.
​
​

  • You can search by the product name or by the supplier product number.
    ​
    ​

7. Enter the Quantity you are contracted to purchase.
​
8. Click the edit pencil next to 'Price per Unit' to enter a per-unit price.
​
​

  • Note: If you are entering a lump sum, move on to the 'Enter lump sum pricing' step (10).
    ​
    ​

9. Click the open field in the 'Price per Unit' column to enter the unit pricing.

10. To enter a lump sum price for this product, click the edit pencil next to 'Extended price'.
​
​

  • This should be done if the contract terms are total cost per product based.
    ​
    ​

11. Click the open field in the Extended price column to enter the lump sum pricing.
​
​

  • Price per unit will automatically update based on extended price divided by quantity.

12. Click in the open field in the Product column, below the most recently added product to continue adding additional products.
​
​

13. Add Contract Costs to the Contract Period by clicking on Add Contract Cost.
​
​14. Search for the Vendor this contract cost is being paid out to.Vendors can be found by searching the vendor name or using the dropdown menu to scroll.
​
15. Select the Cost Type.
​
16. Enter the total contracted cost, for this cost type, for this vendor., in the Amount field.
​
17. Click Save Changes to finalize the contract period.

Fields And Definitions

  • Name - This is an alphanumeric field and will only be relevant within the contract. Name this something simple and transparent. If you're contracting bags of malt in 2026, a suggested Contract Period name is "2026MaltBags".
    ​
    ​

  • Start Date - This is the date you will begin receiving product, also referred to as the pricing date. This is important because Production Cloud will recognize the contracted costs as the default costs for contracted products.
    ​
    ​

  • End Date - This is the latest date you will receive product, also referred to as the fulfillment date. This is important because Production Cloud will recognize the contracted costs as the default costs for contracted products.
    ​
    ​

  • Quantity - This is the package quantity, or inventory unit, which is noted underneath the product.
    ​
    ​

  • Price Per Unit - Purchase contracts support unit pricing to 6 decimals of precision. The extended price will automatically update based on quantity times unit price.
    ​
    ​

  • Contract Cost - Contract costs are explicit costs, not included in the price of the product(s), that are known at contract signing and will apply to all product(s) on the contract.
    ​
    ​

  • Vendor - This is almost always a different vendor than you are contracted with.
    ​
    ​

  • Cost Type - 'Freight' and 'Other Cost' are the only available selections. The 'Tax' field is an excise-tax-only field that should be automatically calculated.
    ​
    ​

  • Contract periods can be updated, edited, and rebalanced later through the 'Edit' button on the Purchase Contract View dashboard.

Distributor steps for setting up a new customer in Encompass by copying a similar one, then checking AR account, chain, promo zone, charge area, license, stops and split invoices. Requires v22.01+.

Pre-Conditions

  • This guide assumes that the user already has a similar customer set up in their system and has all necessary permissions for customer setup.

Steps

  1. Identify a similar customer to the one you are setting up. This customer might be part of the same chain or a customer of the same type located nearby.
    ​
    ​

  2. Create a new customer by following the Customer Copy help resource. Note: By default, the following associated tables are copied to the new record unless they are unselected during the copy process: Customer Notes, Customers Promotions Zones, Promotions Customers, Service Windows, Store Locations. If you unselect any of these fields, you will need to go back and add the correct records for the newly created customer.


Once the new customer record is created, edit it and confirm the following fields:

  1. AR Account - if the AR Account should be the same as the original record (the same financial entity is responsible for paying invoices for both customers) then it does not need to be updated. If it is independent and should have its own AR Account, you will need to create a new AR Account and set it on the record.
    ​
    ​

  2. Chain - Is the new customer part of the same chain as the one that as copied? If not update the chain to the correct record.
    ​
    ​

  3. Product Group - Does the new customer qualify to purchase the same group of products as the original? If not, update the Product Group to the correct record.
    ​
    ​

  4. Distribution Area - Does the customer belong to the same distribution area as the original? Typically this means that they are serviced by the same location and that their accounting should flow to the same company as the original customer record.
    ​
    ​

  5. Promo Zone - Should the customer qualify for the same group of promotions as the original? If not, update this to the correct Promo Zone.
    ​
    ​

  6. Charge Area - Does the same set of Invoice Charges apply to this customer as the original? If not, select the correct Charge Area.
    ​
    ​

  7. Jurisdiction - Is this customer physically in the same Jurisdiction as the original? Typically, Jurisdictions are used to calculate depletions taxes.
    ​
    ​

  8. Deposit Area - Should this customer be charged the same amount for deposits as the original? If not, update its Deposit Area
    ​
    ​

  9. State License Num and License Expiration Date will need to be updated to reflect the accurate licensing information for the new customer.
    ​
    ​

  10. Save Changes
    ​
    ​
    ​

Next, add routing:

    ​
    ​

  2. Select Add Stops
    ​
    ​

  3. Select the current route version, Activity and Route for the new customer according to your configuration. You might add a Delivery and Presell stop or a Peddle Sell stop depending on your organization's configuration.

    ​
    ​

If a customer should have different invoices for different product groups, add split invoice records using the Split Invoices subtable. 16989962:
Reference for the Promotions EDBL import in Encompass: bulk-add, update or delete promotions and their products, zones, customers and discount amounts. Needs the PromoEdit permission; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • You must have permission to edit promotions (PromoEdit permission) to update or modify certain promotion fields

  • ProductID or ProductID_Translation must be mapped in your import file

  • For delete actions, PromotionID or PromotionID_Translation must be mapped

Steps

The Promotions EDBL routine allows you to import, update, or delete promotions and their associated product relationships. It handles single or multiple products per promotion and can work with different promotion types (e.g., FrontLine). The routine can process zone-specific promotions and supports customer-specific promotions.

Steps/General Instructions

  1. Create an import file containing promotion data with the required fields

  2. Map your file columns to the appropriate EDBL fields

  3. Select the appropriate import action

  4. Delete: Removes promotion-product relationships

  5. Run the import routine

  6. Review the processing results to confirm successful imports, updates, or deletions

Behavior Notes

  • When using Delete action, the routine removes promotion-product relationships but not the promotions themselves

  • Setting LimitLinesToASingleProduct restricts each promotion to a single product

  • The system will attempt to match records using translations if available

  • The routine supports zero-padding correction for product IDs when matching to existing products

  • Import performance may decrease with large numbers of promotions or products

Fields And Definitions

Promotion Information:

  • PromotionName: Name of the promotion (text, max 50 characters)

  • PromotionType: Type of promotion (integer, default is FrontLine)

  • StartDate: Beginning date for the promotion (date, defaults to today's date)

  • Memo: Notes or additional information about the promotion (text, max 500 characters)

  • Active: Whether the promotion is active (yes/no, default is Yes)

Product Information:

  • ProductID: Internal product identifier (required if ProductID_Translation is not provided)

  • ProductID_Translation: External product identifier used for matching to internal product records

Location and Zone Information:

  • LocationID: Internal location identifier

  • LocationID_Translation: External location identifier

  • ZoneID: Internal zone identifier

  • ZoneID_Translation: External zone identifier

Customer Information:

  • CustomerID: Internal customer identifier

  • CustomerID_Translation: External customer identifier

Pricing Information:

  • Amount: General discount amount (currency, default is 0)

  • CaseAmount: Discount amount per case (currency, default is 0)

  • UnitAmount: Discount amount per unit (currency, default is 0)

  • Participation: Supplier participation amount (currency, default is 0)

  • CaseParticipation: Supplier participation amount per case (currency, default is 0)

  • UnitParticipation: Supplier participation amount per unit (currency, default is 0)

Quantity Information:

  • FreeUnits: Number of free units in promotion (integer, default is 0)

  • minNumUnits: Minimum number of units required (integer, default is 0)

  • minProductCount: Minimum number of products required (integer, default is 0)

Advanced Fields:

  • PromotionID: Internal promotion identifier (used for updating or deleting)

  • PromotionID_Translation: External promotion identifier

  • Condition: Conditional rule for the promotion

  • MarketID: Market identifier for the promotion

  • EndDate: Ending date for the promotion

  • OverrideLevel: Defines how the promotion overrides other promotions

  • OverrideLevel_Value: Text version of override level ("All Rules", "Min Num Units", etc.)

Best Practices

  • Always include ProductID or ProductID_Translation in your import file

  • Map as many fields as possible to ensure complete promotion data

  • Use consistent external IDs across imports to maintain translation integrity

  • Consider splitting large imports into smaller batches for better performance

  • When updating existing promotions, include the PromotionID or PromotionID_Translation for accurate matching

  • Include LocationID or LocationID_Translation to ensure promotions are associated with the correct location

  • Set proper StartDate and EndDate values to control promotion availability

  • Consider using PromotionName consistently across imports for easier identification

  • Test your imports with a small sample before running full production imports

Distributor troubleshooting for invoice sales posting to the wrong income account in Encompass: trace Distribution Area, Income Area and Income Account Maps, then re-close AR or reverse. v25.04+.

Pre-Conditions

  • You have identified an Invoice where the resulting journal entries posted to an incorrect income account.
    ​
    ​

  • You have access to the system's Income Account Maps table, Customer records, Distribution Areas, and Income Areas.
    ​
    ​

  • You have the necessary permissions to view and potentially edit these tables and records.

  • You know the specific invoice and potentially the customer, product, or other relevant details of the transaction.

Steps

1. Navigate from the Invoice to the Customer Record:
​

  • Open the specific Invoice in question.
    ​
    ​

  • From Invoice View, you can click the Journal Entry button to see the exact related entry.
    ​
    ​

  • Navigate to and open the associated Customer record.
    ​
    ​

2. Identify the Distribution Area:
​
​

  • Within the Customer record, note the assigned Distribution Area.
    ​
    ​

3. Identify the Income Area:
​
​

  • Navigate to and view the Income Area that is linked to the Distribution Area found in Step 2. The system's setup will define this relationship.

    ​

​
​

  • Use the universal search functionality within the system.
    ​
    ​

  • Search for "Income Account Maps" and select the corresponding table.
    ​
    ​

  • In the Income Account Maps table, filter the records by the Company of the invoice and the Income Area identified in Step 3.
    ​
    ​

6. Check for Second-Tier Filters (Product Type, Supplier, Product):
​
​

  • Within the filtered Income Account Maps, examine if there are any active filters for:
    ​
    ​

    • Product Type
      ​
      ​

    • Supplier
      ​
      ​

    • Product
      ​
      ​

  • Determine if any of these second-tier filters match the specifics of the product(s) sold on the problematic invoice. More specific filters will take precedence over "catchall" maps.
    ​
    ​

7. Identify the Applicable Income Account Map:
​
​

  • The correct Income Account Map is the one that matches the Company, Income Area, and any relevant Product Type, Supplier, or Product filters of the invoice transaction. If no specific filters match, the "catchall" map for that Company and Income Area will be used.

    ​

8. Verify the Income Account:

​

    ​
    ​

    • Option 1 (Recommended if within the allowed rollback period): Roll back the AR Close date (if applicable and permitted), un-verify the affected invoice(s), and then re-run the AR Close process.

      ​
      ​

      • Reverse the incorrect invoice(s).
        ​
        ​

        ​

        ​

      • Process the new invoice(s) through the AR Close.

        ​

    • Option 3 (For historical balance correction):
      ​
      ​

      • Make the necessary corrections to the Income Account Maps or Customer/Distribution/Income Area assignments.
        ​
        ​

      • Create a simple journal entry to transfer the balance from the incorrect income account to the correct income account to adjust historical financials. This will not change the original invoice journal entry details.

Best Practices

  • Establish a clear understanding of how Income Areas, Distribution Areas, and Customer assignments interact with Income Account Maps.
    ​
    ​

  • Utilize specific Product Type, Supplier, or Product filters in Income Account Maps for targeted GL assignment.
    ​
    ​

  • Create "catchall" Income Account Maps at the Company and Income Area level to handle sales that don't meet specific filter criteria.
    ​
    ​

  • Regularly review and audit Income Account Maps to ensure they accurately reflect your desired revenue recognition.
    ​
    ​

  • Train users on the importance of accurate Customer assignments to the correct Distribution and Income Areas.
