Distributor guide to auto-linking Encompass products to dsdlink global products by Supplier Product Number or Carrier UPC, and fixing products that don't link. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

Important Rules
​
​

1. Data Consistency Rule:
​
​

  • There should never be a situation where a Product has a GlobalProductID but its corresponding Brand’s GlobalBrandID is NULL.
    ​
    ​

  • If such a case is identified, submit a ticket to support, as it indicates a potential issue.
    ​
    ​

2. Matching Logic:
​
​

  • Matches are made when either the Supplier Product Numberor the Carrier UPC aligns between Local Products and dsdlink Global Products.

Key Rules for Auto-Linking
​
​

1. Auto-linking relies on either SPN or Carrier UPC for matching.
​
2. When a match is found:
​
​

  • The system sets the Local Products.GlobalProductID.
    ​
    ​

  • If the Local Brand’s GlobalBrandID is NULL, it is also set automatically.
    ​
    ​

3. A nightly routine runs to check and update links.

Steps

How to Auto-Link Local Products to dsdlink Global Products

This document explains the process and requirements for auto-linking Local Products to dsdlink Global Products. It ensures data consistency, improves product information quality, and identifies potential issues for resolution.
​
​

Overview of Auto-Linking

The auto-linking process establishes connections between Local Products and dsdlink Global Products by matching key identifiers. This process is essential for maintaining clean and reliable data when using platforms like dsdlink Retailer and Distributor Ordering, BEES, Connect Distributor Reporting in dsdlink, and many other areas of Encompass.
​
​


Steps for Auto-Linking:
​
​

1. Link One Product Per BrandFamily
​
​

  • Manually link one product within each BrandFamily. This step:
    ​
    ​

- Sets the BrandFamilies.GlobalSupplierID and BrandFamilies.GlobalBrandFamilyID.

- Tells the system to check under those global suppliers for matching records.

2. Verify and Update Product Data
​
​

  • Ensure that the remaining products in the BrandFamily meet one of the following criteria:
    ​
    ​

1. A valid Supplier Product Number (SPN) is assigned.

2. A valid Carrier UPC is assigned.

Note: Ensure data accuracy for better auto-linking outcomes.

3. Nightly Auto-Linking Routine

The system runs nightly to:
​
​
1. Match Local Products with dsdlink Global Products using:
​
​

  • Local Products.SupplierProductNum with dsdlink Products.SupplierProductNum.
    ​
    ​

  • Products.CarrierUPC with dsdlink Products.CarrierUPC.
    ​
    ​

2. Set the following upon a successful match:
​
​

  • Local Products.GlobalProductID
    ​
    ​

  • Local Brands.GlobalBrandID, if it is currently NULL.

Fields And Definitions

1. Supplier Product Number (SPN): A unique number assigned by the supplier/manufacturer.
​
​

2. Carrier UPC: Universal Product Code.
​
​

3. Global Product ID: The ID assigned to a product in the dsdlink global database.
​
​

4. Global Brand ID: The ID assigned to a brand in the dsdlink global database.
​
​

5. Local Brand: The brand within an Encompass ECP site.
​
​

6. Local Product: The product within an Encompass ECP site.

Best Practices

1. Maintain Clean Data: Regularly audit product data to ensure accurate SPNs and Carrier UPCs.
​
2. Monitor Linking Updates: Verify that expected matches are made when going through the product catalog.
​
3. Report Unexpected Behavior to Support: Identify and report any inconsistencies in GlobalProductID and GlobalBrandID assignments.

Common Issues and Troubleshooting
​
​

1. Missing SPNs or Carrier UPCs: Products without these identifiers cannot be auto-linked and would otherwise need to be manually set via Product Manager.
​
2. Mismatch Between Data Sets: Ensure that local product data is up-to-date and accurate. dsdlink is overseen by support, reach out for any inaccuracies that can't be corrected via Product Manager.
​
3. Data Gaps: Report cases where:
​
​

  • Products.GlobalProductID is set but the Brands.GlobalBrandID is NULL.

Conclusion:

By following this guide, users can optimize the auto-linking process, ensure data integrity, and maintain clean product information across Local and Global systems.

Distributor setup for receiving Molson Coors Drive ASN and Drive Shipment files in Encompass via OpenText: mailboxes, exchange configurations, and supplier reports. Requires v25.01+.

Pre-Conditions

Distributors setting up these data feeds must:

Work with OpenText to begin sending files
​
​

1. Confirm the following information:

  • Which Locations should be receiving these files?
    ​
    ​

  • Which files would each Location like to receive? (Most distributors utilize both Drive Shipment and Drive ASN.)

2. Send an email to [email protected] with the following request:

  • {Distributor name} ({distributor number}) would like to begin receiving {Drive ASN, Drive Shipment, and/or Drive Order} files to their Encompass site. Their expected go-live date is {Go-live date}. Additionally, what is the ‘Receiver Routing Number’? (formerly known as Legacy MillerCoors Dist Num)

Set up the ECP site to ingest these files
​
​

1. Set up the Mailbox in the distributor site with the same field values as below. The mailbox name is important, and should be ‘MB{Receiver Routing Number}’
​
​

Screenshot

2. Set up one ExchangeConfiguration per Location and file type.

a. For Drive ASNs, set the Mailbox, SenderID, and ReceiverID
​
​

Screenshot

b. For Drive Shipments and Drive Orders

i. Create another Mailbox with the Drive_Inbound API Command. The Mailbox name should be the same as the Drive SuppliersReports.DistributorNumber. Make one of these for each Location. NOTE: This mailbox may already be created if Drive Supplier Reporting is already set up.
​
​
​

Screenshot

ii. Add Exchange Configuration(s) as well. These records should not have the new mailbox assigned to them. Only the ExchangeMap needs to be set on these. Use the MolsonCoors Drive Inbound Shipments Exchange Map for Drive Shipments and MolsonCoors Drive Inbound Orders for Drive Orders

3. Add corresponding ExchangeConfigurationsLocation record(s).
​
4. Ensure that a SuppliersReports record is set up with ReportType=Drive

Fields And Definitions

MolsonCoors Drive has the capability to send 3 different files to Encompass. These files are used to automatically create future Purchases and Shipments in the distributor’s ECP site.

File Types:
​
​

  • Drive Order - Rough estimates of upcoming shipments used. Does not contain pallet-level data, and does not completely align with the ECP table structure. Most distributors do not utilize this file, as it typically tends to just muddy up the shipments and purchases tables with inaccurate data that does not get automatically updated.
    ​
    ​

  • Drive Shipment - More official Drive Order. Basically what MolsonCoors thinks they will likely deliver.
    ​
    ​

  • Drive ASN - Sent after the shipment is loaded and is in transit. Contains pallet-level data used for scanning in these shipments when received.

Other terms:
​
​

  • OpenText: A file trading partner. MolsonCoors uses OpenText as the “middleman” to facilitate these file transfers.
    ​
    ​

  • Receiver Routing Number: Formerly known as the Legacy MillerCoors distributor number. This is one of the identifiers that MC uses to identify a warehouse.

Best Practices

  • Ensure that all MolsonCoors products have accurate OSKUs (Products.SupplierProductNum). These values can be pulled from the global product catalog by using the ‘Product Manager’ tool.
    ​
    ​

  • Do not set up Drive Order files. These files will clutter up your Purchases table and Shipments table with data that does not automatically get updated or cleaned up.

  • Required Permission - FusionEdit
    ​
    ​

  • Recommended Fusion I/II Certification

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Concatenates two or more strings. No function required, only a double pipe between values. The ANSI standard for concatenate only supports 2 arguments. So, CONCAT(1,2) works but it's only helpful when there are 2 arguments. || works with any number of arguments, and it's a bit easier to write.

​Syntax
​
Value1 || Value2 || Value3
​
​

​Arguments
​
Can be text, numbers, a field in Encompass, HTML..etc. Concat is used to create pictures, links, colors, custom text and many other types of reporting fields. If a field you are concatting has the potential to be NULL, use an IFNULL statement to avoid the entire concatenation being NULL


​
Example

"Products"."ProductID"||"Products"."ProductName" = 123ProductName

Surfsight Camera Implementation INTERNAL ONLY May 22, 2023

Summary This document will guide a user through how to do setup and implement the Surfsight Integration with Encompass Purpose (if applicable) The Surfsight camera integration will allow customers to view and report on camera data in Encompass Precondition(s) The following workflow assumes you already have the Geotab integration. Example: Hi [customer name], I am excited to hear about your decision to integrate Encompass with Geotab and Surfsight. In order for the camera data to import into Encompass, can you reply to this task and give Encompass access to the API via a user account and authorize Geotab and Surfsight to create a user ID for Encompass to access your Surfsight account? They can then create the account and provide the credentials to Encompass. I will forward your reply to Geotab. Let me know if you have any questions. Thank You, [Your name] Take a screenshot of your email from step 1 with the consent from the customer and send an email to: Jason Wilda, [email protected] Denise Oliver, [email protected] Jacob Gafa, [email protected] Victor Garcia, [email protected] Email Example: Hi Jason, I hope this email finds you well. I am excited to inform you that we have a new customer, [company name], that has ordered x Surfsight Cameras. Similar to how you all created the user accounts in the past, this is to request a new account for the SurfSight API for [company name]. Settings > Change my Password Add Surfsight credentials to Customer Notes on Support. Ex Customer Notes - 22998 Create a new GPS Authentications record on the customer’s Encompass site API Provider Name = Surfsight User Name = username from Geotab Password = new password Example: GPS Authentications - 2 [email protected] How to create the Surfsight Add-in on the customer’s Geotab site Login to the customer’s Goetab site Go to Administration > System… > System Setting Click on the Add-Ins tab Set Allow unsigned Add-Ins toggle button to On Click New Add-In button Clear out the content in the dialog box and replace it with the following text { "url": "https://app.geotab.com/addins/surf/surfsight/manifest.json" } Click OK Click Save When done, a new Surfsight Add-in will appear. See example below: This will also create a new Surfsight menu on the left Pairing or Adding Surfsight Cameras Pairing or Adding Surfsight Cameras in Geotab Get an Excel or CSV file from the customer with the Geotab Device’s Serial Number and the Surfsight Camera’s IMEI number. Click on the Surfsight > Vehicles Menu Click on the Bulk Add Cameras button Copy and paste the the content of the Excel or CSV file Pairing or Adding Surfsight Cameras in Encompass With the same Excel or CSV file provided by the customer, create a table import (updated only) into the GPS Devices table. Try_Cast is a special version of the CAST function that is available for a subset of data type conversions. It performs the same operation (i.e converts a value of one data type into another data type), but returns a NULL value instead of raising an error when the conversion can not be performed.

​

Syntax

TRY_CAST(source_string_expr AS target_data_type)

TRY_CAST('abc' AS NUMBER) = NULL

16990104:
Distributor explanation of the {LastStartTime} filter in Encompass Fusion reports behind Advanced Fusion Alerts, and why changing the alert's Import Project breaks it. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Users should be familiar with Advanced Fusion Alert setups

Steps

  • When alerts are initially created, and there is a fusion report that fuels them, there will be a filter in the fusion report that references {LastStartTime}. You may notice that this {LastStartTime} is not pre-defined as a variable in the report.
    ​
    ​

  • The LastStartTime only takes effect when the Import Routine for the alert is under ImportProjectID=1126, 2044, 2043, 2046, or 2045. These are system Import Projects that are hardcoded to utilize this LastStartTime, and they technically reference the Last Run Time of the corresponding ImportRoutineSettings record.
    ​
    ​

  • If the ImportProject is changed, none of those system import projects can be placed back on the Import Routine. Instead, the options are to:
    ​
    - Create a new Alert from scratch, or modify the LastStartTime filters of the report to use a pre-defined variable.

Best Practices

If a report is working, do not move the Import Routine to a different Import Project

Distributor guide to the LAST_DAY advanced expression in Encompass Fusion reports: get the last day of the month, quarter, week or year for a date. Needs FusionEdit permission and v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Required Permission - FusionEdit
    ​
    ​

  • Recommended Fusion I/II Certification

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Returns the last day of the specified date part for a date or timestamp. Commonly used to return the last day of the month for a date or timestamp. Date Part can include Year, Month, Quarter, Week. Keep in mind that this will be the databases evaluation of the standard calendar format. This will not consider the Date Conversions table if it has been configured specifically. Sunday is considered the Last_Day for the WEEK time part.

​
​Syntax

LAST_DAY(Date Value, Date Part)

​
​Arguments

Date Value:

The date you start with to determine how your LAST_DAY function will operate.

Date Part:

Determines which Last Day that you want to see. Month will give you the last Day of the month based on the month that your Date Value is in. Week will give you the last day of the week that your Date Value is in.

​
​Example

LAST_DAY(2/4/2019, MONTH) = 2/28/2019
​
LAST_DAY(2/4/2019, WEEK) = 2/10/2019 (Sunday)
16990107:
Warehouse guide to the Pallet Cuts dashboard in Encompass Mobile Warehouse: re-pick cut products onto pallets before loading when inventory is available. Needs ePick, PalletAddUnits permission and v24.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.06

Pre-Conditions

Must have ePick (formerly Voice Pick) included in your current Encompass subscription.

Steps

The Pallet Cuts dashboard allows users to identify and re-pick pallets with cut products, ensuring that available inventory is utilized to fulfill ordered quantities before lost sales leave the warehouse.
​
​

1. Ensure that users responsible for re-picking have the PalletAddUnits Permission.
​
​

2. Navigate to the Encompass Mobile Warehouse.
​
​

3. Prior to loading the pallet onto the delivery truck, go to the Pallet Cuts dashboard within the Load section of the menu.
​
​

4. This dashboard is divided into two sections:

  • Inventory Available: Lists pallets with cut products where on-floor inventory is now available, and offers the option to re-pick.
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory Unavailable: Lists pallets with cut products where inventory is not available, simply for visibility.
    ​
    ​

5. In the Inventory Available section:

  1. Review the list of cut products displayed by pallet.
    ​
    ​

  2. Select the checkbox next to each product to mark it for re-picking.
    ​
    ​

  3. Tap the “Complete Re-Picks” button at the bottom of the page to fill the quantities back into the pallet.

Fields And Definitions

  • Bin Transaction: Record of inventory movement or management
    ​
    ​

  • Skip: Opting to move on from a prompted pick without reducing the pick quantity, usually based on available inventory. This happens in ePick+ by tapping on the menu in the top right corner, then selecting Products and selecting a another product from the list.
    ​
    ​

  • Cut: Reducing the pick quantity for a product based on available inventory. This action happens with ePick+ by tapping on the quantity box and editing the value to anything less than the starting quantity.
    ​
    ​

  • Re-pick: A way to restore orders with cut products after the picking process has been completed.
    ​
    ​

  • Load Groups: A table in Encompass used for configuration of pallet behavior.
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 3231: Prompt picker to correct bin inventory to zero when cutting or skipping a product. (Off by Default)
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 527: Allow Users to Request Replenishments from ePick. (Off by Default)

Best Practices

To get the most out of ePick+ while remaining efficient, we recommend this workflow, with System Settings 3231 and 527 both enabled:

  1. When arriving at an empty or low-inventory bin while picking, Skip the product on the first pass.
    ​
    ​

  2. Upon skipping, ensure a replenishment is requested and accept the prompt to correct bin inventory if it is empty.
    ​
    ​

  3. Continue picking the pallet; ePick+ will prompt users to circle back for any product they skipped while picking.
    ​
    ​

  4. Because a replenishment was requested, inventory should be at a pickable level, but if not, Cut the product.
    ​
    ​

  5. Before truck loading, check the Pallet Cuts dashboard, and re-pick any product that’s now available.

Distributor guide to the DATE_TRUNC advanced expression in Encompass Fusion reports: round a date back to the start of its year, month, week or day. Needs FusionEdit permission and v23.01+.

Pre-Conditions

  • Required Permission - FusionEdit
    ​
    ​

  • Recommended Fusion I/II Certification

Steps

Truncates a date, time, or timestamp to the specified part. Think of this as rounding back in time. Truncating to the week would give the first date of the week. Date Part examples: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour, Minute, Second. NOTE: The database returns Monday as the beginning of the week and Sunday as the last day in the week.

​Syntax

DATE_TRUNC(Date or Time Part,Date/Time value)

​
​Arguments

Date or Time Part:

The keyword that will determine what you are trying to truncate your Date or Time field to be.

Date/Time value:

The Date or Time you want to truncate.

​
​Example

DATE_TRUNC(WEEK, '2019-02-01') = 1/28/2019
​
2/1/2019 is Friday
​
1/28/2019 is the Monday of that week.
​
​

DATE_TRUNC('YEAR', '2019-03-25') =2019-01-01
​
DATE_TRUNC('MONTH', '2019-03-25') =2019-03-01

Warehouse picker guide to clearing bin inventory and requesting replenishment after cutting or skipping a pick in ePick+ on Encompass Mobile. Needs ePick, System Settings 3231 and 527; v24.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.06

Pre-Conditions

Must have ePick (formerly Voice Pick) included in your current Encompass subscription.

Steps

Clear Bin Inventory and/or Request Replenishment from Cuts and Skips in ePick+

This feature lets users reset bin inventory to zero, as well as request a replenishment, upon cutting a pick quantity or skipping a pick. For cuts, this is prompted whether the pick quantity is cut entirely, or reduced for a partial pick. Resetting bin inventories and requesting replenishments from ePick+ improves inventory accuracy and speeds up communication to the system, helping to avoid lost sales.
​
​

  1. Enable System Setting 3231 to allow pickers to clear bin inventories.
    ​
    ​

  2. Enable System Setting 527 to allow pickers to request replenishments.
    ​
    ​

  3. Access ePick+ from the Encompass Mobile Warehouse menu.
    ​
    ​

  4. Begin picking a pallet and follow the instructions on screen.
    ​
    ​

  5. Cut or skip a product to trigger the enabled prompts. A message will appear: “You are skipping [or cutting] the product. Please choose the next operation.”
    ​
    ​

  6. Check boxes will be displayed that align with System Settings 3231 and 527.
    ​
    ​

  7. The boxes will be pre-selected by default, uncheck any actions that are not desired.
    ​
    ​

  8. Tap “Next” to continue with the picking process, and complete the selected actions. Any variance from clearing a bin will be sent to the default adjustment bin, and ePick replenish requests will automatically be prioritized.

Pair these actions with the Pallet Cuts mobile dashboard to keep track of cuts and perform re-picks, or the Replenisment Task Management report to review replenishments requested from ePick+.

Fields And Definitions

  • Bin Transaction: Record of inventory movement or management
    ​
    ​

  • Skip: Opting to move on from a prompted pick without reducing the pick quantity, usually based on available inventory. This happens in ePick+ by tapping on the menu in the top right corner, then selecting Products and selecting a another product from the list.
    ​
    ​

  • Cut: Reducing the pick quantity for a product based on available inventory. This action happens with ePick+ by tapping on the quantity box and editing the value to anything less than the starting quantity.
    ​
    ​

  • Re-pick: A way to restore orders with cut products after the picking process has been completed.
    ​
    ​

  • Load Groups: A table in Encompass used for configuration of pallet behavior.
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 3231: Prompt picker to correct bin inventory to zero when cutting or skipping a product. (Off by Default)
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 527: Allow Users to Request Replenishments from ePick. (Off by Default)

Best Practices

To get the most out of ePick+ while remaining efficient, we recommend this workflow, with System Settings 3231 and 527 both enabled:

  1. When arriving at an empty or low-inventory bin while picking, Skip the product on the first pass.
    ​
    ​

  2. Upon skipping, ensure a replenishment is requested and accept the prompt to correct bin inventory if it is empty.
    ​
    ​

  3. Continue picking the pallet; ePick+ will prompt users to circle back for any product they skipped while picking.
    ​
    ​

  4. Because a replenishment was requested, inventory should be at a pickable level, but if not, Cut the product.
    ​
    ​

  5. Before truck loading, check the Pallet Cuts dashboard, and re-pick any product that’s now available.
16990112:
Distributor guide to Data Insights in Encompass: ask questions in plain English about sales, AR, purchases, inventory and survey data (beta) and get report results. Requires v25.01+ and dashboard access.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

Before you begin using the Data Insights feature in Encompass, ensure that the following conditions are met:

  • You can access the new Encompass Dashboard for Data Insights.

- If you do not have access to this dashboard, reach out to your local administrator to request access.

  • The Data Insights Beta feature is enabled on your dashboard, when first visiting the dashboard, the beta will need to be enabled.

- You have the necessary permissions to access the data you wish to query.
​
​
​

- If you do not have permission to see certain values in the system, such as laid in cost, then you will not be able to ask questions about this data on the data sets.

Steps

Steps:
​
​

  1. Navigate to the Data Insights dashboard
    ​
    ​

  2. Enable the Data Insights Beta (if not already enabled)
    ​
    ​

  3. Choose the data domain you want to explore, which begins with the Cubes in Encompass reporting (future versions plan to have additional options added)
    ​
    ​

  4. In the query input field, type your question using everyday language.
    ​
    ​

Data Insights will process your query and display the results.

If needed, ask follow-up questions or adjust your query for more specific information, at this time, Data Insights is not aware of your previous query when the next query is asked, so you will need to restate the premise of the question if refining your original results.

Example queries, for the Sales Cube:

  • Show me the top customers by revenue this quarter.
    ​
    ​

  • What's the average revenue per invoice?
    ​
    ​

  • What was the total dollar volume and number of cases sold for each brand family in the last quarter?
    ​
    ​

  • Which sales representatives achieved margins above 15% on their sales last month, and what was their total revenue?
    ​
    ​

  • What are the top 10 customers by gross profit?
    ​
    ​

  • Which chain accounts have increased their case equivalent purchases year-over-year while maintaining or improving their margin percentage?
    ​
    ​

  • For each supplier family, what is the ratio of full price sales to discounted sales, and how does their participation amount compare?
    ​
    ​

  • What is the average order size and frequency by customer type, focusing only on customers with at least 10 orders?
    ​
    ​

  • Which products have the highest buyer count but lowest placement count, suggesting opportunities for distribution expansion?
    ​
    ​

  • For each sales manager, what is the distribution of their team's sales across different product types, and how does their average margin compare to the company average?

Example queries, for the Accounts Receivable Cube:

  • Show me the total outstanding balance for accounts with payments more than 30 days past due, broken down by collection agent.
    ​
    ​

  • What are the top 5 AR accounts by total debit amount in the last quarter, and what percentage of their charges have been credited?
    ​
    ​

  • What is the average days to payment for each payment terms category, considering only fully paid transactions?
    ​
    ​

  • Which collection agents have improved their collection rate over the past 6 months compared to the previous 6 months?
    ​
    ​

  • Show me accounts where the total credits exceed the total debits by more than $1000, grouped by AR account and sorted by the largest discrepancy.

​
​Example queries, for the Objectives Survey Cube:

  • What percentage of surveys were completed within the last month across each sales manager's team, and what was their average numerical response score?
    ​
    ​

  • Show me all survey questions in the "Product Placement" section where customers received an answer score below 3, grouped by delivery route
    ​
    ​

  • Which sales representatives have the highest completion rates for their assigned surveys this quarter?
    ​
    ​

  • For each objective, what is the distribution of text responses versus numerical scores, and how many included supporting images?
    ​
    ​

  • Show me a comparison of survey completion times between chain accounts versus independent customers, broken down by survey section
    ​

Example queries, for the Purchases Cube:

  • For each product, what is the variance between ordered quantities and received quantities in the last month, highlighting items with over 10% difference?
    ​
    ​

  • What is the average freight cost as a percentage of total laid-in cost for each destination location, considering only verified purchases?
    ​
    ​

  • Show me all purchases of wine products where the vintage is 2020 or newer and the expiration date is within the next 6 months
    ​
    ​

  • What are the top 10 products by total purchase value this quarter, including their average unit cost and total freight charges?

Example queries, for the Days Of Inventory Cube:

  • Which products have less than 7 days of inventory remaining across all locations, ordered by lowest DOI first?
    ​
    ​

  • What is the average daily consumption rate for each product location where the current on-floor inventory is above 1000 units?
    ​
    ​

  • Show me locations that have more than 30 days of inventory for products that are selling less than 10 units per day
    ​
    ​

  • What is the total on-floor inventory and estimated days remaining for our top 10 products by daily rate?
    ​
    ​

  • Which locations have the biggest mismatch between daily consumption rate and current inventory levels (high inventory but low daily rate or vice versa)?

*During the Beta phase, your feedback is crucial. Use the feedback option within the tool to report issues or suggest improvements.

Fields And Definitions

  • Data Insights: A conversational AI feature within Encompass that allows users to query business data using natural language.
    ​
    ​

  • Natural Language Query: A method of asking questions in everyday language without the need for specialized query syntax.
    ​
    ​

  • Data Domain: Specific categories of business data available in Encompass (e.g., Sales, Inventory).
    ​
    ​

  • Beta Feature: A pre-release version of a feature made available for testing and feedback purposes.

Best Practices

Be Specific in Your Queries:

Clearly articulate what information you are seeking.

Let it know what columns you want returned, what filters to include, etc.

Don't use specific 'names' of items, unless you plan to type out an exact match of the name.

  • For example: Searching for 'Top customers to purchase Fat Tire' will result in a product name search for exactly 'Fat Tire', if your product is called 'Fat Tire 2/12', it will not find it.

Use Simple Language:

Ask questions as if you are speaking to a colleague.

Avoid overly complex sentences or technical jargon unless necessary.

Understand System Limitations:

Remember that Data Insights operates within the scope of your permissions.

If data seems missing, verify your access rights or consult an administrator.

Maintain Data Security:

Do not share sensitive information obtained from Data Insights with unauthorized parties.

Follow your organization's data handling policies.

Explore and Learn:

Experiment with different types of queries to become familiar with the tool's capabilities.

Review the results to gain insights into your business operations.

Provide Constructive Feedback:

Report any bugs, errors, or issues encountered during use.

Suggest features or improvements to enhance functionality.

Stay Informed:

Keep an eye on updates or communications regarding the Beta feature.

Participate in any offered training sessions or webinars.

By following this guide, you can effectively leverage Data Insights to make informed decisions and streamline your data analysis processes within Encompass.

Distributor guide to the DATEADD advanced expression in Encompass Fusion reports: add days, weeks, months or other time units to a date. Needs FusionEdit permission and v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Required Permission - FusionEdit
    ​
    ​

  • Recommended Fusion I/II Certification

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Adds the specified value for the specified date or time part to a date, time, or timestamp. This function is redundant with the Add_Days() etc. functions which were added to be a bit more simple and clear. Both functions are adequate. Date Part examples: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour, Minute, Second.

​Syntax

DATEADD(Date or Time Part,Value,Date/Time)

​
​Arguments

Date or Time Part:

This indicates the units of time that you want to add. For example, if you wanted to add 2 days this would be DAY.

Value:

This is the number of units of time that you want to add. For example, if you wanted to add 2 days, this would 2.

Date/Time:

This is the data, time, or timestamp to which you want to add. For example, if you wanted to add 2 days to August 1, 2018 this would be "2018-08-01".

​
​Example

"LoadSheet"."Date" = 3/21/2019
​
DATEADD(DAY,2,"LoadSheet"."Date") = 3/23/2019

16990115:
Distributor guide to the BinInventories EDBL import in Encompass: update bin inventory levels for integrations or data migration, with required fields and how adjustment bin trans are created.

Minimum Version Required: 20.01

Pre-Conditions

The BinInventories EDBL updates and manages inventory levels for bins. This guide outlines the mappable fields, their purposes, prerequisites, and important considerations to ensure a smooth process.

1. Review data & map fields

Ensure that all required and desired fields are properly mapped in the import data. See Fields & Definitions for more information about each field in the EDBL.

2. Before running the EDBL, ensure the following:

  • Location Mapping: Either LocationID or LocationID_Translation must be mapped.
    If no matching LocationID is found in the system, a warning will appear: "LocationID not mapped."

3. Import Actions

Only the following import actions are respected:

  • AddOnly

  • UpdateOnly

  • UpdateOrAdd

If other import actions are used, no data will be processed.

4. How Inventory Updates Work

This EDBL updates bin inventory levels directly. Here’s how the process works:

  • The provided inventory value replaces the current BinInventory.Inventory.

  • Two BinTrans records are created to adjust the bin inventory:

    • A negative adjustment (AdjBinID) to decrease the previous inventory level.

    • A positive adjustment to reflect the new inventory level.

Example:
If BinInventoryID 1 has an initial inventory of 10 units and the import file specifies 20 units:

  1. The final inventory becomes 20 units.

  2. Two BinTrans records are added:

    • AdjBin reduces inventory by -10 units.

    • Bin adds +10 units.

5. Additional Notes

There are no scheduled tasks that need to run after this EDBL. Bin Inventories are immediately updated, and matching BinTrans records are created to reflect any moves. Bin Trans may take up to 15 minutes to be visible in the Bin Trans table. Immediate impact can be seen on the Bin Inventories table or in the Bin Audit tool, where changes to bin inventory over time can be reviewed for a specified product and bin.

Fields And Definitions

  • LocationID_Translation: Maps to LocationID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID: Directly provides the LocationID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • BinID_Translation: Maps to the BinID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • BinID: Specifies the target bin ID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • AdjBinID: Specifies the adjustment bin ID; defaults to DefaultBins.AdjustBinID if not mapped.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID_Translation: Maps to the ProductID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID: Specifies the target product ID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory: Updates the number of units (NumUnits).
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseID: If mapped, finds a PurchaseTransID for the product in the specified purchase.
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseTransID: Updates BinInventory.PurchaseTransID. Creates BinLots if the bin’s BinZones.RequirePalletTag > 0.
    ​
    ​

  • WholesaleUnitsPerCase: Defaults to the product’s Package.WholesaleUnitsPerCase if not mapped.

*Only one of the noted fields must be mapped, but both are not simultaneously required.

Best Practices

  • When to use: The BinInventories EDBL is best suited for situations where the "from bin" needs to be specified, but any variance in inventory can shift into an adjustment bin. If new inventory quantities simply need to be updated for a collection of bins, for example, the BinInventories EDBL is the right choice.
    ​
    ​

  • The BinInventories EDBL is primarily intended for use within integrations or during the data migration process.
16990116:
Distributor guide to the DATEDIFF advanced expression in Encompass Fusion reports: count the days, weeks, months or years between two dates. Needs FusionEdit permission and v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Required Permission - FusionEdit
    ​
    ​

  • Recommended Fusion I/II Certification

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Calculates the difference between two date, time, or timestamp expressions based on the date or time part requested. The function returns the result of subtracting the second argument from the third argument. Keep the syntax as (Date Part, StartDate, EndDate) to get positive results. (Date Part, EndDate, StartDate) will give negative results.
​
Date Part examples: Year, Month, Week, Day.

​Syntax

DATEDIFF(Date or Time Part, StartDate, EndDate)

​
​Arguments

Date or Time Part:

A keyword to determine the "Diff" output. Use 'Day' to see the number of days. Use 'Week' to see the number of weeks. Use Minute to see the number of minutes. Etc. (You can only use Time parts for DateTime fields.)
​
​

StartDate:

This can be a Date or DateTime depending on which part you are using.
​
​

EndDate:

This can be a Date or DateTime depending on which part you are using.

​
​Examples

DATEDIFF(YEAR, '2019-01-01', '2020-01-05') = 1
​
DATEDIFF(MONTH, '2019-01-01', '2020-01-05') = 12
​
DATEDIFF(DAY, '2020-01-01', '2020-01-05') = 4
​
DATEDIFF(HOUR, '2020-01-01', '2020-01-05') = 96
​
DATEDIFF(MINUTE, '2020-01-01', '2020-01-05') = 5760
​
DATEDIFF(SECOND, '2020-01-01', '2020-01-05') = 345600

16990118:
Distributor guide to the BinTrans EDBL import in Encompass WMS: import bin-to-bin inventory moves and other bin transactions for integrations or data migration, with field definitions.

Minimum Version Required: 20.01

Pre-Conditions

The BinTrans EDBL is typically only needed for warehouses where WMS is enabled. Non-WMS warehouses have simplified inventory management that generally does not call for imported Bin Trans.

Steps

The BinTrans EDBL is designed to update, manage, and process bin transactions—records of inventory movement—in the system. This guide provides a detailed breakdown of the mappable fields, their purposes, prerequisites, and key considerations for running the EDBL successfully.

1. Review data & map fields

Ensure that all required and desired fields are properly mapped in the import data. See Fields & Definitions for more information about each field in the EDBL.

2. Before running the EDBL, ensure the following:
​
​

  • Location Mapping: Either LocationID or LocationID_Translation must be mapped.
    If no matching LocationID is found in the system, a warning will appear: "LocationID not mapped."

3. Import Actions
​
​

Only the following import actions are respected:

  • AddOnly

  • UpdateOrAdd

If other import actions are used, no data will be processed.

4. Special Cases
​
​

  • Updating PurchaseTransID:
    If PurchaseTransID is mapped, BinInventory.PurchaseTransID will be updated for the related product and bin combination.
    ​
    ​

  • Adding Bin Lot Data:
    If PurchaseTrans is not null, Bin Lot data will be added under these conditions:
    - The bin's BinZones.TrackBinLots field is set to Required or Optional
    - The product's tracking flags are enabled for Code Dates, Batch Codes, or Vintages.

5. Additional Notes
​
​

There are no scheduled tasks that need to run after this EDBL. BinTrans records are immediately created and impacting the system, though they may take up to 15 minutes to be visible in the Bin Trans table. Immediate impact can be seen in the Bin Audit tool, where changes to bin inventory over time can be reviewed for a specified product and bin.

Fields And Definitions

  • LocationID_Translation: Maps to LocationID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID: Directly provides the LocationID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • BinID_Translation: Maps to the BinID through table translation.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID_Translation: Maps to the ProductID through table translation.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID: Directly provides the ProductID.
    ​
    ​

  • BinTransType: Specifies the transaction type (BinTrans.BinTransType).
    Values: 1,Received;2,Unreceived;3,Put Away;4,Replenished;5,Pick Complete;6,Pick Uncompleted;7,Loaded;17,Add Ons;8,Unloaded;9,Returned;10,Unreturned;11,Return Put Away;12,Invoiced;13,Inventory Adjust;14,Moved;15,Skip;16,Picker Cut;18,Production Queue;19,Reverse Production Queue;20,Equipment Transfer;21,Re-picked
    ​
    ​

  • NumUnits: Specifies the number of units involved in the transaction (BinTrans.NumUnits).
    ​
    ​

  • BinID: Specifies the target bin ID.
    ​
    ​

  • LoadSheetID: Links the transaction to a load sheet (BinTrans.LoadSheetID).
    ​
    ​

  • PalletID: Links the transaction to a pallet (BinTrans.PalletID). This is only for picking outbound pallets, not for the pallet inventory is stored on while it resides in the warehouse.
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceTransID: Links the transaction to a specific invoice transaction (BinTrans.InvoiceTransID).
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseTransID: Links the transaction to a specific purchase layer of inventory (BinTrans.PurchaseTransID). This is how specific expiration dates, batch codes, or vintages are noted during a move, translating to a Bin Lot, if that data is being tracked.
    ​
    ​

  • BoxID: Links the transaction to a box used in unit or bottle picking. (BinTrans.BoxID).
    ​
    ​

  • Date: Specifies the transaction date. Defaults to the current date (LocalToday()) if not provided.

*Only one of the noted fields must be mapped, but both are not simultaneously required.

Best Practices

  • When to use: The BinTrans EDBL is best suited for situations where the "from bin" and the "to bin" need to be specified, as opposed to allowing inventory to always shift into an adjustment bin. If inventory is moving from one on-floor bin to another, for example, the BinTrans EDBL is the right choice.
    ​
    ​

  • The BinTrans EDBL is primarily intended for use within integrations or during the data migration process.
    ​
    ​

  • In most imports, the Bin Trans Type should be 14, Moved which simply notes that inventory is shifting from one bin to another, without involving more specific processes like receiving.

  • Invoice Mapping: InvoiceNum or InvoiceID must be provided.
    The corresponding invoice must exist in the system for the pallet to be added, and InvoiceTransID must be accurate.
    If it is missing or incorrect, the pallet will not link to any invoice transaction, rendering it meaningless.

3. Import Actions
​
​

Only the following import actions are respected:

  • UpdateOnly

  • UpdateOrAdd

If other import actions are used, the process cannot link InvoiceTrans or update any other data.

4. Special Cases
​
​

  • Creating New Pallets:
    If only PalletID_Translation is mapped, and not PalletID, a new pallet will be created.
    ​
    ​

  • NumUnits Discrepancies:
    If the NumUnits in the provided InvoiceTransID does not match the system’s current value, the system will adjust the values.
    The latest provided value will overwrite and become the new NumUnits. This is how cuts can be communicated via the EDBL.

5. Additional Notes
​
​

There are no scheduled tasks that need to run after this EDBL. Pallet records are immediately updated, along with their related invoice trans data.

Fields And Definitions

  • LocationID_Translation: Maps to LocationID through table translation. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID: Directly provides the LocationID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • PalletID_Translation: Maps to PalletID through table translation; if not found, a new pallet is created.
    ​
    ​

  • PalletID: Directly provides the PalletID.
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceNum: Maps to InvoiceID through table translation using InvoiceNum. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceID: Links the pallet to an existing invoice via Pallet.InvoiceID. (Required*)
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID_Translation: Maps to ProductID through table translation, in the end providing InvoiceTrans.ProductID.
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID: Directly provides InvoiceTrans.ProductID.
    ​
    ​

  • NumUnits: Updates InvoiceTrans.NumUnits.
    ​
    ​

  • SSCC18: Updates the SSCC18 value for pallets, which is the serialized shipping container code used universally for pallet recognition across systems.
    ​
    ​

  • Status: Updates pallet status; defaults to "New" if no value is provided.
    ​
    ​

  • PalletSeq: Updates InvoiceTrans.PalletSequence.
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceTransID: Links a related invoice transaction with the pallet.
    ​
    ​

  • PickedByUserID: Updates the PickedByUserID field for the pallet, indicating the User ID of the person that completed the pallet pick.

*Only one of the noted fields must be mapped, but both are not simultaneously required.

Best Practices

The Pallets EDBL is primarily intended for use within integrations or during the data migration process.

16990126:
Producer troubleshooting when no inventory is available to assign production components on a production order in Encompass: unreceived purchases, open WIP orders, or missing batch/code date bin lots. v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Production Order has been scheduled and is in Planned/In Progress Status
    ​
    ​

  • Production Components are in Planned Status
    ​
    ​

  • Products have been Received into inventory on a Purchase

Steps

If a User goes to assign a Production Component and sees no available inventory, there could be a few different reasons as to why.

Product has zero inventory:

  • A Product that has a Product Type with TrackInventory=True must consume inventory when it is used. If Raw Material was not put on a Purchase and Received into inventory, then it will not be available. If WIP is to be consumed, the Production Order that created it must be completed for that inventory to be available.

  • If inventory was over-consumed and driven negative previously, then Received (RM)/Created (WIP)will backfill the negative values and may result in understated inventory on floor.

TO FIX: Ensure all Purchases with the RM/WIP are in Received Status at the same Location that Production is processing. Ensure all Production Orders that make WIP at that Location have been completed.

Product is in Inventory but not available:

  • A Product that is set to either TrackBatchCodes (TBC), TrackCodeDates (TCD) or TrackVintages (TV) = TRUE will require Bin Lots to be used in Production Processing. When material is through a Production Order or Received on a Purchase, if TBC, TCD or TV = TRUE, then Users will have to record a batch, date or vintage to record that layer of inventory.

TO FIX in Non-WMS: Un-Receive the Purchase, enter the required fields, then re-receive the Purchase. If Bin Lots are still not created, make sure the DefaultPickBin set in Default Bins table has a Bin Zone with TrackBinLots=TRUE

TO FIXin WMS: Perform an inventory count by Bin Lot on the handheld. When the inventory is counted, use the Date, Code or Vintage that Product requires as set on its record.

Fields And Definitions

  • Products.TrackBatchCodes - When set to TRUE, this requires every layer of inventory of a Product to have a Batch Code assigned to it. Users will be unable to interact with inventory of this Product unless a Batch Code has been assigned to that layer of inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Products.TrackCodeDates - When set to TRUE, this requires every layer of inventory of a Product to have a Code Date assigned to it. Users will be unable to interact with inventory of this Product unless a Code Date has been assigned to that layer of inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Products.TrackVintages - When set to TRUE, this requires every layer of inventory of a Product to have a Batch Code assigned to it. Users will be unable to interact with inventory of this Product unless a Batch Code has been assigned to that layer of inventory.

Best Practices

  • Set TBC or TCD = TRUE on all WIP Products since those fields are auto-filled in Production
    ​
    ​

  • Only track Batches and Codes where it is necessary for operations to function. Tracking inventory layers adds complexity to receiving and production

Distillery troubleshooting in Encompass when spirit components show no available inventory on a production order: missing proof on received or produced inventory, or missing batch/code date bin lots. v25.03+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.03

Pre-Conditions

  • A Product with Brands.TTBCategory=Spirit is to be used in a Planned/InProgress Production Order
    ​
    ​

  • Products have been Received into inventory on a Purchase

Steps

If a User goes to assign a Spirituous Production Component and sees no available inventory, there could be a few different reasons as to why:

Inventory of this Product has no Proof:

  • A Product that has a Brand.TTBCategory=Spirit will require all Inventory to have a Proof on it. Proof is recorded when Products are brought in on a Purchase or created through a Production Order. If a User did not record Proof when bringing spirituous inventory in, the system will prevent Users from using that inventory until the Proof has been corrected. This prevents Proof Gallon calculation errors on monthly/quarterly TTB Compliance reporting.

TO FIX: Re-process the Production Order that created the spirituous material, being sure to input Proof accurately when the Order is Completed. If the material came in on a Purchase, Un-Receive the Purchase, correct the Transaction for that spirituous item and re-receive the Purchase in order to record Proof and calculate Proof Gallons.

Product is in Inventory but not available:

  • A Product that is set to either TrackBatchCodes (TBC), TrackCodeDates (TCD) or TrackVintages (TV) = TRUE will require Bin Lots to be used in Processing. When material is created through a Production Order or Received on a Purchase, if TBC, TCD or TV = TRUE, then Users will have to record a batch, date or vintage to record that layer of inventory.

TO FIX in Non-WMS: Un-Receive the Purchase, enter the required fields, then re-receive the Purchase. If Bin Lots are still not created, make sure the DefaultPickBin set in Default Bins table has a Bin Zone with TrackBinLots=TRUE

TO FIX in WMS: Perform an inventory count by Bin Lot on the handheld. When the inventory is counted, use the Date, Code or Vintage that Product requires as set on its record.

Fields And Definitions

  • Products.TrackBatchCodes - When set to TRUE, this requires every layer of inventory of a Product to have a Batch Code assigned to it. Users will be unable to interact with inventory of this Product unless a Batch Code has been assigned to that layer of inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Products.TrackCodeDates - When set to TRUE, this requires every layer of inventory of a Product to have a Code Date assigned to it. Users will be unable to interact with inventory of this Product unless a Code Date has been assigned to that layer of inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Products.TrackVintages - When set to TRUE, this requires every layer of inventory of a Product to have a Batch Code assigned to it. Users will be unable to interact with inventory of this Product unless a Batch Code has been assigned to that layer of inventory.

Best Practices

  • Record Proof on Production Orders as they are closed out
    ​
    ​

  • When receiving materials, make sure proof is accurately recorded on the Purchase
    ​
    ​

  • Set TBC or TCD = TRUE on all WIP Products since those fields are auto-filled in Production
    ​
    ​

  • Only track Batches and Codes where it is necessary for operations to function. Tracking inventory layers adds complexity to receiving and production

Producer steps for reopening a verified production order in Encompass by opening the AP close date, un-verifying the shipment, then re-verifying and re-closing AP. Needs the UnVerify permission and v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

Verified Production Orders are locked to prevent Users from making changes to them that would impact costing and financials. In the event that a Verified Production Order needs to be reopened:
​
​

  • A Production Order has been completed and Verified. (If a Production Order is in completed status, see "Reopen Completed Production Order" Help Resource)
    ​
    ​

  • A User with the UnVerify permission will need to follow this process

Steps

Step 1:
​
​

  1. Go to Companies Table
    ​
    ​

  2. Set AP Close date to the day before the date on the Production Order that needs to be corrected
    ​
    ​
    ​

Step 2:
​
​

  1. Go to Production Orders table
    ​
    ​

  2. Filter to the Production Order that needs to be rolled back
    ​
    ​

  3. Select Subtables -> Purchases
    ​
    ​

  4. On the Subtabled Purchase, click the hyperlink for the Shipment associated with that Purchase
    ​
    ​

  5. Select the Un-Verify link in the ReceiveTime field

Once these steps are completed, the Production Order will be in Completed Status. Correct the Production Order as needed by following "Reopen Completed Production Order" Help Resource.

Step 3:
​
​

  1. Re-Verify the Production Order using Production Confirmation Costingdashboard
    ​
    ​

  2. Re-Close AP to current date using the End of Day dashboard

Fields And Definitions

  • Verified Production Orders - A Production Order that has been completed, with costs verified and Journal Entries made against it. Correcting these means Journal Entries also have to be corrected (opening up days to re-record AP)

Best Practices

  • Double Check Production Orders before Verifying them to prevent having to roll back PdO's
    ​
    ​

  • Opening Accounts Payable in this process is risky. It allows users to back-date transactional documents to the period that was opened, and will re-calculate any transactions that were unlocked. When rolling back days, have a game plan, fix the records that need fixing and re-close as soon as possible to reduce the risk of Users unexpectedly back-dating transactions for periods that have been closed
    ​
    ​

  • If correcting costing for one PdO, make sure any others that may have been affected will also be corrected (Example: if WIP is incorrectly costed, all Packaging Runs that packaged that WIP will also be costed incorrectly)

Producer steps for setting up package conversions in Encompass when raw materials are bought in one unit of measure type (mass, volume, units) and used in another in production. Requires v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

When Raw Materials are Purchased in a different Unit of Measure (UoM) Type than they are Consumed as a Production Component in Production, Conversions need to be used to ensure the correct quantities of inventory are consumed at the correct cost.

**Please Note- Conversions do not need to be set up if the Products UoM Type does not change. Example: a Product can be received in Kilos then used in Pounds because those are both measurements of Mass.**

  • Products have been set up
    ​
    ​

  • Packages have been configured and assigned to Products using a UoM Type that corresponds with how the Vendor sells it. Example: If we purchase Honey in Pounds, then Honey's Package should be set to a Package where UoMType=Mass

If the Product is being converted from Units->Volume or Mass, the Volume or Weight of each of those Units need to be known to set up Conversions. Example: A Box of Puree is 5 Gallons and weighs 59.6 Pounds

Steps

Setting up Conversions
​
​Navigate to the Product in the Products Table that needs to have a unique Package Conversion set up for it.

For Products Purchased/Received/Inventoried in Mass and Consumed in Volume:

  • Make sure Product's Package.UoMType=Mass
    ​
    ​

  • Edit the Product
    ​
    ​

  • Set Products.CaseWeightInLbs=1
    ​
    ​

  • Set Products.Ounces=however many fluid ounces are in a single pound of that Product
    ​
    ​

  • Save Changes

For Products Purchased/Received/Inventoried in Volume and Consumed in Mass:

  • Make sure Product's Package.UoMType=Volume
    ​
    ​

  • Edit the Product
    ​
    ​

  • Set Products.Ounces=1
    ​
    ​

  • Set Products.CaseWeightInLbs=however many pounds are in a single ounce of that Product
    ​
    ​

  • Save Changes

For Products Purchased/Received/Inventoried Units Consumed in Volume or Mass:

  • Make sure Product's Package.UoMType=Units
    ​
    ​

  • Edit the Product
    ​
    ​

  • Set Products.Ounces=however many fluid ounces are in a single Unit of that Product
    ​
    ​

  • Set Products.CaseWeightInLbs=however many pounds are in a single Unit of that Product
    ​
    ​

  • Save Changes

Once a Product is set up, the Packages Conversions table will calculate Conversions that will be used throughout the Products Inventory Lifecycle. Search the specific Product in the Packages Conversions table to make sure all Units of Measure will calculate correctly.

Fields And Definitions

  • Packages.UnitOfMeasure (UoM) Type: Determines whether we measure something using Mass, Volume or Units
    ​
    ​

  • UoM Type = Volume: Measure of the area a Product occupies; Liters, Gallons, Fluid Ounces, etc...
    ​
    ​

  • UoM Type = Mass: Measure of a Products Weight; Pounds, Weight Ounces, Kilograms, Grams, etc...
    ​
    ​

  • UoM Type = Units: When Products are received in a bound package; 3gal Box, 55gal Drum, 55lb Sac, etc...

Best Practices

  • Always set Packages.UoMType to the unit of measure that Vendors sell the item in
    ​
    ​

  • For Products we purchase in Units, exclude the weight of the container when entering CaseWeightInLbs. Example: A 55gal HDPE Food Grade Drum weighs around 20lbs. If a full Drum is weighed to determine the weight of a Product, it will be 20lbs off and skew inventory depletions.
    ​
    ​

  • Create a new Package record for each unique Unit that Products are received in: 5gal Bucket, 3gal Box, etc. Use the same Package for multiple Products, then set individual Product Records to the correct ounces/weight so their conversions are accurate.
    ​
    ​

  • Communicate with teams that manage inventory for all Products that run through conversions when we go from Receiving to Production
    ​
    ​

  • Use naming conventions such as a suffix on the Product Record so Users interacting with the material understand what conversions are for each Product
    ​
    ​

  • Minimize Packages Conversions where possible. This adds a level of complexity for these inventoried Products that can be difficult for teams to handle across the organization.

16990141:
Distributor workflow for CONA Blockchain purchase orders in Encompass: vendor setup, sending POs, automated updates, receiving, and fixing common Exchange Task warnings. Requires v24.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.09

Steps

Step 1: Purchase Creation

Purchase is created in Encompass with a vendor with the following requirements:

  • Vendor Trading Partner = “CONA Blockchain”
    ​
    ​

  • Vendor License = CONA To Entity Code
    ​
    ​

  • Vendor Plant Code = CONA Ship From

Step 2: Update Shipment to Ordered Status

Export_CONABlockchain_Purchases will send PO information to validate the PO with CONA. to Create Purchase Order
​
​

If ok:

  • Exchange Task status will be Successfully Sent
    ​
    ​

  • We will get back a TransactionPayload and will
    ​
    ​

  • We will send another request with the TransactionPayload
    ​
    ​

  • Purchase EDI Status update to Purchase Order Sent
    ​
    ​

  • So, it is normal to see two exchange tasks for a purchase that have been Successfully Sent
    ​
    ​

If failed:

  • Exchange Task status will be Warning.
    ​
    ​

  • Purchase EDI Status update to Purchase Order Failed.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Common Failures or Warnings:

  • Product Setup - This has usually been caused by a product configuration with an incorrect Supplier Product Num or Case UPC. Odom will need to confirm the Supplier Product Num and Case UPC is correct OR CONA will need to fix the product on their end. Once the product is fixed, users will need to set the EDI Status back to Not Yet Transmitted and can run Export_CONABlockchain_Purchases.
    ​
    ​

  • Purchase Order Not Found - This happens when we send the purchase receive confirmation. This happens because a PO was created and received before Export_CONABlockchain_Purchases. Odom is aware this is not the expected workflow.

Step 3: Import_CONABlockchain_Purchases (automated)

  • This will update the PO by possible adjusting quantities, adding dunnage product, setting pallet tag, code dates, memo (Carrier), and trailer num
    ​
    ​

  • Uses Import Routine 558138 - CONA Blockchain (PurchaseOrders EDBL)


Comments:

  • Multiple exchange tasks will be created
    ​
    ​

  • All updates will not happen at once. Dunnage product may get added first. Perhaps days later, when the product is picked at the CONA facility, pallet tag, code dates, memo (Carrier), and trailer number will be updated.

Step 4: Purchase is shipped and received by Odom

Once the shipment is received by Odom, Export_CONABlockchain_Purchases_GR_GI will send the PO to CONA Blockchain (GR - Goods Received or GI - Goods Issued)
​
​

  • GR - Goods Received (BUYS). Positive purchases
    ​
    ​

  • GI - Goods Issued (RETURNS) Negative purchases

CONA Blockchain Dashboard

CONA Blockchain - used to monitor, has link to scheduled tasks to resend, and link to the CONA Blockchain Alert

Best Practices

BUYS: Only positive units should be put on a purchase order. Enter +/- num units will not be accepted by CONA

RETURNS: Only negative units. Usually for dunnage but can also be finished goods

Ensure PO is sent before receiving. This will result in a Purchase Order Not Found warning.

16990146:
Distributor checklist for finding why an unexpected FIFO Adjustment Invoice was created in Encompass: FOB changes, case pack changes, Setting 3245, or Track Inventory changes. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

FIFO Adjustment Invoice was generated and the root cause is unknown.

Steps

1. On the FIFO Adjustment Invoice, navigate to one of the Products in table view. Sub-Table Inventory, and review the FOB. If there is a change to the FOB, then that is likely the cause of the adjustment. Further investigation can be completed to determine which Purchase Trans caused a change in FOB.
​
2. Check if the Product's Wholesale Units Per Case has been changed recently. WUPC is a virtual field from the Package, but it can still be viewed in the Product audit.
​
3. Check System Setting 3245. This was a change as of Q4 2024 that changed all databases from 24 months to 12 months. This is unexpected for many customers who did not see the release note, so a FIFO Adjustment would be also unexpected if this is the cause.
​
4. Check whether or not the Product Type has been updated from Track inventory = True to False, or False to True. This would cause an adjustment for every unit that was on Purchase Trans for every Product under that Product Type.

Fields And Definitions

FIFO- First In, First Out. Used in the context of picking the oldest products first.

Layer- Group of Products in inventory that are costed the same

Best Practices

General ledger (GL) Impact: All FIFO Adjustment Invoices will build a related Journal Entry to account for the value changes.Most of the time, FIFO Adjustments will only impact the related Inventory Account (set in Inventory Account Maps) and a COGS Account (set in Income Account Maps). There should never be an impact to Accounts Receivable. if there is, then there is a misconfiguration.

Distributor steps for setting up California (CA) finance charges in Encompass on overdue invoices: finance charge product, statement charge route, settings 90 and 91, and credit terms. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

1. Setup a finance charge product
​
​

  • Configure the income account maps accordingly to ensure it is hitting the general ledger the way users would like.
    ​
    ​

  • This should be a non-inventory product.
    ​
    ​

  • Set the price of the product to the percentage they would like billed (As an example, 1% should have the price set to $0.01).

​
2. Create a CA Finance Charge route
​
​

  • CA Finance Charge Invoices are typically put on load sheets with the LS Type set to 'Statement Charge'.|
    ​
    -This can be completed by creating a new route type if one does not already exist.
    ​
    ​

  • By design, finance charges are not generated for invoices on a 'Statement Charge' load sheet.

​
3. Configure System Settings 90 & 91
​
​

  • System setting 90 is set by the system when CA finance charges are generated.
    ​
    ​

  • System setting 91 controls what product will be used for the finance charge. This will use the product created in step 1.

​
4. Enable Finance Charges on the Credit Term:
​
​

  • Go to the Credit Terms settings.
    ​
    ​

  • Locate the relevant credit term.
    ​
    ​

  • Ensure that the 'Charge Finance Charge' field is set to 'True'. This enables the calculation of finance charges for overdue invoices using this credit term.
    ​
    ​

5. Set Up the AR Account:
​
​

  • Ensure that the 'ARAccount.Term' field is set to the credit term they configured in step 3. This links the AR account to the credit term that has finance charges enabled.

Fields And Definitions

How it Works:
​
​

  • When an invoice associated with the configured AR account becomes overdue, the system will automatically calculate finance charges based on the settings in the associated credit term.
    ​
    ​

  • A CA Finance charge will automatically accrue on invoices that are overdue by 42 days.
    ​
    ​

  • The calculated finance charges will be added to the customer's account balance as a separate finance charge invoice.

Best Practices

Additional Notes:
​
​

  • There may be other factors or configurations that can influence CA finance charge calculations.
    ​
    ​

  • It is recommended to thoroughly test any changes to the CA finance charge settings in a controlled environment such as a test site before applying them to the live system.
    ​
    ​

  • These finance charges are designed for the state of California. Any configuration or customization would need to be handled outside of the CA Finance charge process.

Distributor steps for adding an Omni Filter to an Encompass dashboard to filter all reports at once, plus fixes when filters are missing or don't apply. Pinned report filters needed; v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

  • A Report or Report Graph widget must be added to the dashboard first before an Omni Filter can be added.
    ​
    ​

  • The filters or variables from the reports that will be added to the omni filter must be pinned.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

  1. Create any reports that will be displayed and filtered on the dashboard
    ​
    ​

  2. Create a new dashboard or edit an existing dashboard
    ​
    ​

  3. Add any reports and report graphs to the dashboard
    ​
    ​

  4. Add an 'Omni-Filter' widget to the dashboard
    ​
    ​

  5. Select the filters you would like to use from your reports (only pinned filters or variables can be added), or create a custom filter (must match the name of the report filters exactly)
    ​
    ​

  6. After selecting a filter, determine the filter's properties:
    ​
    -Primary filters will always be displayed in the filter row.
    ​
    ​-Non-primary filters will be stored inside the 'Add Filter' menu and grouped by Category. Select up to 4 filters to be primary. Dashboard viewers can select a non-primary filter from the menu to add it to the row of filters and apply it to the dashboard view.
    ​
    - The properties of each filter will default to the filter properties from the report. To change the filter to use a different set of properties, set the desired properties in the inline add row and click the + button. Select which set of properties to be used.
    ​
    ​

  7. Save the dashboard
    ​
    ​

  8. Use the new filters to filter all of the reports and graphs on the dashboard at once
    ​
    ​
    ​

Issue

Likely Cause

Solution

Filter is missing from selection list

The filter isn't pinned in the report.

Open the source report, find the filter/variable, and click the Pin icon. Save the report.

Filter only updates some reports

Naming mismatch or different fields.

Check that all reports use the same table field. If using a Custom Filter, ensure the name is an exact text match to the report column.

"Add Filter" menu is empty

No non-primary filters selected.

Edit the Omni Filter widget and ensure you have assigned additional pinned filters as "Non-Primary."

Best Practices

  • Only pinned filters and variables from Fusion reports can be added to omni filters.
    ​
    ​

  • Configure pinned variables and filters in your reports the same way they should be display on the dashboard. This ensures that the default filters in the omni filter can be used without requiring any modification to the properties.
    ​
    ​

  • Use the same table field and settings for all filters and variables with the same name across dashboard reports. This ensures that the omni filter will pass in the filter value the same way to all report filters.
    ​
    ​

  • A custom filter can be added for filtering comparison reports or table views. The custom filter name must be an exact text match to the comparison filter or table view column.
