Distributor overview of getting started with EDI in Encompass: product, customer and AR setup, resending 810/856/894 files, fixing exchange task warnings, and requesting a new EDI setup. v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) is a standardized and automated way to exchange business documents, such as purchase orders and invoices, electronically. This guide will help you understand how EDI works and why it’s important for improving the efficiency and accuracy of your business communications and operations.

What is EDI and why it matters
​
​

  • Definition: EDI is the electronic exchange of business documents between companies in a standardized format, such as purchase orders or invoices.
    ​
    ​

  • Why It’s Important: EDI replaces paper-based processes and manual data entry with automated, real-time communication, leading to faster and more accurate transactions.

How EDI benefits your business
​
​

  • Efficiency & Speed: Transactions are processed automatically, reducing turnaround times and freeing up resources.
    ​
    ​

  • Cost Savings: EDI reduces the need for paper, printing, and storage, and minimizes costly errors caused by manual entry.
    ​
    ​

  • Enhanced Accuracy & Compliance: Automated data exchange helps ensure accuracy, reduces rework, and can aid in meeting compliance standards.
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory Management & Forecasting: Real-time data on orders and stock levels allows businesses to manage inventory more effectively, reducing out-of-stocks and overstocks, and helping to optimize inventory.

Fundamentals for EDI success

Sending and receiving EDI documents relies on the core configuration of your Encompass site. Accurate and consistent data lays the foundation for EDI success.
​
​
​EDI-Related Product Management

  • Confirm product controls are set up as expected by running Comparison Invoice Pricing Report. Fields such as Carrier/Case/Unit UPC, Product Pricing, Supplier Product Num, and Package Dimensions are critical values for EDI success.
    ​
    ​

  • Product Authorizations: When Product record controls are not sufficient to meet the EDI requirements for a specific trading partner (supplier/retailer), applicable Product Authorization record(s) are required. Values such as UPC and Package Dimensions can be modified per Chain, via Product Authorizations.

Customer Setup

Customer Identifiers: In order for retailers to identify their individual retail locations, a Customer ID value must be sent/received in an EDI file. The most commonly used customer identifier value, aside from the Customer ID itself (Customer.CustomerID), is what Encompass calls Chain Store Number (set on the Customers Table). Retailers will often use the terms Store #, Site ID, or Retailer ID to signify this value.

  • Other customer identifiers include DUNS # (9-digit value assigned by Dun & Bradstreet) and Global Location Number (GLN, most commonly used by Walmart).

AR Configuration

  • AR Accounts are the primary means by which outbound EDI data (810, 856, 894, etc.) is filtered. By assigning an AR Account to an Exchange Configuration, you are instructing your site to only send invoices under this AR Account through the assigned Exchange Configuration.
    ​
    ​

  • Split Invoices: When a trading partner requires invoice data to be split, usually between alcohol and non-alcohol products (using differing Vendor Numbers), the creation of Split Invoice records is required.
    ​
    ​

  • Other important values that are transmitted via Split Invoicing are: Distributors Vendor DUNS (when the trading partner requires the Encompass customer to send a different DUNS # value than what is found at Locations.DUNS), Retailer Dept Number (most commonly required for Walmart and Target EDI transactions), and EDI Price Group Code (used in EDI pricing files).
    ​
    ​

  • Encompass suggests, whenever possible, to create Split Invoice records at the Chain level.

EDI Troubleshooting

  • Monitoring Exchange Tasks for Warnings is the most effective way to identify and fix issues with EDI transmissions. The warning will provide specific information in the memo to guide you on what to fix and where this might be found.
    ​
    ​

  • Common issues include missing data points (Chain Store Numbers, Chain Product Numbers, UPCs, etc.), Unavailable/Discontinued/OOS Products, and locked Load Sheets.
    ​
    ​

  • If an exchange task is in pending status and it has been over 1 hour since the file was created, please contact Encompass Support.
    ​
    ​

  • If an exchange task is in an error status, you can attempt to resend the invoices if it is an outbound file. If this does not work or the file is inbound, please contact Encompass Support.

Resending EDI
​
​

Steps:

1. Go to the Invoices table
​
2. Filter to invoices that need to be resent. You can filter by date range, chain, AR Account, etc. (Note: Check the Time Updated column to see all results)
​
3. Edit Column for EDI Status column
​
4. Change the status to the resend status for the document you need to resend and fill down
​
5. Save Changes

The corresponding Scheduled task will transmit the files:

  • Generate_Outbound_EDI_PaymentRequest: PayLink 810, Fintech, iControl, other 810 Payment Requests
    ​
    ​

  • Generate_Outbound_EDI_Invoices: 810 Post-Delivery Invoice, 856 (ASN), 894
    ​
    ​

  • Generate_Outbound_NACHA: NACHA (legacy PayLink), EFT

Resend EDI Statuses

Invoices can be resent by changing the EDI Status field on the Invoice to one of the following based on the type of file you need to resend. To see what type of file you are sending, you can view the functional type on the exchange configuration.
​
​

Note: If you need to resend all EDI for the invoice or are unsure of what status to set the invoice to, you can set the status to ‘Not Yet Transmitted’ to resend all EDI.
​
​

  • Resend Pre-Delivery Notice: 894
    ​
    ​

  • Resend ASN: 856
    ​
    ​

  • Resend Post-Delivery: 810 Post-Delivery Invoice
    ​
    ​

  • Resend Payment Request: PayLink 810, Fintech, iControl
    ​
    ​

  • ACH Push Pay: NACHA (legacy PayLink), EFT

Indirect EDI (ie: GXS, OrderBud, etc.)

Depending on the products that your business distributes, manufacturers, and/or bottles/packages, a third party EDI processor will be required. Below is a breakdown of cohort and EDI processor:

  • Anheuser-Busch: AB OrderBud (formerly BudEC)

  • Brewery: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • Coca-Cola: OpenText CIS4

  • Craft Beer: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • Dairy: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • Distillery: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • DPSG: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • Food: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • MolsonCoors: OpenText GXS (MillerUFF)

  • Pepsi: PBEX

  • Red Bull: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • Soda: Direct w/ Trading Partner

  • Wine and Spirits: Direct w/ Trading Partner

Initiating a new EDI Setup
​
​

When a trading partner (supplier or retailer) has contacted your business, requesting an EDI implementation integration, follow these steps:
​
​

1. Navigate to your ‘Encompass Customer Pourtal’
​
2. Find the ‘Get Professional Services Help’ section (bottom right)
​
3. Click the ‘Create a new EDI Implementation service request’ link
​
4. Fill out and submit the EDI Implementation Project Request form
​
a. Submit a Zendesk ticket if you require any assistance filling out the form
​
5. When the form is submitted, an Encompass Task is created, where all implementation project updates and progress will be documented
16990154:
Distributor steps for amortizing a prepaid expense on an Accounts purchase in Encompass: set up Prepaid Amortization Account Maps and choose a Prepaid Schedule. Needs Encompass AP, Purchase Cost permission, v24.11+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.11

Pre-Conditions

  • Companies.EnableEncompassAP = True
    ​
    ​

  • Companies.GeneralAccountSystem = Encompass
    ​
    ​

  • Purchases.TransType = Accounts
    ​
    ​

  • View Permission = Purchase View
    ​
    ​

  • Edit Permission = Purchase Cost
    ​
    ​

  • EditPrepaidAccountMaps.LifeInMonths <= 24

Steps

New Purchase:
​
​

  • The IsPrepaid flag will appear for all Purchases where TransType = Accounts
    ​

- This happens after Add Purchase in the table view workflow
​
- This happens on the Create Bills dashboard
​
​

  • When changing IsPrepaid to True, a pop up will appear to select a Prepaid Schedule

- You must select a Prepaid Schedule to select 'Yes'
​
- If you select 'No', you will be taken back to Purchase Edit and IsPrepaid will be flagged back to False
​
​

  • Once the Prepaid Schedule is selected, it appears in the Purchase View and Edit dashboards
    ​

  • No amortization entries will post until after Purchase Confirmation

Purchase Confirmation:
​
​

  • This Purchase will be Confirmed as usual
    ​

- The Prepaid Schedule can be changed on the Purchase Confirm dashboard
​
​

  • Once the Purchase is Confirmed, amortization entries will be created

- These entries will be in the same Journal Entry as the Purchase
​
- The entirety of the amortization life will be posted
​
​

  • UnConfirming and Confirming again will recalculate these entries

Fields And Definitions

Prepaid Amortization Account Maps:
​
​1. Required to amortize prepaid expenses, must have at least 1 record to successfully set Purchases.IsPrepaid = True
​
2. Prepaid Schedule Name

  • Open text field for the user to name this something that makes sense (12 Month Immediate) is an example
    ​
    ​

  • This is what will appear on Purchase Edit
    ​
    ​

3. Company is a searchable dropdown
​
4. Expense Account is a searchable dropdown for the selected Company
​
5. Amortization Frequency

  • Monthly - amortization entries will post on the 1st of the month, every month, until the life in months expires
    ​
    ​

  • Quarterly - amortization entries will post on the 1st of the quarter (Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct) every quarter until the life in months expires
    ​
    ​

  • Bi-Annually - amortization entries will post bi-annually (Jan/Jul) until the life in months expires
    ​
    ​

6. Life in Months

  • Numerical entry that determines the duration of the amortization
    ​
    ​

  • Will be calculated either from Purchases.PostDate or the 1st of the month following the Purchase

7. Amortize in 1st month

  • Yes - first amortization entry will post on Purchases.PostDate, all other entries will post as noted above
    ​
    ​

  • No - first amortization entry will post on the 1st of the next period determined by Amortization Frequency


Purchases.IsPrepaid
​
​

1. Flag to enable selection of a Prepaid Schedule (Prepaid Amortization Account Maps) to amortize the expense
​
2. Not editable

  • If this is flagged by mistake, the purchase should be deleted and the user create a new purchase
    ​
    ​

3. Setting Purchases.IsPrepaid = True requires Purchases.PrepaidScheduleID = NOT NULL
​
4. Only selectable for Purchases.TransType = Accounts
​
​
​
​

Purchases.PrepaidSchedule
​
​

1. Selected record from Prepaid Amortization Account Maps to determine amortization details
​
2. Must be NOT NULL when Purchases.IsPrepaid = True
​
3. Can be changed until Purchase is Confirmed, including during the Purchase Confirmation workflow

Best Practices

  • Purchases.Total is used as the total amount ($Total)
    ​
    ​

  • Life in Months is used as the primary divider (LiM)
    ​
    ​

  • Amortization Method is used as a secondary divider (AM)

- Monthly = 1, Quarterly = 3, Bi-annually = 6
​

  • Calculation is $Total/(LiM/AM)

Example:

  • $Total = $12,000
    ​
    ​

  • Life in Months = 15
    ​
    ​

  • Amortization Method = Quarterly
    ​
    ​

  • 12,000/(15/3)
    ​
    ​

  • 12,000/5
    ​
    ​

  • We will get 5 amortization entries, posted every 3 months, each of $2,400

16990158:
Distributor steps for setting up fixed assets and monthly depreciation in Encompass: add Asset Categories and account maps, then create an Asset purchase. Needs Encompass Financials, Fixed Assets on, v24.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.12

Pre-Conditions

Must be using Encompass Financials (General Accounting System = Encompass).

Must have Fixed Assets enabled on the Company(s) record.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to add Asset Categories
​
​1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Asset Categories table.
​
2. Click the Add Asset Categories button.
​
3. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the Add Asset Categories form and click the Add Record button when complete.
​
4. Select the ‘Sub Tables’ button and choose Fixed Asset Account Map.
​
5. Click the Add Asset Account Map button to tie the account you wish to be used for the Asset Category (you may need to select the + button next to the record).
​
​
a. The Asset Account should be the account you want to be credited by each Depreciations/Amortization entry.
​
i. For a capitalized asset, this would be the related accumulated Depreciation account.
​
ii. For a Prepaid Expense, this would be the Prepaid Expense account.
​
​
b. The Expense Account should be the Account you want to be debited by each Depreciation/Amortization entry.
​
1. If this is a new Asset Type select the Sub Tables button and choose Asset Types.
​
​ 2. Select Add Asset Types to tie the account you wish to be used for the Asset Category.
(you may need to select the + button next to the record)
​
3. If using an existingAsset Type, navigate to the Asset Types table and update the Asset Category field with the newly created Category.

How to add an Asset
​
​

1. Create a Purchase with the Trans Type set to Asset on the Purchase.
​
2. If purchasing Fixed Assets, you must flag IsFixedAsset = True on the Purchase.
​
3. Set the Asset Category, Asset Type, Asset Description, Serial Number, Placed Service Date, and Asset Cost.
​
4. This creates the Asset Record on the Assets table with the information populated from the purchase.
​
5. This also creates the Fixed Asset record on the Fixed Assets table.

Fields And Definitions

Key Tables

  • Asset Categories - Used to tie Asset Types and Fixed Asset Accounts together and also inform how the depreciation/amortization should behave
    ​
    ​

  • Asset Types - This table is used to set a new asset category for a group of assets, and must be added prior to the Purchase
    ​
    ​

  • Asset Account Maps - This table is used to set up account mapping for an Asset Category
    ​
    ​

  • Assets - This table is used to set the placed-in-service date and other deployment-related fields
    ​
    ​

  • Fixed Assets - This table is used to set the cost, remaining value, salvage value, and other financial-related fields

Fields and Definitions For Asset Categories Table

  • Asset Category - This field serves as a label for the asset category
    ​
    ​

  • Depreciation Method - Use this field to determine the type of depreciation applied to assets under this category
    ​
    ​

  • Required Serial Number - Use this field to determine if a serial number is required
    ​
    ​

  • Depreciation Life in Months - This field determines how much an item value will depreciate from the start of the placed-in-service date set on the asset record, Cost/Deprecation Life in Months = Monthly depreciation

Related Fields and Definitions on the Assets Table

  • Asset Description - Used to label the purpose of the recurring depreciation entry (set/created when Purchase is created)
    ​
    ​

  • Serial Number - Used to precisely identify the asset related to this series of entries (set/created when Purchase is created)
    ​
    ​

  • Placed In Service Date - The date that determines when the Asset will be placed in service and will trigger depreciating entries the following month (set/created when Purchase is created)

Related Fields and Definitions on the Fixed Assets Table

  • Cost - Initial acquisition cost, this amount is reflected on the balance sheet in a Fixed Asset account
    ​
    ​

  • Remaining Value - Cost minus depreciation; this value can never go below the Salvage Value
    ​
    ​

  • Salvage Value - The salvage, or minimum, value of the asset; Remaining Value will never go below this amount

Best Practices

  • Asset Account and Expense Account should be different Accounts

16990162:
Distributor best practices for using All Products = True on promotions in Encompass, e.g. pricing inventory adjustment, transfer or employee customers at zero or laid-in cost, and avoiding extra promo zones. v24.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.10

Best Practices

When setting up a Promotion, you have the option to set a field, All Products = True/False. This field can be useful when utilized correctly.

Business Case:

  • The All Products field is used in special cases where a promotion affects all products.
    ​
    ​

  • This becomes very useful when you are trying to set up an Inventory Adjustment customer. In this use case, users would expect all products invoiced for that customer would be zero, as you do not want it to affect Income.
    ​
    ​

  • Another popular use case is Transfer customers or Employee customers that get charged Laid-In cost for all products. In this use case, users would expect all products to be invoiced at cost.

Not Used For:

  • The All Products should not be used for other Promotion Types such as Frontline, Discount, and Pricing. These promotion types are segmented to a specific Products and therefore are not good candidates for this functionality.

Note:

  • Encompass will always look for the best price, regardless of the All Products flag. Therefore, if a customer belongs to both a Promotion Zone (All Products = True) and a Promotion Zone (All Products = False), you would remove this customer from the Discount Zone to ensure they are not eligible for any discounts.
    ​
    ​

  • When setting up Inventory Adjustment or Transfer customers, it is important to ensure they are only tied to promotion zones that qualify them for the correct pricing. If they are tied to any other zones, you can go to the Customers Promotions Zones table to remove the customer from any unnecessary zones. If the source on the Customers Promotion Zone = Customer you will need to change the zone on the Customer record. If the source on the Customer Promotions Zone = Chain you will need to remove the promo zone on the chain record.

Pre-Conditions

1. Distribution Area and Income Area, Charge Area, Deposit Area, and Jurisdiction for transfers must exist. These attributes or fields will likely be different for those dependent on the retail or wholesale customers.
​
2. The Transfer Planner Setup dashboard will now automatically designate a predetermined transfer clearing product in the Companies table.

3. To opt into this new feature, set the Transfer Clearing Product field in the Companies table.

  • Note: This transfer clearing configuration is best suited for simple company configurations. Customers with a more complex configuration or that require inter-company clearing should use the Auto AR/AP write off functionality. See the Transfer Planner Overview and Workflow help resource for how to set this up.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Creating Transfer Direction

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the 'Transfer Planner Setup' Dashboard.
​
2. Select 'Add Transfer Direction'.
​
3. Select the 'FromLocation' where Transfers will be picked and loaded from.
​
4. Select the 'ToLocation' where Transfers will be Received and put away in.
​
5. Select the 'ToCompany' that the AP will be created under.
​
6. To prevent creating Transfers at cost, utilize the 'Transfer Clearing Product' field. Next, enter the Product created to clear AP/AR in the site. This is not required and can be added later on in the process.
​
​

  • The Transfer Planner Setup dashboard will automatically designate a predetermined transfer-clearing product in the Companies table.

7. Enter a Transfer Clearing account if the site utilizes one. This is not required, and each Transfer Customer and Vendor will automatically create their own AP/AR Accounts. These will be created for the user and can have a Transfer Clearing product added to them to ensure they are automatically cleared when running end of Day.
​
8. Select the 'DistributionArea' needed for the 'FromLocation'. Only relevant Distribution Areas will show in the drop-down to select.
​
9. Select the Desired 'Charge Area' for Transfer Invoices. This will be set on the transfer customer, usually this is a "No Charge" charge area because there are not usually any invoice charges for transfer customers or invoices.
​
10. Select the Desired 'Deposit Area' for Transfer Purchases. This will be set on the transfer customer, it is recommended to use a deposit areas with packages deposits setup so that the deposit costs is transfer for kegs.
​
11. Select the desired 'Jurisdiction' for the Transfer Customer to utilize. This will be set on the transfer customer, usually this is a jurisdiction that is not setup that is not set up with any depletion taxes.

12. Select 'Create Transfer Direction'.

Transfer Rules
​
​

  • Transfer Rules are now created and will show just below the filters on the Transfer Planner Setup Dashboard. Transfer Vendors and Customers will also be created, as well as the EDI used between locations.

Data that is created:
​
​

1. Customer Type = Transfer
​
2. Customer = Transfer Location A to Location B
​
3. ARAccount = Transfer Location A to Location B
​
4. Route Type = Transfer
​
5. Routes: A transfer route for each day of the week will be created. Ex. Transfer From 'LocationAMon'
​
6. Stops for the 5 routes for the transfer customer
​
7. If the transfer clearing product / account are entered in using the Transfer Setup Dashboard - Step 4, "Transfer" AR and AP terms will be created, as well as the income and expense account mapping.
​
8. Vendor = Transfer Location A to Location B
​
9. AP Account = Transfer Location A to Location B

10. Trading Partners = Set on Customers, Vendors and Exchange Configurations

NOTE: Company on the AP Account the Company selected in Using the Transfer Setup Dashboard - Step 3.
​
​
11. Exchange Congurations and Exchange Configuration AP/AR Accounts
​
12. Inventory Transfer Rules

Cross Company - No Transfer Clearing - Terms can write off to company due to/due from or use AR/AP to track

1 Location - 2 Companies

  1. User Transfer Planner Setup Dashboard to 1st Company

  2. Setup Split Invoices on customer from step 1

  3. Create New AR Account

  4. Create New Vendor and AP Account

  5. Create 3 New Exchange Maps - copied from step 1

  6. Update AR Account and AP Account

  7. Update Receiver ID and SenderID to have prefix for company

  8. Test

Fields And Definitions

  • From Location - Where Transfers will be picked and loaded from.
    ​
    ​

  • To Location - where Transfers will be Received and put away in.

Best Practices

Create each Transfer Location and test that the Purchase and invoice are created as expected. This includes ensuring the correct location is used on the Purchase in the 'To Location'.

Setup Best Practices

- Address Locations must be Unique (multiple locations can't be the same Ex. Brewery and Taproom, Beer and Spirits)

- Set the From Customer address = From Location so loadsheets go to correct location

- Set the To Vendor address = To Location Address so purchases go to correct location

- Click the arrow to view the Inventory Transfer Rule and set the Purchase Cost Rule - usually do not accrue.

- If no cross company transfers - Set the Company Transfer Clearing Product with Transfer Clearing Product with Income/Expense Account Maps

**If there is cross company or split invoices for cross company reach out to support.

Distributor steps for setting up single sign-on with a generic OAuth2 provider in Encompass: register the redirect URL, then add an OAuth Settings record with app ID, secret and URLs. Requires v24.11+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.11

Pre-Conditions

Your OAuth provider must meet the OAuth2 protocol.

The provider must support including these items in the response:

  • User ID Identifier
    ​
    ​

  • Email Identifier
    ​
    ​

  • Name Identifier

Steps

Before starting in Encompass, the OAuth integration must be setup in the 3rd party OAuth provider.

  • Typically the 'type' in the 3rd party provider will need to be set to 'Web Application'.

The following information will be needed in the setup of the 3rd party provider:

  • Sign-in redirect URL = https://{Your Encompass URL}/aspx1/OAuth.aspx
    ​
    ​

  • Example: https://encompasstech.com/OAuth.aspx

Contact your 3rd party OAuth provider for additional details about how to set up an Application for OAuth in their environment.

You will need the following information out of the 3rd party OAuth provider system to be entered in Encompass in the below steps:

  • App ID
    ​
    ​

  • App Secret
    ​
    ​

  • Request URL
    ​
    ​

  • Authorization URL
    ​
    ​

  • Token URL
    ​
    ​

  • Response UserID Identifier
    ​
    ​

  • Response Email Identifier
    ​
    ​

  • Response Name Identifier
    ​
    ​

  • Scope

After the application is setup in the 3rd party OAuth provider, in Encompass:

  1. Go to the OAuth Settings table
    ​
    ​

  2. Click Add OAuth Settings at the top to add a new record
    ​
    ​

  3. Select Generic as the service provider
    ​
    ​

  4. Fill in the App ID and Client Secret from the 3rd party application
    ​
    ​

  5. Fill in the Request URL, Authorization URL, and Token URL from the 3rd party application
    ​
    ​

  6. Leave Auto Verify Email turned on - This would only be turned off if you want to enforce your users to verify their own email address manually in Encompass. This is typically done when the OAuth provider does not do this automatically.
    ​
    ​

  7. Populate the Response UserID Identifier, Response Email Identifier, and Response Name Identifier with the names of what these values will be in the JWT from the 3rd party provider.
    ​
    ​

  8. Populate the Scope with whatever is required by the 3rd party provider to obtain the UserID, Email, and Name information in Step 7
    ​
    ​

  9. Populate the Icon URL with an image URL that should be displayed on the login page for users to click for the OAuth sign-in method. It is recommended that this is png image, square (equal height and width), between 30x30px and 100x100px in size.
    ​
    ​

  10. Populate the Display Name with the name of the 3rd Party application, this will be displayed in a few places, such as the profile page, as the sign-in method.

Other optional settings, as needed for certain providers:

  • Token Type: Can be set to 'AccessToken' for if the provider uses an AccessToken (instead of the default ID token) for JWT decoding
    ​
    ​

  • Token Post Data: Extra URL values that need to be included in the HTTP request
    ​
    ​

  • LogOut URL: Extra URL to call on the OAuth provider when the user logs out

Best Practices

  • After setup, fully test the OAuth login flow with a sample user before turning on any OAuth requirements (Roles - Require OAuth Login setting)
    ​
    ​

  • Ensure email is matching between Encompass and the 3rd party OAuth system, this is the primary linking mechanism for Encompass.

16990184:
Distributor setup for the Service Time Controls table in Encompass to capture customer average service times from GPS geofences, set date ranges, reset averages and find reports. Needs Fleet Tracker, v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

Service Time Controls require the Fleet Tracker integration.

Steps

The Service Time Controls table is a straightforward table with three records for merchandising, delivery, and sales based on when a vehicle is within a customer's geofenced area

  • Type: Merchandiser, Delivery, or Sales: Based on the type of activity.
    ​
    ​

  • Start date: Date to start capturing service times
    ​
    ​

  • End date (optional): Date to stop capturing service times. If empty, the end date will be today's date.

For example, if a delivery vehicle has a GPS installed and the vehicle is on the the route/loadsheet, "OBD at Customer Location" time clock events will be created, which will be used to set the Delivery Average Service Time on the Customers table.

When are average service times set on customers?
​
​There is a scheduled task named Update_CustomerAvgServiceTimes_OBD that runs nightly. This can be ran manually if a user has Gloabal Setting Edit permissions.

Can the average service times on the customer be reset?
​
​Yes, the average service times data can be reset to no values by clearing out the Start and End Date on the Service Time Controls table.

Is the a limit on how far back the start date can be set?
​
​Yes, average service times can be calculated for the past 365 days, with the earliest start date limited to last year. Once the start date is over a year ago, the system will keep advancing the start date to today - 365 days.

Can the average service times be set for a specific date range?
​
​Yes. As long as the start date is within one year. For example, if today is January 1, 2025, and you wanted to have the system calculate average service times from the beginning of May through the end of September for 2024, set the start date equal to 5/1/2024 and the end date equal to 9/30/2024. Once the Update_CustomerAvgServiceTimes_OBD scheduled task runs, the update averages will be set on the customer table.

Where are the averages stored again?
​
​Service time averages are stored on the Customers table, including the Merchandiser Average Service Time, Delivery Averages Service Time, and Sales Averages Service Time.

Are there any pre-built reports that will show average service times?
​
​Yes. Check out the Average Service Times report on the Fleet Reports dashboard. Change the layout of the report to group by chain, customer type, customer, etc; The default start date of the report is the current week (starting Monday) and the default end date is today. Use the filters to change the start or end date as well as add additional filters.

The following assumes that a given distributor is ready to begin trading EDI files with a defined trading partner and the distributor does not have an EDI Implementation service request Task ID already assigned.

Steps

How to Create a New EDI Implementation Service Request

Screenshot

3. In the Encompass Customer field, enter the name of your organization (if you already have an existing EDI implementation Task ID, enter that ID in the 'Task ID' field and skip the Encompass Customer field)

Fields And Definitions

  • Task ID: The Encompass Task ID provided to the distributor by Encompass directly

Steps

How do Tap Handle Surveys Work?
​
​
​Tap Handle Surveys have special functionality to take a photo of the tap handles at a customer and then select the brands and count the number of tap handles for each brand. Encompass provides a System Objective with the setup needed for this survey that you can begin using anytime.
​
​
​Setup Tap Handle Survey

1. Navigate to the Objectives table

2. Add a Column to the Objectives table: System Objective ID
​
3. Search for System Objective ID "1"
​
4. If the Survey is not found, click the Active column header and include "Inactive" results.
​
5. To begin deploying the survey, add an Objective Schedule.
​
*Tap Handle Surveys typically have an Objective Schedule set to On Premise=True to target On Premise Customers only.
​
​
​Taking the Survey on Encompass Mobile
​
​
​1. Tap the Tap Handle survey task from Customer Event View
​
2. Select the Bar Location you want to count first
​
3. Tap the camera icon to take or upload a photo of the tap handles in the Bar Location
​
4. Tap Add Taps
​
5. The Brands that display automatically are the Brands that were previously logged for the Customer/Bar Location
​
6. To add an additional Brand, Tap Next Brand in the top right corner
​
7. Search for and tap the Brands to add to the list
​
8. Tap the check mark to return to the Customer's Brands
​
9. Tap each Brand to increase the number of Tap Handles for each Brand. The max is 4. After 4, the Brand will be set back to 0
​
10. Tap Next Bar Location and repeat these steps for each location as necessary
​
11. Once all Bar Locations are complete, tap Continue
​
​12. Tap Completed

Best Practices

  • If you need to ask questions about the taps or the customer, this survey will not allow for survey questions in addition to the special functionality of the Tap Handle Survey. It is recommended to create an additional survey without the Objective Type Tap Handle. Then, add questions and set the Repeat Questions field on the Survey Section to "Repeat for Multiple Brands". This will allow the user to still select a brand and then answer the survey questions for each brand.
    ​
    ​

  • The Bar Locations cannot be edited on the System Objective. To customize the Bar Locations that display, use the Table Copy function to copy the Tap Handle Objective and edit the Survey Section Values.
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • The System Objective prompts users to complete the Tap Handle Survey at the beginning of their customer event. They will not be able to complete their other tasks until the Tap Handle Survey is completed. If you want to change when the task is prompted, copy the System Objective and Update the Prompt Task field on the Assigned status.
    ​
    ​

  • The System Objective assigns Tap Handle Surveys to the Assigned Sales Rep for Customers that meet the criteria of the Objective Schedule created. If you want to change who completes the surveys, copy the System Objective and update the Assign To Group on the Objective Statuses.

16990194:
Distributor reference on Encompass Table Import time limits (1 hour manual, 5 minutes automated) and why failed imports get automations disabled, plus how to re-enable them. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

Table Import has timeout quotas and limitations on usage to ensure your system maintains good performance for others.
​
​

These quotas include:

  • Maximum execution time of an Import Task when run manually: 1 hour
    ​
    ​

  • Maximum execution time of an Import Task when run via scheduled task/automation: 5 minutes

Executions times include the time taken to get new data (from a report/source) and for the actual import of the data. Table Imports are stopped immediately after passing the allowed time. EDBL Imports are allowed to attempt to finish execution after the allowed time has passed, up to a maximum of 1 hour, then are stopped forcefully. The failure count is incremented anytime these routines go past the allowed timeout.

If an Import Routine runs past the allowed time, the Fail Count value will be increased by 1.

Failures will cause a delay in future executions:

  • 1 failure = automations disabled for 1 hour

  • 2 failures = automations disabled for 4 hours

  • 3-9 failures = automations disabled for 28 hours

  • 10+ failures = automations permenantly disabled

A disabled import routine can be re-enabled by manually running it again successfully (after optimizing as needed)
16990195:
Distributor/API builder steps for allowing external websites to call your Encompass API Commands (CORS) by adding API Origins to an Application. Needs Solution Authentications and API Edit permissions.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

All modern browsers support Cross-Origin Resource Sharing, or CORS. This means that by default, the javascript on a page cannot make a request to a different domain unless the receiving domain has explicitly allowed it.
​
​
To allow this in Encompass, API builders need to add records to the API Origins table under their Application.

  • A record in the API Origins table allows your requests from another system to be requested back to the Encompass servers, for your API commands, from the javascipt on that external page.
    ​
    ​

  • For example, this would allow a public site for your company to reach into an API Command you created in your Encompass system to get a product listing.

By default, if no API Origins are created, only requests from the same Encompass domain are allowed to the API Commands.

You must have permission (Solution Authentications) to edit an Application in order to add API Origins to that Application, and the API Edit permission.

Actual: Unable to access site

Be sure to note the server and attach any screenshots you have of errors received.

16990203:
Distributor steps for setting up Costco ASN pallet tags in Encompass: create a Costco customer pick type, load group, pick methods and pick rules. Needs Costco ASN EDI and a ZPL printer, v24.05+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.05

Pre-Conditions

  • Must have ASN EDI configurations set up with Costco
    ​
    ​

  • Must have the ability to print pallet tags to a ZPL label printer

Steps

This article will guide a user through all the steps needed to create a separate Load Group for Costco picking so the new Costco ASN Pallet Tag template can be assigned. A new Load Group is necessary if you require separate ASN Pallet Tag formats for different customers, such as our original ASN template for Walmart and the new template for Costco.

Create a new Customer Pick Type and assigning it to Costco customers

  1. Go to the Customer Pick Types table

  2. Click Add Record

  3. Name the new record “Costco”

  4. Click Add Record

  5. Go to the Customers table, and filter to all Costco customers

  6. Click the Columns button at the top of the page, select the “Customer Pick Type” column and click Create View

  7. Click on the Customer Pick Type column header to use Column Edit and fill down all customers to the new Costco customer pick type created in steps 1-4

  8. Save Changes to complete the Customer Pick Type update

How to create a new Load Group and assign the new ASN Pallet Tag Template

  1. Go to the Load Groups table

  2. Filter to or arrow-into a Load Group that matches the setup you’d like Costco to mimic (recommended: any Load Group that is already set up for ASN customers)

  3. Click on Subtables > Copy Load Groups

  4. Update the Load Group field to a new name for this Load Group, like “Costco”

  5. Update the ASN Pallet Tag Template field to the new Costco ASN pallet tag template

  6. If you are not currently printing ASN tags, make sure to set the Pallet Confirmed Action field to include “Print Pallet ASN”

  7. Deselect the option to copy related Pick Methods

  8. Click Copy Record

How to create a new Pick Method(s) for the new Load Group

  1. Go to the Pick Methods table

  2. Filter to any Pick Methods that are used to pick ASN customers

  3. Click on Subtables > Copy Pick Methods

  4. Deselect the option to copy related Pick Rules, but keep Pick Team Pick Methods selected

  5. Click Copy Record, then View New Records

  6. Use Column Edit on the Pick Method column to update the Pick Method names, adding 'Costco' to the beginning, and removing any '_2'

How to create new Pick Rule(s) for the new Pick Method(s)

  1. Go to the Pick Rules table

  2. Filter to any Pick Rules that are used to pick ASN customers

  3. Click on Subtables > Copy Pick Rules

  4. Fill in the Customer Pick Type field as the Costco customer pick type created in the first section of this document

  5. If all Pick Rules will use the same Pick Method, fill in the Pick Method field with the newly created Costco Pick Method

  6. Click Copy Record, then View New Records

  7. Use Column Edit on the Priority column to shift the new pick rules to slightly higher within the overall list of Pick Rules

  8. If the new Pick Rules will use different Pick Methods, use Column Edit on the Pick Method column to assign the individual new Pick Methods as desired

  9. Save Changes to complete the updates to the new Pick Rules

Fields And Definitions

  • Load Group - Table holding configurations that determine what actions occur for a pallet throughout its picking lifecycle.
    ​
    ​

  • LoadGroups.ASNPalletTagTemplate - This field on the Load Groups table determines what the ASN tag will look like when printed.
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Method - Table holding configurations that determine how a pallet is built, and how a user will interact with that pallet during picking.
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Rule - Table holding configurations that help identify groupings of products on invoices that should be assigned the same Pick Method during palletization.
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Team - A group of employees that are assigned to certain Pick Methods during the picking process. For example, a layer pick team or a keg pick team.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Pick Type - Used to group certain customers together that need to have their orders built in a certain way.

Best Practices

  • Do not make any changes to Pick Rules, Pick Methods, or Load Groups without first considering the greater context of those changes. The steps in this article should not be followed verbatim; make sure you are referencing current warehouse processes and pick rule configurations to properly fit any new Costco-related records into the larger workflow.
    ​
    ​

  • Make sure to prioritize any new pick rules so that they fit within the current picking priorities during palletization. A priority that is too high or too low may interfere with non-Costco pallets, or result in Costco pallets not being labeled properly.
    ​
    ​

  • Make sure new Costco Pick Methods are added to a Pick Team, that way warehouse team members are allowed to pick the pallets.

16990205:
Distributor steps for fixing a purchase blocked by Strict Purchase Confirmation in Encompass due to $0 FOB or deposit cost, or confirming with AP Override. Needs System Setting 3217 on and v25.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.09

Pre-Conditions

  • The user must be attempting to confirm a Purchase within the Encompass system.

  • System Setting 3217 must be set to True to enable Strict Purchase Confirmation.

  • The Product Type of the affected product must have ProductTypes.TrackInventory set to True.

  • The Product Type of the affected product must have either:

    • ProductTypes.EnforceFOB set to True (for FOB enforcement).

    • Inventory.DefaultDepositCost set to > $0 (for Deposit Cost enforcement).

  • The Purchase Transaction must have a non-zero number of units (NumUnits <> 0).

  • The user must have the AP Override permission assigned to their account to bypass the enforcement block (if necessary).

Steps

  • Identify the Blocked Products and Costs: When the "Confirm Bill" button is clicked and the process is blocked, review the displayed screen. Note which products are listed in red text; these are the transactions with an FOB or Deposit Cost equal to $0.

  • Return to Purchase Edit: Click the "Back to Purchase" button. This action will redirect you to the Purchase Edit screen for the affected Purchase ID, which is necessary to adjust the pricing.

  • Correct the FOB (Unit Price):

    • Locate the product(s) identified in Step 1.

    • Update the Unit Price (which is the FOB) for the transaction to a value greater than $0.

  • Correct the Deposit Cost:

    • Locate the product(s) identified in Step 1.

    • Update the Deposit Cost for the transaction to a value greater than $0. Note: This applies only if Deposit Cost enforcement is blocking confirmation.

  • Re-attempt Purchase Confirmation: Save the changes on the Purchase Edit screen and attempt the Confirm Bill process again.

  • Use AP Override (If Authorized and Necessary): If the issue cannot be immediately resolved, and the user has the AP Override permission, they may choose to bypass the enforcement:

    • Click the "Confirm with AP Override" button on the blocked screen.

    • Note: This action will confirm all Purchases on the Shipment and is logged in the Shipments Field Audit. The $0 costing will need to be remedied later via the End of Day Rollback dashboard or the FIFO Adjustment Tool.

Fields And Definitions

  • FOB (Freight On Board): In this context, it refers to the cost of the product, equivalent to the value stored in PurchaseTransactions.UnitPrice. It must be greater than $0 for enforced products.

  • Strict Purchase Confirmation: A feature enabled by System Setting 3217 = True that adds mandatory checks for non-zero FOB and Deposit Cost during the Purchase Confirmation workflow.

  • ProductTypes.EnforceFOB: A new setting at the Product Type level. When set to True (along with TrackInventory = True), it enforces a non-zero FOB during Purchase Confirmation.

  • Inventory.DefaultDepositCost: The default deposit cost set for a product in the Inventory master record. A value > $0 triggers Deposit Cost enforcement if the product's type is tracked.

  • AP Override Permission: A user-level permission that allows a user to bypass the Strict Purchase Confirmation enforcement block by clicking "Confirm with AP Override," thereby posting a Purchase with a $0 cost.

  • Purchase Confirmation: The workflow of receiving and reconciling a physical shipment with a vendor invoice (bill) and posting the resulting transaction data to the general ledger.

  • Shipments Field Audit: A system log that records when the Confirm with AP Override action is used.

Best Practices

  • Proactive Cost Entry: Always ensure that new purchases of inventoried products include a non-zero Unit Price (FOB) and, if applicable, a non-zero Deposit Costbefore attempting the confirmation workflow.

  • Product Type Management: For Product Types that are intended to Track Inventory but not cost (e.g., contract brewing, tap handles, POS items), explicitly set ProductTypes.EnforceFOB to False to prevent unnecessary blocks.

  • AP Override Restriction: Grant the AP Override permission only to high-level financial users. Use this workflow sparingly, as overriding the enforcement block carries the risk of inaccurate costing and general ledger data.

  • Post-Override Remediation: If the AP Override is used, ensure the inaccurate $0 costing is corrected immediately after the Accounts Payable period is closed using the FIFO Adjustment Tool or the End of Day Rollback dashboard.
16990206:
Distributor steps for exporting routes and customers from a Route Version to the Wise Systems Strategic Planner for route optimization in Encompass. Needs the Strategic Routing App, v24.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.09

Pre-Conditions

Requires the Strategic Routing App to be installed.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Exporting Data to Wise Systems Strategic Planner

​
​
1. Navigate to the Route Versions table

  • The Route Versions table is the entry point of the Strategic Planner integration.

2. Click on the table action icon/3 dots next to the inactive Route Version
​
3. Select the Strategic Planner menu option
​
4. Click "Add a planning session"
​
5. Give the Planning Session a descriptive name and click the "Create" button.

  • After a few seconds, the planning session will be updated with a unique session ID and will be set to the New status.

6. Select the planning session and click the "Next Fleet" button to begin the process to determine what routes and activities will be included in the route planning session.
​
7. Select the Activity

  • The fleet includes what routes and vehicles you want to include in the planning session. The activity selected will filter on those routes. For example, selecting presell activities will filter on presell routes. It is not recommended to combine presell and delivery in the same planning session.

8. Add any additional filters and click the "Search" button to load the fleet data
​
9. Exclude vehicles from the plan

  • You may not want certain vehicles or routes to be included in the route planning session. After the data is returned, check the Exclude checkbox to prevent that vehicle and route from being included.

10. Once you have the desired vehicles and routes included, click the "Next Customers" button to begin setting up the customer data
​
11. Load customers by selecting a sales history date range and applying any other desired filters
​
12. Then, click the "Search" button to load the matching customers
​
13. The customer data will include sales cycle averages, which are calculated using the average weekly sales for the date range selected. The average is then multiplied by the frequency of the customer's visits in a 4-week cycle.

  • For example, if a weekly visited customer had an average sales of 100 cases per week, the sales cycle average would be 400 cases.

14. Leaving a customer assigned to a route will leave that customer on their current route in the planning session. To unassign a customer from a route, click "Unassign Route". This will tell the strategic planner that this customer can be assigned to any route.

  • If you have filtered on customers that are currently on a route that is not included in the fleet file, they will automatically be unassigned. For example, if you did not include route 100 in the fleet data, but are including customers that are currently on route 100, they would have to be unassigned from the route.

15. A service pattern includes the day of the week and phase. Unassigning a customer from a service pattern will allow that customer to be routed to other days and different phases.

  • The current frequency of a customer will not change, for example, if a service pattern for a customer is currently phase one only, that customer could be moved to phase 2, 3, or 4.

16. It is possible to unassign a customer from a vehicle type as well by checking "Unassign Vehicle Types".

  • If the vehicle type is not unassigned, that customer will only be put on a route with the same vehicle type that is included in the fleet file.

17. To send your fleet and customer data, click "Send to Strategic Planner".
​
18. Then, click "Login to Strategic Planner". This will open the Wise Systems Strategic Planning tool in a new tab in your browser.

Best Practices

Before sending data to Wise:

  • Review the data on the Service Windows table. Having accurate start and end times, and days of the week data will greatly improve route optimization results.

  • Have 1 vehicle and 1 user on 1 route. For example if you are including route 101 in your route plan, in Encompass, this typically is 5 route records (101 Mon, 101 Tue, 101 Wed, 101 Thu, 101 Fri). These 5 records should have the same vehicle and same user. Having mixed vehicles or users on the same route number will cause duplication in Wise.

  • By design, Encompass only allows inactive route version to be exported or imported from/to Encompass. Copying the active version as the baseline is the best practice.

  • Do not export delivery, presell, merchandising, etc; on the same route planning session. Wise doesn't handle this well. For presell and delivery, we have the functionality in place to keep delivery and presell stops aligned when importing back into Encompass.

16990210:
Warehouse manager steps for calculating bin Case Capacity: set up Bin Types (pallet capacity, dimensions or manual), assign them to Bins, and run Update_Inventories_Properties. Needs BinEdit permission; v19.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 19.01

Steps

The Case Capacity of a Bin is calculated using the Bin Type assigned to a Bin. This article reviews the Bin Type configuration process and related data for calculating Case Capacity.
​
​

  1. Create or Manage Bin Types

    • Navigate to the Bin Types table via Universal Search.
      ​
      ​

    • For each physically unique kind of bin found in the warehouse, create a Bin Type record and fill in the appropriate fields:
      ​
      ​

      • Name the Bin Type something recognizable, like "2 Pallet," "Flow Rack," or "Manual Capacity" for example.
        ​
        ​

      • Pallet Capacity: Enter the number of full pallets that can fit in the bin. This may be "0" for bins that do not fit a full pallet.
        ​
        ​

      • Dimensions: Enter the Height, Width, and Length of the bin using the same unit of measurement as product case dimensions. These fields may be set as "0" for Bin Types where Pallet Capacity will be used.
        ​
        ​

      • All fields may be set to "0" if manual Case Capacity entry is preferred for relevant bins.
        ​
        ​

  2. Assign Bin Types to Bins

    • Navigate to the Bins table.
      ​
      ​

    • Filter to the desired set of Bins.
      ​
      ​

    • For each Bin, assign a Bin Type:
      ​
      ​

      • Click the "Bin Type" column header and select "Column Edit" to assign Bin Types in bulk.
        ​
        ​

      • Click the edit icon next to each Bin to assign Bin Types individually.
        ​
        ​

    • Once all Bins have beed assigned a Bin Type, make sure changes have been saved. The "Case Capacity" field will not update immediately.
      ​
      ​

  3. Trigger "Case Capacity" calculation

    • Navitage to the Scheduled Tasks table, and filter to the "Update_Inventories_Properties" Scheduled Task.
      ​
      ​

    • Execute "Update_Inventories_Properties" to calculate and update the Case Capacity for each bin.
      ​
      ​

    • This task can be run manually at any time, but it will be run automatically overnight.
      ​
      ​

  4. Verify and Adjust

    • After the scheduled task has run, verify that the Case Capacity field for each bin has been updated correctly.
      ​
      ​

    • Make any necessary adjustments directly in the Bins table for bins with manual case capacity settings.

Fields And Definitions

  • The BinEdit permission is needed to make changes to the Bin Types and Bins tables.

Best Practices

Understanding Case Capacity Calculation
​
​

  • Using Dimensions: If Height, Width, and Length are specified in the Bin Type of a given Bin, the system will compare these dimensions with the product's case dimensions to calculate the bin's case capacity.
    ​
    ​

    • Bin Type Dimensions: Height = 24, Width = 18, Length = 96. Bin Type Volume = 41472.
      ​
      ​

    • Product Case Dimensions: Height = 12, Width = 18, Length = 12. Product Case Volue = 2592.
      ​
      ​

    • Bin Case Capacity = 41472/2592 = 16 Cases.
      ​
      ​

  • Using Pallet Capacity: If only the pallet capacity is specified in the Bin Type of a given Bin, the system will multiply this number by the product's cases per pallet to determine the bin's case capacity.
    ​
    ​

    • Bin Type Pallet Capacity = 10.
      ​
      ​

    • Product Cases Per Pallet = 100.
      ​
      ​

    • Bin Case Capacity = 10 * 100 = 1000 Cases.
      ​
      ​

  • Manual Case Capacity: If Height, Width, Length, and Pallet Capacity are all set to 0, the bin's case capacity must be entered manually by the warehouse manager or another high-permission team member. The system will not automatically calculate bin case capacities based on the assigned product with this method.
    ​
    ​

    • Bin record is edited to have Bin Type = Manual Capacity, and Case Capacity = 12.
      ​
      ​

    • Bin Case Capacity = 12 Cases.
      ​
      ​

    • This calculation method is typically used for flow racks that are regularly re-slotted to have new products assigned.

Distributor steps for importing a Wise Systems Strategic Planner session into Encompass Route Versions, previewing new stops and keeping presell/delivery stops aligned. Requires v24.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.09

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Strategic Routing: Importing Data from Wise Systems Strategic Planner

​
1. Click "Import Strategic Plan" from the Route Versions table.
​
​

Screenshot

2. Send the import request to Wise Systems by selecting the Planning Session to be imported and clicking on the "Send Import Request to Wise" button.
​

  • In order for a planning session to be imported, it must be in exported status.
    ​
    ​

3. After about 3 to 4 seconds, the status of the Planning Session will update to "Import Pending" status.
​
4. Click on the "Next: Preview Data" button to continue the import process.
​

  • The preview will show customers' current and new route information for you to review before actually importing the new routing data. The Wise Systems strategic planner will sequence stops, so it is important to know that multiple stops may be imported for the same customer.
    ​

  • For example, suppose a customer has a current delivery stop that is every week or phase "all" and the stop sequence is #1 every week. If the strategic planner sequence that customer to a different sequence every week, there will be 4 stops imported for the customer, 1 only, 2 only, 3 only, and 4 only; each with a different sequence.

16990217:
Field reference for the InvoiceOrders EDBL import routine in Encompass, used to create or update non-verified invoices and lines from a file. Advanced use, outside standard support. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

Required:

  • Date: Enter the date in MM/dd/yyyy format for the intended Invoice Date
    ​
    ​

  • InvoiceNum: InvoiceNum
    ​
    ​

  • ProductID or ProductID_Translation: Product to be on invoice
    ​
    ​

  • CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation: Customer of the invoice
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID or LocationID_Translation: Location of the invoice
    ​
    ​

  • NumUnits: NumUnits for this transaction line

Steps

EDBL Routines Disclaimer: This EDBL routine represents advanced functionality primarily intended for use by Encompass technical staff. While technically proficient customers may utilize these routines, please be aware that they fall outside the scope of standard support. Assistance with EDBL routines is not covered under standard support agreements and may require billable services from our Professional Services team. Please ensure you thoroughly understand this routine before implementation in your production environment

Overview

The InvoiceOrders EDBL routine allows you to import non-verified invoice data into the system. This routine can create new invoices or update existing ones along with their related transaction line items. Each row in your imported file will represent a single line item to be added to an invoice.

Key Behaviors

  • Creates or updates invoices and their transaction line items

  • Groups rows with the same customer, date, route, PO number, and invoice number into a single invoice

  • Matches to existing invoices using various identifiers (InvoiceID, InvoiceNum, TranslationInvoiceNum, PONum)

  • Can set load sheet status during import

  • Supports multiple currency handling with exchange rate conversion

  • Can create payments on invoices when receipt amounts are included

Field Considerations

Required Fields

  • CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation: The customer for the invoice

  • ProductID or ProductID_Translation: The product for each invoice transaction

  • Date: The date for the invoice/load sheet

Key Matching Fields

  • InvoiceID: Direct match to an existing invoice ID

  • InvoiceNum: Match by invoice number

  • TranslationInvoiceNum: Match by external system invoice number

  • PONum: Match by purchase order number

  • LoadSheetID: Used for matching and grouping

Currency and Pricing Fields

  • FullPrice, UnitPrice, Discount, Discount2: Price components

  • CurrencyID or CurrencyID_Translation: Currency identifier

  • ExchangeRate: Exchange rate for currency conversion

  • NumUnits: Quantity of the product

  • NumUnitsCases: Alternative quantity as cases (will be converted to units)

Payment Fields

  • Receipt: Payment amount

  • PaymentTypeID or PaymentTypeID_Translation: Payment type

  • Paid: Mark invoice as paid (1) or unpaid (0)

Routing Fields

  • RouteID: Direct route assignment

  • RouteNum: Route number for matching to a route

  • RoutingMethod: Controls how invoices are routed

  • LoadSheetStatus: Controls status of the load sheet

Static Fields

  • Location: Numeric LocationID

  • PromoOverridden = 1 (required for Invoice; used for InvoiceOrders if current pricing structure cannot be used, Overrides Promotions if necessary)

  • LockPrices = 1 (to ensure Imported Prices are Locked and will not be recalculated)

Special Features

Date Formatting Options: Import accepts multiple date formats:

  • Standard date format in Date field

  • DateYYYYMMDD (8-digit format: YYYYMMDD)

  • DateMMDDYY (6-digit format: MMDDYY)

  • DateYYMMDD (6-digit format: YYMMDD)

Price Calculations: System will calculate missing price components:

  • If ExtPrice is provided but UnitPrice is missing, UnitPrice will be calculated

  • If FullPrice/UnitPrice and Discount are provided, missing components will be calculated

  • Currency conversion will be applied if CurrencyID/ExchangeRate are provided

Case/Unit Conversion: If NumUnitsCases is provided, it will be converted to NumUnits using the product's WholesaleUnitsPerCase value

Automatic Receipt Processing: If Paid=1 or Receipt value is provided, system will create payment records

ClearAllTrans Option: When set to 1, this will clear all existing transactions on an invoice that aren't in the imported data

Multiple Charge Types: Supports up to 5 different charge types per transaction (InvoiceChargeType1-5)

Import Actions

  • Add Only: Creates new invoices only, skips records that match existing invoices

  • Update or Add: Creates new invoices or updates existing ones based on matching fields

  • Update Only: Updates only existing invoices, will not create new ones

Notes and Limitations

  • If both InvoiceID and InvoiceNum are provided, InvoiceID takes precedence

  • When updating existing invoices, the system may create a new invoice audit record

  • Balanced or verified load sheets cannot be modified through this import

  • For secure payments, ensure PaymentTypeID is properly mapped

  • The ImportGroupID field helps segregate import data from different sources

  • EntrySource field allows tracking where invoices originated

Error Handling

If validation errors occur, they will appear in the import report warnings section. Common errors include:

  • Missing required fields (CustomerID, ProductID)

  • Non-existent references (products or customers that don't exist)

  • Permissions issues for locked invoices

  • Invalid LoadSheetStatus transitions

16990222:
Field reference for the Customers EDBL import in Encompass: creating or updating customers, chains, AR accounts and contacts from a file, with matching and default rules. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

Overview

The Customers EDBL routine imports customer data into your Encompass system. It can create new customer records, update existing ones, and establish relationships with many supporting tables like Chains, AR Accounts, and Customer Types.

Import Actions

  • Add Only: Creates new customer records based on imported data

  • Update Only: Updates existing customer records without creating new ones

  • Update or Add: Updates existing customers when found or creates new ones when not found

Matching Logic

The system attempts to match existing customers using:

  • CustomerID (direct match to internal ID)

  • CustomerID_Translation (external identifier that maps to an internal ID)

  • Google Place ID (when MatchOnGooglePlaceID is enabled)

Key Fields

Required Fields

  • CustomerID OR CustomerID_Translation: At least one identifier is required

Important Fields

  • CustomerName: The customer's name (labeled as "Company" in some views)

  • LocationID: Defaults to your user's location if not provided

  • CustomerTypeID/CustomerTypeID_Translation: Defaults to "*" if not provided

Main Features

Customer Records

  • Creates or updates core customer data (name, address, contact info)

  • Sets default values for missing fields (Address="Not Available", City="Not Available", etc.)

  • Handles address information, contact details, and account status

Chain Integration

  • Links customers to chains via ChainID or ChainID_Translation

  • Can create new chain records if they don't exist

  • Manages chain AR account relationships

AR Accounts

  • Creates or updates AR accounts linked to customers

  • Handles billing address information

  • Maps AR account relationships to customers and chains

Customer Contacts

  • Creates user records for customer contacts when contact info is provided

  • Sets up primary contacts for customers using contact information

  • Associates email, phone, and contact name with customer records

Location/Territory Integration

  • Associates customers with locations, territories, areas, and jurisdictions

  • Manages income areas, charge areas, deposit areas, and counties

  • Supports geographic hierarchy relationships

Special Processing

Google Place ID Matching - When MatchOnGooglePlaceID is enabled, the system can:

  • Find existing customers using Google Place IDs

  • Create global customer records that map to distributor customers

  • Update geolocation data like longitude, latitude, and GPS accuracy

Bud Distributor Support - Special fields and processing for Bud distributors:

  • BudNet_BudRPF18_CustomerTypes mapping

  • Trade channel integration

  • Special customer type mapping

Common Use Cases

  • Customer Master Data Import: Bringing in your core customer list with basic information

  • AR System Integration: Importing customer data with AR information from financial systems

  • Chain/Corporate Customer Import: Creating chain relationships and hierarchies

  • Google Place Integration: Matching customers to Google Places for geolocation

Technical Notes

  • The routine creates TableTranslations entries to maintain mappings between external and internal IDs

  • Zero-padding correction is automatically applied to numeric identifiers to handle format variations

  • Default values are used extensively to ensure complete customer records even with partial data

  • Customer status can be set with values like "Active", "Inactive", or "OutOfBus"

Fields And Definitions

Required:

  • CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation: CustomerID_Translation will create customers, and their Table Translations, if they are not yet translated. CustomerID will not work if it doesn't exist.
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID or LocationID_Translation: LocationID_Translation will not create a Location, as other ID_Translations do.

Recommended:

  • Company: Customer Name. If not mapped, will use CustomerID_Translation.
    ​
    ​

  • AccountStatus: Will default to Active, if not mapped. 'Active', 'Inactive', 'OutofBus'
    ​
    ​

  • Address: Customer Shipping Address
    ​
    ​

  • Address2: Customer Shipping Address 2. Recommended, if exists.
    ​
    ​

  • City: Customer City
    ​
    ​

  • State: Customer State Abbreviation. 3 characters max
    ​
    ​

  • ARAccountID or ARAccountID_Translation: Map same as CustomerID_Translation or Company. If you don't map, then it will choose Company name but with an _2.
    ​
    ​

  • PostalCode: Customer Postal Code.
    ​
    ​

  • ChainID or ChainID_Translation: If not mapped, will create Chain of 'Default' and assign to it.
    ​
    ​

  • CustomerTypeID or CustomerTypeID_Translation: Creates Customer Types. It will fill in with a default if not provided.
    ​
    ​

  • AreaID or AreaID_Translation: Distribution area to which to assign the Customer. Map this when there are multiple locations or the location mapped could be overridden.
    ​
    ​

  • TerritoryID or TerritoryID_Translation: Territory to which to assign the Customer


Optional:

  • BillAddress: AR Account Address. Will assume Customer.Address if not mapped.
    ​
    ​

  • BillAddress2: AR Account Address2. Will assume Customer.Address2 if not mapped.
    ​
    ​

  • BillCity: AR Account City. Will assume Customer.City if not mapped.
    ​
    ​

  • BillState: AR Account State. Will assume Customer.State if not mapped.
    ​
    ​

  • BillPostalCode: AR Account Postal Code. Will assume Customer.PostalCode if not mapped.
    ​
    ​

  • TermsID or TermsID_Translation: Will not create terms; set to existing term in system
    ​
    ​

  • Contact: Name of user for contact information. This must be mapped for email or phone mapping to work; however if the value is null the name gets set to email or phone.
    ​
    ​

  • SalesUserID_Translation/ID: ID or Translation of the SalesRep desired. This must exist before import. Use Users EDBL to import first.

16990225:
Field reference for the AccountsRec EDBL import in Encompass to load open AR invoice balances, with option to zero out prior imported AR. Needs AccountsRecApply permission; v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

Overview

The AccountsRec EDBL routine allows you to import accounts receivable data into the system. This includes invoice balances, payments, and customer AR information. This routine creates or updates invoice records and their corresponding open balances in the system.

Primary Purpose

  • Import historical or current accounts receivable data

  • Set open balances for invoices

  • Create missing load sheets and invoices if required

  • Optionally zero out existing imported accounts receivable balances

Key Fields

Required Fields

  • CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation: Customer identifier (either internal ID or external reference)

  • InvoiceNum: Identifier for the invoice

  • Date: Transaction date

  • OpenBalance: The amount owed on the invoice

Important Optional Fields

  • ZeroImportedAccountsRec: When set to True (1), zeroes out existing imported AR balances before importing new ones

  • LSTypeID: Determines whether records are imported as "Imported" or "Sales History" type (defaults to "Imported" for regular users)

  • ImportGroupID: Groups records for tracking purposes (defaults to "1")

  • ARAccountID: AR Account identifier (if not provided, will use the Customer's default AR Account)

  • DateYYYYMMDD or DateMMDDYY: Alternative date formats if Date is not provided

  • LocationID_Translation or LocationID: Business location identifier

  • CheckNum: Check number for payments

  • PONum: Purchase order number

  • ARNote: Notes for the AR transaction

  • DueDate: When payment is due (defaults to transaction date if not provided)

Behavior

Data Flow

  1. Validates imported data

  2. Optionally zeros out existing imported AR if ZeroImportedAccountsRec=True

  3. Translates customer IDs and creates missing customers if needed

  4. Determines location information

  5. Sets default values for missing data (AR Account, Term, Date, Due Date)

  6. Creates missing load sheets and invoices as needed

  7. Updates invoice balances based on imported OpenBalance

  8. Creates necessary payment history records

Load Sheet Type Control

If the user has SalesHistoryImport permission, the system will:

  • Default to LSType = "Sales History"

  • Allow mapping to LSType = "Imported" if needed

If the user does NOT have this permission:

  • Always use LSType = "Imported"

  • Override any attempt to use "Sales History"

Open Balance Handling

  • Sets Invoice.OpenDebit if OpenBalance is positive

  • Sets Invoice.OpenCredit if OpenBalance is negative

  • Updates Invoice.Receipt accordingly

Default Value Assignment

  • Fills in ARAccountID from Customer if not provided

  • Fills in TermID from ARAccount if not provided

  • Converts DateYYYYMMDD or DateMMDDYY to standard date format if Date not provided

  • Uses transaction date as DueDate if not specified

  • Defaults InvoiceNum to '000000' if not provided

Use Cases

  • Historical AR Import: Import historical AR data from another system

  • AR Balances Reset: Zero out AR balances and reimport corrected values

  • AR to Sales History: Import sales history from another system (requires appropriate permissions)

  • Customer Invoice Recreation: Create invoices that may be missing in the system

Best Practices

  • Provide CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation: Ensures correct customer assignment

  • Include Accurate OpenBalance: This determines the AR amounts in the system

  • Set Proper Date Values: Determines accounting periods and aging

  • Consider ImportGroupID: Useful for tracking and potentially reversing imported batches

  • Include InvoiceNum: Helps with matching existing invoices in the system

  • Verify LocationID: Important for multi-location businesses

Warnings and Considerations

  • Importing with ZeroImportedAccountsRec=True will reset existing imported AR balances to zero

  • Dates more than one month in the future will be rejected

  • Both InvoiceNum and CustomerID are used to match existing invoices

  • The routine will report any invoices it couldn't find or create

Permission Requirements

  • Users need the AccountsRecApply permission to use this EDBL routine.

Related EDBL Routines

  • AccountsRecPaymentApplication: For applying payments to imported AR

  • Remittance: For importing payment receipts

  • InvoicesAndPayments: For importing both invoices and payment data

Fields And Definitions

Required:

  • InvoiceNum: The number for the Invoice. Needs to be only one line per invoice and date

Recommended:

  • CustomerID or CustomerID_Translation: CustomerID is preferred. Join Table Translations to Customers table. (Required if OpenBalance is provided)
    ​
    ​

  • OpenBalance: The balance remaining on the invoice. Will only open imported invoices.
    ​
    ​

  • LocationID or LocationID_Translation: Technically you can run with just InvoiceNum and LocationID. Though, it will do nothing.
    ​
    ​

  • Date: Works without Date, though Date is highly recommended. Without Date, invoice is likely to be made on 1/1/2000.

Optional:

  • ZeroImportedAccountsRec: Default value is 0. When mapped to 1, it zeroes all previously imported AR before importing new AR.

Cross Company Payment Account Maps help define the general ledger accounts that will be used when customer payments are received by one company; but applied to open invoices owned by a different company.

16990239:
Field definitions for the Encompass Routes Metrics table: how distributor route distance, travel and service time, cost, cases and sales volume are calculated daily. Needs Route View permission; v24.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.06

Steps

  • Data in the Routes Metrics table is calculated by the system automatically on a daily basis. Data is calculated for active route versions and "future" inactive route versions.
    ​
    ​

  • Search for the "Routes Metrics" table in the "Search for anything.." field. Users or roles must have Route View permissions to view the route metrics table.

Fields And Definitions

  • Route - Route name.
    ​
    ​

  • Active - This is a virtual field from the Route Versions table indicating if the route is active or not.
    ​
    ​

  • Phase - There will be a Routes Metrics record for each possible phase option. See the phase column on the Stops table. So even if all stops on a route are phase All, there will be a Routes Metrics record for each phase. This will allow the system to recalculate if there are mixed phases on a route, similar to selecting the phase options in Mapped Routing.
    ​
    ​

  • Distance - This is the overall distance for the route. This is calculated from Google Maps and is sorted on 1) Stops Sequence and 2) Customer ID. It is recommended to NOT have stops on a route with the same sequence.
    ​
    ​

  • Travel Time - This is the total drive time. This is calculated from Google Maps and is sorted on 1) Stops Sequence and 2) Customer ID. It is recommended to NOT have stops on a route with the same sequence. Travel Time does NOT consider traffic.
    ​
    ​

  • Service Time - This is the calculated service time that it will take to service the customers on the route. Service Time is calculated from average times from data where GPS Devices are installed in vehicles, which requires Fleet Tracker integration with Geotab or Samsara. If turned on with Fleet Tracker, the average service times are stored on the Delivery/Sales/Merchandiser Average Service Times on the Customer table. If Fleet Tracker is not integrated, or if average service times are not calculated from GPS data, the service time is calculated from Fixed Service Minutes or Presell Service Minutes, and Seconds per Case on the Customer or Customer Types tables.
    ​
    ​

  • Average Service Time - Service Time / Number of Stops
    ​
    ​

  • Total Time - This is the sum of the Travel Time and Service Time.
    ​
    ​

  • Route Cost - This is calculated from the Cost Per Mile for the vehicle on the route * the Route Distance. Cost Per Mile can be set on the Vehicles table.
    ​
    ​

  • Cases - Number of cases sold on the route based on the Route Metrics Duration, which is a default of 60 days. Routes Metric Duration can be changed on the Routes table to options including 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, and 120 days.
    ​
    ​

  • Kegs - Number of Kegs sold on the route based on the Route Metrics Duration.
    ​
    ​

  • $Vol Cases - Sales Volume for cases sold on the route based on the Route Metrics Duration.
    ​
    ​

  • $Vol Kegs - Sales Volume for cases sold on the route based on the Route Metrics Duration.
