Distributor steps for setting up AR Accounts (bill-to) in Encompass: terms, statement groups, payment customer, EDI/ACH details and related subtables. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Configure AR Accounts
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the AR Accounts table.
​
​

2. To create a new AR Account, click the Add AR Account button.
​
​

3. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields and click the ‘Add Record’ button when complete.
​
​

  • Address section - Sets the billing address for the AR Account.
    ​
    ​

  • EDI/ACH section - Set the values needed for different types of online payments to be requested or received.
    ​
    ​

4. Sub tables show the key relationships between AR Accounts and other tables, click the Sub Tables button to see those relationships and related records.
​
​

  • Accounts Receivable - The table that stores any outstanding balance for this AR Account.
    ​
    ​

  • AR Accounts Users - The Users tied to AR Accounts, they receive any statements that are sent from Encompass.
    ​
    ​

  • Chains, Customers, and Split Invoices - Sub tables that an AR Account is responsible for.
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Payments, Invoice Payments Hist - The table that stores all payments received from the AR Account, both current and historical.
    ​
    ​

  • Invoices - The actual invoices for the entities of this AR Account.
    ​
    ​

Fields And Definitions

* = required field
​
​

  • *AR Account - the name of the AR Account
    ​
    ​

  • *Term - The Credit Term set on the AR Account. This is the key determiner of how AR behaves and is collected
    ​
    ​

  • Payment Customer - Used to aggregate payments under a single customer when the same AR Account is used for multiple Customers or on a Chain
    ​
    ​

  • Collection Agent - The User assigned to collect payments
    ​
    ​

  • *Statement Group - a grouping of AR Accounts that receive the same delivery method and frequency of statement
    ​
    ​

  • Company - Distributor's company associated with this AR Account
    ​
    ​

  • Mapped Location - If the payor's invoices are for a different invoicing 'location'
    ​
    ​

  • Statement Print Group By - What order invoices/customers appear on the statement
    ​
    ​

  • AR Sort Order - Order open invoices/credits will appear when applying payments
    ​
    ​

  • Print Statement - Link to print a statement
    ​
    ​

  • Apply Payments - Redirects to the Load Sheet Receipts dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  • Vendor Num - For chain accounts (distributor's vendor number for the retailer)
    ​
    ​

  • DUNS - Payors DUNS number
    ​
    ​

Best Practices

  • A Payment Customer is sometimes used if there are multiple customers that are all owned by the same entity. Payments for their invoices can be grouped together for reporting purposes.
    ​
    ​

  • Create different statement groups to manage the how and when a Statement is generated. Examples include monthly automated statements that are sent to a specified list of AR Accounts Users via email or bi-weekly paper statements that are manually printed and mailed out
    ​
    ​

  • AR Accounts can best be described as the billing entity for a Customer. The location to which products are delivered is not always the same entity that pays for those products, and in those cases, an AR Account may not be the same as a Customer. In other words, the Customer is the "Ship To" while the AR Account is the "Bill To".
    ​
    ​

  • AR Accounts can be set on the Customer, Chain, or Split Invoice

4. Tap "Add To Invoice". An Invoice transaction will be added and the product will be removed from the Shopping Cart.
​
5. If the Product will not be placed at the customer, it can be removed from the shopping cart. Tap the edit icon at the top of the Shopping Cart.
​
6. Use the checkboxes to select the Products to remove.
​
7. Tap "Remove From Shopping Cart"
​
8. The Shopping Cart New Placement Survey is then displayed. Fill in the survey questions then tap "Continue".

Best Practices

  • Shopping Cart tasks that will not be placed at the Customer should be removed using the steps in this resource. This ensures that the Shopping Cart is not cluttered with old records, especially if there is no deadline set on the task.

    ​

  • Check the Shopping Cart frequently. An orange badge displays on the Shopping Cart when the user has not yet viewed a new Shopping Cart record.

    ​

  • The survey triggered when removing a product from the Shopping cart is triggered by the Objective field on the Shopping Carts table. It is recommended to select the Shopping Cart: New Placement objecitvein the Objective field when adding Shopping Cart record to trigger the survey when removing products from the shopping cart or any objective with the "Shopping Cart" Mobile Item.

16990246:
Distributor steps for building a custom Encompass Mobile app: copy a Mobile Application, edit Mobile Links, test it on the device and assign it to a Role. Needs ClientEdit and GlobalSettingEdit; v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Required permission:
​
​

  • ClientEdit
    ​
    ​

  • GlobalSettingEdit

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Mobile Applications represent the interface a user sees when viewing Encompass Mobile. Mobile Applications can be customized to add, remove, and modify Mobile Items (the individual pages in Encompass Mobile). Each Role can be assigned a different Mobile Application to give a customized view for each Role.

Create A New Mobile Application
​
It is recommended to copy an existing Mobile Application to get started. Copying an existing Mobile Application will also copy all of the Mobile Links.
​
1. Navigate to the Mobile Applications table using the Universal Search bar.
​
2. Arrow into the Mobile Application you want to copy.
​
3. Click "Sub Tables"
​
4. Click "Copy Mobile Applications"
​
5. Rename the Mobile Application
​
6. Click "Copy Record"
​
7. Click "View New Records"
​
​
​
​Modify Mobile Links
​
​The existing Mobile Link (buttons) can be modified from the Mobile Application record. The Mobile Items must already exist before creating Mobile Links.
​
1. Click Sub Tables -> Mobile Links.
​
2. To delete a Mobile Link, click the hamburger menu on the record and click "Delete".
​
3. To add a new Mobile Link, click "Add Mobile Links".
​
4. Name the Mobile Link. The Name will be displayed as the title of the button in Encompass Mobile.
​
5. Set the From and ToMobile Items.
​
6. Click "Add Record"
​
​
​
​Test the Mobile Application
​
​Once the Mobile Application is complete, allow at least 30 minutes for it to be available on Encompass Mobile.
​
1. On Encompass Mobile, manually sync then tap "Control Panel" on the home screen.
​
2. Tap "Complete Settings"
​
3. Expand the "Mobile Applications" drop-down menu.
​
4. Select the new Mobile Application.
​
5. Tap the back arrow to return to the home screen.
​
​
​
​Assign A Mobile Application To A Role
​
Once you have tested the Mobile Application, assign it to a Role. If the Mobile Application is not assigned to a role, the only way to access it is through Complete Settings.
​
1. Navigate to the Roles table.
​
2. Select the Role and click "Edit".
​
3. Set the "EM Mobile Application" field to the new Mobile Application.
​
4. Save Changes
​
5. The next time users with the Role sync, they will see the new Mobile Application.

Fields And Definitions

*=Required field
​
*Mobile Application - The record that holds the Mobile Links and Mobile Items.
​
​*Mobile Items - Individual destinations in Encompass Mobile. Each page that you visit is a Mobile Item.
​
​*Mobile Links - The record that defines where buttons are displayed and where the button redirects the user.
​
​*From Mobile Item - Where a button in Encompass Mobile is displayed. Ex. Home - Encompass Mobile to display the link on the Home screen.
​
​*To Mobile Item - Where the user is redirected when clicking on the Mobile Link (button).
​
​Category - When Mobile Links have a value in the "Category" field, they will display in a folder named as the Category. Multiple Mobile Links can be set to the same Category to be in the same folder.
​
​Sequence - Numerical value to set where a Mobile Link will display in relation to the other Mobile Links on the same screen.
​
​*Grid Layout - Defaults to "Main" which is the main view of the each page in Encompass Mobile. Navigation Tools and Navigation Menu allow you to add Mobile Links to the "hamburger menus" throughout the application.
​

Best Practices

  • The Default Mobile Application cannot be edited.
    ​
    ​

  • It is recommended to copy an existing Mobile Application when creating a new one. If you do not copy and existing Mobile Application, you will need to manually add each Mobile Link (button).
    ​
    ​

  • Utilizing custom Mobile Applications is great for minimizing buttons available on Encompass Mobile that certain Roles won't need to utilize. For example, removing the Warehouse Mobile Link from a Sales Rep's view.
    ​
    ​

  • Frequently used reports, dashboards or any other pages on the server of Encompass can be linked as a new button in a Custom Mobile Application by creating a new Mobile Item.
    ​
    ​

  • The Mobile Item records must exist before adding a Mobile Link.
    ​
    ​

  • Test new Mobile Applications before assigning them to a Role to ensure they are working as expected.

Steps

How to Use the Updated Fusion Report View

This Improved Report View interface allows end users to manipulate pre-built reports. Easily filter and group data, add and remove predefined columns, adjust graph views, drill down, and more without needing FusionEdit permissions.
​
​
​

1. The new Report View beta is now available in versions 23.12 and above. To turn on Beta, click the "Enable Beta" option in the top right header next to the universal search bar.
​
2. The name of the report is displayed in the page header. Click "Save" to save any changes to an existing report if you are already the owner. “Save as new report” will save a new copy of the report.
​
3. If there is a cache on the report, refresh the data by clicking the “Refresh” link.
​
4. Quick Edit tabs are displayed to the left of the report. Click on these tabs to open the Quick Edit panel.
​
5. The data and organization of the report can be managed in the Layout tab. Organize how the report data is grouped under Groupings, select which values to calculate on the report under Metrics, and select a Comparison to compare metrics across multiple columns.
​
6. Click the “Add” section to add a new grouping or metric. Drag groupings down to create Subgroups on the report.
​
7. On the Filters tab, add or adjust filters and time periods that are applied to the report. Click “Add another time period” or “Add more filters” to add additional filters from the available list.
​
8. A graph can be added to the top of the report from the “Graph” tab to visualize the data. Select a graph type, manage graph settings, and set the color theme from this tab.
​
9. Adjust any display settings for the full report from the Settings tab. This can include adding column totals to your report such as Unit Difference or Percentage Difference, displaying a total row, changing the format, or setting a color theme.
​
10. The “Details” tab displays important information about the report including the owner, cache times, all applied filters on the report data, and table sync information.
​
11. Users with FusionEdit permission will also see the Fusion Edit button at the bottom of the panel. Clicking this will take you to the Fusion Edit screen to edit the data source behind this report.
​
12. Click the “Manage beta” option in the header at any time to submit your feedback on the new design or revert back to the original Fusion View display.

16990257:
Distributor troubleshooting for M360 Azure B2C login to Encompass: wrong site after login, missing Azure login icon, and pre-fetch or authentication errors fixed by reconnecting on the Profile page. v22.02+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.02

Steps

Scenario: Azure Login takes the user to a different Encompass Site

  • This occurs when the wholesaler's Redirect URI has not been added to the OAuth configuration in Azure.

  • M360 Support will need to add the Redirect URI, it is not something encompass has access to.

Scenario: Azure login icon is not available on the Encompass Login Page

  • This is more common for new wholesalers

  • Ensure that the URI has been added in M360

  • The settings for Oauth B2C can be set on the Oauth Settings table in Encompass

  • Once this is set, users should be able to log into via AzureB2C and connect their authentication from the Profile page in ECP

Troubleshooting for Pre-Fetch Errors / Authentication Errors:

  1. Have the user logout and log back in to m360 using AzureB2C, if this does not work proceed to step 2

  2. Have the user confirm that their email address on the Encompass user table is identical to the email address setup in Azure

  3. Have the user check the Oauth Authentications table to ensure that there is an authentication available for Azure B2C connected to their authentication. Their authentication ID can be found on the Users table.

  4. If the authentication does not exist, or the token is expired:

  1. Have the user log into ECP

  2. Navigate to their Profile page (this is accessed by clicking on their username@encompassID in the lower right-hand corner of the screen and selecting profile)

  3. There will be an AzureB2C logo to the left of the screen, disconnect this authentication and then reconnect it by clicking the disconnect button and then the connect button.

Distributor walkthrough of Strategic Route Planning with Wise Systems in Encompass: send fleet and customer data, optimize territories and service patterns, and import the plan back. Needs Strategic Routing App, v24.05+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.05

Pre-Conditions

The Strategic Routing App must be installed from the App Library.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Empower your employees to use the Strategic Planner tool with Encompass and Wise Systems to build efficient routes, lower costs, improve resource utilization, customer satisfaction, and increase driver retention and job satisfaction.
​
As the beverage industry becomes increasingly complex with more products, more suppliers, rising costs, increased driver turnover, and higher retail demand, the need for fast and efficient strategic routing tools has never been more essential.

Use cases

The Encompass Strategic Planner integration, powered by Wise Systems, covers a wide range of scenarios seen here:
​
​

Screenshot

Steps
​
​

Before creating a routing plan or session, it is recommended to make a copy of the active Route Version. You will need to leave the new Route Version inactive and set the Start Date to some time well in the future.

1. To start the Strategic Routing process, click on the 3 dots next to an inactive Route Version and click Strategic Planner.
​
2. If this is the first time using Strategic Planner, you will need to add a new Planning Session. Name the Planning Session something that makes sense to you. Then, select the Planning Session and click the Next: Fleet button.
​
3. To begin selecting the Fleet data, first choose the Activity type: Delivery, Presell, or Merchandising. Then, click the Search button to retrieve the Vehicle and Route data for the selected Activity.
​
​

  • If there are any Routes you wish to exclude from the Route Plan or Session, check the "Exclude" checkbox for those Routes.

4. To begin setting up the Customer data, click the Next: Customers button.
​
5. Load Customers by selecting a Sales History date range and applying any other desired filters. Then, click the Search button to load the matching Customers.
​
6. The Customer data will include Sales Cycle Averages, which are calculated using the average weekly sales for the date range selected. The average is then multiplied by the frequency of the customer's visits in a 4-week cycle.
​
- For example, if a weekly visited Customer had an average sales of 100 cases per week, the Sales Cycle Average would be 400 cases.
​
7. To unassign a Customer from a Route, click Unassign Route. This will tell the Strategic Planner that this Customer can be assigned to any route. Also, a customer can be unassigned from a specific day of the week or phased week by checking Unassign Service Pattern.

  • Customers can be unassigned once the data is in Strategic Planner as well.

8. To send your Fleet and Customer data, click Send to Strategic Planner.
​
9. Click Login to Strategic Planner. This will open the Wise Systems Strategic Planning tool in a new tab in your browser.
​
10. The Fleet and Customer data will be automatically uploaded into Wise Systems Strategic Planner. Successful uploads of both Fleet and Customer data will be indicated by the green upload indicator.
​
11. You will notice the Session or Plan names that were created in Encompass will also be available in Strategic Planner. Click the Plan dropdown to open and view, or copy Planning Sessions.
​
12. Click Run Strategic Planner to start optimizing your Routes.
​
13. Select any Constraints, Capacity and Time Window options, and Balancing options then click Run Strategic Planner.
​
14. Once the Strategic Planner has run, you can view your Territories and their metrics. Each polygon on the map represents a single Territory over a cycle. Use the map to see where Territories are overlapping.
​
15. Hover over a Customer’s map marker to view key information and service pattern details.
​
16. Click on an individual Territory to zoom in on all of the Customers assigned to that Territory.
​
17. Search for a Customer by entering the Customer Number or Name in the search box in the top-right.
​
18. To view Routes for a specified period, select individual weeks and days of the cycle. When an individual day is selected, the Route's Stops will display on the right side of the screen in sequence order.
​
19. To reassign Stops between Territories, select the Customer you would like to reassign by clicking on the Customer’s map marker. From the dropdown, select the Territory you would like to reassign the Customer to. You can also select the Remove From Territory option to unassign a Stop from a Territory.
​
20. Click on the pencil icon beside the Service Pattern displayed within a customer card to edit Service Patterns from either map view or metrics view.
​
21. When the edit pencil is selected, the editing modal will open where you can update the days or weeks for which the Customer should be serviced. Click Update to save the changes to the Service Pattern.
​
22. Strategic Planner lets you view metrics for your routes in a separate table view page by clicking the table icon in the bottom left.
​
​

  • In this view, you can examine metrics at the Territory level, across weeks within the cycle, and on individual weekdays. This view is useful for identifying problem areas and ensuring Routes remain balanced as edits and modifications are made. The Group By toggle at the top of the page allows you to group the data by weekday or by week.

23. Select all Customers on a Route by clicking the select "All Customers icon" next to the Route Name. Selected Customers will appear on the right of the screen.
​
24. Remove Customers from the current Territory by clicking the Territory dropdown and selecting Remove From Territory.
​
25. Unassigned Customers will show in the Unserviced Customers section located at the top-left of the page and can be shown on the map.
​
​

  • Run Strategic Planner to assign Unserviced Customers. Customers will be assigned to the selected routes, or if no routes are selected, they will be assigned based on the selected configurations.
    ​
    ​

  • Check the configurations in the Configurations tab and initiate the Strategic Planner tool by clicking Run Strategic Planner.
    ​
    ​

26. Once you have completed your Routing Plan in Wise Systems and are ready to import Routes back into Encompass, go to the Route Versions table and click Import Strategic Plan.
​
27. Select the appropriate Plan and click Import Data.
​
28. To confirm the Routes imported as expected, run the Routing Report in Encompass.
16990263:
Distributor glossary of Encompass reporting terms: distribution and base periods, buyers, non-buyers, re-buys, new and lost placements, potential placements and product count. v24.03+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.03

Fields And Definitions

Definitions
​
​

  • Distribution Period: The period against which you are checking for placements.
    ​
    ​

  • Base Period: The period that the distribution period is compared against to see if a placement is new or lost.
    ​
    ​

  • Buyer: A customer that has bought the product during the distribution period.
    ​
    ​

  • Non-Buyer: A customer that has not bought the product during the distribution period.
    ​
    ​

  • Buyer %: The percentage of eligible customers that have bought the product.
    ​
    ​

  • Re-Buy: A product bought by a customer during the base period that was bought again during the distribution period.
    ​
    ​

  • Placement: A product bought at a customer during the distribution period. Each unique Product x Customer combination is one placement.
    ​
    ​

  • Non-Placement: A placement that the customer is eligible to buy but has not bought during the distribution period.
    ​
    ​

  • New Placement: A product bought by a customer during the distribution period that had not been bought during the base period.
    ​
    ​

  • Lost Placement: A product bought by a customer during the base period that was not bought during the distribution period.
    ​
    ​

  • Potential Buyers: Customers that are eligible to buy that product.
    ​
    ​

  • Potential Placements: The number of unique Product x Customer combinations that are possible.
    ​
    ​

  • Product Count: The number of products in that grouping. (Ex. Number of products in a Supplier)

16990276:
Encompass developer guide to writing Mocha/Chai test scripts for JavaScript Code Blocks on custom Dashboards; scripts need 80% statement coverage before release. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

Test Scripts are required to release any Dashboard with a Code Block that contains JavaScript.

Test Scripts must hit a minimum of 80% Statement coverage.

Steps

Test Scripts are required to release any Dashboard with a Code Block that contains JavaScript.
​
Test Scripts must hit a minimum of 80% Statement coverage.

Things to Know

  • Put the corresponding code in the correct code tab
    ​
    ​

    • i.e. Don't put JavaScript in a <script> tag in the HTML tab
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • The HTML tab contents do NOT have access to the JavaScript file directly
    ​
    ​

    • This means you cannot create <input> tags with built-in ECP-ECP-ECP-onclick/onchange/etc. events
      ​
      ​

    • To set event listeners use document.querySelector or document.getElementById to get the element then call element.addEventListener
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • The test scripts use the Chai Assert APIs and the Mocha testing framework
    ​
    ​

  • Tests run sequentially, in the order they are written
    ​
    ​

  • You cannot debug test scripts
    ​
    ​

    • If a test script is failing for an unknown reason try using console.log to see data during the test (make sure to remove once done)
      ​
      ​

    • console.log can only be used in the Test Script tab, it cannot be in the JavaScript tab otherwise the test won't run due to an error
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • Test scripts will fail if the page is unloaded for some reason (redirect on click for example)
    ​
    ​

    • Make sure the actual redirect is not run during the test
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • Use EC_Fmt.TriggerEvent to trigger specific events on elements during testing
    ​
    ​

    • Most commonly used for UI based tests
      ​
      ​
      ​

Best Practices

  • Write test cases for as much code as possible
    ​
    ​

    • 80% is the minimum allowed but should not be the goal
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • Don't write test scripts without at least 1 assert call
    ​
    ​

    • This may require some refactoring of JavaScript tab code to return data to check against
      ​
      ​

    • Check DOM changes when testing UI
      ​
      ​

    • Async tests with done are an exception
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • Avoid calling APIs, downloading files, prompting to print, etc. in test scripts
    ​
    ​

    • APIs take more time to run and typically the result is all that is needed
      ​
      ​

    • Create test results and put those in the test scripts to feed into tests
      ​
      ​

    • Use a "is testing" variable to know when tests are running; if running don't call the APIs (example below)
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • Keep test cases simple and focused
    ​
    ​

    • Don't test multiple things in a single test
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • If using manual delays in test scripts, modify the test's expected slow time to avoid timeouts and false flags of slowness
    ​
    ​

    • See Mocha's test duration info for more information
      ​
      ​

    • Example below
      ​
      ​

  • If testing UI changes (dialog opening, text changing, etc.) query the DOM for the effected elements and assert the changes you expect those elements to have
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

Definitions

  • describe - Function called to describe a set of test scripts
    ​
    ​

    • Could be a specific function or a workflow
      ​
      ​

    • Dictates how the final test results are grouped
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • it - Function called to perform a particular test
    ​
    ​

    • Typically nested inside describe calls but can be by themselves
      ​
      ​
      ​

  • assert - Used to confirm test script values are expected
    ​
    ​

    • Will fail a test script if the assert fails

Templates/Examples

Basic

const assert = chai.assert;describe("Some Function", () => { it("will do this", () => { const TestData = { Test: "abc" }; const result = SomeFunction(TestData); assert.equal(result, "cba", "result should be reversed"); });});;

Debug Variable

JavaScript tab

// At the toplet TestsAreRunning = false;function Enable_Testing() { TestsAreRunning = true;}[...]// inside a function that redirects or calls an APIconst myRequest = new EC_Request("SomeAPICommand")if (!TestsAreRunning) { myRequest.submit()}

Test Script tab

const assert = chai.assert;before(() => { Enable_Testing();});describe("Some Function", () => { it("will do this", () => { const TestData = { Test: "abc" }; const result = SomeFunction(TestData); assert.equal(result, "cba", "result should be reversed"); });});

Manual Delay

This is typically used when waiting for a UI action to occur and checking results of that action

const assert = chai.assert;describe("Some Function", () => { it("will open a dialog", async () => { // FAST = slow/2 // We are waiting 1 seconds always, default is 75ms this.slow(2075); const TestData = { Test: "abc" }; SomeFunction(TestData); // Wait 1 second to make sure dialog has time to popup await delay(1000); assert.isTrue(Dialog_IsShowing(), "dialog should be showing"); assert.equal(Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Title(), TestData.Test, "dialog title should match passed in data"); }); after(() => { // Cleanup any open dialogs after the test Click_CloseButton_On_ShowingDialogs(); })});

UI Test

const assert = chai.assert;describe("Clicking the open dialog button", () => { it("will open a dialog when valid data set", async () => { // FAST = slow/2 // We are waiting 1 seconds always, default is 75ms this.slow(2075); const ValidData = { Test: "abc" }; UpdateFormData(ValidData); EC_Fmt.TriggerEvent(document.getElementById("my-button"), "click", { bubbles: true }); // Wait 1 second to make sure dialog has time to popup await delay(1000); assert.isTrue(Dialog_IsShowing(), "dialog should be showing"); assert.equal(Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Title(), ValidData.Test, "dialog title should match passed in data"); }); it("will not open a dialog with inputs when valid data set", async () => { // FAST = slow/2 // We are waiting 1 seconds always, default is 75ms this.slow(2075); const InvalidData; UpdateFormData(InvalidData); EC_Fmt.TriggerEvent(document.getElementById("my-button"), "click", { bubbles: true }); // Wait 1 second to make sure dialog has time to popup await delay(1000); assert.isFalse(Dialog_IsShowing(), "dialog should not be showing"); assert.isTrue(document.querySelector("input[name=my-input]").hasAttribute("error"), "input should be in error"); }); after(() => { // Cleanup any open dialogs after the test Click_CloseButton_On_ShowingDialogs(); })});;

Asynchronous Tests

See Mocha's Asynchronous Code for more information about done

const assert = chai.assert;describe("Async Functions", () => { // passing in a callback // testing will wait until done() is called it("will work without failing", (done) => { SomeFunction((error) => { if (error) { done(error); } else { done(); } }); }); // Asserting with a returned Promise it("will return a promise with the correct results", (done) => { return SomeFunction().then((data) => { assert.equal(data.value, "1234", "function returns 1234"); }); }); // Awaiting a promise it("will return correct results", async (done) => { const Data = await SomeFunction(); assert.equal(Data.value, "1234", "function returns 1234"); });});

Helpful Functions

delay(milliseconds)

Halts execution for the specified milliseconds

  • milliseconds: number Number of milliseconds to wait for

function delay(milliseconds) { return new Promise(res => setTimeout(res, milliseconds));};

Example

// wait for 1 secondawait delay(1000);

Click_ConfirmButton_On_ShowingDialogs()

Click the confirm button on all showing dialogs

function Click_ConfirmButton_On_ShowingDialogs() { const dialogs = document.querySelectorAll(".ecp-dialog"); for (let i = 0; i < dialogs.length; ++i) { // Find dialogs that are still showing if (dialogs[i].style.display !== "none") { EC_Fmt.TriggerEvent(dialogs[i].querySelector(".ecp-dialog-confirm-button"), "click", { bubbles: true }); } }}

Example

SomeFunctionThatOpenDialog();// wait for the dialog to show upawait delay(1000);// Click confirm to test the confirm action on a dialogClick_ConfirmButton_On_ShowingDialogs();

Click_CloseButton_On_ShowingDialogs()

Click the close button (top-right X button) on all showing dialogs

function Click_CloseButton_On_ShowingDialogs() { const Dialogs = document.querySelectorAll(".ecp-dialog"); for (let i = 0; i < Dialogs.length; ++i) { // Find dialogs that are still showing if (Dialogs[i].style.display !== "none") { EC_Fmt.TriggerEvent(Dialogs[i].querySelector(".ecp-dialog-close"), "click", { bubbles: true }); } }}

Example

// close all opened dialogs after test cases run before the next setafter(() => { // Click confirm to test the confirm action on a dialog Click_CloseButton_On_ShowingDialogs();});

Dialog_IsShowing()

Determines if there is a dialog currently displayed during tests

  • Returns: booleantrue if a dialog is on screen, false if no dialog is showing

function Dialog_IsShowing() { const dialogs = document.querySelectorAll(".ecp-dialog"); for (let i = 0; i < dialogs.length; ++i) { // Find dialogs that are still showing if (dialogs[i].style.display !== "none") { return true; } } return false;}

Example

SomeFunctionThatOpenDialog();// wait for the dialog to show upawait delay(1000);assert.isTrue(Dialog_IsShowing(), "dialog should be showing");

Get_OnScreen_Dialog()

Gets the first showing dialog and returns the whole Element

  • Returns: Element The first showing dialog element, containing header, contents, and buttons; null otherwise

function Get_OnScreen_Dialog() { const dialogs = document.querySelectorAll(".ecp-dialog"); for (let i = 0; i < dialogs.length; ++i) { // Find dialogs that are still showing if (dialogs[i].style.display !== "none") { return dialogs[i]; } } return null;}

Example

SomeFunctionThatOpenDialog();// wait for the dialog to show upawait delay(1000);const OpenDialog = Get_OnScreen_Dialog();assert.exists(OpenDialog.querySelector("[name=SomeName]"), "dialog should be open");

Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Title()

Returns the title string of the first showing dialog

  • Returns: string The title of first found open dialog; "" (empty string) returned if no Dialog found

function Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Title() { const dialogs = document.querySelectorAll(".ecp-dialog"); for (let i = 0; i < dialogs.length; ++i) { // Find dialogs that are still showing if (dialogs[i].style.display !== "none") { return dialogs[i].querySelector(".ecp-dialog-title").innerText; } } return "";}

Example

SomeFunctionThatOpenDialog();// wait for the dialog to show upawait delay(1000);assert.equal(Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Title(), "My Dialog Title", "title should match");

Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Content()

Returns the innerHTML string of the content of the first open dialog
Used for simple dialog content checking

  • Returns: string The innerHTML of the found dialog

function Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Content() { const dialogs = document.querySelectorAll(".ecp-dialog"); for (let i = 0; i < dialogs.length; ++i) { // Find dialogs that are still showing if (dialogs[i].style.display !== "none") { return dialogs[i].querySelector(".ecp-dialog-content div").innerHTML; } } return "";}

Example

SomeFunctionThatOpenDialog();// wait for the dialog to show upawait delay(1000);assert.equal(Get_OnScreen_Dialog_Content(), "Are you sure you want to do this action?", "contents should match");

16990279:
Distributor explanation of Geo Counties, Counties and customer county assignment in Encompass, including why the system auto-changes a customer's county and how to stop it. Requires v24.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.06

Steps

Geo Counties -

The Geo Counties is a system table containing county data of the 50 US states and the District of Columbia.

Counties -

It is recommended that you geocode all counties that you have created, meaning that you should set the Geo County. The system will create county records and assign customers to that county if there are no geocoded counties found.

Customers -

Customers must be assigned to a county. If customer is assigned to a non-geocoded county, the system will automatically update the customer and set the county to a geocoded county based on the customers longitude and latitude.

There are 2 ways to prevent the system from updating the county a customer reccord:

  1. Set the GPS accuracy equal to Manually Set on the customer

  2. Set the Geo County on the county associated to the customer

In order to have accurate customer county data, the system will create county records and assign them to customers when there are customer that have a GPS accuracy equal to Not Set, this would noramally happen when new customers are created and again, if the county set on the customer is not geocoded.

  • Products/Items
    ​
    ​

  • Classifications (Locations, Departments, Classes, etc.)

Steps

The Bill.com Sync dashboard has 5 primary workflows:

1. Login: Connects ECP to Bill.com using the saved login credentials

2. Send Vendors: Sends AP Accounts with ListID IS NULL to Bill.com and matches on/creates Vendors in Bill.com (populates APAccounts.ListID with LIKE '009%’)

3. Pull Accounts: Pulls Accounts from Bill.com, finds an exact match in Encompass (Account to Accounts.Account) and links (populates Accounts.ListID with LIKE '0ca%’) and creates new ECP Accounts for any Bill.com Accounts that did not find a match

4. Purchases Sync: (Note: The Vendor on the Purchase must be synced first)
​
​

  • Send Purchases: Sends Purchases in >= Confirmed Status with TxnID IS NULL and Open Balance <> $0 from ECP to Bill.com and creates Bills in Bill.com
    ​
    ​

  • Pull Purchases: Pulls Bills from Bill.com and creates Purchases with TransType = Accounts in ECP

5. Payments Sync: Pulls Payments from Bill.com, creates Check Runs in ECP and applies payments to the Purchases.

To get started:
​
​

  1. Select the Company you want to connect to Bill.com and Click Login
    ​
    ​

  2. Click Send Vendors
    ​
    ​

  3. Click Pull Accounts
    ​
    ​

  4. Select the appropriate date range - this references Purchases.PostDate. Click Send Purchases
    ​
    ​

  5. Select the appropriate date range - this references Invoice Date in Bill.com. Click Pull Purchases
    ​
    ​

  6. Payments Sync: Select the appropriate date range - this references Process Date in Bill.com. Click Payments Sync

Distributor checklist in Encompass for why a product is or is not reporting to VIP SRS: IncludeInSalesReportByDefault, Supplier Report Code, and Suppliers Vendors data access and Distributor Number. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • The product must have IncludeInSalesReportByDefault=True.
    ​
    ​

  • Brand Family must be linked to the global product catalog.
    ​
    ​

  • SuppliersVendors record must exist for each location expected to report.

Steps

1. Use this Report - SRS Reporting by Product to help determine which products are reporting to VIP SRS.
​
​ Note: There are a couple of connections in dsdlink that need to be made to completely ensure a product is reporting. Encompass employees maintain these connections. The instructions below help ensure that everything is set up correctly on the distributor site only.

2. In an Encompass site, there are 3 fields to check to ensure that a specific product is reporting to SRS.
​
​

  1. The brand family that the product is under must have a "SupplierReportCode". If it does not, link a product underneath the brand family to the global database, using Product Manager. After linking a product, this link will cascade up through the hierarchy in your site, and your brand family will acquire the "SupplierReportCode" that is found on the global supplier record in dsdlink.
    ​
    ​

  2. The supplier that the product is under must have a "SuppliersVendors" record (one per location selling the product) attached to it with SupplierDataAccess=Allow. This tells the system that it is 'okay to share this data with the supplier through dsdlink'. This applies to both suppliers accessing their distributor data in dsdlink AND suppliers accessing their data in SRS. If this data does not wish to be shared with suppliers, set SupplierDataAccess=Block.
    ​
    ​

  3. The "SuppliersVendors" record also needs a "DistributorNumber". This value is provided by SRS in the initial setup, and it tells their system what Location the data belongs to.

Fields And Definitions

  • SuppliersVendors.DistributorNumber: This value is provided by SRS. It is how they determine which Location the data belongs to.
    ​
    ​

  • SuppliersVendors.SupplierDataAccess: This value tells the system whether or not to share the data with the supplier via dsdlink. This works for both sending data to SRS and for suppliers accessing their data in dsdlink.
    ​
    ​

  • BrandFamily.SupplierReportCode: This value is maintained in dsdlink by Encompass employees. It is how SRS knows what supplier to provide the data to on their end.

Best Practices

  • Link All Products - Product linking cascades up through the Brand, BrandFamily, and Supplier. Product linking helps ensure a correct "BrandFamily.SupplierReportCode".

16990288:
Distributor steps for creating a custom table in Encompass from Table Map or a Table Import spreadsheet, adding columns, and finding, editing or deleting it. Needs CustomTableEdit permission, v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

CustomTableEdit permission is required.

To create a custom table through the Table Import Wizard, a spreadsheet must already be created. Structure the spreadsheet to match the schema for your new table. The number of columns and their headers in the spreadsheet should match the number of table fields and their names, respectively.

Steps

Create a new Custom Table from Table Map

1. In the universal search bar search for Table Map
​
​2. From the Table Map dashboard, click Create New Custom Table button at the top
​
3. Name your Custom Table in the Table Name field
​
4. Set the View, Add, and Delete Permissions. Click the arrow to the right to expand the Advanced section
​
5. (Optional) Click the Filters button in the top row to set a default filter for your table when it is viewed, or to filter what data is visible to viewers by User Type or permission.
​
6. Click the Add Column button to add new Columns to table.
​
a. Enter a Column Alias to give a custom field on the table a display name
​
b. Review column properties to ensure correct data type, maximum length, permissions, etc. See the Fields and Definitions section of this resource for more details on each column property.

7. Repeat the Add Column process as needed until all columns for the Custom Table have been added
​
8. Click the Save Changes button
​
​
​
​Create a Custom Table from an Import Routine

1. Expand the Import/Export section in the sidebar menu and select Table Import or search for New Table Import in the universal search bar.

a. Click Add New Table Import
​
b. Select a data source to be imported into your new table (Supported local file types are: *.xlsx, *.csv, *.zip)
​
​c. Click Create Custom Table. This will take you to the Table Editor to configure your new custom table
​
d. Enter the Basic Information for the table such as the Table Name and View, Add, and Delete permissions
​
e. The table's columns will automatically be created to match the data in your import data source.
​

  • Data Type: Ensure that each column is of the correct Data Type. (Text, Integer, Decimal, Date, Currency, etc.)
    ​
    ​

  • Length: Confirm that the length of each column
    ​
    ​

  • If necessary, add an additional column
    ​

f. Click Save Changes

2. Select the new custom table that was just created in the Destination Table field

a. Select the desired Import Action for the import.
​
b. Click Save Changes to move to the next step in the Wizard

3. Field Mapping: Map the source fields from the file to the destination fields on the table.
​
​

  • If necessary, add a Static Value. This value will be the same for all records imported into the new table.
    ​
    ​

  • Click Save Changes

4. Import Tasks: In the Import Tasks tab, the first import task is automatically created.
​
​

  • Click Execute on the import task to import the data into the custom table
    ​
    ​

  • The import results will be displayed, click on View to see the created table
    ​
    ​
    ​

Navigate to your Custom Table
​
​

1. Search for your Custom Table by name in the Universal Search Bar.


​
Edit or delete your Custom Table
​
​

1. In the Universal Search Bar, search Table Map
​
2. In the search field next to Table, search for the name of your Custom Table that you just created
​
3. From this table map, you can view the Table, Audit, Edit, or Delete your table

Fields And Definitions

There are several attributes for each column. Each field you see under Add Column is an attribute that you can specify
​
​

  • Column Alias - The name of the column that will show up in your custom field
    ​
    ​

  • Data Type - The Type that your column field will accept
    ​
    ​

  • Maximum Length - If the field is a string type, then specify how many characters are allowed
    ​
    ​

  • View Permission / Edit Permission - Specify the permissions necessary to view or edit this field in your table
    ​
    ​

  • Required - Specifies whether or not the field is required/mandatory
    ​
    ​

  • Display By Default / Display By Default In Subs - Choose if you want this field to show in Table View by default and if you want this field to show in Sub Tables by default
    ​
    ​

  • Duplicates - Specify if there can be duplicate values in this field
    ​
    ​

  • Sort - Choose if you want the table to be sorted in Descending or Ascending order according to this field
    ​
    ​

  • Reference Table - Specify if you want your table to reference a field in another table
    ​
    ​

  • Under Advanced Fields, there are several more attributes that you can alter
    ​
    ​

  • Ref Field Filter - This allows you to filter on a Ref Field that you have added to the table

Best Practices

We recommend creating a Custom Table in different ways, for different conditions:
​
​

  • When no data exists and you need to start creating data, create the Custom Table from the Table Map and begin collecting data.
    ​
    ​

  • When data does exist and needs to be pulled into Encompass, create the Custom Table from an Import Routine to create and migrate data at the same time.

There are some Field Properties that once saved after the point of creation, cannot be changed.
​

  • The data type will have limited options after creation.
    ​
    ​

  • Length cannot be changed after creation.

Using a source file with the same column names as the created custom table will allow field mapping to work automatically and will streamline importing data.

Set Basic information permissions as well as column permissions as they are separate as will dictate what columns show

Distributor FAQ on how and when Encompass sends sales and inventory data to VIP SRS, and how the SRS team handles re-sends. Distributors do not need to re-send data themselves. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Users must have the Product SRS Config permission to view the setup. See Help Resources - How to set up a supplier to report to SRS
    ​
    ​

  • A SuppliersVendors record must be set up with a valid distributor number (provided by SRS), and SupplierDataAccess=Allow
    ​
    ​

  • All BrandFamilies with Products that are expected to report must have a SupplierReportCode.

Steps

1. SRS data is automatically sent to VIP multiple times a day.
​
​

  • Previous-day sales are sent 4 times a day.
    ​
    ​

  • Last month to current sales are sent every night.
    ​
    ​

  • The last 14 days of Inventory is sent every night.

2. All manual SRS re-sending activities are controlled by the SRS team.
​
3. Distributors do not need to take any action to re-send SRS data, the SRS team can do this themselves
​
4. The process for the SRS team is:
​
​

  1. An SRS team member runs a sales or inventory report in dsdlink to compare the data in Encompass vs the data in SRS.
    ​
    ​

  2. An SRS team member can issue their own resend of data to correct missing data or incorrect data on their end.
    ​
    ​

  3. If something needs to be changed in the distributor site before resending data, or if a new setup is requested, a member of the SRS team will reach out to the distributor with instructions.
    ​
    ​

  4. SRS will resend historical data the following day if they need it.
    ​

Distributor steps for turning on license plate (pallet) tracking in Encompass: enable Split License Plates By Pallet on Locations and set Track License Plates on bin zones. Requires v23.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.12

Pre-Conditions

The purpose of License Plates is to uniquely label and track individual pallets as they move through a warehouse. License plates make it easier to control individual pallet configurations, and communicate the need for specific pallet configurations within other warehouse processes like picking.

License Plate tracking should not be adopted unless pallet-level inventory or configurations are needed during the picking process. For example, pre-stacking CHEP pallets in a different configuration for club store picking. Other use cases for License Plates include hardware integrations that require pallet-level data, such as importing inventory into an ASRS system.

For all other granular inventory tracking needs, Bin Lots are recommended. Please visit our Bin Lots Help Resource article for more information.

Steps

1. Use Universal Search to navigate to the Locations table
​
2. Identify the desired location, if multiple exist, then click the edit/pencil icon on the left side of the record
​
3. Set Split License Plates By Pallet to ‘True’
​
4. Click ‘Save Changes’
​
5. Repeat steps 2-4 for any additional locations
​
6. Use Universal Search to navigate to the Bin Zones table
​
7. Locate the bin zone used for receiving shipments, typically named ‘Receive’ or ‘Receiving’
​
8. Click the edit/pencil icon on the left side of the record
​
9. Set Track License Plates to '1) Always: Transactional License Plates' or '2) Optional: FIFO License Plates'
​
​

  • 1) Always: Transactional License Plates will force a user to scan a license plate every single time inventory in the related bin zone is interacted with, meaning that the physical pallet tags will need to be easily accessible to scan.
    ​
    ​

  • 2) Optional: FIFO License Plates will allow a user to scan a license plate when they have access to the related barcode, but will still allow for inventory interaction without scanning. For instances when inventory actions are taken without scanning, the system will use FIFO/FEFO logic to rotate inventory in the most logical manner with respect to expiration dates.
    ​
    ​

10. Click ‘Save Changes’
​
11. Repeat steps 8-10 for any additional bin zones that should track license plates, such as backstock bin zones

Fields And Definitions

2) Optional: FIFO License Plates value in the Track License Plates field:
​
Refers to system-managed inventory rotation when a user does not provide a date via scan or selection. Though the value says "FIFO," this can also refer to FEFO rotation and is based on System Setting 372.
​
​

  • Receive Date/FIFO - First In First Out, denoting inventory rotation based on receive date
    ​
    ​

  • Expiration Date/FEFO - First Expires First Out, denoting inventory rotation based on expiration date

Best Practices

  • Scan license plates whenever possible, even in scanning-optional bin zones.
    ​
    ​

  • Double-check pallet configurations as inventory is counted and moved.
    ​
    ​

  • Require license plates in more pallet-regulated zones like backstock, and set pick zones as optional for continued tracking that doesn’t rely on the ability to scan.
    ​
    ​

  • Scan license plates during ePick to confirm the pick, and assign accurate date/batch information if confirming by pallet tag.
    ​
    ​

  • Supplier pallet tags can be used as license plates at any time by filling in the Pallet Tag field on a license plate record.
    ​
    ​

  • When reviewing the license plates table, search by the SSCC18 or Pallet Tag fields instead of License Plate ID.
16990295:
Distributor guide to the recommended brand hierarchy in Encompass: supplier family, supplier, vendor, brand family, brand and product, with examples and tips for VIP/SRS reporting. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

While there are several schools of thought on Brand Hierarchy, Encompass assumes the following, and recommends that distributors set up their data accordingly:

Supplier Family: Owning parent/entity of a group of suppliers.

Supplier: Who makes the product, from the consumer's perspective. This is often what is displayed on the label itself.

Vendor: Who you buy the product from.

  • Encompass does not recommend using the supplier field to denote 3PLs/distributor partners, importers, etc. Instead, these entities should be notated on the vendor record.

Brand Family: Collection of brands (ex: Barrel Aged Series, Seasonal, Etc.). Sometimes, this can be the same as the supplier.

Brand: The liquid itself - the flavor. This is generally package agnostic, unless the package is included in part of the branding. Think value-added packaging (VAP), or special or non-traditional packaging.

Product: The brand + packaging (most granular).

Example Hierarchy:

Supplier Family: Anheuser Busch Inc.
​
​

Supplier: Budweiser
​

Brand Family: Bud Light
​
​

Brand: Bud Light, Bud Light Platinum, Bud Light Chelada, etc.
​
​

Product: Bud Light 4/6 pack 16oz Cans, Bud Light 4/6 pack 16oz Bottles, Bud Light Chelada 2/12 pack 8oz Cans, etc.

Additional Considerations:

  • A brand family should only 'point' to one singular global supplier, meaning that all of the brands/products under a brand family should all point to the same global supplier.
    ​
    ​

  • A supplier record, ideally, should only have brand families underneath it that point to the same global supplier/supplier report code. Distributor numbers are typically unique for each supplier and provided by VIP/SRS. However, we are unable to add multiple Suppliers Vendors records (necessary for VIP/SRS reporting) for a single location with different distributor numbers.

Related articles:

  • Brands and Brand Families

  • Suppliers and Supplier Families

  • Add a Vendor
16990296:
Distributor steps in Encompass for SRS-requested configuration changes: update the Supplier Report Code on Brand Families or the Distributor Number on Suppliers Vendors, or restructure brands. v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

  • For a variety of reasons, the SRS team will reach out to update one or more parts of the configuration to ensure the suppliers' data makes it to SRS as expected.
    ​
    ​

  • The SRS team will provide all the necessary information to make these changes. These changes can be as simple as updating a specific field, or at the most complex, they will require some manipulation of the brand hierarchy.

Steps

1. Update Supplier Report Code - The Supplier Report Code lives on the Brand Families table, and is inherited from dsdlink after at least one product or brand has been linked.
​
​

  • See How to populate the Supplier Report Code on the Brand Family for a deeper explanation. If all the steps have been tried then try and populate or update the supplier report code, and if there is an unexpected report code, please reach out to Encompass Support.

2. Update Distributor Number - The Distributor Number lives on the Suppliers Vendors table, and is maintained by the distributor. There can be one Supplier Vendors record per each Supplier Location combination.

3. These are the only fields that need updating for configuration changes. However, there may be instances where products, brands, or brand families will be moved around to satisfy the request.
​
​ For example, if two brand families are under the same supplier with different report codes, and SRS is requesting that only one of the brand families has a different distributor number, then that brand family will need to be broken out into its own supplier, as the distributor number lives at the supplier level of the hierarchy.

Best Practices

  • Use this report (SRS Reporting by Product) to double-check work.
    ​
    ​

  • Use the recommended Brand Hierarchy to maintain a clean portfolio and ensure SRS setups and configuration changes are quick and easy.
16990298:
Distributor guide to the updated Report View beta in Encompass: filter, group, add metrics and comparisons, graphs, settings and comments on reports without FusionEdit permission. v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Use the Updated Report View

This Improved Report View interface allows end users to manipulate pre-built reports. Easily filter and group data, add and remove predefined columns, adjust graph views, drill down, and more without needing FusionEdit permissions.
​
​
​

1. The new Report View beta is now available in versions 23.12 and above. To turn on Beta, click the "Enable Beta" option in the top right header next to the universal search bar.
​
2. The name of the report is displayed in the page header. Click "Save" to save any changes to an existing report if you are already the owner. “Save as new report” will save a new copy of the report.
​
3. If there is a cache on the report, refresh the data by clicking the “Refresh” link.
​
4. Quick Edit tabs are displayed to the left of the report. Click on these tabs to open the Quick Edit panel.
​
5. The data and organization of the report can be managed in the Layout tab. Organize how the report data is grouped under Groupings, select which values to calculate on the report under Metrics, and select a Comparison to compare metrics across multiple columns.
​
6. Click the “Add” section to add a new grouping or metric. Drag groupings down to create Subgroups on the report.
​
7. On the Filters tab, add or adjust filters and time periods that are applied to the report. Click “Add another time period” or “Add more filters” to add additional filters from the available list.
​
8. A graph can be added to the top of the report from the “Graph” tab to visualize the data. Select a graph type, manage graph settings, and set the color theme from this tab.
​
9. Adjust any display settings for the full report from the Settings tab. This can include adding column totals to your report such as Unit Difference or Percentage Difference, displaying a total row, changing the format, or setting a color theme.
​
10. The “Details” tab displays important information about the report including the owner, cache times, all applied filters on the report data, and table sync information.
​
11. Users with FusionEdit permission will also see the Fusion Edit button at the bottom of the panel. Clicking this will take you to the Fusion Edit screen to edit the data source behind this report.
​
12. Click the “Manage beta” option in the header at any time to submit your feedback on the new design or revert back to the original Fusion View display.

Layout

  • Drag and drop field from the primary grouping to Sub Groups

  • The Mertrics available is made up by the Additional Values list in the Fusion Edit screen

  • Drag and drop Metrics to reorder the columns of the report.

Comparison:

  • Formally known as Columns or Column Group By

  • Allow you to add additional columns to compare Metrics (ex. YTD comparison)

  • Comparisons available is made up by the Additional Columns section in the Fusion Edit screen.

Filters

Time Period:

  • Allow for Date Range, Period, and Week Range filtering.

  • Time Periods available is made up by the pinned Date filters on the Fusion Edit screen.

Filters:

  • Filter the data in your report.

  • List of filters is made up by the Pinned Filters on the Fusion Edit screen.

16990301:
Distributor steps in Encompass to stop VIP SRS reporting for a supplier: set the Distributor Number to 00000 to keep dsdlink access, or set Supplier Data Access to Block. v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

The supplier is currently reporting sales and inventory data to SRS.

Steps

There are two methods of turning off SRS reporting, and each has a slightly different outcome, explained below.

Option 1 - Turn off reporting to SRS while still allowing the supplier to access this data by logging into dsdlink.
​
​

  • For each existing Suppliers Vendors record, set the distributor number to 00000 (five zeroes).

Option 2 - Restrict the supplier's access to your Encompass data completely.
​
​

  • For each existing Suppliers Vendors record, set Supplier Data Access to Block.

Best Practices

Unless there is a specific reason you would like to restrict the supplier's access to your Encompass data completely, it is best to use Option 1. This prevents unnecessary data from being sent to SRS, but also still gives suppliers access to the data.

16990305:
Distributor reference for promotion and pricing imports with PromotionEDBL and PromoOverrideEDBL: required fields, how promotions are matched or created, and updating PromotionProducts safely. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Minimum Requirements of Report or spreadsheet used to import:
​
​

  • ProductID or ProductIDTranslation
    ​
    ​

  • Amount or Case Amount
    ​
    ​
    ​

Additional Optional Fields:
​
​

  • PromotionID or PromotionIDTranslation to link to an existing promotion, or be able to easily update imported promotions in bulk
    ​
    ​

  • Promotion Type to help dictate what type of promotion should be used
    ​
    ​

  • Market
    ​
    ​

  • Participation
    ​
    ​

  • Min Purchase (Quantity necessary for quantity discount)
    ​
    ​

  • Min Product Count
    ​
    ​

  • Start Date
    ​
    ​

  • End Date
    ​
    ​

  • Salesman Override
    ​
    ​

  • Promotion Name

Steps

System Behavior:

PromotionEDBL

  • Used to import new pricing or update full promotion records
    ​
    ​

  • Will create products that do not already exist in the system if ProductIDTranslation is mapped
    ​
    ​

  • Will create promotions, promotion products, markets, zones, and promotion customers as needed
    ​
    ​

PromoOverrideEDBL
​
​

  • Used to override invoice transactions to a specific promotion
    ​
    ​
    ​

Recommendations:
​
​

  • If using PromotionEDBL to update existing pricing, please include all PromotionProducts of the Promotion. PromotionProducts that are not included will be deleted from the Promotion.
    ​
    ​

  • Break the data down by promotion type and import each promotion type separately.
    ​
    ​

  • If importing new promotions, use PromotionIDTranslation to help easily link on promotions in the system.
    ​
    ​

  • If updating existing promotions, map the PromotionID.
    ​
    ​

  • Import initially using markets and later use a table import to import zones to make it simpler to initially map the import.

Fields And Definitions

PromotionEDBL:

Best Used for:

  • Pricing Imports
    ​
    ​

  • Pricing Updates. Include all PromotionProducts of the Promotion. PromotionProducts that are not included will be deleted from the Promotion
    ​
    ​

Other Promotion EDBL Information

  • The minimum requirement for the Promotions EDBL is a Product column. As long as there is a Product in the source file, the Promotions EDBL can run successfully, and without a Product, the EDBL reports an error.
    ​
    ​

  • When Promotion ID or Promotion ID Translation is mapped, and the EDLB can match an existing Promotion based on it, that Promotion and its related Promotions Products records will get updated.
    ​
    ​

  • When Promotion ID or Promotion ID Translation is not mapped, but PromotionName, Condition, PromotionType, MarketID, StartDate, and EndDate are mapped, those fields will be used to match an existing Promotion ID, and if found, that Promotion and its related Promotions Products records get updated.
    ​
    ​

  • When no existing Promotions record can be match through any of the above conditions, a new Promotions records gets created, and the related tables' records are created or updated accordingly.
    ​
    ​
    ​

InvoicePromoOverrideEDBL:

Best Used for:
​
​

  • Overriding invoice transactions to a specific promotion

Best Practices

Import routines are an incredibly powerful tool and if used incorrectly, can affect alot of data. Test thoroughly on small data sets before importing.

If users are running into setup issues or have questions, reach out to Encompass Support.

If there is a complex process that consists of a report and import routines that the user doesn't want to setup? Contact our professional services to team to assist.
16990308:
Distributor guide to License Plates in Encompass WMS: track individual pallets by SSCC18 or pallet tag, pallet configurations and pick rules. Needs SplitLicensePlatesByPallet and TrackLicensePlates; v23.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.12

Pre-Conditions

  • "Locations.SplitLicensePlatesByPallet" and "BinZones.TrackLicensePlates" must both be set to Track License Plates for license plate records to be created.

  • If only "Locations.SplitLicensePlatesByPallet" is set to True, then the legacy behavior of Purchase Transactions splitting by pallet will occur instead.

Steps

  • The purpose of License Plates is to uniquely label and track individual pallets as they move through a warehouse. License plates make it easier to control individual pallet configurations, and communicate the need for specific pallet configurations within other warehouse processes like picking.
    ​
    ​Note: License Plate tracking should not be adopted unless pallet-level inventory or configurations are needed during the picking process. For example, pre-stacking CHEP pallets in a different configuration for club store picking. Other use cases for License Plates include hardware integrations that require pallet-level data, such as importing inventory into an ASRS system.

  • For all other granular inventory tracking needs, Bin Lots are recommended. Please visit the Bin Lots Help Resource for more information.

Understanding License Plate Data
​
​

  • Bin: The bin the license plate is residing in. A new license plate record will be created each time the pallet moves to a new bin. See SSCC18 for more information.
    ​
    ​

  • Product: The product found on the pallet the license plate represents. Only one product per license plate is permitted.
    ​
    ​

  • Batch Code: If applicable, the production batch code associated with the pallet. This information pulls from the related Purchase Transaction.
    ​
    ​

  • Expiration Date: If applicable, the expiration date of the inventory on the pallet. This information pulls from the related Purchase Transaction.
    ​
    ​

  • Vintage: If applicable, the vintage of the inventory on the pallet. This information pulls from the related Purchase Transaction.
    ​
    ​

  • Purchase Trans ID: This field notes the overall layer of inventory that the license plate pull from, referencing the data entered when the inventory was received.
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Lot ID: Bin Lots keep track of multiple different layers of inventory residing in the same bin. As a license plate moves from bin to bin, it will also belong to a bin lot.
    ​
    ​

  • Location: This is the warehouse location the license plate belongs to, if the company has multiple locations.
    ​
    ​

  • Pallet Configuration Type: This field allows users to assign a specific categorization to license plates based on pallet configuration. Certain retailers may not accept full pallets exactly as they are stacked when received into the warehouse.
    ​
    - For example, inventory that may need to be restacked onto CHEP pallets for club stores may result in different cases per pallet/cases per layer pallet configuration.
    ​
    - Noting the pallet configuration directly on the license plate helps direct pallets being picked for delivery to those specific license plates later, by tying to "Customer Pick Type" on the Pick Rules table. The Pallet Configuration Types table allows users to connect certain configuration types to certain "Customer Pick Types", completing the link between License Plates and Pick Rules.
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory: This is the number of cases physically residing on the pallet, or belonging to the license plate.
    ​
    ​

  • SSCC18: This is the unique identifier generated by the Encompass system when creating a license plate for the first time. This is also the barcode printed on the physical license plate label and will be maintained as the license plate moves from bin to bin.
    ​
    - When reviewing license plate data on the License Plates table, search by SSCC18, not License Plate ID.
    ​
    ​

  • Cases Per Pallet: This is the total number of cases per a full pallet of inventory for a specific license plate. This can differ from the original cases per pallet the product was received at, meaning that restacked pallets can be adjusted to accurately reflect their new configuration.
    ​
    ​

  • Cases Per Layer: This is the total cases per single layer of inventory for a specific license plate. This can differ from the original cases per layer the product was received at, meaning that restacked pallets can be adjusted to accurately reflect their new configuration.
    ​
    ​

  • Pallet Tag: This field represents the supplier pallet tag. Some suppliers may send this to Encompass with other shipment data, so Pallet Tag will be pre-populated during receiving, but this data can also be entered later. If using a supplier pallet tag to scan, printing an Encompass license plate is not necessary.
    ​
    - When reviewing license plate data on the License Plates table, be sure to search by Pallet Tag, not License Plate ID.


​
Mobile View
​
​

  • Some license plate data can be managed from the WMS handheld.
    ​
    ​

  • Fields that can be entered directly on mobile: "Pallet Configuration Type", "Pallet Tag", "Cases Per Pallet", "Cases Per Layer", and "Inventory" (Total).
    ​
    ​

  • Not pictured, but also accessible on mobile: "Purchase Trans ID", "Batch Code", "Expiration Date", and "Vintage".

Fields And Definitions

*Indicates a required field.
​
​

  • Locations.SplitLicensePlatesByPallet* - Used to create license plates during receiving; a purchase transaction having multiple pallets will have the same number of license plates as physical pallets.
    ​Values: True, False.
    ​
    ​

  • BinZones.TrackLicensePlates* - Indicates to the system which bin zones will require scanning license plates as inventory moves in and out of the zone. License plates will not be created if the related bin zones aren’t tracking them.
    ​Values: Do Not Track, Scanning Required, or Scanning Optional.
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 350: Supplier EDI Import Purchase Transactions by Pallet - While the fields above focus on purchases created internally, this field determines if imported supplier POs also split by pallet. Utilizing this function means that pre-applied supplier pallet tags can be used as license plates.
    ​Values: True, False.
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 372: Sort FIFO Layers descending by this Date field - This setting is used to determine which date the system will auto-rotate inventory by in scanning-optional situations.
    ​Values: Expiration Date (FEFO), Receive Date (FIFO).

Best Practices

  • Scan license plates whenever possible, even in scanning-optional bin zones.
    ​
    ​

  • Double-check pallet configurations as inventory is counted and moved.
    ​
    ​

  • Require license plates in more pallet-regulated zones like backstock, and set pick zones as optional for continued tracking that doesn’t rely on the ability to scan.
    ​
    ​

  • Scan license plates during ePick to confirm the pick, and assign accurate date/batch information if confirmed by pallet tag.
    ​
    ​

  • Supplier pallet tags can be used as license plates by filling in the "Pallet Tag" field on a license plate record.
    ​
    ​

  • When reviewing the License Plates table, search by the "SSCC18" or "Pallet Tag" fields instead of License Plate ID.

16990328:
Distributor warehouse steps for moving invoices to another load sheet on Encompass Mobile, and how Move Not-Delivered, Off-Load and Re-deliver treat inventory. Needs InvoiceEdit and LoadSheetEdit; v21.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 21.01

Pre-Conditions

Required Permissions:

  • InvoiceEdit
    ​

  • InvoiceEditLoaded
    ​

  • LoadSheetEdit

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

1. Tap the warehouse button on the home screen of Encompass Mobile.
​
2. Log in to Warehouse.
​
3. If the company has multiple locations, tap the location working out of.
​
4. Tap Load Sheet Load/Return.
​
​5. Select the date of the Load Sheet.
​
6. Tap the Load Sheet the invoice is currently on.
​
7. Tap the Invoices tab.
​
8. Use the checkboxes to select the invoices to move.
​
9. Tap 'Move Invoice'.
​
10. Select a move option.
​
11. Select the new Load Sheet to move the invoices to.

Fields And Definitions

The various move options interact with related inventory differently.

Inventory does not move with invoice:

Move Not-Delivered

  • Can select any status load sheet to move the invoice to

  • Does not bring the loaded inventory with the moved invoice, the product will stay in the original route bin

  • Invoice has to be re-palletized on the new load sheet and re-picked

  • When to use: when moving an Invoice from one load sheet to another, with no intention of moving the related pallets onto another truck

  • What is unique about this option: leaves product in the route bin to be reconciled during truck return

Inventory does move with invoice:

Move Off-Load

  • Can select any load sheets in the Loaded status to move the invoice to; New status load sheets are also available if the route bins match

  • Brings inventory and pallet record with moved invoice, product goes to the new route bin

  • Invoice does not have to be re-palletized or re-picked

  • When to use: when moving an invoice from one loaded load sheet to another loaded load sheet, or when you don't need to print a new pallet tag or unload the inventory from its destination route bin

  • What is unique about this option: leaves pallets in loaded status, and will not require a new pallet tag

Move Re-deliver

  • Can select any load sheets in the New status to move the invoice to

  • Brings inventory with the invoice, but creates a new pallet record tied to the new load sheet (for more accurate pallet labeling, if needed)

  • Product goes to the new route bin once a new pallet tag is printed from the original load sheet's Route Reconciliation Redeliver tab

  • When to use: When moving an invoice from a loaded load sheet to a new load sheet sharing the same route bin, with the intention to re-load related pallets later

  • What is unique about this option: allows a user to move an invoice between two routes that share the same route bin, with better control of when the related inventory is loaded

Best Practices

Based on the impact to inventory that comess with each invoice move option, consider which option best fits common situations for the business. Determine a standard practice for each situation, and communicate it with the team.

​ - Build Height: How high can this Pallet be built
​
​ - Width / Length: The width and length of the physical pallet
​
​ - Weight: Is used for QA ONLY. (This is included on the weight in Delivery Optimizer)

4. Click Add Record when complete.
​
​

Add Pick Methods
​
​1. Using Universal search, navigate to the Pick Methods table
​
​

  • Pick Methods determine how a product needs to be picked
    ​
    ​

2. Click the Add Pick Methods button.
​
3. Enter values in the fields displayed on the Add Pick Methods form.

​ Note: Many of the required fields are default and can be changed based on the intended workflow.
​
4. Click Add Record when complete.
​
​

Add Pick Rules
​
​1. Using Universal search, navigate to the Pick Rules table.
​
​

  • Pick Rules determine which Pick Method will be used by looking at the Invoice Transaction. Think of them as IF-THEN statements. Example: IF the Invoice Transaction holds true for everything on the Pick Rule from Location to Bin Zone, THEN use the Pick Method on the record.
    ​
    ​

2. Click the Add Pick Rules button.
​
3. Enter values in the fields displayed on the Add Pick Rules form.
​
​

  • *Priority - This determines the order a Pick Rule is checked
    ​
    ​ Note: Pick Rules should never have the same priority
    ​
    ​

  • *Location - Will ONLY affect multi-location Distributorships and looks to the location on the Load Sheet
    ​
    ​

  • Route Type - Points to the Route’s Route Type on the Load Sheet
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Pick Type - Points to the Customer Record
    ​
    ​

  • Product Pick Type - On the Product Type or the Inventory Record. Note: A product’s Inventory record’s Product Pick Type will override the Product Type
    ​
    ​

  • Minimum Cases - Minimum requirement of cases to apply this pick rule. (Typically used for Bulk Picks to pick by Pallet)
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Unit - Determined by the Product record and is set on the Invoice Transaction when you apply Pick Rules
    ​
    ​

  • Close Date - Used for Close Dated Products. If this field is True the Bin Zone should be set to CLOSE DATED to ensure the products are being picked from the correct location
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Zone - What Bin Zone does this product live in and where does Encompass send the Pickers when this rule is applied? (IF NULL Bin Zone defaults to all Pick Zones.)
    ​
    ​

  • *Pick Method - How the Pick Method is tied to the Pick Rule
    ​
    ​

  • Oddball Bin - Used for Dynamic or Double Picking ONLY (Moving from Backstock to only one bin)
    ​
    ​

  • Dynamic Pick Line Bin Zone - Used for Dynamic or Double Picking Only (Moving from Backstock to Multiple Bins)
    ​

  • Skip - When Skip is set to True, if the inventory in a particular bin is not sufficient for palletization, this will skip over the bin with insuffiecient inventory, and move onto the next bin in the bin zone. This ignores the default logic of sending picks to bins regardless of inventory, as long as the inventory is active.
    ​
    ​

  • Label Printer - Indicates which APS printer box labels will print if the pick method is set to print box labels
    ​
    ​

  • Box Print Template - Set template for printing box labels when pick method is set to print box labels
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Sheet Printer - Indicates which APS printer pick sheets will print too if the pick method is set to voice pick = false

4. Click Add Record when complete.
