16990337:
Distributor steps for turning on license plate (pallet) tracking in Encompass: set License Plates By Pallet on Locations and Track License Plates on receiving bin zones. Includes video; v23.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.12

Pre-Conditions

  • The purpose of License Plates is to uniquely label and track individual pallets as they move through a warehouse.
    ​
    ​

  • License plates make it easier to control individual pallet configurations, and communicate the need for specific pallet configurations within other warehouse processes like picking.
    ​
    ​

  • License Plate tracking should not be adopted unless pallet-level inventory or configurations are needed during the picking process. For example, pre-stacking CHEP pallets in a different configuration for club store picking. Other use cases for License Plates include hardware integrations that require pallet-level data, such as importing inventory into an ASRS system.
    ​
    ​

  • For all other granular inventory tracking needs, Bin Lots are recommended. Please visit the Bin Lots Help Resource for more information.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Turn on License Plate Tracking

1. Using the Universal Search, navigate to the Locations table.
​
2. Identify the desired location, if multiple locations exist, then arrow into the record.
​
3. Under the "Warehouse & Bins" subheader, Set "License Plates By Pallet" to True.
​
4. Click the "Save" icon.
​
5. Repeat steps 2-4 for any additional locations.
​
6. Using the Universal Search, navigate to the Bin Zones table.
​
7. Locate the Bin Zone used for receiving shipments, typically named ‘Receive’ or ‘Receiving’.
​
8. Arrow into the Bin Zone record.
​
9. Set "Track License Plates" to '1) Always: Transactional License Plates' or '2) Optional: FIFO License Plates'.
​
​

  • 1) Always: Transactional License Plates will force a user to scan a license plate every single time inventory in the related bin zone is interacted with, meaning that the physical pallet tags will need to be easily accessible to scan.
    ​
    ​

  • 2) Optional: FIFO License Plates will allow a user to scan a license plate when they have access to the related barcode, but will still allow for inventory interaction without scanning. For instances when inventory actions are taken without scanning, the system will use FIFO/FEFO logic to rotate inventory most logically concerning expiration dates.
    ​
    ​

10. Click the "Save" icon.
​
11. Repeat steps 8-10 for any additional bin zones that should track license plates, such as backstock bin zones.

Fields And Definitions

2) Optional: FIFO License Plates value in the Track License Plates field:
​
​

  • Refers to system-managed inventory rotation when a user does not provide a date via scan or selection. Though the value says "FIFO," this can also refer to FEFO rotation and is based on System Setting 372.
    ​
    ​

  • Receive Date/FIFO - First In First Out, denoting inventory rotation based on the receive date.
    ​
    ​

  • Expiration Date/FEFO - First Expires First Out, denoting inventory rotation based on expiration date.

Best Practices

  • Scan license plates whenever possible, even in scanning-optional bin zones.
    ​
    ​

  • Double-check pallet configurations as inventory is counted and moved.
    ​
    ​

  • Require license plates in more pallet-regulated zones like backstock, and set pick zones as optional for continued tracking that doesn’t rely on the ability to scan.
    ​
    ​

  • Scan license plates during ePick to confirm the pick, and assign accurate date/batch information if confirming by pallet tag.
    ​
    ​

  • Supplier pallet tags can be used as license plates at any time by filling in the Pallet Tag field on a license plate record.
    ​
    ​

  • When reviewing the license plates table, search by the SSCC18 or Pallet Tag fields instead of License Plate ID.

16990360:
Distributor/producer guide to the Transfer Variance Report in Encompass: find case, price and $0 cost differences between transfer invoices and purchases. Needs PurchaseCostEdit permission and v24.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.10

Pre-Conditions

*Required Permission - PurchaseCostEdit

* The Products Product Type must have 'Track Inventory' set to 'True' to show on the Transfer Variance Report.

Steps

The Transfer Variance Report is used to show inventory and price differences between transfer invoices and purchases. This report is useful to catch any mistakes during picking, loading, and receiving transfers. A Products Product Type must have 'Track Inventory' set to 'True' to show on the Transfer Variance Report. Otherwise, these Products will not show.

Filters:
​
​

  • From Location: Loadsheet or sending location
    ​
    ​

  • To Location: Shipment or receiving location
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Status: Status of the loadsheet/invoice
    ​
    ​

  • PO Status: Status of the shipment/purchase
    ​
    ​

  • Start Date / End Date: Date range of the loadsheet and shipment date. Default Start Date = today - 30 days. Default End Date = today + 15 days
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Num: Invoice number on both the invoice and purchase
    ​
    ​

  • Only Show Differences: Only shows transfer with a case and/or price variance between the transfer invoice and purchase
    ​
    ​

  • Show $0 Costing: Only shows products that were transferred at a $0 price or $0 keg deposit

Show $0 Costing Logic:
​
​$0.00 Case or Deposit will show as an Error on the report and the amount will show in red $0.00.
​
Deposit cost with $0.00 will only show if the following condistions are true:
​
​

  1. The package (ex. 1/2 BBL) on the product has a Packages Deposits record
    ​
    ​

  2. The transfer date is between the Packages Deposits Start Date and End Date or the End Date is blank
    ​
    ​

  3. The transfer customer is in the Deposit Area on the Packages Deposit record
    ​
    ​

  4. The Deposit Method = 1) Calculate as In-Line Deposit
    ​
    ​

  5. The Deposit amount on the Packages Deposit must be greater than $0.00

Best Practices

It is recommended to transfer inventory at a laid-in cost or laid-in + tax prices using a transfer out inventory customer. When creating new products, the costing may not be initially known, and due to timing issues, it is possible that products can be transferred at $0 before the costing is set up.

* The Products Product Type must have 'Track Inventory' set to 'True' to show on the Transfer Variance Report.

Pre-Conditions

Setting up accessibility to Auto Transfers from the Server:
​
​Users must be given access to the Auto Transfer dashboard by setting Dashboard Roles here. Once a user's role has been given access, they will be able to access the Auto Transfer dashboard by searching for "Auto Transfer" in the Universal Search bar.

Steps

Configuration Setup:

Auto Transfers was made with your taproom employees in mind. Create transfers on Encompass Mobile in just a few seconds. The transfer invoice will be automatically returned and the purchase for the destination location will be automatically received.

If you are already creating transfers with Transfer Planner or using existing Inventory Transfer Rules, you an edit the Transfer Method on the Inventory Transfer Rules record to Auto Transfer. This will allow transfers to be created with the auto transfer workflow.

If this is the first time setting up transfers, it is recommended to get started by using the Transfer Planner Setup dashboard. This dashboard will create the data necessary for the transfer. Once the setup is complete, you an change the Transfer Method on the Inventory Transfer Rules record to Auto Transfer.

It is also possible to have two transfer methods for the same from/to locations. One transfer rule could be for auto transfers, and the other for transfer planner.

16990379:
Distributor steps in Encompass for rolling back Invoice, AR, AP or Financial close dates on the End of Day Rollback Dashboard to reopen closed periods. Needs EndOfDayRollback permission and v24.04+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.04

Pre-Conditions

  • This dashboard respects regular close date rules: Invoice Close Date >= AR/AP Close Date >= Financial Close Date
    ​
    ​

  • Dashboards Roles must be manually added
    ​
    ​

  • EndOfDayRollback Permission, which must be manually added to Users or Roles, is required to access Dashboard functions

In Scope:
​
​

  • Rolling back sub-ledger closes (Invoice, AR, AP) up to 30 days from the maximum date ever closed through
    ​
    ​

  • Rolling back Financial Close Date up to the Financial Go-Live Date
    ​
    ​

  • Normal End of Day period close rules apply (Invoice Close >= AR/AP Close >= Financial Close)

Out of Scope:

  • Rolling periods forward (once rolled back, End of Day processes MUST be run)
    ​
    ​

  • Transactional updates (unverification, recalculation, etc.)
    ​
    ​

  • Preparation for re-syncing data to external systems
    ​
    ​

  • Unrestricted date range for rollback

Steps

The End of Day Rollback Dashboard has five (5) total functions:
​
​
​

Update Invoice Close Date:
​
​

  1. Select the Location(s) you wish to roll back Invoice Close Date for
    ​
    ​

  2. The Current Close Date for each selected Location will appear as the records are selected
    ​
    ​

  3. Select the New Close Date for all selected Locations
    ​
    ​

  4. Only one (1) New Close Date may be selected per rollback action
    ​
    ​

  5. Press the Update Invoice Close Date button
    ​
    ​

  6. Read and accept the Risk Acknowledgement by clicking the I agree button - this must be accepted to proceed
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Close Date is restricted to rolling back 30 days from the maximum date the Location(s) have ever been closed through
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

Update AR Close Date:
​

  1. Select the Company(ies) you wish to roll back Accounts Receivable Close Date for
    ​
    ​

  2. The Current Close Date for each selected Company will appear as the records are selected
    ​
    ​

  3. Select the New Close Date for all selected Companies
    ​
    ​

  4. Only one (1) New Close Date may be selected per rollback action
    ​
    ​

  5. Press the Update AR Close Date button
    ​
    ​

  6. Read and accept the Risk Acknowledgement by clicking the I agree button - this must be accepted to proceed

  • Accounts Receivable Close Date is restricted to rolling back 30 days from the maximum date the Company(ies) have ever been closed through
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

Update AP Close Date:
​

  1. Select the Company(ies) you wish to roll back Accounts Payable Close Date for
    ​
    ​

  2. The Current Close Date for each selected Company will appear as the records are selected
    ​
    ​

  3. Select the New Close Date for all selected Companies
    ​
    ​

  4. Only one (1) New Close Date may be selected per rollback action
    ​
    ​

  5. Press the Update AP Close Date button
    ​
    ​

  6. Read and accept the Risk Acknowledgement by clicking the I agree button - this must be accepted to proceed

  • Accounts Payable Close Date is restricted to rolling back 30 days from the maximum date the Company(ies) have ever been closed through
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

Update Financial Close Date:
​

  1. Select the Company(ies) you wish to roll back Financial Close Date for
    ​
    ​

  2. The Current Close Date for each selected Company will appear as the records are selected
    ​
    ​

  3. Select the New Close Date for all selected Companies
    ​
    ​

  4. Only one (1) New Close Date may be selected per rollback action
    ​
    ​

  5. Press the Update Financial Close Date button
    ​
    ​

  6. Read and accept the Risk Acknowledgement by clicking the I agree button - this must be accepted to proceed

  • Financial Close Date is restricted to rolling back to the Financial Go-Live Date noted on the Company record
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

Update All Close Dates:
​

  1. Follow Steps 1-4 from above for all Locations and Companies you wish to roll back
    ​
    ​

  2. Select the appropriate New Close Dates for each period you are rolling back
    ​
    ​

  3. Press the Update All Close Dates button
    ​
    ​

  4. Read and accept the Risk Acknowledgement by clicking the I agree button - this must be accepted to proceed

  • Update All Close Dates respects all date range rules as noted on the individual records above

Fields And Definitions

Locations.InvoiceCloseDate - Designates the calendar date each Location has closed their sales through
​
​

Companies.ARCloseDate - Designates the calendar date each Company has closed their Accounts Receivable through
​
​

Companies.APCloseDate - Designates the calendar date each Company has closed their Accounts Payable through
​
​

Companies.FinancialCloseDate- Designates the calendar date each Company has closed their Financials through

Best Practices

When selecting the date to roll back to, you are selecting the new Close Date. This means the date you select will NOT be reopened. All dates up to the new Close Date selected will be reopened.
​
​

  • For example, if you need to correct a verified Deposit from 7/15/2024, select 7/14/2024 as the new Close Date.

16990409:
Reference table for distributors explaining how Encompass report value fields are calculated, e.g. $Vol, Case Equiv, Gross, Margin %, Barrels, Stop Count, per Drop averages. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Field

Definition

$Vol

Total sales price of units sold. If the product had a Deposit from the Packages Deposits table, then the deposit value is included as part of the sales price. Invoice Charges are not included.

$Vol - Deposit

Total sales price of units sold. If the product had a deposit, then this Deposit value is not included as part of the sales price. Invoice Charges are not included.

$Vol - Deposit per Drop

Total $Vol - Deposit (see definition) divided by the total number of days when the customer was delivered to

Avg Case Discount

SUM( Discount * Num Units ) / SUM( Cases )

Avg Case Full Price

SUM( Full Price * Num Units ) / SUM( Cases )

Avg Case Participation

SUM( Participation * Num Units ) / SUM( Cases )

Avg Case Unit Price

SUM( Unit Price * Num Units ) / SUM( Cases )

Avg Cost

SUM((Laid In Cost + Tax Cost – Participation) * Num Units) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Discount

SUM( Discount * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg FOB

SUM( FOB * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Freight

SUM( PurchaseTrans.Freight * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Full Price

SUM( Full Price * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Gross

SUM(( Unit Price – Deposit + Participation – Laid In Cost – Tax Cost) * Num Units) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Laid-in Cost

SUM( Laid In * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Other Cost

SUM( PurchaseTrans.OtherCost * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Participation

SUM( Participation * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Tax

SUM( PurchaseTrans.Tax * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Depletion Tax

SUM( TaxCost * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Unit Price

SUM( Unit Price * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Avg Weekly $Vol

SUM( $Vol - Deposit ) / (Number of days in the report date range / 7)

Avg Weekly Case Equiv

SUM( Case Equivs ) / (Number of days in the report date range / 7)

Avg Weekly Retail Units

SUM( Retail Units ) / (Number of days in the report date range / 7)

Avg Weekly Units

SUM( Units ) / (Number of days in the report date range / 7)

Avg Weekly Units per Placement

SUM( Case Equivs ) / the count of unique combinations of Product ID & Customer ID (placements) / (Number of days in the report date range / 7)

Avg Tax Cost 2

SUM( Tax Cost 2 * Num Units ) / SUM( Num Units )

Barrels

Cases are converted to Barrels based on the value of the Ounces field in the Packages table. (1 ounce = 0.000252016129 barrels.)

Buyer Count

The total number of unique Customers (by Customer ID).

Case Equiv

Cases are converted to represent their volume equivalence to the “Standard” case of that product type using the CaseEquiv field of the Packages table. Beer (& Soda) = 288 ounces (24 x 12 oz); RedBull = 199.2 ounces (24 x 8.3 oz); Wine = 304.326 ounces (12 x 750 ml); e-shot= 48 ounces (24 x 2 oz); 12 x 341 ml = 138.367 ounces.

Case Equiv per Drop

Number of Items sold (in Case Equivalences) per Customer Drop over included Loadsheets. Customers that had multiple Invoices on a single Loadsheet count as single Drop. Customers that had Invoices on more that one Loadsheet count as one Drop per Loadsheet on which an Invoice appears.

Case Equiv Forecasted

Packages.CaseEquiv * Sum of Forecasts.SalesForecast for the same Year and Months where Period Type = Months

Cases

If sold by the case, then this is Units; otherwise units values are converted to case values using Sell Units Per Case in the Packages table. Kegs have a Sell Units per case of 1, so 1 keg is also 1 case in reports.

Commission

Total Summed Commission for all Employee Commission records set up.

Consumable Units

Total Consumable Units. The total number of unique Customers (by Customer ID).

Deposit

Total in $ of Deposits of Units sold.

Deposit Cost

Total of Deposit Cost for all Deposit types

Discount

Every Discount amount for a product

FOB

Total Freight On Board (FOB) for the Items.

Full Price

Summed Full Price for the units

Full Price + Deposit

Total Full Price + Deposit amount

Gallons

Cases are converted to Gallons based on the value of the Ounces field in the Packages table. (1 ounce = 0.0078125 gallons.)

Gross

Total in $ per Item of: $Vol – Deposit (Unit Price) + Participation – Laid In Cost – Tax Cost.

Gross per CaseEquiv

Average Gross per Item converted to Case Equivalence.

Gross per Drop

Gross averaged over the total number of Customer Drops over included Loadsheets. Customers that had multiple Invoices on a single Loadsheet count as single Drop. Customers that had Invoices on more that one Loadsheet count as one Drop per Loadsheet on which an Invoice appears.

Half Barrels

1 half barrel = 1980 oz(Oz per Unit * Sum of Units) / 1980

Hectoliters

hectoliter = 3381.4022558919 oz(Oz per Unit * Sum of Units) / 3381.4

InvoiceCharge1

Total $ amount of Invoice Charge 1

InvoiceCharge2

Total $ amount of Invoice Charge 2

InvoiceCharge3

Total $ amount of Invoice Charge 3

InvoiceCharge4

Total $ amount of Invoice Charge 4

InvoiceCharge5

Total $ amount of Invoice Charge 5

Laid-in Cost

Total of Laid In Cost + Tax Cost(1&2)

Laid-in + Deposit

Total of Laid In Cost + Tax Cost(1&2) + Deposit Cost (all Deposit Types)

Liters

Cases are converted to Liters based on the value of the Ounces field in the Packages table. (1 ounce = 0.0295735297 liters.)

Load Sheet Count

The total number of unique Loadsheets (by Loadsheet ID).

Lost Sales Units

The number difference between Units Ordered and Num Units on Invoice Trans

Lost Sales Cases

The number difference between Cases Ordered and Cases on Invoice Trans

Margin %

Sum(Gross) / Income, represented as a percentage. Income is defined as Unit Price (Full price less discount).Value for Deposits added automatically to the Sales Price are excluded from the calculations of Gross and Income.

Margin % (if participation is considered as income)

Sum(Gross) / Income, represented as a percentage. Income is defined as Unit Price plus Participation. If you choose to treat participation as income, Setting 98 should be set to True. (Control Panel -> Program Settings -> Sales -> Margin %). Value for Deposits added automatically to the Sales Price are excluded from the calculations of Gross and Income.

Participation %

Total Participation / Total Discounts as a percentage.

Placement Count

The count of unique combinations of Product ID & Customer ID

Product Count

The total number of unique Products (by Product ID).

Retail Units

Total Retail Units

Servings

Total Cases * Servings per case

Shrinkage Rate

(1000 X Sum(Inv Adj Case Equivs)) / Sum(Sales Case Equivs). If there are no Sales, then this is just the Inv Adj Case Equivs.

Stop Count

Stop Count is the distinct count of a Load Sheet Date and a Customer ID. Customers that had multiple Invoices on a single Loadsheet count as single Stop. Customers that had Invoices on more that one Loadsheets count as one Stop as long as they are for the same date. Customer count will match Stop count if you are looking at one day of data

Discount

The summed amount of InvoiceTrans.Discount * InvoiceTrans.NumUnits

Ounces

Total Cases * Ounces per Case

Participation

Total $ amount of Participation from the invoice transaction

Depletion Tax

Total of Excise Tax Cost

Tax Cost 2

Total of Jurisdictional or Local Tax Cost

Units

Total Num Units

Weight

The summed total Weight of the product (Units * Weight)

Pre-Conditions

For a variety of reasons, the SRS team will reach out to have you update one or more parts of the configuration that ensure your suppliers' data makes it to SRS as expected. The SRS team will provide you with all the necessary information to make these changes. These changes can be as simple as updating a specific field, or at the most complex, they will require some manipulation of your brand hierarchy.

Steps

Update Supplier Report Code - The Supplier Report Code lives on the Brand Families table, and is inherited from the dsdlink after you have linked at least one product or brand. See How to populate the Supplier Report Code on the Brand Family for a deeper explanation. If you have tried all the steps to try and populate or update the supplier report code, and you still cannot get the expected report code, please reach out to Encompass Support.

Update Distributor Number - The Distributor Number lives on the Suppliers Vendors table, and is maintained by you, the distributor. You can have one Suppliers Vendors record per each Supplier Location combination.

These are the only fields that need updating for configuration changes. However, there may be instances where you will have to move products, brands, or brand families around in order to satisfy the request. For example, if you have two brand families under the same supplier with different report codes, and SRS is requesting that only one of the brand families has a different distributor number, then that brand family will need to be broken out into it's own supplier, as the distributor number lives at the supplier level of the hierarchy.

Steps

A price may change for many reasons, common ones include:
​
​

  • The invoice no longer meets the requirements of a promotion.
    ​

  • A promotion may have changed.
    ​
    ​

  • The customer may no longer be qualified for a promotion.
    ​
    ​

    ​

  • Someone may have performed a promotion override.

How to Troubleshoot:

​

​

  • If the customer no longer qualifies for the promotion, qualify them naturally by adding them to the right zones or adding the necessary products.

16990429:
Distributor overview of Skills Kickstart, Encompass's recurring live training webinars for users new to Encompass or a role: who should attend, where recordings live, and Featured Courses.

Minimum Version Required: 23.10

Steps

What is Skills Kickstart at Encompass?

What is the Skills Kickstart series?

The Skills Kickstart is a series of live webinars designed to train and inform Encompass users about our platform. This training program is crafted for users who are new to their role or company and are keen to delve into topics specifically relevant to them. Whether you're starting a new job or transitioning within your current organization, these sessions provide targeted insights and knowledge essential for navigating and utilizing Encompass.

Who should attend the sessions?

These sessions are intended for people who are new to using Encompass or new to using a specific feature set in Encompass. Think about the Warehouseman who moves into a team lead role - they'd need to know different reports, dashboards, and tools than they did before. Or think about a newly hired Sales Rep or Accountant who has never worked on Encompass before. These trainings are designed to provide introductory information for those employees on the core features they may use on a day to day basis as a complement to the onboarding you're providing.

Do I have to attend the whole series?

No! While the information does build to a certain degree as we go through it, you do not have to sign up for every session offered in Skills Kickstart. We encourage you to attend just the sessions that are most relevant to you and your role.

What if I am unable to attend a session?

All the recordings will be posted in the Recording Archive so you will have an opportunity to review this content on-demand. Additionally, this series will repeat every 6 months, so if you missed a session and want to attend live next time, you haven't missed your chance. Keep an eye on the eLearning dashboard for it to come around again.

What are Featured Courses?

Featured Courses are the content that is most relevant at specific times of the year - topics like "Preparing 1099 Data in Encompass" is best presented in January, not July because that is when Accounting teams are preparing to file 1099 forms to the IRS. Or "Pricing and Promotion Management" is best at the end of the year when you know the pricing is going to change for certain Brands in predictable ways in the following year. These courses don't fall within a twice-yearly recurring cadence but we still want to offer this content at times that make sense with your seasonal workflows.

Steps

  • This feature is currently in EAP with select customers.

  • Please view the License Plates: Configuration & Use knowledge document for a full review of license plate setup & processes.

Fields And Definitions

  • Locations.SplitLicensePlatesByPallet* - Used to create license plates during receiving; a purchase transaction having multiple pallets will have the same number of license plates as physical pallets.
    Values: True, False.
    ​
    ​

  • BinZones.TrackLicensePlates* - Indicates to the system which bin zones will require scanning license plates as inventory moves in and out of the zone. License plates will not be created if the related bin zones aren’t tracking them.
    Values: Do Not Track, Scanning Required, or Scanning Optional.
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 350: Supplier EDI Import Purchase Transactions by Pallet - While the fields above focus on purchases created internally, this field determines if imported supplier POs also split by pallet. Utilizing this function means that pre-applied supplier pallet tags can be used as license plates.
    Values: True, False.
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 372: Sort FIFO Layers descending by this Date field - This setting is used to determine which date the system will auto-rotate inventory by in scanning-optional situations.
    Values: Expiration Date (FEFO), Receive Date (FIFO).

Best Practices

  • Scan license plates whenever possible, even in scanning-optional bin zones.
    ​
    ​

  • Double-check pallet configurations as inventory is counted and moved.
    ​
    ​

  • Require license plates in more pallet-regulated zones like backstock, and set pick zones as optional for continued tracking that doesn’t rely on the ability to scan.
    ​
    ​

  • Scan license plates during ePick to confirm the pick, and assign accurate date/batch information if confirming by pallet tag.
    ​
    ​

  • Supplier pallet tags can be used as license plates at any time by filling in the Pallet Tag field on a license plate record.

  • When reviewing the license plates table, search by the SSCC18 or Pallet Tag fields instead of License Plate ID.

Distributor guide to the Recommended Phasing reports in Encompass: use average weekly case equivalents to recommend how often to deliver to each customer. Needs beta enabled; v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

The recommended phasing reports include using historical sales for invoice creation rate, average weekly CEs, average weekly cases, and average weekly $Vol or invoice totals.

These report can be access by going to the Operations Report Library. NOTE. You will have to enable beta to see this reports. The recommended phasing reports will be located in the delivery section.

State Date and End Date are optional, but will pull the sales history for the selected date range

  • If blank, the start date will default to today -180 days
    ​
    ​

  • If blank, the end date will default to today

​
Only Customers with Recommendations.

  • If True the report will only show customers that the current phasing is different than the recommended phase based on the thresholds you enter.
    ​
    ​

  • If False all customers will be displayed, even if their current phasing matches the recommendation.

Thresholds - Avg CEs/Week
​
​ Enter the desired weekly Avg CEs/Week thresholds to calculate the Recommendation for Phasing

  • Every Other Week: Customers with Avg CEs/Week between the Every Other Week and Every Week will be recommended for every other week. Avg CEs/Week less than this amount will be recommended for once every 4 weeks.

  • Every Week: Customers with Avg CEs/Week between the Every Week and Twice Per Week will be recommended for every week.

  • Twice Per Week: Customers with Avg CEs/Week >0 the Twice Per Week and Every Week will be recommended for 2 twice per week visits.

Example:
​
​

  • Every Other Week = 10. Every Week = 25. Twice Per Week = 100.
    ​
    ​

  • Customers that have less than 10 Avg CEs/Week will be recommended for every 4 weeks
    ​
    ​

  • Customers that have 10 to 24.9 Avg CEs/Week will be recommended for every 2 weeks
    ​
    ​

  • Customers that have 25 to 99.9 Avg CEs/Week will be recommended for every week
    ​
    ​

  • Customers that have 100 or more Avg CEs/Week will be recommended for 2 per week.

16990480:
Distributor overview of the Encompass Snowflake Reader: a paid, read-only Snowflake account for querying production data or connecting BI tools like Power BI. Requires setup by Encompass; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Encompass Snowflake Readers require a manual setup by Encompass, and do incur a fee.
    ​
    ​

  • Please contact Encompass to get started.

Steps

Warning: Snowflake Reader Accounts are recommended only for technical users. Utilizing and managing the account requires SQL database management experience.

Encompass does not provide direct support on managing your Snowflake account.

Encompass systems can opt-in to utilizing a Snowflake Reader instance. This is a Snowflake account, setup by the Encompass team as a sub-account to the primary Encompass Snowflake instance.

In this account, Encompass will share a read-only database that contains all of the same information as the production Encompass database, allowing you to connect to it directly (example: via ODBC) and run queries on the data. This also includes access to the online Snowflake interface, called Snowsight.
​
​

It is important to note: the data is not replicated to the reader account, it instead provides a direct read-only view to the actual production data, so there is no additional delay in data updating for queries run in the reader account.

More information about how Snowflake data sharing works

Example use cases include:

  • Connecting a 3rd party BI tool, such as Tableau, PowerBI, Qlik, Looker, Sigma, etc.
    ​
    ​

  • Extracting the data for usage in another service or integration (note: Encompass APIs are typically more efficient for this, but sometimes ODBC access is preferred)
    ​
    ​

  • Running direct queries in the Snowflake UI to troubleshoot or gain insight into the underlying system data

Setup process for Encompass Snowflake Readers:

  1. Reach out to Encompass to request a reader account is added
    ​
    ​

  2. Encompass will send you an SOW for the cost of adding the account
    ​
    ​

  3. After the SOW is signed, Encompass will create the account and setup 1 initial admin user, which is shared to the primary contact at your organization
    ​
    ​

  4. The person who receives the initial user can login and add addional users with their desired permission levels
    ​
    ​

  5. Usage of the Snowflake account is tracked by Snowflake, and Encompass places the usage charges (a pass-through) onto your quarterly Encompass invoice

Other items to be aware of:

  • After the initial account creation, Encompass is not responsible for access controls in the reader account. It is your organization's responsibility to control the permissions and users in that sub-account.
    ​
    ​

  • Snowflake does support various levels of permission, includuing row level permissions. For information about these controls, start with the Snowflake GRANT Documentation, User Management Documentation, and the Row Access Policy Documentation. These are not setup by default and will need to be setup by the administrator at your organization, if they are needed.
    ​
    ​

  • Because this is a technical service, standard Encompass support cannot help with configuring the account or troubleshooting queries. Please use the Snowflake documentation to research issues in these areas
    ​
    ​

  • Snowflake performance varies based on the size of the warehouse selected, and the amount of time it is running. Encompass charges are a pass-through of your actual Snowflake usage. See Understanding Snowflake Cost for more information
    ​
    ​

  • Enrolling in a Encompass Snowflake Reader has a minimum time period of 1 quarter, but can be cancelled at any time after.

Best Practices

  • Ensure your warehouses in Snowflake are always auto-suspending.
    ​
    ​

  • Always start with the X-Small instance size in Snowflake and scale up from there as needed. Most workloads do not have issues running on a single X-Small warehouse.
    ​
    ​

  • Snowflake is a columar database, which means that queries are typically faster when utilizing the least amount of columns possible. Use the Snowflake Query Profiler to optimize queries and make them faster/cheaper.
    ​
    ​

  • More information on cost optimization
    ​
    ​

  • Create individual users for each person who will be accessing Snowflake (not shared users) and close access when they no longer need it. This ensures security, especially if someone were to leave the company or move to another department.
    ​
    ​

  • More information on Snowflake security

Distributor steps for changing the EDI Status on an invoice in Encompass to resend or stop EDI files (894, 856, 810, PayLink), with a list of every status code. Requires v21.01+.

Steps

How to edit EDI Status on an Invoice:

  1. Go to the invoices table

Fields And Definitions

What is EDI Status?

EDI Status is how Encompass Tracks how Invoices send through EDI. A single Invoice can send multiple different files throughout its lifecycle, so this field helps ensure the proper order of files is followed. EDI Status will follow a general hierarchy so it can only move to a higher status. Generally there are 3 statuses that each file type has:

  • Resend File

  • File Sent

  • File Failed

To resend a file of any type, you can set the EDI Status to resend for that file type.

Not sure what file type you need to send?

Check the exchange configuration to find the functional type. This will help you understand what the file type is as well as what to set the EDI Status to.

File types and and Statuses Defined:

No EDI Sent

  • 0,Not Yet Transmitted

    ​

Order Acknowledgement:

  • 99,Resend Order Acknowledgment

  • 100,Order Acknowledgment Sent

  • 110,OrderAckFailed

  • 119,PO Canceled
    ​
    ​

Pre-Delivery (894):

  • 199,Resend Pre-Delivery

  • 200,Pre-Delivery Sent

  • 201,Pre-Delivery Changed

  • 210,Pre-Delivery Failed
    ​
    ​

Advanced Shipment Notice (856):

  • 249,Resend ASN

  • 250,ASN Sent

  • 252,Resend TransferPortalASN

  • 253,TransferPortalASN Sent

  • 254,ASN Changed

  • 260,ASN Failed
    ​
    ​

Post Delivery (810):

  • 280,Email Post-Delivery Sent

  • 299,Resend Post-Delivery

  • 300,Post-Delivery Sent

  • 310,Post-Delivery Failed
    ​
    ​

Payment Request (810 Payment Request)

  • 399,Resend Payment Request

  • 400,Payment Request Sent

  • 410,Payment Request Failed
    ​
    ​

ACH

  • 500,ACH Push-Pay

  • 600,PayLink Sent

  • 610,PayLink Failed
    ​
    ​

Do not Transmit any EDI:

  • 900,No Auto Transmission

  • 1000,Never Send

Distributor steps for moving invoices off a Loaded load sheet in Encompass via Route Reconciliation, and when to use Off Load, Not Delivered or Re-deliver. Needs InvoiceEditLoaded and LoadSheetEdit; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

The Load Sheet holding invoices to be moved must be in Loaded status.

Those moving invoices will need the InvoiceEdit, InvoiceEditLoaded, and LoadSheetEdit permissions.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Move an Invoice on a Loaded Load Sheet

  1. Navigate to the Load Sheets table
    ​
    ​

  2. Click on the Return link for the Load Sheet currently holding the invoices that need to be moved
    ​

  3. Within Route Reconciliation, go to the Invoices tab
    ​
    ​

  4. Select the invoices that need to be moved
    ​
    ​

  5. Click the Move button at the top of the screen
    ​
    ​

  6. Select from Off Load, Not Delivered, or Re-deliver
    ​
    ​

  7. Select the destination Load Sheet to complete the move
    ​
    ​

  8. Click to view the invoice as desired
    ​
    ​

  9. For instances of moving an invoice using the Re-deliver option, be sure to navigate to the Re-deliver tab after the invoice move is completed
    ​
    ​

  10. On the Re-deliver tab, select a printer and re-print related pallet tags to ensure inventory also moves to the new load sheet

Fields And Definitions

The various move options interact with related inventory differently.

Inventory does not move with invoice:

Move Not-Delivered

  • Can select any status load sheet to move the invoice to

  • Does not bring the loaded inventory with the moved invoice, the product will stay in the original route bin

  • Invoice has to be re-palletized on the new load sheet and re-picked

  • When to use: when moving an Invoice from one load sheet to another, with no intention of moving the related pallets onto another truck

  • What is unique about this option: leaves product in the route bin to be reconciled during truck return

Inventory does move with invoice:

Move Off-Load

  • Can select any load sheets in the Loaded status to move the invoice to; New status load sheets are also available if the route bins match

  • Brings inventory and pallet record with moved invoice, product goes to the new route bin

  • Invoice does not have to be re-palletized or re-picked

  • When to use: when moving an invoice from one loaded load sheet to another loaded load sheet, or when you don't need to print a new pallet tag or unload the inventory from its destination route bin

  • What is unique about this option: leaves pallets in loaded status, and will not require a new pallet tag

Move Re-deliver

  • Can select any load sheets in the New status to move the invoice to

  • Brings inventory with the invoice, but creates a new pallet record tied to the new load sheet (for more accurate pallet labeling, if needed)

  • Product goes to the new route bin once a new pallet tag is printed from the original load sheet's Route Reconciliation Redeliver tab

  • When to use: When moving an invoice from a loaded load sheet to a new load sheet sharing the same route bin, with intention to re-load related pallets later

  • What is unique about this option: allows a user to move an invoice between two routes that share the same route bin, with better control of when the related inventory is loaded

Best Practices

Based on the impact to inventory that comess with each invoice move option, consider which option best fits common situations for your business. Determine a standard practice for each situation, and communicate it with your team.

16990520:
Distributor overview of Segment Ranking (Industry Volume) in Encompass: how customers get A/B/C or B-U-D ranks by segment volume, set via the Segments table and settings 149 and 176. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • System Setting 149 determines how your rankings are set. Options are B-U-D, A-B-C, and A-B-C-D
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 176 determines whether Industry Volume is calculated by the system (using a Weekly Scheduled Task) or if it is an editable field on the Customer table that users can set

Steps

Screenshot

  • System Setting 149 determines how your rankings are set. Options are B-U-D, A-B-C, and A-B-C-D
    ​
    ​

  • System Setting 176 determines whether Industry Volume is calculated by the system (using a Weekly Scheduled Task) or if it is an editable field on the Customer table that users can set
    ​
    ​
    ​

The Segments Table determines how Segments are set in the system.
​
​

  • Segments are often similar to Product Types, but can be set separately. Each Brand is associated with a different Segment.
    ​
    ​

  • When Include in Overall Ind Volume Ranking is set to True, Brands in the Segment will be used to determine a customer's Industry Volume ranking. If this is set to False, this Segment will not be used for Ranking. For example: You may want only your main Supplier(s) to be used for ranking, so you would create a Segment of only that Supplier's brands and only set that Segment to Include in Overall Ind Volume Ranking = True. Typically miscellaneous products, dunnage, etc. are all put into a Segment where this field is False.
    ​
    ​

  • The Rank Byfield determines how Customers are grouped to be ranked. This can be for All Locations, within a single Location, or by Territory
    ​
    ​
    ​

Encompass has two possible Rank By methods for each Segment:
​
​

  • Percentage of Volume: Ranks Customers according to how much of the total volume sold they were responsible for. Example: If you have 10 customers and you rank the top 20% as A customers and a single customer is responsible for 20% of the total volume done, then that customer would be your only A customer. If two customers together did 20% of the total volume, then they would both be A customers.
    ​
    ​

  • Percentage of Customers: Puts a specific percentage of Customers in each tier. Example: If you have 10 customers and are ranking the top 20% as A customers, the system will rank the top two Customers by Segment volume as your A customers, regardless of what that volume was.
    ​
    ​
    ​

The Ranking Historical Period field determines the historical period over which the system looks at volume to determine ranking. Example: If this field is set to 12 months, then when the weekly scheduled task will run a report looking at 12 months of data to determine new rankings. Because of this, the shorter the period, the more impact recent data will have on these rankings.
​
​
​

On-Premise A Percentage determines what percentage of Customers (as determined by the Rank By method) are included in the top tier for On-Premise Customers
​
​

On-Premise B Percentage determines what percentage of the remaining Customers (as determined by the Rank By method) are included in the middle tier for On-Premise Customers
​

  • All other Customers will be considered in the lowest tier.

Off-Premise A Percentage determines what percentage of Customers (as determined by the Rank By method) are included in the top tier for Off-Premise Customers
​
​

Off-Premise B Percentage determines what percentage of the remaining Customers (as determined by the Rank By method) are included in the middle tier for Off-Premise Customers

  • All other Customers will be considered in the lowest tier.

Notes:

Segment Ranking will respect Product Groups and Product Areas. So, only Customers authorized to buy a specific segment will be included in its ranking.

To review Segment Ranking in one place, please use the Segment Ranking (Industry Volume) link which can be accessed from Universal Search. This dashboard provides an overview of the current segment ranking setup and allows users to report on their segment ranking based on current settings.

Fields And Definitions

  • Segment Ranking and Industry Volume are synonymous in Encompass

Distillery/winery explanation of how barrel cost is spread to aging liquid at each barrel fill in Encompass based on the Equipment Type's Planned Fill Count, with an example. Requires v24.01+.

Pre-Conditions

Equipment Type:

  • Is Barrel = True

  • Is Portable = True

  • Product = NOT NULL (set as non-inventory barrel product)

Steps

Click here for documentation with screenshots.

How to Use:

  1. The Barrel Cost is established at the time of purchasing the barrel using either the ‘Buy Empty Barrels’ or ‘Buy Filled Barrels’ function

  2. The Barrel Cost is stored on the Barrel Attributes record for each Barrel Equipment. After buying a barrel, click on the Barrel Name hyperlink to open the Barrel Equipment record, where you will see the associated Barrel Attributes subtable.

  3. Barrel Cost is disbursed to the aging liquid at the time of the barrel fill
    -The amount of barrel cost to disburse on each fill is determined by dividing Planned Fill Count by the Barrel Cost
    -So in this example:
    4/$100 = $25 of barrel cost will be disbursed over 4 barrel fill
    -Barrel Cost Disbursement will end once Planned Fill Count = Fill Count. All subsequent barrel fills will not include barrel cost

  4. Example:
    -Fill Barrel 304 with 53 gallons of ‘Krill Barrel Proofed Rum’ that is valued at an Extended Cost of $106.57
    -Barrel 304 now shows as ‘Filled’ in the BMC
    -Click on the barrel name in the BMC to access the Equipment and Barrel Attributes records
    -See that the barrel shows as ‘Filled’ with Fill Count = 1
    -Liquid Cost in Barrel = Value of liquid + Barrel Cost Disbursement
    $106.57 + $25.00 = $131.57
    -The ‘Liquid Cost in Barrel’ is the value that will be passed to the remaining liquid in the barrel at the time of the barrel dump

Distributor guide to the End of Day tab on the Daily/Monthly Best Practices dashboard in Encompass: see what's left before running Invoice, AR, AP and Financial Close. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Navigating Daily/Monthly Best Practices

1. Using the Universal Search Bar, navigate to the Daily/Monthly Best Practices Dashboard

2. The End of Day tab of this Dashboard serves as an overview of information relevant to each End of Day process (Invoice Close, Accounts Receivable Close, Accounts Payable Close, and Financial Close)

3. Start by selecting a Company from the Company dropdown menu, and the date that you are going to close

4. Click the arrow to reset the data for the Company and date selected

5. Clicking Load Sheets to Balance will redirect you to Returned Load Sheets dated on or before the date selected

6. Back in Daily/Monthly Best Practices, click Enter Mail In Load Sheets if you need to add payments to Balance the Returned Load Sheets from the previous step

7. Once you have Balanced Load Sheets, you are ready to run Invoice Close

8. Clicking Receipts Without Deposits will direct you to Balanced Invoices dated on or before the date selected that have not been added to a Deposit

9. Navigate to the Deposits Table to add or edit Deposits

10. Once you have added or edited Deposits, you are ready to run Accounts Receivable Close

11. Clicking Vendor Purchases to Confirm will direct you to Received Purchases dated on or before the date selected

12. Confirm Purchases that are Received

13. Once you have confirmed Purchases, you are ready to run Accounts Payable Close

14. Clicking Enter Manual Journal Entries will direct you to the Journal Entries Table

15. You can then add or edit Journal Entries

16. Once you have added or edited Journal Entries, you are ready to run Financial Close

17. Clicking End of Day will direct you to the End of Day Dashboard where you can close each period

Fields And Definitions

Invoice Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Invoices through. In other words, Balanced Load Sheets and Invoices dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Accounts Receivable Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Accounts Receivable through. In other words, Balanced Deposits dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Accounts Payable Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Accounts Payable through. In other words, Confirmed Purchases dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Financial Close - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Financials through. In other words, Balanced Journal Entries dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Best Practices

  • Run Invoice Close, Accounts Receivable Close, and Accounts Payable Close on a daily basis or as frequently as possible.

Fields And Definitions

The various move options interact with related inventory differently. If a load sheet has been palletized by the time an invoice is being moved, the related pallets and inventory also need to be addressed during the move. Understanding the different options is particularly important if the invoice being moved is on a multi-customer pallet.

Inventory does not move with invoice:

Delete Palletization and Re-pick the invoice

  • This option will move only the invoice you want to move, without touching the other invoices on the pallet

  • The original pallet is reduced by the amount of cases on the invoice that moved

  • The moved invoice is now on the destination load sheet, but needs to be re-palletized

Inventory does move with invoice:

Move All Related Invoices and Loaded Products to a different Load Sheet

  • Because a pallet has already been generated with multiple invoices on it, the pallet can only be moved in its current status if all related invoices move with it

Best Practices

Based on the impact to inventory that comess with each invoice move option, consider which option best fits common situations for your business. Determine a standard practice for each situation, and communicate it with your team.

Distributor reference for how each invoice charge calculation method in Encompass computes tax, split-case bottle charges, deposits, fuel surcharges and per-gallon or proof-gallon charges. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

Tax Based Calculation Methods:
​
​

1,1) Percentage of Invoice Total (Tax);

  • InvoiceTrans.NumUnits * InvoiceTrans.UnitPrice

6,6) Percentage of Invoice Total Display In-Line Only;

  • InvoiceTrans.NumUnits * InvoiceTrans.UnitPrice

7,7) Split Case Percentage of Invoice Total (Tax);

  • CASE WHEN Products.WholesaleUnitsPerCase > 1 THEN

  • CASE WHEN CAST(InvoiceTrans.NumUnits AS signed) % Products.WholesaleUnitsPerCase <> 0 THEN Round((InvoiceTrans.NumUnits * InvoiceTrans.UnitPrice), 2)

  • ELSE 0 END

  • ELSE

  • CASE WHEN 1 * (InvoiceTrans.NumUnits % 1) <> 0 THEN Round((InvoiceTrans.NumUnits * InvoiceTrans.UnitPrice), 2)

  • ELSE 0 END

  • END

8,8) Per Gallon (Volume Tax);

  • (InvoiceTrans.NumUnits * Products.Ounces / Products.WholesaleUnitsPerCase) / 128

Distributor setup for Objective Statuses in Encompass: add custom survey statuses like Approval Pending, set prompts, and restrict who can set a status by permission. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

Objective Statuses
​
​

Objective Status is a subtable of the Objectives table. When a new Objective is created, three default statuses of Assigned, Failed to Complete, and Completed are created. Additional statuses can be added to Objectives to create different workflows of surveys. For example, an Approval Pending status can be added to require a survey to be approved by a manager before being set to Completed.

​
​Add New Objective Status
​
​

1. Navigate to the Objectives table and select the Objective to edit.
​
2. Click 'View' on the Objective Status subtable.
​
3. Click 'Add Objective Status'
​
4. Select the desired Status.
​
​

Note: If the status desired does not exist in the drop-down, a new status can be created on the Task Status table.
​
5. Select the Assign To Group based on which group of users the survey will be assigned to.
​
6. Select the User Level.
​
7. Click 'Add Record'.

​
​Set Permissions on Objective Statuses
​
​

Setting Permissions on Objective Statuses prevents users without the selected permission from being able to put a task in that status. This is beneficial for approval workflows such as Asset Manager, Sign Shop, and more. If a user does not have the permission set on the Objective Status, it will not display as a status option to select.
​
1. Navigate to the Objectives table and select the Objective to edit.
​
2. In the Objective Status subtable, click the arrow next to the status.
​
3. Edit the Permission field and select the permission required to set a task to this status.
​
4. Click 'Save Changes'

Fields And Definitions

  • Objective Status* - A Task Status that is linked to a specific Objective.
    ​
    ​

  • User Level* - determines whether a task in this status will be assigned to the User (for example the Sales Rep), their Manager, or their Manager's Manager.
    ​
    ​

  • Assign To Group - The Group of Users the Survey Task will be assigned to.
    ​
    ​

  • Sequence* - The order the Objective Statuses will be listed at the end of the survey.
    ​
    ​

  • Prompt Task* - Prompts the Assigned User when accessing a specific area.
    ​
    ​-Do Not Prompt - User will not be prompted.
    ​
    ​-Service Event Start - User will be prompted to take the survey when selecting the customer from My Day on Encompass Mobile (This status will force the user to complete the survey before moving forward with other tasks. This does not apply to Assignment surveys such as DOT surveys).
    ​
    ​-Service Event End - User will be prompted to take the survey when backing out of the customer event.
    ​
    ​-Invoice Total - User will be prompted to take the survey when backing out of the Invoice Edit screen to the Invoice Total screen.
    ​
    ​-Add New Product - User will be prompted to take the survey when adding a new product to an invoice.
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • Deadline Required - When set to True, a calendar selection displays at the end of the survey to select a Deadline (Ex. Deadline for Sign Shop Request to be completed).
    ​

  • Permission - Users must have the selected permission to be able to move a task to that Objective Status.

    ​

  • Min/Max Points - Only displays the Objective Status as an option to select when survey answers meet the point requirements.

    ​

    ​

Distillery steps for spreading barrel cost to aging spirits at barrel fill in Encompass using the Planned Fill Count on the barrel Equipment Type. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

Equipment Type:

  • Is Barrel = True

  • Is Portable = True

  • Product = NOT NULL (set as non-inventory barrel product)

  • Planned Fill Count - set to the desired number of fills for all Equipment under this Equipment Type. This will be used to disburse the barrel cost to the liquid in the barrel at the time of the barrel fill.

Steps

Click here for documentation with screenshots.
​
​

How to Use:

  1. The Barrel Cost is established at the time of purchasing the barrel using either the ‘Buy Empty Barrels’ or ‘Buy Filled Barrels’ function
    ​

  2. The Barrel Cost is stored on the Barrel Attributes record for each Barrel Equipment. After buying a barrel, click on the Barrel Name hyperlink to open the Barrel Equipment record, where you will see the associated Barrel Attributes subtable.
    ​
    ​

  3. Barrel Cost is disbursed to the aging liquid at the time of the barrel fill
    ​
    -The amount of barrel cost to disburse on each fill is determined by dividing Planned Fill Count by the Barrel Cost
    ​
    -In this example:
    4/$100 = $25 of barrel cost will be disbursed over 4 barrel fill
    ​
    -Barrel Cost Disbursement will end once Planned Fill Count = Fill Count. All subsequent barrel fills will not include barrel cost
    ​
    ​

  4. Example:
    ​
    -Fill Barrel 304 with 53 gallons of ‘Krill Barrel Proofed Rum’ that is valued at an Extended Cost of $106.57
    ​
    -Barrel 304 now shows as ‘Filled’ in the BMC
    ​
    -Click on the barrel name in the BMC to access the Equipment and Barrel Attributes records
    ​
    -See that the barrel shows as ‘Filled’ with Fill Count = 1
    ​
    -Liquid Cost in Barrel = Value of liquid + Barrel Cost Disbursement
    $106.57 + $25.00 = $131.57
    ​
    -The ‘Liquid Cost in Barrel’ is the value that will be passed to the remaining liquid in the barrel at the time of the barrel dump
16990586:
Distributor setup for tracking keg deposits in Encompass: empty keg products and account maps so deposits clear when kegs are bought, sold, picked up and returned, incl. third-party kegs. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

Setup

1. Products
​
​

a) add empty keg products for each supplier (even if 3rd party) and size
​
b) add non-inventory product for any 3rd party keg suppliers
​
​
​

2. Account Mapping
​
​

a) Inventory Asset Account Maps
​
i. at a minimum, two Inventory Asset Account Maps are needed to clear the deposit balance at the end of this work flow
​
ii. the Deposit Account on the first map (bringing in a full keg fro supplier) should be the same Account that is set on the Inventory Asset Account on the 2nd map (sending an empty keg shell back to supplier).
​
iii. specify either a Product Type or Product on the map so the correct map is hit when kegs come in and out of inventory

b) Income Account Maps
​
i. at a minimum, two Income Account Maps are needed to clear the deposit balance when picking up kegs from your customer
​
ii. the Deposit Income Account and Deposit Cogs Sold Account for the first map (delivering a full keg to customer) should match the Income Account and COGS Account for the second map (picking up an empty keg shell from the customer)

c) Expense Account Maps (for 3rd party keg providers)
​
i. set the product type for the 3rd party keg
​
ii. set the 3rd party keg deposit account

Best Practices

The Entire Work Flow:
​
​

1. Bring kegs into inventory via a Purchase (use the full keg product)

a) FOB = value of the liquid

b) Deposit = value of the keg shell

2. Sell kegs to customer (use the full keg product)

a) Income = value of the liquid

b) Deposit = value of the keg shell

3. Pickup kegs from customer (use the empty keg product)

a) Income = value of the keg shell

4. Return kegs to supplier (use the empty keg product)

a) FOB = value of the keg shell

Third Party Keg Supplier
​
​

1. On the original purchase found in step 1 above:

a) add a Purchase Trans using the non-inventory product for the 3rd party keg supplier

b) set the number of units for the Purchase Trans to be opposite that of the kegs coming in that are owned by the 3rd party keg supplier (negative num units)

c) FOB for the Purchase Trans should be the same amount as the Deposit cost found on the original Purchase Trans for the full kegs coming from the brewer

i. By doing this, the AP for the brewer will be correct, and the deposit balance in the 3rd party keg supplier expense account should match the bill from the 3rd party keg supplier when received.
​
​

Screenshot

​
2. On the second purchase found in step 4 above:

a) use the Vendor for the relevant third party keg supplier instead of the brewer

b) the first Purchase Trans will clear the empty keg Product from your inventory (negative num units)

c) add a second Purchase Trans using the non-inventory product for the third party keg supplier (positive num units)

d) set the number of units for the second Purchase Trans to be opposite that of the kegs returning to the third party keg supplier

e) FOB for the first and second Purchase Trans should be the same amount as the Deposit cost found on the original Purchase Trans for the full kegs coming from the brewer

i. This will be a $0.00 purchase because the FOB for the first Purchase Trans will alleviate inventory, and the second Purchase Trans will alleviate the deposit cost from the original Purchase
​
​

Distributor setup and workflow for keg deposits in Encompass: empty keg products, inventory/income/expense account maps, and handling third-party keg supplier deposits on purchases. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

Setup

1. Products

a) add empty keg products for each supplier (even if 3rd party) and size

b) add non-inventory product for any 3rd party keg suppliers

2. Account Mapping

a) Inventory Asset Account Maps

i. at a minimum, two Inventory Asset Account Maps are needed to clear the deposit balance at the end of this work flow

ii. the Deposit Account on the first map (bringing in a full keg fro supplier) should be the same Account that is set on the Inventory Asset Account on the 2nd map (sending an empty keg shell back to supplier).

iii. specify either a Product Type or Product on the map so the correct map is hit when kegs come in and out of inventory

b) Income Account Maps

i. at a minimum, two Income Account Maps are needed to clear the deposit balance when picking up kegs from your customer

ii. the Deposit Income Account and Deposit Cogs Sold Account for the first map (delivering a full keg to customer) should match the Income Account and COGS Account for the second map (picking up an empty keg shell from the customer)

c) Expense Account Maps (for 3rd party keg providers)

i. set the product type for the 3rd party keg

ii. set the 3rd party keg deposit account

Best Practices

The Entire Work Flow:

1. Bring kegs into inventory via a Purchase (use the full keg product)

a) FOB = value of the liquid

b) Deposit = value of the keg shell

2. Sell kegs to customer (use the full keg product)

a) Income = value of the liquid

b) Deposit = value of the keg shell

3. Pickup kegs from customer (use the empty keg product)

a) Income = value of the keg shell

4. Return kegs to supplier (use the empty keg product)

a) FOB = value of the keg shell

Third Party Keg Supplier

1. On the original purchase found in step 1 above:

a) add a Purchase Trans using the non-inventory product for the 3rd party keg supplier

b) set the number of units for the Purchase Trans to be opposite that of the kegs coming in that are owned by the 3rd party keg supplier (negative num units)

c) FOB for the Purchase Trans should be the same amount as the Deposit cost found on the original Purchase Trans for the full kegs coming from the brewer

i. By doing this, the AP for the brewer will be correct, and the deposit balance in the 3rd party keg supplier expense account should match the bill from the 3rd party keg supplier when received.

Screenshot

2. On the second purchase found in step 4 above:

a) use the Vendor for the relevant third party keg supplier instead of the brewer

b) the first Purchase Trans will clear the empty keg Product from your inventory (negative num units)

c) add a second Purchase Trans using the non-inventory product for the third party keg supplier (positive num units)

d) set the number of units for the second Purchase Trans to be opposite that of the kegs returning to the third party keg supplier

e) FOB for the first and second Purchase Trans should be the same amount as the Deposit cost found on the original Purchase Trans for the full kegs coming from the brewer

i. This will be a $0.00 purchase because the FOB for the first Purchase Trans will alleviate inventory, and the second Purchase Trans will alleviate the deposit cost from the original Purchase

16990612:
Distributor reference for the SalesHistoryEDBL import routine in Encompass to import verified sales history or supplier billbacks; required fields and cautions. Requires v23.01+; contact support first.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Minimum Requirements of Report or spreadsheet used to import:

  • Customer ID
    ​

  • Date (Invoices will use Routing method 1)
    ​

  • Product ID
    ​

  • Num Units
    ​

  • Location = Numeric LocationID
    ​
    ​

Additional Optional Fields:

  • Product Name (Only if overriding non-inventory Product Name)

  • Full Price (Only required if current pricing structure cannot be used)

  • PromoOverridden = 1 (Used to lock in specific pricing if current pricing structure cannot be used)

  • Routing Method (How the invoice will be routed)

  • Route Number or RouteID (Used to specify a specific route)

  • Invoice ID, Invoice Num, or PONum (Used to match and update an existing invoice)

Steps

System Behavior:

  • Will import verified Invoice(s) on the date(s) provided. It will affect inventory.

  • If you have more than one Invoice EDBL Routine, an ImportGroupID must be used. Otherwise, the 2nd routine will zero any invoices from the 1st routine, for any dates that exist on the 2nd routine.

  • Reimports after importing AR: Likely will have to rerun AR import. AR is deleted on reimport of invoices for a given day

  • After importing Sales Run Inventories Import to reverse sales history

  • Pricing - At a minimum map EXTPrice, numUnits, participation and discount

  • Reimport - Close the day to verify all Invoice Payments. Any not verified could be deleted. If you have to export/reimport grab Invoice IDs for payment and invoice, AR Account ID, Customer ID
    ​
    ​

Recommendations:

  • Deposit: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • DepositID: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • Discount: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • ImportGroupID: If not mapped, it is recommended to set the default value to 1. However, it is recommended to explicitly map it for better control.

  • LaidInCost: It is recommended to include this field; otherwise, historical invoices may lack costing information.

  • LocationID or LocationID_Translation: It is necessary to have an actual Location record existing. If only one location is used, it is recommended to statically map it. If neither is provided, LocationID defaults to Customer.Location. This mapping is recommended.

  • Participation: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • Pricing: For UnitPrice, FullPrice, ExtPrice, and Discount, it is possible to leave a value of 0, but there aren't many use cases for that. It is recommended to fill in at least 2 out of 3 fields, and it is sufficient to provide just one of them. Unit Price is preferred over Ext Price; it is not necessary to provide both.

Fields And Definitions

Sales History EDBL:

  • Start in Verified Status and cannot be deleted/edited without a new import or Developer permission

  • Do NOT run recalculation to split invoices OR to calculate pricing

  • Do NOT affect inventory without using an Inventory Adjustment
    ​
    ​

  • Note: This will clear all sales for the date range by default as this EDBL is assuming you will be importing the full data set for this date range. Clear all sales for date range must be explicitly mapped to false for all sales to not be cleared. Please contact support before running an InvoiceEDBL.

​Best used for:

  • Supplier Billbacks

  • Sales History (Go-Live)

Best Practices

Import routines are an incredibly powerful tool and if used incorrectly, can affect a lot of data. Test thoroughly on small data sets before importing.

If you are running into setup issues or have questions, reach out to Encompass Support.

Do you have a complex process that consists of a report and import routines that you do not want to set up? Contact our professional services to team to assist.

16990621:
What to do when PayLink charged the wrong customer because bank info was entered on the wrong AR Account: refund via credit invoice, fix the bank details, resend payment requests, and clear the open credit.

Minimum Version Required: 23.08

Pre-Conditions

  • Incorrect Banking information filled out on AR Account in Encompass
    ​
    ​

  • Invoices paid by incorrect bank account through paylink
    ​
    ​

  • Auto-send credits must be enabled on the paylink Onboarding & Settings dashboard

Steps

How to credit the customer who was charged incorrectly:
​
​

  1. Create an invoice for the customer that was incorrectly charged and needs to be credited back (If a customer does not exist, please create a customer)
    ​
    ​

  2. Add a Non-Inventory Product of your choosing to the invoice
    ​
    ​

  3. Set the Purchase Quantity to -1
    ​
    ​

  4. Set the price of the product to the total amount that needs to be credited
    ​
    ​

  5. Click Save Changes
    ​
    ​

  6. Load, Return, and Balance the load sheet
    ​
    ​

Following these steps will request a payment through paylink to pay the customer that was incorrectly charged.
​
​

Note: Auto-send credits must be enabled on the paylink Onboarding & Settings dashboard.
​
​

Note: The customers 'AR Accounts' Credit Term that the credit is being sent to, must be on a paylink Auto type credit term.


How to update Bank Information on an AR Account:

  1. Go to the AR Accounts Table
    ​
    ​

  2. Filter to the AR Account with incorrect information
    ​
    ​

  3. Open the AR Account Record
    ​
    ​

  4. Hover over the EFT Bank Routing Num and/or Bank Account Number fields
    ​
    ​

  5. Click the edit pencil
    ​
    ​

  6. Update information
    ​
    ​

  7. Click save changes
    ​
    ​

Following these steps will ensure all payments going forward are for the correct bank account.
​
​
​

How to resend the invoices to the correct customer:

  1. Find the invoices that were incorrectly paid
    ​
    ​

  2. Unapply all the incorrect payments from the original invoices
    ​
    ​

  3. Update the EDI Status on the invoices that need to be paid to 'Resend Payment Request' (For more information on how to update EDI Status, please see our help resource on how to update EDI Status)
    ​
    ​

Note: Do NOT complete the above steps until the bank information has been updated on the AR Account to the correct information.
​
​

Following these steps will re-request payment on the original invoices.
​
​
​

How to remove the open credit caused by the incorrect payments on the incorrect customer:

  1. Create an invoice for the customer that had its invoices incorrectly paid by another customer's account.
    ​
    ​

  2. Add a Non-Inventory Product of your choosing to the invoice
    ​
    ​

  3. Set the Purchase Quantity to 1
    ​
    ​

  4. Set the price of the product to the total amount that needs to be corrected that was incorrectly paid
    ​
    ​

  5. Click Save Changes
    ​
    ​

  6. Click Apply Payments
    ​
    ​

  7. Apply this invoice to all the incorrect payments (The Open balance on the invoice should be 0 after payment application)
    ​
    ​

  8. Load, Return, and Balance the load sheet
    ​
    ​

Note: Please make sure to apply the payments before balancing the load sheet so we do not credit the customer back the money incorrectly.
​
​

Following these steps will remove the incorrectly received payments that were from a different customer.

Fields And Definitions

  • Non-Inventory Product: A product that does not impact inventory and usually has a product type with allow manual price entry set to true
    ​
    ​

  • EDI Status: A field that shows how an invoice has been sent through EDI, and can be editted to resend EDI
    ​
    ​

  • AR Account: Stores all AR information and banking information

Best Practices

  • If you are manully entering bank information, always double check to ensure you entered the correct information on the correct account
    ​
    ​

  • Customers can fill out their own banking information by going through the sign up for paylink process which can reduce errors and help reduce effort in setting up and managing banking information

Producer reference for the Spirits 'Distillation' Recipe Type: Production Stage Types (Stage Class = Spirits), Production Cut Types (low wines, heads, hearts, tails) and Byproducts Management. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Pre-Conditions

  • The ‘Distillation’ Recipe Type should be used by spirits producers who are 'birthing' spirits through the act of distillation.
    ​
    ​

  • Proof gallons produced through Distillation-type Production Orders are reported on the TTB DRO Production Report.

Steps

Click here for documentation with screenshots.
​
​

Pre-Recipe Build Setup:
​
​

Production Stage Types:

The Production Stage Types Table is used to define the different types of distillation stages used at your facility. Distillation Recipes require the use of Production Stage Types with Stage Class = Spirits. Stage Class = Spirits enforces the collection of proof data when processing the PdO. The ‘Stage Type’ dropdown in Recipe Management will be auto-filtered down to only those Production Stage Types with Stage Class = Spirits.
​
​
​

Production Cut Types:

The Production Cut Types Table is used to define the types of distillation cuts you will be producing. Set up one record for each of the following cut types:

  • Low Wines

  • Heads

  • Hearts

  • Tails
    ​
    ​
    ​

Production Stage Types Cut Types:
​
​

The Production Stage Types Cut Types Table is a subtable of Production Cut Types that is used to link Production Stage Types to a Product Type that will be used to provide a list of possible Products when setting up distillation cuts in Distillation type Recipes. Here is the common setup that will be used:
​
​

This setup will be referenced again when discussing how to set up distillation cuts when building a Distillation Recipe.

Recipe Setup & Configuration:

​

  • Distillation Recipes require the use of Production Stage Types with Stage Class = Spirits.
    ​

Distributor guide to the beta Fusion report view in Encompass: filter, group, add columns, graphs and comparisons on reports without FusionEdit permission, and turn the beta on or off. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Use the Updated Report View

This Improved Report View interface allows end users to manipulate pre-built reports. Easily filter and group data, add and remove predefined columns, adjust graph views, drill down, and more without needing FusionEdit permissions.

1. The new Report View beta is now available in versions 23.12 and above. To turn on Beta, click the "Enable Beta" option in the top right header next to the universal search bar.

2. The name of the report is displayed in the page header. Click "Save" to save any changes to an existing report if you are already the owner. “Save as new report” will save a new copy of the report.

3. If there is a cache on the report, refresh the data by clicking the “Refresh” link. Click the calculator icon to open the Calculator tool.

4. Quick Edit Tabs are displayed to the left of the report. Click on these tabs to open the Quick Edit panel.

5. The data and organization of the report can be managed in the Layout tab. Organize how the report data is grouped under Groupings, select which values to calculate on the report under Metrics, and select a Comparison to compare metrics across multiple columns.

6. Click the “Add” section to add a new grouping or metric. Drag groupings down to create sub groups on the report.

7. On the Filters tab, add or adjust filters and time periods that are applied to the report. Click “Add another time period” or “Add more filters” to add additional filters from the available list

8. A graph can be added to the top of the report from the “Graph” tab to visualize the data. Select a graph type, manage graph settings, and set the color theme from this tab.

9. Adjust any display settings for the full report from the Settings tab. This can include adding column totals to your report such as Unit Difference or Percentage Difference, displaying a total row, changing the format, or setting a color theme.

10. The “Details” tab displays important information about the report including the owner, cache times, all applied filters on the report data, and table sync information.

11. Users with Fusion Edit permission will also see the Fusion Edit option at the bottom of the panel. Clicking this will take you into the Fusion Edit screen to edit the data source behind this report.

12. Click the “Manage beta” option in the header at any time to submit your feedback on the new design or revert back to the original Fusion View display.
