Distributor steps in Encompass for building a survey objective: sections, questions, data types, repeat by brand/product and ask-if logic, plus how reps save partial answers in Mobile. Requires v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Set up an Objective
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Objectives table.
​
2. Click the Add Objectives button.
​
3. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the Objective form. See Fields & Definitions.
​
4. Click the Add Survey Section button.
​
5. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the Survey Section form.
​
6. Then, click the ‘+’ button.
​
7. Click the Add Survey Questions button.
​
8. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the Add Survey Question form. Repeat as needed until all questions are entered.
​
9. When all Objective information, Survey Sections, Section Values, and Survey Questions are complete, click the Save Changes button.
​
8. Create an Objective Schedule, Activity Objective, or Assignment Objective if the survey needs to be automatically assigned.

Fields And Definitions

  • Survey - Set of questions to obtain data
    ​
    ​

  • Objective - The overall record that holds the Survey Questions, Objective Statuses, Objective Schedules, etc.
    ​
    1. Objective Type - This field is typically only used for System Objectives or copies of System Objectives. These include additional functionality that is not included with a normal survey. Examples of these are the Asset Request and Display Surveys or DOT surveys. Leave this field blank unless you are specifically creating a survey that falls under the Objective Type.
    ​
    2. Delete Tasks After Days - This defaults at one (1) year and will only delete the tasks, does not delete Survey answers.
    ​
    3. Copy Answers to Details - This copies Survey answers to the task details tied to the survey. Typically this is set to True.
    ​
    4. Active - Status to tell if the Survey will be live or not.
    ​
    5. New Task Status - What status the Survey will be in when first assigned.
    ​
    6. After Deadline Task Status - The status the system will switch the Survey to if it is not taken within the time frame
    ​
    7. Mobile Item - Typically used for System Objectives. Ties the survey to a button/Mobile Item in Encompass Mobile. Allows users to tap a button and be taken to the survey. Mobile Items are typically used in combination with an Objective Type. Leave this field blank unless you are creating a survey with this intended functionality.
    ​
    8. Customer ID Required - If a Survey will need to be taken at customer accounts. This should be set to yes unless taking a survey that is not customer-specific such as a DOT survey.
    ​
    ​

  • Survey Section - This is the container that defines a set of survey questions.
    ​
    ​    1. Sequence - Allows you to organize questions in a set numerical order.
    ​
    2. Survey Section - Creates multiple sections of questions. Allows for more organization of longer surveys or surveys that require selecting multiple products or brands.
    ​
    3. Section Type - Does not change the functionality of the survey. This is for categorization for Reporting purposes.
    ​
    4. Repeat Questions - Choose if needed to repeat questions for either Brand or Products. Links the Brand or Products to the task.
    ​
    5. Last Answer Auto Populate - Populates the last collected answer for the customer for all questions in the section. The answer can still be edited.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Section Values - Allows for repeating the questions in the survey section multiple times for different categories.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Survey Questions - The questions users will answer.
    ​
    ​    1. Sequence - The order in which the questions will be displayed. Drag and drop questions to reorder using the arrows.
    ​
    2. Question - The text displayed in the survey as the Question.
    ​
    3. Data Types - Used to collect different types of data. See Survey Question Data Types.
    ​
    4. Required - Required to complete the Survey. The question must be answered to complete.
    ​
    5. Remember - Populates the answer from the previous answer on a question by question basis instead of the entire section.
    ​
    6. Repeat - Use if you want the question to repeat for multiple Brands or Products.
    ​
    7. Ask if Survey Question - When set, the question will only be asked if the Ask If Questions answer meets the following:
    ​
    - Ask If Operator - Defines whether the answer to a question should be greater than, less than, equal to, etc.
    ​
    - Ask If Value - In combination with the Ask If Operator, how the Ask If Question needs to be answered to display the question.
    ​
    ​

  • Objective Status - Status of the task determining task flow. Additional statuses can be created for use on the Task Status table. See Objective Statuses.
    ​
    ​

  • Task - Individual instances of surveys being assigned/completed.

Best Practices

  • Before creating a Survey, have the questions, answers, and what information is needed already collected.
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • Set up surveys to be assigned automatically. Choose the option that meets your survey needs.
    ​
    ​Objective Schedules
    ​
    ​Assignment Objectives
    ​
    ​Activity Objectives

​
When the Repeat for Multiple Brands or Products setting is active, mobile users have the ability to select multiple products or brands at the start of a survey.
​
​

To enable:

  • Toggle on "Select multiple..." at the top of the product or brand selection list.
    ​
    ​

  • Choose all desired products or brands at the same time.

Invite to dsdlink

Distributors can invite Customers Users to dsdlink through the Customers Users table in Encompass. By doing this, the user will automatically have an account created through dsdlink and will be linked with their business and the distributorship.

All templates:

Distributor steps for adding, editing or deleting custom fields on an Encompass table with Table Map: set alias, data type, permissions and drop-down values. Deleting a field erases its data. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Update Custom Fields

1. Navigate to the Table Map, using Universal Search.
​
2. Search for the table that needs to be updated using the search.
​
3. Click "Map Table".
​
​4. Click "Edit".
​
5. To delete a field, click the "Delete Column" button at the bottom of the field.
​

  • Deleting a field does not fully remove the field until all changes in the Table Editor are saved, but once saved the table field and all data in it will be permanently deleted.
    ​
    ​

6. To edit an existing field, find the field in the editor and make any desired changes to the properties below.
​
7. To add a new field, Click the "Add Column" button at the top of the table column section, then fill in the column properties.
​
8. Click "Save Changes" at the top of the page to apply the changes to the table.

Fields And Definitions

  • Column Alias - This is the name that will display for the custom field. Anything that still says 'CustomField' is available to use.
    ​
    ​

  • Column Field - This is the system name for the custom field and cannot be changed.
    ​
    ​

  • Data Type - This determines the data type input the field will use. For custom fields, we recommend TextArea.
    ​
    ​

  • View Permission - This determines which permission is needed to view this field.
    ​
    ​

  • Edit Permission - This determines which permission is needed to edit this field.
    ​
    ​

  • Display by Default - Should this field display in the default view of the table? If so, set it to Yes.
    ​
    ​

  • Values - If the Custom Field should be a text field, leave this blank. If it should be a drop-down, enter the drop-down option to be created, followed by a semi-colon and the next option. Do not enter any spaces. Example: Bronze; Silver; Gold.
    ​
    ​

  • Reference Table - Specify if the table will reference a field in another table. The values can also be set to reference a value in the database but show this value as a different name in the drop-down. Example: stored value, display value; stored value, display value;.
    ​
    ​

  • Under Advanced Fields, there are several more attributes that can be altered, including Virtual Field, Ref Field Filter, and Audit Retention Days.

16990676:
Distributor guide to Scheduler route phasing in Encompass: stops repeating every 1-16 weeks or months via Start On Date and Repeat Every. Needs Setting 581 = Scheduler (cannot be undone) and v24.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.12

Pre-Conditions

  • System Setting 581 must be set to 'Scheduler'. GeneralAccountingEdit permission is required to updated this System Setting.
    ​
    ​

  • Be advised that due to data structure changes and other complexities, this setting cannot be reverted back to the Phase 4 option once it is changed.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Scheduler Route Phasing

Industry phasing has typically been a 4-week cycle. To keep up with trends, feedback, and other requirements, Encompass now has a 'Scheduler' phasing option available.

Setting 581, Route System Phase Type
​
​

  • The additional route phasing options are made available by System Setting 581.
    ​
    ​

  • Updating this setting from 'Phase 4' to 'Scheduler', allows phasing to be every week to every 16 weeks.

2. Routes Table - Frequency
​
​

  • The frequency options on the Routes table are more restrictive with only Manual, Weekly, and Monthly options available.
    ​
    ​

  • The Frequency options for Every Other, Every Third, and Every Fourth, are now available on the Stops table instead.

3. Stops Table - Phase
​
​

  • The Phase column will remain visible on the Stops table, but it will serve only as a reference.
    ​
    ​

  • The "phasing" is now controlled by the 'Repeat Every' field on the Stops table.

4. Stops Table Changes - Start On Date
​
​

  • The Start On Date field determines when the Stop will begin.
    ​
    ​

  • When Setting 581 is set to 'Scheduler', the Start On Date will automatically be updated using the previous phasing dates.
    ​
    ​

  • The Start On Date field also allows for the service of new Stops to begin on a future date.

5. Stops Table Changes - Repeat Every
​
​

  • The Repeat Every field replaces the functionality of the Phase field.
    ​
    ​

  • When Setting 581 is set to 'Scheduler', the Repeat Every field is updated based on the Phase column.
    ​
    a. Phase 'All' stops will be Repeat Every 1.
    ​
    b. Phase 1&3 or 2&4 stops will be Repeat Every 2.
    ​
    c. Phase 1, 2, 3, and 4 only stops will be Repeat Every 4.
    ​
    d. Stops can also be updated manually to Repeat Every 1 to 16 weeks, or every 1 to 16 months, depending on the Frequency setting of the Route.

6. Stops Table Changes - Week of Month
​
​

  • For Routes that have a Frequency of Monthly, the Week of Month field can be set to First, Second, Third, Fourth, or Last Week.

16990683:
Distributor steps for accruing goods received but not invoiced (GRNI) at month-end in Encompass, automatically via Accrual Account Maps or with a manual journal entry. Manual needs Integrated Financials; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Manual accrual workflow requires Integrated Financials subscription.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Accruing for Goods/Services Received but Not Invoiced (GRNI/SRNI) is an important accounting process to ensure the accuracy of stated assets and liabilities on the balance sheet.

There are automated and manual workflows that can be used to complete this process in Encompass.

Automated Workflow using Accrual Account Maps
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to "Accrual Account Maps" table.
​
2. Click Add Accrual Account Maps.
​
​3. In the Account field, enter the General Ledger account that should receive the accrued inventory or expense.
​
4. In the Accrual Account field, select the Current Liability account that should receive the cumulative vendor liability.
​
5. Click Add Record.
​
​

Now that the map is configured, an automated routine will run during Accounts Payable Close, to look for any Received purchases that have been posted to the GL Accounts assigned in the Accrual Account Maps with a Receive Date less than or equal the date that Accounts Payable is being closed to. A balanced journal entry with a source of Inventory Accrual will be posted to the general ledger with reversing transactions contained in the journal entry trans.

Note: Table Imports can be used to create many accrual account maps at once. Please contact Support if you need assistance with the importing process.

Manual Acccrual(Requires Integrated Financials subscription)
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to "Accounts Payable" dashboard and select the Confirming Purchases tab.
​
2. Click the Purchases to Confirm link.
​
3. Users are redirected to the "Purchases"table that is filtered to all purchases in a "Received" status.
​
4. If accruing for a specific financial period (month-end or year-end), add a filter on Receive Date column to view only the purchases orders that were received prior to or on month end (Ex: Receive Date is <= 12/31/2022).
​
5. Review list to ensure there are no purchases that have been invoiced and need to be taken through Purchase Confirmation workflow.
​
6. Once list is confirmed, sum the Open Balance column.

​

Steps

Schedule Reports to be Sent

3. Click Schedule Reports.

4. Set the following fields in the Scheduled Reports dialog:
​

  • Frequency
    ​

  • Send Time
    ​

  • Require Recipient to Log On
    ​

  • Expiration Days
    ​

  • Message - Enter text if the Report Link should be sent with a Message in the body of the communication
    ​
    ​

6. To add users, search for them within the search bar.

Fields And Definitions

  • Expiration Days* - Because recipients access the reports sent to them via a quick link, this setting determines how long that quick link is active.

16990706:
Distributor setup for Alternate Locations in Encompass so inventory from another warehouse is combined and can be picked from it, including product groups and transfer rules. Encompass/CSM creates records. v25.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.10

Pre-Conditions

Alternate Locations Table:

Alternate Location records are critical for managing sensitive inventory flow and providing users with accurate location alternatives. Therefore, the ability to add or edit these records is restricted to GA Setup permissions, which is an Encompass only permission.

The view permissions for the Alternate Location table is Bin Edit.

Inventory Transfer Rules Table:

See the steps in the Guide tab. It is important to set up a Inventory Transfer Rule as well.

Steps

Alternate Location Inventory Setup Guide

This guide outlines the steps for setting up Alternate Locations to combine inventory for display in mobile applications and to manage inventory transfer rules.

Alternate Location Configuration

This setup defines which location's inventory will be combined with another, as well as allowing product to be picked from the alternate location.

  • Navigate to the Alternate Locations table.
    ​
    ​
    ​    As mentioned on the Pre-Conditions tab, the permissions to add Alternate Locations records is current GA Setup, which is an Encompass only permission. Please work with your CSM to get these records created.

  • Define the Location and Alternate Location:

    • Set the Location and the corresponding Alternate Location.

    • Uniqueness Constraint: Each combination of Location and Alternate Location must be unique. A single Location can have multiple records, each pointing to a different Alternate Location.

  • Optional Product Group Setup:

    • You can optionally use the Product Groups field on the Alternate Locations table to apply the alternate location logic to all products within a specific group.

    • Visibility Constraint: Only Product Groups where the Type is set to Alternate Location will be visible for selection.

Product Setup: Determining Eligibility

This section explains how a product is configured to utilize the Alternate Location inventory logic.

The system determines if a product should use combined inventory based on a tiered approach:

1. New Option (25.10 and Later)

  • Product Group Type: Starting in version 25.10, a new Type named Alternate Locations is available on the Product Groups table.

  • Prioritization: If a Product Group with Type = Alternate Locations is specified on the Alternate Locations table, all related products within that group will be included in the combined inventory logic. This method takes precedence.

2. Legacy Option (If Product Group is Not Set)

  • Inventory Table Check: If the Product Group field is not set on the Alternate Locations table, the system will check the Inventories table.

  • Field: The Use Alternate Locations field on the Inventories table will determine if the combined inventory should be displayed for that specific product.

    • Default: When new products are added, the Use Alternate Locations field defaults to "True".

System Behavior & Impact

When a product is set up to use Alternate Locations, the combined inventory is displayed in the following areas:

  • Mobile Applications: Sales representatives will see the combined inventory (customer's location + alternate location) in Encompass Mobile and the servicer invoice edit screen.

  • DSDLink: Alternate Locations logic is used to determine if a product is displayed as in stock or unavailable.

  • Alternate Locations dashboard will allow invoice transactions with qualifying products to be picked or delivered from an alternate location. If Setting 555 = True, transactions will stay on the current invoice and be flagged to be picked from an alternate location. Transactions will be moved to a new invoice with a loadsheet equal to the alternate location is setting 555 = false.

Inventory Transfer Rules

Inventory Transfer Rules are critical for managing the movement of goods between locations.

  • Setup Dashboard: Use the Transfer Planner Setup dashboard to define and configure Inventory Transfer Rules.

  • Alternate Location Transfers: This setup is especially important if the system setting 555 is set to "True," as the inventory transfer rule data will be used to correctly identify the customer and vendor when an alternate location transfer record is created.

Fields And Definitions

Product Group: When defining an alternate location, this field allows you to restrict the link to a specific group of products. If populated, the system will only look at this alternate location for items within that group.

​Use Alternate Location (Inventory Setting): A system setting that determines inventory visibility. If a primary location is not an alternate itself, this setting allows users to see a "combined inventory" view comprising stock from the primary and all linked alternate locations.

Best Practices

Utilize Product Grouping: To maximize efficiency, map alternate locations based on distinct product lines (e.g., Warehouse A for Winse and Spirits, Warehouse B for Beer). This prevents the system from searching the wrong warehouse for specific inventory.

Steps

Purpose

The purpose of this tool is to pick orders from a different location.

How to navigate to Alternate Locations

The Alternate Locations dashboard is accessible when going to any of the Delivery Optimizer related tabs, such as Import Conflicts, Out of Stock Rules, Delivery Optimizer, etc;

Using Alternate Locations

The Alternate Locations tab is strategically located to support the left-to-right workflow for processing orders for delivery. It is recommended that Import Conflicts are processed before taking the following steps using Alternate Locations. Once those steps are completed, continue working across the tabs from left to right.

Filters
​
Filtering on the delivery date and location that you want the product to be picked from is most important. Use any other filters as necessary.
​
​

  • Date = LoadSheet - Date
    ​
    ​

  • Location = LoadSheet - Location
    ​
    ​

  • Alternate Location = Alternate location on Aternate Locations table.

  • Route = LoadSheet - Route
    ​
    ​

  • Truck Group = LoadSheet - Truck Group
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Pick Type = Customers - Customer Pick Type
    ​
    ​

  • Product Group = Product Group on Alternate Location Table. Filters on product within the product group

  • Product Pick Type = Inventory - Product Pick Type Effective
    ​
    ​

  • Product Type = Products - Product Type
    ​
    ​

  • Product = Invoice Trans - Product
    ​
    ​

  • Supplier = Products - Supplier
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Account Type = Customer Types - Customer Account Type
    ​
    ​

  • Use Alternate Locations = Inventory - Use Alternate Locations
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Partial Cases: 1) All Locations = Bottle pick or partial cases will be picked from all locations. 2) Alternate Location Only = Bottle pick or partial cases will ONLY be picked from the alternate locations. So partial transactions will be picked even if the satellite location has inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Show All Transactions: True = Show transactions even if the satellite locations have enough inventory. This would allow the alternate location to still pick products even though the satellite location has enough inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Show Alternate Pick Transaction = When true, this will show transactions that have been previously set to be picked from an alternate location. This is a way to "undo" transactions.
    ​
    ​

NOTE: Click on the column headers to provide additional filtering and sorting

Options for Selecting Transactions

  • Select all transactions by clicking on the checkbox in the header.
    ​
    ​

  • Select a range of transactions by clicking the first transaction, then shift+click on the last transaction.
    ​
    ​

  • Click the Pick from Alternate Location or Delivery From Alternate Location button to process the selected transactions’
    ​
    ​

  • Be sure to run Out of Stock Rules, and Close Dated Product after running Alternate Locations.

Using Delivery Optimizer with Alternate Locations
​
​It is expected that routes for invoices processed in alternate locations will show up when filtering on the alternate location in Delivery Optimizer. For example, the non-alternate location’s routes will show when filtering on the Alternate Location in Deliver Optimizer.

Using the Alternate Locations filter in Delivery Optimizer (only available if setting 555 is true)
​
​The Alternate Locations filter is useful to filter out the data in the Delivery Optimizer to what is to be picked out of the alternate location, or not to be picked out of the alternate location.

From Delivery Optimizer, if filtering on the Alternate Location:

  • Show All: All routes and transactions will be displayed (current behavior).
    ​
    ​

  • Hide All: Only the Routes where the Location on the Route equals the Alternate Location will be displayed. In other words, do not show any routes from other locations.
    ​
    ​

  • Show Trans Only: Only show routes and transactions from other locations that will be picked out of the Alternate Location.

From Delivery Optimizer, if filtering on another location and NOT the Alternate Location:

  • Show All: All routes and transactions will be displayed.
    ​
    ​

  • Hide All: Only the routes and transactions to be picked out of the selected location will be displayed. So, any transactions to be picked out of the Alternate Location will be hidden.
    ​
    ​

  • Show Trans Only: Only routes and transactions will be displayed are set to be picked out of the Alternate Location, so normally nothing will be displayed.

Screenshot

Warehouse Truck Return

During truck return, if there is good product getting returned to the Alternate Location and that is not going to be redelivered due to mis-shipments, customer refusal, etc; It is recommended to create a reason code “Good Return to Alternate Location”. A return rule should be used to help get the product out of the satellite location using an invoice or putting product into a specified bin.

Return Rules: Using an Adj Customer -

  • Invoice is created during the return process and the product will be taken out of the satellite inventory by an invoice. This could be an invoice for every route and every day.
    ​
    ​

Return Rules: Using a Return Bin -

  • During the return process, the inventory will be accumulated to a specified return bin, where it can invoiced when the product is shipped back to the alternate location
    ​
    ​

  • When the product is physically returned to the alternate location, a purchase should be created for the alternate location so it can be received back into inventory.

16990717:
Distributor guide to how Encompass expects the brand hierarchy set up: supplier family, supplier, vendor, brand family, brand and product, with examples and VIP/SRS reporting considerations. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

While there are several schools of thought on Brand Hierarchy, Encompass assumes the following, and recommends that distributors set up their data accordingly:

Supplier Family: Owning parent/entity of a group of suppliers.

Supplier: Who makes the product, from the consumer's perspective. This is often what is displayed on the label itself.

Vendor: Who you buy the product from.

  • Encompass does not recommend using the supplier field to denote 3PLs/distributor partners, importers, etc. Instead, these entities should be notated on the vendor record.

Brand Family: Collection of brands (ex: Barrel Aged Series, Seasonal, Etc.). Sometimes, this can be the same as the supplier.

Brand: The liquid itself - the flavor. This is package agnostic (there should not be any package identifiers in a brand title).

Product: The brand + packaging - most granular.

Example Hierarchy:

Supplier Family: Anheuser Busch Inc.
​
​

Supplier: Budweiser
​

Brand Family: Bud Light
​
​

Brand: Bud Light, Bud Light Platinum, Bud Light Chelada, etc.
​
​

Product: Bud Light 4/6 pack 16oz Cans, Bud Light 4/6 pack 16oz Bottles, Bud Light Chelada 2/12 pack 8oz Cans, etc.

Additional Considerations:

  • A brand family should only 'point' to one singular global supplier, meaning that all of the brands/products under a brand family should all point to the same global supplier.
    ​
    ​

  • A supplier record, ideally, should only have brand families underneath it that point to the same global supplier/supplier report code. Distributor numbers are typically unique for each supplier and provided by VIP/SRS. However, we are unable to add multiple Suppliers Vendors records (necessary for VIP/SRS reporting) for a single location with different distributor numbers.

Related articles:

  • Brands and Brand Families

  • Suppliers and Supplier Families

  • Add a Vendor

Days of Inventory (DOI) Calculations in Transfer Planner

The User Forecast DOI toggle switch in Transfer Planner will allow DOI to be calculated from Forecast Days of Inventory (DOI), or from available inventory. The Use Forecast DOI toggle switch will be set to TRUE by default.
​
​

DOI Calculation when Using Forecast DOI = True:
​
​

Before a transfer quantity is entered:

  • DOI = Forecasted DOI
    ​
    ​

  • Forecasted DOI = (Lead Time Days * On Hand Inventory) / Lead Time Demand

After a Transfer quantity is entered:

  • DOI = (Available - Forecasted Sales for the Period) / (Average Sales / Lead Time Days) Transfer Planner

DOI Calculation when Using Forecast DOI = False:

This option will calculate DOI based on the avg period of 10, 15, or 30 days. DOI = Available Inventory / (Sales / Average Period)

Example:
​

  • Available inventory = 804
    ​
    ​

  • Sales (last 10 weekdays) = 277
    ​
    ​

  • AveragePeriod = 10
    ​
    ​

  • DOI = 804/(277/10) = 29
    ​
    ​

If alternate locations are set up, this is useful to prevent products from showing in the Transfer Planner when using the alternate locations workflow to pick product.

Distributor reference explaining each routing method and the Find Route logic that decides which load sheet an imported or new invoice lands on (event, stop, or off-day route) in Encompass. Requires v26.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 26.10

Steps

Routing Structure (Routing Methods and Find Route Logic)
​
​Routing Methods are set on the Activities, OrderRouting EDBL Import Routines, or Exchange Configurations and are used in Find Route Logic. All Routing Methods follow the same Routing Logic. (The difference between the routing methods is the date that is checked)


​
Routing Methods
​
​1) Requested Delivery Date: Runs Find Route Logic ON Invoice Audit Date
​
2) Next Scheduled Delivery Event Then Stop: Runs Find Route Logic AFTER Today's Date.
​
3) Sales Receipt (Exchange Configurations or InvoiceOrder EDBL Only): This will find or create a sales receipt loadsheet.
​
4) Auto Route To Event Then Stop On or After Requested Date: Runs Find Route Logic ON or AFTER Invoice Audit Date.
​
5) Route to Import Route Num: (Exchange Configurations or InvoiceOrder EDBL Only): Will import to the selected RouteNum in the file
​
6) OffDayRoute (Used by Customer Search > Add Off-Day Invoice): Create an Off-Day Load Sheet for the selected day.
​
7) One Customer Per Load Sheet: Will find Load Sheet with Status <= Loaded. On Distributor Order Portal, the distributor can only select a

date after the Current Date + Order Cut-Off Days in Advance.
​
8) Earliest Delivery Event or Stop: This will find the first Event OR Stop which is > Today.
​
9) One Invoice Per Load Sheet On Or After Requested DATE: Same as #4, but only one invoice per load sheet.
​
10) Next Delivery Stop: This method will ONLY find the stop and will not find Events, so it does not use Find Route Logic Checks mentioned below.
​
​
Routing methods 2, 4, and 10 will not create import conflicts based on after the cut-off time. Invoices will be created for the next scheduled date before the cut-off time. NOTE: If the user has Invoice Edit Routing permissions, the invoice will sync to the Load Sheet even if it is after the cut-off time.


​
Find Route Logic and Flowchart
​
​

Does an Event (with Activity.IsDelivery= True) exist for this Customer?
​
​

■ If an Event is found: Invoice is imported to the Load Sheet linked to the Plans.Route, again Routing Method #10 will not find events.

  • If NO Event exists, does a Stop (with ActivityEffective.IsDelivery = True & Product Group) exist for this Customer?

■ If a Stop is found: Invoice is imported to the Load Sheet related to the Stops.Route

  • If NO Stop and NO Event Exists for this Customer, Invoice will be imported to the Off Day Route

Distributor reference for 832, 879 and 889 pricing EDI files in Encompass, plus troubleshooting missing products, stores, wrong pricing or files not received. Needs a Price Posting Template and v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Price Posting Template is Setup. For more information on Price posting template setup and functionality, please see the price posting template help resource.

Fields And Definitions

832 Files:

  • 832 files are commonly pricing catalog files. They will include all pricing information including frontline pricing as well as any discounts
    ​
    ​

879 Files:

  • 879 files are pricing catalogs that only include frontline pricing information. These files do not include any discounts and are commonly used in tandem with 889 files


889 Files:

  • 879 files are pricing catalogs that only include Promotion Pricing information (Discounts, price, and other promotions that are not frontline promotions). These files do not include Frontline Promotions and are commonly used in tandem with 879 files

Best Practices

Troubleshooting Errors:
​
​

Products not included?

  • Typically when products are not included in a pricing file, the customer on the price posting template or the product group on the price posting template do not allow the product to show. The first thing to check is the most recent price posting export for this template and see if the product is showing. If the product is showing, you should look for an exchange task that sent this price posting export (This will show in the memo of the exchange task) to confirm the data is in the file that was sent. If the product cannot be found in the price posting export it is being filtered out. The first thing to check is if there is a product group on the price posting template. If there is then make sure the product type of the product in question is included in the product group. If this is not the issue, then the customer is not able to purchase the product due to product controls. Please see our help resources on product controls for more details on the different product controls.
    ​
    ​

Pricing is not expected?

  • Typically when pricing is not expected in a pricing file, the customer on the price posting template is not setup to qualify for the correct promotions. The first thing to check is the most recent price posting export for this template and see if the product and pricing is showing. If the product and pricing is showing as expected, you should look for an exchange task that sent this price posting export (This will show in the memo of the exchange task) to confirm the data is in the file that was sent. If the product is not showing at all, please see above to find out how to troubleshoot products that are not showing. If the product is showing, but is not showing the correct pricing, the customer is either not qualified for the promotion you expect, or qualified for an unexpected promotion. To troubleshoot you should look at the promotions and make sure the customer is qualified for the proper promotions through promotion zones and promotion locations.
    ​
    ​

Store is not included?

  • Typically when a store is not included in a pricing file, they are not attached to the market on the price posting template. Please check the market and make sure to add the customer to the market. If there is no market on the price posting template, you will want to make sure you have exchange configurations price posting templates set up for all your locations to ensure the chain is receiving pricing for all locations.
    ​
    ​

Pricing files not received?

  • If a pricing file has not been received, there was either an error on the exchange task, or the pricing file did not generate. The first thing to check is the price posting exports under the price posting template to make sure an export has generated. If a price posting export was not generated as expected, make sure the next run date is set to a future date such as today's date so it can generate a new price posting export. If the price posting export was generated, you should look for an exchange task that sent this price posting export (This will show in the memo of the exchange task) to confirm the export was sent.

Distributor steps for building a warehouse map on iPad with the Encompass Warehouse Map app: draw walls and racks, generate or link bins, and set pick sequence and path. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

How to set up an Encompass Warehouse Map

Summary

This document will guide you on accessing the Encompass Warehouse Map design tool on an iPad and navigating through the map creation process. The map can then be used to view location-based reporting in a map-layout view.

Purpose

The purpose of this document is to provide instruction on warehouse map creation and usage from start to finish.

Topics

1. Downloading and logging into the iPad app

2. Navigating the app

3. Defining the tools & how to use

Downloading and logging into the iPad app

1. On your device, navigate to the iOS App Store and search “Encompass Warehouse Map”

  • Encompass Warehouse Map is only available on iPad

2. Tap “Get” to start the installation process. Once installed, tap the “Open” button or the app icon from your device’s home screen to open the app.

3. The first screen of the warehouse map app will prompt you to enter an EncompassID, Encompass Server URL, User Name, and Password.

  • EncompassID can be found in the top right corner of your Encompass site when logged in

  • Encompass Server URL is the url associated with that site.

  • User Name can also be found in the top right corner of your Encompass site.

  • Enter these values, as well as your password, then tap “Done” to login. 2

Navigating the app

1. Once logged in, the main screen will look blank if a warehouse map has not yet been created. Each of the buttons along the top and bottom of the screen can be used to take additional actions.

2. The Settings icon can be used to toggle visibility on or off for certain aspects of the warehouse map, such as Path and Labels. Captuvo scanning can also be enabled here.

3. Tapping on your username will allow you log out, switch sites, or switch users as needed. OAuth logins can also be used here, once your Encompass site has been linked to the app.

4. Tapping on the Location will allow you to switch to another location, if your Encompass site has multiple locations that you have access to.

5. Tapping the refresh button will update the map view with any data that might have been more recently entered on your Encompass site.

6. The Search bar allows you to look up specific bins and products within a completed warehouse map

7. The lower navigation menu is a toolbar that offers access to the many different design options available in the Warehouse Map app. These options will be covered in the next section.

8. Using a dragging motion with a single finger will shift the map around on the screen, and using a pinching motion on the screen will zoom in or out.

9. It’s important to maintain a stable data or wifi connection when working on the warehouse map.

Defining the tools & how to use

The options in the toolbar at the bottom of the screen are typically approached working from left to right as a warehouse map is built out. In this section, the tools will be listed in left to right order.

Design Map

a. This tool allows you to set the dimensions of the map.

b. There are two options for setting dimensions:

  • Relating to a warehouse map background image (typically a CAD drawing provided by the warehouse layout designer)

  • Manually without a background

c. Regardless of the dimension method chosen, it’s important to make sure that the dimensions set match the exact measurements of the warehouse floor in feet.

d. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Design Walls

a. Once the dimensions of the map have been set, the layout of the warehouse can begin to take shape. The Design Walls tool allows you to draw out the walls of the warehouse, creating the basic structure that racks and bins will later be placed within.

b. Long-press the screen to start a wall segment, then drag the point in the direction the wall needs to go.

  • Tip: Make sure Accessibility settings on the iPad have not disabled or assigned another action to the long-press.

c. Once a wall segment has been created, a short tap on the segment will select the wall so that it can be resized or moved as needed.

d. With a wall segment selected, tapping the “Actions” button in the top right corner allows you to:

  • Enter specific wall coordinates

  • Add a door by entering coordinates or drag and drop

  • Delete the wall

e. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Design Racks

a. Design Racks is where the bulk of the warehouse map creation work occurs. This tool allows you to create a template for each of the rack slotting

layouts on your warehouse floor. Design Racks is also where the creation of floor bins occurs. The more accurate dimensions are in this section, the

more accurate spatial inventory data will be when reporting.

b. To create a new rack type, tap the “New” button on the bottom of the screen, then select Rack or Floor Bin.

c. For Racks:

  • Rack: Name the Rack Type, select a color, then enter the overall dimensions of the structure, along with the number of levels in the rack. Tap “Next” to move on.

  • Level: On this screen, you’ll design each level of the rack. By default, the system will distribute your levels equally across the height entered for the rack; so individual dimensions can be changed on this page, as well as entering the number of slots or bins for each level. Add or remove levels from the rack as needed from here. Tap “Next” to move on.

  • Bin: You can also set specific dimensions for individual bins if slots are not exactly even across a level, as well as split bins into additional spots on the rack. At the Bin level is also where certain inventory controls are set, such as Bin Type and Bin Zone, which control capacity and inventory category, respectively.

d. For Floor Bins:

  • Because Floor Bins sit directly on the warehouse floor, this workflow does not include Rack or Level setup. Floor Bins are still considered “Rack Types” within the design mode.

  • Bin: Name the Rack Type and select a color. Set Floor Bin capacity by entering the bin dimensions directly, or set a pallet count that the system can use to calculate dimensions. This page also offers the same Bin Type and Bin Zone selection.

e. Once you’ve created a Rack Type, it will appear to the left of the “New” button in the lower bar. Press and hold a Rack Type to select it, then drag it onto the warehouse map. The Rack Type template will be used to create an individual Rack.

f. Tapping on a Rack placed on the warehouse map will select it, showing in a darker color. Selecting a rack will display additional editing options:

  • Rack direction, or the way it faces on the floor

  • Rack coordinates—in addition to drag and drop functionality, the exact location of the rack in the warehouse can be set manually

  • Moving the rack by entering a distance in feet or inches and selecting a direction in which to shift

  • Duplicating the rack by entering a number of copies and the direction in which the copies should generate

  • Changing the Rack Type or making adjustments to the Rack Type currently selected

  • Deleting the rack, and potentially unlinking or deleting related bins if bin records have already been connected (see Design Racks, 5. Generate Bins and 6. Link Bins)

  • Racks can be multi-selected and moved or edited in bulk by first tapping the “Multi-select” option in the top right corner of the screen.

g. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Bin Direction

a. Bin Direction can be checked once all racks in the warehouse have been placed and arranged within the map. This indicates the typical direction a team member would walk as they visit each rack or bin.

b. Arrows will display automatically over each rack or floor bin. If the arrows do not match the physical direction someone would walk, simply tap the arrow once and it will change directions.

c. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Generate Bins

a. Generate Bins should only be used if there are not already bin records imported or otherwise created in Encompass. Typically bins are generated if the bins or racks in the warehouse did not previously have labels, or if the warehouse is being rearranged, resulting in brand new bins. Move on to Design Racks, 6. Link Bins if Bins already exist in the Encompass system.

b. If new Bins need to be created, Generate Bins can be used to do this very quickly by defining aisles and rack numbers.

c. Tap on the Aisle box in the top right corner, enter the letter of the aisle you will be assigning, then tap each rack (or floor bin) on the map that falls within that aisle. By default, rack numbers will start at 1, then count up from there.

d. Rack number can be changed using the box in the top right corner of the screen, and if the incorrect number or aisle is assigned to a rack, simply double-tap the rack to reset it.

e. For floor bins, using Generate Bins will only generate one bin per tap, as the “rack” shown on the warehouse map only represents a single bin.

f. For true racks, tapping each rack will create a bin for each spot within the rack, based on the rack type setup. Bin names are calculated using the pattern Aisle - Rack+Slot - Level(letter). For example, if a bin is located in aisle A, rack 11, and is the 2nd slot on the 3rd level, the system would generate the name as A-112-C.

g. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Link Bins

a. Link Bins should be used if your Bins have already been created in the Encompass system, and they are physically labeled in the warehouse. This can be done via table import, or by manually adding bins on the server.

b. Link Bins allows you to attach previously created Bins to newly created Racks in the warehouse map.

c. Linking Bins can be done in two ways:

  • By Scanning: Turn on the “Scan” option in the top right corner, then tap on the rack that needs to have bins linked. Use a bluetooth scanner to scan each Bin barcode in the order and direction set on the rack. After scanning, make sure the bin name appears on the desired spot on the rack—pausing for about 1 full second before scanning the next bin is typically enough time for the first scan assignment to finish loading.

  • By Searching: Tap on the rack that needs to have bins linked, then use the search bar in the top corner to look up a bin—the search works with partial names, so this is a good way to pull up multiple of the bins that will be linked to the rack. Tap a spot on the rack, then tap on the matching bin listed in the search results.

d. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Edit Bins

a. Edit Bins is used to make small changes to individual bins within the warehouse map.

b. To edit a bin,

c. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Pick Sequence

a. Pick Sequence can be set to define the order in which team members should visit the bins while building orders for delivery. This can be set manually by tapping each bin on the map in sequence, or by scanning each physical bin in the warehouse.

b. To assign pick sequence by tapping, simply set the starting sequence in the top right corner, then tap each rack in the sequence you’d like them to follow. If there’s multiple pick bins in one rack, those bins will be individually sequenced based on the direction of the rack.

c. To assign pick sequence by scanning, set the starting sequence in the top right corner, and scan each bin in the sequence you’d like to follow.

d. Pick Sequence can always be adjusted by editing the sequence box shown in the top right corner, then tapping again on the rack that needs to change.

e. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Path

a. Path defines the route team members will follow through the warehouse as they build orders for delivery, and helps calculate distance traveled.

b. Path can be auto-generated by the system, or set manually. When the system automatically generates the path, it sets a stop in front of each rack or floor bin, and connects each stop in the direction set on the bins.

c. Path can be defined manually by tapping on the screen to create a stop.

d. To make edits to the path or specific stops, tap once to display additional options. To delete a stop or path, tap twice.

e. Path can be displayed or hidden using the Settings icon in the top left corner of the screen.

f. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Label

a. Labels are used to identify different areas of the warehouse and provide context to those viewing the map.

b. To add a label to the map, tap on the area that needs labeling, type the name, then tap “Done.”

c. Labels can be moved by tapping and holding, then dragging the label to the desired location.

d. Labels can be displayed or hidden using the Settings icon in the top left corner of the screen.

e. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Photos

a. Photos can be added to the warehouse map to provide context to certain areas.

b. To add an image to the map, tap on the area of the map that the photo will be of, then take a picture of the physical area. Once happy with the image, tap “Use” to confirm it, then tap back to navigate back to the map display.

c. Any added images will be displayed as a photo icon on the screen, and can be tapped to take a closer look, add another image, or delete.

d. Tap “Done” once you are ready to move on.

Fields And Definitions

  • Aisle: A row of racks, typically noted with a letter that is used to define an “address” within the warehouse.
    ​
    ​

  • Bin: A single slot in the warehouse identified with a unique name and coordinates. A bin can be a slot on a rack, or directly on the floor. Bins can be created on the server, or within the Warehouse Map app.
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Type: Refers to the physical characteristics of a bin to indicate capacity. For example, a “1 Pallet” Bin Type would be a bin that fits one full pallet of inventory. Bin Types are created on the server.
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Zone: Refers to the physical area where a bin is located. Some examples of Bin Zones are “Floor Pick,” “Rack Backstock,” “Keg Cooler.” Bin Zones are created on the server.
    ​
    ​

  • Capacity: Can also be known as par or par level, capacity refers to the amount of inventory that can fit into a given bin. Case capacity is calculated for a bin once it has inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Captuvo: A specific brand of “sled” scanner that is built-in to an iPad case. Floor Bin: A kind of slot in the warehouse that sits directly on the warehouse floor.
    ​
    ​

  • Level: One shelf on a rack, that may hold multiple bins. If a rack has three shelves, then it has three levels.
    ​
    ​

  • Location: A physical warehouse that has its own inventory and supplies its own deliveries. Multiple separate warehouses typically indicates multiple locations.
    ​
    ​

  • OAuth: A method of logging in that involves using an account from another business tool, usually email. Available OAuth login options include Gmail and Microsoft.
    ​
    ​

  • Path: The route through the warehouse that team members are expected to follow as they build orders for delivery, defined by connecting stops together in sequence. Path can be used to calculate travel distances during order building.
    ​
    ​

  • Rack: A single structure with multiple shelves that hold inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Rack Type: A rack layout that applies to multiple racks in the warehouse that look and function the same.
    ​
    ​

  • Sequence: The order in which racks and bins will be visited as team members build orders for delivery.
    ​
    ​

  • Stop: A spot in front of a rack or floor bin where a team member is expected to pause and pull inventory as they build an order for delivery.

Best Practices

  • Certain tools within Warehouse Map, such as Design Walls, use the long-press function. Accessibility settings on the iPad can sometimes interfere with the behavior of a long-press action, so double-check Accessibility within your iPad Settings to make sure the long-press action is not assigned a specific behavior.

16990762:
Producer/brewery guide to WIP accounting in Encompass OCloud: set up Production Stage Groups and WIP product types so raw material value posts to WIP accounts during production. Requires v23.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.06

Pre-Conditions

Applies to all OCloud producers.

Impacts all non-Packaging type Recipes/Production Orders.

Steps

Click here for documentation with screenshots

Value Statement:

Enable GAAP compliant WIP accounting visibility by creating accounting transactions throughout the production process.

Requirements:

  • Applies to all OCloud producers

  • Impacts all non-Packaging type Recipes/Production Orders

Problem Statement:

Prior to 23.06 (June 2023), Production Orders passed the value of consumed raw materials to a WIP Account at the time of completing the Production Order. This meant that the value of consumed raw materials was not passed to a WIP Account while the Production Order was in process. This resulted in an overstated Raw Materials Inventory Account and an understated WIP Account while the Production Order was in process. This was most impactful when using multi-stage Recipes/Production Orders that cover the brewing process from mash-to-bright beer, which typically takes between 2-4 weeks to fully complete.

The brewing industry standard is to break the production process into three common phases: Wort WIP -> Green Beer WIP -> Bright Beer WIP, and pass the value of all consumed raw materials to WIP Accounts for each production phase.

The Solution:

  • Allow defining production phases using Production Stage Groups.

  • Pass the value of consumed raw materials to WIP Accounts for each phase of production.

  • Minimize Recipe setup by auto-creating WIP Products for each Production Stage Group.

About Production Stage Groups

The purpose of Production Stage Groups is to define the phase(s) of the production process and temporarily store the value of all consumed ingredients in a WIP Account for each phase while the Production Order is in process.

Production Stage Groups define the phase(s) of the production process by associating Production Stage Types to a production phase. This is achieved by assigning Production Stage Types to a Production Stage Group.

How Production Stage Groups work with Recipes & Recipe Stages

Recipes consist of one or multiple Recipe Stages. Every Recipe Stage is assigned to a Production Stage Type and every Production Stage Type is assigned to a Production Stage Group.

The system auto-generates a WIP Product for each Recipe Stage based on the Production Stage Groups + Recipe Brand. The WIP Product is used to store the value of consumed raw materials in a WIP Account. The consumed raw material value is passed from one WIP Product to the next WIP Product as the brew moves through each production phase (e.g. Wort WIP -> Green Beer WIP).

How consumed raw material value flows through WIP accounts while a Production Order is in process

Every Recipe Stage has an assigned WIP Product, and Recipe Stages have raw materials consumed in each stage. Raw material value is passed to the WIP Account mapped to the Recipe Stage’s WIP Product when the raw material is consumed. The value of the WIP Account increases as each raw material is consumed.

WIP products map to a WIP account that stores the value of all consumed raw materials while the Production Order is in process. WIP value will pass from one WIP account to the next WIP account when the Production Order progresses through the phases of the production process (e.g. Wort WIP -> Green Beer WIP -> Bright Beer WIP).

Upon completion of the Production Order, the total value from all consumed raw materials is passed to the account assigned to the Output Product on the Production Order. This functionality has not changed with the addition of Production Stage Groups.

Fields And Definitions

  1. Define the phases of the production process that you wish to capture WIP value while production is in process.
    --As previously stated, the best practice for brewing production phases is Wort WIP -> Green Beer WIP -> Bright Beer WIP. However, a single In-Process WIP phase is also acceptable.
    --This does not apply to the packaging phase, only the phases leading up to packaging.
    ​
    ​

  2. Create one WIP Product Type for each production phase.
    Product Type Fields
    --Track Inventory = True
    --Type Code = WIP
    --Store in Equipment = True
    ​
    ​

  3. Product Type Account Mapping
    Link all WIP Product Types to an Inventory Asset Account Maps record that links to the Inventory Asset Account that will store the value of this phase.
    ​
    ​

  4. Create one Production Stage Group for each production phase.
    Production Stage Group Fields
    --Product Type = set the WIP Product Type created in step 2.
    --Package = set the unit of measure Package that you would want set by default on the auto-created WIP Products.
    ----BBLs is commonly used on beer Production Stage Groups.
    ----Gallons is commonly used on spirit Production Stage Groups.
    ​
    ​

  5. Link all non-packaging Production Stage Types to the Production Stage Group that best represents the stage’s production phase.
    For example, Production Stage Types: Mash, Lauter, Boil, & Whirlpool are commonly grouped under the ‘Wort’ phase, and therefore would be placed under a ‘Wort WIP’ Production Stage Group.
    --Once this setup is in place, WIP Products will auto-generate for each Production Stage Group + Recipe Brand.
    --These WIP Products map to a WIP Account where the value of the WIP is stored while the Production Order is in process.
    --These WIP Products are automatically set on each Recipe Stage.

Best Practices

All of the examples provided in this Help Resource have been focused on the general best practice of using Production Stage Groups, WIP Products, and WIP Accounts to represent the three common phases of the brewing process: Wort WIP -> Green Beer WIP -> Bright Beer WIP. This is the general best practice because these phases best represent the major physical transformation processes and change to accumulate WIP value as a result of this transformation. While this is the general best practice, this is not the only way that Production Stage Groups, WIP Products, and WIP Accounts can be used.

The Production Stage Group solution supports a setup as simple as a single generic ‘In-Process WIP’ Production Stage Group, where all Production Stage Types share the same ‘In-Process WIP’ Production Stage Group. This simple setup stores the value of all consumed raw materials in a single WIP Account while Production Orders are in process, and then passes the final value of all consumed raw materials to the account mapped to the Output Product when the Production Order is completed.
16990763:
Distributor explanation of how Encompass assigns sales tasks to off-day and holiday-week invoices (dsdlink, EDI, server orders) based on route frequency, so reps see them in My Day. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

When plans are generated using the steps in the Holiday Routing Workflow and Best Practices Dashboard, sales reps will be sure to see invoices in Encompass Mobile during holiday weeks. This mainly includes invoices from dsdlink, Provi, Quantiphi, or other ordering platforms, as well as normal 850 EDI orders.

Regardless of a holiday week or not, an invoice is considered as an off day when the day of week of the invoice is not the same as the customer's scheduled delivery stop. Instead of finding the Sales Rep's existing sales task, a new sales task was created.
​
​

Previous Logic (before 24.01):

A new Sales Task ID was attached to invoices that were imported in as an Off-Day Delivery.

New Logic (24.01+):

Instead of just looking at the Off-Day Delivery flag, the system will now also look at the frequency of the route to determine if a new Sales Task ID should be created.

A new Sales Task ID will be attached to invoices that are imported in as an Off-Day Delivery OR if the frequency of the route is Manual. An existing Sales Task ID will be attached to invoices that are imported in as an On-Day Delivery or if the frequency of route is not Manual.

What about invoices created on Encompass Mobile?

There is no change in how the Sales Tasks IDs or Invoices are created on Encompass Mobile.

What about invoices created on the Server?

The new logic will apply. It is best practice to be sure the Frequency be set to Manual for Hot Shot, House, and other "non-scheduled" routes.

Other benefits of this logic change?

You now have better control if you want the sales rep to see an invoice when going into "My Day" and viewing their plan when creating invoices on the server. This means if you want the sales rep to see an invoice, use a scheduled route (Frequency = Weekly, Monthly, Every Other Week, etc;), otherwise use a Manual route.

    -If users fail to enter a valid password after 6 attempts, they will be prompted with the message: You have exceeded the amounts of sign-in attempts. In this situation, the user must then reset their password to be allowed to log in again

Best Practices

General Best Practices

  • Give all users who need to sign into the system an email address (preferred) or a mobile number
    ​
    ​

  • Encourage users to reset their own passwords to limit administrative burdens
    ​
    ​

Note: Users are required to set their own password after signing in for the first time using a password set by an admin.

*Encompass specifically does not allow anyone other than the user themselves to know a permanent password.
​
This is a security best practice for several reasons:

  • Turnover Security: Having users be the only person to know their permanent password ensures that an Admin leaving the organization does not accidentally retain the login information for another employee.
    ​
    ​

  • Reduced Password Exposure: When administrators have the ability to set permanent passwords, those passwords are more likely to be exposed or written down somewhere, increasing the attack surface. Temporary passwords mitigate this risk.
    ​
    ​

  • Auditability and Accountability: Ensuring only the actual users have access to their password provides reliability in the audits and changes being made throughout the system, allowing you to know confidently that when an audit says that ____ user made a change, that user was the actual human making the change. Requiring password resets also means all password changes are logged and traceable back to the administrator who initiated them.
    ​
    ​

  • User Password Hygiene: Requiring users to set their own passwords encourages better password hygiene, such as using unique, complex passwords. This is better than admins setting weak, reused passwords.
    ​
    ​

  • Delegated User Control: Empowering users to manage their own passwords gives them a greater sense of ownership and control over their account security.
    ​
    ​

  • Reduced Admin Workload: While it may seem more convenient for admins to set permanent passwords, the tradeoffs in security and user experience outweigh this. Admins actually save time in the long run by not having to constantly reset forgotten or compromised passwords.
    ​
    ​

  • Compliance and Regulatory Requirements: Many compliance frameworks and regulations mandate that users have control over their own credentials. Restricting admin access to permanent passwords helps organizations meet these requirements.

Distributor explainer on how Encompass builds customer Peer Groups from premise type, product mix and geography, and how they drive suggested products in dsdlink and Invoice Edit. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Creation and Definition of Peer Groups and Peer Products

This document outlines the technical process for creating and defining Peer Groups and Peer Products.

The process involves several steps, including initial grouping, iterative refinement, and final assignment of peer groups and products.

Peer Group Calculation Process

Peer groups in our system are designed to group similar customers together based on their characteristics and purchasing behaviors. Here's how the algorithm works:

Initial Classification

Basic Premise Types: Customers are initially divided into three basic groups:

  • On-Premise Draft (bars/restaurants with draft)

  • On-Premise Package (bars/restaurants with bottles/cans only)

  • Off-Premise (retailers)

Parameter Calculation

The system calculates two important parameters:

  • Minimum Peer Group Size: 0.5% of total active customers (minimum of 10)

  • Product Sample Size: 20% of the average ranking of top products

Iterative Product-Based Clustering

The system then runs through multiple refinement cycles:

1. Product Purchase Analysis:

  • Examines purchase patterns of top products across customers

  • Identifies products that are commonly purchased by subsets of customers

2. Group Formation:

  • Creates new peer groups when it finds a significant number of customers who purchase the same products

  • Ensures each new group has at least the minimum required customers

  • Moves customers from their original group to the new product-based group

3. Multiple Iterations:

  • Performs up to 3 cycles with increasingly larger product sample sizes

  • Within each cycle, runs up to 100 iterations to find optimal product-based groupings

  • Stops when no more significant product-based clusters can be found

Geographic and Customer Type Grouping

After product-based grouping, the system creates additional peer groups based on:

  • Customer Type and Area

  • Customer Type and Location

  • Customer Type alone

  • Premise Type and Location (if multiple locations exist)

Naming and Metadata

Peer group names are generated based on distinguishing characteristics:

  • Premise type (On/Off Premise, Draft/Package)

  • Product names when there's a single dominant product

  • Brand, brand family, supplier, package type, or segment information

  • Geographic and customer-type attributes

Sales Metrics Calculation

Finally, the system calculates key metrics for each peer group's products:

  • Sales per customer

  • Average product rank within the group

  • Buyer percentage

Result

The end result is a set of peer groups where:

  • Each customer belongs to exactly one peer group

  • Each peer group contains similar customers based on premise type, product preferences, and geographic/customer type attributes

  • Each peer group has at least the minimum required number of customers

  • Each peer group has associated products that are relevant to that customer segment

This multi-layered approach allows for meaningful comparisons between similar customers and helps identify product selling opportunities based on what similar customers are purchasing.

Fields And Definitions

What are Peer Groups?
​
​

  • Peer Groups are used to group like customers together and provide a list of suggested products.

​How are they grouped?
​
​

  • Peer Groups are first grouped by on/off premise and then looking at the product mix of the group of customers. It builds the most specific list of customers that have similar purchasing behavior of products and sales of those products.

​When are they used?
​
​

  • Peer Groups are primarily used for recommended order processes throughout the system, including dsdlink, standard Invoice Edit, and AI Recommended Placements.

Steps

How to View emails sent from Encompass

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Messages table.
​
​ Note: All emails sent out from Encompass, including scheduled emails such as alerts or scheduled reports, are recorded and tracked on the Messages table.
​
2. On the Messages table, the 'Status' value will show the most important information:
​
- Queued: The message has been generated and will be sent in the next few minutes.
​
- Sent: Message has been sent from the Encompass email servers.
​
- Delivered: Message was succesfully delivered to the receiver's inbox (it is possible it went to SPAM still).

​

​

​
4. The 'Open Count' will indicate each time the email is opened, as long as the tracker is not blocked.
​
​5. Audit the Message record to see changes to these fields over time
​
See also the Email Report Tracker and Who Reads Their Email reports, along with several others in the Report Library, for additional insights.

Fields And Definitions

  • Domain Verification = Required in AWS to allow Encompass to send email on behalf of the customer's domain
    ​
    ​

  • DKIM = A security key added to the DNS settings that tells all the other email servers in the world "It's ok for Encompass to send emails on behalf of ___ domain"
    ​
    ​

  • DMARC = A DNS setting (entirely controlled on the customer's side) that tells the email server what to do with stuff that is not DKIM verified

Note: Encompass always sends links in the email to any documents/attachments for the email, it does not attach the document directly to the email itself.

4. Clicking Load Sheets to Balance will redirect you to Returned Load Sheets dated on or before the date selected

5. Back in End of Day Status, click Enter Mail In Load Sheets if you need to add payments to Balance the Returned Load Sheets from the previous step

6. Once you have Balanced Load Sheets, you are ready to run Invoice Close

7. Clicking Receipts Without Deposits will direct you to Balanced Invoices dated on or before the date selected that have not been added to a Deposit

8. Navigate to the Deposits Table to add or edit Deposits

9. Once you have added or edited Deposits, you are ready to run Accounts Receivable Close

10. Clicking Vendor Purchases to Confirm will direct you to Received Purchases dated on or before the date selected

11. Confirm Purchases that are Received

12. Once you have confirmed Purchases, you are ready to run Accounts Payable Close

13. Clicking Enter Manual Journal Entries will direct you to the Journal Entries Table

14. You can then add or edit Journal Entries

15. Once you have added or edited Journal Entries, you are ready to run Financial Close

16. At the end of the month, click the End of Month Preparation tab to review AR, Inventory, Deposit and Laid In Valuation.

17. Clicking End of Day will direct you to the End of Day Dashboard where you can close each period

Fields And Definitions

Invoice Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Invoices through. In other words, Balanced Load Sheets and Invoices dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Accounts Receivable Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Accounts Receivable through. In other words, Balanced Deposits dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Accounts Payable Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Accounts Payable through. In other words, Confirmed Purchases dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Financial Close - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Financials through. In other words, Balanced Journal Entries dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Best Practices

  • Run Invoice Close, Accounts Receivable Close, and Accounts Payable Close on a daily basis or as frequently as possible.
