Distributor steps for creating API Tokens on an Application in Encompass so API Commands run without a logged-in user, plus token security tips. Needs API Edit and API Solution Admin permissions.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • User must have API Edit and API Solution Admin permission to be able to view, create, and edit API Tokens.

Steps

When an API request is made to Encompass, the request must either being from an actively logged in user, or it must include an active API Token in the request body.

API Tokens are what allows your API Commands to be accessible without being actively logged into the system.

If an actively logged in user accesses a URL with an API Token on it, the API Token will be ignored, the user's session will take preference over the API Token.

To create an API Token (requires API Solution Admin permission):

  1. Go to your Application on the Applications table, the same Application with the API Commands that the token will be used on.
    ​
    ​

  2. Click Sub-Tables -> API Tokens
    ​
    ​

  3. Click the 'Add API Tokens' button
    ​
    ​

  4. For the Permission Code Arr value, you will need to enter a delimited list of permissions that this API Token should have, separated by the ! (exclamation) character

Example PermissionCodeArr:

Everyone!IsEmployee!TableImport!FusionView!CustomerView

Best Practices

  • API Tokens must be kept secret, they should be treated the same as a username/password combination
    ​
    ​

  • Periodically rotate your API Tokens by creating a new one, replacing it in your application/code, and then deactivating the old one
    ​
    ​

  • If an API Token is suspected to be compromised, replace it with a new one
    ​
    ​

  • API Tokens should be sent in the HTTP request body for improved security
    ​
    ​

  • Do not grant your API Token more permission codes than are necessary
16990810:
Distributor steps for setting up 2023 Red Bull VIP promotions in Encompass by importing Lines, Markets, Zones, Promotions Zones and Promotions, then adding customers to zones and activating. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

How to Set up RedBull VIP Promotions

The Codes table in your Encompass database (ECP 21.01 and above) has been updated with the 2023 Red Bull VIP Codes. The 2023 Red Bull VIP Promotion structure and the structure of the import files is exactly the same as it was for 2022. Again this year, Encompass has included an example of each of the 4 import files that are needed with the purpose of presenting the correct structure (columns) for the import files. Please note that while these files are structurally correct, they are also incomplete. You will need to ensure that the import files you create contain all the data that is needed

  1. Create Lines
    ​
    See “Example - 2023 VIP Lines.xlsx”
    ​
    You will need 4 Lines: RB 8 oz, RB 12 oz, RB 16 oz, and RB 20 oz. If you do not already have these Lines set up, you will need to create them.
    ​
    ​
    ​

  2. Create Import Files
    ​
    ​Markets Import File
    ​
    See “Example - 2023 VIP Markets.xlsx”
    ​
    Market records carry the RB VIP Code that will be associated with invoice transactions that utilize promotion(s) associated with the Market.
    ​
    This import file should contain one line for each separate Market that you need to support the 2023 VIP promotional structure, along with the 2023 VIP Code that goes with that Market.
    ​
    Pricing Program Markets: Display Drive Promotions will still be referred to as “Pricing Programs”. These Pricing Program Markets will have different VIP Codes starting with RBNA20DD1, RBNA20DD2, etc.
    ​
    ​Zones Import File
    ​
    ​    See “Example - 2023 VIP Zones.xlsx”
    ​
    Zones will be used to specify which customers qualify for which specific 2023 VIP Program. In this approach to setting up the 2023 VIP promotional structure, there should be one Zone record for each Market created.
    ​
    This import file should contain one line for each separate Zone that you need to support the 2023 VIP promotional structure, along with a column “Add to New Customers” set to a value of 0 to ensure that new customers are not automatically added to the Zone.
    ​
    ​Promotions Zones Import File
    ​
    ​    See “Example - 2023 VIP Promotions Zones.xlsx”
    ​
    Promotions Zones record link a Zone to a Market.
    ​
    This import file should contain one line for each separate Zone and Market combination. There should only be as many lines in this file as there are Zones (or Markets) as in this approach, there is a 1-to-1 relationship between Zones and Markets.
    ​
    ​Promotions Import File
    ​
    ​    See “Example - 2023 VIP Promotions.xlsx”
    ​
    Promotions are where we bring it all together: Markets (with their Zone and VIP Codes) and the 2023 Pricing structure. As in years before, Encompass recommends that VIP Promotions are set up as “Price” type promotions, where the Amount on the promotion record is the actual price to retailers. For example, a product has a full price of $50. To create a record where the retailer gets a $4.00 discount and you get a $2.00 bill back, create a Price type promotion for that product with an Amount = $46.00 and Participation = $2.00.
    ​
    Again this year, RBNA has also asked that distributors “set up zero discount promotions on 16/20oz for VIP stores so that VIP promo codes (e.g. RBNA2056BN) is sent on all SKU's per invoice”. This is supported in Encompass using the same Price type promotions as for the 8oz and 12oz products, only where the Amount field contains the Full Price and the Participation =$0. The example import file shows entries for the “zero discount” promotions highlighted with BLUE letters.
    ​
    The approach recommended by Encompass will organize Promotions that are organized by product Lines (8oz, 12 oz, 16 oz, and 20 oz), so that for each Market (e.g. 2023 TDiamond Premium FDC Cooler) you will generally have four (4) promotions associated with that Market, one for each Line. In the case of Pricing Programs (new Display Drives), a single Market will have one promotion for each Line / Display Drive combination (again, see Example - 2023 VIP Promotions.xlsx file).
    ​
    The example file contains the columns required to properly import promotions into Encompass using Table Import. The file should contain a single record for each unique promotion (Market -> Line -> Date Range). Be sure that values in the Lines column exactly match the names of the Lines in your system (see Section I above). You will need to enter the proper Amount, Participation, and Start/End Dates values based on the information you received from RBNA. Also, it is important that the data in the Active column is 0. This will create each promotion as Inactive, allowing you to review and confirm the data in the created promotions.
    ​
    ​

  3. Import the Files
    ​
    Once you have created the 4 import files and confirmed that they contain all the required: Markets, Zones, Promotions Zones, and Promotions (check this one twice!), you will need to import these files.
    ​
    Unsure of how to map the fields? Take a look at the screenshots in this guide: Red Bull VIP Promotions Setup - Encompass
    ​
    ​

  4. Confirm Data and Next Steps
    ​
    Once the data is in Encompass, there are only a couple of steps left to complete the 2023 RedBull VIP Promotional setup.
    ​
    1) Confirm the imported data - Take a look at each of the tables for which data was imported--Markets, Zones, Promotions Zones, and Promotions--and confirm that the data you intended to import was actually imported. The Promotions were imported in the Inactive status, so you will need to change the default view of the Promotions table to see the data that you imported.
    ​
    2) Add Customers to Zones
    ​
    You will need to add customers to the appropriate Zones for each of the Zones records that you created importing the Zones import file.
    ​
    3) Add Promotions Locations to the Market or to the Promotion Record
    ​
    Once the Market has been created you will need to add Promotions Locations for each Market record that you created importing the Markets import file (Step 1 of Section II) or you will need to add Promotions Locations for each Promotion record that you created importing the Promotions import file.
    ​
    4) Activate the imported Promotions
    ​
    Once the imported data is confirmed and all the customers are associated with the appropriate Zones, you can activate the promotions imported during this process. You are ready to go!
    ​
    ​
    ​

At this point, you have now completed all necessary imports to set up the 2023 Red Bull VIP Promotions in your site. Again, please ensure that customers are in the correct Zones and that Products are in the correct Lines.

For questions about pricing, requirements surrounding the special “zero discount” promotions for 16oz and 20oz products, or about the 2023 Red Bull VIP Program itself, please contact RBNA.

Distributor steps for creating, editing and assigning Document Templates (invoice, BOL, quote) in Encompass, and finding which template prints for a customer, chain, location or split invoice. Requires v23.01+.

Steps

Once an Invoice template is created in Template designer, the next step is to assign the Template to a Document Template. Then, The Document Template is assigned at the Location, Chain, Customer or Split Invoice level.
​
​
​How to create a document template:
​
​

  1. Go to the Document Template Table

    ​

  2. Click Add Document Template

  3. Enter a document template name

    ​

    ​
    ​

  5. Click Add Record
    ​
    ​
    ​

How to edit a Document Template:
​
​

  1. Go to the Document Template Table
    ​
    ​

  2. Select a Document Template
    ​
    ​

  3. Click edit record or edit a specific field
    ​
    ​

  4. Update the name or templates

    ​

  5. Click Save Changes

​
​How to set a Document Template:
​
​

  1. Go to the Table where you would like to check or set the Document Template (Locations, Chains, Customers, or Split Invoices)
    ​
    ​

  2. Filter to the specific record you would like to update.
    ​
    ​

  3. Click the edit icon under the Document Template field
    ​
    ​

  4. Select your Document Template
    ​
    ​

  5. Click Save Changes

Troubleshooting Which Template is BeingUsed
​
​

  1. Open the Split invoice record on a particular invoice. Is there a Document Template assigned? If yes, we will be using this template on this invoice.
    ​
    ​

  2. If not, open the Customer record on the Invoice. Is there a Document Template assigned? If yes, this Customer uses the Invoice/BOL/Quote template within the assigned Document Template.
    ​
    ​

  3. If not, open the Chain record the Customer belongs to. Is there a Document Template assigned? If yes, the Chain as a whole uses the Invoice/BOL/Quote template within the assigned Document Template.
    ​
    ​

  4. If the Document Template is not assigned to any of the above records, then click on the Location on the Customer record. The Document Template (and thus the Invoice/BOL/Quote template within the Document Template) assigned here applies to all customers within the Location as the Default.

Fields And Definitions

  • Document Templates: Acts as a folder containing your Invoice, Bill of Lading, and Quote Templates. The templates can be specifically formatted in the Template Designer to ensure when printing, each print as expected and as desired for specific invoices, customers, chains, or locations. The Document Template can be set in 4 places and is a granular hierarchy on which is chosen. Essentially this means if it is set on the lowest level, it will override whatever is higher in the hierarchy.
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Template: The invoice template that prints once invoices are locked.
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice Bill of Lading Template: The Invoice Bill of Lading Template that prints when invoices are not yet locked/delivered.
    ​
    ​

  • Quote Template: The Quote Template that prints for all invoices on a Quote route type.

Best Practices

Template Hierarchy
​
​(Highest level of granularity to lowest level)
​
​

  1. Split Invoice - set on the Customer or Chain Split Invoice Record. This is used when a customer needs something like non-alc and alc products looking different on split invoices. (Overrides Customer, Chain and Location Template)
    ​
    ​

  2. Customer - set on the Customers Table. Used for a specific customer needing a specific invoice view. (Overrides Chain and Location Template)
    ​
    ​

  3. Chain - set on the Chains Table. Used when a specific chain needs a specific template view. (Overrides Location Template)
    ​
    ​

  4. *Location - linked through the Customers Location. Applies to all Customers in the Location. (Default Template when none of the above are set)

  • If the Document Template is set at any level, it will override any Document Template set at a lower level of granularity.
    ​
    - Example: If a Document Template is set on both the Customer and the Chain, the Customer Document Template is used because it is higher in the heirarchy.
    ​
    - If all Customers in a Chain should use the same Document Template, the Document Template should be left blank/Null on the Customer records.
    ​
    ​

  • Document Templates are required on the Locations Table, so if a Customer/Chain does not have a Custom Template, it will default to the Location Document Template.
    ​
    ​

  • Make Document Template names descriptive to let others know at a glance what the Template is for. (Walmart Chain, Location A Default, Walmart #293 w/ AR, etc.)

16990823:
Distributor guide to UPC formats Encompass accepts (UPC-A, UPC-E, EAN-13, GTIN-14), how check digits are auto-validated, and setting retailer UPC overrides. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

The Universal Product Code (UPC or UPC code) is a barcode symbology that is widely used worldwide for tracking trade items in stores.

Resources for general learning on the UPC standard:

  • Wikipedia
    ​
    ​

  • GS1
    ​
    ​

  • How Stuff Works

Encompass supports the entry of the following UPC formats in the UPC fields in the system:

  • UPC-A, commonly called just UPC, also known as GTIN-12
    ​
    ​

  • UPC-E, also known as GTIN-8, or a compressed UPC, can be 7 digits as well
    ​
    ​

  • EAN-13, also known as GTIN-13, or just EAN
    ​
    ​

  • GTIN-14

When a UPC value is entered into Encompass, the system will check that it is a valid UPC.
​
​

These checks include:

  • If length = 10, a 0 is automatically added to the beginning of the UPC, and the check-digit (last digit) is automatically calculated and added
    ​
    ​

  • If length = 11, the check-digit (last digit) is automatically calculated and added
    ​
    ​

  • If length = 12 13 or 14, the check-digit (last digit) is re-calculated to ensure it is a valid calculation for barcode scanners to be able to read

In EDI and other formats where a particular UPC format from the list above is required, the system will attempt to convert the UPC to the right format.
​
This is not always possible when going from a larger format to a smaller format.
​
For example: a UPC-E can always be converted to a UPC-A or EAN-13, but a UPC-A cannot always be compressed to a UPC-E

Best Practices

  • Encompass recommends putting the UPC-A code throughout the system, this code format tends to scan the easiest by barcode scanners.
    ​
    ​

  • Overrides for certain retailers that require their UPCs in a different format can be put on the Product Authorizations table for that chain, in the UPC Override column.

16990830:
Driver/rep guide to the DEX steps on Encompass Mobile (SendInvoice, SendTotal, StoreResponse, ErrorMessage) in the invoice DEX audit, to troubleshoot failed DEX connections. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

1. PFD Type

The type of device that is selected to be DEXed. This will include the serial number of the device and PFD if it was DEXed on a PFDex unit or GKP if it was DEXed on a Gimme Key device
​
​

2. SendInvoice

If DEX is connecting, SendInvoice status will appear in invoice DEX audit. SendInvoice represents the connected data and the current DEX status is connecting. If successful, it will enter the SendTotal state, and the data will be sent from the handheld to the DEX device. And the handheld terminal will prompt that the connection is successful. If it fails, the connection fails and ErrorMessage is added.


3. SendTotal

When the DEX connection is successful, it will enter the SendTotal state. At this time, the correct DEX operation should be that we view the invoice data to be modified in the DEX system and modify it. After the modification is completed. The handset will perform get response. At this time, the DEX system will send to the handheld terminal, and the handheld terminal will receive. Successful reception will lead to StoreResponse. Failure will prompt 'StoreResponse not received. The connection may have dropped, or the Duns and UCCI are not configured correctly. Please check your configurations and try to DEX again'。


4. StoreResponse

When the handheld terminal receives the data modified by DEX, it will be reflected by the StoreResponse status. At this time, the handheld terminal will update the data of the current invoice and recalculate the price according to the current invoice. After the StoreResponse is completed, the invoice will be locked.


5. ErrorMessage:

The function of ErrorMessage is to clearly know the reason of DEX failure. If we have problems in the normal operation of DEX, there will be an error message. At this point, we can learn why it failed from ErrorMessage. Therefore, in DEX operation, please do not close the connection or interrupt at will.

Fields And Definitions

  • If the data in invoice DEX audit is not present it is likely that the DEX operation was not performed. The connection has not been executed. It may be that the Bluetooth connection is not properly operated. Or customer and settings related DEX configuration is not added.

Distributor steps for tracking pallet code dates with Bin Lots in Encompass: set a Bin Zone to require pallet tags, create lots via PocketWMS moves, then view, count and track them. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

How to set up Bin Zones

In order to create Bin Lots, a Bin Zone will be designated to require Pallet Tag scanning. When this is changed, any movement of a pallet into or out of the Bin Zone will require a scan of the pallet tag.

1. In Encompass, search for Bin Zones

2. Edit the Bin Zone that will monitor and create Bin Lots. Edit “Require Pallet Tag” from No to Always: Transactional Bin Lots

How to Create Bin Lots

Bin Lot records are created when performing a Move in PocketWMS into the Bin Zone created in "How to set up Bin Zones". This section will step through that process.

1. On the handheld, navigate to PocketWMS. Click Move.

2. Scan the From Bin. This feature is intended to be used upon Receiving, so this will most likely be the Receiving bin, but Bin Lots will be created whenever a pallet is moved into or out of the Bin Zones edited in “How to set up Bin Zones”

3. Select a product in the From Bin. Check that an entire pallet is about to be moved.

4. Select a Bin inside the Bin Zone that has “Require Pallet Tag = True” that was set up in “How to set up Bin Zones.” A prompt will appear to scan the Pallet Tag for the Pallet that is being moved.

5. After the Pallet Tag is scanned, a Bin Lot will be created on the Bin Lots table. See the next section. Currently, Bin Lots are created when performing a move on PocketWMS. This action will also occur in Directed Replenish and Directed Inventory.

How to View Bin Lots on WMS Handheld

1. On the handheld, navigate to pocket WMS. Click Warehouse Search.

2. Scan product, then tap the plus button next to a Bin to display all the Lots within that Bin

How to Count Bin Lots

Counting of Bin Lots must occur if the total Bin inventory entered during a count does not match the existing count in the system. At that point, the counter will be prompted to enter specific quantities for each Lot in the Bin.

1. On the handheld, navigate to pocket WMS. Click Inventory Count

2. Scan Bin/Product and enter count

3. If entered count does not match expected count, user will be prompted and required to enter specific quantities of each Lot in that Bin

How to View/Track on Bin Lots Table

When pallets are scanned and moved into or out of a Bin Zone with Require Pallet Tag = Always, Bin Lot records are created on the Bin Lots table.

1. Search for the Bin Lots table

2. On this table, each pallet and its original Purchase Trans ID can be seen as it moves around the warehouse. Notice that, although we have multiple records for the same product, we have differing Purchase Trans ID.

3. Click on a Purchase Trans ID for a product, and hit the plus button next to “Layer”. This is where the actual code date for that pallet is stored.

Following these steps will allow you to more accurately and easily monitor code dates for pallets as they move into and out of specific Bin Zones.

16990854:
Distributor guide to the VIPR (BudNet) pricing file layout from Encompass and which customers, frontline zones and promotions it includes, to troubleshoot missing pricing or products. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Communicating VIPR pricing through EDI
    ​

  • Legacy Front Line Zone needs to be set on Distribution Area

  • Legacy Front Line Zone needs to tied to Frontline Promotions

Steps

VIPR File Format:
​
​Line number:
Description of line and related fields
​
​
Header:
PHDR00: File Name
​
​
​Areas and Zones
​01: Legacy Front line zones tied to distribution areas (Format = AR + ZoneID of the legacy frontline zone on the distribution area)
​
02: Promotion Zones tied to pricing (Format = ZN + ZoneID)
​
​
​Customers:
​10: CustomerID
​
11: Distribution Area Legacy Front line zone this customer is associated with
​
12: Pricing areas this customer is associated with
​
​
​Frontlines:
​20: Product Information
​
21: Pricing information associated with a specific Legacy Front line zone
​
​
​Promotions:
​40: Promotion/Product Line
​
45: Zones where this promotion applies
​
50: EDI Codes
​
51: Discount amount
​
54: Product ID and Unit Discount/price

Fields And Definitions

What customers are commincated through VIPR:
​
​Customers found by below checks will be in the BudNet VIPR file:
​
​

  1. CustomerListTempTable.CustomerID = Customers.CustomerID
    ​
    ​

  2. Customers.AccountStatus = Active or CustomerID in CustomerIDAccountStatusChangeArr or CustomerID in CustomerIDHasInvoiceOnLastSentDateArr
    ​
    ​

  3. Customers.CustomerType -> CustomerTypes.CustomerAccountType = 1
    ​
    ​

  4. Customers.DistributionArea -> Areas.Location = SuppliersReports.Location.

What pricing is included in a VIPR File:
​
​

Promotions found by below checks will be in the BudNet VIPR file:
​
1. The PromotionsProducts or the Line Products of Promotions.Line have Inventories with VALID Inventory.SupplierProductNumEffective and TRUE Inventory.ActiveEffective.

A. Products.IncludeinSupplierReports <> Exclude.
​
B. Inventory.SupplierProductNumEffective<> NULL.
​
C. Inventory.SupplierProductNumEffective recorded in the Suppliers Products table.
​
D. The SuppliersProducts.Supplier of theSupplier Products in item(c.) recorded in the Suppliers Reports table with ReportType=BudNet.
​
E. SuppliersReports.LocationID in item (d.) = Inventory.LocationID.
​
F. SuppliersReports.SupplierID = Inventory.SupplierIDEffective.
​
2. The PromotionsZones, PromotionsChains or PromotionsCustomers enable them to buy the products.
​
3.The Promotions.PromotionType should be of the below four types.
​
A. Discount
​
B. Case Discount
​
C. Price
​
D. Case Price

Best Practices

  • Check the file to determine how to correct the issue.
    ​
    ​

  • Is pricing not reported correctly? Are the right zones tied to the promotion? Is the promotion Active? Does it meet the requirements outlined in fields and definitions?
    ​
    ​

  • Is a product not reporting? Can that customer purchase the product? Is it active? Does it meet the requirements outlined in fields and definitions?

16990867:
Distributor/producer steps for fixing leftover inventory value on a product with zero quantity under Average Costing in Encompass, using an in/out purchase to COGS. Requires v23.04+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.04

Pre-Conditions

  • Costing Method = Average

Steps

When using Average Costing, certain conditions can lead to a product having Inventory Value even when Inventory Quantity is zero.

Two common reasons for this condition are:
​
1. Selling inventory prior to confirming the related purchase
​
2. Incurring significant delays in running End of Day

Either of these can result in a lag in updating the moving average which can result in over/under application of cost of goods sold. This valuation can be corrected with an in/out purchase.

If Inventory Value is positive:
​
1. Create purchase under the vendor you use for production orders
​
2. Add the product(s) that need revaluation
​
3. Add quantity of -1 and populate FOB with the value needing to write-off
​
4. Add that same product again with a quantity of 1 and FOB = $0
​
5. Add a non-inventory product mapped to an inventory adjustment COGS account
​
​6. Add quantity of 1 and FOB = value in Step 3
​
7. Ensure purchase total = $0 and check purchase accounts for desired GL impact
​
8. Confirm purchase

If Inventory Value is negative:
​
1. Create purchase under the vendor you use for production orders
​
2. Add the product(s) that need revaluation
​
3. Add quantity of 1 and populate FOB with the value needing to write-up
​
4. Add that same product again with a quantity of -1 and FOB = $0
​
5. Add a non-inventory product mapped to an inventory adjustment COGS account
​
​6. Add quantity of -1 and FOB = value in Step 3
​
7. Ensure purchase total = $0 and check purchase accounts for desired GL impact
​
8. Confirm purchase

Steps

Breakage Bin


Click to View Adjustments Bin Types to find Breakage Bin with Bin Inventories showing


Broken cases should always be moved into the Breakage bin.

How to Address Breakage in the Warehouse

  1. Log into Encompass Mobile Warehouse

    ​

  2. From the main menu, tap "Move"

    ​

  3. Scan the bin that breakage was found in, this is usually a pick or backstock bin

  4. Scan the product

    ​

  6. Scan the Breakage bin, or search for "break" to find it

    ​

  7. If searching, tap the Breakage bin when it appears in the search

    ​

  8. The broken cases have now been moved

How to Address Breakage on a Truck

  1. When doing truck return, go to the "Count In" tab
    ​
    ​

  2. Fill in full case quantities for any broken cases to the Breakage reason
    ​
    ​

  3. These broken cases will be either immediately written off, or directed to the warehouse breakage bin, according to Return Rules
    ​
    ​

  4. For more information on Return Rules, please visit Help Resources

Repack Bin
​
​

Click to View Adjustments Bin Types to find Repack Bin with Bin Inventories showing
​
​

Repacked cases should always be moved from the Repack bin.
​
​

Repacked cases can be the same package or a different from what was originally broken.

How to Address Newly Repacked Product

  1. Log into Encompass Mobile Warehouse
    ​
    ​

  2. From the main menu, tap "Move"
    ​
    ​

  3. Scan the Repack bin, or search for "repack" to find it
    ​
    ​

  4. Scan the product
    ​
    ​

  5. Enter the quantity of repacked cases
    ​
    ​

  6. Scan the bin the repacked product is being moved to, or type the bin name in the search box to find it
    ​
    ​

  7. If searching, tap the searched bin when it appears
    ​
    ​

  8. The repacked cases have now been moved

Reconciling Breakage & Repack
​
​

Link to the Breakage & Repack Bin Zones on the Warehouse Inventory Bins Report
​
​

The Breakage bin should always have all positive units, while the Repack bin should always have all negative units. While the case quantity between the two bins may not be an exact match, the net value between the two bins shows the true money loss from broken cases, regardless of the packages.
​
​

IMPORTANT: No movement should ever occur between the Breakage and Repack bins. Breakage ALWAYS goes to the Breakage bin, and Repacks ALWAYS comes from the Repack bin.

How to Adjust Breakage & Repack Inventory

  1. Click the button above to get to the Inventory Bins report

Fields And Definitions

16990873:
Distributor explanation of how Encompass Financials creates the year-end Retained Earnings journal entry at Financial Close based on Fiscal Year Last Month, and how to redo it. Requires v20.05+.

Minimum Version Required: 20.05

Pre-Conditions

  • Must be on Encompass Financials

Steps

There is a field on the Companies Table called Fiscal Year Last Month. When Financial Period Close is run for the first day of the following period, Retained Earnings Journal Entries will be created.
​
​

Here is how the logic works:
​
1. On Financial Close, calculate what the date of the year-end entry would be. For Fiscal Year End = September, the date would be 10/1/2023
​
2. Check that the current Financial Close Date is less than that calculated Year End Entry Date
​
3. Check that the new Financial Close Date we want to close through is greater than or equal to the calculated Year End Entry Date
​
4. Look for an existing Year End Journal Entry with a Date = 10/1/2023
​
5. If the Journal Entry does not already exist, Encompass will create a new one and calculate its transactions.
​
6. These Journal Entries are calculated by zeroing all accounts from the Income Statement and moving them to Retained Earnings.

Please note, if the year-end Retained Earnings Entry needs to be adjusted, this can be accomplished by reopening and re-closing the financial period.

Steps

Oftentimes, we want to package out a partial case or keg of finished goods. Products.SellByCaseOnly determines what partials the system allows.
​
​

  • If Products.SellByCaseOnly=SellByCaseOnly, users can enter packaged totals in whole numbers.

By allowing decimals, users can input decimals up to four which is ideal for packaging into kegs or totes. Best practice for packaged product is to create full consumable units at a time.

​
​

Consumable Units Per Case:

Consumable units per case can be found on the Package record. For example, a case of 24 cans has 24 consumable units in it. To avoid packaging a partial can, the system will round to the nearest full can when a user inputs a partial case when expressing the packaging prodution order.

Best Practices

  • When building new Products, copy similar existing Products which have the fields already set accordingly.
    ​
    ​

  • Set draft to package by decimals, but cases of cans or bottles to package by the COnsumable Unit to avoid inventorying low-fills.

Producer steps for reviewing and verifying Production Order input and output costs on the Production Costing Confirmation dashboard. Needs System Setting 553, Production Edit permission and v23.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.10

Pre-Conditions

Once this feature is enabled, all PdOs and their respective Purchases for the associated Vendor(s) must be Verified through this workflow.

  • System Setting 553 = True
    ​
    ​

  • Vendors.ConfirmProductionCost = True (this is for all Production Vendors)
    ​
    ​

  • ProductionOrders.Status = Confirmed
    ​
    ​

  • User must have Production Edit permission
    ​
    ​

  • ProductionOrders.ProductionOrderType <> SAP Imported

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Empty State Dashboard:
​
​

  • For ANY results to show, the Production Vendor(s) must be set to Confirm Production Cost = True.
    ​
    ​

  • All filters will be empty to begin, at least one filter must be filled to return results.
    ​
    ​

  • If no filters are filled in, a snackbar will appear at the bottom of the screen saying to please select filters.

Apply Filters:
​
​

1. Once the desired filter(s) have been populated, clicking Apply Filters will bring results.
​
2. The initial view will be at the Batch level and list the most important information. Total Value, specifically, is a sum of the Produced value of all Production Orders in that Batch.
​
3. Clicking the + icon will expand the view to all Completed Production Orders for the associated Batch(es).
​
4. Viewing the “drill down” section on the right, for an output Product (ProductionOrders.Product) gives instant insight into produced cost, historical cost, and inventoried cost:

  • Produced at gives the selected Product's completed output cost for the selected Production Order - hover over the tooltip for 6 decimal places of precision
    ​
    ​

  • Last produced at will tell you the produced cost of the Product on the most recent Verified Production Order - tooltip gives the date the Production Order was completed
    ​
    ​

  • Current cost will match the Current Laid-In Cost (FIFO) or the current Average Cost (Average) - tooltip tells the user if the Product is using FIFO or Average costing
    ​
    ​

  • Product Cost Plan will only populate if a Product Cost Plan exists for the selected Product
    ​
    ​

  • Bottom right section will show the five most recent, Verified, Production Orders for the selected Product, giving you a snapshot comparison of costing trends

Production Components:
​
​

1. Clicking the + icon next to a Production Order will populate a list of all Production Components. This gives you the full view of every contributing factor to the costing of the output product.
​
2. Clicking on a Production Component will populate the drill down section with relevant costing information.
​
3. The top section of the Production Component drill down contains:

  • The Product and it's assigned Package (purchasing unit) listed underneath - this is to give immediate reference when there is a discrepancy between purchasing unit and consumption unit
    ​
    ​

  • Consumed at cost - gives the selected Product's consumed Unit of Measure cost for the selected Production Order to easily compare purchasing unit costing and historically consumed unit costing - hover over the tooltip for 6 decimal places of precisionl
    ​
    ​

  • Product Cost Plan - This field only appears if a Product Cost Plan for the Product exists and will reference the Case Cost (which is identical to the purchasing unit cost)
    ​
    ​

  • Last consumed at is an immediate reference to the Verified costing used the last time this Product was consumed as a Production Component - the tooltip gives you the completion date of the Production Order being referenced
    ​
    ​

  • Current cost is the active costing for the purchasing unit which references the Current Laid-In Cost (FIFO) or Average Cost (Average) - hover over the tooltip to see if the Product is using FIFO or Average costing
    ​
    ​

  • Note: Only production components with actual units greater than 0 will be shown in this section

The bottom right section of the Production Component drill down contains all Purchase Transactions (costing layers) that currently have On Hand inventory - this is relevant for both FIFO and Average costing because this information is ALL FIFO layers to show the user the upcoming trends in costing AND all costing layers that contribute to the Average Cost calculation.

Verify Costing:

1. Once you have reviewed and confirmed all input and output costing appears as expected, proceed to Verify Costing. Once this feature is enabled, all PdOs and their respective Purchases for the associated Vendor(s) must be Verified through this workflow.
​
​2. When the user clicks the Verify Costing button, the screen will appear very similar to AR Aging, AP Aging, Inventory Bins Write-Off, etc. with a checkbox enabled multi-select view, condensed to the Batch level.
​
3. Clicking the + icon will expand the view to the Production Order level. You can select the entire Batch, individual Production Orders, and any combination of those to quickly verify the costing they have reviewed and confirmed.
​
4. Once the desired Batch(es) and Production Order(s) have been selected, clicking the Verify button at the bottom of the screen will Verify all related Production Orders.

Fields And Definitions

Vendors.ConfirmProductionCost - this field enables and requires Production Orders from this Vendor to be Verified through the Production Costing Confirmation dashboard

Best Practices

  • Set Vendors.ConfirmProductionCost = True for all Production Vendors
    ​
    ​

  • Show In Progress Batches = True
    ​
    ​

  • If costing on the Production Component summary does not appear accurate, click the Production Component to get detailed information
    ​
    ​

  • Two decimal places of precision are shown, hover over the tooltip of Produced at or Consumed at to get 6 decimal places of precision (detailed costing)

  • BarrelType

  • Condition

  • CharLevel

  • UnitPrice. The cost of the product filled in the barrel

  • NumUnits. The quantity of product filled in the barrel

  • Proof. The Proof of the product filled in the barrel

  • Expiration date. The expiration date of the product filled in the barrel

  • CodeDate. The code date of the product filled in the barrel

  • BatchCode. The batch of the product filled in the barrel

  • BinLotID. When the BinLotID is mapped, EDBL will fill its inventory into the barrel

  • ReceiveDate. Only set if you need to create a wine barrel purchase record

  • VendorID or VendorID_Translation. Only set if you need to create a wine barrel purchase record

Best Practices

  • Break the data down by Location and import each Location separately

Steps

My Profile is available to all users to allow them to set many personal system configuration options

Sections:

Authentication (left side)

  • Email Verified: will display if the system has verified that you are the owner of the email address attached to this account. Click the 'verify' link if not yet verified, and an email will be sent to you.

  • Mobile Verified: will display if the system has verified that you are the owner of the mobile phone number attached to this account. Click the 'verify' link if not yet verified, and a text message will be sent to you.

  • Reset Password: will reset your own password to a new value

  • Trusted Devices: For systems with MFA enabled, this button will bring up a list of devices where you have trusted the device for 30 days. You can manually remove trusted devices from the dialog.

  • OAuth connections (if enabled): If your administrator has setup OAuth (aka: Sign in with Google, Sign in with Microsoft, etc...) then the options to connect your 3rd party account to your Encompass account will display here

Global Authentication Information

These settings apply to ALL Encompass systems accessed by this user.

  • Time zone: Controls which time zone all of the date/time values in the system are displayed in

  • Date display format: Controls how the dates throughout Encompass are displayed

  • Time display format: Controls how the times throughout Encompass are displayed

  • Preferred Support Communication method (see related Help Resource): Controls the default communication method when interacting with Support

  • Language: Controls the system language

Session Information

These settings only apply to the local system you are currently on.

  • Release Cycle: Controls if you are on the nightly (A) or weekly (B) release of code. Changing this is a convenient way to toggle between code versions in case of a recent issue in a code release from Encompass.

  • Companies: Filters the entire system to only display information for the selected Companies

  • Locations: Filters the entire system to only display information for the selected Locations

User Information

This is static information for the local system. You can update the following information from this section:

  • Full Name - This is the name on your user account on the current site. If updated from your primary site, this will also update the name on your global authentication.

  • Username - This is the username associated with your account. It can be used to log into the current site. Updating username does not retroactively update field audits or table fields that store user name. If you are an employee of this site, please ensure your site administrator is aware if you plan to change this field.

  • Email - This is the email that links your user to your global authentication and can be used to log into any Encompass site you have access to.

    ​    *Attention* Changing your email will impact your Global Authentication. Please contact your site administrator before making any changes to your email if you are not on your primary site or your email is currently blank.

16990933:
Distributor steps (no video) for removing special-event invoices or invoice lines from sales forecasts on the Exclude Invoices from Forecast dashboard in Encompass, and undoing it. Requires v23.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.10

Steps

If special order invoices are skewing your forecasted sales data, and you just want the sales from those invoice out of forecast data, this feature is for you! Special event invoices might include sales for fairs and rodeos, concerts, or even displays promotions.

Introducing the Exclude Invoices from Forecasting Dashboard.

How to exclude an invoice transaction or an entire invoice from forecasts:

  1. Go to the Exclude Invoices from Forecast Dashboard

  2. Apply any filters including Route, Customer, Invoice Num, Product, and Date Range

  3. Check the box next to any transaction that is to be excluded from forecasts

  4. Check the box next to any invoice to exclude the entire invoice from forecasts

  5. Click Save Changes

How to Exclude from the Forecasting Dashboard:

  1. Click on a link for any sales values for Sales, Backorders, or Backfills

  2. This will open the Forecast Sales Report Drilldown fusion report in a new tab

  3. Click on the Exclude link in the report, this will open the Exclude Invoices from Forecasts Dashboard

  4. Follow steps 3 - 5 above.

How to "undo" an invoice transaction or entire invoice that has previously been excluded from forecasts:

  1. Go to the Exclude Invoices from Forecast Dashboard

  2. Filter on the Invoice Num, Product, or Date Range

  3. Un-check the box next to the transaction or invoice

  4. Click Save Changes

How to see changes in Forcasting:

  1. In the Forecast dashboard, click the Refresh Data button to see updated sales forecasts after invoice data has bee excluded.

  2. These changes will not be reflected immediately and will require the data warehouse to sync, which runs every 15 minutes.

16990938:
Distributor guide to the Table Map in Encompass: explore how tables relate (live ERD) to find where data lives, build Fusion reports, and create or edit custom tables and fields. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

The Encompass Table Map is a live Entity Relationship Diagram (ERD) that shows how the tables in Encompass are related to each other. This can be very helpful in finding where data is stored, and how it relates to other data in the system.

It can also help with building fusion reports, and is where the functionality lives for creating/modifying/removing custom tables and custom fields (see the related Help Resource)

To use the table map:

  1. Navigate to the Table Map using the universal search at the top of any page
    ​
    ​

  2. Search for the table you would like to get information on
    ​
    ​

  3. Drag around and click the elements on the diagram to explore how the data relates to eachother
    ​
    ​

  • The ERD will draw out 2 layers of tables, unless the 'Show One Layer' option is turned at the top of the page.
    ​
    ​

  • The ERD will also only show common/default tables in the system, to show less common tables, turn on the 'Show More Tables' option at the top of the page

The Encompass database is designed in 3rd normal form.

Note: There are rare exceptions made to this for performance optimization reasons.

Fields And Definitions

Key: This contains a brief description of the color-coding used to designate parent vs child tables in the relationships

  • Options -> Center Table: This will center the table you last clicked on into view, often used if you scroll/pan too far and lose where you started
    ​
    ​

  • Options -> Map this Table: If selecting a table that is different than the one you originally search for
    ​
    ​

  • Options -> View Table: Will take you to the standard table view for this table (aka: will show the actual records in the table with the normal columns/filter options)
    ​
    ​

  • Options -> Audit: Will take you to all of the audit/change records for this table
    ​
    ​

  • Options -> Edit: Will take you to the table editor for this table. This is commonly used for Custom Tables but can be used to edit Custom Fields, Sub Tables displayed by default and more.
    ​
    ​

  • Options -> Delete: Only available on custom tables, will delete the table from the system. This is permanent. The system will prevent you from deleting a table that is used in any saved reports, or table import routines.

Fields: Lists all of the columns/fields on the table, their data type, and length of the field. More detailed information on columns/fields is available in the TableFields table.
​
Parent Tables: Listing of all of the tables that have this table as a 'Child Table/Sub-Table'
16990939:
Distributor steps for sending pricing to 99 Bottles automatically: install the app, set up 99B Price Posting Templates, and troubleshoot missing prices or products. Requires v22.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.08

Steps

The 99 Bottles Pricing API, 99Bottles_GetPricePostingData, provides a method for 99 Bottles to query Encompass for the most recent pricing for a pre-arranged set of Chains or Customers. It is designed to replace the manual generation and upload of pricing data to the 99 Bottles website. To get started, users must first download the Application in the App Library and begin to setup their Price Posting Templates.
​
​
​

General Setup:
​
​

1. Install the Application from the App Library
​
2. Create Price Positng Templates
​
3. Provide EncompassID and CustomerID set on the price posting template to 99Bottles (Note: EncompassID can be found by expanding the side menu and viewing the EncompassID under your username)
​
4. Pull data from 99 Bottles
​
​
​

Price Posting Template Setup Steps:
​
​

1. The Price Posting Template field must contain “99B” somewhere in the name. For examples, “Walmart 99B East Area”.
​

  • Posting Interval = Weekly
    ​
    ​

  • Pricing Days in the Future = 12 Weeks Out
    ​
    ​

  • Best Price = False
    ​
    ​

  • Refresh Posting = True

5. Fields such as Customer and Next Run Date must be filled in accordingly.
​
​

  • Let 99 Bottles know the initial Next Run Date value so that they can schedule their API calls to match when the data is generated.

6. Product Group is optional and could be used to filter the set of products that might appear in the data sent to 99 Bottles via the API
​
​

  • Note: Do not use the same customer twice in Price Posting Templates created for 99 Bottles as this will generate duplicate data records for the API

Fields And Definitions

Troubleshooting:
​
​

99 Bottles uses the information from Encompass to generate pricing information. If information is not correct, or you are not seeing all the expected products, you will want to check your encompass system to make sure the customer is qualified for the correct promotions and is able to purchase the product.

Pricing Issues:
​
​

  1. Check the most recent price posting for the product in question on your 99 bottles price posting template. Filter to the product in Price Posting Trans to see if the pricing/promotion is being posted. If it is not posted, you will want to make sure the customer is tied to the correct promotion zones and location to ensure they qualify for the pricing.

Product Issues:
​
​

  1. Check the most recent price posting for the product in question on your 99 bottles price posting template. Filter to the product in Price Posting Trans to see if the product is being posted. If it is not posted, you will want to make sure the customer is able to purchase this product by looking through the standard product controls such as: Product group, Brand family areas, supplier family areas, product authorizations, allocations, product status and seasonality. For more detailed information on product controls please view the help resources under 'Product Controls' in the order management section.
    ​
    ​

  2. If you are continuing to find issues in different customers under the same chain with different product sets and authorizations, you can set up a 99 bottles customer for the chain or pricing group that is not tied to any of the related product controls so you can post pricing for all products. This can be done by copying a similar customer and including the customers promotions zones when the customer is copied. Steps are included below:
    ​
    ​

​Steps to create a pricing customer:
​
​

  1. Go to the Customers table
    ​
    ​

  2. Find a customer that is receiving the pricing you would like to post to 99 Bottles
    ​
    ​

  3. Copy the customer and rename it to something relevant to your business such as 99Bottles Pricing Only *note ensure the customers promotions zones subtable is selected when copying the customer
    ​
    ​

  4. Check to make sure the customer was copied and the promotion zones are correct
    ​
    ​

  5. Update the distribution area on the customer to a distribution area with no supplier or brand family restrictions. This could be done by creating a new distribution area.
    ​
    ​

  6. Ensure the product group set on the customer contains all the product types you would like to post
    ​
    ​

  7. Finally, set the customer on the respective price posting template

Products/Pricing not coming over entirely?:
​
​

  1. Go to the App Library
    ​
    ​

  2. Go to Installed Apps
    ​
    ​

  3. Click on 99 Bottles Pricing Automation
    ​
    ​

  4. Click on 99B Price Posting Application Report
    ​
    ​

  5. Type in the Customer ID
    ​
    ​

  6. Click Create Report
    ​
    ​
    ​

If the report is generating data, contact 99 bottles to make sure they are using the correct customerID and EncompassID.
​
​

If the report is not generating any data, Please confirm you are using the correct customerID, Confirm the template has 99B in the name, and confirm the price posting template has generated a price posting export (Go to price posting templates and click subtables to select price posting exports).

Best Practices

Selecting a reference Customer:
​
​

The 99Bottles_GetPricePostingData API utilizes data generated from Price Posting Trans records belonging to Price Posting Templates set up in a specific manner and for a set of chain(s)/customer(s) that is fully controlled by the distributor. Each Price Posting Template is associated with a single Customer that represents a pricing area. A separate Price Posting Template is needed for each pricing area. For example, If there are multiple pricing areas within a single chain, you will need a separate Pricing Posting Template setup for each pricing area within that chain. If you send pricing to 99 Bottles for both Walmart and ABC Liquors, and both of these chains receive the same pricing, then you will only need a single Price Posting Template.
​
​
​
​
​Other Best Practices:
​
​

  1. Always set Next Price Posting Date in future so the system can generate pricing on the next posting date
    ​
    ​

  2. Ensure the customer on the price posting template can purchase all the products you would like to post. If this product list needs to be further refined, you can add a product group on the price posting template to further limit the products being posted
    ​
    ​

  3. After setup, I would recommend reviewing the price posting template to ensure the next posting date is updated accordingly the day after the next posting date manually set on the template.
    ​
    ​

  4. Price posting will generate data overnight, so you will be able to post pricing in 99 Bottles the day after the posting.

*Note: Promotions in Encompass that are setup with no min purchase will show in 99 bottles as a min purchase of 1 to better match retailer requirements
16990940:
Distributor troubleshooting for QuickBooks Desktop sync errors at End of Day in Encompass: mismatched journal entries, invoice numbers over 20 characters, missing ListIDs, can't open QB file. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Companies.GeneralAccountSystem = QuickBooks

Steps

Common QuickBooks Desktop Sync errors and how to troubleshoot them:

Journal Entry in Encompass Does Not Match QB Journal Entry:

  • This message appears when the sync detects a Journal No. in QuickBooks (Enc JE ID: ####) that matches a Journal Entry ID in Encompass (####) AND the Journal Entry amounts do not match

  • Ensure the Journal No. in QuickBooks is not being posted from another source (many QuickBooks integrations will take the most recent Journal No. and replicate it)

  • If the Journal Entry is from Encompass, ensure the Journal Entry in QuickBooks was not manually edited

  • Syncing to QuickBooks requires any validated Journal Entry match between both systems to prevent subledger discrepancies

  • Once the Journal Entry in QuickBooks is updated, run the sync client again

Quickbooks requires that the length of Purchases.InvoiceNum cannot exceed 20 characters:

  • This message appears due to a QuickBooks restriction on the length of an Invoice Number on a synced Purchase

  • Copy the PurchaseID(s) listed

  • Go to the Purchases table and select the PurchaseID(s) from the error message

  • Edit the Invoice Number on the Purchase(s) to be 20 or fewer total characters (including spaces)

  • Editing the Purchase(s) may require UnConfirming

  • Once all Purchases have been updated with the allowable length Invoice Number re-sync to QuickBooks

AccountID = # on JE #### has an empty string ListID:

  • This message appears when an Account in Encompass has not been synced to an Account in QuickBooks and Encompass cannot find an exact match (Accounts.Account, Accounts.QBAccountType)

  • If the Account listed does exist in QuickBooks, Encompass has already matched the QuickBooks Account with a different Encompass Account

  • Check similarly named Accounts in Encompass and clear the ListID field if this is a mismatch

  • If the Account listed does not exist in QuickBooks, create the Account in QuickBooks

  • Once the above step(s) have been completed, re-run the sync client

AccountID # is set as the Accounts Payable Account on APAccount ____ and is missing a ListID:

  • This message appears when an Account with AccountType = AccountsPayable in Encompass has not been synced to an Account in QuickBooks and Encompass cannot find an exact match

  • If the Account listed does exist in QuickBooks, Encompass has already matched the QuickBooks Account with a different Encompass Account

  • Check similarly named Accounts in Encompass and clear the ListID field if this is a mismatch

  • If the Account listed does not exist in QuickBooks, create the Account in QuickBooks

  • Once the above step(s) have been completed, re-run the sync client

Could not open QuickBooks File:

  • This message appears when the sync client cannot detect the QuickBooks file

  • Ensure your QuickBooks company file is open

  • In QuickBooks, press Ctrl + 1 to view the file path for your QuickBooks company file

  • In Encompass, go to the Companies table and compare the file path set in the Company File field to the file path displayed in QuickBooks

  • If these do not match, edit the Company File field to match the file path displayed in QuickBooks and then re-run the sync client

  • If these do match, re-run the sync client

  • If the same message appears, edit the Company File field to [none] and re-run the sync client with the QuickBooks company file open

Fields And Definitions

The system uses the following condition to sync the purchase to QB:

  1. APAccounts.CompanyID = Currenct select Company in QB

  2. Purchases.PostDate = New PeriodCloseDate of Company

  3. PurchaseAccounts.Debit <> 0 OR PurchaseAccounts.Credit <> 0

  4. Shipments.Status =Verified

  5. PurchaseAccounts.AccountID <> APAccounts.AccountsPayableAccountID

  6. Purchases.TxnID IS NULL
16990942:
Distributor overview of the Encompass Design System, the UI/UX framework and component library for building custom screens in Encompass. Needs a Dashboard Role for access; v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

The Encompass Design System is a UI/UX framework for building screens and customizations throughout Encompass.

Encompass internal development utilizes this same design system to build the core Encompass pages and functionality for the entire system.

You can find the Encompass Design System in the universal search, as long as a Dashboard Role has been added to grant you access.

The principles of Encompass design offer designers, product managers, and developers with ways to evaluate their designs, as well as give direction to design system components and patterns. These principles are in service to the Encompass brand, and should be thought of throughout the design process.

Build trust between the user and the product

Encompass customers trust our products with sensitive data. Because of this, users should always feel a sense of confidence that their data is safe (and in many cases, more powerful) in our hands. Many things contribute to building trust with a user, including:

- Text content throughout the product. Incorrect grammar/spelling, or even an out-of-place tone can cause the user to feel confused and hesitant.

- Consistent spacing, alignment, sizing, etc.

- Meeting expectations. Surprising results or actions that aren’t expected can cause hesitancy when using Encompass products.

Maintain consistency across the experience

Encompass works to connect multiple tiers with software. Consistent experiences between groups of users allow them to communicate easier, as well as adopt new features internally. Work to apply the same solution to the same problem across Encompass products.

Enable users to act confidently on data

Our users use rich data to make business decisions every day. Encompass products should always clearly and specifically guide the user towards actions they can take. Users should be able to act on data with confidence.

The design system consists of many pieces, including:

  • Design Principals

  • Color Palette

  • Semantic Tokens

  • UI Containers

  • Typography

  • Motion standards

  • Component Library (HTML Web Components based)

  • Patterns

For more information about the design system, it is recommended to pursue a Code Block certification from Encompass.

16990945:
Distributor troubleshooting for Accounts Receivable Close errors at End of Day in Encompass: company/account mismatches on journal entries, missing Income Account Map accounts, unaligned close dates. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Accounts Receivable Close has been/is being run for at least 1 day

Steps

Common Accounts Receivable Close Errors and how to troubleshoot them:

Can not balance Journal Entry because the Company on the Journal Entry record does not match the Company on the Account for every Journal Entry Trans record:

  • Click the View transactions with mis-matched Accounts hyperlink on the error message

  • This will take you to the Journal Entry Trans table and show all Journal Entry Trans where the Account's Company does not match the Journal Entry's Company

  • Click the hyperlink in the Detail column to view a report detailing which transaction(s) are causing the misalignment

  • If the Memo field is Asset or DepositAsset, go to Inventory Asset Account Maps to update, or add, necessary Account Mapping

  • If the Memo field is AccountsRec, confirm the AR Account on the transaction(s) are correct

  • If so, go to AR Account Maps to update Account Mapping

  • If not, set the AR Account on the transaction(s) to the proper AR Account

  • If the Memo field is anything else, the hyperlinked report in the Detail column will tell you the Income Account Map ID that was selected. Update or add any necessary Account Mapping

  • Once Account Mapping has been updated, run Accounts Receivable Close again

Income Account Maps The following records are incorrectly mapped. Income Account Maps _____ Account is required. Please set a valid Account value:

  • Income Account Maps require all fields to have an Active Account set

  • Click the edit pencil next to the IncomeMapID designated in the error message

  • Set an Active Account on the field(s) where there is no Account set

  • You can click the column header (i.e. Income Account, COGS Account, etc.) and filter to No Value to find other Income Account Maps that need to be updated

  • Once all Income Account Maps have valid Accounts set on all fields, run Accounts Receivable Close

Can not close the selected Companies at the same time:

  • All End of Day processes, when run with multiple selections, require the current Close Dates to be identical

  • If Company 1 is closed through 12/31 and Company 2 is closed through 1/1, they cannot be closed at the same time

  • Run Accounts Receivable Close for the Company with the least current Close Date through the most current Close Date (in the above example, run Accounts Receivable Close for Company 1 for 1/1)

  • Once Close Dates are aligned, you can run the End of Day process for multiple Companies at the same time
16990947:
Distributor steps for setting up the Auto-Bump Promotions app in Encompass so invoices are automatically topped up to a promotion's minimum quantity for chosen chains or customers. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

How to Install the Application:

  1. Go to the App Library

  2. Search or find the app in the library

  3. Click Install

  4. Assign report and dashboard roles

  5. Set a schedule for the import routine to run

  6. Update application settings as needed

  7. Accept Terms

  8. Click Install

Creating Auto-Bump Promotion Rules Records:

  1. Review promotion setup and expected pricing for relevant chains

  2. Go to Auto-Bump Promotion Rules Table

  3. Add records for Chains/Customers in question

  4. Add records by Chain if all customers under the chain should receive the Auto-Bump Rule

  5. Add records by Customer if not every customer under a Chain should receive the Auto-Bump Rule

  6. Record the start and end dates

  7. Set the Promotion and Auto-Bump Product (Product to be added when the invoice does not meet the minimum quantity on the promotion)

Fields And Definitions

What it is:

Auto-Bump to Quantity Discounts is a process for Distributors to help ensure specific chains and customers are able to receive the expected pricing based on what they have bought. After an invoice is created, the system will look at the auto-bump rules to determine if there is a product on the invoice tied to an auto-bump promotion that needs to have its quantity increased to meet a minimum promotion amount. There needs to be a product on the invoice that is part of a promotion on the Auto-Bump Rules table for the auto-bump logic to be triggered. If the system determines there is a transaction that needs to be bumped, an import routine runs to automatically add the auto-bump product to the invoice to meet the minimum quantity on the promotion so they receive the deal.

How it Works:

  • Auto Bump Rules Promotion Table

Auto-Bump rules are set up on the Auto-Bump Promotion Rules table. This is where the Distributor will set the rules for Auto-Bump Promotions. On this table, they can specify a Chain or a Customer that will qualify for the rule. The table is inclusive and will include only records set on this table for the Auto-Bump Rules. They will also need to select a start and end date to determine when this rule will take effect. Finally, the distributor will set the promotion and auto-bump product on these rules. By setting a promotion, we are determining the minimum quantity we want the customer purchasing for a set of products and the set of products itself. If the customer has not purchased this minimum quantity, there is an import routine that will use the Auto-Bump product set on the rules table to qualify the invoice for the promotion.

  • Reports and Import routine

After Rules have been specified on the Auto-Bump Promotion Rules Table, there is a report that is run automatically to determine the invoices that need to be adjusted or bumped. The report is looking for New Invoices that were not created by EDI in between the start and end date on the Auto-Bump Promotion Rules Table and the start and end of the promotion. If the report finds an invoice that has products from the Auto-Bump Promotion Rules Table that do not add up to the minimum order quantity, it will report the difference between the minimum order quantity and the current amount on the invoice.

Distiller setup reference for the Barrel Management Console in Encompass: configure barrel Equipment Types, non-inventory barrel Products and Equipment records. Requires v23.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.08

Fields And Definitions

Tables & Fields Definitions

Equipment Types

The Equipment Types table defines the different types of barrels. Create one Equipment Type for each unique combination of the following:

  • Volume Capacity: 55 Gallons, 53 Gallons, 1 Liter, 3 Liter, etc.

  • Wood Type: Oak, Elm, Beech, Cherry, Chestnut, Ash

  • Barrel Type: Rum, Bourbon, Scotch, Whiskey, Tequila, Cognac, Sherry, White Wine, Red Wine, Rye, Brandy

Equipment Types Fields

Ensure the Equipment Types that represent barrels have the following configuration:

  • Is Portable* = True

  • Is Barrel* = True

  • Capacity* = NOT NULL

  • Unit of Measure* = Volume UoM, likely Gallons or Liters

  • Barrel Type = NOT NULL

  • Wood Type = NOT NULL

  • Product* = NOT NULL (see Barrel Product)

Barrel Product

Create one non-inventory barrel Product per Equipment Type. This Product will be used on Purchases when buying barrels, and Invoices when selling barrels. The actual barrel inventory, physical location, and status of each barrel is represented on the Equipment record.

Barrel Product Setup

The barrel Products records will need the following configuration:

Products

  • Track Batch Codes = False

Product Types

  • Track Inventory = False

  • Store in Equipment = False

  • TTB Process Type = Not Set Yet

Ensure that the barrel Product OR the barrel Product’s Product Type is mapped to the correct Inventory Asset Account Maps & Income Account Maps.

Equipment

The actual barrel inventory, physical location, status, and condition of each barrel is represented on the Equipment record.

Equipment Fields

The barrel Equipment records will need the following configuration:

  • Equipment Name* = System generated as ‘Volume + UoM + Equipment ID’, but can be customized.

  • Location* = System set

  • Bin* = System set, represents inside of the barrel

  • Condition*

  • Char Level/Toast Level

  • Cost

  • Write-off Threshold - will prompt the user to write off existing liquid remaining in the barrel after a dump.

  • Equipment Location Bin - represents the physical Bin location of the barrel.

Distributor guide to adding custom HTML, CSS and JavaScript Code Blocks to Encompass dashboards, writing Mocha test scripts and releasing the dashboard. Needs DashboardEdit permission and v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

Must have the DashboardEdit permission to be able edit dashboards to get access to the Code Block editor.

Steps

Screenshot

Encompass Code Blocks are a way to create custom HTML, CSS, and Javascript pages on any dashboard.

Code Blocks can fill the entire page, they can just be a small component of the page, or anything inbetween.

Disclaimer: Code Blocks are advanced functionality and require technical ability to write code.

Encompass Support cannot help with writing, debugging, or troubleshooting the users code.

Adding a Code Block

1. After creating a dashboard, add the code block widget.
​
2. After adding a code block to the page, there will be an integrated development environment (IDE) specifically for HTML, CSS, Javascript, and automated testing through Mocha.js.
​
3. Each tab across the top is where the corresponding HTML, CSS, and Javascript code will be placed.

HTML
​
​

This tab is standard HTML.

HTML basics can be found here.

CSS
​
​

This tab supports standard CSS, or SCSS.

CSS basic can be found here.

Javascript
​
​

This tab contains all of the javascript code for the Code Block.

There is a linter (eslint) enforced in the javascript tab.

This ensures that the javascript code adhears to the Encompass standards for maintainability and performance, and cannot be turned off.

Encompass is written entirely in vanilla Javascript, no frameworks. But users can import a framework of their chosing in the code block itself (see EC_Fmt.LoadScript() in the SDK)

Test Script
​
​

This tab contains mocha testing scripts that are executed during every 'Save As Released' process on the dashboard, and during every major version release of Encompass.

Run these tests manually using the 'Run Test' button at the top of the page.

Test scripts are written in Mocha.js, with Chai.js available for assertions

Documentation
​
​

This is markdown code.

It is only shown in the Code Block editor, and is intended as a place to leave documentation and notes for other developers or the users future self (similar to a ReadMe.md file).

SDK
​
​

This is a documentation tab for the Encompass Javascript SDK and all of the functions/helpers built into it.

It also includes links to the design system for help keep code blocks consistent in UI and behavior with the rest of the system.

Releasing a dashboard

1. When finished with the code block, 'Save' to exit the Code Block Editor.
​
2. Then save the dashboard.
​
3. Whenever a dashboard is saved there are options for:
​
​

  • "Save as Draft": Testing is not run, dashboard is in draft mode for the user to interact with and do personal testing
    ​
    ​

  • "Save as Released": If the system detects that it has at least one Code Block on it, it will run the Test Script on the code. The Test Script must have 80% code and function coverage, and pass all tests to be allowed to release the dashboard. This ensures that Encompass can automatically tests and keep the dashboard working long into the future. If the page has no Javascript, then testing is not required.

4. When a dashboard is released, Encompass will also minify, compress, and delivery the HTML/CSS/JS to a CDN network to improve page performance.

​ Note: This is why 'Save as Released' is slower, and it is recommended to not use this option until the dashboard is finished and ready.

Fields And Definitions

Mocha.js: the testing framework that the user tests in the 'Test Script' tab run on. Example code for this is available in the Test Script tab, on the right side. More information is available here.
​
​

SDK: Software Development Kit - Encompass javascript library of tools that make building pages that behave like the rest of Encompass easier.

Best Practices

  • Use the right-click -> Format Document option to make the code easier to read.
    ​
    ​

  • Do not use 'Save As Released' until the dashboard is finished, has been tested in 'Save as Draft', and is ready for all users to see. 'Save As Released' is a much slower process that includes global delivery of the HTML/CSS/JS to improve page performance for end users.
    ​
    ​

  • Utilize the SDK whenever possible. This ensures that future changes to the underlying platform do not break the code, because Encompass maintains the SDK to continue working during those changes.
    ​
    ​

  • Utilize the Encompass Design System to ensure the pages have a cohesive and consistent design with the rest of the system.

Distributor guide to writing custom Snowflake SQL expressions (fx) in Fusion reports in Encompass, including aggregate function rules and testing. Needs FusionEdit permission and v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

User must have the FusionEdit permission to be able to edit a Fusion report and the expressions inside of it.

It is recommended to have a good understanding of SQL and basic technical skills before using Fusion Expressions.

Steps

Disclaimer: Fusion expressions are advanced functionality that involves writing SQL and a more technical skill set.

Encompass Support may not be able to help build or troubleshoot your custom SQL in Fusion expressions.

  • When building a Fusion report, Encompass offers several places that you can use an 'Expression' instead of the standard drop-down of fields to select from.

  • These expressions are custom SQL statements that are placed into the final report query, in various places based on where you add the expression in Fusion Edit.

Where can expressions be used?

Answer: Anywhere in Fusion Edit you see thefxsymbol, clicking on this symbol toggles between a standard fusion field and an expression.
​
​

Screenshot

Building Expressions

  • After clicking the fx symbol to toggle a field to an expression, click on the icon on the right side to open the expression builder:

Screenshot

  • It is recommended to always test the expression and ensure the SQL written is valid and will work on the report.
    ​
    ​

  • If a report is run with invalid SQL, the entire report will fail.

Aggregate Functions
​
​

Aggregate functions are a special type of function that operate over multiple rows in the underlying data.

A simple example is SUM(), which will add together all of the values into a single number.

These functions cannot be present in the 'Parent/Child/Detail' section of the report in expressions.

They can be present in the 'Values' section of the report, but if they are added then the default aggregate function on the right side must be removed.

Further Information
​
​

More can about available functions, how they are used, and general SQL information can be be found on the Snowflake Documentation.

Fields And Definitions

Fusion Expression: Section of the fusion edit engine that can be modified to contain a custom SQL statement
​
​

Snowflake: The underlying data warehouse that Encompass utilizes for Fusion reports. The SQL written in expressions must be in Snowflake compatible format

Best Practices

  • Always test your expression and ensure the SQL written is valid and will work on the report. If a report is run with invalid SQL, the entire report will fail.
    ​
    ​

  • Utilize the 'Run Test' tab at the top of Fusion Edit to test all expressions on the report at once.
    ​
    ​

  • Remember to remove the aggregate option if you are adding an expression in the 'Values' section of the report, and your expression already includes a SQL aggregate function inside of it
