Distillery steps for setting up Tax Entities (DSPs), Product Types, Brands, Vendors and Customer TTB Tax Codes in Encompass so the TTB Distillers Report of Operations (DRO) is accurate. Requires v23.09+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.09

Pre-Conditions

This document guides users through the configuration of core data like Tax Entities, Product Types, Suppliers, Brand Families, Brands, Products, Vendors, & Customers to ensure accurate representation of all spirit production and removal data required for the Federal TTB Distiller's Report of Operations (DRO).

Steps

Configuring Tax Entities
​
​

  • Set up Tax Entity records that represent your Distilled Spirits Plant (DSP) license
    ​
    ​

  • Add a separate Tax Entity record for each Distilled Spirits Plant (DSP) that you produce spirits under in your distillery

Screenshot

Enter the following information:
​
​

  • Tax Entity - The name of your Distilled Spirit Plant (DSP)
    ​
    ​

  • License Number - TTB defined DSP license number
    ​
    ​

  • FEIN - Your Federal Employer Identification Number

Configuring Product Types
​
The common Product Types that we suggest setting up for reporting spirits on the TTB DRO include:
​

Screenshot


​

  • Wash Pre-Distillate - fermented wash that will be distilled into a spirit
    ​
    ​

  • WIP Low Wines - unfinished spirits produced on the first stripping distillation run
    ​
    ​

  • WIP Hearts - finished spirits produced on the spirit distillation run
    ​
    ​

  • WIP Feints (Heads/Tails) - unfinished spirits produced on the spirit distillation run. These unfinished spirits will either be redistilled or dumped
    ​
    ​

  • WIP Bulk Spirits - represents finished spirits purchased in bulk. These finished spirits will either be blended, barrel-aged, or redistilled

Link Tax Entities to Product Types:
​
​

Assign the spirits Product Types that are split by production partner to their appropriate Tax Entity (DSP) using the Locations Product Types table.

Screenshot

In this example we can see that in the ‘Krill Brewing & Distilling’ Location:
​
​

  • ‘Wash Pre-Distillate’ will not report on either DSP’s TTB DRO.
    ​
    ​

  • ‘IS’ Product Types will report under DSP: DRO-CO-ISD-99
    ​
    ​

  • All ‘KD’ Product Types will report under DSP: DRO-CO-KRD-01


​
Configuring Brands
​
​

1. Create a Supplier for each spirit production partner. Continue using production partner prefixes
​
2. Create a BrandFamily for each spirit being produced and another for bulk WIP spirits being purchased for blending, like GNS. Continue using production partner prefixes
​
​

Screenshot

3. Create separate spirit Brands for each phase of the distillation process, as well as for packaging material, for example: September 2023 TTB DRO Configuration 6

Screenshot

  • Wash Pre-Distillate - fermented wash that will be distilled into a spirit.

○ TTB Category = Not set because not reported on DRO
​
​

  • Low Wines - unfinished spirits produced on the first stripping distillation run

○ TTB Category = Unfinished Spirit for the spirit type in question
​
​

  • Feints - unfinished spirit that will either be redistilled or dumped

○ TTB Category = Unfinished Spirit for the spirit type in question
​
​

  • Hearts Full Strength - hearts at full strength coming off of the still

○ TTB Category set to appropriate spirit type. Do not use ‘Unfinished Spirit’
​
​

  • Hearts Barrel Proofed - hearts proofed down to barrel strength

○ TTB Category set match the ‘Hearts Full Strength’ Brand of this spirit type
​
​

  • Bottle Proofed - aged spirit proofed down to bottle strength

○ TTB Category set match the ‘Hearts Full Strength’ Brand of this spirit type
​
​

  • Packaging Material - represents all brand-specific packaging material for this September 2023 TTB DRO Configuration 7 spirit

○ TTB Category not set.

Configuring Vendors
​
​

Transfer-in-Bond Vendors Vendors are categorized with a TTB Tax Code that helps differentiate between different types of transactions on the DRO. Important TTB Tax Codes values for the TTB DRO include:
​
​

  • Received in Bond - Represents a spirit inventory transaction where your DSP will assume the proof gallon tax liability, aka a Transfer-in-Bond transaction. Set on all Vendors that will provide you spirits ‘in bond’
    ​
    ​

  • When the Vendor TTB Tax Code is left blank, the purchase transactions from this Vendor represent tax-paid receipts. This may occur if purchasing finished good spirits for resale, where the previous DSP paid taxes at the time of shipping you the inventory.
    ​
    ​

Production Partner Vendors Recipes built for contract production partners should have a Vendor set on the Recipe Version. Setting up a Vendor for each contract production partner allows receiving raw material inventory from the production partner for future production. Set the following fields on Vendor records representing a production partner:
​
​

  • TTB Tax Code = Received in Bond
    ​
    ​

  • Is Production Partner = True

○ This is required to be able to set the Vendor on the Recipe VersionDoing so will ensure all inventory created from this recipe will be created under this production partner Vendor.

Configuring Customers
​
​

Customers are categorized with a TTB Tax Code that the DRO uses to categorize different types of withdrawals. Important TTB Tax Codes for the DRO include:
​
​

  • Laboratory Samples - Set on Customer(s) that is used to Invoice spirit inventory consumed for the purpose of lab samples
    ​
    ​

  • Transfer to Distillery - Customers are cate
    ​
    ​

  • Unfit for Sale - Set on Adjustment Customer(s) that will be used when writing off inventory for the reason of ‘unit for sale’
    ​
    ​

  • Research and Development - Set on Customer(s) that is used to Invoice spirit inventory consumed for the purpose of R&D
    ​
    ​

  • Consumed on Premise - Set on Customer(s) that represent an on-premise tasting room
    ​
    ​

  • Destroyed - Set on Adjustment Customer(s) that will be used when writing off inventory for the reason of ‘destroyed’
    ​
    ​

  • Overage or Shortage - Set on generic Adjustment Customer(s) that are used for general inventory adjustments from inventory discrepancies when counting
    ​
    ​

  • Used as Supplies - Set on Customer(s) that will be used to Invoice spirit inventory consumed as supplies, like cleaning supplies
    ​
    ​

  • Export - Set on Customers that will be used to deplete spirit inventory to an international business partner
    ​
    ​

  • DRO Storage Loss - Set on the Customer that will collect proof gallon loss during storage, like angel's share during barrel aging. These proof gallon losses are reported on the TTB DRO Storage Line 22. Other Losses
    ​
    ​

  • DRO Processing Bulk Loss - Set on the Customer that will collect proof gallon loss when packaging bulk spirits into a bottle. These proof gallon losses are reported on the TTB DRO Processing Part I Bulk Ingredients - Line 24. Losses
    ​
    ​

  • DRO Processing FG Loss - Set on the Customer that will collect proof gallon loss from broken finished goods. These proof gallon losses are reported on the TTB DRO Processing Part II Finished Products - Line 44. Recorded Losses
    ​
    ​

  • Removed Without Payment of Tax - Set on transfer Customers that will be used to deplete spirit inventory on intercompany transfer Invoices. This represents an outbound transfer-in-bond
    ​
    ​

  • None - Set on all ‘sale-type’ Customers that you will be shipping spirits, tax paid. These proof gallons are reported on the DRO Processing Part II Finished Products - Line 33. Withdrawn Tax Determined.

TTB DRO Setup & Configuration

Best Practices

We suggest creating separate Product Types for each production partner producing spirits in the facility. Define a unique prefix for each production partner, including your primary distillery, and use that prefix when setting up Product Types, Suppliers, Brand Families, and Brands.
​
​

Why?
​
​This helps separate inventory ownership, and allows linking specific Product Types to Tax Entities (DSP’s) for proper TTB DRO reporting. Separating Products in this way also provides more flexibility in account mapping.
​

Screenshot

  • ‘KD’ represents Product Types for my distillery ‘Krill Distilling’
    ​
    ​

  • ‘IS’ represents Product Types for our distilling contract partner ‘Island Sun Distilling’
    ​
    ​

1. Set these Product Type fields for proper TTB DRO reporting:

a. TTB Process Type

i. Set to ‘Produced’ for bulk WIP spirits, whether made or purchased

ii. Set to ‘Packaged’ for FG spirits

iii. Set to ‘Not Set Yet’ for ‘Wash Pre-distillate’ or other Product Types that should not report on the DRO

b. TTB Process Category - auto-populates based on the TTB Process Type

c. Track Inventory = True September 2023 TTB DRO Configuration 3

d. Type Code = Spirits e. Store in Equipment - set to ‘True’ for all WIP (not FG) Product Types.
​
​

2. Set these Product fields for proper TTB DRO reporting:

a. Track Batch Codes = True

Pre-Conditions

Product must have IncludeInSalesReportByDefault=True

Steps

Note: There are a couple of connections in DSDLink that need to be made to completely ensure a product is reporting. Encompass employees maintain these connections. The instructions below help ensure that everything is set up correctly in the distributor site only.

In a distribution system, there are 3 fields to check to ensure that a specific product is reporting to SRS.

  1. The brand family that the product is under must have a SupplierReportCode. If it does not, link a product underneath it using Product Manager. After linking a product, this link will cascade up through the hierarchy, and you brand family will acquire the SupplierReportCode from DSDLink

  2. The supplier that the product is under must have a SuppliersVendors record (one per location selling the product) attached to it with SupplierDataAccess=Allow. This tells the system that it is okay to share this data to the supplier through DSDLink. This applies to both suppliers accessing their distributor data in dsdlink AND suppliers accessing their data in SRS. If you do not wish to share this data with your suppliers, set SupplierDataAccess to Block

  3. The SuppliersVendors record also needs a DistributorNumber. This value is provided by SRS in the initial setup, and it tells their system what Location of yours the data belongs to

Fields And Definitions

SuppliersVendors.DistributorNumber: This value is provided by SRS. It is how they determine which Location the data belongs to

SuppliersVendors.SupplierDataAccess: This value tells the system whether or not to share the data with the supplier via DSDLink. This works for both sending data to SRS and for suppliers accessing their data in DSDLink

BrandFamily.SupplierReportCode: This value is maintained in DSDLink by Encompass employees. It is how SRS knows what supplier to provide the data to on their end

Best Practices

Link all your products. Product linking cascades up through the Brand, BrandFamily, and Supplier. Product linking helps ensure a correct BrandFamily.SupplierReportCode.

Distributor steps for extending expiration dates on received inventory in Encompass in bulk, using a report export and an import routine to add days. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

1. Run this report
​
​

2. The report is designed to find any purchase transactions where the On Hand is greater than 0, the shipment has been received, and the purchase transaction has not had the expiration date changed since the Last Time Updated.
​
​

3. Filter the report to the data that needs to be updated. Package Code will make it easy to filter on Keg or Package. Exclude Brand will make it easy to remove specific brands from a whole supplier.
​
​

4. The Days To Add filter will add on that number of days to the existing expiration date in the system. No need to change the actual shelf life on the product. The Current Expiration Date and New Expiration Date are included in the report to make it easy to see what is changing.
​
​

5. The report is designed to exclude any purchase transactions that have already had the expiration date changed by any method. The filter called Last Time Updated is looking for any purchase transaction that has not been updated since the selected DateTime. This will prevent the same purchase trans from getting updated twice, and it will allow products to go through a second wave of extenstions. If users update everything by 4/9 and then the supplier comes back and says that 40 more days can be added, then the filter can get changed to 4/9 and the purchase trans can be updated a second time.
​
​

6. Run the report with the needed fitlers and export the results to CSV. It's always good to keep a record.
​
​

7. Click here for the link to the import routine. This is designed to accept the data exactly how it comes out of the above report.
​
​

8. Click Add New Task.
​
​

9. Choose the CSV from the report.
​
​

10. Click Add Task.
​
​

11. Click the Execute button next to the added task.
​
​

12. The expiration dates are now updated and they will drop out of the previous report as soon as the Data Warheouse is updated.

Distributor steps for reversing or correcting a verified invoice in Encompass from the Invoices table or Invoice view, including picking a reason and route. Includes a video. Requires v22.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.08

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Correct/Reverse an Invoice
​

From the Invoices Table:

  1. Select Reverse or Correct Invoice

  2. Search for and select invoices to be reversed or corrected

  3. Select the reason for why these invoices need to be reversed or corrected

  4. Select the route for the invoices to go on

  5. Review the invoices and select if you would like to reverse or correct the invoices

  6. For Corrections: The invoice is now editable using the Edit button at the top of the Invoice view. Make changes as needed and click Save Changes when complete

From the Invoice View:

  1. Go to an invoice you would like to reverse or correct

  2. Select Reverse or Correct Invoice

  3. Select the reason for why these invoices need to be reversed or corrected

  4. Select the route for the invoices to go on

  5. Review the invoices and select if you would like to reverse or correct the invoices

  6. For Corrections: The invoice is now editable using the Edit button at the top of the Invoice view. Make changes as needed and click Save Changes when complete

Best Practices

  • Unapply payments before reversing or correcting an invoice, if possible
    ​
    ​

  • Be aware that correcting a previously corrected invoice will create additional reversal and correction records
    ​
    ​

  • Reversals and Corrections DO NOT change the original invoice, they create new records that either nullify OR nullify AND recreate Invoices. This is because Verified Invoices cannot be edited
    ​
    ​

  • Reversing an Invoice will result in the creation of ONE new invoice record, and it should be an exact match for all products, quantities, prices, and invoice charges found on the original in the opposite amount. This means that positive amounts are now negative and negative amounts are now positive
    ​
    ​

  • Correcting an Invoice will result in the creation of TWO new invoice records; one will be a reversal as described above, and one will be a recreation of the original invoice that is now editable
    ​
    ​

Q: Why are some fields not editable?

A: Many fields on the Customers table are inherited from a record on another table. This means that the field cannot be edited on the Customers table and must be edited on the table from which it is inherited. Here are a few examples:
​
​

  • Customer Account Type: Inherited from the Customer Type field.

  • Phone Number and Email: Inherited from the Primary Contact field.

    ​

​
A: The Customer record will only be in the Active status between the Seasonal Open Month/Day and Seasonal Close/Month Day. When not within the Seasonal dates, the Customer Record will be set to the Inactive status automatically and reactivated upon the Open date.

16991058:
Distributor reference for Encompass API policies: when unused API Commands are auto-deactivated (210/760 days) and deleted, plus API Token security and timeout/processing limit rules. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Fields And Definitions

Auto deactivate and delete policies

In order to maintain a clean system and ensure reliability and performance, API Commands are automatically deactivated and deleted after certain periods of inactivity.

  • Any API Command that is not used for 210 days will be auto-deactivated, as long as Delete Protection is turned OFF.
    ​
    ​

  • Usage is measured from production systems only.
    ​
    ​

  • If Delete Protection is turned ON, the API Command will be auto-deactivated after 760 days of no usage.
    ​
    ​

  • There is not a way to extend the time limit beyond 760 days.
    ​
    ​

  • Any API Command that has been in the Active=False state for more than 365 days will be automatically deleted.
    ​
    ​

  • The deleted record for the API Command and the API Parameters under it will be available in the deleted records table for an additional 6 months, if they are needed for reference.

Security policies

If an API is accessed using the API Token (instead of the session of a logged in user), then the API Token should be send in the body of the HTTP request.
​
​

  • APITokens must not be shared outside of the users working on the APIs, Tokens should be treated with the same level of security as someone's password.
    ​
    ​

  • The 'Timeout In Seconds' and 'Processing Limit (Minutes per Hour)' should be set within a reasonable limit based on the intended usage of the API. Encompass reserves the right to change these settings if an API is causing larger system performance impacts.

How to use Routing on Delivery Optimizer
​
​

​

​
3. In the main body of the page, use the checkbox to select Route(s) to Optimize

4. Under the Routing header, select from the options provided:


​

​

1. Drag Stops to reorder or move to a different Route

​ NOTE: This table displays all selected Routes, it also displays:

  • The Route color
    ​

  • The assigned Delivery rep
    ​

  • The number of stops on the route
    ​

  • The loaded Products Types and their total weight

    ​

NOTE: Stops can be resequenced automatically by selecting a priority type in the Re-Seq drop-down. Additional details can be displayed by selecting Columns from the Column drop-down.

2. Select Product Pick Types for additional product information
​
3. Select Stops via a rectangular selection
​
4. Reposition the map by clicking and dragging
​
5. Select Stops via polygon selection
​
6. Deselect all stops
​
7. Display all stops on the map
​
8. Display all routes and their stops on the map
​
9. Display colored route path for all visible routes

10. There are different methods to reassign Stops to different Routes:

  • Method 1: Select the stops you would like to move and click on the new Route’s delivery path on the map
    ​

  • Method 2: Select the stops you would like to move and click on the Route in the table
    ​
    ​

  • Method 3: Select the stops you would like to move, hover over a stop, and select ‘Place selected stops after this stop’
    ​
    ​

11. Save the changes to either the selected Load Sheet/s or both the Load Sheet/s and associated Route/s
​
​


Route Optimizer: Optimize or transfer Stops for multiple Routes at once
​
​

1. Specify the Optimization method for the selected Routes
​
2. Select Routes to transfer FROM, as well as the Routes to transfer those stops TO
​
​
​ NOTE: in addition to the chosen Optimization method, Stops transfer is determined by (in order of priority)
​

  • The amount of Stops already on the TO route (if Stops > 23, the Route is considered full)
    ​
    ​

  • The weight limit of the delivery vehicle
    ​
    ​

  • The Total Time of the Route (if Total Time > 10 hours, the Route is considered full)
    ​
    ​

3. Click Optimize
​
4. Save the changes to the Current Load Sheet or the Current Load Sheet and its Route

  • Use Mapped Routing in Delivery Optimizer to make changes to the delivery driver temporarily but without changing the driver on the route

  • Dynamic Routing is a fast way to re-sequence the routes based on the locations that have invoices for that route

Distributor reference for how Encompass assigns invoice numbers from Encompass Mobile, Mobility and EDBL imports, including Chain max length and invoice number prefix settings. v21.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 21.01

Pre-Conditions

Encompass Mobile import:
​
​

  • If unlocked Invoice is uploaded to the server, will use InvoiceID.
    ​
    ​

  • If locked Invoice is uploaded to the server or an invoice is added to a loaded loadsheet, will use Mobile InvoiceNum.
    ​
    ​

For Mobility Import:
​
​

  • Will use Mobility OrderNbr as InvoiceNum when OrderNbr is not null.
    ​
    ​

For EDBL import and other Exchange import:
​
​

  • Will use Server InvoiceNum even if InvoiceNum is mapped.

Steps

Mobile Invoice Num Calculation:
​
​

HandheldID-HandheldInvoiceNum
​
​

Step 1: Pad InvoiceID with zeros 4 places up to a maximum of 6 places

  • 907-38 => 9070038
    ​
    ​

  • 957-38 => 9570038
    ​
    ​

Step 2: Shorten Invoice Num to Chains.InvoiceNumMaxLength
​
​

  • 907-38 => 9070038
    ​
    ​

  • 957-38 => 9570038
    ​
    ​

Step 3: Replace any leading 0's with 5
​
​

  • 907-38 => 9070038
    ​
    ​

  • 957-38 => 9570038

Fields And Definitions

Chains.InvoiceNumMaxLength: The maximum length of an invoice number that the chain will accept.

ProductGroups.InvoiceNumPreFix: The leading character of the server invoice number when the split invoice product group matches the invoice. This will override setting 249.

System Setting 249 Default Invoice Number Prefix: Sets the default invoice num prefix for all invoices regardless of product group.

16991079:
Distributor reference for the WMS Move Tasks and WMS Move Task Trans tables in Encompass: replenish task statuses, who is assigned, and what product moved between which bins. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to get to the WMS Move Tasks and WMS Move Task Trans tables

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the WMS Move Tasks or WMS Move Task Trans table
    ​

If you cannot see the tables, there will be a message displayed when hovering over the table names telling you which permission you are missing to see them.

Fields And Definitions

What is the purpose of these tables and how they are used:


WMS Move Tasks table:
​
​

  • This table allows users to view the Replenish Move Tasks that have been created. Every Replenish Task will start in theNewstatus. Once a Replenish Task is complete, it will move to the Completed Status
    ​
    ​

  • WMS Move Tasks will expire based on what System Setting 365 is set to
    ​
    ​

  • The WMS Move Task table is a great resource to use when assigning users to Replenish Tasks on the server, seeing what users are assigned to a task, showing the status of move tasks, or viewing what Replenish Plan the move task was created for
    ​
    ​

WMS Move Task Trans table:
​
​

  • This table shows the transactions that will or have occurred within the replenish task. Once a Replenish Task has been started, it will move from the New status to the In-Transit status. Then, once the product is moved to its destination bin, it will move from the In-Transit status to the Completedstatus
    ​
    ​

  • The WMS Move Task Trans table is a great resource to use when researching what replenishment transactions occurred within a replenish task, such as who completed the task, what product was moved, how much was moved, and where it was moved from/to
    ​
    ​
    ​

WMS Move Task table column definitions:
​
​

  • Move Task Type: Defines what type of move is occurring (Replenish, Put Away, Move, Dynamic Pick, Slotting). The Move Task Type we are focused on for Replenishment Tasks are Replenish or Dynamic Pick
    ​
    ​

  • Status:Lets users know the state of the task (New, Printed, Completed, and Expired)
    ​
    ​

  • Assigned To:Lets users know whom this task is assigned to
    ​
    ​

  • Print Template:This is the template that will be used and printed if required when completing a Move Task
    ​
    ​

  • Print Job ID:This field will be filled in if there is a record of a print job occurring for a move task. Gives users a direct link to the print job so they can preview what was actually printed
    ​
    >

  • Replenish Plan:Lets users know what Replenish Plan this Move Task is for
    ​
    ​

  • Location:Defines what warehouse location this Replenish Task is for
    ​
    ​

  • Load Sequence: This is used more for Dynamic Picking. The Load Sequence is set on the Route but can be changed on the Load Sheet itself. The Load Sequence is created when the Load sheet is processed

WMS Move Task Trans table column definitions:

  • WMS Move Task Trans ID: A record that is created when a Move Task Trans is created
    ​
    ​

  • WMS Move Task ID: Gives users the Move Task ID so they can view the Move Task record for the Move Task Transactions
    ​
    ​

  • Product: Lets users know what product this transaction is for
    ​
    ​

  • From Bin: Defines which bin the user took the product from
    ​
    ​

  • To Bin: Defines the bin that the user will be bringing the product to
    ​
    ​

  • Num Units: Displays how many Num Units are being moved
    ​
    ​

  • Cases: Displays how many Cases are being moved
    ​
    ​

  • Status: There are three different statuses the WMS Move Task Trans can be in:
    ​
    ​

  1. New:The task has not been started yet
    ​
    ​

  2. In Transit: A user has started the task. The user went to the From Bin to grab the product and stated they picked up this product by taping Next on their handheld device
    ​
    ​

  3. Completed: The user has brought the product in the task to the To Bin, thus completing the Move Task Transaction for that product
    ​
    ​

  • Purchase Trans ID: The Purchase Trans ID would populate here if Bin Lots are being tracked. This is based on what physical pallet tag (Purchase Trans) was actually scanned

Distributor guide to finding load sheets and invoices in Encompass and what each load sheet status means (New, Locked for Routing, Loaded, Returned, Balanced, Verified). Requires v23.01+.

    ​

Note: Inventory has been reconciled, receipts have NOT yet been balanced.
​
​

  • Balanced: Receipts from customers have been counted and balanced.
    ​
    ​

  • Verified: After closing the day, Load Sheets that were Balanced in the Balanced status are now Verified and can no longer be edited.

4. Click → icon to view a Load Sheet and the Invoices included.

​

16991086:
Distributor steps for creating a WMS Replenish Plan for directed warehouse replenishment in Encompass: move unit, pallet type, start/end times, on-demand tasks. Needs Bin View/Bin Edit; v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

Permissions needed:

  • Bin View: View Tables Related to Bin Data permission to view the table

  • Bin Edit: Edit Tables Related to Bin Datato edit the table
    ​

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Create a new WMS Replenish Plan

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the WMS Replenish Plans table
    ​
    ​

  2. Click the Add WMS Replenish Plans button
    ​
    ​

  3. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the New Replenish Plans form and click the Add Record button when complete
    ​
    ​

  4. Make sure to add WMS Replenish Rules to the plan after it is created.

Fields And Definitions

  • *WMS Replenish Plan - This field controls the name of the WMS Replenish Plan.
    ​
    ​

  • *Priority - This field controls the sequence of assignment for existing WMS Replenish Tasks when multiple Replenish Plans overlap.
    ​
    ​

  • *Move Unit - This field determines the quantity by which product will be moved. There are 3 options: Case, Layer, and Pallet.
    ​
    ​

  • Pallet Type - This field references the Pallet Types table, which controls the dimensions, or space available, on a physical pallet. For WMS Replenish Plans where Move Unit = Case,Pallet Type should be set. This data will be used to calculate pallet and product dimensions to determine how many cases can fit onto one pallet, and thus one move task. Plans where Pallet Type is not specified will always create one task per product.
    ​
    ​

  • Start Time - This field will control what time you want the system to start generating replenishment tasks for the plan. This is not a required field and users have the option to manually create their own tasks on their handheld devices
    ​
    ​

  • End Time - This field controls what time you want the system to stop generating replenishment tasks, and expire any leftover tasks for the plan. This is not a required field, but if you have a start time set, set an end time as well.
    ​
    ​

  • *Dynamic Pick - This field has two options: True, and False, and is ONLY used if for a singular Dynamic Pick Replenish Plan per location. The need for a Dynamic Pick Replenish Plan is based on the presence of "Dynamic" Pick Rules, previously known as "Oddball" Pick Rules. Set this field to True on the Dynamic Pick Replenish Plan, then create WMS Replenish Rules that help control the confirmation actions needed during dynamic picking.
    ​
    ​

  • *Sort Method - This field has three options: To Bin, From Bin,andQuantity Needed.This will allow Move Task Trans to be sorted in the task either by Bin Sequence or by the Quantity needed, which is the (To Bin Inventories. Inventory - To Bin Inventories. Target Inventory) / To Bin Inventories Target Inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • *Pre-Generate Tasks - This field has two options: True, and False. When set to True, the system will automatically create replenishment tasks in advance, based on the Start Time and End Time of a plan. When set to False, tasks will not be created in advance, but can instead be prompted to generate On Demand when a user taps "Begin" in the Directed Replenishment section of a WMS handheld.
    Using the On Demand method will create 5 tasks at a time, based on the most relevant replenishments needed at the time of creation. Users can continue to tap "Begin" after tasks are completed to get more work.
    ​

Best Practices

  • When naming WMS Replenish Plans, clear and precise naming conventions work best.
    Names can vary quite a bit, but should reflect the area of the warehouse users are replenishing (pick lines, flow racks, etc.), or the type of replenishment occurring (replenishing to the amount ordered, to capacity target days of inventory, case, layer, etc.).
    ​
    ​

  • When deciding whether or not to pre-generate WMS Replenish Tasks, we recommend the On Demand method of replenishment task generation.
    This ensures the most up-to-date information is being used to create tasks, as opposed to using inventory data right at the start time of a WMS Replenish Plan.

16991092:
Distributor setup for invoice charges in Encompass such as split case fees, bottle deposits/CRV, taxes, and surcharges: charge types, calculation methods, areas, and column names. Requires v24.0+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.0

Pre-Conditions

Invoice Charges configuration requires supporting records and settings to be in place before configuration can be successful. These records are:
​
​

  • Charge Type records are used to define the type of charge.
    ​
    ​

  • Package or Product Type.
    ​
    ​

  • Non-Inventory Product.
    ​
    ​

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

What are Invoice Charges?

Invoice Charges are rules that define what types of fees accumulate in certain areas. Once configured, they are added automatically to invoices that meet the criteria set up in the System Settings, Charge Types, and Invoice Charges. Common uses of Invoice Charges include (but are not limited to) Split Case Fees, Sales Tax, Volume Based Taxes, Fees/Surcharges, and Bottle Deposits/CRV.

How to add an Invoice Charge

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Invoice Charges Table.
​
2. Click Add New Invoice Charge at the top of the screen.
​
3. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the New Invoice Charge form.
​
4. Enterthe Charge Type field.
​
​5. Select a Product Type and/or Package.
​
​ Note: The Product and Package Type fields are optional but help specify if a charge is specifically for a product or package type. If no Product Type or Package is selected, the Invoice Charge will be applied to all invoices for Customers in the Charge/Deposit Area.
​
6. Select the Calculation Method, Calculate Layer, and Invoice Charge Column.
​
​ Note: The calculation Method determines how it is calculated (flat fee, percentage, etc.) The Calculate Layer will be ‘1’ unless using multiple invoice layers. Invoice Charge Column indicates the charge column it will be a part of.
​
7. Select the Charge Area or Deposit Area
​
8. Select values for Units, Rate, Product, Start Date, and End Date fields.
​
​

  • Units - how many times this charge can be on an invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • Rate - Dollar or percentage amount for the charge.
    ​
    ​

  • Product - how it appears on an invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • Start date - When the charge starts.
    ​
    ​

  • End date - Optional time for the charge to end.

9. Click the Add Record button when complete.


​
Name or Rename Invoice Charge Columns
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the System Settings dashboard.
​
2. Enter Invoice Charges to the Category filter.
​
3. Click the Filter Results button.
​
4. There are 5 Invoice Charge Columns: enter a new name or edit an existing name then click Save Changes.
​
​

  • Default Values may come pre-populated in some Invoice Charge Aliases, these can be modified as needed.
    ​
    ​

  • Examples of common Invoice Charge Aliases include: Tax, Bottle Charge, CRV, Split Case Fee, Delivery Fee, Fuel Surcharge, etc

Fields And Definitions

  • *Charge Type - This is a required field that acts as an identifier to tell the user what kind of charge it is, and find the one that fits the charge best.
    ​
    ​

  • Product Type - This field will control when this invoice charge will trigger. If a product is in that Product Type and is on the invoice, Encompass will create a charge.
    ​
    ​

  • Package - This field will control when this invoice charge will trigger, if a product in that package is on the invoice we will create a charge.
    ​
    ​

  • *Calculation Method - This will control what is included in the calculation and how that charge will be displayed.
    ​
    ​

  • *Calculate layer - This allows the user to tier the charges. It will be calculated in ascending order.
    ​
    ​

  • *Invoice Change Column - This is a required field that acts as an identifier to tell the user what kind of charge it is. These can be set on system settings 367 - 371.
    ​
    ​

  • Charge Area - This will allow the user to determine what customers will receive this charge, if the customer is part of the set charge area they will receive the charge.
    ​
    ​

  • Deposit Area - This will allow the user to determine what customers will receive this charge, if the customer is part of the set deposit area they will receive the charge.
    ​
    ​

  • *Units - Depending on the calculation method, this will be how many times wanted to calculate the charge for every time this charge is initiated.
    ​
    ​

  • *Rate - Depending on the calculation method this is how to calculate how much the charge will be, either in percentage of, or if not specified on the calculation method it will be price per unit. The percentage will be a decimal value.
    ​
    ​

  • *Product - This needs to be a non-inventory product that can be used to show up on the invoice when this charge is added.
    ​
    ​

  • *Start Date - When would this invoice charge start creating charges on invoices.
    ​
    ​

Best Practices

  • Use different Calculation Methods to determine how the Invoice Charge will show on an invoice; either as its own line item, the amount rolled into the total, or the amount rolled into the product, there are different ways of displaying this on the invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • If no Package AND no Product Type are set, the Invoice Charge will be applied to EVERY invoice for the customers under the Deposit Area/Charge Area selected.
    ​
    ​

  • It is best to determine the values for the required fields before setting up the new invoice charge in the system. It is recommended to set up or review the charged product, packages/product types, deposit areas/charge areas, and the invoice charge columns prior to setup. To add additional Invoice Charge Columns, view System Settings 367 - 371.
    ​
    ​

Distributor or producer steps for reconciling a completed bin count in Encompass (non-WMS): review count errors, assign write-off reasons and generate inventory adjustment invoices. Needs Return Rules. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

  • This method of counting inventory is for Non-WMS warehouses and Producers only.
    ​
    ​

  • Return Rules should be set up for each desired write-off customer and reason. Access to these Return Rules can be controlled by setting the "Route Count Type" field to only your Inventory Adjustment routes.
    ​
    ​

  • Only Reasons that are assigned an Adj Customer in Return Rules will be displayed in Bin Count Task Reconciliation. Reasons also need to have "Allow Return Error" set to "True" on the Reasons table.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Reconcile the Completed Inventory Count
​
​
​

1. Navigate to the Bin Count Tasks table.
​
2. Click the Reconcile link on the Bin Count Task that was completed.
​
3. Select the completed Bin Count Task(s) or Bin Count Task(s) to be combined and click Next.
​
​4. Review Errors:

  • Following a completed count, only inventory with counting errors will be displayed
    ​
    ​

  • The variances from the count are displayed in the Errors column
    ​
    ​

  • Products with the largest variances should be recounted
    ​

5. Once satisfied with the remaining error quantities, fill in the write-off quantity in each desired Reason column, or click the blue column header to fill down all errors to the selected write-off reason.
​
6. The Errors column will display all "0" values when write-off Reasons have been successfully populated. Click the Save button to complete the reconciliation and generate the related write-off invoices.
​
7. Select a Route and Date to hold the write-off invoices. Invoice Memo can also be set at this time.
​
8. Click Generate Inventory Adj Invoice.
​
​9. Click View Inventory Write Off Load Sheet.
​
​10. Inventory adjustment invoices are created and the Load Sheet is automatically set to the Balanced Status.

Fields And Definitions

  • Bin Count Tasks table - Table to view, create, edit, and reconcile Bin Count Tasks.
    ​
    ​

  • Reconcile - The process of comparing physical inventory counts with records of inventory on hand. This is where the inventory will actually be written in/off.
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory Count - Monitoring what is in stock for certain products or Bin Locations. During an inventory count, the product(s) are counted and recorded. When the inventory count is complete, the warehouse's inventory records are updated.

Best Practices

  • Count Inventory when nothing in the warehouse is moving. Utilize the weekend if necessary.
    ​
    ​

  • Do not load pallets, unload pallets, return any load sheets, or receive during the inventory count, if possible.
    ​
    ​

  • Counting regularly ensures that you catch any variance while there is still time to research.

Steps

Deleting and Merging records should be done with caution. It is typically only recommended to delete or merge records when duplicates exist or a record was created by mistake. Use the Decision Trees below to help decide the best course of action when deleting records from these common tables:
​
​Records Management Decision Trees (Load Sheets, Customers, Products)
​
​
​How to Delete and Merge Records
​
​

  1. Using Universal Search, enter the name of a table where you want to delete or merge a record
    ​
    ​

    NOTE: Deleting and merging is FINAL, you cannot unmerge. You have an option to input a memo as to why you are deleting/merging the item. This can be helpful for auditing purposes.
    ​
    ​

  2. Identify a record and click on the hamburger menu, then the Trash Can icon
    ​
    ​

    NOTE: Delete and merge certain records is dependent on permissions. If you are unable to delete something, please check if you have the necessary permission
    ​
    ​

  3. The tables and subtables are displayed on the Merge/Delete view
    ​
    ​

    • Any related subtables are displayed. Review each suitable to determine whether the Subtable records should be deleted, merged into the new record, or set to Null.
      ​
      ​

    • Some Subtables have to be merged, deleted or set to NULL by default. Click the 'More Info' hyperlinks to view which tables this applies to

    ​

    ​

Best Practices

  • Only delete records that you no longer need any historical data for. Once a record is deleted, you can no longer report on it.
    ​

  • Most records in Encompass will not allow you to delete when there are related sub tables. In this case, you must merge into a different record.
    ​
    ​

  • Review every sub table to ensure that you are maintaining the historical information you need.

    ​

  • Do not merge records unless they are truly the same information. If a record does not exist that you can merge to, a status change may be the more appropriate course of action (Inactive, Out of Business, etc.).

Distributor steps for finding which permissions are needed to view, add, edit or delete a table or field in Encompass via Table Definitions, plus how Users, Roles and permissions fit together. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Screenshot

How to View What Permissions are needed to Interact With a Table in Encompass
​
​

1. Navigate to any Table using the Universal Search bar (In this example the Products table is used).
​
2. Click Sub Tables, Then select Products "Table Definition".
​
​3. Here users can view the different Permissions for that table:
​
​

  • View Permission - This is the Permission required to view the 'Products' table.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Permission - This is the Permission required to add records to the 'Products' table or edit existing ones.
    ​
    ​

  • Delete Permission - This is the Permission required to delete records from the 'Products' table.
    ​
    ​

  • Table Fields Permissions - Each field in a table also has Permissions required to view and edit that field. Users can see what permissions are required for each field on this sub-table.
    ​
    ​

Fields And Definitions

Users
​
​

Every person who logs into Encompass must have a User record. Each User record needs specific permissions assigned to control what that User can do throughout the system.
​
​

Note:
​
​

1. A User is assigned to one Role that holds their permissions.
​
​

2. Users can be assigned to one or many Locations.
​
​

3. Users can also be given additional individual, or ‘one-off’ User Permissions outside of the Role.
​
​

  • Full Name - User’s full name or descriptive name.
    ​
    ​

  • User Name - This is what the user uses for logging in along with their password.
    ​
    ​

  • Role - Each user has a Role, which determines the permissions that a user has. A user has one and only one Role.
    ​
    ​

  • User Type - Collection of Roles. This determines whether the user can see data for all Customers, for all Customers in a Chain, or for a Single Customer.


Roles
​
​

A Role is a collection of permissions. Generally, a Role is related to a User’s title or job functions. Assigning a User a Role allows that user to absorb all of the permissions of that Role instead of needing each permission to be added individually to the User record.
​
​

Note:
​
​

1. A User can only be assigned to one Role.
​
​

2. Roles control which Dashboards and Mobile Applications a User sees.
​
​

  • Role - Typically named to be a description of a user's job within the company.


Roles Permissions
​
​

  • View the Permissions that make up a Role by viewing Roles Permissions as a subtable of the Role.

Best Practices

  • If a User no longer works for the company set User’s Role = None and Status = Inactive.

a. Ensure ‘None’ Role has no Permissions.

b. Remove email address and phone number from the User record to prevent password resets.
​
​

  • Avoid granting a lot of permissions to individual users. It makes Permission management more cumbersome. Generally speaking if 2 users share the same job duties, there should be a Role created to hold all of the permissions that those Users should have.

16991153:
Distributor steps for creating a display survey in Encompass by copying the Display Survey system objective, editing questions, setting prompts and an Objective Schedule. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Create the Display Survey Objective
​
​It's recommended to use the System Objective for display surveys as it contains specific pre-configured settings.
​
​

  1. Navigate to the Objectives table using Universal Search.
    ​
    ​

  2. Locate the Display Survey system objective.
    ​
    ​

  3. Click the Sub Tables button on the record and select Copy Objectives.
    ​
    ​

  4. Enter a new Name for your custom survey.
    ​
    - Important: Under "Subtables to Copy," ensure you click the plus (+) icon and check Survey Questions and Survey Question Values to include the actual questions in your copy.
    ​
    ​

  5. Click Copy Record, then select View New Record.

Edit Survey Questions
​
​

  1. Click Edit on your new objective record to open the Objective Edit Dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  2. To Add a Question: Click Add Survey Questions.
    ​
    ​

  3. Enter the question text (e.g., "How many competitive brands are on display?").
    ​
    ​

  4. Set the Data Type (e.g., Decimal for numbers, Photo for images).
    ​
    ​

  5. Toggle Required to True if the response is mandatory.
    ​
    ​

  6. Repeat Logic: Set the Repeat column to "False" for general questions you only want to ask once per visit. Leave the overall section set to "Repeat for multiple products" for questions that apply to every specific product found on display.
    ​
    ​

  7. Click Save Changesand Edit Objective Status.
    ​
    ​

See Create An Objective - Survey for more detailed steps on editing surveys.

Configure Statuses and Assignment
​
​

1. In the Objective Statuses section, locate the Assigned status.
​
​

Set the Prompt Task field:
​
​

  • Service Event Start: Prompts the user immediately upon tapping the customer event (forces completion before other tasks).
    ​
    ​

  • Service Event End: Prompts the user when they attempt to leave the customer event.
    ​
    ​

Set the Assign To Group: Change the dropdown from "Salesman" to the desired role (e.g., Merchandiser) for the Assigned, Failed, and Completed statuses to ensure the correct user receives credit.
​
​

2. Click Save Changes.

Deploy via Objective Schedule

Using an Objective Schedule is the best practice for Display Surveys as it allows for specific frequency and customer filtering.

  1. From the Objective record, click Sub Tables and select Objective Schedule.
    ​
    ​

  2. Click Add Objective Schedule.
    ​
    ​

  3. Set the Frequency (e.g., Weekly).
    ​
    ​

  4. Set Filters (Location, On Premise, Customer Type, etc.) Filters are additive meaning that multiple filters further limit the customers that will be assigned surveys.
    ​
    ​

  5. Set a Start Date: It is best practice to set this at least several days (or a full week) in advance to align with route generation cycles.
    ​
    ​

  6. Click Add Record.

Fields And Definitions

  • Survey - Set of questions to obtain data
    ​
    ​

  • Objective - The overall record that holds the Survey Questions, Objective Statuses, Objective Schedules, etc.
    ​
    1. Objective Type - This field is typically only used for System Objectives or copies of System Objectives. These include additional functionality that is not included with a normal survey. Examples of these are the Asset Request and Display Surveys or DOT surveys. Leave this field blank unless you are specifically creating a survey that falls under the Objective Type.
    ​
    2. Delete Tasks After Days - This defaults at one (1) year and will only delete the tasks, does not delete Survey answers.
    ​
    3. Copy Answers to Details - This copies Survey answers to the task details tied to the survey. Typically this is set to True.
    ​
    4. Active - Status to tell if the Survey will be live or not.
    ​
    5. New Task Status - What status the Survey will be in when first assigned.
    ​
    6. After Deadline Task Status - The status the system will switch the Survey to if it is not taken within the time frame
    ​
    7. Mobile Item - Typically used for System Objectives. Ties the survey to a button/Mobile Item in Encompass Mobile. Allows users to tap a button and be taken to the survey. Mobile Items are typically used in combination with an Objective Type. Leave this field blank unless you are creating a survey with this intended functionality.
    ​
    8. Customer ID Required - If a Survey will need to be taken at customer accounts. This should be set to yes unless taking a survey that is not customer-specific such as a DOT survey.
    ​
    ​

  • Survey Section - This is the container that defines a set of survey questions.
    ​
    ​    1. Sequence - Allows you to organize questions in a set numerical order.
    ​
    2. Survey Section - Creates multiple sections of questions. Allows for more organization of longer surveys or surveys that require selecting multiple products or brands.
    ​
    3. Section Type - Does not change the functionality of the survey. This is for categorization for Reporting purposes.
    ​
    4. Repeat Questions - Choose if needed to repeat questions for either Brand or Products. Links the Brand or Products to the task.
    ​
    5. Last Answer Auto Populate - Populates the last collected answer for the customer for all questions in the section. The answer can still be edited.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Section Values - Allows for repeating the questions in the survey section multiple times for different categories.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Survey Questions - The questions users will answer.
    ​
    ​    1. Sequence - The order in which the questions will be displayed. Drag and drop questions to reorder using the arrows.
    ​
    2. Question - The text displayed in the survey as the Question.
    ​
    3. Data Types - Used to collect different types of data. See Survey Question Data Types.
    ​
    4. Required - Required to complete the Survey. The question must be answered to complete.
    ​
    5. Remember - Populates the answer from the previous answer on a question by question basis instead of the entire section.
    ​
    6. Repeat - Use if you want the question to repeat for multiple Brands or Products.
    ​
    7. Ask if Survey Question - When set, the question will only be asked if the Ask If Questions answer meets the following:
    ​
    - Ask If Operator - Defines whether the answer to a question should be greater than, less than, equal to, etc.
    ​
    - Ask If Value - In combination with the Ask If Operator, how the Ask If Question needs to be answered to display the question.
    ​
    ​

  • Objective Status - Status of the task determining task flow. Additional statuses can be created for use on the Task Status table. See Objective Statuses.
    ​
    ​

  • Task - Individual instances of surveys being assigned/completed.

Best Practices

  • Start Dates: Always push the Start Date of a new objective schedule out as far as possible (matching your "Days in Advance" route settings) to ensure tasks populate on user plans correctly.
    ​
    ​

  • Copying over New: Avoid creating display surveys from scratch. Copy the system objective to ensure "Repeat" logic and product-linking settings remain intact.
    ​
    ​

  • Testing: Use the Take a Survey dashboard on the server to test the flow and sequence of questions before deploying to the field.

When the Repeat for Multiple Brands or Products setting is active, mobile users have the ability to select multiple products or brands at the start of a survey.
​
​

To enable:

  • Toggle on "Select multiple..." at the top of the product or brand selection list.
    ​
    ​

  • Choose all desired products or brands at the same time.
    ​
    ​

  • The survey will generate questions for each selection and track which have been answered and which are still in progress.
    ​
    ​

Screenshot

​
Users can save their survey answers when backing out of an incomplete survey, ensuring progress is preserved until the survey is completed. If a survey is incomplete, a prompt appears when the user clicks "Back," offering three options:

  • Save: Saves the answers and returns to the previous page.
    ​
    ​

  • Don’t Save: Discards the answers and returns to the previous page.
    ​
    ​

  • Cancel: Keeps the user on the current page.

When saved, answers are flagged as "Pending" and won’t be uploaded until the survey is edited again and completed. The Surveys page will display surveys with "Pending" or "Edited" statuses, ensuring easy tracking of incomplete tasks.
​
​

Fields And Definitions

  • Reversed Invoice - the exact opposite of the original. This essentially voids out the original invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • Correct Invoice - this is an exact copy of the original invoice that can now be edited to apply promotions.

Best Practices

  • Do NOT change the Reversed Invoice (the exact opposite of the original)
    ​
    ​

  • Balance the Load Sheet and ensure the reversal is applied to the original
    ​
    ​

  • Unapply payments before reversing or correcting an invoice, if possible.
    ​
    ​

  • Be aware that correcting a previously corrected invoice will create additional reversal and correction records.
    ​
    ​

  • Reversals and Corrections do not change the original invoice, they create new records that either nullify OR nullify and recreate Invoices. This is because Verified Invoices cannot be edited.
    ​
    ​

  • Reversing an Invoice will result in the creation of one new invoice record, and it should be an exact match for all products, quantities, prices, and invoice charges found on the original in the opposite amount. Meaning, positive amounts are now negative, and negative amounts are now positive.
    ​
    ​

  • Correcting an Invoice will result in the creation of two new invoice records; one will be a reversal as described above, and one will be a recreation of the original invoice that is now editable.

16991181:
Distributor guide to Promotions Zones in Encompass: create zones, add chains and customers so a group gets promo pricing, and when to use Promotions Customers for one-off pricing instead. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Zones Overview

Promotions Zones allow you to connect a group of customers to a single promotion. By grouping customers with similar characteristics into a reusable zone, you can quickly and flexibly apply unique pricing for specific periods. Examples of common Zones might be Military, Chain-Specific, or Geographically based. A Promotions Zone can be further grouped under a Market or it can be used on a Promotion, depending on internal processes or preferences for Promotion management.

Customers can belong to multiple Promotions Zones, and each Zone can contain many customers. For example, a single liquor store might be in zones for their county, their city, and for all independent stores. This flexibility allows Encompass to apply the lowest qualifying price across all promotions a customer is eligible for.

How to Add Zones and Customers

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Zones table
​
​

2. Review existing Zones
​
​

a. Use the Arrow icon to view an individual Zone record
​
​

b. Click the Edit button or icon to edit the whole record or a single field
​
​

c. Save changes when complete
​
​

3. To add a new Zone, click Add Zones button
​
​

  • Enter Promo Zone name
    ​
    ​

  • Toggling the switch means all new customers will automatically be added to this zone
    ​
    ​

  • Click Add Record
    ​
    ​

4. Do you want to add one or more chains to this zone?
​
​

  • If Yes, search for Chains in the universal search bar
    ​
    ​

  • Select the chain and click the Pencil icon to edit, and attach it to a zone
    ​
    ​

  • Select the Zone and click Save Changes
    ​
    ​

5. To add a Customers Promotions Zone, click the Sub Tables button and select Customers Promotions Zones
​
​

6. Click the Add Customers Promotions Zones button
​
​

a. Search and select Customer
​
​

b. Start Date is set to Today and determines when the Customer qualifies for Promotions tied to this Zone; modify this field if needed
​
​

c. Click to Add Record
​
​

NOTE: If you have multiple customers to add to a zone, consider using a Table Import.

Promotions Customers Overview

Promotions Customers connect a single customer directly to a promotion. This is most effective for unique pricing scenarios that don't apply to a wider group, such as for samples, donations, or special negotiated rates. Using Promotions Customers saves time by directly applying pricing to a single customer, rather than creating a separate group for just one or two individuals.

How to Add Promotions Customers

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Promotions table
​
2. Search and Select a Promotion to view
​
3. Find (or add) the Promotions Customers sub table
​
4. Reivew and add Promotions Customers, as needed to tie individual Customers to the Promotion via the "Add Promotions Customers" button
​

Promotions Zones or Promotions Customers?
​

Q: How do I know when to use Promotions Zones versus Promotions Customers?

A: The choice between Promotions Zones and Promotions Customers comes down to efficiency: whether you need to apply a promotion to a large group of customers or to a unique, individual customer.

Promotions Zones

Use Promotions Zones when you want to apply a promotion to a large group of customers who share a common characteristic, like a specific chain or location. This is the most efficient method for promotions that will apply to many people. By putting customers into a zone, you can connect the entire group to a promotion with a single record, saving you from having to make dozens or even hundreds of individual connections.

Promotions Customers

Use Promotions Customers for unique, single-customer pricing scenarios. This is the ideal choice when a promotion applies to only one or a few customers, such as for a donation, sample, or negotiated pricing. Instead of creating a zone for a single customer—which would require extra steps—you can connect that customer directly to the promotion, making the process faster and more direct.

16991207:
Distributor steps for creating credit terms in Encompass (days of credit, account on hold, finance charges, auto write-off, payment application) and how credit limits work. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How To Configure Credit Terms
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Credit Terms table.
​
​

2. Click the Add Credit Terms button.
​
​

3. Enter values to the fields on the New Credit Terms form and click Add Record when complete.
​
​

4. Sub Tables show the relationship between Credit Terms and other tables. Click the Sub Tables button to see those relationships.
​
​

  • AR Accounts - Credit Terms
    ​
    ​

  • Split Invoice - Split Invoices where the AR collection is different for each group of products
    ​
    ​

  • Terms Payment Types - The allowed payment types for this Credit Term

Fields And Definitions

* = required field
​
​

● *Terms - Alias or name of Credit Term. Be as clear and descriptive as possible

Example: Fintech 30 Day, Net 30 - [Location], Cash Only
​
​

● *Days of Credit - The number of days from delivery to remit. Default is ‘0’
​
​

● *Enforce AR Collection - Determines how and when payment is expected to be collected for delivery. Default is ‘Before Invoice Print at Delivery (Enforce on Print Rules when Exiting a Customer)
​
​

● *Account on Hold - Prevents delivery when AR is Overdue. Default is False
​
​

● *Charge Finance Charge - Determines if Finance Charge is assessed automatically when the balance is Overdue. Default is False
​
​

● *Due Date Method - Business logic to calculate when payment is due. Default is Standard, which calculates the Load Sheet Date + Days of Credit to = Invoice Due Date
​

Example: If 0 Days of Credit, Invoice Due Date is the same as the Invoice Date. If 30 Days of Credit, Invoice Due Date is Invoice Date plus 30 Days.
​
​

● *Auto Application Method - Determines when/if remittances will have Payments automatically applied. Default is Same Invoice or Same Amount
​
​

● *Age Credits - Determines if Credits are Aged the same way as Debits. Default is False
​
​

● Auto AR Write Off Limit - Sets a limit for automated AR Write Offs to be created for both Credits and Debits
​

Example: If this field is set to $1.00, Open Debits and Open Credits that are between $0.00 and $1.00 will be automatically written off
​
​

● Auto AR Write Off Product - The product used for automated AR Write Offs
​
​

Best Practices

  • Consider the name of your credit term carefully - does it convey exactly what the expected behavior of the Credit Term is?
    ​
    ​

  • Credit Terms are applied to an AR Account or Split Invoice record. Clicking the ‘Add AR Account’ or ‘Add Split Invoice’ button on the sub tables will result in the creation of a new AR Account or Split Invoice record, not add the Credit Term to an existing AR Account or Split Invoice
    ​
    ​

  • Match Auto Application to the collection process: Auto Application of payments is recommended when automated remittances are created. Manual application is recommended when payments are collected manually
    ​
    ​

  • Credit Limit prevents a sale if the current AR already exceeds the credit limit. It is important to note that it will not prevent a sale if the new invoice will put them over their credit limit.For example, if the credit limit is $100 and the customer has $98 of AR, it won't prevent another $100 invoice from being created. Overrides do not work if a Customer is over their credit limit.
    ​
    ​
16991209:
Distributor steps for shifting routes for a holiday week in Encompass: generate and move pre-sell and delivery plans in Plan Optimizer, use setting 521, and change activity routing methods. v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • Generate Pre-sell/Delivery Plans using Plan Optimizer
    ​
    ​

  • Set System Setting 521 = True, only if you would like pre-sell events to move alongside the delivery events they are tied to
    ​
    ​

  • Move Plans to appropriate dates, making sure to align pre-sell and delivery dates
    ​
    ​

  • Move Events (Optional)
    ​
    ​

  • Set Routing Methods to make sure your delivery events do NOT change back to non-Holiday Routing. Set Setting 521 = False
    ​
    ​

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Screenshot

Navigating through Holiday Routing Workflow and Best Practices Steps
​
​

Using the Universal Search Bar, navigate to the ‘Holiday Routing Workflow and Best Practices’ dashboard. Use this dashboard as an additional step by step guide, with links included, to perform your Holiday Routing setup.
​
​

  1. (Optional) Only do this step if you have already pre-sold into the holiday week and have existing delivery load sheets in the holiday week. Using the Universal Search Bar, navigate to the ‘Delivery Optimizer’ dashboard or navigate to Plan Optimizer through the ‘Delivery Home’ dashboard.
    ​
    ​
    a. Select location(s) and dates in the holiday week
    ​
    b. Check the box for all routes and click the Dynamic Routing Button
    ​
    c. Move delivery load sheets to the desired Holiday Routing schedule delivery day
    ​
    d. By omitting this step, you may see duplicate load sheets if pre-sold events have already been completed prior to the holiday week
    ​
    ​

  2. Using the Universal Search Bar, navigate to the ‘Plan Optimizer’ dashboard or navigate to Plan Optimizer through the ‘Delivery Home’ dashboard.
    ​
    ​

  3. Click ‘Generate Plans’.
    ​
    ​
    a. Set ‘End Date’ to the last day in the holiday week.
    ​
    ​
    b. Select all ‘Activities’ that you plan on updating including pre-sell, driver-sell, and delivery.
    ​
    ​
    c. Select ‘Location’ if applicable.
    ​
    d. Select ‘Show’.
    ​
    ​
    e. Unselect any plans you DON'T want to generate Plans for (examples: Hot Shots, Special Events, etc.) Then click the ‘Generate Plans’ button.
    ​
    ​

  4. Once Plans for the holiday week have been generated, navigate to System Settings and search for system setting 521.
    ​
    a. Set System Setting 521 to ‘True’ to shift Pre-generated Events when a related event has changed the date and click ‘Save Changes'.
    ​
    ​NOTE: Setting this to True while you set up for Holiday Week will ensure that your Presell Events are moved when you move Delivery Events (or vice versa) to keep the Days in advance on the Activity the same.
    ​
    b. If you leave this setting as ‘False’ you will need to move pre-sell and delivery events separately.
    ​
    ​

  5. Move pre-generated Plans to reflect Holiday Routing Schedule.
    ​
    ​NOTE: Moving plans for a user to a day where the same user already has a plan will merge the user’s plans. Work “backwards” when moving plans to avoid this overlap.
    ​
    ​Example: If the normal work week is Monday-Friday and the holiday week is Tuesday-Saturday (taking Monday off and adding Saturday), all pre-sell and delivery days would be shifting one day. To do this start by moving the regularly scheduled Friday plans to Saturday, then the regularly scheduled Thursday plans to Friday, etc. This can be done in the opposite manner for a different scenario
    ​
    a. Select the ‘Location’ and ‘Plan Date’ in Plan Optimizer to view the plans for a day that you want to start moving. You can also filter by ‘Activity’ if you only want to move pre-sell plans or delivery plans at a time.
    ​
    ​
    b. Select ‘Edit Plan Date’.
    ​
    ​
    c. Update the date on the first Plan by selecting the calendar icon and selecting the date you want to move the plan to.
    ​
    ​
    d. Click on ‘Plan Date’ directly above the first date and select ‘Fill Down’. Select ‘Save Plan Date’.
    ​
    ​NOTE: Repeat for each day of plans you are moving and for each activity, if done separately.
    ​
    ​
    e. Change System Setting 521 back to False if set to True in Step 3.
    ​
    ​

  6. (Optional) Move Events between Plans (similar to moving stops between routes, but only for the holiday week pre-generated plans).
    ​
    a. If you would like to move events between the Plans generated for the holiday week, select the plans you want to move events between.
    ​
    b. Select the ‘Mapped Routing’ button.
    ​
    ​
    c. Drag and drop Events between Routes or update users/vehicles if necessary to the plans.
    ​
    d. Select ‘Save Changes’ to update the plans.
    ​
    ​

  7. Update Pre-sell Activities prior to User’s selling for the Holiday Week.
    ​
    Example: If salesreps begin selling on the Thursday prior to the Holiday Week, update the activities by Wednesday evening.
    ​
    a. Activities with Pre-sell Days in Advance of 1 or more should be updated to use Routing Method 2) Next Scheduled Delivery. Use the link in the Holiday Routing Worflow and Best Practices Dashboard to access these activities.
    ​
    b. Same Day Pre-sells will need to be updated to Routing Method 4) Auto-Route on or After Requested Date. Use the link in the Holiday Routing Worflow and Best Practices Dashboard to access these activities.
    ​
    ​
    c. Check that the LS Type = Scheduled on the Delivery Route Types so that the events are found.
    ​
    ​

  8. Plans are now ready for the Holiday Week.
    ​
    ​

  9. At the End of the Holiday Week, Update all Activities back to Routing Method 1) Requested Delivery Date.
    ​
    ​

    ii. For a Prepaid Expense, this would be the Prepaid Expense account
    ​
    ​

    b. The Expense Account should be the Account you want to be debited by each Depreciations/Amortization entry
    ​
    ​

  5. If this will be a new Asset Type select the black Sub Tables button and choose Asset Types Then select Add Asset Types to tie the account you wish to be used for the Asset Category (you may need to select the + button next to the record)
    ​
    ​

  6. If an already existing Asset Type will be used you can navigate to the Asset Types table and populate the Asset Category field with the Category that was just created

How to add an Asset

  1. Create a purchase with the Trans Type set to Asset on the Purchase
    ​

  2. If you are purchasing Fixed Assets, you must flag IsFixedAsset = True on the Purchase

  3. From here you can set your Asset Category, Asset Type, Asset Description, Serial Number, Placed Service Date, and Asset Cost

  4. This will create the Asset Record on the Assets table with the information populated from the purchase
    ​

  5. This will also create the Fixed Asset record on the Fixed Assets table

Fields And Definitions

Key Tables

  • Asset Categories - Used to tie Asset Types and Fixed Asset Accounts together and also inform how the depreciation/amortization should behave
    ​
    ​

  • Asset Types - This table is used to set a new asset category for a group of assets, and must be added prior to the Purchase
    ​
    ​

  • Asset Account Maps - This table is used to set up account mapping for an Asset Category
    ​
    ​

  • Assets - This table is used to set the placed-in-service date and other deployment related fields
    ​

  • Fixed Assets - This table is used to set the cost, remaining value, salvage value, and other financial related fields

Fields and Definitions For Asset Categories Table

  • Asset Category - This field will serve as a label for the asset category
    ​
    ​

  • Depreciation Method - Use this field to determine the type of depreciation applied to assets under this category
    ​
    ​

  • Required Serial Number - Use this field to determine if a serial number will be required
    ​
    ​

  • Depreciation Life in Months - This field will determine how much an item value will depreciate from the start of the placed-in-service date set on the asset record, Cost/Deprecation Life in Months = Monthly depreciation

Related Fields and Definitions on the Assets Table

  • Asset Description - Used to label the purpose of the recurring depreciation entry (set/created when Purchase is created)
    ​
    ​

  • Serial Number - Used to precisely identify the asset related to this series of entries (set/created when Purchase is created)
    ​
    ​

  • Placed In Service Date - The date that will determine when the Asset will be placed in service and will trigger depreciating entries the following month (set/created when Purchase is created)

Related Fields and Definitions on the Fixed Assets Table

  • Cost - Initial acquisition cost, this amount is reflected on the balance sheet in a Fixed Asset account
    ​
    ​

  • Remaining Value - Cost minus depreciation; this value can never go below the Salvage Value
    ​
    ​

  • Salvage Value - The salvage, or minimum, value of the asset; Remaining Value will never go below this amount

Best Practices

  • Asset Account and Expense Account should be different Accounts

Distributor reference for how backorders and backfills work in Encompass: expiration dates, auto-backfill rules (System Setting 29), and why a backorder did not backfill. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Fields And Definitions

1. Backorders are products that are cut from an invoice or ordered to be delivered on a future date.
​
2. Backfills are products that were previously backordered that have now been put on an invoice.
​
​
​

  • System setting 85(Use Backorder in Promotion min Num Units calculation for Quantity Restricted Promotions) will control whether backorders are included in the calculation to determine if an invoice transaction qualifies for a promotion.
    ​
    ​

  • Backorders are stored on the customer history table.
    ​
    ​

  • Backorder date will be set to the invoice date the original order was delivered. Backorder date will update to the latest invoice date the product was ordered.
    ​
    ​

  • Backorder expiration is set based on the invoice date plus the amount of days specified in System setting 14(Default Backorder Expiration Days: Set Default Backorder Expiration Date to this many days after original requested delivery date).
    ​
    ​

  • When a backorder expires, the system will create an invoice transaction to show the backfill expired.
    ​
    ​

  • When out of stock rules runs, we will backfill full backorder amounts based on the priorities set.
    ​
    ​

  • Backorders can be keyed in manually during order entry, or generated from a product being reduced by a reason that has Auto-Backorder set to true.

Best Practices

The following criteria must be met for System Setting 29: Auto Backfill Backorders to complete:
​
​

  • System Settings - 29 = 'True'
    ​
    ​

  • Customer = 'Active'
    ​
    ​

  • Product = 'Active'
    ​
    ​

  • Inventory = 'Active'
    ​
    ​

  • Backorder Expiration Date >= {Local Today}
    ​
    ​

  • Backorder Quantity > 0
    ​
    ​

  • On Floor Inventory > Backorder Quantity
    ​
    ​

  • The code compares the Backorder Expiration Date agains the Invoice's Load Sheet Date, but for Invoices created on the handheld, there is not a Load Sheet yet, so that date is essentially {Local Today}.
    ​
    ​

  • Setting 29 does not work on loaded Load Sheets.

16991246:
Distributor FAQ on Encompass server versions: monthly major and nightly minor releases, upgrade timing and waves on the Manage Upgrade dashboard, mobile app updates and release notes. Requires v23.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.06

Fields And Definitions

How frequently does Encompass release new versions?

Encompass releases a new Major Version every month.

The major version numbers line up with this monthly release schedule, for example:

- 23.10 = October 2023 release

- 24.01 = January 2024 release

etc.

Minor versions of Encompass are released every night, these include minor bug fixes and security updates.

Minor version numbers are incrementally increased at the end of the major version number:

23.10.015

23.10.023

etc...

How long does a major upgrade take to complete?

Typically major version upgrades take between 5 minutes to 30 minutes to complete, but may take longer for larger systems.

Where can I change when my system is upgraded?

You can control the weekend of the month that your system upgrades on the Manage Upgrade dashboard, which can be found in Universal Search (requires Global Setting Edit)

This dashboard also allows you to pick the time of day that the upgrade will begin, based on what works best for your organization.

What if I select 'Alpha' as my upgrade wave, when does this upgrade?

The alpha wave is on the last weekend of the previous month, this code is generally only recommended for customers who need the latest release before it is available to others.

What if I select 'Weekend 4' as my upgrade and the month only has 3 weekends?

Your system will be upgraded on the first weekend of the next month.

aka: 4 weekends after release, regardless of how long the month is

Do the mobile apps (Android/iOS) upgrade at the same time as the server?

The iOS App Store will upgrade all apps automatically based on when Encompass releases each app to Apple. These iOS app versions support all current server versions.

The Android apps are set to upgrade once the server completes a major version upgrade. Users are prompted to download the new version the next time they sign into the Android app.

Where can I find Release Notes about the changes made between versions?

Release Notes can be found on the Release Notes dashboard, search for this in the universal search at the top of any page.
