Distributor admin guide (with Connect Summit video) to user management best practices: roles vs user types, role vs user permissions, inviting and inactivating users, password policy, SSO/MFA and cleanup apps. v22.10+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.10

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

From the Connect Summit 2022

Screenshot

User Management Best Practices

1. Overview

This guide outlines the core strategies for managing users within the Encompass ecosystem. The objective is to streamline data access, maintain security, and ensure flexibility for organizational nuances.

2. Roles and User Types

Understanding the hierarchy of access is the first step to effective user management.

The Role (The "Who" and "Where")

Role defines who the user is within the organization (e.g., Warehouse Supervisor, Sales Rep). It dictates:

  • Permissions: Access to specific tables and fields.

  • Navigation: Which dashboards and reports are visible.

  • Mobile Experience: The interface view on Encompass Mobile.

> Tip: Use the Role Management Console dashboard to compare two roles side-by-side. This helps identify discrepancies in access or dashboard visibility between different job functions.

User Types (The "Scope")

User Types function one level above Roles. They define the scope of data a user can access.

  • Example: A *Customer User* type limits the user to seeing only data relevant to their specific customer account (e.g., their invoices), whereas an *Employee* type might see data across multiple accounts based on assignment.

  • Resource: Visit the **User Home Dashboard** for detailed definitions and restriction settings.

3. Permissions Architecture

Permissions are the specific controls that allow users to view, edit, or delete data.

Hierarchy of Assignment

1. Role Permissions (Standard): Assigned to the Role itself. Every user in this role inherits these permissions automatically. This is the preferred method.

2. User Permissions (Exceptions): Assigned directly to an individual user. This overrides or adds to their role-based permissions.

Best Practices for Permissions

  • Minimize User Permissions: Avoid stacking individual permissions on specific users. If a user needs different access, consider if their Role is accurately defined.

  • Limit Scope: Grant only the permissions necessary for the user's specific duties to prevent data accidents.

  • Clone to Test: If you are unsure about a permission set, clone the user profile to test exactly what they can see and do.

4. User Lifecycle Management

Onboarding: Adding New Users

There are three primary methods to add users:

Method

Best Use Case

Description

Invite New User Dashboard

Standard/Recommended

Enter Name/Email/Role. Sends an email invite allowing the user to set their own password

Copy User (Subtables)

Cloning Roles

Select an existing user with similar duties and use "Subtables > Copy Users." Ensures all roles/settings match the peer

Manual Add (Users Table)

No Email Access

Manually enter details in the Users table. Requires the admin to set a temporary password manually

Offboarding: Inactivation

When a user leaves the company or changes roles:

  • Set to Inactive: Immediately change the status in the Users table to **Inactive**.

  • Do Not Delete: Inactivation preserves historical data (logs, orders written) but prevents login.

  • Transfer Assets: Reassign ownership of any scheduled reports or dashboards owned by the inactive user.

5. Authentication & Security

Global Authentication

Encompass uses Global Authentication tied to the user's email address. This allows:

  • Single Login: One email/password combination for all Encompass sites (e.g., Organization, Support, Test sites).

  • Site Switching: Users can switch between sites via the user menu without logging out.

Password Policy

  • Expiration: Passwords expire annually (1 year).

  • Lockout: Accounts lock after 6 failed login attempts.

  • Complexity: 8–64 characters; cannot contain 3 consecutive characters (e.g., `AAA`); cannot reuse the last 4 passwords.

Single Sign-On (SSO) & MFA

SSO (OAuth): Supports login via third-party providers (Google, Microsoft, Azure AD). If the emails match, accounts can link automatically.

MFA (Multi-Factor Authentication):

  • Internal: Push notifications to the Encompass Mobile app.

  • External: Relies on the SSO provider's MFA settings (e.g., Google 2FA).

6. Maintenance Tools & Applications

Utilize the App Library to automate hygiene and security.

Essential Management Apps

  • Clone User Dashboard: Allows admins to temporarily mirror a user's permissions to troubleshoot issues without asking for their password.

  • User Analysis & Security Dashboard: Provides a visual overview of login locations (Map view), successful vs. failed logins, and lists of users who haven't logged in recently.

  • Roles Cleanup App: Automatically deletes roles that have **zero** users assigned to keep the role list clean. (Recommended schedule: Weekly).

  • Auto Inactivate Users (End Date): Checks the "End Date" field on a user profile and automatically inactivates them when that date is reached. (Recommended schedule: Daily).

  • Deactivate Users After Inactivity: Automatically inactivates users who have not logged in for a set period (e.g., 60 days).

Distributor overview of how EDI 894 pre-delivery notices are sent through dsdlink to 99 Bottles and ABC boards as a daily CSV, and how to troubleshoot missing files. Needs an EDI connection; v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

The following document assumes the trading partner already has an EDI connection setup with Encompass and/or Non-Encompass RAS.

Steps

Many ABC boards are not able to process EDI files. For this reason, Encompass has partnered with 99 Bottles to help deliver their 894 pre-delivery notices to ABC board customers. We do this by receiving 99 Bottles EDI files (894) and translating them into a CSV file via a Fusion Report. We then send this CSV file to the relevant ABC board.
​
​
​

1. Distributor creates an invoice in their RAS system (both Encompass and non-Encompass distributors are participating in this process).
​
​

2. At the appropriate time, the RAS system generates one or more EDI 894 documents and sends these to Encompass, which is process in dsdlink. A single 894 document can contain data for one or more invoices. Example: Documents.
​
​

3. 894 processing in dsdlink creates a dsdlink Order/OrderTrans for each invoice called out in the 894 document. When created, the dsdlink Order is set to Status = Received 894 from Distributor.
​
​

4. One per day, a scheduled task is executed on dsdlink that will generate a single CSV file containing all the Order/Invoice information from all dsdlink Order where Status = Received 894 from Distributor. Example: dsdlink Orders.
​
​

5. CSV file is submitted to 99 Bottles.
​
​

6. All dsdlink Orders participating in Step 4 above have their status changed to Status = Sent 894 to Retailer.

Fields And Definitions

  • EDI (Electronic Data Interchange) - business-to-business exchange of essential organizational documents (Purchase Order, Remittance, etc...).
    ​
    ​

  • Exchange Configuration -stores all necessary information relevant to file transfer (Mailbox, ISA IDs, Functional Type, etc…) Example: Exchange Configurations.
    ​
    ​

  • Exchange Task - a collection of invoices, pricing exports, etc., packaged into a single file, all of which is documented here.

Best Practices

If something is not going as expected, check first to see if the inbound 894 EDI file was processed successfully. Exchange Task in the warning status will point to data issues in the file data coming from the distributor.
​
Values that are required (outside of the standard set) in the inbound file that need to be transmitted to 99Bottles/ABC:

Fields And Definitions

  • Market* - A grouping of Zones and/or Locations that receive the same pricing

  • Promotion Name - Alias, or common name, of the Promotion

  • Amount* - The discount or price of the promotion, dependent on the promotion type (See Promotion Types)
    ​
    ​

  • Participation* - The amount the supplier contributes to a Promotion, usually billed back by the distributor to the supplier
    ​
    ​

  • Currency - The medium for the promotion, defaults to USD.
    ​
    ​

  • min Purchase* - The number of Units required to qualify for the Promotion
    ​Example: If min Purchase = 20, there must be at least 20 total Num Units of any product on the Promotion to qualify for the Promotion
    ​
    ​

  • min Product Count* - The number of unique products needed to receive the Promotion
    ​Example: If min Product Count = 3, at least three unique products on the promotion must be on the invoice to qualify for the promotion. The number of units is not a factor
    ​
    ​

  • Start Date* - Date the Promotion begins. Invoices qualify to receive a promotion if they are dated on or after the Promotion’s Start date
    ​
    ​

  • End Date - Date the Promotion ends. Invoices dated after the Promotion’s end date no longer qualify
    ​
    ​

  • Salesman Override* - Determines if the Promotion can be by sales reps and other users
    ​
    ​

  • Active* - Determines if the Promotion is currently eligible to be applied to invoices.
    ​
    ​

  • All Products* - Determines if the promotion should be applied to every product.
    ​
    ​

  • Free Units - The number of free product units applied by the Promotion
    ​
    ​
    ​

Promotion Types
​
​

  • Front Line - The base price for Customers, essentially the Full Price
    ​
    - If a Front Line promotion does not exist, the price set on the Product record is used (see Best Practices)
    ​
    ​

  • Discount - Allows you to set an amount that is subtracted from the Full Price.
    ​
    - Entering 1.00 in the Amount field would result in a $1 subtraction off of the Full Price
    ​
    ​

  • Case Discount - Allows you to set an amount that is subtracted from the Full Price only when the Product is sold in full case amounts
    ​
    ​

  • Price - This allows you to set a selling Price for the Product.
    ​
    - Entering 25 in the Amount field would result in the product being priced at $25 when applied
    ​
    ​

  • Case Price - This allows you to set the selling Price for the Product only when the Product is sold in full case amounts
    ​
    ​

  • Percentage - Sets the discount amount based on a percentage of the Full Price
    ​
    - Entering 0.25 in the Amount field would result in a 25% discount off of the Full Price
    ​
    ​

  • Rebate - Allows you to sell at Full Price and then run the ‘Month End Rebate Builder’ to issue credits to qualified customers on qualified sales
    ​
    ​

  • Zero - Product is sold at $0. Typically used for Inventory Adjustments, Donations, or Samples, use with caution
    ​
    ​

  • FOB - Product is sold at the FOB (Freight on Board) cost value pulled from the Product's Inventory record
    ​
    ​

  • Laid In - The product is sold at the Laid In Cost value pulled from the Product's Inventory record
    ​
    ​

  • Laid In - Tax - Product is sold at the FOB + Freight + OtherCost pulled from the Product's Inventory record
    ​
    ​

  • Laid In + Tax - The product is sold at the Laid In Cost + Tax pulled from the Product's Inventory record

Best Practices

  • Front Line Price and Product Price - Always set the Price field on the Product record to the highest possible price for the product, then set a Front Line promotion for the actual pricing for the product. This allows distributors to determine if a promotion wasn’t applied as it should have, because the price is much higher than expected. If the price on the product is set as $0, this would be much more difficult to determine.
    ​
    ​

  • When you are creating a new promotion and if you copy an old promotion and the PromotionType, MarketID, LineID, minNumUnits, and minProductCount are the same and the Start Date on the new promotion is in the future, the system will auto-end date the old promotion before the new one starts.

Steps

All transactions (Invoice, Deposit) will create a Balanced Journal Entry when the transaction (LoadSheet, Deposit) is Balanced. This JournalEntry will follow the status of the source transaction and update accordingly.

​Invoice:
​

​Deposit:
​
​

  • Deposit source Journal Entries will be created once the Deposit is first Balanced.

  • Invoices.InvoiceTransJournalEntryID - this field is NULL before the InvoiceTrans Journal Entry for the Invoice is created and NOT NULL after the JournalEntry is created

16991283:
Distributor overview of allocation types in Encompass (Reserve Inventory, Limit Purchase, Unrestricted, Not Authorized, etc.) for restricting or reserving products by customer, chain or rep. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

What are Allocations?

Allocations are used as a reservation, restriction and control of Products. They can be set on a Customer, Chain, Salesman, Customer Type, or to On/Off Premise customers.

What does each Allocation Type do?
​
​
​

  • Reserve Inventory - Allocation quantity reserves that quantity for the exclusive use by that customer (but does not limit the quantity that customer can purchase).
    ​
    ​

  • Limit Purchase - Allocation quantity establishes an upper limit of how many of the product the customer can purchase (but does not reserve that same quantity for the exclusive use by that customer).
    ​
    ​

  • Limit Purchase Quantity and Reserve Inventory - Allocation quantity will establish an upper limit of how many of the product the customer can purchase as well as reserves that same quantity for the exclusive use by that customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Reserve Inventory Depleting - Allocation quantity reserves that quantity for the exclusive use by that customer (but does not limit the quantity that customer can purchase) and decreases the allocated amount as the customer purchases the product.

  • Max Purchase QTY Per Invoice - This allocation type will limit the amount of product that can be on a single invoice to a maximum. This allocation will not deplete and can be set across locations, chains and any other related allocation fields to help prevent a single customer from eating up all the inventory.

  • Unrestricted - Allows the customer to purchase the product, used in conjunction allocation type Not Authorized to provide overrides to more finely filtered allocations. For example, if you wanted to restrict a certain product to only On-Premise accounts, you would then add an allocation of type Not Authorized for Off Premise customers. If you then want to allow a specific liquor store to purchase that same product, you could then add an allocation of type Unrestricted for that one customer. As this second allocation is filtered more granularly than the first, the Unrestricted overrides the Not Authorized for that one customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Not Authorized - Prevents the customer from purchasing the product. The customer is able to view and retun the product, but sales of this product are not authorized.

Allocations by Sales Rep

  • Used to block orders by all external sources (850 PO, dsdlink, ETC.) Internal Employees can still sell this product to retailers, but retailers are not able to order the product on their own.
    ​
    ​

  • This can be used with any allocation type above, and will offer the functionality of the allocation type selected with the limitation of only allowing internal users to use the allocation.
    ​
    ​

  • Allocations by sales rep will determine the customers that are assigned to the sales rep to enable this behavior, but does not only allow the sales rep to place orders. All internal users are able to place orders for the customers that qualify for this allocation.

Allocation Type Examples:

Fields And Definitions

  • *Location - Select the location that will be affected
    ​
    ​

  • *Product - Select the product that the allocation will be for.
    ​
    ​

  • *Allocation Type - determines the Customers impacted by the Allocation and the expected behavior on product Inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • *Start date - When the allocation starts **This is the date that will determine eligibility for the allocation. This refers to the Time Entered for the Invoice, not the Invoice date. Salesmen/customers can NOT invoice the product until this date.
    ​
    ​

  • *Units Allocated - Number of units in the allocation
    ​
    ​

  • On-Premise - Select if the product is available to on-premise accounts.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Type - Select the type of customers that this product is available to under this allocation.
    ​
    ​

  • Salesman User ID - If the allocation is for a salesman, select the user ID from the Drop down menu. ***This will allow customers that have this salesman assigned to them to purchase this item. ***It is not for the salesmen to use on any customer they want.
    ​
    ​

  • Chain - If the allocation is going to be set up for a chain put the chain in this field.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer - If the allocation is going to be set up for a customer put the customer in this field.
    ​
    ​

  • End Date - The end date of the allocation. After this date, any units that are still allocated will be put back into available inventory.

Best Practices

  • In most cases, there is no need to 'layer' Allocation set filters on Customer, Chain, Salesmen, Customer Type, or to On/Off Premise.
    ​Example: If the Allocation is created for a certain Customer, the Salesperson and Premise are already set for that customer and adding the Salesman or On Premise conditions only complicates the logic required to process the Allocation.
    ​
    ​

  • As a best practice, Allocations Start Date should be set to a future date.
    ​
    ​

  • Allocations can stack to better create exclusions or align with business rules. The priority to determine what allocation is assigned is as follows:

  1. LocationID
    ​
    ​

  2. CustomerID
    ​
    ​

  3. SalesmanUserID
    ​
    ​

  4. CustomerTypeID
    ​
    ​

  5. OnPremise
    ​
    ​

  6. Allocations.UnitsRemaining + Allocations.UnitsOrdered

Steps

Distributor Tab FAQ

Overview
The Distributors tab is where you are able to manage your distributors and product linking to Encompass distributor sites. Once you have all of your global products created in PIM you will want to utilize this tab. Ensuring proper linking makes your reporting accurate and also ensures that the branding information you created in PIM maps to the correct local products in distributor sites.

Q: How do I link a distributor product to a global product?

A: Assuming that the global product has been created in PIM or already exists you can click on a distributor, navigate to the products section and click either "manage link" or "new link" to accomplish this. "New link" is where you establish a new link between a distributor product and a global product. "Edit Link" is where you can manage the already existing links between global products and distributor products. If there is not a global product to link to, a product will need to be created in PIM before this can be done. Ensure that you are conscious of the package and vintage if you want reporting to reflect correctly.

Q: I am having trouble correcting a misaligned link with "edit link"?

A: Please contact Encompass support from the support dashboard on the left-hand side and an analyst will receive the task. From here an analyst will work to correct the linking on their end. Please be specific and provide an example of the issue.

    ​
    ​

  • *Units Allocated - number of units in the allocation
    ​
    ​

Best Practices

  • A scheduled task runs overnight to update the Units Ordered, Units Sold, and Units remaining fields. We do not recommend manually executing the task mid-day as there are several recalculations performed that can impact site performance
    ​
    ​

  • If changes are needed to an Allocation that is already active and past the Start Date, End the Allocation and create a new one to make sure that Invoice Transactions are tagged correctly and Allocated Units deplete as expected.
    ​

  • The Allocations dashboard has more information on Allocation Types and Allocation Examples
    ​
    ​

  • There is no need to ‘layer’ optional filters or use them in combination. For example, there is no need to add a Chain when the Customer filter is set.
    ​
    ​

  • Allocations always work best in pairs or in multiples. If looking to make it so that only a small set of customers can buy a product there should be a “Not Authorized” Allocation for the Location blocking everyone from buying the product. Then, have specific “Unrestricted” Allocations for the specific customer to allow them to buy it.
    ​

  • if using an Allocation Type that has “Limit Purchase” or “Reserve Inventory” in the name and wanting to make a change to it, it is always better to end date the previous Allocation and set up a new one with the values looking for moving forward.
    ​
    ​

  • As a best practice, Allocations Start Date should be set to a future date.

Distributor guide to the InvoiceEDBL import routine for loading verified sales history or supplier billbacks into Encompass: required fields, pricing mapping and reimport risks. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Minimum Requirements of Report or spreadsheet used to import:

  • Customer ID

  • Date (Invoices will use Routing method 1)

  • Product ID

  • Num Units

  • Location = Numeric LocationID

Additional Optional Fields:

  • Product Name (Only if overriding non-inventory Product Name)

  • Full Price (Only required if current pricing structure cannot be used)

  • PromoOverridden = 1 (Used to lock in specific pricing if current pricing structure cannot be used)

  • Routing Method (How the invoice will be routed)

  • Route Number or RouteID (Used to specify a specific route)

  • Invoice ID, Invoice Num, or PONum (Used to match and update an existing invoice)

Steps

System Behavior:

  • Will import verified Invoice(s) on the date(s) provided. It will affect inventory.

  • If you have more than one Invoice EDBL Routine, an ImportGroupID must be used. Otherwise, the 2nd routine will zero any invoices from the 1st routine, for any dates that exist on the 2nd routine.

  • Reimports after importing AR: Likely will have to rerun AR import. AR is deleted on reimport of invoices for a given day

  • After importing Sales Run Inventories Import to reverse sales history

  • Pricing - At a minimum map EXTPrice, numUnits, participation and discount

  • Reimport - Close the day to verify all Invoice Payments. Any not verified could be deleted. If you have to export/reimport grab Invoice IDs for payment and invoice, AR Account ID, Customer ID

Recommendations:

  • Deposit: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • DepositID: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • Discount: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • ImportGroupID: If not mapped, it is recommended to set the default value to 1. However, it is recommended to explicitly map it for better control.

  • LaidInCost: It is recommended to include this field; otherwise, historical invoices may lack costing information.

  • LocationID or LocationID_Translation: It is necessary to have an actual Location record existing. If only one location is used, it is recommended to statically map it. If neither is provided, LocationID defaults to Customer.Location. This mapping is recommended.

  • Participation: It is recommended to set the default value to zero if not mapped.

  • Pricing: For UnitPrice, FullPrice, ExtPrice, and Discount, it is possible to leave a value of 0, but there aren't many use cases for that. It is recommended to fill in at least 2 out of 3 fields, and it is sufficient to provide just one of them. Unit Price is preferred over Ext Price; it is not necessary to provide both.

Fields And Definitions

Invoices EDBL:

  • Start in Verified Status and cannot be deleted/edited without a new import or Developer permission

  • Do NOT run recalculation to split invoices OR to calculate pricing

  • Do NOT affect inventory without using an Inventory Adjustment

  • Note: This will clear all sales for the date range by default as this EDBL is assuming you will be importing the full data set for this date range. Clear all sales for date range must be explicitly mapped to false for all sales to not be cleared. Please contact support before running an InvoiceEDBL.

  • Best used for:

  • Supplier Billbacks

  • Sales History (Go-Live)

Best Practices

Import routines are an incredibly powerful tool and if used incorrectly, can affect alot of data. Test thoroughly on small data sets before importing.

If you are running into setup issues or have questions, reach out to Encompass Support.

Do you have a complex process that consists of a report and import routines that you do not want to setup? Contact our professional services to team to assist.

16991312:
Supplier FAQ for Connect Distributor Reporting (CDR) in dsdlink: fixing Products Not Mapped, filters vs columns, export format issues, saving reports and setting custom date ranges. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Reporting- Reporting FAQ

-Why is some of my data within a report displaying as 'Products Not Mapped'?

-> "Products Not Mapped" displayed because there are products in a distributor's site that are not linked to the global database (dsdlink). The recommended solution is to use the distributors tab to link global products created in PIM to the corresponding local products in the distributor site. Once the links are set the data will display in the reporting tab as you have created the data in PIM. This is especially helpful when running a report across multiple distributors at once, you will not see duplicate products since all local distributor products are mapped to 1globalproduct. Ultimately this workflow will help to mitigate discrepancies and will make reporting cleaner for export.

Another solution that does not require product mapping is to utilize the filter "Unmapped Product Behavior" and set it to "Display Distributor Data". When you run a report with this filter, displayed will be the names of the products as the distributor has them in their individual site. Product names can vary greatly from distributor to distributor, so keep that in mind. Using this workflow will cause some duplicates and likely some discrepancies when running a report across multiple distributors at once. Local product names will be indicated with a "*" by the product names. Products with no "*" are already linked to the global database. Please check the distributors tab for linking accuracy.

-What are Filters?

-> Filters in CDR are very similar to any other reporting software or data management software. Filters allow you to sort through and display only the selected data that you want to see. i.e. only 1 distributor, 3 different product packages

-What are Columns?

-> Columns are where you can manipulate how you want your data to display. Parent, Child, and Detail is the hierarchy with Detail being the most granular and Parent being the most broad. You have the ability to customize these columns by clicking and dragging the different fields to the location that you want them. You can also do this further down on the screen and change the Values that you see in the report.

-My Exported files are displayed differently than what is in CDR?

-> When exporting data, Excel export tends to work best for more complex and layered reports. CSV downloads can have issues populating as CSV formatting can struggle with complexlayered reports.

- I have a report that I like, how do I save it for future reference?

-> You have the ability to save a report. Just click "Save Report As" and you can then categorize it how you would like. You can save the report under your user or another user within your company that currently has access. Saved Reports can then be accessed for later use under the "Saved Reports" category at the bottom of the Reporting tab.

-I want a report with a more specificdaterange than is offered in the drop down, how do I do this?

-> You can create a "New Report" and this will allow you to set a specific date range i.e. June 5th -> June 13th

Distributor guide to setting wholesale, retail and consumable units per case in Encompass, plus Sell By Case Only and EDI unit of measure, so products sell in cases or eaches. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

When to Setup Product Authorizations:
​
​

  • When a specific retailer sells the product to a consumer differently than other retailers, Product Authorizations should be created.
    ​
    ​

  • Chains like Costco and WalMart sell many products by the Wholesale Unit or Consumable instead of the Retail Unit.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Setting Retail Units = Wholesale Units:
​
​

  • When the Retailer sells the product as a full case and does not break it out, the Retail Units will match Wholesale Units. These are generally large cases without smaller individual packages inside of them.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Setting Consumable Units = Retail Units:
​
​

  • When the Retailer sells the product by individual Bottle, the Retail Units should match the Consumable Units. These are generally larger format products or ‘Loose’ products that are sold to Bars/Restaurants/Convenience Store
    ​
    ​
    ​

How to determine what to set wholesale units per case to:
​
​

  • First you need to think about how you want your company to interact with the product. If on purchase, sale, and inventory of the product you want to have your team able to enter cases and eaches in seperate boxes, then wholesale units should be greater than 1.
    ​
    ​

  • If you price the product by each unit, then you will also want to have wholesale units per case greater than 1.
    ​
    ​

  • If you want to price by the case, but still allow your reps to sell inidividual units, you can set wholesale units per case to 1 and set sell by case only to allow sell by consumable units on the product or allow decimals so your team can sell a partial case.

Fields And Definitions

Package: Packages table defines how the product is organized for sale to Distributors, Retailers, & Consumers. Packages may be setup to sell specific products to different types of customers (On-Premise / Off-Premise). This will define the Retail Units Per Case that are set on the Package. If unique packages are not setup, Product Authorizations may be needed to override the default Retail Units per Case
​
​Wholesale Units Per Case: Wholesale Units per Case defines how the Distributor sells the product to a Retailer AND how the Distributor purchases the product from a Supplier. This field determines how you receive and sell the product. If wholesale units per case is set to 1, you will only see a box to enter case quantities. If wholesale units is greater than 1, you will see a box for Cases and a box for Eaches.
​
​

  • Beer and Non-Alcoholic products are normally sold by the Case (Wholesale Units Per Case = 1).
    ​
    ​

  • Wine & Spirits are normally sold by the Bottle (Wholesale Units Per Case >1)
    ​
    ​

Retail Units Per Case: Retail Units define how the Retailer sells the product to the Consumer. These values are used to convert the Wholesale Units into quantities that match the Retailer’s Software. Depending on the type of Retailer the product may be sold in different Retail Units. Product Authorizations can be used to manage these differences
​
​Consumable Units Per Case: Consumable Units define the total number of individual units in the Package. This is used to define the smallest units that can be picked up from the retailer.
​
​Unit of Measure: This will determine how units are translated through EDI. If this is set to Case, this will transmit all num units as cases. If it is set to each or bottle, it will transmit each num unit as an each or a bottle.
​
​Sell By Case Only: Set on the product record to determine how your reps are able to sell the product to your customers. This can also be set on the inventory record if different locations need to interact with the product differently.
​
​Pick Units: Set on the package to determine how many units should be picked to make up a full case

Note: When customer type is set to vending, on invoices the user is able to see both cases and eaches regardless of wholesale units. Eaches references the consumable units in this scenario.

Best Practices

  • Retail Units should always be greater than or equal to Wholesale Units
    ​
    ​

  • Consumable Units should always be greater than or equal to Retail Units
    ​
    ​

  • Wholesale units should be less than or equal to the consumable unit

What is DEX?

​

Best Practices

Need a different DUNs for individual product groups?

Steps

PIM- Product Information Management FAQ

Q: How were my existing Brands and Products created in the first place?
​
​

  • Connect Distributor Reporting and PIM are directly connected to dsdlink which is the Encompass crowd sourced global database. This means that previous users of dsdlink (likely from distributors) created the existing Brands/Products for your supplier(s). The goal of PIM is to make sure that suppliers have the ability to manage their own Brands/Products within dsdlink. Once data is created in PIM, that data is then accessible across Encompass.

Q: What is the difference between a Brand Family, Brand, and Product?
​
​

  • A Brand Family is a group or collection of similarly branded flavors (examples- a rotating IPA series, seasonals, barrel aged).
    ​
    ​

  • A Brand is the flavor, so anytime that there is a new/distinct flavor produced by your company it should be a new Brand in PIM. For vintage conscious users, each vintage should be its own flavor. Please add the vintage after the Brand name, i.e. 2019
    ​
    ​

  • A Product is simply the package configuration tied to a brand. It is common to have many different products under a single brand if your company utilizes different packages.

Q: I have duplicates of Brands/Products, how do I consolidate them?
​
​

  • This functionality is not offered in PIM and you will need to contact Support via the Support Dashboard on the left hand side of the screen to have this completed by an analyst.

Q: What images should I be using?
​
​

  • For Brands a brand logo should be used that is not package specific. For Products, a package with a brand logo on it is appropriate, i.e. a bottle or 6pack with the brand logo

Distributor guide to AR Enforcement Methods on credit terms in Encompass: when drivers or reps on Encompass Mobile must collect past-due AR or an override code. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

When is AR Enforced?

AR is due on an invoice when it is equal to or past the invoices due date. AR can be enforced when there is ARDue in excess of a customers credit limit. If there is no credit limit set, AR will be enforced when ARDue is >0. AR is enforced based on the AR Enforcment Method set on the credit term.

AR Enforcement Methods:
​

0) Do not Enforce: the system will not prompt for payment and allow the driver to print the invoice without collection. Note: The Total Balance and Amount Due Fields are visible in Invoice Total page(handheld).
​
​
​1) Before Invoice Print at Delivery (Enforce on Print Rules when Exiting a Customer): prompts the delivery driver to collect AR (or an override code) upon signing the invoice, printing the invoice, and backing out of the customer event. The current load sheet should be loaded.
​
​
​5) Before Invoice Print at Delivery: prompts the user to collect AR upon signing and printing the invoice. The current load sheet should be loaded. It will not enforce AR collection if the invoice is not signed or printed.
​
​
​2) Before Order Entry at Pre-Sales: prompts users to collect AR when they attempt to print or enter invoice. The current load sheet status should be less than Loaded.
​
​
​3) Before Invoice Print or Before Pre-Sales (Enforce on Print Rules when Exiting a Customer): prompts delivery users to collect AR (or an override code) upon entering a new invoice, signing the invoice, and printing the invoice. The current load sheet should be new or loaded.
​
​
​6) Before Invoice Print or Before Pre-Sales: prompts delivery users to collect AR (or an override code) upon entering a new invoice, signing the invoice, printing the invoice, and backing out of the customer event. The current load sheet should be new or loaded.
​
​
​4) Before Order Entry at Driver-Sell (Enforce on Print Rules when Exiting a Customer): prompts the user to collect AR when they click on the invoice link to enter the invoice, upon printing the invoice, and when backing out of the customer event. The current load sheet must be loaded.
​
​
​7) Before Order Entry at Driver-Sell: prompts driver sell user to collect AR when they attempt to print or enter invoice. The current load sheet must be loaded.
​
​
​8) Do Not Enforce and Hide AR Collection Fields: The system will not prompt for payment and allow the driver to print the invoice without collection. Note: The Total Balance and Amount Due fields are hidden from view in Invoice Total page(handheld).

Fields And Definitions

  • Credit Term: Dictates the time limit and way a customer is able to pay for an invoice before it is overdue.
    ​
    ​

  • Days of Credit: How long after an invoice is delivered before the invoice is due.
    ​
    ​

  • AR Enforcement Method: How internal reps interact with AR for this customer.

Need to set a Price Posting EDI, but not sure which one? Below are some key functionalities of each!

EDI 832 - also known as a Price/Sales Catalog: EDI 832 is usually sent periodically (quarterly, for example), and offers price and product information for an entire catalog of items.

EDI 888 - also known as an Item Maintenance document. It carries details about a specific product or product. This document is multidirectional, meaning it can be used by a variety of supply chain businesses, but is most commonly used by sellers and brokers.

The awesome thing about EDI is that there is so much online help to troubleshoot, here is one for EDI transaction codes.

16991329:
Distributor guide to the month-end Bill & Ship process in Encompass: book sales this month for delivery next month using Bill & Ship routes and the Month End Rebate Builder. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

What is a Bill & Ship?
​
​

  • The salesmen will sell items to a customer on the last day of the month. The sales are counted as sales for the current month, but they will not actually be delivered till the next month. This allows for the customer to pay for pricing during the current month, when the invoices are delivered the following month.


​
How does a Bill & Ship start?
​
​

  1. The salesmen adds an invoice for a customer on his iPad, he selects a "Bill & Ship" Route and a delivery date equal to the last day of the current month (example invoice # 124-25 on 9/30) NOTE: The bill & Ship routes are titled like "Bill & Ship 2nd Tuesday". The date portion of the route name is important; it indicates when the invoice will actually be delivered.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Then what?
​
​

  1. When all Bill & Ship orders are entered, a user must make sure all of the load sheets with a Bill & Ship route are dated for the last day of the month.
    ​
    ​

  2. Then the user goes to Control Panel, then searches for Month End Rebate Builder, and then clicks on the Bill & Ship Tab. From here you select the last day of the month and click process.
    ​
    ​
    ​

What happens during the Month End Rebate builder?
​
​

  1. We make a copy of all of the Bill & Ship invoices, and append an S to the front of the invoice number (example S124-25). Those Invoices are then verified - thus counting the sale under the current month.
    ​
    ​

  2. We also reverse the S invoice, but attach a R to the invoice number (example R124-25), this invoice is put on a verified load sheet dated for the 2nd Tuesday of the next month (the second Tuesday date is determined by the date described on the Bill & Ship Route)
    ​
    ​

  3. The Original Invoice is moved from the last day of the current month to the 2nd Tuesday of next month. The invoice is on New status load sheet, and the Route is Bill & Ship 2nd Tuesday

Best Practices

  • Bill and Ship can be run for an individual location by selecting it in the dashboard. To run Bill and Ship for All Locations, select All Locations.
    ​
    ​

  • Ensure all loadsheets are in new status
    ​
    ​

  • Bill and ship can be run after the last day of the month, just ensure you have not performed end of day for the last day of the month

  • If Bill and Ship has been run for a location already and there are additional invoices that need to have the bill and ship process run, please set all loadsheets to a new status to rerun the process for all loadsheets. Re-running the process will delete all S and R invoices that were already created.

Promotion Override Rules:
​
​

1. All Rules
​
​

  • A promotion with override level of 'All Rules' would allow the mobile device user to apply to a Product any active promotion in the system currently associated with said Product and that customer, regardless of Start/End Date and Num Units filters.

2. Min Num Units
​
​

  • A promotion with override level of 'Min Num Units' would allow a mobile device user to apply that promotion to an item for a customer where that customer meets all the qualifications of the promotion except for the minimum number of units (quantity discount). For example, Customer C is set up to receive a $2 discount D on product P if they purchase 10 units on an invoice. The invoice has ordered only 8 units, so the system did not automatically apply discount D to product P. However, if discount D was set to Override Level 'Min Num Units', a mobile device user would be able to apply discount D manually for Product P on that invoice.

3. No Override To
​
​

  • A promotion with an override level of 'No Override To' indicates that the user cannot override to that promotion on the mobile device, regardless of other options and qualifications.

4. No Override From
​
​

  • A promotion with override level of 'No Override From' indicates that the user cannot override to any other promotion except for that one. With this, the user can select either that promotion or no promotion.

16991344:
Distributor guide to AR Account Maps in Encompass: how an AR Account gets its company and GL accounts by location/product group, how to change it, and fixing a missing invoice logo. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

The purpose of AR Account Maps is to determine which General Ledger Accounts and which Company an AR Account will be tied to. The AR Account Maps table allows users to map AR Accounts to specific Accounts Receivable, Undeposited Funds, and other accounts based on the customer's location or product group.
​
​
​How is the Company Determined?
​
​

  • The company on an AR Account is determined from the AR Map ID.
    ​
    ​

  • AR Maps can be created or modified as needed to generate the desired structure.
    ​
    ​

How is ARMapID Calculated on the AR Account?
​
​

AR Map is calculated by matching Location and Product Groups to determine the AR Map that should be used. Encompass will try to find the most granular level of data first to determine a match, and then if no matches are found, Encompass will move to the next step.
​
​

1. Customers.LocationID = ARMaps.LocationID
​
​OR
​
ARMaps.LocationID IS NULL AND SplitInvoice.ProductGroupID = ARMaps.ProductGroupID

2. Customers.LocationID = ARMaps.LocationID
​
​OR
​
ARMaps.LocationID IS NULL AND Customers.ProductGroupID = ARMaps.ProductGroupID

3. Customers.LocationID = ARMaps.LocationID AND ARMaps.ProductGroupID IS NULL

4. ARMaps.LocationID Is Null AND ARMaps.ProductGroupID Is Null

5. MIN(ARMaps.ARMapID)
​
​

How to change an AR Map on an AR Account?
​
​

ARMap is a calculated field on the AR Account and cannot be directly edited. To change the ARMap on an AR Account users must either update the Customer's split invoicing to match an ARAccount Map, update the Customer's Product Group to match an ARAccount Map, or update/add an AR Account Map to match the criteria they need.

Logo Is Not Printing?
​
​

If other Invoices using the same template are printing the logo correctly, check the ARAccount.ARMapID if there is a Mapped Location set on the AR Map. If there is, the mapped location may be missing an Invoice Logo Document and the user will need to add one.

Fields And Definitions

AR Map: An AR Map will determine which Accounts in the General Ledger and which Company an AR Account will be tied to.
​
​Mapped Location: This will control the mapped location and logo that is printed for Invoices tied to AR Accounts on this AR Account Map
​
Transaction Source: Invoices
​
​Determining Factors:
​

  • Company
    ​
    ​

  • Location
    ​
    ​

  • Product Group

Best Practices

  • Ensure AR Account Maps are set up for each of the locations without a product group assigned to ensure that if there are no matches on steps 1-2 above, an AR Account can match on location.
    ​
    ​

  • If users have specific products tied to a different company, make sure they have split invoicing setup for these products and separate AR Account maps so these products can be assigned to the correct company

Tip: When troubleshooting why an Invoice hit a certain AR Map, check the Payment Customer set on the AR Account.

Brewery/producer overview of how the automated taproom POS integration imports POS sales into Encompass, translates POS products, and generates taproom invoices. Requires v23.03+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.03

Steps

How does the TapRoom POS Integration Work?

Importing Data to ECP:
​
​

Fully Automated:
​
​

  1. Data is collected from the POS System and uploaded to an API to the Handoff site.
    ​
    ​

  2. The data is then transformed to a standard format in handoff.
    ​
    ​

  3. Using an API and POS Translation Table We will pull the standard data to Encompass to populate the POS Orders and POS Order Trans tables.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Semi-Automated:
​
​

  1. Data is collected in a POS System.
    ​
    ​

  2. Raw data is formatted using reports/import routines to be translated to the standard format.
    ​
    ​

  3. Raw data is imported directly to POS Orders and POS Order Trans.
    ​
    ​
    ​

Translating products from POS to ECP:
​
​

  1. The POS Translation Table is how we determine what POS Products are tied to what ECP products and how we will convert the Num Units from the POS System to ECP
    ​
    ​

Generating Invoices:
​
​

16991351:
Supplier FAQ for Connect Distributor Reporting in dsdlink: why data shows as Products Not Mapped, using filters and columns, Excel vs CSV exports, saving reports and custom date ranges. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Reporting- Reporting FAQ

-Why is some of my data within a report displaying as 'Products Not Mapped'?

-> "Products Not Mapped" displayed because there are products in a distributor's site that are not linked to the global database (DSDLink). The recommended solution is to use the distributors tab to link global products created in PIM to the corresponding local products in the distributor site. Once the links are set the data will display in the reporting tab as you have created the data in PIM. This is especially helpful when running a report across multiple distributors at once, you will not see duplicate products since all local distributor products are mapped to 1globalproduct. Ultimately this workflow will help to mitigate discrepancies and will make reporting cleaner for export.

Another solution that does not require product mapping is to utilize the filter "Unmapped Product Behavior" and set it to "Display Distributor Data". When you run a report with this filter, displayed will be the names of the products as the distributor has them in their individual site. Product names can vary greatly from distributor to distributor, so keep that in mind. Using this workflow will cause some duplicates and likely some discrepancies when running a report across multiple distributors at once. Local product names will be indicated with a "*" by the product names. Products with no "*" are already linked to the global database. Please check the distributors tab for linking accuracy.

-What are Filters?

-> Filters in CDR are very similar to any other reporting software or data management software. Filters allow you to sort through and display only the selected data that you want to see. i.e. only 1 distributor, 3 different product packages

-What are Columns?

-> Columns are where you can manipulate how you want your data to display. Parent, Child, and Detail is the hierarchy with Detail being the most granular and Parent being the most broad. You have the ability to customize these columns by clicking and dragging the different fields to the location that you want them. You can also do this further down on the screen and change the Values that you see in the report.

-My Exported files are displayed differently than what is in CDR?

-> When exporting data, Excel export tends to work best for more complex and layered reports. CSV downloads can have issues populating as CSV formatting can struggle with complexlayered reports.

- I have a report that I like, how do I save it for future reference?

-> You have the ability to save a report. Just click "Save Report As" and you can then categorize it how you would like. You can save the report under your user or another user within your company that currently has access. Saved Reports can then be accessed for later use under the "Saved Reports" category at the bottom of the Reporting tab.

-I want a report with a more specificdaterange than is offered in the drop down, how do I do this?

-> You can create a "New Report" and this will allow you to set a specific date range i.e. June 5th -> June 13th

16991354:
Distributor guide to 894 pre-delivery and 856 ASN EDI files in Encompass: when they send, how to resend, and how to check if a retailer received one. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

When Do 894s and 856s send:
​
​

  • 894s and 856s will send when all pallets on an invoice have been confirmed after the time set on system setting 253: Auto-Send Start Time: Start sending Confirmed Outbound Pre-Delivery/ASN EDI at this time.
    ​
    ​

  • If pallets have been created but are not yet confirmed by the deadline set on system setting 254: Auto-Send Deadline Time: Send all un-sent Outbound Pre-Delivery/ASN EDI at this time. We will send all unconfirmed invoices at this time to ensure they make it to the retailer by delivery. 856 files must have all pallets confirmed prior to sending.
    ​
    ​
    ​

How is a customer or chain connected to an 894 or 856 configuration?
​
​

  • A customer or chain can be linked to an exchange configuration through an AR Account, a product group, or terms but is most commonly linked through an AR Account on the Exchange Configuration AR Account table.
    ​
    ​

How to resend an 894 or 856 file?
​
​

  1. Find the Invoice(s) that need to be resent.
    ​
    ​

  2. Set the EDI Status on the invoice to Resend Pre-Delivery.
    ​
    ​

  3. "Generate Outbound EDI Invoices" will run in the next 15 minutes to automatically send a new file to the retailer.
    ​
    ​

How can I see if an invoice has sent through EDI?
​
​

  1. Go to the invoice wanting to review.
    ​
    ​

  2. Open Invoice View.
    ​
    ​

  3. Scroll to the bottom and view the Exchange tasks (Note: All EDI files will have a link to the file that was sent to the retailer).
    ​
    ​

Is a retailer saying they did not receive a file?
​
​

  • If users check the exchange task that sent to the customer make sure to check the status. If it is showing successfully sent, that means the file was transmitted from the users ECP site.
    ​
    ​

  • Sometime trading partners will send an MDN to confirm the file was received. This can be seen by viewing the details on an exchange task.
    ​
    ​

  • If the exchange task shows successfully sent and there is an MDN it means the file was successfully sent and was received by the trading partner but does not guarentee the file processed successfully.
    ​
    ​

  • If there is no exchange task on the invoice, nothing will have sent. Users can try resending the file to see if it will resend, or users may need to check to see if the invoice is tied to an exchange configuration by looking at the terms, ar account, and product group to see if it meets the filters on the configuration.
    ​
    ​

  • If the file is not sent directly to the retailer, please contact the trading partner it sent to first before reaching out to Encompass to ensure the file was received and processed successfully on their end.

Fields And Definitions

856/ASN: An ASN or advanced shipment notice is a form of EDI that sends prior to delivery. This file contains the products and pallets that are expected to be delievered. ASNs can make the check in process quicker as the check in person scans the pallet, their system already knows exactly what is on the pallet. This file does not include prices.

894: An 894 or predevlivery invoices is a form of EDI that is sent prior to delivery. An 894 will usually contain all the invoice data such as pricing, products and quantities. An 894 can help get an invoice into a retailers system prior to check-in.

EDI Status: A field which will show the last type of EDI sent on the invoice. This can be used to resend EDI by manually changing the EDI Status.

MDN: A form of confirmation a file was received.

16991357:
Distributor explanation of how Encompass calculates an invoice price: Front Line, Product Price fallback, deepest discount, promotion types, and attaching customers and products. Includes video. v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Pre-Conditions

Promotion Types Overview
​
​1) Front Line: First level of pricing for Customers, essentially the Full Price. NOTE: If a Front Line price is not set up for a Customer or Product, the system will default to the Price field on the Product.
​
​

2) Discount: Allows users to set the Discount amount that will be subtracted from the Front Line Price. For example, ".50" in the Amount field equates to a 50 cent discount.
​
​

3) Case Discount: Allows users to set the Discount amount that will be subtracted from the Front Line Price only when the Product is sold in full case amounts.
​
​

4) Price: Allows users to set the desired selling Price for the Product. If the Front Line Price is $35 and the Price type discount Amount is set to $30, the system will calculate a discount of $5 and make sure the selling price is $30.
​
​

5) Case Price: Allows users to set the desired selling Price for the Product only when the Product is sold in full case amounts.
​
​

6) Percentage: Sets the discount amount based on a percentage of the Front Line Price. Amount of .10 would create a discount of 10% off the Front Line Price of the Product.
​
​

7) Rebate: Allows users to sell at full price throughout the month and then run the Month End Rebate Builder at the end of the month to issue credits to qualified customers on qualified sales.
​
​

8) Zero: This will sell the Product at $0. Typically used for Inventory Adjustments, Donations, or Samples.
​
​

9) FOB: Product will sell at the FOB (Freight on Board) cost value pulled from the Product's Inventory Record.
​
​

10) Laid-In - Tax: formerly FOB + Freight + OtherCost): Product will sell at the FOB + Freight + OtherCost pulled from the Product's Inventory record.
​
​

11) Laid-in: Product will sell at the Laid In Cost pulled from the Product's Inventory record.
​
​

12) Laid In +Tax: Product will sell at the Laid In Cost + Tax pulled from the Product's Inventory record.
​
13) Rebate Equivalencies: Allows users to sell at full price throughout the month and then run the Month End Rebate Builder at the end of the month to issue credits to qualified customers on qualified sales. In rebate Builder, it will allow users to specify the equivalency for the Products within the Promotion.

Watch video on YouTube

Fields And Definitions

Frontline Price
​
​

  • Picks the LOWEST Frontline price available for this Customer, for this Product, for this delivery day.
    ​
    ​

Product Price
​
​

  • Only uses the Price from the Product record if no Frontline exists for this customer, this product, this day. This is the fallback, default price.
    ​
    ​

  • If the customer account type is set to Transfer Out, the customer will get pricing at laid-in cost if they do not have a frontline price.
    ​
    ​

  • If the customer account type is set to Inventory Adjustment, the customer will get pricing at zero cost if they do not have a frontline price.
    ​
    ​

Discount
​
​

  • Applies the best (DEEPEST) available Promotion (Type = Discount, Price, etc.) for this Customer, this Product, this day


Taxes and Deposits
​
​

  • Calculates and adds in any Sales Taxes, Fees, and Deposits

Attaching Customers
​
​

  • Markets: Markets can be used to group Zones together. A Market is a collection of Customers who receive the same Promotion. A Customer may belong to multiple Zones, therefore, belonging to multiple Markets.
    ​
    ​

  • Zones: Used to assign groups of Customers together. A Zone is a collection of Customers that receive similar pricing. Chains may also be attached through Zones.
    ​
    ​

  • Individually: A single Customer can be linked to a Promotion with a Promotions Customers Record.

Assigning Products
​
​

Products can be linked to a Promotion through:
​
​

  • Lines: A Line is a group of Products that receive the same Promotion. A Product may belong to multiple Lines.
    ​
    ​

  • Individually: A single Product can be added to a Promotion with a Promotions Products record.
    ​
    ​

  • All Products Field: This is typically used for Zero Promotions, Laid In Promotions, and Cost Type Promotions. Toggling the All Products field on a Promotion to True, will indicate All Products will receive that Promotion.

Best Practices

Best Practices
​
​

  • On any invoice, click on a price to bring up the price calculator. This will show what promotion was applied, what other promotions it was qualified for, and if promotions were not qualified, why they were not qualified.
    ​
    ​

  • If every Customer receives the same Front Line price, use Products.Price on the Products Table.
    ​
    ​

  • Set up at least one Front Line price for each Product. Use a different Front Line Promotion or each Supplier (or Brand if the Supplier is large).
    ​
    ​

  • Set Products.Price to highest Front Line price for that Product through enabling a weekly Import Project to copy the highest Front Line price to Products.Price.
    ​
    ​

  • Use Table Copy to create new promotions and put an end-date on the old promotions. This is particularly important on large Front Line promotions.

Bad Practices
​
​

  • Editing amounts on existing promotions for price changes.
    ​
    ​

  • Deleting existing Promotions.
    ​
    ​

  • Setting Products.Price to $999.99 or $0.00.
    ​
    ​

  • Having a single Frontline for All Products when dealing with a large SKU count.

Distributor steps for sending pricing to 99 Bottles automatically: install the app in Encompass, set up 99B Price Posting Templates, and share your EncompassID. Requires v22.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.08

Steps

The 99 Bottles Pricing API, 99Bottles_GetPricePostingData, provides a method for 99 Bottles to query Encompass for the most recent pricing for a pre-arranged set of Chains or Customers. It is designed to replace the manual generation and upload of pricing data to the 99 Bottles website. To get started, users must first download the Application in the App Library and begin to setup their Price Posting Templates.

General Setup:

  1. Install the Application

  2. Create Price Positng Templates

  3. Provide EncompassID and CustomerID to 99Bottles

  4. Pull data from 99 Bottles

Price Posting Template Setup Steps:

  1. The Price Posting Template field must contain “99B” somewhere in the name. For examples, “Walmart

  2. 99B East Area”.

  3. Posting Interval = Weekly

  4. Pricing Days in the Future = 12 Weeks Out

  5. Best Price = False

  6. Refresh Posting = True

  7. Fields such as Customer and Next Run Date must be filled in accordingly. Let 99 Bottles know the initial Next Run Date value so that they can schedule their API calls to match when the data is generated.

  8. Product Group is optional and could be used to filter the set of products that might appear in the data sent to 99 Bottles via the API

NOTE: Do not use the same customer twice in Price Posting Templates created for 99 Bottles as this will generate duplicate data records for the API

Best Practices

Selecting a reference Customer:

The 99Bottles_GetPricePostingData API utilizes data generated from Price Posting Trans records belonging to Price Posting Templates set up in a specific manner and for a set of chain(s)/customer(s) that is fully controlled by the distributor. Each Price Posting Template is associated with a single Customer that represents a pricing area. A separate Price Posting Template is needed for each pricing area. For example, If there are multiple pricing areas within a single chain, you will need a separate Pricing Posting Template setup for each pricing area within that chain. If you send pricing to 99 Bottles for both Walmart and ABC Liquors, and both of these chains receive the same pricing, then you will only need a single Price Posting Template.
​
​Other Best Practices:

  1. Always set Next Price Posting Date in future so the system can generate pricing on the next posting date

  2. Ensure the customer on the price posting template can purchase all the products you would like to post. If this product list needs to be further refined, you can add a product group on the price posting template to further limit the products being posted

  3. After setup, I would recommend reviewing the price posting template to ensure the next posting date is updated accordingly the day after the next posting date manually set on the template.

  4. Price posting will generate data overnight, so you will be able to post pricing in 99 Bottles the day after the posting.

16991362:
Distributor explanation of how return prices are calculated in Encompass, including the chain's Return At Last Price setting and last price, discount and deposit on Customer History. Requires v23.02+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.02

Steps

When Return At Last Price = False:
​
​

Always return products at the current price they can be sold. This will use regular pricing logic to calculate the return price.

When Return At Last Price = True:
​
​

Has the product been sold to this customer before?
​
​

If Yes:
​
​

If the product has been sold to the customer before, we will use the last full price, last discount, and last deposit to calculate the price the product should be returned at. This will also use the same promotion and participation that the product received when it was sold.
​
​
​

If No:
​
​

If the product has not been sold to the customer before but is still being returned, we will use the current price they can be sold to the customer at as the price to return the product. This will use regular pricing logic to calculate the return price.

Fields And Definitions

Customer History Fields for Returning Products:
​
​

  • Last Full Price: The last full price the Product has been sold to the Customer for. If the product has not been sold before, last full price will default to Product.Price.
    ​
    ​

  • Last Discount: The last discount the Product received when sold to a Customer. If the product has not been sold before, last full discount will default to $0.00.
    ​
    ​

  • Last Deposit: The last deposit the Product received when sold to a Customer. If the product has not been sold before, last full deposit will default to $0.00.
    ​
    ​

  • Last Participation: The last Participation accrued on the Product when sold to a Customer. If the product has not been sold before, last full Participation will default to $0.00.
    ​
    ​

  • Last Promotion: The last Promotion accrued on the Product when sold to a Customer. If the product has not been sold before, last full Promotion will default to an empty field.
    ​
    ​

  • Current Full Price: The current full price the customer will receive if a product is sold to the customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Current Discount: The current Discount the customer will receive if a product is sold to the customer. Note: This does not include promotions with min quantities.
    ​
    ​

  • Current Deposit: The current Deposit the customer will receive if a product is sold to the customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Current Participation: The current Participation the customer will receive on a product if a product is sold to the customer. Note: This does not include promotions with min quantities.

Chain Fields for Returning Products:
​
​

  • Return at last price: This will determine if we price returns at the current price or the last price it was sold in at to determine pricing on returns.

Product Fields for Returning Products:
​
​

  • Pick Up By Units: If set to false, partial case returns of this product will not be allowed.

Best Practices

  • Ensure Customers qualify for the pricing expected of them to receive to ensure returns are always priced correctly.

  • To change the price at which a product is returned if it has been sold to a customer, users can create an invoice with a negative and a positive transaction at the price users would like the customer to get so the last price fields on customer history update.

Distributor steps for inviting supplier users to Connect Distributor Reporting in dsdlink: check the Global Supplier ID and Supplier Vendors, add a Supplier user, and send the invite. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

How to Invite Supplier Users to Connect Distributor Reporting

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Suppliers table
    ​
    ​

  2. Search and select a Supplier to confirm that they have a Global Supplier ID which ties them to the Global Database
    ​
    ​TIP: If the Supplier does not have a Global Supplier ID, navigate to the Products table, search and select a Product, and click the 'Product Manager button to connect them. Select the matching Product in the Global Products database. The Global Supplier ID cascades up to Brand Family and Supplier records from the Product.
    ​
    ​

  3. From the Supplier record, click the Sub Tables button and select Supplier Vendors to confirm the Supplier has Suppliers Vendors record(s) linked for all Locations that sell their Products; this ties the Company you are purchasing Products from with the Supplier.
    ​
    ​NOTE: When the Supplier Data Access field is set to Allow, your data is accessed by the appropriate Supplier User in dsdlink. When set to Block, the flow of data to Suppliers Users is not permitted, should you want to stop reporting for any Location(s).
    ​
    ​

  4. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Users table
    ​
    ​

  5. Click Add Users to create a new user. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed the ‘New User’ form and click the ‘Add Record’ button when complete
    ​
    - Enter the Name, Email address to send the invitation to, and phone number if you have it
    ​
    - Set the Role field to Supplier
    ​
    ​

  6. Click the Sub Tables button from the new User's record and select 'Suppliers Users'
    ​
    ​

  7. Click the 'Add Suppliers Users' button to connect the Supplier's and User's records - this ensures that the User can only see Products under that Supplier.
    ​
    ​

  8. Now that the User has been created and connected to a Supplier, and the Supplier is linked in the Global Database through the Global Supplier ID, Click the 'Invite to dsdlink' link on the Suppliers Users record to send an invite via email.
    ​
    ​Optional - Let the user know in a friendly email that they have been invited to the platform! Once the user logs in and sets a password they are able to access Encompass Support and Help Resources.
    ​

Possible barriers that you may encounter when inviting users:

  • The global supplier that you are trying to connect to does not exist when trying to link a brand or product. You will want to submit a support task to Encompass so that they can get that record added.
    ​
    ​

  • The users email domain does not match that of the global supplier in dsdlink. You also will want to submit a ticket to Encompass so that an analyst can add the domain to our records which helps to ensure data integrity for all of our users.

Distributor steps for controlling which products a chain can buy (authorization lists) and overriding UPC or chain product numbers for EDI with Product Authorizations in Encompass. Includes video. v22.06+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.06

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

What is a Product Authorization:
​
​

  • Product Authorizations are a way to control which products can be purchased at the chain level, which is common when chains have an 'authorization list' of products that are allowed to be sold into their stores. These also affect how these products are communicated to the chain through EDI.
    ​
    ​

  • Product Authorizations also allow for overriding certain product values for that specific chain. For example: Overriding the normal product UPC when they chain needs this product to have a different UPC.

How to set up a Product Authorization:
​
​

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the 'Product Authorizations' table
    ​
    ​

  2. Click the 'Add Product Authorizations' button
    ​
    ​

  3. Select a Chain
    ​
    ​

  4. Select a Product
    ​
    ​

  5. Configure the Authorized field to determine if the Chain should purchase this Product
    ​
    ​

  6. Select a Start Date
    ​
    ​

  7. Fill in other information as needed
    ​
    ​

  8. Click Add Record

Fields And Definitions

Require Product Authorizations:
​
​

  • If Requires Product Authorization = False (default), All products are authorized based on other product controls.
    ​
    ​

  • If Requires Product Authorization = True, The only products that can be purchased by customers in the chain are product that have been authorized through product authorizations.
    ​
    ​

  • This field is set on the Chain
    ​
    ​

Product Authorization:
​
​

  • A way to limit or enable sales of a product based on the associated chain.
    ​
    ​

Chain Product Num:
​
​

  • The product number the chain associates with this product
    ​
    ​

Authorized:
​
​

  • When set to True, the Chain can buy this Product.
    ​
    ​

  • When set to False, the Chain cannot buy this Product.
    ​
    ​

Retail Units Per Case:
​
​

  • Retail Units define how the Retailer sells the product to the Consumer.
    ​
    ​

  • These values are used to convert the Wholesale Units into quantities that match the Retailer’s Software.
    ​
    ​

Unit of Measure:
​
​

  • Unit of Measure determines how this product is sold.
    ​
    ​

  • These values are used to convert the unit of measure to match the Retailer’s Software.
    ​
    ​

Unit of Measure Code:
​
​

  • How the Unit of Measure will be sent through EDI.
    ​
    ​

UPC Override:
​
​

  • A UPC that will override the UPC set on the Product record for this Chain.
    ​
    ​

  • This field is very useful for seasonal product management.
    ​
    ​

Start/End Date:
​
​

  • Start and End Date dictate how long a Product Authorization will last.

Pre-Conditions

Minimum Requirements of Report or spreadsheet used to import:

​

    ​

    ​
    ​

  • Import Projects that look to add a fee to one invoice per Customer per.

    ​

  • Day (not all invoices).

  • If a complex process that consists of a report and import routines that users do not want to setup? Contact our professional services to team to assist.

Distributor reference for nightly OMS scheduled tasks in Encompass (pricing recalcs, Customer History, AR open credit/debit) and which tasks must be run manually. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Steps

Tasks That are automatically run Daily:
​
​

Check_ProductsAreas

  • Time: 11:00 PM - 4:15 AM
    ​
    ​

  • Function: Determines where products can be sold and if product areas have changed.

Recalculate Invoice Pricing All

  • Time: 11:10 PM - 4:15 AM
    ​
    ​

  • Function: When running, it looks for with Products or Prices not zero, the Invoice must be unlocked and the Loadsheet.Status must be Loaded or less


Update_Customer_History

  • Time: 10:35 PM - 4:15 AM
    ​
    ​

  • Function: updates the sales and inventory into Customer History records. Checks if there are Load Sheets that are in Returned or above status, or if Store Depletions records were created at that day.


Set_DelayedInvoiceTotals

  • Time: 12:15 AM - 12:14 AM
    ​
    ​

  • Repeat: 15 min
    ​
    ​

  • Function: Calculates Pricing on all Invoices that have been Changed but Update Pricing was deleted

Update_AccountsRec

  • Time: 10:45 PM - 4:15 AM
    ​
    ​

  • Repeat: 60 min
    ​
    ​

  • Function: Change the EDIStatus whenever an Invoice meets the following conditions:
    ​
    - LoadSheet.`Status` = Verified
    ​
    -Invoice.EDIStatus = NotYetTransmitted
    ​
    -Invoice.DueDate <= time of day minus 7 days


Update_OpenCredit_OpenDebit

  • Time: 10:45 PM - 4:15 AM
    ​
    ​

  • Repeat: 60 min
    ​
    ​

  • Function: it will consider the Setting 360 (Number of years back to recalculate Open Debit/Credit on Invoices (on Load Sheet Date) and Purchases (on Receive Date)
    ​
    ​

  • Note: See Setting 481 for last time AR Open Debit/Credit was calculated.

Tasks that must be manually run:
​
​

create_AccountsRecTrans

  • Function: As part of general setup, this will populate the Accounts Rec Trans Table.
    ​
    ​

  • Note: Should run after AR Period is closed and after InvoicePaymentsHist is synced to the DataWarehouse

Rebuild_CustomerHistory

  • Function: Checks if there are Load Sheets that are in Returned or above status, or if Store Depletions records were created in past 1 month. If the Scheduled Task finds any returned Load Sheets, it further checks a field on the Load Sheets records called 'Customer History Updated'. If the field is true, that Load Sheet is skipped. If it is false, the Scheduled Task uses the Invoices on those Load Sheets to update corresponding Customer History records, and updates the 'Customer History Updated' field on those Load Sheets to true

Recalculate_Invoice_Pricing_All

  • Function: When running, it looks for with Products or Prices not zero, the Invoice must be unlocked and the Loadsheet.Status must be Loaded or less

Fields And Definitions

  • API Command - These pre-built blocks of code perform functions with-in Encompass free of human input

Distributor reference for Route Types in Encompass: order cut-off time, initial Load Sheet status, bin type and Load Sheet types like Bill and Ship, Remittance and Mail-in Checks. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Steps

Routes Types are how routes function for Picking, Cut-Off Time, Bin & Load Sheet Types.

Route Type Fields and Definitions
​
​

*Order Cut-Off Time - Enforces a cut-off time for selling. After the set cut-off time, Load Sheets are automatically updated to the Locked for Routing status.
​
​ Note: This will force any new invoices or invoice changes to sync to Import Conflicts. (Users with the InvoiceEditRouting permission can still import invoices after the cut-off time).
​
​

*Initial Status - Determines the status of the Load Sheet when it is initially generated. (Scheduled Routes are generated in the new status; however, some routes need to generate in a status other than new).
​
​

  • Example: Route Type of Mail in Checks initial status is Returned
    ​
    ​

*LS Bin Type - Indicates the type of bin the Route will use. (Route Num / Vehicle Trailer Bin / User Bin / Manual Route Bin).
​
​
​ Note: The Route Type will default to LS bin Type = 1) Route Num when creating a new Route Type. (This means the Bin will be the same as the Route Num on the Route).
​
​

If no Bin that matches the Route Num exists, Encompass will automatically make one upon creating a Route.
​
Encompass will look for a Route Bin in the following order:

1. Route Bin
​
2. Vehicle’s Trailer Bin
​
3. User Bin
​
4. Locations Bin
​
​

*LS Type - Indicates the type of Load Sheet used for the Route (The LS Type is selected on the Route Type ONLY).
​
​ Note: There is no LS Type Table. Users can see which LS Type is being used in two ways: From the Route Type on the Route or The Load Sheet itself.
​
​

  • Load Sheet types have special logic behind them to perform a specific function. Load Sheet Types where Plans can be generated: Scheduled/Empty: In Find Route Logic → Find existing where Route Type’s LS type = Scheduled/Empty. Multiple Load Sheets can be generated per route, per day

Note: In ECP 18.05+ Encompass will no longer look for events where LS Type = Empty but multiple Load Sheets can still be generated per route, per day.
​
​

  • Inventory Adjustments: Used for Inventory Counts in Non-WMS locations.
    ​
    ​

  • Off-Day: Per day, only one Load Sheet can be created per location
    ​
    ​

  • Imported: Load Sheets created from an EDBL Import
    ​
    ​

  • Bill and Ship: Will only create one Load Sheet per Route. These load sheets are checked during the Bill & Ships process.
    ​
    ​

  • Transfer Planner: Load Sheets created using the Transfer Planner Tool
    ​
    ​
    ​

Load Sheet Types where Plans will NOT be generated:
​
​

  • Sales Receipts: When Salesmen add a payment invoice on handheld, will create a Salesmen Receipts Load Sheet and set it as returned.
    ​
    ​

  • Remittance: When EFT/ACH/820 remittance invoice is imported, a new remittance Load Sheet is created. Setting 342 will be used to update the Load Sheet to ‘Balanced’ status.
    ​
    ​

  • Mail-in Checks: Are manually created on Mail-In Checks Route. The load Sheet’s initial Status is set as Returned.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Rebates: Create one Load Sheet for a month for Rebates Promotions on Rebate Route. (Example: Load Sheet 3/1 will be created for promotions in February).
    ​
    ​

  • Statement Charge: Used in conjunction with Monthly Billing Frequency.
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO Adjustment: Load Sheets are created to correct inventory costing when products are sold in a FIFO layer prior to confirmation of the Purchase.
    ​
    ​

  • Price Correction: Used when making price adjustments without affecting inventory. The total Case Quantity on the Load Sheet must equal zero.
    ​
    ​

  • Opening Inventory: Created during the initial data conversion to import inventory from the previous RAS/WMS software.
