Distributor guide to App Settings in Encompass: what they are, how to add one to an app in App Manager, and how to use {setting_####} in Fusion Reports. Requires v23.02+.

Steps

What is an App Setting?
​
​

An App Setting is a value attached to an app that can be set independently for each site and dynamically referenced. They allow the user who is installing an app on their site to customize certain values that the app will use.
​
​

For example, the Security Automation: Deactivate Users After Inactivity app has an App Setting for "number of days inactive before users are deactivated". When a user installs the app, they will be asked to fill in this value. Then, the App Setting is used in reports and dynamically pulls the value for each site and inactivate users accordinly.

How does it work?
​
​

- App Settings are created under an app.
​
​

- When a user installs the app, they will enter in values for each required App Setting.
​
​

- Once installed, the values are stored in the site's Settings table.

How to create an App Setting:

1. Go to App Manager dashboard by searching "App Manager" in the Universal search bar.
​
2. Search for the app.
​
3. Select the App Settings tab.
​
4. Click the Add button

How to reference an App Setting in a Fusion Report:

1. To use Application Settings in Fusion Reports, enter the following: {setting_####}where #### is the Application Setting ID
​
Note: Users do NOT need to join in the Settings Table. This is very similar to how variables are used, the system will automatically replace the syntax above with the value of the Setting.
16991387:
Brewery setup in Encompass for the TTB Brewers Report of Operations (BRO): configure tax entities, locations, product types, brand TTB categories and customer/vendor TTB tax codes. Requires v22.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.12

Pre-Conditions


This document will guide users through the configuration of a Manufacturer site on ECP to ensure accurate representation of all beer production and removal data required for the Federal TTB Brewers Report of Operations

Steps


Setting up Tax Entities

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Tax Entities table

2. Select Add Tax Entities

NOTE: You will need to add a separate Tax Entity for every active TTB Brewer’s Notice license your organization holds

3. Enter the following information:

Tax Entity - The name of the facility that holds the Brewer’s Notice

License Number - Your Brewer’s Notice license number

FEIN - Your Federal Employer Identification Number

4. Click Save Records

Configuring Locations

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Locations table

2. Hover over the Tax Entity column and click the edit pencil

3. Select the correct Tax Entity(s) for each location

4. Click Save Records

Configuring Product Types

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Product Types table

The common Product Types that we will want to configure for reporting on the TTB BRO Report are Finished Goods (cans, bottles, kegs, etc.) and Bright Beer

2. Set the TTB Process Type on the appropriate Product Type

NOTE: Your site’s Product Type naming conventions may differ

  • For Product Type: FG - Bottles you will chose TTB Process Type = Bottled
  • For Product Type: FG - Cans you will chose TTB Process Type = Canned
  • For Product Type: FG - Kegs you will chose TTB Process Type = Racked
  • For Product Type: WIP - Bright Beer you will chose TTB Process Type = Produced

3. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Locations Product Types table

4. Set the correct Tax Entity on the Product Type to correspond with your Location(s)

Configuring Brands

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Brands table

2. Ensure all of your Brands are categorized correctly under the ‘TTB Category’ column

3. For all beer Brands, choose the TTB Category: Beer

Note: The TTB defines beer as the following: Beer, ale, porter, stout, and other similar fermented beverages (including saké and similar products) of any name or description – containing one-half of one percent or more of alcohol by volume – brewed or produced from malt, wholly or in part, or from any substitute for malt.

4.For all non alcoholic beer Brands, choose the TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV

Note: The TTB defines non alcoholic beer as the following: A beverage, produced either wholly or in part from malt (or a substitute for malt), and either fermented or unfermented, which contains, when ready for consumption, less than one-half of 1 percent (0.5%) of alcohol by volume. Substitutes for malt are rice, grain of any kind, bran, glucose, sugar, and molasses.

Configuring Customers

Customers can be categorized with a TTB Tax Code that the BRO will pull data from. For initial TTB reporting configuration, we will want to ensure the proper Tax Code is set for the tavern on brewery premises (the taproom) as well as any contract brewing partners that receive beer from the facility without payment of tax.

Setting up Tavern on Brewery Premises Customers

If your brewery is classified as a ‘brewpub’ or contains a ‘tavern on brewery premises’, you will need to set up the relevant Customer record through the following steps:

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Customers table

2. Select the Customer that represents your tavern on brewery premises

3. On the TTB Tax Code field, select Tavern on Brewery Premises and click save

Setting up Contract Partner Customers for Beer Removed Without Payment of Tax

If your brewery produces beer for another brewery Customer of the same or different ownership and you will not be tax liable for these removals, you will need to set up these Customers through the following steps:

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Customers table

2. Select the Customer that you invoice beer to without payment of tax

3. On the TTB Tax Code field, select Removed Without Payment of Tax to Other Breweries and click save

Note: If these Customers also receive tax paid removals from your brewery, an additional customer must be added to reflect this

Setting up Contract Partner Vendors for Beer Received in Bond

If your brewery purchases beer in bond from another brewery to be taxed upon removal from your facility, you will need to set up these Vendors through the following steps:

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Vendors table

2. Select the Vendor that you invoice beer to without payment of tax

3. On the TTB Tax Code field, select Received In Bond and click save

Fields And Definitions


Tax Entities - The manufacturing facility represented by your Brewer’s Notice

Product Types - The term which describes a specific group of Products

TTB Process Type: Bottled and TTB Process Type: Canned will both report as ‘Bottling’ on the BRO

TTB Process Type: Racked will report under the ‘Racking’ columns on the BRO (aka: kegged finished goods)

Brands - For the BRO, the Brands table will allow you to define the TTB Category

TTB Category: ‘Beer’ should be used for all beer brands

TTB Category: ‘Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV’ should be used for all non-alcoholic beer brands

Best Practices


  • All Load Sheets must be in ‘Balanced’ Status to accurately reflect removals data for the BRO date period chosen
  • When adding new Brands, ensure that you set the correct TTB Brand Category brands without a TTB Brand Category will be omitted from the BRO

Pre-Conditions

Setup Steps:
​
​

1. Install The Application.
​
2. Select the default route and unmapped ProductID Application Settings.
​
3. Reach out to Encompass to setup POS Integration API Commands and set EDBL ID on the application (To get started visit the Get Connected dashboard).

Steps

How to Use:
​
1. Go to the Taproom Invoice Import Dashboard.
​
2. Review Unmapped Products and Map Products.
​
3. Select Start and End Dates.
​
4. Click 'Execute' to Execute the Import Routines and generate Invoices

Fields And Definitions

POS Customer Translation

The Customer POS Translation Table is how we map the POS Data to a customer in Encompass.

POS Translation

The POS Translation Table is how we map a Product from the POS System to a Product in ECP.

  • POS Product Num maps to ECP Product ID

  • All quantities, discounts, and pricing translated via the ratio of POS Units to ECP Units

  • POS transactions for which no mapping is found are assigned to the default non-inventory item that is set on the application setting. These records should be added before running the imports. If the imports are run, and there are unmapped products, they can be manually corrected, or you can delete and recreate the invoices once the mappings are completed.

POS Order Trans

The POS Order Trans is the Order Transactions from the POS System in a standard format that can be interpreted by Encompass

POS Orders

The POS Orders is the Order records from the POS System in a standard format that can be interpreted by Encompass

Important Fields:

  • POS Location can be used to classify different sales locations and break out invoices by location

  • Sales Source determines how the order was created or generated

  • EDBLID is the ID related to your POS Integration

  • POS Map is the POS System for the data being imported

Best Practices

  • Determine a regular schedule in which you run the import. (Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Etc.)
    ​
    ​

Brewery reference for where each line of the TTB Brewers Report of Operations (BRO) dashboard in Encompass gets its data, and which statuses and TTB codes are required to show. Requires v22.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.12

Steps

  • All calculations are based on data from a chosen Location and its related Tax Entity
    ​
    ​

  • All Invoice Load Sheets must be in Loaded, Balanced, or Verified status in order to populate on report
    ​
    ​

  • All Production Orders must be in Confirmed or Verified status in order to populate on report
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO Adjustment invoices as well as Inventory Adjustment invoices created without a TTB Tax Code are omitted from the report

Monthly BRO
​
​

Additions to Beer Inventory
​

Line 1 - On hand beginning of this report period: Sum of Inventory on given start date of all Brands.TTB Category: Beer and Products with Product Type.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled
​

  • Note: The SUM of these values should match the Expected amount in Line 33 of the previous month's report. It will NOT match the Calculated amount which can be the result of issues stemming from configuration, processing transactions or manual cell overrides.

Line 2 - Beer produced by fermentation: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced brought into inventory through a Production Order
​

Line 3 - Addition of water and other liquids: Not calculated. Additions of water and other liquids in ECP should be expressed by Production Orders
​

Line 4 - Beer received from racking and bottling: This is for beer that was previously sent to a dedicated kegging or bottling area and returned to the facility. This line is not currently calculated.
​

Line 5 - Beer received in bond: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled brought into inventory on a Purchase with positive NumUnits using Vendors with TTBTaxCode: Received in Bond
​
​

Line 6 - Beer received from cellars: Same as Line 9 Column D and Line 10 Column F
​

Line 7 - Beer returned to this brewery after removal from this brewery: Sum of Product with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled brought back into inventory on a negative Invoice
​

Line 8 - Beer returned to the brewery after removal from another brewery of same ownership: This line is not currently calculated
​

Line 9 - Racked: Sum of Products brought into inventory through a Production Order with Brands.TTBCategory: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Racked
​

Line 10 - Bottled: Sum of Products brought into inventory through a Production Order with Brands.TTBCategory: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Bottled and/or Canned
​

Line 11 - Physical inventory disclosed an overage: Sum of Product with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled written out of inventory on an Inventory Adjustment type Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Overage or Shortage
​

Line 13 - Total additions to inventory, plus beer on hand: The sum of Lines: 1 - 12

Removals from Beer Inventory
​
​

Line 14 - Removed for consumption or sale: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice
​
​

Line 15 - Removed tax-determined for consumption or sale to tavern on brewery premises: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Tavern on Brewery Premises

-And Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through a negative PurchaseTrans using Vendors with TTBTaxCode: Tavern on Brewery Premises
​

Line 16 - Removed without payment of tax for export: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Export
​

Line 17 - Removed without payment of tax for use as supplies (vessels/aircraft): Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Used as Supplies
​

Line 18 - Removed without payment of tax for use in research and development: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Research and Development
​

Line 19 - Removed without payment of tax to other breweries and pilot brewing plants of same ownership: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Removed Without Payment of Tax to Other Brewery
​

Line 20 - Removed without payment of tax as beer unfit for sale removed for use in manufacturing: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Unfit for Sale
​
​

Line 21 - Beer consumed on premises: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Consumed on Premise
​

Line 22 - Beer transferred for racking: Same as Line 9 Column D
​

Line 23 - Beer transferred for bottling: Same as Line 10 Column F
​

Line 24 - Beer returned to cellars: This is for beer that was previously sent to a dedicated kegging or bottling area and returned to the facility. This line is not currently calculated
​

Line 25 - Beer racked: Same as Line 9 Column D
​
​

Line 26 - Beer bottled: Same as Line 10 Column F
​

Line 27 - Laboratory samples: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Laboratory Samples
​
​

Line 28 - Beer destroyed at brewery: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Destroyed
​

Line 29 - Beer transferred to a distilled spirits plant: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Transfer to Distillery
​

Line 30 - Losses, including theft: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Loss
​
​

Line 31 - Physical inventory disclosed a shortage: Sum of Product with Brands.TTB Category: Beer and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled written into inventory on an Inventory Adjustment type Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Overage or Shortage
​

Line 33 - Total amount of beer on hand at the end of this period: Sum of Inventory on given end date of all Brands.TTB Category: Beer and Products with Product Type.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled
​

  • Calculated = Amount needed to balance Lines 13 and 34 given the report inputs.

  • Expected = Amount based on actual ending inventory in the system. A difference between expected and calculated is indicative of overriding report values without fixing the root transactions, configuration issues with brands or customers resulting in missing removals/additions or error transactions.

Line 34 - Total Beer: The Sum of Lines 14 - 33


Part 2 - Cereal Beverage Summary

Line 1 - Produced: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced brought into inventory through a Production
​
​

Line 2 - Removed: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice
​

Line 3 - Received: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled brought into inventory on a Purchase with positive NumUnits using

Vendors with TTBTaxCode: Received in Bond
​
​

Line 4 - Loss and Wastage: Sum of Products with Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and ProductType.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled removed from inventory through an Invoice using Customer with TTBTaxCode: Loss
​

Line 6 - Total on hand at end of period: Sum of Inventory on given end date of all Brands.TTB Category: Cereal Beverage - Below .5% ABV and Products with Product Type.TTBProcessType: Produced, Canned, Racked, or Bottled

Steps

Screenshot

How to add Employee Commissions and Commission Groups
​

  1. Navigate to the Commission Groups table using the Universal Search.
    ​

  2. Click the Add Commission Groups button.
    ​
    ​

  3. Enter the name of the Commission Group and click Add Record.
    ​
    ​

  4. Navigate to the Products table using the Universal Search.
    ​
    ​

  5. Apply filters to locate a product to be added to the Commission Group and click the Arrow icon to view the Product record.
    ​
    ​

  6. Locate the Commission Group field and click the Edit icon.
    ​
    ​

  7. Select a Commission Group from the list provided.
    ​
    ​

  8. Click the Save icon.
    ​
    ​

  9. Navigate to the Employee Commissions table using Universal Search.
    ​
    ​

  10. Click the Add Employee Commissions button.
    ​
    ​

  11. Enter values to all required fields displayed in the 'New Employee Commissions' form and click the ‘Add Record’ button when complete
    ​
    - Commission Role: Allows for choice of how the user receives credit for a sale. If they are assigned to that route or the actual salesperson.
    ​
    - Calculation Method: Measurement of what is considered a sale, then multiplied by the rate.
    ​
    - Rate: Decimal value multiplied by the calculation method to determine dollar value commission.

Fields And Definitions

  • Commission Groups- Organization/grouping of commissioned products.
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • Commission Role- Determines what sales the user will receive credit for; their actual sales or sales for customers they are assigned to. Picklist options include:
    ​
    - Salesman Assigned: The assigned salesman on the customer record
    ​
    - Salesman Actual: The salesman who entered the invoice
    ​
    - Deliveryman Assigned: The assigned deliveryman on the customer's route
    ​
    - Deliveryman Actual: The deliveryman who actually completed the delivery
    ​
    - Managers (1-4): Manager assigned to a user on the user record. See Managers Help Resource for information on custom manager roles.

  • Calculation Method- Measurement of what is considered a sale (Units, Case Equiv, $Vol-Deposit or Gross).
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • Rate- Decimal value multiplied by the calculation method to determine the commission payout.
    Example-> 50 units sold * rate of .50 = $25.00 payout

Best Practices

  • Products assigned to a Commission Group should be of similar products types (liquor, kegs, beer, etc.) as they will be all commissioned at the same rate.
    ​
    ​

  • Rates are determined at the user level meaning that each user could have a different Rate for the same Commission Group
    ​
    ​

  • Once Commission Groups and Employee Commissions records are created, reporting tools are utilized to track commissions. Comparison Sales Reports have predefined fields for commissions. Any additional customizations to the Sales Comparison Report requires converting to a Fusion Report. See Sales Comparison Report and Converting to Fusion help resources for more information.

16991416:
Distributor steps for installing the Automated Vendor Remittances app in Encompass to email remittance advice to vendors after balanced check runs, and resending failed emails. Needs Encompass AP and v22.12+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.12

Pre-Conditions

The Guide assumes you have the following set up in your system:

1. Users with email addresses where the remittance advice will be sent.

2. Check Run functionality (Encompass AP must be enabled for your Company).

Steps

How to Install the Automated Vendor Remittances Application

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the App Library dashboard.

2. Search for 'Automated Vendor Remittances'.

3. Select the Automated Vendor Remittances app icon.

4. Click Install.

5. Select Roles that will be able to access the related Dashboard and Roles that will be able to access the related Reports. These can be modified after installation.

6. In the Schedules section, click the edit pencil.

7. First select the Frequency at which automated remittance advice emails will send. Then select a Start Time and End Time between which the emails will send, as well as a Next Run Time. The recommended setup is as follows:

  • Frequency: Daily

  • Leave 'Repeat Every Minutes' blank

  • Start Time: Early Morning (5:00AM)

  • End Time: Early Morning (7:00AM)

  • Next Run Time: Date and Time of first email batch

*This setup would send one batch of remittance emails every morning, delivered to inboxes just after 5:00AM. The purpose of setting an End Time is just to ensure the emails send within the specified timeframe in case your site is managing mutliple scheduled tasks at that time.

8. Click Set Schedule.

9. Decide on elements that the email body will include.

  • Contact Email

  • Signature Email

  • Signature Name

  • Phone Number to Contact

*To see each of these elements in an example outbound remittance email, view Release Notes.

10. Read the acknowledgement and Install the App.

11. You will then see the App within the My Apps section of the App Library.

12. To amend the scheduled project, click the edit pencil in the Schedules section and Create a New Schedule. To amend the elements of the email body, type new values into the text field.

13. If you make any changes, be sure to Save Settings.

14. If you would like to uninstall the App, click Uninstall.
​
​
​

How to Use the Automated Vendor Remittances Application

1. Select Automated Vendor Remittances in the My Apps section of the App Library.

2. Under Dashboards, click the link to open the Automated Vendor Remittance Emails dashboard.

3. By installing the App and setting your Schedule, the system will begin to generate automated emails based on the established frequency. The purposed of the Automated Vendor Remittance Emails dashboard is to manage AP Accounts Users and to monitor automated messages.

4. An AP Account User is the simply the marriage of an AP Account and a User. By entering an Email for a User and tying it to an AP Account, you are telling the system where to deliver remittance advice for that account. You can add new AP Accounts Users from the table view in the dashboard, and you can have multiple AP Accounts Users for one account.

5. The Monitor Remittance Advice Email Status report will allow you to check the status of automatically generated messages. If you need to check on the status of an Email, click Create Report after adding relevant filters.

6. The View Email link in the report will open up the Message record in Encompass. To resend an Email, set the Status of the Message to 'Queued' or copy and paste the Email Body and send it to your Vendor.

7. The Preview Remittance Advice Emails report allows you to preview remittances based on Check Runs you have Balanced that day. It is worth noting that messages will be built for Balanced Check Runs dated within 7 days. Messages will not be duplicated, nor will they be built for Check Runs with an Amount of $0.00 or less. Correction checks will prompt automated messages.

8. If Preview Remittance Advice Emails is missing data, make sure AP Accounts Users are properly set up and that you have waited for the Data Warehouse to return updated information.

Fields And Definitions

Remittance Advice - A form of notification sent to a Supplier informing them that their Invoice has been paid.

AP Account User - A record within Encompass that ties a User and their Email to a specified AP Account. Each AP Account is tied to a Vendor.

Check Run - A way of aggregating Invoices (or Purchases) in Encompass that have been paid or are going to be paid. Upon Balancing a Check Run, a Payment Purchase, or Check, is created for each AP Account included on the Check Run.

Best Practices

1. Always Balance Check Runs well before your scheduled send time if emails need to be sent that day.

2. Check for typos in AP Accounts Users' emails. Invalid email addresses will result in failed messages.

3. Communicate with your Vendors to ensure they have whitelisted the email address you are sending from. This will either be [email protected], or an address you have authorized in Amazon SES. If Vendors have security in place to block an unknown email address or place messages in a spam folder, they might not see the remittance advice.

4. Monitor the Status of automated emails through the Vendor Remittance Advice Emails dashboard. The Monitor Remittance Advice Email Status report allows you to search for messages in a selected timeframe and see the status of a message. If you need to resend an Email, set the status of the message to 'Queued' in the Messages table.

5. Keep in mind that if you Balance a Correction Check Run, remittance advice emails will still send. Vendors will be notified of these corrections, so make them aware if there are any emails they might not expect to receive. Vendors will not receive notifications of Reversed Check Runs or Check Runs with a total of $0.00 or less.

6. To prevent an email from being sent, first use the Preview Vendor Remittance Advice Emails report to find the Payment Purchase ID link for the prepared email. Click the link to go to the Payment Purchase, and set the EDIStatus field to 'All'.

Reopen upstream Production Stages to correct Production Component batch assignments

Distributor reference for pre-order auto-fill: how the Auto Fill Pre Order Invoices task adds pre-order products to invoices via Allocations.AutoShip, on-floor inventory, Customer History and Setting 201. Requires v22.11+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.11

Pre-Conditions

Must meet all conditions:

  1. Allocations.AutoShip field for the specific product/customer allocation must be set to Auto Ship (or equivalent internal value of 1).

  2. Inventories.OnFloorInventory for the product must be greater than 0 (available inventory exists).

  3. Customer History record for the specific product and customer must exist in the system.

  4. Product's Inventories.StatusEffective must be PreOrder or Active.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Scheduled Task (Auto Fill Pre Order Invoices) Logic includes:
​
​

  • Creating a Purchase Order with Pre-Order Products through the PO Generator sets the Auto-Ship field to True by default.
    ​
    ​NOTE: The Auto-Ship field is set on the Allocations table but is not included in the default view. See the Add/Remove Columns in Table View for a guide.
    ​
    ​

  • If Auto-Ship is set to False the Pre-Order Products are prevented from automatically being added to the existing invoice after the purchase is in the received status.
    ​
    ​

  • If Auto-Ship is set to True, the 'Auto Fill Pre Order Invoices' Scheduled Task adds the product(s) to the customer's next delivery invoice.
    ​
    ​

  • Once the Purchase Order with the pre-order products is in the received status, the product(s) are automatically added to the customer's next delivery invoice via the 'Auto Fill Pre Order Invoices' Scheduled Task when Auto-Ship is set to True.
    ​
    ​

  • The Scheduled Task, 'Auto Fill Pre Order Invoices' is run every 3 hours from 8 AM to 5 PM.

Allocations with Pre-Order Products
​
​

  • When the status of a Product changes from Active to Pre-Order, a zero Allocation (Limited Purchase Quantity and Reserve Inventory) is created. This only occurs when Setting 201 is set to True and is required for the Pre-Order workflow to add products to invoices as expected.
    ​
    ​

  • Once a Pre-Order Product is ordered on an Invoice, a Backorder is set on the Customer History record for that Product and Customer. When the Purchase Order of the Pre-Order Products is generated from the PO Generator, the Backorder is set back to 0 on the Customer History record.
    ​
    ​

  • Creating a Purchase Order with Pre-Order Products through the PO Generator automatically creates an Allocation (Limited Purchase Quantity and Reserve Inventory) with the Customer, and # of Units Allocated. The Start Date on the Allocations table matches the Receive Date of the Purchase Order.
    ​
    ​

  • Once Products are delivered to the Customer, the Units Allocated, Units Ordered, Units Sold, and Units Remaining fields are updated accordingly on the Allocation record

New Setup Process for Pre-Orders
​
​

If you have not used pre-orders before, and are looking to get setup, please follow the process on the Pre-Order Setup Dashboard

Creating Pre-Order Allocations

  • Standard Pre-Order: Allocations created via the Pre-Order (PO) Generator inherently tie the allocation to a purchase transaction (Purchase Trans ID), which reliably creates the necessary backorder and subsequent Customer History record. This method is the most reliable for auto-ship.

  • Import Routine: Allocations created via an Import Routine must be verified to ensure the routine explicitly sets the Allocations.AutoShip field to 'Auto Ship.' Imports may not automatically create the required Purchase Trans or Customer History.

Fields And Definitions

  • Allocation Type: Limit Purchase Quantity and Reserve Inventory - Allocation quantity will establish an upper limit of how many of the products the customer can purchase as well as reserve that same quantity for exclusive use by that customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Setting 201 - This is a system setting that can be marked as True or False. If set to true, it will require Allocations for Pre-Order Products to create an automatic zero Allocation.

  • Allocation: A designated quantity of product reserved for a specific customer or group of customers.

  • Allocations.AutoShip (Auto Ship): A setting on an allocation record that, when active, tells the system to automatically add the allocated quantity to a customer's invoice when the required conditions (inventory, history) are met.

  • Customer History: A system record that tracks a customer's prior sales/purchases for a specific product. This record is a key dependency for the auto-fill logic.

  • Inventories.OnFloorInventory: The current, available quantity of a product in stock.

  • API Commands - 14028 Auto_Fill_PreOrder_Invoices: A scheduled command or task responsible for processing allocations with AutoShip = 1 and applying them to pending invoices, provided all other criteria (Customer History, inventory) are satisfied. This function name can be misleading as it affects products with StatusEffective = Active as well as PreOrder.

  • Pre-Order (PO) Generator: The standard system tool/process for creating allocations tied to a formal pre-order process, typically resulting in a Purchase Trans ID.

Best Practices

  • To follow the Pre-Order workflow and to not change Auto-Ship to False
    ​
    ​

  • Create the purchase through the PO Generator tool. This automatically creates the Allocations needed for your customers.

Use Case for Auto-Ship set to False
​
​

  • Use Case: A customer orders 50 cases of a Pre-Order product. The distributor agrees to store the 50 cases and only deliver partial quantities of the order at the customer's request.
    ​
    ​

  • Users can set the Auto-Ship field on the Allocation to False to prevent the Units Remaining on the Allocation from automatically getting added when the 'Auto Fill Pre Order Invoices' scheduled task executes.
    ​
    ​

  • If Auto-Ship = False, Pre-Order Products must be manually invoiced.

Distributor reference for period filters on Encompass Comparison and Fusion reports, explaining each rolling date range (Year to Date, Last 4 Weeks, Month to Selling Day, etc.). Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Overview:

Period filters on Comparison and Fusion reports are dynamically updating date ranges.
These allow you to setup a report once, and not have to change the date range filter each day it is run.

For example: If the Period filter is set to 'Today', and it is run on January 1st, the report will filter to January 1st only.

If that same report is executed on January 2nd, it will automatically filter to data from January 2nd

The period options always run in context of the Close Day selected on the report, unless explicitly stated otherwise below.

Year to Date: Janurary 1st of this year to the current Close Day selected

Year to Day of Year: Comparing multiple years to the same 'day number'

- Example: used to compare 365 days of 2 different years, even though one of those was a leap year (had 366 days)

Year to Selling Day: Comparing multiple years using an equal number of selling days, because both years may or may not have started on the same week day

This Year Complete Months: Janurary 1st of this year to end of the last complete month

This Year Complete Weeks: Janurary 1st of this year to end of the last complete week

Last Year: The entire year, last year

This Year: The entire year, this year

Next Year: The entire year, next year

Today: A single day, always matching the current date

Tomorrow: A single day, always matching the current date + 1 day

Yesterday: A single day, always matching the current date - 1 day

Close Date: A single day, matching the close day selected

Last 30 Days: 30 day date range, based on close day selected - 30 days

Last 60 Days: 60 day date range, based on close day selected - 60 days

Last 90 Days: 90 day date range, based on close day selected - 90 days

This Week: Current week, based on close day selected

Week to Date: Current week up to the day of the week selected in the Close Day

Next Week: All of next week, based on close day selected

Last Week: All of last week, based on close day selected

Last 2 Weeks: Last 2 weeks, based on close day selected

Last 4 Weeks: Last 4 weeks, based on close day selected

Last 8 Weeks: Last 8 weeks, based on close day selected

Last 13 Weeks: Last 13 weeks, based on close day selected

Last 26 Weeks: Last 26 weeks, based on close day selected

Last 52 Weeks: Last 52 weeks, based on close day selected

This Month: This month, beginning to end, based on close day selected

Month to Date: This month up to the current day number, based on close day selected

Month to Selling Day: This month selling days only. Selling days might be different in previous years when comparing years

Last Month: Last month, beginning to end, based on close day selected

Next Month: Next month, beginning to end, based on close day selected

Last Complete 3 Months: Last complete 3 months, based on close day selected

Last Complete 6 Months: Last complete 6 months, based on close day selected

Last Complete 9 Months: Last complete 9 months, based on close day selected

Last Complete 12 Months: Last complete 12 months, based on close day selected

Last Complete 24 Months: Last complete 24 months, based on close day selected

Last Complete 4 Quarters: Last complete 4 quarters, based on close day selected

Rolling 12 Months: A 365 day date range, based on the close day selected and - 365 days

Rolling 7 Days: A 7 day date range, based on the close day selected and - 7 days

Rolling 14 Days: A 14 day date range, based on the close day selected and - 14 days

Last Year This Month: This month - 1 year, beginning to end, based on close day selected

Last Year Next Month: Next month - 1 year, beginning to end, based on close day selected

Last Year Last Month: Last month - 1 year, beginning to end, based on close day selected

This Quarter: This quarter, beginning to end, based on close day selected

Quarter to Date: This quarter up to the current day number, based on close day selected

Last Quarter: Last quarter, beginning to end, based on close day selected

This Trimester: This trimester, beginning to end, based on close day selected

Trimester to Date: This trimester up to the current day number, based on close day selected

Last Trimester: This trimester, beginning to end, based on close day selected

    ​
    - Product Edit - to create Package and Products
    ​
    - General Accounting Management - to create Expense Account Maps
    ​
    - Purchase Cost Edit - to create Product Cost Plans
    ​
    *All required Permissions are included in the 'Full Access' role. These users do not need to add additional permissions to complete Overhead Allocation set up.

Steps

How to Set Up Manufacturing Overhead Allocations

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Product Types table
    ​
    ​

  2. Click Add Product Types to create a new Non Inventory Product Type
    ​
    ​

  3. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed the ‘New Product Types’ form and click the ‘Add Record’ button when complete

  6. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed the ‘New Products’ form and click the ‘Add Record’ button when complete
    ​
    Field values:
    ​
    - Product Name - Enter a unique name for the Overhead product. If multiple Products will be created for these, consider appending the Product Name with the Type of Overhead.
    ​Example: Overhead - Labor, Overhead - Facilities
    ​
    - Package - set to 'Misc'
    ​
    - Product Type - set to 'Overhead Allocation Setting'
    ​
    - Brand - set to 'Misc'
    ​
    ​

  7. Repeat Steps 5 & 6 as needed until all Overhead Products are created
    ​
    ​

  8. Using Universal Search, navigate to the 'Expense Account Maps' table
    ​
    ​

  9. Click the Add Expense Maps button
    ​
    ​

  10. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed the ‘New Expense Account Maps’ form and click the ‘Add Record’ button when complete
    ​NOTE: If multiple Overhead Products were created, an Expense Account Map is required for each Overhead Product. If only one Overhead Product was created, create one Expense Account Map against the Overhead Allocation Setting Product Type.

    ​
    - Case FOB - set to the Allocation Rate per Unit --> Be sure the UOM (Unit of Measure) when determining the allocation rate is the same as the UOM for each production stage you plan to allocate the product too. (Ex: Barrels, Cases, etc.)

Best Practices

  • Most common account type mapped is a Contra - Cost of Goods Sold account. If an account like this does not exist, create one on the Accounts table.
    ​
    ​

  • Refresh your allocation rates annually, at a minimum. Use the Expiration Date field to schedule the change in Allocation Rates as desired.

Additional workflow options:

1. Add a final 'Overhead' stage at the end of the Recipe, and add the non-inventory Overhead product as a RecipeComponent.

  • Use this if the amount of overhead is static by Recipe. Meaning, it will always be added and typically the same amount for every PdO using that Recipe. This would mean the overhead is pre-defined and known prior to PdO completion.
    ​
    ​

  • This means you have to add overhead prior to the inventory from the PdO becomes available.

2. Manually add a Production Component in the final Stage prior to completing the PdO.

  • Use this if the amount of overhead is not static. Meaning, it varies based on real-life activity on that actual PdO. This would mean the overhead is not pre-defined, but is manually calculated prior to PdO completion.
    ​
    ​

  • This means you have to add overhead prior to the inventory from the PdO becomes available.
    ​
    ​

3. Manually add a Production Component in the final Stage AFTER completing the PdO.

  • Use this if the amount of overhead is not static. Meaning, it varies based on real-life activity on that actual PdO.
    ​
    ​

  • This would mean the overhead is not pre-defined, but is manually calculated AFTER the completion of the PdO. This would be used if the PdO is being completed on the handheld, and then someone in the front office goes through and adds overhead to all PdOs at one time.
    ​
    ​

  • This means the inventory from the PdO becomes available (at a lower cost) prior to the overhead being added. This will result in a FIFO adjustment if the inventory is consumed or sold prior to adding the overhead.

Steps

How to Install Auto Print Services


Auto Print Service Pre-Install Steps:
​
1. Ensure you are signed in to the computer as an administrator.
​
2. Confirm your printer driver is installed on the same computer you are installing the APS.
​
3. Connect the printer to the network.
​
4. Verify there is a connection between the computer and the printer by completing a Windows test print outside of Encompass.
​
5. Confirm the machine is running Windows 8 or higher (recommended Windows 10) and .Net Framework 4.8. (See How to Check Your Computer's .NET Framework)
​
6. Ensure the 8083 port is not blocked by any antivirus software or firewalls on the computer or virtual machine: Whitelist your Encompass URL/Domain in the firewall/antivirus setup.

How to Install APS:
​
1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the ‘Client Versions’ table.
​
2. Click the ‘Client Application’ column header.
​
3. Search ‘Auto Print Services for PC’ then click Go.
​
​4. Locate the highest available APS version and click the ‘Download’ link.
​
5. Once downloaded, open the Encompass APS Installation .exe file on the desktop.
​
6. Click Next then Install.
​
​7. Click Finish.
​
​8. Fill in the fields on the Connections tab:
a. Encompass ID - Encompass ID can be found in the bottom left corner of the Encompass site and is case-sensitive.
b. Select Location.
c. Check the box for Secure Connection.
​
​

9. Click Save.

Adding a Printer to APS:
​
1. Locate the Windows Task Tray in the bottom right corner of the desktop.
​
2. APS is represented by an icon of a small printer with a green tube, right-click the icon.
​
3. Select Add a Printer.
​
4. Select the printer name that you would like to add (repeat to add additional printers).

Printer Fields and Test Printing from Encompass:
​
​1. In Encompass, search for Auto Print Services using the Universal Search bar.
​
2. Locate the APS that was installed.
​
3. Click Sub Tables and select 'Printers'.
​
​4. Here, the printer settings can be edited for what will print from Encompass to the printer:
​
​

  • Pick Pallet Tags: Pallet labels for retail delivery.
    ​
    ​

  • Receiving Pallet tags: Pallet labels for date tracking.
    ​
    ​

  • Warehouse Reports: Load Sheet Manifests, Invoices, etc.
    ​
    ​

  • Print Receiving Case Tag: Individual labels for special cases and kegs.
    ​
    ​

  • Print Asset Tag: Labels for assets such as coolers or neon signs.
    ​
    ​

  • Print Retailer Label Tag: Shelf labels for retail placements.

How to Uninstall APS
​
1. Navigate to the Windows Control Panel.
​
2. Select Add/Remove Programs.
​
3. Locate ‘Encompass Auto Print Service’.
​
4. Select Uninstall Program.
​
5. Restart Computer.

Troubleshooting:
​
Do not begin troubleshooting APS without first confirming a Windows test print; APS will not work if the connection between printer and computer is not established.

How to Restart Auto Print Service:
​
1. Open Auto Print Services in the Windows Task Bar in the bottom right corner of the screen (you may need to click on the carrot or ‘^’ to expand the tray).
​
2. Right-click on the APS icon (printer with green tube).
​
3. Select Restart or Start.

How to Restart Print Spooler
​
​1. From Windows search 'Services'.
​
2. Click on the Services option.
​
3. Search for “Print Spooler”.
​
4. Right-click on the Print Spooler, where the options to Stop/Start/Restart will be displayed.
​
5. Select Restart.

Restart the Computer
​
1. Ensure the user has sufficient permissions to log back into the computer.
​
2. From the desktop, open the Start menu.
​
3. Click on the power icon.
​
4. Select the option to Restart the computer.

Check the Printer IP address and update, if needed
​
​1. Log into your PC as an administrator. Depending on your computer's security settings, this may not be necessary.
​
2. From the Start Menu, select Settings->Printers.
​
3. Right-click on the printer and select Properties from the pull-down menu.
​
4. Select Ports, then Configure (This button will be grayed out if you're not the administrator.)
​
5. In the type-in labeled ‘Printer Name or IP address’, you'll see the old IP address. You need to edit it to reflect the new one.
​
6. Then click ‘OK’, and close the Properties menu. Try printing something. If it doesn't come out, double-check the new IP address.

Check Print Permissions on the C Drive
​
​1. From the Files folder of the desktop, open the C drive.
​
2. Search for Program Files (x86).
​
3. Right-click on Encompass Technologies.
​
4. Select Properties.
​
5. Click Security.
​
6. Click edit/add: permission needs to be Everyone (type in 'every' in the dialogue box, then use the check names button to pull up the Everyone permission).
​
7. Select Full on the next screen.
​
8. Apply changes.

How to Upgrade APS

To ensure optimal performance, confirm you're using the newest version of APS. If you're experiencing persistent issues, upgrading is recommended.
​
​

1. To update, simply right-click the APS icon in your task tray (lower right corner of the screen) and select "Upgrade."
​
​

2. If this option isn't available, you'll need to manually uninstall the current version:
​

  1. Navigate to the Windows Control Panel.
    ​
    ​

  2. Select Add/Remove Programs.
    ​
    ​

  3. Locate ‘Encompass Auto Print Service’.
    ​
    ​

  4. Select Uninstall Program.
    ​
    ​

  5. Restart Computer.
    ​
    ​

3. Download the newest one from the Client Versions table

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the ‘Client Versions’ table.
    ​
    ​

  2. Click the ‘Client Application’ column header.
    ​
    ​

  3. Search ‘Auto Print Services for PC’ then click Go.
    ​
    ​

  4. Locate the highest available APS version and click the ‘Download’ link.
    ​
    ​

  5. Once downloaded, open the Encompass APS Installation .exe file on the desktop.
    ​
    ​

  6. Click Next then Install.
    ​
    ​

  7. Click Finish.
    ​
    ​

  8. Fill in the fields on the Connections tab
    ​
    a. Encompass ID - Encompass ID can be found in the bottom left corner of the Encompass site and is case-sensitive.
    ​
    b. Select Location.
    ​
    c. Check the box for Secure Connection.
    ​
    ​

  9. Click Save.

See Also:

  • Connecting a Printer Wirelessly Using Zebra Setup Utility
    ​
    ​

  • Zebra Setup Utilities

Fields And Definitions

  • APS - Auto Print Service
    ​
    ​

  • Encompass ID - Encompass ID can be found in the lower left corner of the Encompass site and is case-sensitive
    ​
    ​

  • Auto Print Services - Active field: This field indicates if there is an active connection to the APS client. If the connection to the client is lost, this value will change to False. You can alert on this value to notify local IT staff if an APS client becomes unreachable.

Best Practices

Best Practices
​
​

  • Log in to the computer as an administrator
    ​
    ​

  • Make sure you have the correct User Permissions to change the APS settings
    ​
    ​

  • If Print Jobs are stuck in the “New” status, try restarting APS first, then try an APS upgrade if the issue persists
    ​
    ​

  • If Print Jobs are stuck in the “Printing” status, check the desktop Printer Queue for stuck print jobs first, then restart the computer/printer if the issue persists
    ​
    ​

  • To ensure optimal performance, confirm you're using the newest version of APS. If you're experiencing persistent issues, upgrading is recommended. To update, simply right-click the APS icon in your task tray (lower right corner of the screen) and select "Upgrade." If this option isn't available, you'll need to manually uninstall the current version and then download the newest one from the Client Versions table.

Security Information
​
​

  • While administrator permission is not necessary for processing the print jobs, automatic program management for APS needs admin permission to maintain APS properly. Admin-required actions are related to managing program files, and include remote stop, uninstall, and upgrade controls.

  • Admin permission can be removed from APS, but Encompass's recommendation is to maintain elevated permissions for the best experience. Windows system restrictions require APS to have elevated permissions for the program to perform all functions:
    ​
    ​

  1. APS Print Service: This is the main function of APS, processing print jobs from the Encompass site. Does not need admin permissions to work properly.
    ​
    ​

  2. APS Management: Provides the configuration form for connection to an EncompassID and selection of a Location. Installs and runs the service automatically.*
    ​
    ​

  3. APS Upgrade: Needs to stop and uninstall the service to upgrade APS.*
    ​
    ​

  4. APS Uninstall: Needs to stop and uninstall the service, along with removing all the APS client files.*

All functions marked with * will not work without Administrator permissions.

User Received an 'Invalid Username/Email or password' Notification

  1. If the user entered the correct username but an incorrect password, a failed login attempt will be recorded on their record in the Users Table in the Logon Failure Count field

​

  1. When the maximum number of login attempts on either server is reached, the account will be locked out. This will require the user to reset their password in order to log in to Encompass

  • Mobile app/desktop login = 10 attempts

User received a 'User is not allowed to login' Notification
​

  1. The EveryonePermission has to be granted on the role or user permissions in order to log in, contact a manager or admin from your company to add these permissions, if needed

How to Use Custom Fields

    ​

6. Once the settings have been adjusted, input the table name and select Save Changes to apply the columns and settings

Distributor explanation of FIFO adjustments in Encompass: why the nightly FIFO routine creates adjustment invoices to COGS and inventory when product costs change. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

FIFO Adjustment Logic:
​
​

  • ScheduledTasks Recalculate Inventory FIFO Layers will auto run every day.
    ​
    ​

  • FIFO Adj = Sum(PurchaseTrans.OnHand*PurchaseTrans.LaidInCost) - Inventories.InventoryValue - Inventories.InventoryReceivedValue.
    ​

  • When this FIFO Adj is more than 0.01, the FIFO Adj Invoice will be created.

Steps

What are FIFO Adjustments?
​
​

  • Fifo Adjustments are a way for Encompass to ensure the accuracy of Cost of Goods within the system when changes to product costing occur.

How are they created?
​
​

  • These adjustments are created using a special customer called the FIFO adjustment customer. This customer never accrues AR, and its invoices always have a net 0 impact on inventory. The journal entry for these invoices adjusts the value of your Inventory Asset Account and Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) account to correct for updates in product cost. These invoices are created by a routine that runs nightly to update FIFO layers in Encompass.

Why are they created?
​
​There are four separate situations where a FIFO adjustment is created:
​
​

  1. A purchase is received at one price and confirmed at another. In the meantime, product from that purchase has been sold. This is the most common situation for FIFO adjustments. If a product was received at a cost of $25.00 and we sold 10 cases of that product before confirming the purchase with a cost of $30.00 (The vendor raised the price, freight costs changed, etc.) we will have a $50 adjustment to cost of goods sold because we sold those ten cases out at a cost that was $5 less than it should have been.
    ​
    ​

  2. Product is sold with two different costs on the same day. This is another common cause of FIFO adjustments. Encompass will only sell product from one FIFO layer per day. This doesn’t always work in the real world. If we have a situation where we sell 20 cases of the same product in a day, but 10 of those cases came in on a purchase for $25 each and the other 10 cases came in on a purchase for $30 each, we will sell all 20 cases at the cost of the current FIFO layer ($25) and create the $50 adjustment to COGS and Inventory for the 10 cases that actually came in at $30 when the nightly FIFO routine runs.
    ​
    ​

  3. A purchase was returned or transferred at a different cost than it was purchased for. This is very similar to the first situation, if we purchased 10 cases of a product at $25 and then sent it back to the vendor at a cost of $20.00, a $50 FIFO adjustment will be created to correct our Cost of Goods and Asset Account and make up for the difference in the cost.
    ​
    ​

  4. A product type is changed to Track Inventory = False. If we decide to stop tracking inventory on a certain product type (this sometimes occurs with promotional products), we will adjust the entire value of those products out of Inventory and Cost of Goods Sold.

Steps

How to use PO Generator

1. Using the universal search (Search for anything) at the top of the page, enter PO Generator

2. Apply Filters to generate POs for select Period Types, Periods, Product Status (for Pre-Order workflow), Customers (for Pre-Order workflow), or Forecast Groups.

3. Select a Forecast Group to view Product details within that group

4. Tools in the PO Generator include:

Minus icon

Round the quantity on the PO down, based on the carrying capacity of the carrier

Plus icon

Round the quantity on the PO up to the carrying capacity of the carrier (Pallets or Weight, whichever is capped first)

Set to Min

Reduce the quantity to the min pallets or weight

Set to Max

Increase the quantity on the PO to the max pallets or weight

Zero Out Period

Move selected Orders to the following period

Create POs

Convert the estimated order quantities for each product to actual purchase records

Knowledge

Access the latest Knowledge Documents on the PO Generator tool

Display:

Change the display to show Pallet, Case, and Barrels

When adjusting quantities using the +/- or Set to Min/Max buttons, the system will reduce or increase quantaties based on the product ranking code and DOI DIff amounts.

  • The ranking code priorities are AA, AB, BA, AC, BB, CA, AD, BC, CB, DA, BD, CC, DB, CD, DC, AND DD.

  • DOI Diff = DOI After Order - Target DOI

Increasing Quantities Prioritization:

  • Max DOI thresholds will still be respected, so products quantaties may not be increase if that would cause a product to go over the Max DOI.

  • Look at all products with DOI Diff < 0 (DOI After Order - Target DOI), sort by product ranking and DOI Diff in acending order.

  • Add a purchase by unit for each product until there are no products with negative DOI diff or until a full truck load is met

  • If still not a full truckload:

  • Look at AA ranked products and sort by DOI Diff, add a purchase by unit for each product until a full truck load is met.

  • Continue this process each ranking code until a full truckload is met.

Decreasing Quantities Prioritization:

  • Prioritize by ranking in reverse priority and DOI Diff in descending order

  • Decrease a purchase by unit for each product until until a full truck load is met.

5. Click the edit icon on the Qty on PO header to manually adjust quantities

6. Receive Location data will default to the same value as the forecast location, unless it is set on the forecast group. TIP: Both the receive location and vendor columns have 'fill down' capabilities.

Steps

Navigating Daily/Monthly Best Practices

1. Using the Universal Search Bar, navigate to the Daily/Monthly Best Practices Dashboard

8. Navigate to the Deposits Table to add or edit Deposits

9. Once you have added or edited Deposits, you are ready to run Accounts Receivable Close

10. Clicking Vendor Purchases to Confirm will direct you to Received Purchases dated on or before the date selected

Fields And Definitions

Invoice Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Invoices through. In other words, Balanced Load Sheets and Invoices dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Accounts Receivable Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Accounts Receivable through. In other words, Balanced Deposits dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Accounts Payable Close Date - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Accounts Payable through. In other words, Confirmed Purchases dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Financial Close - If a Company is specified, this is the date that Company has closed Financials through. In other words, Balanced Journal Entries dated on or before this date have been Verified. If a Company is not specified, this defaults to the most historical Invoice Close date of the Companies in the site.

Best Practices

  • Run Invoice Close, Accounts Receivable Close, and Accounts Payable Close on a daily basis or as frequently as possible.

Steps

How to Move an Invoice on a Loaded Load Sheet

  1. Navigate to the Load Sheets table
    ​
    ​

  2. Click on the Return link for the Load Sheet currently holding the invoices that need to be moved
    ​

  10. On the Re-deliver tab, select a printer and re-print related pallet tags to ensure inventory also moves to the new load sheet

Fields And Definitions

The various move options interact with related inventory differently.

Inventory does not move with invoice:

Move Not-Delivered

  • Can select any status load sheet to move the invoice to

  • Does not bring the loaded inventory with the moved invoice, the product will stay in the original route bin

  • Invoice has to be re-palletized on the new load sheet and re-picked

  • When to use: when moving an Invoice from one load sheet to another, with no intention of moving the related pallets onto another truck

  • What is unique about this option: leaves product in the route bin to be reconciled during truck return

Inventory does move with invoice:

Move Off-Load

  • Can select any load sheets in the Loaded status to move the invoice to; New status load sheets are also available if the route bins match

  • Brings inventory and pallet record with moved invoice, product goes to the new route bin

  • Invoice does not have to be re-palletized or re-picked

  • When to use: when moving an Invoices from one loaded load sheet to another loaded load sheet, or when you don't need to print a new pallet tag or unload the inventory from its destination route bin

  • What is unique about this option: leaves pallets in loaded status, and will not require a new pallet tag

Move Re-deliver

  • Can select any load sheets in the New status to move the invoice to

  • Brings inventory with the invoice, but creates a new pallet record tied to the new load sheet (for more accurate pallet labeling, if needed)

  • Product goes to the new route bin once a new pallet tag is printed from the original load sheet's Route Reconciliation Redeliver tab

  • When to use: When moving an invoice from a loaded load sheet to a new load sheet sharing the same route bin, with intention to re-load related pallets later

  • What is unique about this option: allows a user to move an invoice between two routes that share the same route bin, with better control of when the related inventory is loaded

Best Practices

Based on the impact to inventory that comess with each invoice move option, consider which option best fits common situations for your business. Determine a standard practice for each situation, and communicate it with your team.
16991481:
Distributor reference explaining Correction bin transactions in Encompass (Correction3, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12): why the system adjusts bin inventory and how to avoid them. Requires v22.04+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.04

Steps

What are Correction Bin Transactions?
​
​

Correction Bin Transactions (Bin Trans) are the system’s way of making sure that inventory is staying as accurate as possible across all methods of inventory movement.

The goal is to have Correction bin trans occur as infrequently as possible, as Corrections are usually an indication of misaligned inventory movement. Because there are different situations that could lead to a Correction, there is a different number corresponding to each type of correction that inventory could need. The system is safe-guarded against creating situations where Corrections are needed, but Correction bin trans provide a safety net in the case of unexpected behavior.

Definitions and examples

Correction3
​
​

  • Adjusts bin inventories when Verified Inventory ≠ Bin Inventories.
    ​
    ​

  • These types of corrections occur when the SUM of Bin Inventories, or live inventory, does not equal the SUM of Purchased Inventory minus Verified Sales. Correction3 Bin Transactions ensure that live inventory being reported matches the value of inventory officially owned.

  • The delivered value in the audit pulls from: Inventories.Delivered - Loaded Load Sheets where Invoiced Bin Trans have occurred
    ​
    ​EXAMPLE: Inventory has been “Invoiced” out of the system — Invoiced Bin Trans have been created, but then the invoice is deleted without reciprocating or negative Invoiced Bin Trans getting created to put inventory back into the system. A Correction3 Bin Trans would help put the Inventory back.

Correction8
​
​

  • Moves inventory to a user-interactive Bin when inventory is orphaned in the Staging Bin, which is not a Bin Users can directly interact with in the Warehouse Handheld.
    ​
    ​

  • The Staging Bin is a conceptual Bin used to hold inventory that has been Picked, but is still waiting to be Loaded onto Load Sheets. The only way to add inventory to this bin is by picking, and the only way to remove it is by loading or unconfirming a pick. Because of this, any inventory stuck in the Staging Bin has to be moved by the system via a Correction8 Bin Trans.
    ​
    ​EXAMPLE: A pallet is picked and awaiting loading, but then gets deleted. This would orphan the pallet’s inventory in the Staging Bin, calling for a Correction8 to shift the inventory to a Bin where a User can interact with it manually.

Correction9
​
​

  • For use in Scan Based Trading (SBT), compares the customer's delivered invoices and scanned sales to the inventory in their SBT Customer bin, then adjusts inventory if needed.
    ​
    ​

  • The SBT Customer bin is a conceptual bin used to hold inventory that has been sold to a retailer but has not yet been reported as a sale by the retailer based on scan data. The only way to change inventory quantities in this bin is by delivering an invoice to the retail customer, or by receiving scanned sales depletion data via EDI. Because of this, any inventory errors have to be adjusted by the system via a Correction9 Bin Trans.
    ​
    ​EXAMPLE: An order is delivered to the retail customer, but the related load sheet is left in the loaded status. SBT Customer bin inventory should have been increased during truck return, but since this did not occur, Correction9 increases SBT Customer bin inventory that weekend.

Correction10
​
​

  • Removes Bin Inventories for Non-Inventory Products that get Picked.
    ​
    ​

  • If picking is occurring for a product, there will always be Bin Trans created, and Bin Trans always add or subtract from Bin Inventories. In the case of a Non-Inventory Product that needs to be picked, this would leave a negative Bin Inventory for the Product. Correction10 Bin Trans adjust those unnecessary bin inventories back to 0, since Inventory is not actually being tracked.
    ​
    ​EXAMPLE: Picking sets of disposable coasters or cups. Typically these are items that get added to pallets for delivery, but don’t actually have inventory tracked in the warehouse. Those products would get picked, then have a Correction10 Bin Trans to reset the Inventory back to 0 since that is not being tracked in the system.

Correction11

  • Manufacturing only. Moves inventory to a user-interactive Bin when inventory is orphaned in the Production Queue, which is not a bin users can directly interact with in the Warehouse Handheld.
    ​
    ​

  • The Production Queue bin is a conceptual Bin used to hold inventory that will be used in the production process. Inventory can only be added or removed from this Bin via the Production tools, meaning that anything stuck in the Bin could then only be moved by the system. Correction11 Bin Trans are the record of system moving out of the Production Queue.
    ​
    ​EXAMPLE: A new Production Order is started and Inventory is moved into the Production Queue. The Production Order is then deleted, leaving inventory in the Production Queue with no way to move it. The system would then create a Correction11 to move inventory back to a Bin where users can interact.
    ​

Correction12

  • Directed Replenishment only. Moves inventory to a user-interactive bin when inventory is orphaned in the In-Transit Bin.
    ​
    ​

  • The In-Transit Bin is used during the Directed Replenishment process to indicate when inventory has left its “From Bin,” but has not yet made it to the “To Bin” being replenished. In other words, the In-Transit Bin holds inventory that is moving across the Warehouse floor. Inventory should only go into this Bin by completing the first step of Directed Replenishment, and is only be removed from the Bin by fully completing the Replenishment task. If inventory is left in this Bin, the system will move the inventory via a Correction12.
    ​
    ​EXAMPLE: A warehouse user starts a Directed Replenishment task, and indicates to the system that they have picked a product out of the “From Bin.” If the user were to then back out of the task permanently and stop working, that product would be left in the In-Transit Bin, calling for a Correction12 to move it to a Bin where another Warehouse User can interact with it manually.

Best Practices

● Always make sure that processes such as picking, loading, replenishment, or

production are completed if they are started. If the process can’t be

completed, try to make changes from the same tool the process was started in

to properly undo any inventory movement.

● Avoid deleting load sheets, invoices, pallets, move tasks, or production orders

without first checking on any inventory movement that might have already

occurred.

● If a Correction Bin Trans is found in the system without clear reason as to why it

was created, create a Support task for expert advice

Distributor reference for how Encompass calculates invoice due dates for each Credit Terms Due Date Method (Standard, End of Month, End of Week, and state methods like Missouri or New York). Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

Overview of Due Date Methods on Credit Terms:

Standard:
​
​

• Calculation for Due Date:

• Load Sheet Date + Days of Credit
​
​

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 10/01/2017

Customer -> AR Account -> Terms -> Days of Credit = 15

Invoice Due Date = 10/16/2017


Missouri:
​
​

• Calculation for Due Date:

• The Year, Month, and Day of the Month after the Load Sheet Date

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 12/14/2017

(The next month is 01/14/2018)

Year = 2018

Month = 1

Day = 01

If the Load Sheet Date Day is between the 1st and the 15th

New Due Date Day = 01

If the Load Sheet Date Day is between the 16th and the 31st

New Due Date Day = 16

Invoice Due Date = 01/01/2018


New York:
​
​

• Calculation for Due Date:

• 2011-01-10 plus starting from 2011-01-10 to Load Sheet Date total number of weeks, plus 25 days

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 09/04/2017

Total weeks= 347 weeks

Invoice Due Date = 09/29/2017 ('01/10/2017' + 347 weeks + 25 Days)


Nevada:

• Calculation for Due Date:

• The year for the Load Sheet Date's next month & The Load Sheet Date's next month & '15'

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 01/03/2017

Invoice Due Date = 02/15/2017

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 12/04/2017

Invoice Due Date = 01/15/2018


Utah:

• The day of Load Sheet Date is between 1 AND 15

• Calculation for Due Date:

• The year for the Load Sheet Date & The Load Sheet Date's month & '25'

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 02/04/2017

Invoice Due Date = 02/25/2017

• The day of Load Sheet Date is between 16 AND 31

• Calculation for Due Date:

• The year for the Load Sheet Date next month & The Load Sheet Date next month & '10'

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 12/17/2017

Invoice Due Date = 01/10/2018


Maryland:

• Load Sheet Date and 2012-12-02 of the time difference, starting from 2012-12-02 to Load Sheet Date, mod 14, if the result is greater than 0

• Calculation for Due Date:

• 2012-12-02 plus starting from 2012-12-02 Load to Sheet Date total number of weeks, plus 46 days

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 09/10/2017

Invoice Due Date = 10/19/2017

Load Sheet Date and 2012-12-02 of the time difference, starting from 2012-12-02 to Load Sheet Date, mod 14, if the result is less than 0

• Calculation for Due Date:

• 2012-12-02 plus starting from 2012-12-02 to Load Sheet Date since the beginning of the total number of weeks, Plus 32 days

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 08/06/2017

Invoice Due Date = 09/07/2017


Washington DC:

• Calculation for Due Date:

• The year for the Load Sheet Date 's next month & The Load Sheet Date 's next month & 15th

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 06/06/2017

Invoice Due Date = 07/15/2017


End Of Month (+):

• Calculation for Due Date:

• At Load Sheet Date from 1th this month, add a month and Day of Credit days - 1

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 04/17/2017

Customer -> AR Account -> Terms -> Days of Credit = 31

Invoice Due Date = 05/31/2017


End Of Week (+):

• Calculation for Due Date:

• Subtracting the specified time interval from the Load Sheet Date

• SUBDATE(Load Sheet Date, DATE_FORMAT(Load Sheet Date,'%w')-5)

Example:

Load Sheet -> Load Sheet Date = 03/21/2017

Invoice Due Date = 03/24/2017

Distributor steps for fixing handheld sync errors on the Import Conflicts dashboard in Encompass, such as balanced or returned load sheets, signature locks and cut-off times. Requires v22.11+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.11

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to manage Import Conflicts

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Import Conflicts dashboard
    ​
    ​

  2. Invoices with conflicts are displayed with details such as Date, Invoice Number, Customer, Route, and Error
    ​
    ​NOTE: If there are many conflicted Invoices, you can use filters to narrow down the results then click Filter Results
    ​
    ​
    ​

  3. Review the Error. The Error could be:
    ​
    a. Problem 1: Payment can not be edited, Load Sheet (xxxx) is already Balanced. This means the handheld user is trying to add a payment to an invoice that is already balanced
    ​
    To import this conflict select the load sheet link from Import Conflicts
    Edit Load Sheet Status to Loaded
    Confirm the invoice in question is not locked (unlock invoice)
    Return to Import Conflicts
    Select the check box next to Import conflict and execute ‘Import’
    ​
    b. Problem 2:Locked with Signature. This means the handheld user is trying to make changes to an invoice that has already been locked with a signature. Once a signature is captured, you can no longer make changes to that Invoice. One explanation could be that two users have the invoice on their handheld and one user has already synced the signature on the invoice
    ​
    To import this conflict select the Invoice link from Import Conflicts
    Select Arrow next to the invoice
    If the user has ‘Invoice Unlock’ permission select the ‘Unlock’ button
    Return to Import Conflicts
    Select the Check Box next to Import Conflict and execute ‘Import’
    ​
    c. Problem 3:It's currently after the cut-off time. You can no longer send pre­sell invoices for [date]. This means the handheld user (salesman) is trying to sync in a new sale on an invoice after the route's cut-off time
    ​
    To Import this conflict confirm whether the error displays ‘Can Not Move’ or ‘Move Invoice to A Different Load Sheet’
    To import to the original invoice and load sheet select the check box and execute ‘Import’
    To import to a different load sheet select the checkbox next to the import conflict
    Select ‘Import to Load Sheet…’
    Select the delivery date and load sheet intended for delivery
    ​
    d. Problem 4: Pallets for [Customer] Have Already Been Printed. Printed Pallet List = xxxx. This means the handheld user is trying to make an edit to an invoice that has been processed for picking. You can import this conflict with the proper permission, but you must re-process this invoice to picking
    ​
    To Import conflict locate the route and pallet in the delivery optimizer
    Select plus sign next to route
    Select the checkbox next to the customer
    Palletize
    Select pallets
    Select ‘Mark Not Printed’
    Return to Import Conflicts
    Select the check box next to Import conflict and execute ‘Import’
    Imported invoice transactions will need to be palletized
    ​
    e. Problem 5: Load Sheet (xxxx) is already Returned. This means the handheld user is trying to make changes to an invoice that is on a load sheet that is already returned. You may import this conflict, but it will require the load sheet to be un-returned and then returned by the warehouse again
    ​
    To import this conflict select the Load Sheet link from Import Conflicts
    Edit Load Sheet status
    Confirm the invoice in question is not locked (unlock invoice)
    Return to Import Conflicts
    Select the check box next to Import Conflict and execute ‘Import’
    ​
    f. Problem 6: Mismatch Between Customer Location and Load Sheet Location. Review System Setting 128) Allow Cross Location Invoices on other Locations' Routes. If True, 'Problem 6: Location Mismatch Between Customer Location and Load Sheet Location' import conflicts will not occur. If False, when importing to load sheet, users will now see Load Sheets from the Customers location.
    ​
    System setting 128:Allow Cross Location Invoices on other Location's Routes. Remittance Invoices are omitted from this Setting and should be set to TRUE.
    Go to Delivery Optimizer
    Select the Load sheet where the invoice is located and the load sheet where you want it to be moved
    Click Dynamic routing/Mapped routing
    Drag/select the customer invoice to the other load sheet
    Click Save
    ​
    ​
    ​

  4. Select a view or action option to process the invoice
    ​
    ​
    ​
    ​

  • Import: Update the Invoice if it is already an existing member of a Load Sheet
    ​
    ​

  • Cancel Import: Remove the Invoice Audit from Import Conflicts
    ​
    ​

  • View Invoice Audit: View all Invoice Audit records
    ​
    ​

  • View Canceled: View all canceled Invoice Audits
    ​
    ​

  • Import To Load Sheet: Add the Invoice to a new Load Sheet (provided it is not already a member of a Load Sheet)
    ​
    ​

Best Practices

  • You may need to resolve the underlying problem first before importing (such as unreturning the load sheet if it was returned before the route was completed, etc.)

    ​

  • Not all conflicts should be imported or canceled. They must be managed according to the situation
