Distributor steps for setting up Income Account Maps in Encompass so invoice sales post to the right income, COGS, discount, participation and deposit GL accounts. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Pre-Conditions

  • The following workflow assumes you already have added Accounts to be used in the Accounts table.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

Income Account Maps allow you to specify how different types of sales transactions should be recorded in the general ledger. This includes mapping sales to the appropriate income accounts, cost of goods sold accounts, and other relevant accounts. By setting up these mappings, you can ensure that your financial reporting accurately reflects your sales activity.
​
​
​How to Create an Income Account Map
​
​

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Income Account Maps table.
    ​
    ​

  2. Click the +Add Income Account Map button.
    ​
    ​

  3. Select the Company and Income Area, Income Account, COGS Account, Discount Account, Participation Account, Participation AR Account, Deposit Income Account, and Deposit Cogs Accounts
    ​
    ​

  4. To set up separate mapping for a certain Supplier, Product Type, or Product use the fields for these categories to specify what this map will be used for.
    ​
    ​

  5. Then click Add Record.

Fields And Definitions

  • *Company - the financial entity associated with the mapping
    ​
    ​

  • *Income Area - is the collection of customers whose Income Account Maps are mapped the same way.
    ​
    ​

  • Income Account - This is where the full price for the product is recorded, i.e. total revenue.
    ​
    ​

  • COGS Account - This is where the total laid-in cost for the product is recorded, it is the offset for the inventory transaction
    ​
    NOTE: When tax on sale methods are used, tax due to the State is included
    ​
    ​

  • Discount Account - This is where the discount is recorded. if you only want to see gross revenue in your general ledger, set this field with the same account used for Income Account
    ​
    ​

  • Participation Account - This records the participation/bill back/rebates from promotions given to distributors from suppliers. It records as a negative COGS transaction (to increase the margin). If not used can be set the same as the COGS account.
    ​
    ​

  • Participation AR Account - This records the amount of participation that is due to the distributor and is the offset to the Participation Account.
    ​
    ​

  • Deposit Income Account - This records the amount charged to customers for deposits like kegs or trays.
    ​
    ​

  • Deposit Cogs Account - This records the value of the deposit and reduces the inventory account. It can be a liability account if you wish to record that you, not the supplier, are still responsible for the kegs.

Transaction Source: Invoices
​
​Determining Factors:
​

  • Company
    ​
    ​

  • Income Area (customers)
    ​
    ​

  • Product Type
    ​
    ​

  • Supplier
    ​
    ​

  • Product

Best Practices

Create one default income account map per company & income area as a "catch all" map in case of missing maps by product, supplier or product type. AR Close contains logic to check that default maps exist and will create them if they do not. The user will be prompted to assign the GL Accounts in these maps before AR Close can be restarted.

When creating an Income Account Map, you can only set one of the following qualifiers: Product, Supplier, Supplier & Product Type combination, or Product Type.

Tip: When troubleshooting why an invoice hit a certain Income Account Map, check the Distribution Area associated with the Customer on the Invoice.

16991513:
Producer steps for building recipes in Encompass Recipe Management: add a recipe version and stages with turnable settings and lead times. Requires v25.12+ and Products and Production Stage Types set up first.

Minimum Version Required: 25.12

Pre-Conditions

Products and Production Stage Type tables need to be set up before building out recipes. QC Templates require measurements in the Measurements table in order to leverage these in a Recipe.

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Build Recipes
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Recipe Management dashboard.
​
​ Note: The Recipe Management dashboard can also be access from the Production Cloud Home dashboard.
​
2. Click Add Recipe Version.
​
​This is the collection of steps and ingredients that will be used to schedule Production Orders and Batches.
​
3. Fill out all required fields as well as supporting fields:
​
​ a. Recipe Version - The unique name of the version. It is recommended to use: Brand, volume produced, and Product Type

Example: Chow Chillin 30BBL Brite Beer
​
​ b. Location -The Facility this recipe will be made in.
​
c. Product - The Inventoried Product that will be produced at the end of this Recipe.
​
d. Recipe Type - Distinguishes production recipes from packaging, maintenance, distilling etc.
​
e. Planned Units - The amount of Product planned on producing at the end of this recipe.
​
f. UoM (Unit of Measure) - The unit by which the output goods will be measured
​
4. Click Add Recipe Version.
​
​ There is now an empty recipe with no Recipe Stages, Recipe Components or Instructions.
​
​

Adding Recipe Stages:
​
​1. Click Add Recipe Stages.
​
2. Fill out all required fields:
​
a. Stage Type - The action name for the Components and Instructions
Examples: Boiling, Blending, Mashing, Fermenting, Carbonating, etc
​
b. Output per Turn - Identifies how much each turn will produce.
​
c. Planned Units - The amount planned on producing in this stage. Units are measured based on the UoM selected for the Recipe.
​
d. Turnable - How this Recipe Stage plans for multiple batching
​
i. Turnable = True: When this Recipe is scheduled to be executed twice in a row, this recipe stage will be duplicated, back-to-back.
​
ii. Turnable = False: Only the Components and Planned Units will double, but occur in a single vessel as a single stage.
​
e. Lead Time - Estimated time required to complete the Recipe Stage.
​
​

3. Click Add Recipe Stage.

Fields And Definitions

  • Recipe Versions - Set of Instructions, broken up into Stages to produce a predetermined Product.
    ​
    ​

  • Recipe Stages - A singular workflow for Users to follow. Grouping Instructions and Components by Timing and Sequence allows Users to do everything in the proper order at the proper time.
    ​
    ​

  • Recipe Management Dashboard - the hub for managing Recipes:
    ​
    - Products - includes Raw Material Products, Work in Process Products, and Finished Goods Products
    ​
    - Production Stage Types - A grouping of actions/inputs that comprise a single Recipe Stage in a Recipe. Verbs like Blending, Filtering, Pasteurizing, etc. feature here
    ​
    - QC Measurements - Quality Control Measurements that are taken during any Recipe at any Stage. Measurements are pulled from the QC Measurements Table
    ​
    ​ Note: To automatically add QC Templates into Recipes as they are being built, please refer to the QC Templates Training

Recipe Stages:
​
​

  • Transfer When Complete - Determines the end of this stage.
    ​
    Select True: If this stage ends by transferring to a new piece of equipment
    ​
    Select False: The current stage is completed, but we are not yet ready to move product into the equipment required for the next stage.
    ​
    ​

  • Memo - An overall note for Users during this Recipe Stage. It will appear at the top of the card on Users handhelds.
    ​
    ​

  • Add Instruction - Input direction for Users to see during Handheld processing. This adds line-by-line memos to guide users through processing.
    ​
    ​

  • Timing - This dictates the amount of time into the Recipe Stage that an Instruction or a Component is to be followed or added.
    ​
    Note: Timing also dictates which Components and Instructions show up on the same card when processing on the Handheld
    ​
    ​

  • Sequence -The order in which Components or Instructions with the same Timing are displayed on Users Handhelds.

Best Practices

  • Recipes should be built as if one full batch of the Product is being made. Multiple-Batching can be entered at the time Recipes are scheduled, so one recipe can be used for many different Production volumes.
    ​
    ​

  • Build Recipes to a single run - Use ‘turnable’ on a recipe to double brew into a larger vessel.
    ​Example: If brewing 30bbls for ferment on a 15bbl system, make the brew or the mash/boil turnable at 15bbls each then have the fermentation stage plan for 15bbl
    ​
    ​

  • Unit of Measure on recipe Components MUST be set to the correct measurement used in the Recipe.
    ​Example: 2-Row Malt is bought and inventoried pounds, but used in kilograms. The system will automatically make those conversions from the Package set on the Prodcut to the unit it is used in the Recipe. If conversions cross measurement types, (such as buying something in gallons but using it in pounds), the weight per unit of that Component is set on its Product record.
    ​
    ​

  • Pass-Through Equipment such as filtration or pasteurization between stages should be an instruction at the end of the stage users are transferring from.

Distributor steps for setting up directed inventory cycle counts in Encompass WMS: create count plans with count method, schedule and count rules by bin, zone or product. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to create WMS Inventory Count Plans
​
​1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the "WMS Inventory Count Plans" table.
​
2. Click Add WMS Inventory Count Plans.
​
3. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the ‘New WMS Inventory Count Plan’ form.
​
​

  • "WMS Inventory Count Plan" is the name of the plan. It helps to set this name as a short description of what or when inventory is counted.
    ​
    ​

  • "Count Method" determines the priority of items to count.
    ​
    ​ a. Time Since Last Counted: Used to prioritize items to count from the Bin Inventories table, Last Count Field.

b. Most Active Bins: Used to prioritize items to count from the number of Bin Trans.

c. Largest Variance: Used to prioritize items to count from the current Bin Inventory record in the Adjustment Bin that is assigned to this Plan (set in the next step).
​

  • "Adjustment Bin" determines where the Bin Inventory record changes will take place as items are counted.
    ​
    ​

  • Enter "Location".
    ​
    ​

  • "Day of Week" is the day of the week the system will generate a Count Task.
    ​
    ​

  • "Start Time" is the time of the day that the Count Task will be created.
    ​
    ​

  • "Total Counts" is the total number of Bin Inventory records that will be counted in each Count Task.
    ​
    ​ Note: To schedule the Inventory Count Task, fill in ALL three of the fields shown here: The Day of Week, Start Time, and Total Counts.
    ​
    ​

4. Click Add Record when complete.
​
5. Subtable "WMS Inventory Count Rules"
​
6. Click Add WMS Inventory Count Rules
​
7. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the"New WMS Inventory Count Rules" form and click Add Record when complete.
​
​ NOTE: Creating WMS Inventory Count Rules allows for ultimate specification when deciding products to count and where to count them from; combine a mixture of Bins, Bin Zones, Products, Brands, Suppliers, and Brand Families
​
​

  • "Bin Zone" and "Bin": These fields define the Bins and Bin Zones that will be counted as part of this Plan
    ​
    ​

  • "Brand", "Product", "Supplier", and "Brand Family": These fields will define what Products will be counted as part of this Plan

Distributor steps for scheduling a table import to run automatically in Encompass using Import Projects and the Table Import Wizard's Import Scheduling tab. Import must use a report, mailbox or EDBL client.

Steps

How to Schedule an Import
​
Import Routines are scheduled through an Import Project. An Import Project can hold multiple Import Routines. Use an existing Import Project and Schedule or create a new one.
​
1. Navigate to the Import Projects Table
​
2. Click Add Import Projects
​
3. Name the Import Project
​
4. Click Add Record
​
5. Navigate to you Import Routine and open the Table Import Wizard
​
6. Select the Import Scheduling tab
​

Fields And Definitions

  • *Schedule Name - Descriptive name of the frequency, reason for import, etc.
    ​
    ​

  • *Frequency - How often the Import Routine will run (Daily, Weekly, Monthly)
    ​
    ​

  • Repeat Every Minutes - How many minutes the Import Routine will attempt to run within the set run times (For example: If set to 15 minutes and run time is 1 hour, the import routine will run 4 times)
    ​
    ​

  • Start Time - When the Import Routine will run for the first time
    ​
    ​

  • End Time - When the Import Routine will stop running (If the Repeat Every Minutes is longer than the duration between the Start and End Time, the Import Routine will only run once)
    ​
    ​

  • *Next Run Time - The date the Import Project/Routine will run
    ​
    ​

  • *Run Permission - The permission required to manually run the import outside of the schedule

Distributor guide to setting up Return Rules in Encompass so returned products go to the right bin, stay on the truck or post to an adjustment customer based on return reason. Requires v24.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 24.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Check Return Rules
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Return Rules table.
​
2. Review the "Location", "Route Count Type", and "Priority" fields:
​
​

  • Location: The Warehouse where this Return Rule applies to.
    ​
    ​

  • Route Count Type: Limits which "Route Count Types" will see these return rules on Route Reconciliation. Route Count Type is located in the Bin Zone.
    ​
    ​

  • Priority: Determines the order in which the rules are prioritized if a single reason is used more than once.

3. Review the "Product Pick Type", "Pick Unit", and "Reason" fields:
​
​

  • Product Pick Type: this allows users to create a return rule specific to a product pick type. For example, if the product has a pick type of KEG and we use the 'Out of Code' reason, use a return rule to send that keg to a specific bin (ex. Out of Code Kegs Bin) different from where we might send products that have a PKG product pick type.
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Unit: Allows users to create a return rule specific to a pick unit. For example, if users are returning a full pallet and they want to use the 'Refused' reason, we can use a return rule to send that full pallet to a specific bin or adjustment customer (ex. Bulk Return Bin) rather than the default pick bin.
    ​

  • Reason: This comes from the Reasons table. Allows users to use the same reason for multiple return rules without cluttering the return.

4. Review the "Bin Zone" and "Remain on Truck" fields:
​
​

  • Bin Zone: Used to filter products by zone. If we set this on a rule and the product has a bin inventory in this bin zone, we will use the return bin on this return rule (used for larger warehouses).
    ​
    ​

  • Remain On Truck: True or False setting. Set this to true to leave the product on the truck.
    ​
    ​

5. Review the "Return Bin", "Adjustment Customer", and "Return to Default Pick Bin" fields:
​
​

  • Return Bin: (WMS users only) this is the bin, other than the default pick bin, the product will be returned to. Often is an adjustment or return bin.
    ​
    ​

  • Adjustment Customer: Alternately indicate an adjustment customer to write off the product on an invoice when returning the load.
    ​

  • Return To Default Pick Bin: True or False. Set this to true to return product to the default pick bin.


Note: If using "Return Bin", do not use "Adjustment Customer", and vice versa.

Fields And Definitions

  • *Location - Location should be the same as the location of the Warehouse and Load Sheets that the Rule should apply to.
    ​
    ​

  • Route Count Type - Determines the Route Count Type that this Rule should apply to.
    ​
    ​

  • *Priority - If a Route can trigger multiple Return Rules for returned inventory (i.e., multiple rules have the same Location, Route Count Type, and Reason), Priority determines the order the Rules should be executed in.
    ​
    ​

  • Product Pick Type - Determines the type of Product (e.g., can, keg, misc) that will trigger the Return Rule.
    ​
    ​

  • Pick Unit - Determines the Unit (bottle or case) that the product will be returned in. Typically, this should match the Unit type of the Pick Bin Zone to the product that will be returned to.
    ​
    ​

  • Reason - Determines the Reason (AKA Reason Code) for returned product required to trigger the Return Rule.
    ​
    ​NOTE: The Reason Code must have either Allow Return = True or
    ​
    Allow Return Error = True to be chosen within a Return Rule
    ​
    ​

  • Bin Zone - If the returned product has Bin Inventory in the selected Bin Zone, this Return Rule will apply (as long as criteria determined by other fields are met).
    ​
    ​

  • Return Bin - Determines the Bin the returned product should be returned to.
    ​
    ​NOTE: Leave blank if an Adj. Customer is chosen
    ​
    ​

  • ADJ Customer - Instances, where the returned product should not be allocated to a Bin (e.g., Unusable product), can be assigned to an Adj. Customer. This will not replenish the Bin Inventory. In other words, assign an Adj. Customer in place of a Bin
    ​
    ​NOTE: Leave blank if a Return Bin is chosen

Distributor guide to a customer's Assigned Users in Encompass: how stops set the salesman, deliveryman and merchandiser, and how to change a customer's sales rep. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

How to Identify and Manage Assigned Users
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Customer Search dashboard.
​

a. Search for the intended Customer name or ID.
​
b. Click the arrow to view the customer record directly.
​
c. Click Sub Tables.
​
d. Select "Assigned Users" from the dropdown.
​

These are the fields of the assigned users. They are generated automatically based on the Customer's Stops:

  • Product Group: Users can be assigned to different sets of products.
    ​
    ​

  • Route Version: For any given version, there is a minimum of one record for Assigned Users.
    ​
    ​

  • Salesman: The Salesman for that group of products.
    ​
    ​

  • Deliveryman: The Deliveryman for that group of products.
    ​
    ​

  • Merchandiser: The Merchandiser for that group of products

2. Click Sub Tables.

a. Select Stops.

The Stops are what determine the Assigned Users. The Activity Effective (either set on the stop directly or drawn from the route) will point the user (Name column) to its respective field in the Assigned User.

  • Route Version, Active: The Route Version on which this stop resides, and if it is currently active.
    ​

  • Activity Effective: The Activity is either set directly on the stop or is derived from the Route. This determines whether the NAMED user is a Salesman, Deliveryman, or Merchandiser.
    ​
    ​

  • Product Group: the set of products for this stop.

c. Select an Activity from the Stops dropdown.
​

The Activity, set on either STOP or the ROUTE, determines if that user is a Salesman, Deliveryman, or Merchandiser.

Note: If the activity is Salesman, that user will be set as the 'Salesmen' field on the Customer as well.
​
​

Best Practices

To update a Sales Rep on a Customer record the user will need to either:
​
​

  • Update the Routes User for that specific Stop
    ​
    ​

  • Change the Route to a different users Route for that Stop
    ​
    ​

This will then update the Assigned User table and flow into the Sales Rep field on the Customer record

If a customer does not have a presell stop, the assigned user will be set based on the Customers "Sales Rep" field. Whether or not a customer has a presell stop, Assigned Users will always be built for reporting purposes.

Pre-Conditions

Steps

How to Reorder Financial Statements

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Financial Sections table.
​
2. Using the Type column header, apply filtering to display a specific Type.

3. Click the Pencil icon to edit the Sequence field.
​

​

a. Click "Edit Column".

a. The lower the number, the higher it will appear in the statement.

​ Example: Revenue is set to 500, and each relevant Account Type should have a higher number. If Sale Income is set to 501, it will display under Revenue. If Deposit income is set to 502, it will display under Sales Revenue.

Fields And Definitions

Financial Sections table
​

This table is intended to direct components of financial statements into their appropriate statement type.
​
​

  • Type - There are three Types available in Financial Sections, and each one represents a different financial statement. The three types are Balance Sheet, Profit & Loss (Income Statement), and Cash Flow (Statement of Cash Flows).
    ​
    ​

  • Sequence - Sequence numbers are set for Types and Sections that share similar characteristics such as Assets or Liabilities. This enables users to organize financial statements in a way that allows fiscal authorities to verify the completeness of a company’s financial records.
    ​
    ​

  • Section - Represents the components that make up a financial statement
    ​
    ​

  • Sign - Represents how the balance of each Financial Section is calculated (Credit or Debit balance)
    ​
    ​

  • Auto Manage - Automatically classifies Account Types into their respective financial statement

Financial Sections Account Types table
​
​

This table is used to combine Financial Sections and Account Type records.
​
​

  • Section - Determines the Financial Sections that is connected to the referenced Account Type in the following field

  • Account Type - Determines the Account Type that is connected to the referenced Financial Section in the previous field
    ​
    ​

  • Code - Represents Account Code set on the Account Type record referenced
    ​
    ​

  • Child - A high-level component on a financial statement such as Net Income
    ​
    ​

  • Detail - A detailed component on a financial statement such as Net Operating Income or Other Net Income

Best Practices

  • Confirm or set the sequence on each financial section to reflect the order in which the user would like their financial statements to show.
    ​
    ​

  • Remember each sequence may represent a group of Account types. For example, Revenue may have a sequence of 500, and each account type under it such as sales income may have a sequence of 501, Deposit Income may be 502, and so on.

Distributor steps for running the Inventory Status Report from Warehouse Home in Encompass to see on-hand, picked, loaded, allocated and available inventory, with column definitions. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to Create an Inventory Status Report
​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Warehouse Home dashboard.
​
2. Click the Status Report link.
​
3. Apply filters, as needed to refine the data displayed. Filter options include:
​
​

  • Display - Determines how the product is displayed.
    ​
    ​

  • Units - Changes the configuration of how the inventory is tallied.
    ​
    ​

  • Start Date - Determines the start date from which the inventory changes are tracked in the report. If blank, we show changes for today.
    ​

    ​
    ​

  • Columns - These are the columns that will display in the report, and reflect the movement of the product from the warehouse to the customer.
    ​

4. Click Create Report
​
​

Fields And Definitions

Inventory:

Sum of all other columns except Pre-Sales, Allocated, and Available. This number represents the total inventory owned.

Pending Invoices:

Sales on load sheets that have been delivered, returned, and balanced, but are not yet verified.

Loaded:

Total inventory that has been loaded onto Route Bins for delivery.

Picked:

Total inventory that has been picked, but not yet Loaded.

Delivered:

Total inventory that has been delivered, but is still on Load Sheets in the Loaded Status.

Unsellable:

Total inventory in bins that have a Bin Zone Type = Adjustment.

On-Floor:

Total inventory within bins that have a Bin Zone where On Floor = True.

Pre-Sales:

Ordered inventory on a New status Load Sheet that is not yet picked or loaded.

Allocated:

Inventory that has been specifically "set aside" using the Allocations table, and is therefore not universally available.

Available:

On Floor - Pre-Sales and Allocated.

Purchases:

Total inventory that has been received.

Invoices:

Total sales on verified Load Sheets.

Best Practices

Check the not 0 filter on the inventory status report. The "Not 0" filter in the Warehouse Inventory Status dashboard reflects the current inventory status, not the inventory status on a historical date. If the current inventory for a product is 0, the report will not return any results, regardless of past inventory levels.

Distributor steps for checking why Encompass is slow: view page performance (server time, browser render, internet speed) and troubleshoot slowness or the No Internet Connection pop-up. Requires v23.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 23.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to show Page Performance
​
​
​

1. Expand the menu on the left side and click the 3-dots option in the top-right corner of the left-side menu
​
2. Scroll to the bottom of this menu to view Performance information
​
3. The Version, Server Time, Browser Render, and Internet Speed are displayed in this part of the menu

Troubleshooting Slowness

After showing the page performance using the steps above,

  • Slow Server Time (> 5 seconds, depending on the page): The system is running slower, check status.encompasstech.com for known issues, or contact Encompass Support
    ​
    ​

  • Slow Browser Render(> 1 second, depending on the page): Your personal computer is running slow, check for processes or other pages that are slowing it down, or work with your local I.T. department to troubleshoot further
    ​
    ​

  • Slow Internet Speed (< 3-5 Mbps, depending on ISP expectations): Check with your I.T. on making this faster, or contact your local Internet Service Provider (ISP). You can also try checking through awsspeedtest.com to the Oregon region to check for high latency issues with your ISP
    ​
    ​

Internet Speed is a rough estimate based on the last resource file loaded on the page
​
​

No Internet Connection dialog
​
​

  • This pop-up is driven by navigator.onLine value, which is the browser itself telling Encompass if it has connection to the internet or not.
    ​
    ​

  • Encompass checks this value whenever making a call to the server, and if it the browser says you are not connected to the internet, it continues to re-check every 1 second. The dialog goes away if the browser says you are connected again.

Fields And Definitions

  • Version: This is the current Encompass server version
    ​
    ​

  • Web: Name of the server cluster that generated the page
    ​
    ​

  • DB: Primary database hosting this system
    ​
    ​

  • DW: Datawarehouse (Snowflake cluster) used for reporting by this system
    ​
    ​

  • Server Time: Time it takes for the server to generate the page
    ​
    ​

  • Browser Render: Estimate how long it took the browser to deliver the page over the internet and render it
    ​
    ​

  • Internet Speed: Estimate the internet speed of the last resource downloaded
    ​
    ​

  • If the Server Time is high, this means the page was a complex or heavy page for the server to generate, or the Encompass system is running slower
    ​
    ​

  • If the Browser Render time is high, this means the local internet connection is slow, or the computer running your browser is slow
    ​

  • Internet Speed is rough estimate based on the last resource file loaded on the page
    ​
    ​

  • Use Fast.com and AWSSpeedTest.com (to Oregon) to get a more accurate estimate of your local internet speed

Producer steps for copying a recipe in Encompass production via Recipe Management: add a recipe version for a new product and copy stages, components and instructions. Requires v22.08+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.08

Steps

How to copy Recipes

When a Recipe is copied, all Stages, Components, Instructions ByProducts, etc., will populate on the new recipe with the new name and the new Product being produced.

  1. Using Universal search, navigate to the ‘Recipe Management’ dashboard
    ​
    ​

  2. Click on ‘Add Recipe Version’
    ​
    ​

  3. Select the new recipe name in the ‘Recipe Version’ field
    ​
    ​

  4. In the ‘Product’ field, select what the recipe will produce
    ​
    ​

  5. Fill out ‘Location’, ‘Recipe Type’, ‘Planned Units’, and ‘UoM’ fields
    ​
    ​

    Screenshot

  6. In the ‘Copy Stages from Recipe’ field, select which Recipe to copy other Recipe Stages, Components, and Instructions from
    ​
    ​

  7. Click ‘Add Recipe Version’

Fields And Definitions

*required fields

  • Recipes - Templates where Batches and Production Orders are scheduled from.
    ​
    ​

  • Recipe Management Dashboard - Let Users interact with many tables at once. Through the Recipe Management Dashboard, the tables we will be interacting with are:
    ​
    ​- *Products - Raw Material Products, Work in Process Products, and Finished Goods Products need to be on the Products Table to add to Recipes.
    ​
    ​- *Production Stage Types - The term which describes a specific group of actions and/or inputs that comprise a single Recipe Stage in a Recipe. Verbs like Blending, Filtering, Pasteurizing, etc.
    ​
    ​- QC Measurements - Measurements that are taken during any Recipe on any Stage. To add QC to a Recipe, the Measurement must first be in the QC Measurements Table.
    ​
    ​NOTE: If needed, refer to the “QC Templates Training” to have QC Measurement Templates automatically added into Recipes as they are being built.
    ​
    ​

  • UoM (Unit of Measure) - The unit by which the goods are measured

Best Practices

  • Recipes should be built as if one whole batch of the Product is being made. Multiple-Batching can be entered at the time Recipes are scheduled, allowing a single Recipe to be used for many different Production volumes.
    ​
    ​

  • Build Recipes to a single run - Use turns on a recipe to double brew into a larger vessel.
    ​Example: If brewing 30bbls for ferment on a 15bbl system, make the brew or the mash/boil turnable at 15bbls each then have the fermentation stage plan for 15bbl.
    ​
    ​

  • Unit of Measure on recipe Components MUST be set to the correct measurement used in the Recipe. If this field is not set correctly, Inventory will be depleted inaccurately and cause Inventory discrepancies that get worse each time the Recipe is Processed. Volume-to-volume (e.g., gallons to liters) or weight-to-weight (e.g., pounds to kilograms) are calculated automatically from the Product’s Package field
    ​
    ​Example: 2-Row Malt is bought and inventoried pounds, but used in kilograms. The system will automatically make those conversions from the Product’s Package to the unit it is used in the Recipe.
    ​
    If conversions cross measurement types, (i.e., buying something in gallons but using it in pounds), the weight per unit of that Component needs to be set on its Product record.
    ​
    ​

  • Recipe Stages represent a single workflow for Users to follow. Grouping Instructions and Components by Timing and Sequence allow for a repeatable process for Users to do everything in the correct order, at the appropriate time.
    ​
    ​

  • Pass-Through Equipment such as filtration or pasteurization between stages should occur as Instructions at the end of the stage you will be transferring from.

Distributor steps for reconciling AR, AP, inventory and undeposited funds subledgers to the trial balance in Encompass Financials and tracking down variances. Requires Encompass Financials and v25.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 25.01

Pre-Conditions

This can only be done using Encompass Financials.

Steps

Follow these steps once AR and AP have been closed through the date being reconciled. Using an example date of 9/30/25 for below scenarios:

ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE Subledger Reconciliation
​
​

1. Run a trial balance or balance sheet for AR with Statement Date = 9/30/25.
​
​

2. Run the Accounts Receivable Aging report with a Statement Date = 9/30/25.
​
​

If they don't match:
​
​

  • Navigate to the Financial Reporting dashboard, run the Accounts Receivable Sub-Ledger Reconcilation report for 9/30/25.
    ​
    ​

  • If there are offsetting debit and credit dollar amounts, then do a mapping change to move the dollars between 2 accounts.
    ​
    ​

  • If there is a real difference, run the report on various dates to determine what day AR went off track.
    ​
    ​

  • Search invoices on that date for the dollar amount that is off.
    ​
    ​

  • Adjust the Accounts Receivalbe Aging report to see it by "Location/AR Account Map" to identify unexpected pairings (filter further on specific location, add Customer, and AR Account for better details).

ACCOUNTS PAYABLE Subledger Reconciliation
​
​

1. Run trial balance or balance sheet for AP with Statement Date = 9/30/25.
​
​

2. Run Accounts Payable Agingwith a Statement Date = 9/30/25.
​
​

If they don't match:
​
​

  • Navigate to the Financial Reportingdashboard, run Accounts Payable Sub-Ledger Reconcilation report.
    ​
    ​

  • If there are offsetting debit and credit dollar amounts, then do a mapping change to move the dollars between 2 accounts.
    ​
    ​

  • If there is a real difference, run the report on various dates to determine what day AP went off track
    ​
    ​

  • Search purchases on that date for the dollar amount that is off.
    ​
    ​

  • Adjust the Accounts Payable Aging report to see it by GL account to help compare against the Trial Balance.

INVENTORY Subledger Reconciliation
​
​

1. Run trial balance or balance sheet for Inventory with a Statement Date = 9/30/25.
​
​

2. Run the Inventory Valuation report with an End Date = 9/30/25. Look at "Posted Value" in the middle of the report.
​
​

If they don't match:
​
​

  • Navigate to the Financial Reporting dashboard, and run the Inventory Sub-Ledger Reconciliation report.
    ​
    ​

  • If there are offsetting debit and credit dollar amounts, then do a mapping change to move the dollars between 2 accounts.
    ​
    ​

  • If there is a real difference, run the report on various dates to determine what day Inventory went off track.
    ​
    ​

  • Search purchases/invoices on that date for the dollar amount that is off.

UNDEPOSITED FUNDS Subledger Reconciliation

1. Run trial balance or balance sheet for Undeposited Funds with Statement Date = 9/30/25.
​
​

  • Navigate to the Invoices table and filter to invoices dated <10/1/25 but have a deposit date >9/30/25.
    ​
    ​

2. If the sum of the "Credit" column on the Invoices table does not match the undeposited funds total:
​
​

  • Go to the Financial Reporting dashboard, and run the Undeposited Funds Sub-Ledger Reconciliation report.
    ​
    ​

  • If there are offsetting debit and credit dollar amounts, then do a mapping change to move the dollars between 2 accounts.
    ​
    ​

  • If there is a real difference, run the report on various dates to determine what day Undeposited Funds went off track.
    ​
    ​

  • Search the Deposits table or the Invoices table on that date for the dollar amount that is off.
    ​
    ​

  • Look at the Invoice table for "AR Receipt" invoices that were received on a different date than they were deposited.

Best Practices

  • Use the "Sub-Ledger" reports on the Financial Dashboard to help troubleshoot variance.
    ​
    ​

  • Walk back the date on the Sub-Ledger report until the variance disappears, to help identify when exactly data went off track.
    ​
    ​

  • Use the exact amount of the difference in filters to see if variance comes from one source or multiple.
    ​
    ​

  • Use the Journal Entry Details report to pinpoint specific transactions.

16991562:
Developer overview of the Encompass API: API Commands, tokens via API certification, endpoint URL format, data formats, rate limits and $0.01/second processing cost. Requires v22.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.07

Steps

Overview:

Unlike typical Open APIs, Encompass APIs are tailored to each integration, delivering only the necessary data. These endpoints can utilize Encompass's core features or be built with custom Cloud Functions.

To create an API Command in Encompass, select the 'Inherits API Command' to specify the core functionality it extends (unless it's a Cloud Function).

  • Example: To make a Fusion report available via an API, create an API Command with 'Inherits API Command = FusionView' and a 'ReportID={your Report ID}' API Parameter.

Encompass API Commands are identified by a unique name in the API URL.

  • Example: https://api.encompass8.com/api?APICommand=myTableViewTest&EncompassID=Pioneer&APIToken={Token}

This allows access to any data from any Encompass system through a REST URL.

API charges are based on processing time and the amount of data transferred.

Getting Started:

Authentication: All requests require a valid API Token. Get a token via Encompass API Certification (see "Authentication")
​
​Rate/Usage: Be aware of configurable rate and usage limits. API costs $0.01 per processing second.
​
​Security: Only HTTPS is supported. HTTP requests are redirected.
​
​Data Format: Use the "Format" parameter to request data in different formats (e.g., Format=JSON). Options include JSON, XML, CSV, HTML (availability varies).
​
​API Endpoint:

  • For the generic endpoint (api.encompass8.com), include the "EncompassID" parameter.
    ​
    ​

  • System-specific URLs (e.g., training.encompass8.com) don't need "EncompassID."

Redirects: Your code must handle Encompass API redirects.

Authentication:

Access to Encompass APIs is controlled through API Tokens, which are obtained by completing the Encompass API/Code Block Certification. Encompass provides regular certification training.
​
​

Successful completion grants API Edit permission within the Encompass system.
​
​

Upon successful completion API creators can ask for the APISoultionAdmin to access API Tokens. Encompass API Tokens consist of 32 random characters (letters, numbers, and symbols).
​
​

Security Warning: Do not share your API Token!
​
​

Before an API Command can be executed on an Encompass system, it must be "installed" (granted access) through the App Library.

Rate and Usage Limits:

Encompass API usage is subject to a processing fee of $0.01 per second.

NOTE: Processing Time is calculated from the moment Encompass receives the request until the complete response is sent. This includes the time it takes to transfer data, which can impact larger uploads and downloads.

To help manage costs, API creators can configure the following settings:

Timeout In Seconds: The maximum allowed processing time for a single API request (typical values: 5-30 seconds).

Processing Limit (Minutes per Hour): The maximum total processing time allowed for this API Command within a single hour across all Encompass systems. This limit resets hourly.

API Parameters:
​
​

Encompass provides granular control over API Parameters, allowing API creators to define which parameters are allowed or disallowed for each API. They can also configure parameter details, including:

  • Data type
    ​
    ​

  • Maximum length
    ​
    ​

  • How the parameter is passed
    ​
    ​

  • JSON document format (if applicable)

This offers three key benefits:

  • Strong Typing: Encompass enforces parameter settings, reducing validation and error handling in your code.

  • Security: Enforcing parameter expectations minimizes the risk of vulnerabilities arising from unexpected parameter usage.

  • Automatic Documentation: Encompass automatically generates API documentation from these parameter configurations. Access this documentation via the "API Command Lookup" in your Encompass system.

Understanding the API Endpoint:
​
​

All Encompass API calls use the /API endpoint. The desired operation is specified using parameters:

Example: API?APIToken={Your API Token}&EncompassID={Encompass System}&APICommand={API Command Name}

In this example:

  • APIToken: Your unique API security key.

  • EncompassID: The specific Encompass system to access.

  • APICommand: The name of the API function to execute (this acts like a specific endpoint).

  • This approach enables Encompass to handle various API requests through a single URL.

For details on API Certification pricing, please visit the Certification and Training Dashboard in Encompass

Fields And Definitions

  • API = Application Programming Interface
    ​
    ​

  • REST = Representational State Transfer
    ​
    ​

  • URL = Uniform Resource Locator
    ​
    ​

  • API Endpoint = In APIs, an endpoint is typically a uniform resource locator (URL) that provides the location of a resource on the server.
    ​
    ​

AP Account - Accounts Payable (AP) account associated with the vendor

Is Inventory Vendor - Determines if the Vendor can be addressed on Purchases with inventory-tracked products

Carrier SCAC - Standard Carrier Alpha Code, used to identify road transport. Optional field that is relevant when Vendor Type is Carrier

Max Weight in Lbs -This is the max weight a vendor (carrier) can haul based on vehicle, trailer, and government regulations. This field is used by PO Generator to calculate the number of PO to create. Optional field that is relevant when Vendor Type is Carrier

Max Pallets -This is the maximum number of pallets a vendor (carrier) can fit in a trailer. This field is used in conjunction with Max Weight in Lbs to calculate the number of PO to create in PO Generator. Optional field that is relevant when Vendor Type is Carrier

Exercise Tax Exempt - If true, sets Purchases from this Vendor to Exempt from State Excise Taxes

Recalculate Cost On Receiving - If true, the cost is recalculated when receiving purchases, and these costs are not editable until the Shipment is received

Address - section to hold the location details for an individual vendor

License - section for License Number, Business Entity ID, and DUNS

Templates - section for the Purchase, Bill of Lading (BOL), and Print Receiving Pallet Tag information

Best Practices

  • The Vendor Type field can be blank, but if the vendor is also a carrier or trucking company, in order for a vendor (carrier) to be set as a carrier on a Shipment or set as the carrier on a forecast group, the vendor type will need to be set as a carrier. This type of Vendor can still be set as the Vendor on a Purchase.
    ​
    ​

  • A Vendor is a distinct and separate record from a Supplier. However, when these records would represent the same business entity, they can be bridged by creating a record on the Suppliers Vendors table.
    ​
    ​

  • Distributors may choose to use one AP Account for all Vendors or split them out however they wish
    ​
    ​

  • Because Vendors are linked to an AP Account in General Ledger, a Vendor is linked to one and only one Company. If a Distributor has two companies that buy from the same Vendor, they will need to have two unique Vendors set up in Encompass

16991575:
Distributor steps for restricting a new or limited product in Encompass with a Not Authorized allocation, then allocating units to chosen customers, chains or salesmen. Requires v22.07+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.07

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to 'Allocate a New Product' - Not Authorized Allocation
​

A 'Not Authorized' Allocation is used to restrict access to the product so that it can be selectively available and is necessary in cases where only certain Customers and Locations should have access to purchase it. If a Not Authorized is not set, it is available to be purchased by Customers who fit the Location, Distribution Area, Product Group, and other qualifying criteria. To create a Zero Allocation:

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Allocations table
​
​

2. Click Add Allocations button
​
​

a. Choose a Location
​
​

b. Choose a Product
​
​

c. Choose Not Authorized on Allocation Type
​
​

d. Choose a Start Date when the product's allocation process should begin
​
​

NOTE: This should be the same Start Date or later than the Start Date of the Not Authorized Allocation you just created
​
​

3. Click Add Record button
​
​

NOTE: Another Allocation will be used to truly allocate the product that was just 'zeroed out' by the allocation you just made.
​
​
​
​
​

How to Allocate a New Product - Actual Allocation
​

Once the appropriate Not Authorized is created to restrict the purchase of the product, the Reserve Inventory, Limit Purchase, Limit Purchase Quantity and Reserve Inventory, or Reserve Inventory Depleting Allocation must be created to selectively open access to purchase the product. For more information on selecting the right type for your use case, see the Allocations Overview guide.

1. After making a Zero Allocation, Click Add Allocation button
​
​NOTE: This new Allocation is used to truly allocate the product that was just 'zeroed-out' by the allocation you just made and determines which customers can purchase the Product or which Salesman can sell the product
​

a. Choose a Location
​
​

b. Choose a Product
​
​

c. Choose a preferred Allocation Type. Must not be ‘Not Authorized’
​
​

d. Filter additional fields according to preference
​
​

  • Allocation logic follows an order of precedence, prioritizing in the following order (from greatest priority to least): Customer, Chain, Salesman, Customer Type, On Premise or specify a Salesman to allocate the product
    ​
    ​

e. Choose Start Date - Make sure that the start date is the same as the previous ‘Not Authorized’ Allocation (Zero Allocation)
​
​

f. Enter Units Allocated - This is the quantity in Units for this particular product that is permissible for selling
​
​

g. Click Add Record button

Fields And Definitions

Fields

  • Location: The location where customers will be affected.
    ​
    ​

  • Product: The product for which the allocation will apply.
    ​
    ​

  • Allocation Type: The rules governing the allocation, determining its purpose.
    ​
    ​

  • Start Date: The date when the allocation begins. This date determines eligibility based on the invoice's "Time Entered," not the invoice date. Salespeople/customers cannot invoice the product before this date.
    ​
    ​

  • Units Allocated: The number of units included in the allocation
    ​
    ​

  • On Premise: Determines if the product is available to "On Premise" or "Off Premise" accounts.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer Type: Filters the type of customers to whom this product is available under the allocation.
    ​
    ​

  • Salesman: Filters by the assigned sales representative available to sell the product. The sales representative must be assigned to the customer for the allocated product to be invoiced.
    ​
    ​

  • Chain: Filters by the chain to which this product is available under the allocation.
    ​
    ​

  • Customer: Filters by the specific customer to whom this product is available under the allocation.
    ​
    ​

  • End Date: The end date of the allocation. After this date, any unallocated units will revert to available inventory.
    ​
    ​

Allocation Types

  • Reserve Inventory - Allocation quantity reserves that quantity for the exclusive use by that customer (but does not limit the quantity that customer can purchase).
    ​
    ​

  • Limit Purchase - Allocation quantity establishes an upper limit of how many of the product the customer can purchase (but does not reserve that same quantity for the exclusive use by that customer).
    ​
    ​

  • Limit Purchase Quantity and Reserve Inventory - Allocation quantity will establish an upper limit of how many of the product the customer can purchase as well as reserves that same quantity for the exclusive use by that customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Reserve Inventory Depleting - Allocation quantity reserves that quantity for the exclusive use by that customer (but does not limit the quantity that customer can purchase) and decreases the allocated amount as the customer purchases the product.
    ​
    ​

  • Max Purchase QTY Per Invoice - This allocation type will limit the amount of product that can be on a single invoice to a maximum. This allocation will not deplete and can be set across locations, chains and any other related allocation fields to help prevent a single customer from eating up all the inventory.
    ​
    ​

  • Unrestricted - Allows the customer to purchase the product, used in conjunction allocation type Not Authorized to provide overrides to more finely filtered allocations. For example, if you wanted to restrict a certain product to only On-Premise accounts, you would then add an allocation of type Not Authorized for Off Premise customers. If you then want to allow a specific liquor store to purchase that same product, you could then add an allocation of type Unrestricted for that one customer. As this second allocation is filtered more granularly than the first, the Unrestricted overrides the Not Authorized for that one customer.
    ​
    ​

  • Not Authorized - Prevents the customer from purchasing the product. The customer is able to view and retun the product, but sales of this product are not authorized.

Best Practices

1. When allocating a new product, a Not Authorized should be made first and foremost. A Not Authorizedn is used to 'clean the slate' for a new product and prevent ANY customers from purchasing or Salesmen from selling a product. Only after a Not Authorized is made should new Allocations be created.
​
​

2. Couple any new Allocations with a Not Authorized to ensure that the Product is only allocated to the desired Customers.

16991586:
Distributor reference for Code Date Type and Code Date Format on the Product record: Expiration vs Born On dates at receiving, and supplier code formats (Modelo, Heineken, Mikes, Canadian Domestic). Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Steps

  1. Code Date Type and Code Date Format are set on the Product Record.
    ​
    ​

  2. Code Date Type controls whether Expiration or Born On is collected during receiving.
    ​
    ​

  3. Code Date Type should be set to "Expiration Date" or "Born On Date" if the date information entered during receiving will be in the "MMDDYY" format. For any other date format, Code Date Type should be set to "Expiration Code" or "Born On Code"
    ​
    ​

  4. Code Date Format controls how the data information entered will be translated or interpreted by the system and must be populated if Code Date Type is set to "Expiration Code" or "Born on Code" to prevent errors during receiving.
    ​
    ​

  5. Any Code Date Formats using 'D', 'M', or 'Y' specify D for Day, M for Month and Y for Year.
    ​
    ​

  6. All other Code Date Formats are explained in the Fields and Definitions section of this Help Resource Record.

Fields And Definitions

Code Date Format Types for Expiration Date and Born on Code

​Modelo Format 1: ADDY, where D188 represents 4/18/2018. In this format, the first letter represents the month, the next two numbers represent the day, and the last number is the year represented by one number starting at 2011.
​
​Modelo Format 2: AA##, where HI18 represents 4/18/2018. In this format, the first letter represents the year the second letter is the month and the next number is the day.
​
Starting at 2011 or (A) then increasing with a letter all the way to 2022 or (L).
​
The Second letter is on a reverse alphabetical scale going from L-A With L being 1 and A being 12.
​
The last number represents the day going from 1 - 31.
​
​Heineken: #### (1-9)(1-365). The first number represents the year where 1 = 2011 8=2018. The next number represents the number of days in the year. Example: 8010 would equal January 10th, 2018.
​
​Heineken Keg & Heineken CCM: This is a standard DDMMYY format with no spaces or delimiter. Example: 10/12/2017 is represented as 121017.
​
​Mikes: The first 5 characters determine the date and the last 4 represent an ID number. The first letter determines the Month From A-M and skipping the letter “I”. The next 4 digits represent DDYY. Example: M3118A7ME = 12/31/2018 and K2017A7ME = 10/20/2017.
​
​Canadian Domestic: The first character represents the month going from A - M (Excluding the letter “I”). The following 2 characters represent the day, is the days and the last 3 characters represent the year, starting with the letter 'X'. Example: C24X18 = 03/24/18 and M12X16 = 12/12/2016.
​
​Formats without day specified: Some formats only display month and year characters. The first or last day of the specified month is used to determine the code date.
​
For the code date format MMYYYY and MMMYY, the default day is the first day of the month.
​
For the code date format MMYY, the default day is the last day of the month.
​
​

Fields And Definitions

    ​

    ​

  • Table: The table the alert is based on.
    ​
    ​

  • Action: The action that triggers the alert (Add or Edit).
    ​
    ​

  • Frequency: How often the alert is sent (e.g., Hourly).

    ​

  • When To Send: Controls when the alert is sent based on when a record is added or edited.

    ​

  • What To Send: Defines what content is included in the alert. A display field from the selected table or related table that will display as a hyperlink to the record.

    ​
    ​

  • Value: The value used in the alert's filter conditions.
    ​
    ​

  • Auto-Subscribe Users: Automatically subscribe users to the alert.
    ​
    ​

  • Alert Users: Links alert users via the Alert ID.
    ​
    ​

  • SingleSendMD5: A combination of alert message elements such as Alert User, description, record IDs, Delivery Method, etc. These can be customized to meet your needs. This combination of elements converts into a near unique 32 character alphanumeric value. This value attaches a unique value to the combination of elements preventing duplicate messages.

Best Practices

Do not remove the unsubscribe link from the email message unless you are sure that the message does not have commercial intent.

- For more information, see the CAN-SPAM act (US), ACMA (Australia), CASL (Canada), and GDPR (EU)

  • Do Alert when an item needs immediate, time-sensitive attention.

General EDI terms

  • Acknowledgement: In the global data synchronization process, this is an Extensible Markup Language response to a command returned to the originator
    ​
    ​

  • ACH: Automated Clearing House
    ​
    ​

  • Advance Ship Notice (ASN): An electronic version of a printed packing slip that tells a buyer that goods have been shipped, how they have been packed items and the estimated arrival time. Also referred to as a Delivery Notice or Dispatch Advice
    ​
    ​

  • ANSI ASC X12: American National Standards Institute, Accredited Standards Committee X12, which comprises government and industry members who create EDI standards for submission to ANSI for approval and dissemination
    ​
    ​

  • DUNS: Dun & Bradstreet number, type of company identifier
    ​
    ​

  • EDI: Electronic Data Interchange. The computer-to-computer transfer of business transaction information using standard, industry-accepted message formats.
    ​
    ​

  • EDIFACT: Electronic Data Interchange For Administration, Commerce and Transport. The international EDI Standard as developed through the United Nations
    ​
    ​

  • EFT (Electronic funds transfer): Electronic payment in which funds are transferred between bank accounts at different financial institutions
    ​
    ​

  • FTP: File Transfer Protocol. A standard method of transmitting files from one computer to another over the internet
    ​
    ​

  • GLN: A Global Location Number (GLN) is a unique number that is assigned to locations to enable them to be identified uniquely worldwide. These global location numbers can be used to identify any legal, physical and functional locations.
    ​
    ​

  • GS1: A worldwide network of standards bodies and service providers which develops global supply chain standards and solutions used by over one million companies for bar coding, electronic business messaging, data synchronization and through the EPCglobal Network, radio frequency identification
    ​
    ​

  • GTIN: Global Trade Item Number. A unique identifier for each product. UPC is a type of GTIN
    ​
    ​

  • PurchaseOrder: A document issued by a buyer to a seller that details the terms of sale under which the buyer will purchase the seller’s goods.
    ​
    ​

  • SFTP: Secure File Transfer Protocol. A network protocol that provides file transfer and manipulation functionality over any reliable data stream. It is typically used with the SSH-2 protocol to provide secure file transfer.
    ​
    ​

  • Translator: A program used to convert information from flat file to EDI format, or from EDI format to flat file.
    ​
    ​

  • UCS: A subset of the ANSI X12 EDI standard.
    ​
    ​

  • Value-Added Network (VAN): Often abbreviated as VAN and today called an EDI Network Services Provider, a third-party entity which handles the electronic exchange of information between subscribers to its services. Services provided by VANs include electronic mailboxing of EDI transmissions, protocol and speed conversion, and EDI record keeping for audit tracking.

Best Practices

  • Auto-Reduce All: This will reduce the oversold amount one invoice at a time for all products that are oversold. The system will cut one from the customer that ordered the most, then one from the customer that ordered the second most, and so on. This process will repeat until the product is no longer oversold. The cut product will be backordered.
    ​
    ​

  • Auto-Backfill All: This fill orders with available inventory for each invoice for all products that are available for backfill. The customer that ordered the most product will get the first available item, the customer that ordered the second most will get the next available, and so on. This cycle will repeat until all available inventory is filled on orders
    ​
    ​

  • Invoice All: Fill the ordered quantity for all invoices for the product, regardless of inventory levels.

    ​
    ​

Distributor guide to the Reasons table in Encompass: set up codes like Picker Cut, Mis-pick or Refused for invoice cuts, returns and disputes, and control which roles and product types see them.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

What are 'Reasons' in Encompass?

Invoice adjustments are often necessary, and while audit trails can track who made a change, when it occurred, and the original value, they don't capture the reason for the change.

The Reasons table addresses this by providing pre-set options for common adjustments and rules that determine user selection and availability.

For example, if a Picker changes a product's units from 4 to 0, they can select "Picker Cut" as the reason. Similarly, if a product is loaded but not accepted, the Driver can specify whether it was a "Mis-pick," "Damaged Product," or "Refused." This provides valuable context to the warehouse, aiding in inventory management and identifying the cause of any errors for process improvement.

Reasons records contain values that define the rules for user selection, display settings, and the conditions under which the reason options are presented.

How To Use the Reasons Table

  1. Using Universal Search, navigate to the Reasons table
    ​
    ​

  2. Review Reasons displayed, edit Reasons by Record or Value using the Pencil icon
    ​
    ​TIP: Review Reasons for display by Role/Activity or by Product Type. When reviewing Reasons, values named "Allow [Role/Activity]" control display/hide for the Reason code. Reason codes by Product Type controls are set by Reason Product Types records.
    ​
    ​

  3. To review Product Types tied to Reasons, click the Sub Tables button and click "Reason Product Types" to add to view
    ​
    ​

  4. Click "v/+" to expland all or selected Reasons Product Types Sub Tables
    ​
    ​

  5. Review Reason Product Types records
    ​
    ​

  6. To add a Reason Product Types to a Reason code, click "Add Reason Product Types" on the Sub Table displayed below the reason and click "Save" when complete
    ​
    ​NOTE: If no Reason Product Types records exist, review the "All Product Types" field on the Reason record. A Reason should have either Allow All Product types = True OR Reasons Product Types records related to it, but not both/neither. If a product type is only tied to one Reason, that code is used automatically
    ​
    ​

  7. To add a Reasons record, click the Add Reasons button
    ​
    ​

  8. Enter values to all required and applicable optional fields displayed in the Add Reasons form and click the Add Record button when complete.
    ​
    ​TIP: Consider who, when, and how the new Reason code is to be used and set Fields and Reason Products Types, as needed.

Fields And Definitions

1. Table Fields
​

  • Reason: The name of the reason is what will appear for your users and any reports you run
    ​
    ​

  • Sequence: The order in which the reasons will appear
    ​
    ​

  • All Product Types: If this is set to true, we add all product types to this reason. If false, you will need to add product types to the reason
    ​
    ​

  • Auto Adj Invoice Reason: If this is set to true, any pickup or cut quantities with this reason on an invoice will be used to automatically fill in the same quantity for the reason within truck return. Make sure "Allow Count In" is set to true for the reason to be seen in truck return. Combine this with "Auto Adj Invoice Reason" on Route Count Types to enable full functionality.

Note: If a given product type is only attached to one reason, that reason will automatically be chosen when handheld and server users make cuts to that product type
​
​

Screenshot

2. Fields to determine who is able to view reasons
​
​

  • Allow Salesman: If the load sheet is in new status, salesmen will see this reason when editing the invoice
    ​
    ​

  • Allow Deliveryman: If the load sheet is in loaded status, drivers will see this reason when editing the invoice
    ​
    ​

  • Allow Count In: When returning the load sheet, this reason will be seen as a return option
    ​
    ​

  • Allow Return Error: When returning the load sheet and processing errors, this reason appears as an option for making adjustments
    ​
    ​

Screenshot

  • Auto Backorder: If true, this product will automatically generate a backorder when cutting from a higher amount
    ​
    ​

  • Sellable: If true, and this reason is chosen, any products cut are put into the load sheets bin and can be used for other customers
    ​
    ​

  • Accounts Receivable Reason: If true, available as a dispute reason on the invoice
    ​
    ​

Screenshot

Best Practices

  • Use clear and common terminology to avoid mis-labeling
    ​
    ​

  • Limit Reasons in logical ways to prioritize accuracy
    ​
    Example: Pickers are the only users who need to select "Picker Cut" as a Reason, make sure your Sales and Delivery Reps aren't tempted to select it when they should select "Mis-Pick" instead. Consider who needs to select "Good Product" vs "Refused"

What is a Quick Link?


Quick Link: A link with an encrypted URL that is only valid for a set period of time.

​
​

1. Using Universal Search, navigate to a table view.
​
2. Click the 'Share' icon.
​
3. Select 'Quick Link'.
​
4. Set the expiration and login requirements as needed, and click 'Generate'.
​
- The maximum lifespan of a Quick Link is 6 months.
​
​
5. Determine if it the quick link will be sent via eChat, Email, Text, or Copy-paste the URL as needed.
​
6. The history of Quick Links generated in the system can be viewed from the Quick Links Table.
​
- Users with PermissionEdit can extend the expiration dates on specific quick links if needed.
​
- This table will also contain information about when the link was last used by someone (Time Read).

Note: If a user is using a 'Auto Login' quick link, and attempt to navigate to another page, a prompt will appear stating:

"You are impersonating a user. Do you want to leave and go back to your login?"

The user will need to then log in if they want to visit that other page.

Fields And Definitions

  • Quick Link: A link with an encrypted URL that is only valid for a set period of time. The URL may or may not automatically log the user in to be able to access a single page/view.

  • Share: The common option/button in the system that generates quick links.

Best Practices

  • Use as short of a time span as is reasonable, based on what the link needs to be used for. Extending the lifespan of a Quick Link longer than it is needed increases security risk.
    ​
    ​

  • Require user login when creating the quick links when possible. This ensures that users are not seeing information they are not supposed to.
    ​
    ​

  • Do not use QuickLinks for integrations or application development, because they will not last forever and the application may break when they expire.

Distributor steps for creating an email, text or eChat alert from any table in Encompass: choose table update or time notification, set triggers, filters and recipients. Requires v22.01+.

Minimum Version Required: 22.01

Watch video on YouTube

Steps

How to create an Alert
​

  1. Navigate to any table view
    ​
    ​

  2. Click Add Alert button. This button is the bell icon in the top right corner.
    ​
    ​

  3. On the Alert Edit page, select the Alert Type
    ​
    ​

    • Table Update sends a message when a new record has been created or an existing record has been updated
      ​
      ​

    • Time Notification sends a message when a specific time is approaching/passed based on a specific time field
      ​
      ​

  4. Enter an Alert Name
    ​
    ​

  5. The Alert Message Body will show as the message of your Alert.
    ​
    ​

  6. Set the Table field if needed but it will fill based on the table of origin
    ​
    ​

  7. Action defines the trigger:
    ​
    ​-Add sends a message when new records are created on the selected table
    ​
    ​-Edit sends a message when updates to existing records are made on the selected table
    ​
    ​

  8. Optional: Apply filters to further refine alert logic. Click the + icon to add a filter
    ​
    ​

  9. Select ‘What To Send’ using the fields provided, by selected table. The field selected will generate a hyperlink to the corresponding record in the message body.
    ​
    ​

  10. Select ‘Who To Send To’ by Role or User
    ​

    • When sending to an entire Role you can choose to allow them to subscribe on their own, or auto-subscribe all users in the role
      ​
      ​

  11. The Delivery Method field will use the phone number or email address from the user record. If the user does not have eChat permissions, they will not be able to receive eChat alerts
    ​
    ​

  12. Click Save and Preview

Alert Frequency Step Down Logic

The alert frequency will be changed based on the criteria below:

  • If no alert has been sent for more than 1 week, then the alert frequency will be changed to 1 hour.

  • If no alert has been sent for more than 1 month, then the alert frequency will be changed to daily

These changes are being implemented in order to reduce processing times which improves report performance.

Fields And Definitions

  • Alerts - The table that holds Alerts records
    ​
    ​

  • Alert Type - Activity that triggers the notification
    ​
    ​

  • Messages - The table that holds messages sent by an alert

Best Practices

  • All alerts that are created on Alert Edit dashboard will contain an Unsubscribe button
    ​
    ​

  • Each time an email or text message is sent, a record is created in the Messages table
    ​
    ​

  • Use the Alert Library to view Encompass’ collection of alerts
    ​
    ​

  • Alerts can be customized further by clicking the Edit Fusion Report (Advanced) button after creating the alert.
